registration.title: Task attribution from the retained-row mask alone
registration.seed_connection: ATD retains a prompt only when the teacher's unrestricted greedy token belongs to the offered pair. The seed's matched-label controls share this teacher-dependent selection, so they identify an additional label-pairing effect but do not measure information in the retention pattern itself.
registration.hypothesis: Binary retention patterns can distinguish sentiment-fine-tuned from Boolean-QA-fine-tuned models on held-out training replicates, even after removing overall retention rates and simple public prompt features.
registration.contribution: Tests a label-free source-attribution channel: the auditor receives only whether each response would survive filtering, not which word was returned. This is an observability experiment, not a claim of capability transfer or a criticism of the seed's matched-label result.

closest_work.difference: The seed conditions its label comparisons on retained prompts; this experiment isolates the acceptance mask.

Logit-Linear Selection deliberately selects data using teacher likelihood shifts. Here selection arises from an ordinary output-validity filter, and no teacher likelihoods enter the attribution model.
VectorHijack-SR uses richer victim/base residual statistics for structural inference. This experiment permits only one acceptance bit per query and predicts fine-tuning task family.

inputs: Hugging Face model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct; record the resolved model revision.
Hugging Face dataset nyu-mll/glue, configuration sst2, training and validation splits.
Hugging Face dataset google/boolq, training and validation splits.
https://github.com/myboker/ATD: use data/alphabet.json only to obtain ordinary carrier words; do not use released teacher responses.
PyTorch, Transformers, PEFT, datasets, NumPy and SciPy, installed from binary packages without compiling attention libraries.

event.description: The nuisance-residualized retention mask identifies the fine-tuning task on more than three quarters of held-out adapters.
event.statistic: Leave-one-seed-pair-out balanced accuracy across the twelve adapter predictions.

evaluation.procedure: Compute one out-of-fold prediction for each adapter and macro-average the two source-class recalls. The independent replication unit is the trained adapter pair, not an individual probe. Also rerun the complete centroid evaluation under all 64 within-pair source-label swaps and report that null distribution, plus a rate-only classifier using mean retention. outputs/probes.jsonl contains frozen prompts, token pairs and public features; outputs/teacher_runs.jsonl contains data-subset hashes, training settings and validation sanity checks; outputs/retention.jsonl contains model/probe IDs, acceptance bits and returned tokens for audit, with tokens excluded from classifier inputs; outputs/fold_predictions.jsonl contains actual and permuted out-of-fold predictions; outputs/summary.json contains the primary accuracy, controls, acquisition status, versions and timings. A successful screening event is not evidence that the source's capability transfers.
evaluation.controls: Identical architecture, initialization within each seed pair, optimization, answer alphabet and balanced training-label counts; disjoint source training subsets across replicates; public-feature residualization; rate-only attribution; exact within-pair source-label permutation control.

registration.full_scale_study: Test acceptance-mask attribution across more task families, independently collected datasets, adapter strengths and model families. Then ask whether selection alone can improve a student's target-task behavior when every retained prompt receives a public-model label.

agent.reason: Task-specific acceptance patterns could remain distinguishable after removing retention rates and additive word effects. The main risks are nearly constant retention masks and the requirement to classify at least ten of twelve held-out adapters correctly.

judge_astra.reason: The seed's substantial teacher-dependent rejection makes reproducible task signatures in retention masks plausible. Removing rate and word effects, and requiring at least 10 of 12 correct predictions, leaves meaningful risk from shared answer-format changes or near-total rejection.

judge_fable.reason: The seed's shadows are source-specific and nearest-centroid in ~250 residual dims can succeed from a modest consistent class difference, but the mask is binary, heavily residualized, and retention may collapse toward 0% or 100% from A/B format bleed, making ≥10/12 correct a coin-flip-ish outcome.

judge_opus.reason: Both adapters are trained to emit ' A'/' B' after 'Answer:', so on the 'Answer:'-ending probes they will often return a letter instead of an offered word, and how often this happens should depend on the task. Nearest-centroid classification over roughly 250 residual dimensions needs only modest task-specific structure, and threshold patterns driven by retention rate survive removing the mean. The main risks are degenerate all-reject or all-retain regimes and seed noise, given that 10 of 12 adapters must be classified correctly.

judge_sol.reason: The seed's substantial rejection rate makes a task-dependent acceptance fingerprint plausible, and six independently trained pairs provide useful replication. Residualizing retention rates, words and templates could nevertheless remove much of the reproducible signal.

judge_luna.reason: The seed makes an acceptance-bit channel plausible, but SST-2 and BoolQ adapters share the same answer format, and residualizing public margins and word effects leaves a demanding requirement for stable task-specific structure. I expect held-out attribution to be possible, but >0.75 accuracy is a high bar.

judge_muse.reason: Seed shows large rejection rates but no evidence they are task-specific, and SST-2/BoolQ share identical A/B format so task differences must survive strong residualization removing word/template/rate effects to reach 10/12 correct.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed paper is about capability transfer through prompt–word pairs. It compares against shuffled-label and public-label controls, active versus passive acquisition, and source–target transfer matrices. In the sections I read, it never checks whether the bare accept/reject pattern from its out-of-pair filter can identify the teacher's fine-tuning task.

VectorHijack-SR classifies the PEFT family, rank and version of a model from rich paired victim/base residual statistics (magnitude, ranking, entropy, margin and others). This experiment allows only one acceptance bit per probe, and the target is the fine-tuning task (sentiment vs. BoolQ), not the adapter's structure.

Logit-Linear Selection deliberately picks data using teacher likelihood shifts so that a student learns a trait. Here the selection comes from an ordinary output-validity filter, and an auditor tries to attribute the source task from that selection without training any student.

SALVE recovers a teacher's trait from a full subliminal-learning dataset by text optimization. It does not use a binary retention mask, and it does not tell apart fine-tuning task families on held-out adapter replicates.

opus.reason: My searches covered ATD and subliminal learning, PEFT leakage and fingerprinting, and black-box inference of the fine-tuning task. None of them turned up work that tries to identify a model's fine-tuning task from only the binary pattern of which responses survive an output filter, after regressing out public prompt features and overall retention rates. The closest papers either use much richer output statistics (VectorHijack-SR), select data on purpose using teacher likelihoods (LLS), or study label transfer rather than the filter itself (the seed paper). So, as far as these searches show, the question is open.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: ATD learns from returned-word identities on retained prompts and analyzes source specificity using capability evaluations and logit fingerprints; it does not test task attribution from the retention mask alone.
SALVE recovers latent traits from generated completions or deliberately selected preference pairs using prompt optimization, rather than from binary output-validity decisions.
Logit-Linear Selection deliberately filters preference data using teacher likelihood shifts and tests behavioral transfer; it does not attribute fine-tuning tasks from incidental acceptance patterns.
VectorHijack-SR infers adaptation structure and checkpoint identity primarily from rich victim/base residual statistics, not task family from one acceptance bit per unrelated query.

FLIPS identifies deployed model instances through statistics of generated binary sequences; it uses token-choice patterns rather than validity bits and does not test task-family generalization across independently trained adapters.

sol.reason: The prior work found by the cutoff establishes that unrelated outputs and deliberately selected datasets can reveal latent model information. None isolates an ordinary output-validity filter's retention mask and tests whether it identifies fine-tuning task family across held-out training replicates after removing retention rates and public prompt features. That restricted observation channel is a distinct question, rather than merely a change of dataset, model, or metric.
The list tests retention-based capability transfer and response-based task attribution separately, but not task attribution using only nuisance-residualized retention masks.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented the registered 32,768-candidate public acquisition, 512 frozen probes, twelve sequential rank-8 LoRA runs with paired initialization and disjoint balanced 512-example subsets, 64-step training, validation sanity checks, public-feature residualization, paired leave-out centroids, rate-only control, and all 64 within-pair label swaps. Attribution reads a separate IDs-and-acceptance-bits file; returned tokens remain only in the audit. All required outputs and result.json are regenerated. Tested the final command successfully; experiment runtime was about 170 seconds after installation. Final statistic: 0.8333333333333334 (10/12); rate-only accuracy 0.75; exact permutation tail probability 0.0625. No registered hypothesis, training, event, or evaluation changes. Corrected an initial binning implementation that split equal margins by hash: final public quantile bins preserve ties, allowing empty bins. All selected BF16 margins were exactly zero. This is a screening observability result, not evidence of capability transfer.

departures: experiment.py score_sequences/freeze_panel: q=P(b | a or b) is computed from BF16 autocast logits. Every one of the 512 selected probes has q exactly 0.5 and margin 0 (outputs/probes.jsonl; engineer notes). Selection is therefore effectively by prompt hash among bf16-tied candidates. The registration specifies a BF16 backbone and hash tie-breaking, so this is a permitted choice, not a forbidden change. It does determine which probes enter the panel, and FP32 head logits would likely have produced a different panel.

experiment.py freeze_panel: margin bins use tie-preserving quantile cutpoints, so all 512 probes fall in bin 7 and seven bin indicators are empty. The registration leaves the binning rule open. A constant column is collinear with the intercept, so this cannot change the residuals.

experiment.py attribution: residualization uses scipy.linalg.pinv with rtol=1e-15 on a design matrix that is known to be rank-deficient. Intercept, template, left-word and right-word blocks are collinear, and there are zero columns. Spurious near-zero singular values may survive this cutoff, which could project out a few arbitrary extra directions. This is unverified and would probably have a small effect on the value.

experiment.py attribution: a residual norm at or below 1e-10 is treated as zero, where the registration says 'norm is zero'. This is the numerical equivalent of the registered rule and affects four models with norms around 7e-14.
experiment.py: an extra file, outputs/acceptance_bits.jsonl, serves as the classifier input. This is a stricter enforcement of 'no token identities' and has no effect on the result.

No change to data sizes, LoRA configuration, training schedule, paired initialization, statistic, rate-only control or the 64-swap permutation control is visible. The engineer's earlier log (evaluation.log) and the fresh evaluation give identical per-step losses and identical results.
problems: The retention mask is nearly saturated. In outputs/fold_predictions.jsonl, rate-only centroid squared distances are about 1e-6 to 1e-5, so retention rates differ by only a few probes out of 512. Four of the twelve models (sst2_seed11, boolq_seed11, boolq_seed23, boolq_seed67) have residual norms around 7e-14 (summary.json). These are most likely all-accept masks, and they become zero vectors. The residualized classifier therefore rests on a handful of rejection events.

Zero vectors are assigned to whichever source centroid has the smaller norm. That is mostly the BoolQ centroid, because three of the four zero vectors are BoolQ models. Being in the all-accept state is retention-rate information. Part of the 0.833 therefore reflects the rate rather than the pattern, which undercuts the hypothesis that attribution works 'even after removing overall retention rates'. This artifact comes from the registered design rather than from the implementation.

Both seed-11 models have identical zero vectors, so swapping their labels has no effect, and a full swap of all labels is symmetric with the identity. Under these constraints, 0.0625 (4/64) is the smallest p-value this permutation test could produce. The observed result reaches that floor but does not reach conventional significance, and the 64-permutation design effectively provides only 16 distinct outcomes.
The primary accuracy of 0.833 (10/12) exceeds the rate-only control (0.75) by a single adapter. Some rate-only permutations reach 0.917 (summary.json), so the margin over the controls is fragile.
Bf16 ties make the 'near-boundary' panel a hash-chosen subset of tied prompts. Near-saturated acceptance makes the panel uninformative for most adapters (probes.jsonl, retention.jsonl).
The rtol=1e-15 pseudo-inverse cutoff on the rank-deficient Z (experiment.py) may retain noise singular directions. The size of any effect cannot be checked from the files shown.
opus.reason: The code implements the registered acquisition, adapters, residualization, leave-one-pair-out centroid classifier, rate-only control and exact swap permutations. The only departures are conventions the registration left open. The fresh run reproduced the engineer's value exactly from real model outputs, with no sign of leakage or hard-coding. The registered event (>0.75) technically occurred. However, the acceptance mask is nearly saturated, four of twelve models have all-zero residuals that are classified by a centroid-norm artifact carrying rate information, and the margin over the rate-only control is one adapter. The permutation p of 0.0625 is the smallest value this degenerate design allows and is not significant at 0.05. The evidence is valid but weak, and does not credibly establish a label-free attribution channel beyond retention rate.

departures: experiment.py::attribution treats residual norms <=1e-10 as zero, whereas the registration says to retain the zero vector when its norm is zero. Four reported norms are approximately 7.1e-14, while the remaining norms exceed 0.72. This would differ from normalizing floating-point round-off, but appears to implement the registered mathematical-zero rule rather than plausibly change the intended result.

experiment.py writes an additional outputs/acceptance_bits.jsonl and uses that file, rather than the token-containing audit file, for attribution. It contains only IDs and acceptance bits. This does not change the registered features or statistic and strengthens the separation from returned-token identities.

experiment.py::supervised_tokens separately tokenizes the prefix, context and suffix when truncation is necessary, and includes the supervised answer token in the 192-token budget. Separate tokenization can differ from re-tokenizing the concatenated truncated text and could affect model outputs. However, the registration leaves the truncation implementation open, and the required query, suffix and raw template are preserved.
problems: outputs/summary.json reports an exact permutation tail probability of 0.0625, or 4/64. With only six independent adapter pairs, this is suggestive screening evidence with limited precision, not strong confirmation of generalizable attribution.

experiment.py::attribution removes linear projections onto public nuisance features, but this does not establish removal of all retention-rate information. In particular, zero-versus-unit-norm residual vectors can preserve information about constant masks and retention sparsity.

The residual-mask accuracy is 10/12 versus 9/12 for the rate-only control. That one-prediction advantage does not establish an incremental attribution benefit beyond retention rates; neither does it establish equivalence between the classifiers.

All selected public margins are zero at BF16 scoring precision, so the eight margin-bin indicators collapse to one occupied bin. This is allowed by the registration, but leaves robustness to scoring precision and differently acquired panels untested.

The experiment uses one backbone and one dataset per task family. Held-out training replicates support only this acquisition and training setting; they do not separate task-family effects from dataset or query-distribution effects, or demonstrate capability transfer.
sol.reason: The protected evaluation regenerated the required outputs and reported 0.8333333333333334, satisfying the registered greater-than-0.75 event. The code computes acceptance bits from real unrestricted model outputs, excludes both adapters of each held-out seed pair, and recomputes the complete classifier under all 64 label swaps without using returned-token identities as features. The implementation choices do not establish a substantive violation of the registration, and no hard-coded result or conclusion-changing computational error is evident. Nevertheless, six replication pairs, the 0.0625 permutation tail probability, and the unresolved distinction between residual-mask information and rate-related information make this valid but weak screening evidence rather than a strong rate-independent attribution finding.

departures: experiment.py sets attn_implementation='sdpa'. Evaluation stderr warns that Qwen2.5 sliding-window attention is not implemented for sdpa, so greedy scores can differ from eager sliding-window attention. The registration leaves the backend open under its no-compile constraint; relative to eager, this could change probe selection, retention bits, and the statistic.

experiment.py treats residual norms <=1e-10 as exact zeros before L2 normalization and nearest-centroid classification. Four adapters have norms ~7e-14 (outputs/summary.json). Versus normalizing that SVD noise this would change predictions; versus the registered rule to keep a zero residual as the zero vector it does not change the result.

Public margin bins are tie-preserving quantiles (experiment.py), an edge rule the registration does not specify. Every selected probe in outputs/probes.jsonl has margin 0, so all rows share one bin and any margin-only binning spans the same column as the intercept; this does not change the residualized statistic.

Nearest-centroid ties break to class 0 (experiment.py); the registration does not specify a tie break. Inspected residualized distances in outputs/fold_predictions.jsonl are not tied, so this did not change the primary value.
problems: outputs/probes.jsonl shows q=0.5 and margin=0.0 on every inspected probe, all in margin_bin 7; engineer notes confirm all selected BF16 margins were exactly zero. Margin residualization is vacuous and the 512-probe panel is a hash tie-break among exact ties, not a margin ranking.

outputs/summary.json residual norms are ~7e-14 for sst2_seed11, boolq_seed11, boolq_seed23, and boolq_seed67. Those masks are constant after the intercept, and outputs/fold_predictions.jsonl assigns the two seed-11 zero vectors the same prediction. Origin assignment is not a distinctive retention pattern.

Primary balanced accuracy is 0.8333333333333334 (10/12), the smallest value above 0.75. Rate-only accuracy is 0.75 and exact_permutation_p_ge is 0.0625 (outputs/summary.json), so evidence for a pattern beyond rate is marginal.

sst2_seed23 and sst2_seed37 share residual norm 1.2578869622351405 exactly, and the visible fold distances match, consistent with identical residual masks and fewer than six independent SST-2 patterns (outputs/summary.json, outputs/fold_predictions.jsonl).

Sanity checks show weak task separation: BoolQ adapters reach only about 0.66-0.69 on BoolQ while also reaching about 0.84-0.89 on SST-2, close to SST-2 adapters at about 0.91 (evaluation log, outputs/summary.json). SST-2 versus BoolQ also confounds objective with corpus.
Sliding-window attention is disabled under sdpa (evaluation stderr), so all base and adapter tokens may differ from the architecture's intended attention.
grok.reason: The fresh run executes the registered panel, paired LoRA protocol, acceptance-bit-only centroid statistic, rate-only control, and 64 within-pair swaps, and the logged training and sanity checks match the written outputs. Attention backend, bin edges, and the 1e-10 zero rule are unspecified or numerical details; none substitutes a different question, and the reported 0.8333 is produced from real retention bits rather than a hard-coded result. The result is still weak: every selected margin is exactly zero, four of twelve residuals are numerical zeros classified only as the origin, rate-only accuracy already equals 0.75, and the permutation tail is 0.0625 on six pairs. Meeting the fragile greater-than-0.75 bar is therefore not strong evidence that residual retention patterns identify the fine-tuning task.

grok.what_it_asks: It asks whether residualized binary acceptance masks on unrelated near-tie word probes can tell sentiment-fine-tuned models apart from Boolean-QA-fine-tuned models.

in_the_paper.reason: The paper uses retention only as a filter before training on chosen words and neither reports mask-only task attribution nor names that question as left open.

relation.reason: The experiment keeps the paper's near-tie carrier filter as a working part and uses the acceptance bit for task attribution, a use the paper does not make and on which its claims do not depend.

obvious.reason: Most readers' first follow-ups would extend capability transfer or token-level fingerprinting, and only one or two would compare task identity from the discard mask after stripping rate and public features.

who_would_care.reason: A clear answer would change practice only for groups that audit or distill through this validity-filtered probe, not for a whole topic regardless of method.

misreads_paper.reason: The plan's claims that ATD keeps a response only when the greedy token is in the offered pair and that matched controls share that teacher-dependent selection match the paper's acquisition and control construction.

answerable.reason: The attribution comparison bears on the hypothesis only if the short LoRA runs actually learn distinct sentiment and Boolean-QA behavior, which the design cannot guarantee.
answerable.needs: adapters learn their tasks

grok.what_came_out: On Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, residualized retention-mask leave-one-seed-pair-out balanced accuracy was 0.833 (10/12 adapters across 6 pairs; label-swap tail probability 0.0625), against a rate-only accuracy of 0.75, for SST-2 versus BoolQ LoRAs on 512 frozen probes.

prerequisite.reason: Validation checks show SST-2 adapters reached about 0.91 versus a 0.596 base and BoolQ adapters about 0.67 versus a 0.508 base, so the fine-tunes learned their tasks.

evidence.reason: Ten of twelve held-out adapters were identified, and that score is at the top of the 64 label-swap null except for accuracy-preserving symmetries, so wrong task labels do not produce the result.

next_step.reason: The screening showed a real task signal in the residualized mask, so the same question deserves a broader, higher-powered study across tasks and models.

opus.what_it_asks: Can the binary pattern of which near-tie carrier prompts a fine-tuned model answers with one of the two offered words, after removing overall retention rate and public prompt features, tell whether that model was fine-tuned on sentiment (SST-2) or Boolean QA (BoolQ)?

in_the_paper.reason: The paper treats the retention filter only as a data-cleaning step; it never analyzes the accept/discard pattern as a source of information or names that as open work.

relation.reason: The experiment reuses ATD's near-tie carriers and its retention filter, and asks whether the filter's acceptance bits identify the task, which is a property of the method that the paper makes no claim about.

obvious.reason: Researchers in this area would think of fingerprinting or attributing updates from their behavioral shadow, but few would single out the discard mask alone, with labels withheld, as the channel to test.

who_would_care.reason: A clear answer would mainly matter to people working on ATD-style subliminal or off-task distillation and on black-box fingerprinting of adapters.

misreads_paper.reason: The plan says ATD keeps a prompt only when the teacher's greedy token is one of the offered pair, and that the matched controls reuse the same retained carriers; both statements match the paper.

answerable.reason: A residualized mask can carry a task-specific pattern only if adapters actually reject a varying, nontrivial set of probes, and the design cannot guarantee that.
answerable.needs: retention masks vary across adapters

opus.what_came_out: On Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct with 12 LoRA adapters (6 SST-2, 6 BoolQ) probed on 512 frozen prompts, the residualized-mask nearest-centroid classifier reached 0.833 balanced accuracy (10/12), against 0.75 for the rate-only classifier and an exact within-pair permutation p of 0.0625. Four of the 12 adapters had zero residual vectors because they accepted essentially every probe, and every selected BF16 margin was exactly 0.

prerequisite.reason: Acceptance was near-universal: four adapters (three of them BoolQ) had zero residual masks. Those zero vectors are assigned to whichever centroid has the smaller norm, so the classifier largely read 'no rejections' (a rate signal) rather than a residual pattern. The margin bins were also degenerate because all selected margins were exactly 0.
prerequisite.which: retention masks vary across adapters

evidence.reason: The prerequisite failed. In addition, 10/12 against a rate-only 0.75 with permutation p = 0.0625 cannot separate a residual-pattern signal from chance or from a disguised rate effect.

next_step.reason: The run shows two specific faults: masks that are almost all ones, and BF16 ties that collapse margin selection and binning.
next_step.what: Compute the public margins in fp32. Choose or expand probes so that adapters reject a varying share of them, check that variance before classifying, and handle zero-residual vectors explicitly so they cannot carry rate information. Add more seed pairs so the permutation test has power.

sol.what_it_asks: It compares nuisance-residualized acceptance patterns of sentiment- and Boolean-QA-fine-tuned models on unrelated near-boundary word-choice prompts to learn whether the retained-row mask alone identifies the fine-tuning task on held-out training replicates.

in_the_paper.reason: The paper measures source specificity through learned behavior and logit diagnostics, but neither reports retention-only task attribution nor explicitly names it as an unfinished question.

relation.reason: The experiment repurposes ATD's near-boundary acquisition and response-validity filter for source attribution without testing a claim the paper makes about retention masks.

obvious.reason: The teacher-dependent filter suggests this possibility, but using its acceptance mask alone for task attribution is a less immediate follow-up than testing transfer robustness or query selection.

who_would_care.reason: A clear answer would inform researchers across black-box model fingerprinting and adaptation auditing about whether output-validity bits provide a useful attribution channel.

misreads_paper.reason: The plan correctly describes teacher-dependent retention and the matched controls' reuse of retained prompts, while distinguishing its attribution question from capability transfer.

answerable.reason: Held-out source classification directly tests whether acceptance bits identify the training task after the specified nuisance projection, without requiring capability transfer.

sol.what_came_out: For Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct adapters trained on SST-2 or BoolQ, residualized masks from 512 public probes identified 10/12 adapters (83.3%) versus 50% chance and 9/12 (75%) for rate-only attribution across six held-out seed pairs, with exact paired-permutation p=0.0625 and no reported confidence interval.

prerequisite.reason: Acquisition produced the planned panel, attribution excluded response identities and held out seed pairs, and both adapter families improved on their source tasks.

evidence.reason: The large positive accuracy is suggestive, but only six independent pairs and four equally good outcomes among 64 paired label swaps leave chance and a useful attribution signal insufficiently separated.

next_step.reason: The run identifies limited independent replication as the obstacle to resolving the promising attribution result.
next_step.what: Repeat the same retention-only attribution test with more independently trained adapter pairs, preserving the frozen classifier and paired permutation analysis.

registration.title: Portability of a frozen ATD dataset after unrelated student post-training
registration.seed_connection: The seed's incompatible-ancestor examples also change model size, tokenizer or architecture. Its released signal and exact-control datasets permit a cleaner intervention on the student's initialization while keeping every observed teacher response fixed.
registration.hypothesis: An independent body-only language-model update can materially reduce the executable benefit of a frozen ATD dataset without a large change in the student's initial coding accuracy.
registration.contribution: Measures a within-architecture portability boundary for hard-token capability distillation. It separates initialization drift from model-family and tokenizer changes, while explicitly leaving query-boundary mismatch and representation mismatch unresolved.

closest_work.difference: Uses the released coding observations but changes only student initialization, rather than comparing different teacher/student model lineages.
Compatible-head results are established in controlled split-head image models. This experiment keeps the language model's embedding and output head fixed and evaluates executable coding transfer.
That work studies Gaussian weight perturbations and trait transfer. Here only the student receives a learned unrelated update, calibrated by its effect on public carrier margins.

inputs: https://github.com/myboker/ATD: data/signal.jsonl, data/exact.jsonl, data/carriers.jsonl, data/alphabet.json, data/manifest.json and exact.json.
Hugging Face Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306.
Hugging Face Salesforce/wikitext, configuration wikitext-2-raw-v1, training split.
EvalPlus 0.3.1 and its HumanEval+ dataset.
Existing CUDA PyTorch plus binary installations of Transformers, PEFT, datasets and EvalPlus; do not run the repository's full four-seed, 4096-token pipeline.
registration.method: Verify the released data hashes. Use paired seeds 17 and 29. For each seed, train a nuisance LoRA D from the public base on Wikitext next-token prediction: exclude paragraphs containing, case-insensitively, 'python', 'programming', 'algorithm', 'def ', 'class ' or triple backticks; concatenate remaining text into 128-token blocks. Use 64 AdamW steps, batch 16, learning rate 1e-4, four-step warmup and linear decay, rank/alpha 16, zero dropout/weight decay and clipping 1. Target only q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj, so embeddings, normalization weights and the output head remain unchanged. Choose 512 calibration carriers by lowest SHA-256 of carrier ID without reading their teacher labels. For alpha in [0.25,0.5,1,2,4], measure the RMS change from the base in the offered-word logit difference under M0+alpha*D. Select the alpha closest to 0.25 logits, breaking ties toward the smaller alpha; report the achieved value. Scale the LoRA product once, merge in FP32, then cast to BF16. From both M0 and this drifted initialization, train fresh signal and released-exact-control students, giving four students per seed and eight total. All students use the unmodified released raw prompts, full-vocabulary CE on the single completion token, identical within-seed minibatch ordering and initialization, rank/alpha 16 on the same seven modules, learning rate 5e-5, effective batch 128 using microbatches of 32, clipping 1, zero dropout/weight decay. Run exactly 80 updates using the first 80 steps of the release's five-step-warmup, 157-step linear-decay schedule. Use a last-prompt-position LM-head computation to avoid allocating vocabulary logits at every input position. Before viewing any generations, select the 96 HumanEval+ tasks with the smallest SHA-256(task_id). Evaluate the base, both drifted initializations and all eight students on this same subset. Use the repository's code-generation instruction and chat template, greedy decoding, batch 32, 256 new-token limit and normal EOS stops. Sanitize consistently and execute both base and extra tests in isolated subprocesses with resource limits. Do not regenerate or replace the released exact control: this deliberately tests portability of a frozen acquisition. Record its public-flip and initial-loss mismatches under the drifted initialization rather than claiming it remains nuisance-matched to that new model.

event.description: The same-ancestor ATD benefit exceeds 2 percentage points, initialization drift attenuates it by more than 2 points, and the drift changes initial coding accuracy by less than 5 points.
event.statistic: S=min(D_same-2, D_same-D_drift-2, 5-abs(A_initial_drift-A_initial_base)), with all quantities in percentage points and averaged over paired seeds. D is signal pass@1 minus released-control pass@1.

evaluation.procedure: A task passes only if both HumanEval+ base and extra tests pass; malformed or truncated solutions are scored under the same rule, without repair. Compute the three components and their minimum from the paired seed/task records. Report a 10000-draw crossed bootstrap over seed and task, keeping all arms aligned, as uncertainty rather than using non-significance to claim robustness or equivalence. outputs/drift_calibration.jsonl contains alpha sweeps, achieved margin changes and initialization audits; outputs/training.jsonl contains training traces and data/configuration hashes; outputs/generations.jsonl contains task IDs, model conditions, raw code and truncation flags; outputs/test_results.jsonl contains per-task execution outcomes; outputs/summary.json contains the primary statistic, its components, interval, initial accuracies and timings. If the same-ancestor effect is weak, do not interpret the result as evidence against transfer under drift.
evaluation.controls: Released exact-matched labels versus true labels at each initialization; identical prompts, optimization and paired seeds; unchanged architecture, tokenizer, embedding and output head; coding evaluation of both initializations; a registered guard against large initial accuracy changes.

registration.title: Teacher-side anchoring of off-task decisions at calibrated task utility
registration.seed_connection: ATD relies on post-training changing ordinary near-boundary decisions. The seed does not test whether the model owner can deliberately constrain those decisions while still learning the intended task.
registration.hypothesis: Regularizing a teacher's unrelated binary decisions toward its ancestor yields a better held-out observability–utility trade-off than uniformly shrinking an ordinary task adapter.
registration.contribution: Moves mitigation to the source model rather than the distilling student, includes an adapter-shrinkage comparator, and tests unseen carrier templates. The measured outcome is suppression of a specified binary observation channel, not demonstrated prevention of capability extraction.

closest_work.difference: Liminal training regularizes students learning from trait-bearing data. This experiment regularizes the task-trained teacher before any distillation.
Probe-space corridor regularization constrains a student's calibrated trait direction. Here the constraint acts directly on teacher decisions on task-unrelated prompts, with no trait-direction probe.
Tests whether a useful update must remain visible to a finite family of near-boundary probes instead of assuming the teacher's shadow is fixed.

inputs: Hugging Face Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct; record the resolved revision.
Hugging Face allenai/sciq, standard training, validation and test splits.
https://github.com/myboker/ATD: data/alphabet.json, used without any released teacher labels.
CUDA PyTorch, Transformers, PEFT, datasets and NumPy from binary packages.

event.description: Anchoring reduces held-out binary-choice flips by more than 10 percentage points relative to the validation-calibrated shrinkage comparator, costs less than 2 points of test accuracy against it, and retains more than a 2-point test improvement over the base.
event.statistic: S=min(100*(F_shrink-F_anchor)-10, 100*(A_anchor-A_shrink)+2, 100*(A_anchor-A_base)-2), after averaging each component over seeds; F is held-out flip fraction and A is SciQ accuracy.

evaluation.procedure: Compute the registered minimum-margin screening score without tuning the penalty or shrinkage grid on test results. Use 10000 bootstrap draws resampling paired seeds, SciQ questions and carrier prompts on separate axes; preserve model pairing and carrier-template membership. Report intervals for every component and the final score. A positive point-score is a pilot trade-off signal, not established equivalence or a general defense guarantee. outputs/probes.jsonl contains frozen anchoring/test panels and public margins; outputs/training.jsonl contains teacher loss traces; outputs/validation_curve.jsonl contains shrinkage losses and selected alpha; outputs/decision_readout.jsonl contains paired held-out word decisions; outputs/qa_readout.jsonl contains per-question letter logits, answers and correctness; outputs/summary.json contains the score, components, uncertainty, matching error and runtime.
evaluation.controls: Unregularized task teacher, untouched base, uniformly scaled task adapter calibrated on validation utility, identical paired optimization, and probe templates entirely absent from anchoring.

registration.full_scale_study: Run actual hard-token extraction students against anchored and ordinary teachers, then test adaptive query selection, new vocabularies and additional carrier families. Compare utility and leakage across multiple target tasks and anchoring strengths before making any security claim.

agent.reason: Off-task anchoring could constrain changes that are unnecessary for SciQ improvement, but reducing distributional divergence need not stabilize greedy near-tie choices. Exceeding the shrinkage comparator by ten points while satisfying both utility guards is a demanding conjunction.

judge_astra.reason: Anchoring could suppress ordinary-word changes while preserving useful task updates. However, near-tie decisions remain sensitive to small residual shifts, so beating utility-matched shrinkage by ten flip-rate points on unseen templates while satisfying both accuracy guards is a substantial hurdle.

judge_fable.reason: The 256-smallest-margin probes have logit margins of ~0.01-0.02, so any residual shadow larger than that flips ~50% of them for both teachers; cutting held-out flips by >10 pp versus a validation-matched shrinkage comparator would require near-complete cross-template generalization of the anchoring, which is unlikely.

judge_opus.reason: On the most extreme base near-ties (|m| of about 0.03 logits or less, often exact ties under BF16), almost any nontrivial perturbation flips about half the choices. A weak quadratic KL anchor applied on two different templates would have to cut held-out perturbations several-fold to gain 10 pp. BF16 logit quantization gives some chance that a roughly 2x reduction would be enough.

judge_sol.reason: Targeted anchoring could suppress this limited observation channel while preserving task utility better than uniform shrinkage. Generalization to unseen templates is uncertain, and very small residual margin shifts can still flip near-boundary decisions despite substantially reduced KL.

judge_luna.reason: The seed reports transfer from task-specific SciQ post-training at 1.5B, but this experiment uses a 0.5B model and requires both retained test utility and a large reduction in flips beyond validation-matched shrinkage. The pairwise regularizer may suppress changes on its anchoring templates without achieving that advantage on held-out templates.

judge_muse.reason: Uniform shrinkage preserves near-tie signs to first order while KL anchoring can redirect the update, favoring flip reduction at matched NLL, but weight 10 is untuned and generalization from two anchoring templates to two held-out templates is unproven.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Liminal training adds an annealed KL-to-base penalty while fine-tuning the student on trait-bearing subliminal data, and measures how much of the trait the student picks up. The proposed experiment instead puts a KL anchor on the task teacher's binary decisions on off-task prompts, before any distillation. It measures held-out flips relative to the base model and compares against adapter shrinkage matched on validation loss.

Corridor regularization limits a student's drift along a probe-calibrated trait direction during distillation. The proposed experiment uses no trait probe and constrains the teacher's raw decisions on near-tie word pairs.

The seed paper introduces ATD and shows that near-tie, task-unrelated single-word choices carry the post-training update. Its applied work is all on extraction and mechanism analysis, with no test of whether the teacher can hide this channel while keeping its task gains.
This paper uses outputs on random carrier prompts as an intended channel for sharing knowledge. It does not try to suppress that channel on the teacher side.

opus.reason: From my searches, prior mitigation work on subliminal learning acts on the student during distillation (KL drift control, probe-space corridors), and the seed paper does not test any defence on the teacher side. I found no paper that regularizes a task-trained teacher's binary decisions on off-task near-tie prompts and compares the result with a uniformly shrunk adapter matched on utility, tested on carrier templates never used for anchoring. KL penalties toward the base model on unrelated prompts are a standard regularization tool. What looks new is using one to cut ATD-style observability and comparing it with matched shrinkage, though the search was limited and may have missed related work.

closest_work.difference: Establishes capability transfer through near-boundary off-task decisions and studies teacher update strength, but does not train teachers to suppress those decisions or compare anchoring with utility-calibrated adapter shrinkage.

Liminal training anchors the distilling student to its base distribution on training completions. The proposed experiment instead anchors the task-trained teacher on separate off-task binary probes and evaluates unseen carrier templates.
Corridor regularization constrains student drift along a calibrated trait direction during distillation, rather than constraining teacher binary decisions without a trait-direction probe.

DOGe already introduces teacher-side anti-distillation training, but adversarially changes task-related reasoning distributions using proxy students. It does not test ancestor-anchored off-task observability against validation-utility-matched update shrinkage.

sol.reason: Teacher-side defenses and base-referenced regularization both precede this proposal, so neither is novel by itself. However, the work found by 2026-10-06 does not answer whether selectively anchoring a teacher's unrelated near-boundary decisions suppresses held-out binary observability better than uniformly shrinking its task update at calibrated utility. That intervention and comparison constitute a distinct question, scoped to channel observability rather than demonstrated prevention of capability extraction.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented the registered experiment end-to-end: frozen public-base probe panels, paired SciQ LoRA teachers for seeds 17/29, the specified 10x Bernoulli KL anchoring, validation-only adapter shrinkage calibration, all held-out readouts, and 10,000 paired crossed bootstrap draws. Model and dataset revisions are locked; all required outputs and result.json are regenerated from scratch. No substantive design changes; unspecified deterministic hashing/sampling and BF16 backbone with float32 restricted readouts are documented. Tested the complete command twice, with identical score and intervals, and independently audited raw outputs. Observed S=-5.80078125 (95% interval [-10.09765625,-1.6015625]); the registered event did not occur. No extraction or general defense guarantee is claimed.

departures: experiment.py runs the backbone in BF16 and computes the restricted pair and letter readouts in float32. The registration does not specify precision. This could shift near-tie decisions slightly, but it applies to every arm, so it is unlikely to change the conclusion.

Base (M0) held-out choices come from the frozen-panel scoring pass, which uses the plain model with batch size 256. Teacher choices are read through the PEFT-wrapped model in evaluate() with batch size 128. Base flips are therefore zero by construction, and kernel or batch-shape noise near q≈0.5 may add spurious flips. This noise affects anchor and shrink roughly equally, so it should cancel in their paired difference but may raise both flip floors.

experiment.py concatenates anchoring prompts and task prompts into one forward pass per update. The README acknowledges that the anchoring KL is not exactly zero at initialisation. This is an implementation choice the registration leaves open and does not plausibly change the result.

Probe nouns u and v are sampled with replacement and may be the same word. Batching is shuffle-without-replacement with cycling, and SHA256/NumPy choices are used for hashing and permutation. All are unspecified choices, documented in manifest.json, with no plausible effect.
Task cross-entropy is taken over the full vocabulary at the answer position, on the single correct-letter token. This is consistent with the registration.

registration.title: Fresh repeated answers versus broader queries at a fixed one-token budget
registration.seed_connection: The seed uses one greedy response per carrier. Its near-tie design does not establish how to spend a fixed observation budget when the interface returns stochastic rather than deterministic choices.
registration.hypothesis: Four fresh stochastic observations per near-boundary prompt can produce more teacher-specific SciQ predictive benefit than four times as many prompts observed once, at equal returned-token and student-update budgets.
registration.contribution: Separates repeated measurements of a conditional response distribution from merely replaying an existing training example. It tests a precision-versus-coverage trade-off in a one-word off-task channel rather than another unconstrained data-volume or temperature sweep.

closest_work.difference: Its fixed-step repeat control duplicates previously generated examples. This experiment spends new teacher observations on repeated prompts and compares them with fresh prompts under an equal observation budget.
Compares greedy and stochastic subliminal generation, but does not establish the fixed-budget trade-off between prompt coverage and independent repeated labels.
Studies interactions between temperature, LoRA rank and trait transfer. Here temperature and adaptation are fixed while query allocation changes.

inputs: Hugging Face Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct; record the resolved revision.
Hugging Face allenai/sciq, training and test splits.
https://github.com/myboker/ATD: data/alphabet.json only for public carrier words.
CUDA PyTorch, Transformers, PEFT, datasets and NumPy from binary packages.

event.description: Repeated measurement yields a positive teacher-specific predictive benefit and exceeds the breadth policy's benefit by more than 0.01 nats per test question.
event.statistic: I_R-max(0,I_B), where I_policy is mean test NLL(public-control student) minus mean test NLL(teacher-observation student), averaged over repetitions.

evaluation.procedure: Compute paired per-question NLL improvements for each allocation policy, then the registered scalar. Report teacher-versus-base improvement and all student accuracies separately so a loss-calibration effect is not mislabeled an accuracy gain. Use a 10000-draw crossed bootstrap over paired repetitions and test questions. Sampling repetitions within a carrier are observations, not independent trained-model replicates. outputs/probes.jsonl contains the frozen panel, margin strata and selected repeated-query IDs; outputs/observations.jsonl contains each hard draw, source model, policy and draw index; outputs/training.jsonl contains teacher/student traces and settings; outputs/test_scores.jsonl contains per-model, per-question letter logits, NLL and correctness; outputs/summary.json contains I_R, I_B, the primary scalar, interval, logical query counts and timings.
evaluation.controls: Public-model sampled-label control for each query policy; equal returned-token counts, training-row counts, optimizer steps and initialization; stratified repeated-prompt selection; fixed temperature; no teacher-dependent filtering or query selection.

registration.full_scale_study: Map the allocation frontier over temperatures, repeat counts, query budgets and model sizes, including unrestricted-vocabulary interfaces with rejection. Determine whether predictive-loss improvements translate into execution-based capability gains.

agent.reason: Broader coverage has stronger supporting evidence, while repeated queries sacrifice distinct gradient directions for better estimates of individual decisions. Repetition could nevertheless help by reducing hard-label overfitting, but its advantage must also exceed a positive predictive-benefit threshold.

judge_astra.reason: At a fixed observation budget, my stronger prior favors broader coverage of the update over more precise measurements at fewer prompts. Repeated labels could reduce overfitting, but the required benefit must exceed both zero and the breadth policy by 0.01 nats.

judge_fable.reason: At equal token budgets, repeated and breadth sampling give the same expected teacher-aligned signal and the same noise to first order, so I_R − max(0,I_B) > 0.01 nats would mostly have to arise from noise in a weak 0.5B/1024-row SciQ NLL endpoint.

judge_opus.reason: With temperature-0.8 sampling on near-ties, only a small fraction of the coupled teacher and public draws differ, so the teacher-specific SciQ NLL benefit for a 0.5B student from 1024 tokens is probably well below 0.01 nats. Repetition has no clear advantage over breadth, which covers more directions.

judge_sol.reason: Repetition reduces label noise per prompt but sacrifices distinct probe directions, without a clear information advantage at fixed observation count. I expect the stochastic one-token channel to produce a weak signal, making a repetition advantage exceeding 0.01 nats relatively unlikely.

judge_luna.reason: Repeated samples could reduce label noise, but they cover only 256 carriers rather than 1024, and the seed does not establish that repeats beat broader coverage. The smaller model and observation budget add uncertainty, while the event requires a >0.01-nat advantage over the better of zero and the breadth policy.

judge_muse.reason: With 1024 tokens, coupled sampling makes teacher/public rows nearly identical and 0.5B transfer is already small, so both NLL benefits will be near zero and breadth's 4x coverage and more sensitive prompts likely match or beat repetition's conflicting soft labels.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented the registered protocol without changing hypothesis, event, controls, budgets, or endpoint. Uses only seed/data/alphabet.json from seed code, freshly trained teachers for seeds 17/29, frozen public-only stratified carriers, fresh temperature-0.8 hard draws coupled to public controls, and identically initialized/budgeted students. Cached pair logits are sampler-only; final-state vocabulary projection computes the registered full-vocabulary CE efficiently. All five raw outputs and result.json are regenerated. Full evaluation command tested successfully (~3 minutes including setup); independent output audit verified strata, observation/training counts, per-question NLLs, pairing, and statistic. Test statistic 0.00272778 nats (95% crossed bootstrap [-0.01003676, 0.00989608]); registered >0.01 event did not occur. This is not an equivalence conclusion. No protocol changes.

departures: experiment.py `panel`: base pair logits are read in bfloat16, so many carriers have exactly tied logits (q=0.5, margin 0, e.g. 17.0/17.0 in probes.jsonl). The ordering into the 512 lowest-margin carriers and the eight 'public-margin' strata therefore falls back to carrier-ID tie-breaking for a large share of the panel, and several low strata are indistinguishable in margin. The registration leaves precision open. This weakens the stratification but is unlikely to have changed the reported value materially.

experiment.py: prompts are fed as raw text without the Qwen chat template, for both SciQ and carriers. The registration gives the literal prompt strings and does not require a chat template, so this is a permitted choice and does not change the result relative to the registration.

experiment.py `fresh_adapter_state`/`reset_adapter`: each repetition's teacher starts from the same LoRA initialization as its four students. The registration only requires the four students to share an initialization. Teacher-student shared initialization is unspecified; it applies equally to the teacher-label and public-label arms. Allowed choice, though it could affect absolute transfer size.

experiment.py: choices the registration leaves open, all disclosed in README.md: SHA256 for question/prompt hashes, NumPy default_rng permutations, RNG 4102 for repeated-panel selection, rep-derived RNG streams for draws and data order, AdamW betas/eps, TF32 matmuls. None plausibly changes the result.

experiment.py `bootstrap`: the crossed bootstrap resamples the 2 repetitions with replacement (only three distinct repetition combinations) and the 1000 questions. This matches the registered procedure but makes the interval crude. It does not change the point statistic.

No departure was found in data, model revision, sample sizes, temperature, budgets, optimizer settings, loss, controls, test split, statistic or event rule. The evaluation reproduced the engineer's submitted log numbers exactly.

The registered comparison is between two near-null channels, so it says little about precision versus coverage.
