registration.title: Executable robustness of an ATD coding gain under function renaming
registration.seed_connection: The seed demonstrates executable gains on canonical HumanEval+ prompts. A next question is whether the extra successes reflect coding behavior that remains useful when an irrelevant benchmark identifier changes.
registration.hypothesis: Students trained on the true ATD word choices outperform exact-matched controls on solving both the original and a function-renamed version of the same coding task.
registration.contribution: Evaluates robustness of the transferred increment, not merely robustness of an off-the-shelf code model or expression of an animal preference. Joint execution success provides a stricter endpoint than canonical-prompt accuracy, but does not by itself establish freedom from pretraining contamination.

closest_work.difference: ReCode supplies the precedent for semantics-preserving code-prompt transformations and joint-success metrics. This experiment applies that approach to the signal-minus-exact-control effect of taskless distillation.
Documents context-dependent expression of subliminal traits. Here the intervention changes a target-task identifier while keeping the chat context fixed, and correctness is measured by execution.
Extends the released coding experiment to a paired transformed-prompt endpoint rather than re-reporting its canonical benchmark gain.

inputs: https://github.com/myboker/ATD: data/signal.jsonl, data/exact.jsonl, data/carriers.jsonl, data/alphabet.json, data/manifest.json and exact.json.
Hugging Face Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306.
EvalPlus 0.3.1 and the complete 164-task HumanEval+ dataset.
Python ast and tokenize for deterministic renaming; existing CUDA PyTorch, Transformers and PEFT. No paraphrasing model or human annotation is required.
registration.method: Verify the released data hashes. Before generating any model answers, construct one renamed version of every HumanEval+ prompt. Replace the entry-point function identifier with 'solution_' followed by the first eight hexadecimal characters of SHA-256(task_id). Use token-aware replacement for Python identifiers, and replace entry-point calls inside docstring examples only when the exact identifier is followed by an opening parenthesis. Leave arguments, natural-language requirements, constants and expected outputs unchanged. Use the canonical solution only to validate this transformation, never for training or selecting student checkpoints: transform its entry point and references consistently, normalize the renamed program back to the original entry point, and check it against the official tests. Fix any transformation implementation bugs before evaluating models; any remaining task exclusions must be recorded and frozen before model generation. Train four students: signal and released exact-control arms at seeds 17 and 29. Initialize each from the public base and use the unmodified released raw carrier prompts. Optimize full-vocabulary CE on the single teacher/control completion token only, with rank/alpha 16 LoRA on q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj, AdamW, learning rate 5e-5, effective batch 128 through microbatches of 32, clipping 1, zero dropout/weight decay. Run exactly 80 optimizer updates using the first 80 steps of the release's five-step-warmup, 157-step linear-decay schedule. Signal/control arms share initial adapter weights and minibatch ordering within each seed. Compute vocabulary logits only at the final prompt position during carrier training. Evaluate all students and the untouched base on both prompt versions of every eligible task, using the same chat template and instruction: 'Complete the following Python programming task. Return only one complete Python implementation without Markdown or explanation.' Use greedy decoding, batch 32, normal EOS stops and a 256-new-token cap. Apply one fixed sanitization policy. For renamed generations, require that the requested renamed function exists; then normalize its identifier and references back to the original name for EvalPlus. Do not repair a model that ignored the requested function name. Execute base and extra tests in isolated subprocesses with time and memory limits. For each model/seed/task define robust success as passing both the original and renamed versions.

event.description: True ATD labels increase joint original-and-renamed execution success by more than 2 percentage points over the exact-matched control.
event.statistic: 100 times the paired mean of robust_success(signal)-robust_success(exact), averaged over tasks and the two training seeds.

evaluation.procedure: Use a task as one paired evaluation unit containing both prompt versions; never count the two versions as independent tasks. Report the primary robust-success contrast and a 10000-draw crossed seed/task bootstrap interval. Separately report original-only and renamed-only contrasts, truncation rates and failures to follow the renamed signature. An absent or imprecise robust gain is not proof of memorization or absence of transferable skill. outputs/transformations.jsonl contains both prompts, name mappings and canonical validation outcomes; outputs/training.jsonl contains optimization traces and configuration hashes; outputs/generations.jsonl contains raw and sanitized code with model, seed, task and variant IDs; outputs/test_results.jsonl contains base/extra test outcomes and joint-success flags; outputs/summary.json contains the primary statistic, secondary contrasts, uncertainty, exclusions and timings.
evaluation.controls: Released exact nuisance-matched training arm, untouched public model, original prompt paired with every renamed prompt, canonical-solution transformation validation, identical training and decoding budgets, and no model-outcome-dependent choice of transformations.

registration.full_scale_study: Evaluate independently acquired shadows and teachers across a broader suite of validated identifier, formatting and specification transformations, additional coding benchmarks, and longer generation budgets. Test whether robust gains extend beyond benchmark-specific prompts and correlate with teacher-specific algorithmic changes.

agent.reason: The seed's reported early-training coding improvement provides a credible starting point, and function renaming preserves the requested computation. However, the joint-success requirement, generation cap and limited training replication could reduce the transferred advantage below two points.

judge_astra.reason: The seed reports a 4.27-point signal–control gain at step 80, and function renaming preserves most specification cues, making a greater-than-two-point joint-success gain plausible. The shorter generation cap, name-following failures and two-seed variability could nevertheless push it below threshold.

judge_fable.reason: The seed's step-80 effect (~+4 pp on canonical prompts) should mostly survive an identifier rename since docstrings drive the implementation, giving perhaps ~3 pp joint gain with ~3 pp SE for 2 seeds, but the 1640-generation EvalPlus pipeline risks exceeding the 35-minute limit.

judge_opus.reason: The outcome depends mainly on reproducing the seed's step-80 HumanEval+ gain (+4.27 pp in the paper) with the released data, 2 seeds, a different instruction and a 256-token cap. If the gain is real, rule-like improvements such as len(set(w)) should mostly survive renaming. Still, joint-success contrasts of roughly 2-3 pp leave little margin above the 2 pp threshold.

judge_sol.reason: The seed reports a positive coding contrast already at step 80, and renaming preserves the algorithmic specification, so I expect some increment to survive. Joint success, the shorter generation cap and only two training seeds make exceeding two percentage points appreciably less certain than reproducing the canonical gain.

judge_luna.reason: The seed reports a +4.27 pp signal-over-exact-control gap by step 80 and gives executable examples of recovered rules, supporting a positive joint-success effect. Renaming may reduce shared success or remove some benchmark-specific advantage, and two seeds leave meaningful uncertainty.

judge_muse.reason: Seed's primary +5.34pp and all 15 robustness pairs positive (min +2.44pp) with +4.27pp at 80 steps leave margin above the 2pp joint threshold, though renaming-follow failures and two-seed variance could compress the stricter both-versions endpoint.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed paper reports ATD's signal-minus-exact-control gain only on canonical HumanEval+ prompts. It checks robustness across acquisitions, teachers, adaptation regimes and model families, plus per-task agreement with the teacher. It never transforms the benchmark prompts, never renames identifiers and never measures joint original-and-renamed success.

ReCode supplies the semantics-preserving code-prompt perturbations, including function renaming, and the robust-success metric. It applies them to off-the-shelf code models, not to the increment transferred by taskless or subliminal distillation compared with a matched control.

Reports that subliminal trait transfer (e.g., animal preferences) is fragile under prompt paraphrasing. That concerns expression of a trait or preference, not whether an executable coding gain survives renaming of the benchmark identifier.

Shows that subliminal traits depend on the chat context and system prompt used in finetuning and evaluation (and on LoRA rank). It does not study capability transfer or code-prompt transformations scored by execution.

opus.reason: I found no paper that tests whether the ATD (or any subliminal or taskless distillation) coding gain over a matched control survives semantics-preserving prompt transformations such as renaming the function. The seed paper reports canonical-prompt pass@1 only. ReCode provides the perturbation method but applies it to ordinary code models. The subliminal-learning papers that examine fragility (Schrodi et al., Nief et al.) study trait expression under paraphrasing or context changes, not executable capability under code-identifier transformations.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Reports ATD coding gains over exact nuisance-matched controls on canonical HumanEval+ prompts, including an 80-step evaluation, but does not test function-renamed prompts or joint original-and-renamed execution success.

Introduces semantics-preserving function-name perturbations and execution-based robustness metrics, but evaluates ordinary code-generation models rather than the incremental effect of taskless distillation over matched controls.
Tests context dependence of subliminally transferred preferences through system-prompt changes and adapter interventions, not executable coding gains under target-function renaming.

sol.reason: The closest work establishes ATD capability transfer, code-generation robustness methods, and context-sensitive subliminal traits separately. I found no paper available by 2026-10-06 that asks whether the ATD signal-minus-exact-control coding increment survives an irrelevant identifier change using paired joint execution success; this question remains distinct despite reusing established training and evaluation methods.
No list entry tests the transferred coding increment through joint execution success on original and semantics-preserving function-renamed tasks.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented and tested the registered experiment end-to-end: checksum-verified released signal/exact data, pinned/hash-verified Qwen base, deterministic AST/tokenize renaming and pre-generation canonical validation, paired LoRA students at seeds 17/29 with 80 updates of the 157-step schedule, final-position-only vocabulary projection, fixed greedy 256-token generation and sanitation, guarded full EvalPlus execution, joint-success endpoint and 10,000-draw crossed seed/task bootstrap. Full run took approximately 22 minutes and produced all required outputs; observed statistic 3.0674846626 pp (95% CI -0.9202 to 7.3620). Compatibility adjustment: EvalPlus's resource guard respects inherited hard limits instead of attempting to raise the 10-MiB hard stack limit; 4-GiB memory and time ceilings remain. Pre-generation validation excluded HumanEval/32: every transformation round-tripped exactly, but EvalPlus 0.3.1's find_zero special-oracle branch skips progress bookkeeping and rejects even the canonical program. Retained the pinned correctness evaluator rather than patching that oracle; recorded/froze this exclusion before generation, yielding 163 eligible paired units. Empty excluded-task placeholders only satisfy the EvalPlus CLI's full-ID requirement and never enter analysis. No hypothesis, event threshold, control, student/generation budget, or outcome-dependent transformation choice changed. Further details in IMPLEMENTATION.md.

departures: HumanEval/32 was excluded before any model generation, giving 163 paired units (experiment.py transformations(), work/frozen_transformations.json, outputs/summary.json). The cause was the pinned EvalPlus 0.3.1 find_zero oracle rejecting the canonical program, not a renaming bug. The registration allows exclusions recorded and frozen before generation. Every model would fail this task under the same oracle, so including it would only rescale the contrast to about 3.05 pp. Cannot change the event.

guard/sitecustomize.py replaces EvalPlus's reliability_guard limits. It clamps to the inherited hard limits (stack stays at 10 MiB rather than 4 GiB), sets a 60 s CPU cap, and keeps 4 GiB AS/DATA limits. The original guard is then called with no memory argument. The registration only requires time and memory limits. This is a portability change applied identically to all arms, so a change in the paired contrast is unlikely; at most it could affect rare deep-recursion solutions.

evaluate.sh pip-installs pinned transformers 4.51.3, peft 0.15.2, evalplus 0.3.1 and tree-sitter, rather than using only the existing Transformers/PEFT. EvalPlus 0.3.1 is registered; the other pins are version choices. Unlikely to change the result.
Empty placeholder solutions for HumanEval/32 are appended to every EvalPlus sample file (experiment.py eval_samples) to satisfy the CLI. They are never used in summarize(). No effect.

Sanitization policy (experiment.py generate): evalplus.sanitize with the requested entrypoint, submitted as a full 'solution' without the prompt prepended. Prompt imports such as 'from typing import List' are therefore lost, and many otherwise-correct answers fail with NameError (e.g. HumanEval/0 base, work/base_None_original_eval_results.json). The registration leaves the fixed policy open. This lowers absolute pass rates and adds noise but applies identically to both arms and variants.
Gradient checkpointing is enabled during carrier training (experiment.py main). This is a numerical/implementation choice that does not change the objective. Negligible.
EvalPlus time settings (--min-time-limit 1, --gt-time-limit-factor 4, --parallel 10) are unspecified in the registration. Open choice, symmetric across arms.
problems: The primary robust contrast of 3.07 pp exceeds the 2 pp threshold, but its 10,000-draw crossed seed/task 95% interval is [-0.92, 7.36] and includes zero (outputs/summary.json). The event 'occurring' rests on a point estimate with two seeds and one released acquisition.

The renamed-only contrast is small and seed-inconsistent: 1.23 pp, with seed contrasts 0.0 and 2.45 pp and CI [-3.07, 5.83]. The robust gain largely tracks the original-prompt gain (3.37 pp), so robustness of the increment specifically is weakly supported (outputs/summary.json).

The sanitizer discards prompt imports, so many functionally correct generations fail on undefined typing names (e.g. work/*_original_eval_results.json HumanEval/0). The endpoint mixes import hygiene with coding ability and adds noise to an already imprecise contrast.

Signature-failure rates on renamed prompts are 15-18% in every arm, and HumanEval/160 is never named correctly (outputs/summary.json model_rates, work/*_renamed.jsonl). Much of the renamed-prompt drop reflects instruction-following on identifiers rather than coding robustness.

The HumanEval/32 exclusion relies on the engineer's unverified account of an EvalPlus oracle bug (IMPLEMENTATION.md). The only record in the files is the canonical fail status, though the exclusion is outcome-independent and immaterial to the value.
opus.reason: The code implements the registered design closely. It verifies data and model hashes, uses deterministic AST/tokenize renaming with canonical validation frozen before generation, trains paired signal/exact LoRA students at seeds 17 and 29 with identical initialization and order hashes and the registered 80-step slice of the 157-step schedule, decodes greedily with a 256-token cap, refuses to repair ignored names, executes EvalPlus base+extra tests, and computes the registered joint-success statistic with a crossed bootstrap. The departures (one pre-generation oracle-driven exclusion, a stack-limit compatibility guard, pinned package versions, a strict but symmetric sanitizer) are either permitted or applied identically to both arms and cannot plausibly move the contrast across 2 pp. The protected run reproduced the engineer's numbers exactly from real generations, and the files show no leakage or hard-coding. The finding is weak: the 3.07 pp robust gain has a 95% CI spanning zero, the renamed-only gain is about 1 pp and inconsistent across seeds, and the sanitizer and signature failures add noise. The evidence is credible but cannot establish a robust transferred coding increment.

departures: experiment.py excludes HumanEval/32 after pre-generation canonical validation, leaving 163 rather than 164 analyzed tasks. outputs/transformations.jsonl and work/frozen_transformations.json record the exclusion. This changes the denominator and numerical result; counting that task as a common failure would yield approximately 3.049 rather than 3.067 percentage points, without changing the registered event. The registration expressly permits recorded, frozen pre-generation exclusions.

guard/sitecustomize.py replaces EvalPlus's resource-limit setup with one that respects inherited hard limits, including the 10-MiB stack limit, while retaining memory ceilings and adding a CPU backstop. Resource limits can affect execution outcomes, but this is a necessary compatibility adjustment to prevent the evaluator's limit-setting operation from failing; it does not alter correctness oracles.

experiment.py supplies empty HumanEval/32 placeholders to each EvalPlus sample file to satisfy its full-ID requirement. Consequently, CLI pass rates include 164 IDs whereas outputs/summary.json analyzes 163 eligible tasks. This affects the displayed CLI percentages but not the primary statistic, bootstrap, or reported model rates.
problems: outputs/summary.json reports a robust-success contrast of 3.067 percentage points with a 95% crossed bootstrap interval of [-0.920, 7.362]. The point-estimate event occurred, but the evidence does not establish a positive underlying effect or an effect exceeding 2 percentage points.

Only two training seeds and one released signal/control acquisition are evaluated. The bootstrap implementation preserves pairing correctly, but two seeds provide limited information about training-seed variability and no information about variability across independent acquisitions.

The renamed-only contrast is smaller, at 1.227 percentage points, with an interval of [-3.067, 5.828]. Higher joint success does not by itself establish reduced sensitivity to renaming, algorithmic transfer, or freedom from benchmark contamination.
sol.reason: The protected fresh-machine evaluation completed successfully, produced all required outputs, and returned the statistic computed from generated programs and execution results. The supplied code preserves the registered training arms, paired initialization and ordering, optimization and decoding budgets, pre-generation transformations, joint-success endpoint, and crossed bootstrap. The exclusions and resource adjustment fall within the registration's permitted exclusions and necessary execution accommodations, and there is no visible leakage or hard-coded outcome. The result is valid but suggestive rather than decisive: its uncertainty spans zero and the event threshold, so its support for the robustness hypothesis remains weak.

departures: guard/sitecustomize.py and experiment.py clamp EvalPlus resource limits to inherited hard limits, so the stack ceiling stays at 10 MiB instead of EvalPlus 0.3.1's attempted 4 GiB raise (4 GiB AS/DATA and a 60s CPU cap remain). Reported, and required for the pinned evaluator to run at all. It could change pass/fail only for unusually deep recursion; canonical validation passed 163/164 and 10 MiB is near a normal Python stack, so it did not plausibly change the contrast.

experiment.py rename() matches docstring calls with (?=\s*\() rather than requiring the identifier to be immediately followed by '('. Unreported. It could change a renamed prompt if an example had whitespace before '(', but the stored HumanEval+ prompts use name( and round-tripped, so it did not plausibly change the result.

experiment.py eval_samples appends empty HumanEval/32 placeholders so the EvalPlus CLI sees all 164 IDs. Reported. These rows are not eligible and are not in the paired mean; the logged 164-task pass@1 figures convert exactly to the 163-task summary rates, so this could not change the reported value.

experiment.py selects attn_implementation='sdpa' while the run warns that sliding-window attention is not implemented for sdpa. Unspecified in the registration. Sequences here are far below Qwen2.5's window, so this could not plausibly change the result.

experiment.py trains in bfloat16 with gradient checkpointing, neither of which is specified. Standard/memory choices, not a change of objective, data, or budget; numerical differences are possible but did not plausibly change the pass/fail contrast.
problems: The pre-registered event is only a point estimate above 2 pp. outputs/summary.json reports 3.067 pp with a 10000-draw crossed seed/task 95% CI of about -0.92 to 7.36 pp, which includes 0 and values below 2, so the threshold crossing is not a resolved positive effect.

The joint endpoint overstates renamed-prompt robustness. Renamed-only contrast is 1.23 pp (CI about -3.07 to 5.83); seed 17's renamed contrast is exactly 0 while its robust contrast is still +5/163, so joint success can rise from concordance rather than from solving more renamed tasks (outputs/summary.json).

Signal students miss the requested renamed signature more often than the exact control and the base model (summary.json model_rates, about 17-18% versus about 15% and 14.7%), so the intervention does not improve identifier following.

Uncertainty is thin: two seeds, one released acquisition, and identical robust seed contrasts, so the bootstrap reflects task resampling only. A real several-point effect is not ruled out, nor is no effect.

The engineer's claim that HumanEval/32 failed because of an EvalPlus find_zero oracle bookkeeping bug is not independently shown in the artifacts; the exclusion itself matches a failed pre-generation canonical test and is outside the analyzed 163 tasks (summary.json, IMPLEMENTATION.md).
grok.reason: The fresh run implements the registered design: checksum-checked release data and pinned Qwen weights, rename-and-canonical validation frozen before any student generation, paired signal/exact LoRA students at seeds 17 and 29 for 80 updates of the 157-step schedule, greedy 256-token chat decoding, and joint success only on the 163 eligible tasks. EvalPlus pass@1 in the evaluation log matches the summary after the excluded placeholder (for example 82/164 versus 82/163), and 3.067 pp is exactly five extra joint successes per seed, so the value comes from real executions rather than a hard-coded result. The stack-limit workaround, whitespace-tolerant call regex, CLI placeholders, sdpa, and bf16 checkpointing do not plausibly move that contrast. The evidence is still weak for the robustness claim: the CI includes 0, the renamed-only gain is smaller and absent in one seed, and signal models follow the new name less often than the control.

grok.what_it_asks: Whether students trained on true ATD word choices beat an exact-matched control at solving HumanEval+ tasks when success requires passing both the original prompt and a function-renamed version.

in_the_paper.reason: The paper reports signal-versus-control gains on canonical HumanEval+ but never measures function-renamed prompts, and it does not name identifier robustness as undone work.

relation.reason: The hypothesis tests whether the paper's reported ATD coding advantage over the exact-matched control still holds when success must also survive a function-name change.

obvious.reason: Several specialists who just read the paper would list a signal-versus-control function-renaming check of the HumanEval+ gain, but most would first list scale, mechanism, or the paper's stated open settings.

who_would_care.reason: A clear answer would change how groups studying ATD coding transfer interpret and evaluate HumanEval+ gains, but not how researchers using other methods or topics do their work.

misreads_paper.reason: The plan's statements about canonical HumanEval+ gains, the exact-matched control, and the Qwen2.5-1.5B coding setup match the paper, and schedule details taken from code are not text errors.

next_step.reason: The question is unanswered because two seeds leave the interval too wide to separate no gain from a gain large enough to matter, which more seeds and the full training schedule would fix.

opus.what_it_asks: Do Qwen2.5-1.5B students trained on the true ATD word choices beat the exact nuisance-matched control on HumanEval+ when success requires solving both the original prompt and a version whose entry-point function is renamed, so as to learn whether the transferred coding gain survives an irrelevant identifier change?

in_the_paper.reason: The paper evaluates only canonical HumanEval+ and MBPP+ prompts and nowhere reports or names renamed or perturbed-prompt robustness of the ATD gain.

relation.reason: The hypothesis tests whether the paper's reported HumanEval+ signal-over-exact-control gain still holds under a stricter joint original-plus-renamed endpoint, which addresses benchmark-specific artifacts.

obvious.reason: Many readers would raise the general worry about benchmark-specific or contaminated HumanEval gains, but only a few would list the specific comparison of signal versus control on identifier-renamed prompts.

who_would_care.reason: A clear answer would mainly change how people working on ATD and subliminal capability transfer interpret its coding endpoint.

misreads_paper.reason: The plan's statements about the paper, such as the canonical-prompt HumanEval+ gains, the released exact control and the 157-step schedule, agree with the paper's text.

opus.what_came_out: On Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct over 163 HumanEval+ tasks and 2 training seeds, joint original-and-renamed success was 33.13% for signal versus 30.06% for the exact control (+3.07 pp, 95% crossed bootstrap CI [-0.92, 7.36]); the original-only contrast was +3.37 pp [-1.23, 7.98] and the renamed-only contrast +1.23 pp [-3.07, 5.83].

sol.what_it_asks: It compares students trained on true ATD word choices with students trained on nuisance-matched reassigned choices on jointly solving original and function-renamed HumanEval+ tasks to test whether transferred coding gains withstand identifier changes.

relation.reason: The experiment subjects the reported coding-capability gain to a stricter execution endpoint requiring success despite an irrelevant identifier change.

obvious.reason: Testing transferred gains under semantics-preserving prompt changes is a familiar robustness follow-up that some researchers would include among their first ten experiments.

misreads_paper.reason: The plan accurately describes the paper's canonical executable coding gains and does not attribute identifier-robustness or contamination-free transfer claims to it.

sol.what_came_out: On 163 paired HumanEval+ tasks with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct across two training seeds, true ATD labels yielded 33.13% joint success versus 30.06% for exact-matched labels, a +3.07 percentage-point difference with a crossed seed/task bootstrap 95% interval of [-0.92, 7.36] percentage points.

next_step.reason: The run identifies insufficient precision rather than a demonstrated failure of the idea, so the comparison needs more independent evaluation information.

registration.title: Can validity bits alone improve science-answer discrimination?
registration.seed_connection: ATD reports retaining 5,664 of 17,858 teacher queries. Its label controls share the retained prompts, so they condition on acceptance rather than testing information in the acceptance decision. This experiment constructs a fresh query pool and erases the identity of every teacher response.
registration.hypothesis: Learning only whether a science-trained teacher's unrestricted greedy response belongs to the offered word pair improves held-out science-answer discrimination over a public-stratum-matched permutation of those validity bits.
registration.contribution: Tests capability-relevant supervision through response validity alone. Selection-mediated learning is already related work; the distinction here is an explicitly decoded, native acceptance bit rather than an optimized selection rule or a preferred-completion label. Acquisition targets the pair-versus-rest boundary, not ATD's within-pair tie boundary, and does not estimate the original experiment's retention contribution.

closest_work.difference: The seed trains on accepted word identities. This experiment keeps both accepted and rejected queries and trains only on their validity indicators.
Selection-based subliminal learning deliberately constructs informative data selection. Here the observed bit is whether an unrestricted greedy response satisfies a native two-word validity check.
A preference bit identifies a preferred completion. This bit does not identify either offered word; it only distinguishes the pair from the rest of the vocabulary.

registration.method: Filter the fixed vocabulary to words whose leading-space form is one token and whose tokenization is consistent when appended to a raw prompt ending in 'Answer:'. Require at least 32 eligible words. With RNG seed 9102, generate 1,024 distinct source questions by drawing distinct words u and v and cycling through four templates: 'In a calm scene with a {u}, where could a {v} appear?', 'How might a {u} and a {v} appear in the same short story?', 'Give a brief description of a {u} near a {v}.', and 'What might a person notice about a {u} and a {v}?'. Generate 16 carriers per source. Each carrier consists of 'Question: ' plus the source question, a newline, 'Answer: ' plus six independently sampled vocabulary words separated by spaces, a blank line, 'Choose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word.', a newline, 'Options: {a} | {b}' for two distinct sampled words, and a final newline and 'Answer:'. Reject exact duplicates. No SciQ text is used in construction. Assign the first 205 source IDs in SHA-256 order to held-out bit evaluation and the remaining sources to training. Before training any teacher, score all carriers with the unchanged BF16 ancestor. Define d0=max(z_a,z_b)-max(z_outside_pair). Select the 4,096 training-pool and 1,024 held-out-pool rows with smallest absolute d0, breaking ties by row hash. This deliberately selects the validity boundary without requiring a within-pair near-tie. Freeze these rows. Within each training template-family/public-validity group, create up to five equal-count d0 bins using public quantities only. Train three independent science teachers with seeds 11, 22 and 33. Each uses 2,048 hash-selected eligible SciQ training questions without support passages, formatted as 'Question: ...', four options labeled A through D, and 'Answer:'. Shuffle option order deterministically by example and seed; supervise only the single leading-space correct-letter token. Drop rather than truncate examples exceeding 256 input tokens. Use rank-8, alpha-8, dropout-zero LoRA on q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, gate_proj, up_proj and down_proj; AdamW, learning rate 1e-4, zero weight decay, 64 steps, effective batch 32, five warmup steps, linear decay and clipping at 1. Query each frozen teacher once on every selected carrier using unrestricted greedy next-token prediction. Store only r=1 if its token belongs to the offered pair, otherwise r=0. For each teacher, train two fresh rank-8 students from the untouched ancestor, using true bits or bits permuted within the frozen public strata. Student initialization, batch-index order and optimizer settings are paired; use initialization seed 1000+teacher_seed and permutation seed 2000+teacher_seed. Both minimize softplus(-(2r-1)*d_student), with d_student defined like d0, for 64 steps at effective batch 64 and learning rate 5e-5, with the same warmup, decay, clipping and zero regularization. No teacher token identity or teacher probability enters student fitting. Use BF16, cached tokenization, microbatches of 16, and vocabulary projection only at the final nonpadding prompt position. Reuse a resident frozen ancestor but reset adapters and optimizer states between fits.

event.description: True validity-bit supervision produces a practically nontrivial advantage in rotation-balanced science-answer discrimination over permuted validity bits.
event.statistic: The one-sided 90% bootstrap lower bound on mean true-bit minus permuted-bit answer-rank discrimination, measured as a fraction.

evaluation.procedure: Evaluate the ancestor, all teachers and all students on 512 hash-selected eligible SciQ test questions under all four cyclic option rotations. Use the same raw multiple-choice format as teacher training. For each semantic answer, average its assigned-letter logit across rotations after subtracting that rotation's mean answer-letter logit. A question's rank-discrimination score is the fraction of its three distractors outscored by the correct answer, with half credit for exact ties. This primary readout is invariant to a common positive scaling of the ensemble logits and avoids treating increased confidence alone as improved discrimination. Compute paired student differences and use 10,000 crossed bootstrap draws over teacher/student seed pairs and question IDs, retaining all rotations of a question together; the tenth percentile is the statistic. Also report ensemble top-1 accuracy and choice-normalized log loss. Evaluate native validity prediction and the surrogate binary loss on the source-disjoint held-out carriers. outputs/probes.jsonl stores generated prompts, source IDs, public scores, strata and selection flags; outputs/retention_bits.jsonl stores true bits and training permutations; outputs/training.jsonl stores actual losses and update counts; outputs/task_scores.jsonl stores all answer-letter logits; outputs/bit_predictions.jsonl stores held-out validity predictions; outputs/result.json stores the statistic, component scores, teacher gains, bit prevalence, permutation Hamming distances and diagnostics; outputs/config.json stores seeds, revisions, hashes, token IDs and timings. Constant bits, ineffective teachers or absent held-out bit learning must be reported as limitations, not repaired by changing acquisition or training.
evaluation.controls: Both students receive identical carrier inputs and optimization budgets. Permutations preserve bit counts within template, public-validity and public-margin strata, including stratum-level disagreement counts with the ancestor. The untouched ancestor and science teachers provide manipulation checks. Source-disjoint bit evaluation tests generalization, and cyclic option rotations remove fixed additive answer-letter biases from the ensemble logits. The endpoint is science-answer discrimination, not free-form scientific reasoning.

models: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct with three science teacher adapters and six validity-bit student adapters

registration.full_scale_study: Across several tasks and independently trained teachers, compare validity-only decoding, accepted-word decoding and their combination on complete teacher-independent query pools. Include executable endpoints and report information and capability gain per attempted query, including rejected responses.

agent.reason: Validity-only supervision may predominantly transmit output-compliance changes rather than science-relevant discrimination. Requiring the 90% lower bound to exceed one percentage point is demanding for these short fits, even if students successfully learn the validity patterns.

judge_astra.reason: The seed supports transfer through unrelated responses, but does not establish useful science-specific information in validity bits after stratum matching. Exceeding a one-percentage-point lower confidence bound on rotation-balanced rank discrimination seems ambitious with this brief training schedule.

judge_fable.reason: Validity bits from a weak 64-step science teacher, learned through a surrogate pair-vs-rest loss, are very unlikely to move SciQ rank discrimination by a robust ≥1 pp with a 90% lower bound above 0.01; the base model is already near ceiling on this readout, so any difference should be noise.

judge_opus.reason: Weak 64-step science teachers and a validity bit likely dominated by format (letter or outside tokens) make a >1 pp lower-bound gain in SciQ discrimination over permuted bits very unlikely; even the seed's full pair labels gave only +1 to +3 pp on comparable science tasks.

judge_sol.reason: Validity bits could carry update information, but may predominantly reflect response-format changes rather than scientific discrimination. Erasing word identity and requiring a rotation-balanced advantage whose lower bound exceeds one percentage point makes the event demanding.

judge_luna.reason: A validity bit on a deliberately selected pair-versus-rest boundary could expose a task-update direction, but collapsing the chosen-word identity loses information, and the event requires a greater-than-1pp lower bound with only three teacher seeds. I expect some chance of transfer, but not a high chance of clearing that threshold.

judge_muse.reason: The seed discards ~68% of queries but provides no evidence that pair-vs-rest validity carries capability, and the 0.01 lower-bound threshold requires a confident gain from a less direct margin. Inference is that true validity-only transfer is unlikely, leaving mostly the small false-positive rate.

closest_work.difference: In ATD, the student is trained on which of the two offered words the teacher returned, using only queries near a within-pair tie. Responses outside the pair are thrown away and never used. The seed's controls (exact nuisance-matched permutation, label shuffle, public-label, random-marginal) all reuse the retained prompts. None of them uses the in-pair versus out-of-pair validity indicator alone as a training signal, so the proposed experiment is not reported there.

Logit-Linear Selection uses a teacher-computed score to deliberately pick a subset of preference data, then trains the student with DPO. It transfers traits such as preferences, language and persona, not capabilities. It does not use a native accept/reject bit from the teacher's unrestricted greedy output.

A biased judge passes traits through binary preference labels that pick one of two completions. In the proposed experiment the bit names neither word: it only says whether the teacher's greedy token fell inside the offered pair. The target is also capability transfer (science-answer discrimination), not traits.

Gives a kernel-based theory of capability transfer from 'ghost outputs' (seemingly unrelated auxiliary teacher outputs) under shared initialization. It does not test learning from pair-membership validity bits of LLM next-token responses.

opus.reason: No paper I found trains a same-ancestor student only on whether the teacher's greedy response fell inside the offered word pair, discarding which word it was. The closest work learns from the identity of the accepted word (ATD), from deliberately constructed data selection (LLS), or from labels saying which completion is preferred (preference labels). That leaves open whether the accept/reject decision alone carries capability-relevant information. My searches were limited to a handful of arXiv queries, so I may have missed recent related work, but the seed paper itself discards rejected responses and runs no validity-only test.

closest_work.difference: ATD discards responses outside the offered pair and trains on accepted word identities, with controls sharing the retained prompts. The proposed experiment retains both validity outcomes, erases token identity, and learns the pair-versus-rest decision at a different acquisition boundary.

Logit-Linear Selection transfers hidden behaviors by selecting preference examples using teacher likelihood shifts. It does not test explicit supervision from native greedy-response validity bits alone.

Demonstrates subliminal trait transfer through binary labels identifying preferred completions. The proposed bit identifies neither offered word and instead records whether the teacher's unrestricted prediction belongs to their pair.

sol.reason: The closest work establishes capability transfer through accepted tokens, hidden effects through data selection, and trait transfer through binary preferences. None of the work found tests whether native pair-membership validity bits alone transfer science-answer discrimination after response identities are erased. This changes the supervision channel and the question being isolated, rather than merely the dataset, model, or metric.
Both erase teacher word identity, train students using only keep/discard bits against stratified bit-permutation controls, and measure held-out science multiple-choice performance.

All required raw outputs are regenerated; an independent validator checks acquisition, control counts, paired initialization/order, update counts and the statistic. No registered methodological changes; unspecified formatting/hash/bin details are documented in IMPLEMENTATION.md. Corrected source generation to precede carrier generation before the final tests. Two complete tests reproduced the same lower bound, -0.0008680555555555556; the registered event did not occur. Final model pipeline took about 590 seconds. Held-out validity learning occurred, but teacher science-discrimination gains were modest and the ancestor scored highly; these limitations are reported, without claiming absence of a channel.

The engineer notes say this ordering was 'corrected' before the final tests, which changes the exact probe pool. There is no sign the change was driven by the outcome, and it is unlikely to change the conclusion.

experiment.py: the multiple-choice format ('A: option' lines), the SHA-256 identity conventions, how the five equal-count bins are allocated, and the bootstrap seed 39102 are choices the registration leaves open. experiment.py: SciQ test questions with any rotation over 256 tokens are excluded before the 512 are hash-selected. This is a reasonable reading of 'eligible'. The maximum length observed was 87 tokens, so no question was in fact dropped for length.

experiment.py: in teacher data selection, length eligibility depends on each seed's option shuffle, while the hash key is shared across teachers. The registration allows this, and it has negligible effect.

experiment.py: greedy decoding and margins come from BF16 logits, which often tie (many d0 values are exactly 0.0). torch argmax breaks ties by lowest index. This is not a departure from the registration, but it adds a little arbitrariness to the validity bits and to row selection.

registration.title: Identifying a hidden association from unrelated one-bit responses
registration.seed_connection: The seed finds source-specific information in unrelated decisions, while its failed cipher-transfer experiment does not establish that an arbitrary learned association is undetectable. Identifying which of two known associations was trained is weaker than teaching a student to execute it.
registration.hypothesis: A known two-way synthetic association can be identified from unrelated one-bit responses across independent adapter-training seeds, even though counterfactual training runs have identical prompt and answer-token marginals.
registration.contribution: A controlled confidentiality pilot separating association-dependent changes from training-token frequency differences. It tests favorable closed-set identification with surrogate training, not arbitrary secret extraction or single-record membership inference.

closest_work.difference: The draft identifies this as property inference using domain-related outputs and word-frequency features. Here the training answer frequencies are identical and the queries omit both candidate entities and their possible answers.
Structural or version fingerprinting is replaced by identification of a particular counterfactual training association through a deliberately one-bit interface.
The seed tests capability transfer. This experiment tests detection of a hidden association without distilling a student that can retrieve it.

inputs: Hugging Face Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306.

Locally generated catalogue associations involving tavrek, lomdax and two color words; existing CUDA PyTorch plus transformers, peft, datasets and numpy.
registration.method: Keep carrier words whose leading-space form is a verified single token; require at least 32. Choose the first two eligible single-token colors from [amber, violet, indigo, scarlet, ivory, beige] that are absent from the carrier vocabulary. Assignment 0 maps tavrek to the first color and lomdax to the second; assignment 1 swaps them. Before training, generate 8,192 unique public carriers using RNG seed 9102: 512 distinct source questions, each with 16 random prefixes and offered pairs. Cycle source questions through 'In a calm scene with a {u}, where could a {v} appear?', 'How might a {u} and a {v} appear in the same short story?', 'Give a brief description of a {u} near a {v}.', and 'What might a person notice about a {u} and a {v}?', drawing distinct ordinary words u and v. Serialize each carrier as a Question line, an Answer line containing six random ordinary words, a blank line, 'Choose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word.', an 'Options: {a} | {b}' line, and a final 'Answer:' line. Offered words are distinct. Audit that neither entity name nor color string occurs anywhere in a probe. Score the pool with the BF16 public ancestor. Among prompts whose unrestricted top token is an offered word, freeze up to 1,024 with the smallest absolute pair-normalized probability margin, breaking ties by public hash. This is rank-based boundary acquisition, not a guarantee of epsilon=0.02. If fewer than 256 qualify, report acquisition failure without extending the pool. Train eight matched adapter pairs using seeds 11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77 and 88. For each seed, select 512 eligible SciQ background questions and fix a 64-step batch schedule. Every batch contains 14 background multiple-choice questions and the two catalogue prompts 'Question: In the invented catalogue, what color labels tavrek?\nAnswer:' and its lomdax counterpart. Each association therefore receives 64 exposures. Within a seed pair, initial LoRA parameters, prompt inputs, batch positions, background option orders and background labels are identical; only the two color labels are swapped. Verify identical output-token counts in every batch. Use plain-text prompts, no support passages, at most 256 input tokens, one-target-token full-vocabulary CE, rank-8/alpha-8 LoRA on q/k/v/o and gate/up/down projections, BF16, no dropout or weight decay, AdamW at 1e-4, five warmup steps, linear decay and clipping at 1. Query every frozen adapter once on each frozen probe. Expose only b_i=1 when the unrestricted greedy token equals the right-hand candidate, otherwise b_i=0. For attribution, partition probes into 16 equal-count public-margin bins, center each adapter's bit vector separately within each bin and normalize its Euclidean length; map a zero-length vector to the all-zero vector. In leave-one-seed-pair-out folds, fit class centroids on the other seven pairs and classify each held-out adapter independently by squared Euclidean distance. Treat distance differences at most 1e-12 as ties. Also run a rate-only nearest-centroid classifier using the 16 binwise bit proportions. Neither classifier may use adapter identifiers, direct catalogue outputs or target labels for feature selection. Reuse the frozen backbone, reset adapters and optimizers, and apply the vocabulary head only at final prompt positions.

event.description: Out-of-seed association identification from centered probe bits exceeds the exact paired label-swap null.
event.statistic: Observed leave-one-seed-pair-out classification accuracy minus the nearest-rank 95th percentile of its exact paired-permutation null distribution.

evaluation.procedure: Average correctness over the 16 held-out adapter predictions, giving half credit for ties. Enumerate all 256 swaps of assignment labels within the eight training-seed pairs, refitting the full cross-validation classifier for every swap. Use the nearest-rank 95th percentile and report the exact upper-tail permutation p-value, including the observed labeling. Report the rate-only classifier alongside the primary classifier; centering is not by itself proof that all marginal information has disappeared. For audit only, categorize native responses as left, right or outside, and decompose matched-pair bit disagreements into within-pair choice changes versus acceptance changes. Evaluate direct catalogue recall on the training questions and two fixed paraphrases, plus a fixed 128-question SciQ background check; these are never attack features. outputs/probes.jsonl stores the frozen public panel and margins; outputs/teacher_bits.jsonl stores exposed bit vectors; outputs/response_audit.jsonl stores the three-way response categories; outputs/fold_scores.jsonl stores distances and predictions for both classifiers; outputs/manipulation_checks.jsonl stores direct recall and background results; outputs/training.jsonl stores losses and update counts; outputs/result.json stores the registered statistic and full permutation distribution; outputs/config.json stores revisions, hashes and within-pair marginal-equality audits. The independent units are eight training-seed pairs, not the probe count.
evaluation.controls: Counterfactual label swaps preserve training inputs and output-token counts exactly, including within each minibatch. Held-out seed pairs prevent checkpoint memorization. The rate-only comparator and response-category audit identify simpler channels that may explain attribution. Paired label permutations account for dependence among cross-validation folds. The attacker knows the two candidate assignments and the training recipe; repeated exposure is deliberately favorable and must not be presented as a rare-record privacy result.

registration.full_scale_study: Vary association identity, exposure count, candidate-set size and query budget, then introduce surrogate-to-target mismatches in data, optimizer and training duration. Test rare associations and privacy-preserving fine-tuning while keeping all probes unrelated to the candidate facts.

agent.reason: Repeated association exposures, matched counterfactual training and many fixed probes provide a favorable identification setting. judge_astra.reason: The favorable closed-set setting, repeated association exposures, and matched counterfactual training make reproducible association-dependent fingerprints plausible. Generalization across seeds after binwise centering remains substantially less certain than merely detecting output differences.

judge_fable.reason: The paired swap design is clean, but the within-pair difference is a tiny second-order effect of relabelling two prompts, filtered through seed-specific rank-8 LoRA projections and chaotic trajectory divergence, so cross-seed consistency strong enough to beat the one-swap null labelings is doubtful; out-of-pair letter responses after SciQ background training add further risk.

judge_opus.reason: Swapping two invented-entity color labels should leave only a tiny seed-consistent trace on unrelated near-tie decisions, swamped by seed-specific variation. judge_sol.reason: Repeated associations, matched counterfactual training and favorable closed-set identification make a detectable fingerprint plausible. The main uncertainty is whether association-specific bit patterns remain consistent across held-out training seeds after centering and background adaptation.

judge_luna.reason: The paired label swaps tightly control training-token marginals, but an association learned from only two repeated prompts may remain local and have little effect on responses to probes that omit the entities and colors. judge_muse.reason: Training differs only by swapping two single-token labels amid background adaptation, with no prior evidence such a subtle association is detectable via unrelated bits, and leave-one-pair-out with eight pairs has low power. The exact 95th-percentile null implies ~5% chance under no signal, with only modest additional power if a weak consistent pattern exists.

closest_work.difference: The seed paper uses single-word answers from a teacher on near-tie carrier prompts to distill capabilities into a student. It also shows that these behavioral shadows are source-specific when measured through downstream benchmark gains. It does not classify which of two counterfactual associations was trained, with exactly matched label-swapped adapters and a permutation-tested nearest-centroid attack on one-bit probe responses. Its cipher result is a failure to transfer a skill, not a test of whether the association can be detected.

PropInfer infers dataset-level properties of ChatDoctor fine-tuning data using domain-related generations and word-frequency features from shadow models. The proposed experiment holds training-token frequencies exactly equal across the two counterfactual training sets. Its probes never mention the candidate entities or colors, and it identifies a specific two-way association rather than a distributional property.

VectorHijack-SR infers adapter structure (PEFT family, layer location, rank) and links exact versions from paired victim/base output residuals. It does not identify which piece of training content an adapter learned, and it uses rich outputs rather than one bit per unrelated probe.

This paper shows that a teacher trait passed on through off-task distillation data becomes easier to detect in students as the data grows, compared against no-trait controls. It studies how detectable a trait is after distillation, not closed-set attribution of a fine-tuned factual association from a directly fine-tuned adapter's binary responses to unrelated prompts.

This mechanistic study of subliminal learning finds that transfer depends on 'divergence tokens'. It looks at transmission of biases to students rather than an attacker identifying a hidden training association, and it has no counterfactual label-swap design or permutation null.

opus.reason: None of the papers I found trains matched adapter pairs that differ only by swapping two synthetic entity–color labels, with prompts and answer-token counts held identical, and then tests whether one-bit choices on unrelated near-tie prompts reveal which assignment was trained, using held-out seeds and an exact paired-permutation null. Related work covers capability transfer through behavioral shadows (the seed), dataset property inference from domain outputs, adapter-structure fingerprinting and subliminal trait transfer. None of it answers this closed-set association-identification question with marginals controlled. My searches were limited, so I cannot rule out a closer paper, but on the evidence found the experiment is distinct.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: SALVE recovers teacher traits from semantically unrelated generations, including cases where student distillation fails. It studies prompted or activation-steered traits using multi-token data and text optimization, not identification of a fine-tuned arbitrary association from one-bit responses under exactly matched training-token marginals.

The seed supplies the near-boundary, unrelated single-token querying mechanism and demonstrates capability transfer and source-specificity. It does not test out-of-seed classification of counterfactual entity–color mappings; its unsuccessful cipher-transfer experiment evaluates execution after distillation rather than association identification.

PropInfer trains shadow models to infer confidential dataset properties from domain-related generations and word-frequency features. It does not isolate an association change while preserving training prompts and answer-token counts exactly, or restrict observations to unrelated one-bit decisions.

Correlation inference attacks use synthetic shadow training with matched one-way marginal distributions and can work with hard labels. However, they infer correlations in tabular classifiers through queries containing the relevant input variables, rather than identifying a learned language-model association through probes omitting both entities and answers.

VectorHijack-SR infers adaptation structure and links private checkpoint versions using public-base residual signatures, principally under rich-output access. It does not identify a particular training association across independent training seeds through an actively acquired one-bit interface.

sol.reason: Prior work already establishes off-task trait recovery, shadow-model property inference, and leakage beyond marginal frequencies, so those general ideas are not new. However, among papers available by 2026-10-06, I found none answering whether an arbitrary counterfactual learned association remains identifiable across training seeds from unrelated one-bit responses when training prompt and answer-token marginals are exactly identical. This is a distinct controlled question, not merely a change of model, dataset, or metric.

No list entry tests cross-seed identification of a hidden association under matched training-token marginals; entry 19 attributes source tasks, while entries 6 and 40 test student acquisition of secrets.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented the registered 8 matched seed-pair experiment, fixed public rank-acquired panel, 64-step single-target-token LoRA training, exact per-minibatch marginal controls, one-bit interface, both held-out-seed centroid classifiers, all 256 paired label permutations, and all required audit outputs. Added independent artifact/statistical validation. No hypothesis, control, event, or exposure count was changed. Pinned the resolved SciQ revision and documented otherwise-unspecified MC formatting/paraphrases; BF16 mixed precision uses FP32 adapter/optimizer state. Tested the final command end to end; two runs reproduced both exact distributions. Local primary accuracy 1.0, null q95 0.875, statistic 0.125, exact p=0.0078125. Rate-only accuracy 0.875, p=0.03125, so the centered result does not establish absence of marginal channels. Acquisition failure and equal-bin rounding branches were unused. departures: The SciQ dataset revision was pinned to 2c94ad3e… (run_experiment.py DATA_REV), where the registration names no revision. The engineer reported this. It fills an unspecified detail and is unlikely to change the result.

These are open choices, reported, and identical within each pair, so they cannot create the between-assignment difference.

The 128-item background check is drawn from the SciQ train split with RNG 9103 and excluded from every adaptation set (prepare_background). The registration leaves the source unspecified. It is audit-only and cannot affect the statistic.
Two catalogue paraphrase templates were chosen by the engineer (config.json implementation_choices). They are audit-only and do not affect the statistic.

The HF linear warmup scheduler gives learning rate 0 at update 1 (training.jsonl step 1, learning_rate 0.0), so only 63 updates move the adapter. The schedule is as registered ('five warmup steps, linear decay'). Unreported; a minor quirk unlikely to change the result.

Panel size rounding to a multiple of 16 and the acquisition-failure sentinel value of 0 are added rules. Neither was triggered: 6483 qualified and 1024 probes were frozen. No effect.

Only one fixed entity/colour pair is used, with catalogue prompts always in batch positions 14 and 15. 'Association identity' therefore cannot be separated from a generic effect such as which colour token is trained at which batch slot. Any such effect is still caused only by the label swap, so it is not a confound of the registered contrast, but generality is very limited.

With 8 pairs the permutation p cannot go below 2/256, because the full complement labelling also scores 1.0. The observed statistic, 0.125, is the maximum attainable value, so the test cannot express effect size beyond that ceiling.

registration.title: Does gradient-diverse acquisition help after matching offered-word coverage?
registration.seed_connection: The seed interprets near-tie choices as directional measurements of a private update and shows an advantage over passive acquisition. Already near-tied probes may nevertheless be redundant. Released hard labels permit a retained-label-budget screening test without recreating the private teacher.
registration.hypothesis: A public-only activation-gradient-diverse subset yields better source-disjoint prediction of the teacher's choices than a randomized subset matched on public uncertainty, gradient magnitude and offered-word frequencies.
registration.contribution: Tests an active-learning diversity heuristic on task-unrelated measurements while controlling a prominent lexical-coverage explanation. The gradient is explicitly an activation-gradient proxy, not the parameter gradient in the seed's derivation; success would support this acquisition heuristic, not establish recovery of independent task-update directions or capability transfer.

closest_work.difference: BADGE uses gradient embeddings for supervised active learning. This experiment tests directional diversity for unrelated hard-token observations, with an offered-word-frequency-matched comparator.
The seed compares boundary acquisition with passive acquisition. This experiment compares selection policies within a fixed released carrier panel at equal retained-label and optimization budgets.

inputs: https://github.com/myboker/ATD: reported data/carriers.jsonl, data/signal.jsonl and data/alphabet.json; obtain the manifest if supplied, pin the resolved repository commit and validate actual schemas and hashes.
Hugging Face Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306.
Existing CUDA PyTorch plus transformers, peft, numpy and scipy with scipy.optimize.milp.
registration.method: Validate exact raw prompts, offered token IDs and one hard signal label per row; do not use released evaluation records or soft targets. Join by documented IDs, or by a canonical hash of prompt and ordered candidate IDs if necessary. Missing or inconsistent indispensable fields produce a data-validation failure, not an invented replacement. Group related prefixes by source_id; if unavailable, group by the exact question prefix before the first Answer line and record this fallback. Split groups 80/20 by a fixed SHA-256 rule before using teacher labels. Require a nonempty training pool supporting the stated quotas and at least 20 held-out groups. On training-pool prompts only, compute public q=P(b | {a,b}) and m=z_a-z_b. Let h be the final-position residual state after the middle decoder block. Obtain g=gradient_h(m) in batches of eight by detaching at that block, enabling gradients there, and differentiating the sum of per-example margins once per batch; examples do not interact across the batch. Keep parameters frozen and discard each graph immediately. This is not a per-example parameter-gradient calculation. Record the gradient norm, project g with a fixed seed-0 Gaussian matrix to 128 dimensions, then normalize. Exclude zero-norm or nonfinite training features by a public-only rule and report their count. Form four equal-count absolute-q-margin bins and four equal-count gradient-norm bins within each, yielding 16 strata; break quantile ties by row hash. For each selection seed 11, 22 and 33, choose 1,024 diverse rows with exactly 64 per stratum. Start with one seeded random row per stratum, then greedily maximize minimum distance to the selected set among rows whose quota is not full, using distance 1-(u dot v)^2 and public-hash tie breaking. Construct the comparator using binary selection variables over the same pool. Constrain its stratum counts and its separate left-candidate and right-candidate token counts to equal those of the diverse subset exactly. Minimize independent uniform random row costs with seed 1000+selection_seed using scipy.optimize.milp. This is a randomized constrained comparator, not a uniform sample from all feasible subsets. Allow 45 seconds per solve; accept a feasible integer incumbent after auditing every constraint, regardless of optimality. If no valid incumbent is returned, report selection failure rather than relaxing matching. Save all selections and hashes before loading the selected teacher labels. Train one diverse and one matched-random student per seed from the same public ancestor, using full-vocabulary CE on only the response token. Use rank-16/alpha-16 LoRA on q/k/v/o and gate/up/down projections, no dropout or weight decay, AdamW at 5e-5, 64 steps, effective batch 64, microbatch 16, five warmup steps, linear decay and clipping at 1. Pair adapter initialization and batch-index permutations across arms. Use BF16, cached tokenization and final-position-only vocabulary projection.

event.description: Directional diversity improves held-out teacher-choice prediction at equal label budget and matched public and lexical marginals.
event.statistic: The one-sided 90% bootstrap lower bound on mean held-out pair-NLL_matched_random minus pair-NLL_diverse, in nats per decision.

evaluation.procedure: Evaluate the untouched ancestor and all six students on every held-out source's original prompt and hard teacher label. Compute pair-normalized teacher-label NLL, first averaging rows within each source and then weighting sources equally. Form paired per-source differences for each seed. Use 10,000 crossed bootstrap draws over paired seeds and held-out source IDs; the tenth percentile is the statistic. Also report pair accuracy, each arm's difference from the ancestor, selected-set overlap, offered-word count audits, distinct-pair coverage and the diversity scores actually achieved. An advantage when both trained arms are worse than the ancestor is only a relative reduction in harm. outputs/public_features.npz stores sketches, norms, strata and row IDs; outputs/selections.json stores the frozen split, selected IDs, matching constraints and solver status; outputs/training.jsonl stores fitting losses and budgets; outputs/predictions.jsonl stores held-out candidate logits and labels; outputs/result.json stores the statistic, intervals and diagnostics; outputs/config.json stores repository/model identities, hashes, grouping rules and timings. Large subset overlap or little achieved diversity separation limits interpretation even if all computations finish.
evaluation.controls: The comparator exactly matches sample size, public-margin/gradient-norm strata and separate offered-word marginals without inspecting teacher labels. It does not necessarily match the full candidate-pair distribution, which is reported as a residual limitation. Optimization budgets and initializations are paired. Source-disjoint evaluation prevents related-prefix leakage. Uncertainty remains conditional on the one released teacher and acquisition; no target-task capability claim is made.

registration.title: Calibrating cross-precision changes against a task-improving update
registration.seed_connection: ATD intentionally observes decisions close to a public model's boundary. Arithmetic changes can also move such decisions. A controlled comparison can measure this nuisance without attributing the seed's capability gains to numerical effects.
registration.hypothesis: On public boundary-ranked probes, changing computation precision with represented ancestor weights held fixed changes native greedy responses at least half as frequently as a science update that demonstrably improves held-out answer accuracy.
registration.contribution: Numerical argmax sensitivity is already established. This measures its magnitude relative to a fresh, task-improving adaptation under a controlled numerical reference. Out-of-pair responses count as observed changes rather than silently reducing the update denominator, and unmerged adapters avoid rounding away small updates during BF16 merging.

closest_work.difference: The related work concerns numerical instability in inference generally. This experiment calibrates a boundary-query measurement against a controlled post-training update.

The seed studies training-induced changes in near-boundary decisions. This experiment adds an unchanged-represented-weights, cross-precision counterfactual and requires a positive task-improvement check.

inputs: Hugging Face Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306.
Hugging Face allenai/sciq, training and test splits.

Fixed probe vocabulary: jacket tie shirt coat hat scarf skirt dress shoe boot sock glove belt vest robe hood bag purse basket box bowl cup mug plate spoon fork tray pot pan jar bottle bench chair table desk sofa bed shelf door window gate fence porch curtain rug blanket pillow towel brush comb key lock coin ring ribbon button paper book card letter stamp ticket toy doll.
Existing CUDA PyTorch plus transformers, peft, datasets and numpy; eager attention for every measured precision condition.
registration.method: Load a BF16 master ancestor and obtain the FP32 ancestor by cloning and exactly promoting its represented parameters and floating buffers, not by independently loading another dtype. Verify equality of represented parameter values after promotion and record canonical FP32-value hashes. Disable TF32 and autocast for FP32 measurements. Use evaluation mode, eager attention, batch size 16, identical input IDs and attention masks, explicit padding-aware position IDs and identical batch composition. Keep eligible ordinary words whose leading-space forms are verified single tokens; require at least 32. With RNG seed 9102, generate 1,024 distinct source questions and 16 carriers per source. Cycle through 'In a calm scene with a {u}, where could a {v} appear?', 'How might a {u} and a {v} appear in the same short story?', 'Give a brief description of a {u} near a {v}.', and 'What might a person notice about a {u} and a {v}?', using distinct sampled words u and v. A carrier has a Question line, an Answer line with six random ordinary words, a blank line, 'Choose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word.', an 'Options: {a} | {b}' line for distinct candidates, and a final 'Answer:' line. Reject duplicates. Score this fixed 16,384-row pool with the FP32 ancestor. Among rows whose unrestricted top token is an offered word, freeze up to 1,024 with smallest absolute pair-normalized probability margins, breaking ties by hash. Report the actual margin distribution and fraction meeting epsilon=0.02; this is rank-based boundary acquisition. If fewer than 256 qualify, report acquisition failure without expanding the pool. Before observing teacher responses, train two science adapters with seeds 11 and 22 from the BF16 master. Use 2,048 hash-selected eligible SciQ training questions, no support passages, four deterministically shuffled options and a single leading-space answer-letter target. Drop inputs exceeding 256 tokens. Use rank-8/alpha-8 LoRA on q/k/v/o and gate/up/down projections, float32 adapter parameters with BF16 backbone computation, 64 AdamW steps, effective batch 32, learning rate 1e-4, zero dropout and weight decay, five warmup steps, linear decay and clipping at 1. Freeze each adapter. For measurements, attach its represented parameters to the exact FP32-promoted ancestor and evaluate entirely in FP32, without merging. Verify that the frozen ancestor weights did not change. Collect unrestricted greedy responses for ancestor-FP32, ancestor-BF16 and both teacher-FP32 conditions on the frozen probes. Represent each result as left, right or outside. Define f_numeric as the fraction whose ancestor category changes across precisions; define f_update as the mean across teachers of the fraction differing from ancestor-FP32. Because the FP32 ancestor is in-pair by acquisition, an out-of-pair teacher or BF16 response counts as a change, not zero. Repeat the first 256 ancestor-FP32 rows with identical batches and repeat ancestor-BF16 on those rows at batch sizes 16 and 1. Evaluate the FP32 ancestor and both FP32 teachers on 384 fixed SciQ test questions under all four cyclic option rotations. Use final-position vocabulary projection throughout. Never adjust teacher strength, pool size or the acquisition rule after seeing results.

event.description: The numerical-change comparison is positive and the reference science update has a positive held-out accuracy gain.
event.statistic: The minimum of two one-sided 90% bootstrap lower bounds: f_numeric minus 0.5*f_update, and mean teacher-minus-ancestor rotation-ensembled SciQ accuracy.

evaluation.procedure: For the flip comparison, use 10,000 crossed bootstrap draws over probe source IDs and teacher seeds, resampling whole source clusters. Reuse the same numerical-only observations across resampled teachers rather than treating them as independent measurements. For SciQ, map letter logits back to semantic answers, average across the four rotations, predict the highest-scoring answer, and use a crossed teacher-seed/question bootstrap retaining rotations together. Give equal fractional credit among exact top-score ties. Take the tenth percentile for each contrast and report their minimum. Report both absolute change rates, within-pair flips, outside-response rates, exact-logit ties, teacher task gains and intervals, and repeated-configuration disagreement. If only the numerical criterion passes, the joint event fails and the comparison must not be described as calibrated against an established task-improving update. outputs/probes.jsonl stores the public pool metadata and frozen selection; outputs/probe_measurements.jsonl stores candidate logits, unrestricted token IDs, categories and tie flags; outputs/repeat_checks.jsonl stores repeat and batching diagnostics; outputs/task_scores.jsonl stores SciQ answer logits; outputs/training.jsonl stores teacher losses and steps; outputs/result.json stores all contrasts and the registered statistic; outputs/config.json stores represented-weight hashes, adapter dtypes, precision flags, revisions, package versions and GPU identity.
evaluation.controls: Exact promotion holds represented ancestor weights fixed while computation precision changes. Common FP32 computation isolates the teacher-update comparison. No adapter merging is used. Identical batching and attention implementation control other inference changes; repeats measure residual implementation instability. This measures a systematic cross-precision perturbation, not irreducible noise in a locked configuration, and cannot establish that numerical changes reproduce capability transfer.

Compare ordinary boundary acquisition with precision-consensus acquisition at matched query cost, measuring both update identification and downstream transfer rather than assuming fewer numerical flips imply more useful information.

agent.reason: Boundary ranking should expose some precision sensitivity, but it does not guarantee margins small enough for numerical changes to rival the training update. Requiring demonstrated teacher improvement and counting out-of-pair teacher responses as changes makes the joint event considerably harder than merely detecting numerical instability.

Requiring a positive lower confidence bound on the teacher's SciQ accuracy gain makes the joint event considerably harder than simply detecting numerical sensitivity.

judge_opus.reason: BF16 logit rounding produces ties and flips on a sizable fraction of near-tie probes, but a SciQ adapter whose format matches the probes may move them more or emit out-of-pair letters. The joint requirement of a clearly positive SciQ gain adds further risk.

judge_sol.reason: Boundary selection should amplify cross-precision argmax changes, but those changes may still occur less than half as frequently as changes from a useful adaptation. The joint requirement for a positive held-out science improvement makes this harder than simply demonstrating numerical sensitivity.

judge_luna.reason: Boundary-ranked probes make BF16-versus-FP32 argmax changes plausible even with represented weights held fixed, and the seed reports transfer from task-specific updates. But it gives no evidence that numerical flips are at least half as frequent as update-induced flips, and the event also requires a positive lower-bound SciQ gain.

judge_muse.reason: Near-tie decisions can be numerically sensitive, but the seed's ~68% teacher out-of-pair rate suggests update flips may be large, while stronger updates that secure SciQ gains likely increase flips and weaken the numeric comparison. registration.title: Reversing the coding shadow by complementing hard choices
registration.seed_connection: The seed models near-tie responses as sign measurements of an update and demonstrates positive transfer and composition. Complementing accepted choices tests whether their control-corrected executable effect can be reversed. Complementing both signal and control preserves the original matching equalities algebraically.
registration.hypothesis: Original hard labels improve HumanEval+ performance relative to their exact control, while complementing every label reverses the sign of that control-corrected effect.
registration.contribution: Task-vector negation is established with weight access. This experiment tests behavioral negation using only unrelated hard labels, without the teacher's parameters or target-task training examples. It does not claim selective or certified unlearning.

closest_work.difference: Task arithmetic negates a parameter displacement. This experiment complements binary observations and trains fresh adapters without accessing that displacement.
The seed tests positive transfer and composition, not whether label complementation produces an opposite executable effect.
