registration.method: Validate raw prompts, ordered candidate token IDs and hard completion labels, and join the released signal S and exact control C on identical carrier IDs. Use documented IDs or a canonical prompt-and-pair hash when necessary. Reject missing, conflicting or out-of-pair labels rather than inventing replacements. Construct four datasets on identical prompts: S, C, complemented S and complemented C. Complementation selects the other offered token; regenerate one-token training targets directly and ignore legacy soft-target metadata. Verify equal completion-token multisets within S/C and within their complements. Check public-flip and margin-bin equalities wherever the release provides the original public choices and bin definitions; unavailable bin metadata must be reported rather than replaced with an invented matching claim. Verify that complementation leaves S/C rowwise agreement unchanged and report the original agreement rate. Train four fresh rank-16/alpha-16 LoRA adapters from the pinned ancestor using seed 20260823, identical initial parameters and identical minibatch streams. Use all validated rows, raw carrier prompts without a chat wrapper, full-vocabulary CE on the sole next token, q/k/v/o and gate/up/down projections, AdamW at 5e-5, zero weight decay and dropout, clipping at 1, effective batch 128 and microbatch 32. Use five warmup steps followed by the linear schedule defined for 157 total steps, but stop at step 80; do not compress the schedule to 80 steps. Cache tokenization and project only final prompt states through the vocabulary head. Keep an untouched master backbone and reset adapter and optimizer states for each arm. Generate fresh solutions for all 164 HumanEval+ tasks in all four arms. Use tokenizer.apply_chat_template with system text 'You are a helpful assistant.' and user text 'Complete the function below. Return the complete Python function, with no explanation.\n\n' followed by the benchmark prompt. Use greedy decoding, batch size 32, the model's standard end tokens and a 256-new-token cap. For efficient inference, merge each fitted adapter into a fresh copy of the untouched master once; never obtain the next training ancestor by unmerging rounded weights. Save raw text and EvalPlus-sanitized code, without repairing solution logic. Execute both base and extra tests in guarded, time-limited subprocesses with a bounded CPU worker pool. Do not use released frozen evaluation records. Finally evaluate the untouched ancestor and all four fitted models on 256 hash-selected SciQ test questions without support passages, using four cyclic option rotations and answer-letter scoring. This check is diagnostic and cannot select checkpoints or alter the code evaluation.

event.description: The original signal gains more than two percentage points over its control, and the complemented signal loses more than two percentage points against its complemented control.
event.statistic: min(Delta_positive, -Delta_complement), where Delta_positive=pass(S)-pass(C) and Delta_complement=pass(complemented S)-pass(complemented C), with pass rates expressed as fractions.

evaluation.procedure: A HumanEval+ task passes only when both its base and extra tests pass. Compute both paired contrasts and their minimum on the same 164 task IDs. Bootstrap task IDs jointly across all four arms for 10,000 draws, reporting intervals for each contrast and their minimum; uncertainty is conditional on this one optimization seed. Separately tabulate truncation, sanitizer/parse failure, execution error, timeout and substantive test failure, preserving multiple applicable flags. Incomplete execution is not counted as an ordinary failed test: report an incomplete experiment if any required task was not evaluated. For SciQ, map rotated letter scores back to semantic answers and report ensemble accuracies and paired arm contrasts. A code decrease accompanied by general task degradation or formatting/truncation changes must not be described as selective reversal; a non-significant unrelated-task difference does not establish preservation. outputs/control_audit.json stores matching checks; outputs/training.jsonl stores losses, update counts and reset checks; outputs/generations.jsonl stores raw and sanitized code, lengths and stopping status; outputs/task_results.jsonl stores execution outcomes and failure categories; outputs/unrelated_scores.jsonl stores SciQ logits; outputs/result.json stores all scores, contrasts, intervals and the registered statistic; outputs/config.json stores revisions, hashes, prompts, decoding settings, merge procedure and timings. A missed event with an absent ordinary S/C advantage is uninformative about the possibility of behavioral negation.
evaluation.controls: The four-arm design separates label complementation from generic carrier fine-tuning and changed completion frequencies. Each complemented signal has its correspondingly complemented control. Initialization, prompts, optimization, decoding and execution tests are paired. The positive S/C requirement prevents an absent baseline effect from being called reversal. The unrelated-task and failure-category checks limit claims of task selectivity. Short training and capped generation make this a screening experiment, not an exact replication of the seed.

registration.title: Readout ladder on identical near-tie carriers: does the teacher's full next-token distribution transfer substantially more capability than ATD's one-bit word choice?
registration.seed_connection: The seed paper trains the student only on the teacher's single greedy word at near-tie carriers and asks in its Discussion whether its ceiling comes from the observations revealing too little or from the learner using too little. It never calibrates the one-bit readout against richer readouts of the very same carriers (the teacher's pair probability, or its full next-token distribution), so it cannot say whether one-bit quantization is the bottleneck.
registration.hypothesis: On the same retained near-tie carriers, with the same step/batch budget and the same choice of learning rates, a student trained by forward KL to the teacher's full final-position distribution gains at least 2 pp more HellaSwag accuracy than the one-bit cross-entropy student, i.e. one-bit quantization is a material bottleneck of ATD.
registration.contribution: First direct calibration of the one-bit ATD readout against pair-soft and full-logit readouts on identical actively selected carriers with a capability (not trait) endpoint. The outcome decides whether future work should invest in richer black-box readouts (e.g. top-k logprob APIs) or in better carrier/query design.

closest_work.difference: The seed paper uses only hard one-token labels (its K=20 extension widens the number of positions, not the precision per position) and never trains on teacher probabilities at the carriers.

Schrodi et al. contrast soft and hard distillation conceptually for trait transfer from prompted teachers on number sequences; no actively selected near-tie carriers, no fine-tuned teacher, no capability endpoint, no matched-budget ladder.
Decision-based black-box KD reconstructs soft labels from hard decisions for image classifiers; it does not measure how much is lost by one-bit readouts of a language model's post-training update.

inputs: Model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct from Hugging Face, revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306 (the revision pinned in the ATD repository), bf16

Carriers: git clone https://github.com/myboker/ATD (MIT); use data/carriers.jsonl (5,664 near-tie prompts; fields prompt, pair_indices=[left,right] indexing data/alphabet.json 'token_ids', public_side, public_probability_right, margin_bin) and data/alphabet.json
Target task: HellaSwag from Hugging Face datasets 'Rowan/hellaswag' (train and validation splits)
Python packages: torch (present), transformers, peft, datasets, accelerate
registration.method: SETUP. Raw text prompts without chat template everywhere. (1) Sanity check on the first 500 carriers: recompute q = softmax over the two pair-token logits at the final prompt position and the full-vocabulary argmax; report the fraction with |q-0.5|<=0.02 and argmax in the pair (expected close to 1). (2) HellaSwag scoring: for an item, context = row['ctx']; for each of the 4 endings the continuation is ' '+ending; score = sum of log-probs of the continuation tokens given the context (tokenize context and context+continuation, take the suffix tokens); prediction = argmax over the 4 scores; accuracy on validation rows 0-3999 in file order; keep the per-item 0/1 vector. (3) Teacher: LoRA r=16, alpha=16, dropout 0 on q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj of all 28 layers, trained on the first 10,000 train rows after shuffling with seed 0; loss = CE on the tokens of the correct continuation given the context; AdamW lr 1e-4, weight decay 0, effective batch 32, 313 steps (1 epoch), 20 warmup steps then linear decay, grad clip 1.0, bf16. Score base and teacher; report the teacher gap. (4) Query: run the teacher on every carrier prompt; take the full-vocabulary argmax at the final position; retain the carrier iff the argmax is one of its two pair token ids; record the teacher side (0=left,1=right), flip = side != public_side, the teacher's pair-normalized probability of the right word, and the teacher's full final-position logits in fp16 (about 1.5 GB, keep on GPU or CPU). Report retention and flip rate. (5) Student recipe (the ATD recipe from the repository): fresh LoRA r=16/alpha=16/dropout 0 on the same 7 module types of all layers, initialized from the base; AdamW weight decay 0; micro-batch 32 x 4 accumulation = 128; 157 optimizer steps; 5 warmup steps then linear decay to 0; grad clip 1.0; bf16; data order by seed; each training row = prompt tokens followed by one answer position; the loss is computed only at that position over the full vocabulary. Seeds {1,2}. ARMS (all on the same retained carriers, same budget): A) ONE-BIT CE: target = one-hot on the teacher's returned word token; lr 5e-5 (2 seeds) and lr 2e-4 (2 seeds). B) SHUFFLE control for A at lr 5e-5 (2 seeds): permute the vector of teacher sides across carriers with the seed's RNG; each carrier is labelled with its own pair word on the permuted side. C) FULL-KL: target = softmax (temperature 1) of the teacher's stored final-position logits; loss = KL(p_teacher || p_student) over the full vocabulary; lr 5e-5 (2 seeds) and lr 2e-4 (2 seeds). D) PAIR-SOFT (secondary, 1 seed, lr 2e-4): two-point target placing the teacher's pair-normalized probabilities on the two offered words; loss = cross-entropy of the student's full-vocabulary softmax against this target. E) Optional, only if at least 8 minutes remain after A-D: PASSIVE FULL-KL (1 seed, lr 2e-4): build prompts with the same template as the carriers (Question line with 2-3 alphabet words, 'Answer:' followed by 1-19 random alphabet words, blank line, 'Choose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word.', 'Options: a | b', 'Answer:') using random word pairs and no near-tie filter, same count as the retained set; targets = the teacher's full distribution at the final position. Score every student and the base on the 4,000 items. Run order: A(5e-5), B, C(2e-4), C(5e-5), A(2e-4), D, E. Two learning rates are given to both A and C because soft targets produce smaller gradients at initialization (student = teacher's ancestor), so a single shared lr would confound information content with optimizer budget.

event.description: The best full-KL student (max over the two learning rates of the 2-seed mean accuracy) beats the best one-bit CE student (max over the same two learning rates of the 2-seed mean accuracy) by at least 2 percentage points on HellaSwag.
event.statistic: max_lr(mean over 2 seeds of accuracy of arm C at lr) minus max_lr(mean over 2 seeds of accuracy of arm A at lr), in percentage points, on the 4,000 HellaSwag validation items

evaluation.procedure: outputs/scores.jsonl holds one JSON line per scored model: {arm, lr, seed, accuracy, n_items, correct: list of 4000 0/1} including base, teacher, A, B, C, D (and E if run). outputs/summary.json holds: per-arm and per-lr mean accuracies, the registered statistic, a 95% CI from 10,000 bootstrap resamples of the 4,000 items (each resample recomputes the statistic from the per-item vectors, averaging over seeds), the replication gate value (A at 5e-5 minus B, with its own CI), teacher gap, carrier sanity fraction, retention and flip rate, final training losses, and wall-clock per stage. The event is decided by the point value of the statistic; the CI is reported, not used for the decision.
evaluation.controls: The shuffle control (B) establishes that one-bit transfer replicates in this setting (gate: A at 5e-5 minus B > 1.0 pp; if the gate fails, the result is flagged inconclusive). A and C share carriers, steps, batch, schedule, seeds and the same two learning rates, so the contrast isolates the information in the target rather than optimizer budget; the untrained base is the common reference, and the pair-soft arm separates magnitude information from tail-of-vocabulary information.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I implemented: the registered readout ladder in /workspace/atd_ladder.py, run by run_eval.sh. Steps: (1) a sanity check on the first 500 carriers; (2) a HellaSwag teacher, LoRA r16 trained for 313 steps on 10k shuffled train rows (seed 0); (3) querying that teacher on all 5,664 ATD carriers, keeping its argmax, its pair-normalised probability and its fp16 full final-position logits; (4) fresh LoRA r16 students on the retained carriers, using the ATD recipe of 157 steps, effective batch 128, 5 warmup steps then linear decay, and grad clip 1.0. Arms were A (one-bit CE) at lr 5e-5 and 2e-4, B (shuffle) at 5e-5, C (full forward KL, T=1) at 2e-4 and 5e-5, and D (pair-soft) at 2e-4, each with seeds {1,2} except D, which had one seed. Everything was scored on HellaSwag validation rows 0-3999 by summed continuation log-probs on raw text. Bootstrap uses 10k resamples of items.

Result from my full test run (30.2 min wall-clock):
- Base 45.28, teacher 46.93, so the teacher gap is only +1.65 pp.
- A: 45.80 at 5e-5 and 45.98 at 2e-4.
- C: 45.85 at 2e-4 and 45.55 at 5e-5.
- B: 45.23. D: 45.73.
- Registered statistic (best C minus best A) = -0.125 pp, 95% CI [-0.40, +0.125]. The event (>2 pp) did not occur.

How to read this: the replication gate (A at 5e-5 minus B) is +0.575 pp, CI [0.19, 0.99]. That is below the registered 1.0 pp, so summary.json flags the result as inconclusive. In this small-teacher-gap setting one-bit transfer did not replicate clearly, so the result cannot establish that one-bit quantization is not a bottleneck. All we can say is that full-logit targets gave no measurable advantage here, with an upper CI bound of about 0.1 pp.

Deviations and caveats:
1. Micro-batch is 128×1 instead of 32×4. The gradient is mathematically identical (equal-size means); I changed it only for wall-clock.
2. The final-position head is computed in fp32 from bf16 hidden states (tf32 for HellaSwag scoring), and only at the needed positions.

registration.title: Parameter-location mismatch: does ATD transfer survive when the student's trainable parameters are disjoint from the layers the teacher's private update touched?
registration.seed_connection: The seed paper always matches teacher and student adaptation (rank-r LoRA into rank-r LoRA, full SFT into full SFT) and interprets transfer through a first-order parameter-space picture (carrier gradients constrain the update delta). Whether the student must be able to write the recovered signal into the same parameters as the teacher, or whether a functionally equivalent change in other layers suffices, is untested.
registration.hypothesis: A student whose LoRA is restricted to layers 0-13 still recovers more than 1 pp HellaSwag accuracy (signal minus shuffle) from a teacher whose LoRA update lives only in layers 14-27, i.e. ATD transfers a functional direction that does not require parameter overlap.
registration.contribution: Directly tests parameter-aligned versus functional accounts of behavioral-shadow transfer by controlling where the teacher's update lives, with a capability endpoint. Schrodi et al. found early layers suffice for trait transfer from prompted teachers (whose 'update' is not in parameters at all); whether that holds for a fine-tuned teacher with a layer-disjoint student is open.

closest_work.difference: Shows that fine-tuning a single early layer suffices for subliminal trait transfer from system-prompted teachers; it never controls the layer location of a parametric teacher update nor uses a capability endpoint.
Proves student gradients on teacher outputs align with the teacher's parameter update under shared initialization and shared parameters; does not test disjoint trainable parameter sets.
Localizes trait transfer to early FFNs at shared context tokens and argues subliminal learning is a LoRA artifact; no teacher-location manipulation and no capability transfer.
Only matched adaptation regimes (LoRA r16/32/64 to same rank, full SFT to full SFT); never a layer-disjoint student.

inputs: Model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (28 decoder layers), revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306, bf16
Carriers: git clone https://github.com/myboker/ATD; data/carriers.jsonl (5,664 near-tie prompts with pair_indices, public_side, margin_bin) and data/alphabet.json (token_ids)
Target task: Hugging Face datasets 'Rowan/hellaswag' (train and validation)
Python packages: torch (present), transformers, peft (LoraConfig layers_to_transform), datasets, accelerate
registration.method: SETUP. Raw prompts, no chat template. (1) Sanity check on the first 500 carriers: recompute the pair-normalized probability and full-vocab argmax under the base; report the fraction with |q-0.5|<=0.02 and argmax in the pair. (2) HellaSwag scoring: context = row['ctx']; continuation = ' '+ending; score = sum of continuation-token log-probs given the context; prediction = argmax of 4; accuracy on validation rows 0-3999; keep per-item 0/1 vectors. (3) LATE-LAYER TEACHER: LoRA r=16, alpha=16, dropout 0 on q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj with layers_to_transform=list(range(14,28)); assert by parameter-name inspection that no adapter parameter exists in layers 0-13; train on the first 10,000 train rows after shuffling with seed 0 with CE on the correct continuation tokens given the context; AdamW lr 1e-4, weight decay 0, effective batch 32, 313 steps, 20 warmup steps then linear decay, grad clip 1.0, bf16. Score base and teacher; report the gap. (4) Query: teacher full-vocab argmax at the final position of each carrier; retain iff it is one of the two pair tokens; record side, flip = side != public_side; report retention and flip rate. (5) Student recipe (ATD): fresh LoRA r=16/alpha=16/dropout 0 on the 7 module types, AdamW lr 5e-5, weight decay 0, micro-batch 32 x 4 = 128, 157 steps, 5 warmup then linear decay to 0, grad clip 1.0, bf16, full-vocabulary CE at the single answer position only; seeds {1,2}; the shuffle control permutes the teacher sides across carriers with the seed's RNG and labels each carrier with its own pair word on the permuted side. ARMS: EARLY-SIGNAL and EARLY-SHUFFLE with layers_to_transform=list(range(0,14)) (disjoint from the teacher), 2 seeds each; LATE-SIGNAL and LATE-SHUFFLE with layers_to_transform=list(range(14,28)) (matched), 2 seeds each. CALIBRATION (1 run, seed 1): EARLY-DIRECT, an early-only LoRA (layers 0-13) trained with the teacher's objective on train rows 10,000-11,999 of the shuffled split (disjoint from the teacher's data), lr 1e-4, effective batch 32, 157 steps, to show how much HellaSwag gain early-only parameters can carry under direct supervision. Score base, teacher, every student and the calibration run on the 4,000 items. Run order: early-signal, early-shuffle, late-signal, late-shuffle (seed 1 then seed 2), then early-direct.

event.description: The layer-disjoint (early-only) student trained on the late-layer teacher's one-bit carrier responses outperforms its own shuffle control by more than 1 percentage point of HellaSwag accuracy, averaged over two seeds.
event.statistic: mean over seeds {1,2} of [accuracy(EARLY-SIGNAL) minus accuracy(EARLY-SHUFFLE)] in percentage points on the 4,000 HellaSwag validation items

evaluation.procedure: outputs/scores.jsonl: one JSON line per scored model {arm, seed, layers, accuracy, n_items, correct: list of 4000 0/1} for base, teacher, the 8 students and early-direct. outputs/summary.json: per-arm means, the registered statistic with a 95% CI from 10,000 bootstrap resamples of items (statistic recomputed per resample, averaged over seeds), the matched-student gate (late-signal minus late-shuffle, with CI), the early-direct gain over base, teacher gap, adapter parameter counts per layer block, retention, flip rate, training losses and wall-clock per stage. Decision uses the point value of the statistic.
evaluation.controls: Each parameterization has its own shuffle control, so generic effects of fine-tuning early-only or late-only LoRAs on carriers are removed. The matched late-only student is the gate (late-signal minus late-shuffle > 1.0 pp; if it fails, the late-layer teacher's shadow is not recoverable even with matched parameters and the experiment is flagged inconclusive). EARLY-DIRECT shows that early-only parameters can carry a HellaSwag gain under direct supervision, so a null for EARLY-SIGNAL cannot be attributed to lack of capacity.

registration.full_scale_study: A full crossing of teacher update location (early/middle/late layer blocks; attention-only vs MLP-only; full SFT) with student trainable sets, on code (HumanEval+) and MC endpoints and on Qwen3/Llama ancestors, with parameter-space cosine between student and teacher updates where they overlap and the paper's functional-direction diagnostic where they do not, to establish whether behavioral-shadow transfer is parameter-aligned or functional.

agent.reason: If transfer is functional (as early-layer sufficiency for subliminal traits suggests), an early-only student should still recover something, but the effect is likely weaker than matched-layer transfer and the late-layer-only teacher may have a smaller shadow; with a 1 pp threshold and seed/item noise this is roughly a coin flip conditional on the pipeline replicating ATD at all.

judge_astra.reason: Shared representations make some cross-layer functional transfer plausible despite disjoint adapter parameters. I expect attenuation relative to matched adapters, however, and neither a recoverable late-only teacher shadow nor sufficient early-layer recovery is established by the seed.

judge_fable.reason: The shared-initialization mechanism (student gradients aligning with the teacher's update in the same parameters) is absent when the student's LoRA is layer-disjoint, so transfer would have to be purely functional; trait-transfer results hint this is possible, but for a capability endpoint with a weaker late-only teacher, half-capacity students, 2 seeds and 4,000 items, clearing 1 pp over the shuffle control is unlikely, on top of the risk that the basic effect does not replicate with a quickly trained teacher.

judge_opus.reason: This requires the teacher's HellaSwag shadow to replicate and then to be re-expressed through early layers that the teacher never touched. A function-space or steering-vector account allows partial transfer, and fitting random shuffle labels may hurt more than fitting structured ones, but a >1 pp effect from a layer-disjoint student is less likely than not.

judge_sol.reason: Disjoint trainable layers can still modify overlapping output functions, so parameter overlap need not be essential. However, recovering a late-layer capability change through early-layer updates using only off-task signs likely attenuates transfer relative to the matched student.

judge_luna.reason: The seed makes a recoverable HellaSwag shadow plausible, but does not test disjoint layer blocks. Late-only teacher quality and an early-only student's ability to express and generalize the change are separate risks, and the direct-supervision calibration does not resolve the latter.

judge_muse.reason: Early-only LoRAs should have capacity for HellaSwag and prior work localizes transfer to early layers, so a late-layer teacher's one-bit flips should remain learnable functionally with only modest attenuation below the matched late student.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: This is the seed paper. Every teacher and student it reports uses the same adaptation regime (all-linear LoRA into all-linear LoRA, or full SFT into full SFT). It never limits the teacher's update to one block of layers or trains the student on a disjoint block, so whether parameter overlap is needed is left open.

Shows that fine-tuning a single early layer is enough for subliminal trait transfer, but the teacher is system-prompted, so its update does not live in any parameters. The endpoint is a trait preference, not capability, and nothing checks transfer when the teacher's fine-tuned layers and the student's trainable layers are disjoint.

Gives the theory that, with shared initialization, student gradients align with the teacher's parameter update. It assumes both models train the same parameters and does not test disjoint parameter sets.

Localizes subliminal trait transfer to early-layer computation at shared context tokens and ties it to LoRA settings. It does not manipulate where the teacher's update lives and has no capability endpoint.

In a toy MNIST setup, shows subliminal transfer can survive mismatched or re-initialized hidden layers if the output heads are compatible. That is suggestive for a functional account, but it is not a language-model capability experiment with a layer-located fine-tuned teacher and a layer-disjoint LoRA student.

Tests layer freezing only as a way to mitigate trait transfer. It does not cross a layer-located teacher update with student layer sets, and it measures trait acquisition, not capability gains against a shuffle control.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I implemented: everything is in atd_layer/run_experiment.py, run by run_eval.sh. run_eval.sh pip-installs transformers 4.51.3, peft 0.15.2, datasets 3.6.0 and accelerate 1.6.0, then runs the whole registered pipeline in one process using Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct at the pinned revision in bf16:
- base HellaSwag scoring (sum of log-probs of the raw ctx plus ' '+ending, validation rows 0-3999)
- the 500-carrier sanity check
- the late-layer teacher (LoRA r16 on layers 14-27, 313 steps)
- the query over all 5,664 carriers
- 8 students: early or late layers × signal or shuffle × seeds 1 and 2, in the registered order
- the EARLY-DIRECT calibration run
- the bootstrap summary
For every run, parameter-name checks confirm that adapter parameters exist only in the allowed layers. The outputs are outputs/scores.jsonl, outputs/summary.json and /workspace/result.json.

Result of my one full test run (about 17 minutes of compute):
- **Registered statistic: +0.025 pp** (95% CI [-0.19, +0.24]; seed 1 0.00, seed 2 +0.05). This is below the 1.0 threshold, so the event did not occur.
- **The matched-layer gate failed:** late-signal minus late-shuffle was +0.11 pp, CI [-0.04, +0.26]. Under the registration this makes the experiment **inconclusive**: the late-layer teacher's shadow was not recoverable even by a student with matched layers, so the early-layer null cannot be read as evidence against transfer without parameter overlap.
- **Likely cause, inferred and not tested:** the teacher gap was small, +1.12 pp (base 45.23%, teacher 46.35%). The registered teacher recipe (313 steps of continuation cross-entropy, lr 1e-4) barely moves HellaSwag under this scoring.
- **EARLY-DIRECT gained +1.77 pp over base** (CI [0.92, 2.63]), so early-only layers can carry a gain of about that size under direct supervision.
- **Query:** 99.7% of carriers were retained. The flip rate against the released public_side was 49.5%.
- **The students did learn the teacher's labels:** final training loss was about 0.35 for signal students versus about 0.60 for shuffle students.

Caveats:
- The released near-tie margins did not reproduce here. On the first 500 carriers only 45% met |q-0.5|<=0.02 under my recomputation, and my base agreed with the released public_side only 61% of the time. That fits near-ties sitting within bf16 / software numerical noise, so the registered flip rate (measured against the released public_side) is close to uninformative.
- To address this I added a diagnostic: the flip rate against a locally recomputed base side. I added it after the full test run and checked it only with a short smoke run (where it read 21%, but for a barely trained teacher). The full-run value will appear only in the fresh evaluation run. No other code changed between the test run and submission.
- The fresh evaluation may differ slightly from these numbers because of GPU non-determinism.

Choices and deviations, all small:
1. The carriers are read from /workspace/seed/data, which is the same repo; it falls back to git clone only if those files are missing.
2. Hidden states are computed in bf16, but the final projection to vocabulary logits (lm_head) runs in fp32 for HellaSwag scoring and for the carrier argmax (the latter without TF32). This avoids exact bf16 ties between near-tie words; student training uses the seed's bf16 logits.
3. Student cross-entropy is computed from the logits at the last prompt position. This is the same quantity as cross-entropy at the single answer position with full-vocabulary normalisation.
4. Gradient checkpointing is off. This affects speed only.
5. The registration did not specify warmup for EARLY-DIRECT; I used 20 warmup steps then linear decay, as in the teacher recipe.
6. The teacher iterates through the 10,000 shuffled rows in order, in batches of 32. The final batch wraps 16 rows from the start.
7. The shuffle control uses np.random.default_rng(seed).permutation over the retained carriers. Signal and shuffle students with the same seed share data order and LoRA initialisation.
8. The bootstrap uses 10,000 item resamples, recomputing the mean over seeds of the paired difference each time.

registration.title: Shared-ancestor requirement, graded: does a private fine-tune's shadow still transfer to a student initialized from a sibling fine-tune of the same public ancestor?
registration.seed_connection: The seed paper requires the student to start from the exact public ancestor and reports (Appendix H) that transfer fails when the teacher's ancestor is an incompatible model, but the failing pairs differ in tokenizer, family and scale at once. The realistic threat and deployment case, a student that is a sibling descendant of the same ancestor (e.g. the public checkpoint received an unrelated fine-tune), is untested.
registration.hypothesis: A student initialized from M0 merged with an unrelated Alpaca LoRA fine-tune of the same size class as the teacher's update still gains more than 1 pp HellaSwag accuracy (signal minus shuffle) from the teacher's one-bit responses on M0's near-tie carriers.
registration.contribution: First graded test of the shared-initialization requirement within one lineage for capability transfer, with quantified drift (how many ancestor near-ties the sibling has left) and a direct comparison to the exact-ancestor student; informs both the attack surface of public-base services and the mechanism (whether alignment requires the exact parameter point or only lineage proximity).

closest_work.difference: Shows trait transfer fails between different base models; does not test siblings of the same base at controlled drift.
Appendix H tests only incompatible teachers (different family/scale/tokenizer); all successful students start from the exact ancestor.
Argues in an MNIST setting that matched initialization is unnecessary and output-head compatibility is what matters; no language model, no graded within-lineage drift.
Shows same-seed vs different-seed students differ in hidden-trait leakage in small Transformers on synthetic data; no LLM post-training update or capability endpoint.

inputs: Model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306, bf16
Carriers: git clone https://github.com/myboker/ATD; data/carriers.jsonl and data/alphabet.json
Target task: Hugging Face datasets 'Rowan/hellaswag'
Unrelated fine-tuning data for the sibling: Hugging Face datasets 'tatsu-lab/alpaca'
Python packages: torch (present), transformers, peft, datasets, accelerate
registration.method:
SETUP. Raw prompts, no chat template. (1) Sanity check on the first 500 carriers under the base: fraction with |q-0.5|<=0.02 and argmax in the pair. (2) HellaSwag scoring: context = row['ctx']; continuation = ' '+ending; score = sum of continuation-token log-probs; argmax of 4; accuracy on validation rows 0-3999; keep per-item 0/1 vectors. (3) TEACHER (private update of M0): LoRA r=16, alpha=16, dropout 0 on q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj of all layers, trained on the first 10,000 HellaSwag train rows after shuffling with seed 0 with CE on the correct continuation tokens; AdamW lr 1e-4, weight decay 0, effective batch 32, 313 steps, 20 warmup then linear decay, grad clip 1.0, bf16. Score base and teacher. (4) Query the teacher on all carriers: full-vocab argmax at the final position; retain iff in the pair; record side and flip; report retention and flip rate. (5) SIBLING INITIALIZATION M0': a separate LoRA with the same configuration trained on the first 8,000 rows of tatsu-lab/alpaca after shuffling with seed 0, prompt = 'Below is an instruction that describes a task. Write a response that appropriately completes the request.

### Instruction:
{instruction}

' + ('### Input:
{input}

' if input non-empty) + '### Response:
', target = output + eos, max length 512, loss on response tokens only, AdamW lr 1e-4, effective batch 32 (micro 8 x 4), 250 steps, 10 warmup then linear decay, grad clip 1.0; then merge_and_unload into the base weights in bf16 to obtain M0'. Drift diagnostics: HellaSwag accuracy of M0'; on the retained carriers, the pair-normalized probability under M0' and the fraction with |q'-0.5|>0.02 (ancestor near-ties the sibling no longer has); mean absolute change of the pair logit margin; fraction of carriers where M0' prefers the opposite word to M0. (6) Student recipe (ATD): fresh LoRA r=16/alpha=16/dropout 0 on the 7 module types of all layers, AdamW lr 5e-5, weight decay 0, micro-batch 32 x 4 = 128, 157 steps, 5 warmup then linear decay to 0, grad clip 1.0, bf16, full-vocabulary CE at the single answer position; seeds {1,2}; the shuffle control permutes teacher sides across carriers with the seed's RNG. The label set (teacher responses on M0's carriers) is identical for all students. ARMS: M0-SIGNAL, M0-SHUFFLE (students initialized from M0), SIB-SIGNAL, SIB-SHUFFLE (students initialized from M0'), 2 seeds each. Score base, teacher, M0', and all 8 students on the 4,000 items. Run order: sib-signal, sib-shuffle, m0-signal, m0-shuffle (seed 1), then the same for seed 2.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I implemented: the code is in sibexp/run_exp.py and run_eval.sh runs it. It follows the registered method. Base Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct at the pinned revision, raw prompts. HellaSwag scored as the sum of continuation-token log-probs on validation rows 0-3999. Teacher: a HellaSwag LoRA trained for 313 steps on 10k shuffled train rows. The teacher is queried with a full-vocabulary argmax on all 5,664 released carriers, keeping the answer only if it is one of the pair's two words. Sibling M0': an Alpaca LoRA trained for 250 steps (micro 8 x 4) and merged with merge_and_unload in bf16. The registered drift diagnostics are computed. Then 8 ATD students with fresh rank-16 LoRAs, lr 5e-5, 157 steps, effective batch 128, warmup 5 then linear decay. Arms are SIB/M0 x SIGNAL/SHUFFLE x seeds {1,2}, run in the registered order. The shuffle control permutes the teacher's sides across carriers with random.Random(seed). The statistic uses a 10,000-resample item bootstrap. The replication gate is checked, and if it fails the summary is flagged INCONCLUSIVE.

Deviations, all small:
1. Carrier forward passes run in float32 (bf16 weights upcast). These cover the sanity check, the teacher query and the sibling drift diagnostics. In bf16 inference only about 33-38% of the released carriers came out as near-ties; in fp32 the figure was 100% on a 200-carrier check and 97.7% over all carriers. All training and HellaSwag scoring stay in bf16.
2. The student batch of 128 is run as micro-batch 64 x accumulation 2 instead of 32 x 4. Each step is still the mean CE over 128 rows. The data order is a seeded index stream rather than a DataLoader.
3. The answer-token CE is computed from the final prompt position, with right padding and lm_head applied only to the needed positions. This is the same loss as single-token CE on the appended answer.
4. The teacher stays an unmerged LoRA.
5. HellaSwag is loaded from the refs/convert/parquet branch of Rowan/hellaswag.
6. Package versions are pinned: transformers 4.51.3, peft 0.15.2, datasets 3.6.0, accelerate 1.6.0.

Results from my one full run on this machine (about 25 minutes). A fresh run may differ slightly because of GPU non-determinism.
- Base 45.05%, teacher 47.23%: the teacher gap is only +2.18 pp, much smaller than in the paper (their base scores 64.84 under a different scoring setup).
- Teacher retention was 99.9%. Its flip rate against the base's pair choice was 50%, and it chose the right-hand word 72.5% of the time.
- M0' scored 44.73%. It moved far from the ancestor's decision boundaries: 92.5% of the retained near-ties were no longer near-ties (|q'-0.5| > 0.02), the mean absolute change in the pair logit margin was 0.68, and on 50% of carriers it preferred the opposite word to M0.
- Registered statistic: SIB-SIGNAL minus SIB-SHUFFLE = +0.64 pp (95% CI [0.32, 0.96]; per seed +0.55 and +0.73). This is below the 1.0 threshold, so in this run the registered event did not occur.
- Exact-ancestor transfer, M0-SIGNAL minus M0-SHUFFLE, was +0.54 pp (CI [0.16, 0.93]). The replication gate (> 1.0 pp) therefore failed, and summary.json flags the experiment INCONCLUSIVE.

How to read this: with a weak teacher, transfer is small even from the exact ancestor. The sibling-to-ancestor transfer ratio is 1.19. So, with only two seeds and overlapping intervals, the sibling student's small positive gain looks about as large as the ancestor student's. That does not show the two are equivalent, and because the gate failed, a failure of the sibling to clear 1 pp cannot be blamed on drift.

It was justified because bf16 reproduced only about a third of the released near-ties, while fp32 reproduced 97.7% with mean |q - released q| of 0.001.

registration.title: Capability or format? ATD transfer from a true-label HellaSwag teacher versus a self-labelled teacher trained with the identical recipe but no new task information
registration.seed_connection: The seed paper's multiple-choice transfers (0.8-2.9 pp) are measured against controls that destroy all teacher information (shuffle, exact-matched, public-label). None of its controls is a teacher that underwent the same post-training procedure and data format but acquired no capability, so format/sharpening drift that happens to help answer-likelihood scoring cannot be separated from capability transfer. The paper's own public-label control already shows carrier fine-tuning alone moves endpoints.
registration.hypothesis: The capability-specific component of transfer is real: the true-label teacher's students exceed their shuffle control by more than 1.5 pp more than the self-labelled (no new information) teacher's students exceed theirs.
registration.contribution: Adds the missing recipe-matched capability-free teacher control to ATD, decomposing behavioral-shadow transfer into a format/sharpening component and a capability component; a failure would mean the paper's MC transfer is largely procedure transfer, a success would strengthen the capability reading.

closest_work.difference: Its controls (shuffle, exact nuisance-matched, public-label, random-marginal) all remove teacher information; its non-elicitable teachers (memorized answers, cipher) change the content of the update, not the presence of capability at fixed procedure.

Shows teacher-free/self distillation improves accuracy via regularization in image classifiers; it does not ask whether a self-distilled teacher's off-task shadow transfers endpoint gains to another model.
Uses matched no-trait teacher controls for trait recoverability under data scaling; no capability endpoint and no near-tie carrier instrument.

inputs: Model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306, bf16
Carriers: git clone https://github.com/myboker/ATD; data/carriers.jsonl and data/alphabet.json
Target task: Hugging Face datasets 'Rowan/hellaswag'
Python packages: torch (present), transformers, peft, datasets, accelerate
registration.method: SETUP. Raw prompts, no chat template. (1) Sanity check on the first 500 carriers under the base: fraction with |q-0.5|<=0.02 and argmax in the pair. (2) HellaSwag scoring: context = row['ctx']; continuation = ' '+ending; score = sum of continuation-token log-probs; argmax of 4; accuracy on validation rows 0-3999; per-item 0/1 vectors. Training pool = first 10,000 train rows after shuffling with seed 0. (3) TEACHER A (true labels): LoRA r=16, alpha=16, dropout 0 on q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj of all layers; CE on the tokens of the correct ending given the context; AdamW lr 1e-4, weight decay 0, effective batch 32, 313 steps, 20 warmup then linear decay, grad clip 1.0, bf16. (4) TEACHER B (self-labelled, capability-free): first score the base model on the 10,000 training items with the same likelihood scoring and take its argmax ending as the label for each item (report base train accuracy); then train with exactly the recipe of Teacher A (same rows, same order, same hyperparameters, same seed) on these self-labels. Score base, Teacher A and Teacher B on the 4,000 validation items; report both gaps. (5) Query both teachers on all carriers: full-vocab argmax at the final position; retain iff in the pair; record side and flip per teacher; report retention and flip rate per teacher; on carriers retained by both, report side agreement and Cohen's kappa between the two teachers' flip indicators (diagnostic of how much of A's shadow is procedure-generic). (6) Student recipe (ATD): fresh LoRA r=16/alpha=16/dropout 0 on the 7 module types, AdamW lr 5e-5, weight decay 0, micro-batch 32 x 4 = 128, 157 steps, 5 warmup then linear decay to 0, grad clip 1.0, bf16, full-vocabulary CE at the single answer position; seeds {1,2}; a shuffle control permutes the respective teacher's sides across its retained carriers with the seed's RNG. ARMS: S_A (Teacher A responses), C_A (shuffle of A), S_B (Teacher B responses), C_B (shuffle of B), 2 seeds each. Score all 8 students on the 4,000 items. Run order: S_A, C_A, S_B, C_B for seed 1, then seed 2.

event.description: Transfer from the true-label teacher (S_A minus C_A) exceeds transfer from the recipe-matched self-labelled teacher (S_B minus C_B) by more than 1.5 percentage points of HellaSwag accuracy, averaged over two seeds.
event.statistic: [mean over seeds of accuracy(S_A) minus accuracy(C_A)] minus [mean over seeds of accuracy(S_B) minus accuracy(C_B)], in percentage points on the 4,000 HellaSwag validation items

evaluation.procedure: outputs/scores.jsonl: one JSON line per scored model {arm, teacher, seed, accuracy, n_items, correct: list of 4000 0/1} for base, Teacher A, Teacher B and the 8 students. outputs/summary.json: per-arm means; the registered statistic with a 95% CI from 10,000 bootstrap resamples of items (averaged over seeds); the two component transfers (S_A minus C_A and S_B minus C_B) each with CI; both teacher gaps; base train accuracy used for self-labels; retention, flip rates, cross-teacher side agreement and flip kappa; training losses; wall-clock per stage. Decision uses the point value of the statistic.
evaluation.controls: Each teacher has its own shuffle control so both transfers are measured against label-marginal-matched baselines. Teacher B is the key control: identical procedure, prompts, steps and seed, but labels carry no information beyond what the ancestor already expresses, so its shadow isolates format/sharpening drift. Gate: S_A minus C_A > 1.0 pp (otherwise the setting failed to replicate ATD and the result is flagged inconclusive). Teacher B's own gap is reported so that a nonzero S_B minus C_B can be interpreted in proportion to whatever accuracy self-distillation gave the teacher.

registration.full_scale_study: Recipe-matched capability-free teachers (self-labelled SFT, random-preference DPO for the code lineage) for all seven of the paper's tasks and for HumanEval+, with 3+ seeds and multiple acquisitions, decomposing every reported transfer into a procedure component and a capability component and testing whether the capability component scales with the teacher's gap while the procedure component does not.

agent.reason: I expect the true-label teacher to transfer more than the self-labelled one, but the registered contrast is a difference of differences (SE around 0.8 pp) against a 1.5 pp threshold, and some of the paper's MC transfer may indeed be procedure/sharpening transfer that the self-labelled teacher also carries.

judge_astra.reason: Self-labelled training is not capability-free: it can sharpen existing task-relevant knowledge and change domain calibration, potentially producing its own useful shadow. Relative to the seed’s roughly 2.9 pp total HellaSwag transfer, the required 1.5 pp residual is a demanding additional separation.

judge_fable.reason: The self-labelled teacher probably gains little accuracy and its shadow should transfer little, so the event reduces to the true-label transfer exceeding ~1.5-2 pp over its shuffle control; that is near the paper's reported HellaSwag effect and must survive a weaker teacher, a difference-of-differences noise of roughly 1 pp, and the heaviest pipeline (two teachers, 10k-item base scoring, 8 students).

judge_opus.reason: Both teachers share the procedure and agree on roughly half the labels, so their carrier shadows likely overlap heavily. The capability component is probably on the order of 1 pp, and the threshold applies to a noisy difference of differences estimated with two seeds. The run is also heavy because it needs two teachers and scoring 10k training items.

judge_sol.reason: True labels should contribute additional task-specific signal, but self-labelled training can also improve or expose latent capabilities rather than supplying a pure format-only control. The 1.5 pp difference-in-differences is consequently a demanding threshold, especially if this teacher recipe produces weaker transfer than the seed paper's.

judge_luna.reason: The seed's HellaSwag transfer of about 2.9 pp leaves room for the true-label teacher to exceed the self-labelled teacher by 1.5 pp. The pseudo-label teacher lacks gold corrective supervision, but training on the same examples could still create a transferable self-training or sharpening shadow, so the outcome is uncertain.

judge_muse.reason: True-label transfer was +2.90pp in the paper while self-distillation likely yields a small teacher gap and small shadow transfer, but the 1.5pp difference-of-differences threshold is high relative to noise over 4000 items and 2 seeds.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I implemented: exp/run_exp.py, launched by run_eval.sh. It installs transformers 4.56.2, peft 0.17.1, datasets 3.6.0 and accelerate 1.10.1. It follows the registered pipeline: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct at the pinned revision, bf16, raw prompts with no chat template. Steps:
- Sanity check on the first 500 carriers.
- HellaSwag scored as the sum of continuation log-probs on validation rows 0–3999. The training pool is the first 10k train rows after shuffling with seed 0.
- Teacher A uses the true labels. Teacher B uses the base model's own argmax labels. Both use the identical LoRA r16 recipe: lr 1e-4, batch 32, 313 steps, 20 warmup steps, seed 0, same rows in the same order.
- Both teachers are queried on all 5,664 carriers (full-vocabulary argmax, kept if the answer is in the pair).
- 8 ATD students (S_A, C_A, S_B, C_B × seeds 1 and 2) with the seed repo's student recipe. Each shuffle control permutes its own teacher's sides with the seed's RNG.
- Item bootstrap with 10k resamples.
It writes outputs/scores.jsonl (11 models), outputs/summary.json and result.json. Carriers are read from /workspace/seed/data; if that is missing, the script clones github.com/myboker/ATD.

Deviations (small, kept the question the same):
1) Carrier queries (base and both teachers) run in fp32 with TF32 off. In bf16 the logits are coarsely quantized: only 33% of the first 500 carriers came out as near-ties, and only 56% matched the released public side. In fp32 the q values match the released ones almost exactly (correlation 0.9999996), and the sanity check gives 100% near-tie and 100% argmax-in-pair. Training and HellaSwag scoring stay in bf16.
2) LoRA adapters are merged in fp32 and then cast to bf16 for scoring.
3) The lm_head is applied in fp32 when computing scoring log-probs.
4) For speed, logits are computed only at the needed positions (the answer position for students, the ending tokens for teachers). The loss is mathematically the same.
5) Flips are measured against our recomputed base pair-side. Flips against the released public_side are also reported; they are nearly identical.

Result from my full test run of this exact command (26.5 min of compute plus install; a fresh run may differ slightly because of GPU nondeterminism):
- Registered statistic = +0.20 pp (95% item-bootstrap CI [-0.08, +0.49]). The threshold is 1.5, so the event did not occur on the point value.
- Gate failed: S_A − C_A = +0.44 pp (CI [0.05, 0.83]), below the 1.0 pp gate. Per the registration, summary.json flags the result as INCONCLUSIVE: this setting did not replicate an ATD transfer of the paper's size.
- S_B − C_B = +0.24 pp (CI [-0.11, 0.59]).
- Teacher gaps: A +1.95 pp, B −1.50 pp. Base validation accuracy 45.15%, about 20 pp below the paper's reported HellaSwag base of 64.84; base train accuracy used for the self-labels 50.34%.
- Carrier diagnostics: retention 99.9% (A) and 100% (B); flip rates 0.50 (A) and 0.50 (B); side agreement between the two teachers 0.84; flip kappa 0.68. So most of A's carrier shadow is shared with the capability-free teacher B.

Interpretation: A's teacher gap here is much smaller than the paper's (+1.95 vs +22.3 pp). So this is weak evidence about the capability-vs-format split, not proof that the two components are equal. The non-significant difference between the A and B transfers does not establish that they are equivalent.

departures: exp/run_exp.py query_carriers: base and teacher carrier queries run in fp32 with TF32 off, while the registration says bf16. The weights come from bf16 merges and are upcast. The engineer reported this. It plausibly changes teacher sides and therefore student targets: under bf16 only about 33% of carriers were near-ties and about 56% matched the released public side. Without it the registered near-tie instrument and sanity check do not work, and the same procedure applies to both teachers. I treat it as needed for the registered experiment, not as a change to the question.
exp/run_exp.py train_teacher/train_student: LoRA adapters are merged in fp32, then the model is cast to bf16 for scoring. Reported. Numerical effect is minor; unlikely to change the conclusion.

exp/run_exp.py score_mc: lm_head and log-softmax run in fp32 on bf16 hidden states. Reported. This is a small numerical precision difference. It is unlikely to matter at the 0.2 pp scale relative to the 1.5 pp threshold.
exp/run_exp.py: logits are computed only at the needed positions. Reported. The loss is mathematically equivalent, so the result should not change.
exp/run_exp.py: flips are measured against the recomputed base pair-side. The registration does not define the flip reference. Reported. This affects diagnostics only, not the statistic.
exp/run_exp.py: TF32 matmul is enabled globally outside the carrier queries. Unreported. The effect on bf16 autocast training and scoring is negligible.
exp/run_exp.py: the shuffle permutation uses np.random.default_rng(seed). 'The seed's RNG' is left open by the registration. This is an allowed choice.
run_eval.sh: pins transformers 4.56.2, peft 0.17.1, datasets 3.6.0 and accelerate 1.10.1. Versions were left open, so this is not a departure in substance.
exp/run_exp.py load_hellaswag: has a fallback to the parquet conversion. The log shows parquet files loaded from Rowan/hellaswag with no failure message. The data are the same; no effect.
problems: outputs/summary.json: the registered gate failed (S_A−C_A = +0.44 pp, threshold 1.0 pp). By the registration's own rule the result is INCONCLUSIVE, and the summary flags it correctly. The setting did not reproduce an ATD transfer of the paper's size.
outputs/summary.json teacher_gaps_pp: Teacher A's gap is only +1.95 pp, against the +22.3 pp the engineer attributes to the paper. The capability signal available to transfer is therefore small.
outputs/summary.json teacher_gaps_pp: Teacher B's gap is −1.50 pp. B is capability-negative rather than capability-neutral, which muddies its role as a pure format/sharpening control.
Base HellaSwag accuracy under the registered unnormalised sum scoring is 45.15%, versus the 64.84 the engineer attributes to the paper. The endpoint is not comparable to the seed's.
outputs/summary.json: bootstrap CIs resample items only and ignore seed variance; there are only 2 seeds per arm. Transfer B varies across seeds (+0.10 vs +0.375 pp).
engineer_notes: the strong carrier-level overlap between teachers (side agreement 0.84, flip kappa 0.68) is a diagnostic, not a decomposition. Both flip rates are about 0.50 at near-ties.
full_run.out is an engineer-submitted earlier run. Its per-model scores match the protected evaluation exactly, which supports reproducibility but is not independent evidence.
opus.reason: The code implements the registered pipeline: the same pinned model, 4,000 validation items, a 10k pool, two teachers with an identical recipe and seed, eight students, per-teacher shuffle controls, and the registered statistic with an item bootstrap. The main departure, fp32 carrier querying, is disclosed and needed for the near-tie carrier instrument to function; it applies equally to both arms. The fresh evaluation produced real scores matching the engineer's run (statistic +0.20 pp, CI [−0.08, +0.49]). The event clearly did not occur, but the pre-registered gate failed (transfer A +0.44 pp < 1.0 pp), so by the registration's own rule this is inconclusive about the seed paper's capability-versus-format question. Teacher A's small gap and Teacher B's negative gap further limit what the null tells us, so the evidence is valid but weak.

departures: exp/run_exp.py, query_carriers: base and teacher carrier inference runs in fp32 with CUDA matmul TF32 disabled, rather than the registered bf16 setup. This can change near-tie argmaxes, retained carriers, student targets and consequently the registered statistic. The engineer's numerical justification does not establish that this change was necessary for execution.

exp/run_exp.py, train_teacher and train_student: adapters are merged into fp32 weights and the merged model is then rounded to bf16 before evaluation. Registration did not specify this numerical path. Although merging is mathematically equivalent before rounding, rounding merged weights can change logits, particularly near-tie carrier decisions, and could change the result.

exp/run_exp.py, score_mc: the hidden states and lm_head weights are promoted to fp32 for the output projection, with TF32 permitted, rather than using a bf16 output projection. This can change continuation likelihoods, base self-labels and scored accuracies, so it could affect the reported value.

exp/run_exp.py: logits are computed only at required ending-token or answer positions. This is an implementation optimization, not a substantive change to the registered loss or scoring rule; full-vocabulary logits are still used at those positions. No material effect on the result is expected.

exp/run_exp.py: flip diagnostics use recomputed base pair preferences rather than released public_side values; both versions are reported. Registration left the flip reference unspecified. This can change diagnostic flip rates and kappa slightly, but does not affect student targets or the registered statistic.

exp/run_exp.py: the base is queried on all carriers during setup, rather than only the first 500 needed for the registered sanity check. The required first-500 check is still reported, with additional all-carrier diagnostics. This does not plausibly change the reported value.
problems: exp/run_exp.py: the precision changes affect the experiment's near-tie instrument and potentially its endpoint scoring; they are not merely changes to logging or presentation.
outputs/summary.json: the registered replication gate failed. S_A minus C_A is 0.4375 pp, below the required greater-than-1.0-pp gate, so the registration calls for an inconclusive interpretation.

outputs/summary.json: Teacher A improves accuracy by only 1.95 pp, while Teacher B reduces it by 1.50 pp. These results limit interpretation as a comparison between substantial capability acquisition and an otherwise unchanged capability-free teacher.

registration: self-label training removes external correct-label supervision, but does not establish a pure format-only intervention. Both teachers receive task examples, and changing labels changes the training gradients; the transfer contrast does not by itself identify an additive capability-versus-format decomposition.

exp/run_exp.py, boot_ci: confidence intervals resample validation items conditional on the trained models. They do not capture teacher-acquisition variability or uncertainty across training seeds beyond the two fixed student seeds.

outputs/summary.json: high cross-teacher side agreement and flip kappa establish behavioral overlap, not its causal attribution to format or sharpening. Neither that overlap nor the transfer-difference interval establishes equivalence or absence of capability-specific transfer.
sol.reason: The fresh evaluation completed successfully, produced the required output files, and supports a registered statistic of +0.200 pp with a 95% item-bootstrap interval of [-0.075, 0.4875] pp. Fidelity is unfaithful because the explicit carrier-precision change can alter the near-tie labels driving student training, with additional numerical changes in merging and scoring. The evidence is valid for the implemented pipeline: the code computes the value from dataset examples and model outputs, and no leakage, hard-coded outcome or conclusion-changing calculation error is evident. Research value is limited because the replication gate failed and the teacher capability gain was small; this is credible local evidence, but not a supported decomposition of the seed paper's transfers or evidence of equivalence.
