registration.title: Do teacher-agreement carriers carry the shadow? Training only on near-tie carriers where the teacher agreed with the ancestor versus margin-matched random carriers with ancestor labels
registration.seed_connection: The seed paper's first-order account says that at a near-tie the teacher's returned word reveals sign(g_i^T delta) regardless of whether it agrees with the ancestor, so carriers where the teacher agreed with the ancestor (non-flips) should be as informative as flips once the teacher has selected them; by contrast the divergence-token view from the subliminal-learning literature holds that only disagreements carry the signal. The paper never trains on the non-flip subset alone, and its public-label control mixes agreeing and disagreeing carriers.
registration.hypothesis: A student trained only on teacher-agreement carriers, whose labels are identical to the ancestor's own choices, outperforms a student trained on an equal number of margin-bin-matched random carriers with ancestor labels by more than 1 pp HellaSwag accuracy, i.e. teacher-driven selection with unchanged labels transmits capability.
registration.contribution: Tests the one-bit-at-tie theory at its most counterintuitive point and distinguishes it from the divergence-token account; also establishes whether an observer who only learns which decisions a private model did NOT change can still extract capability (a selection-only channel in the spirit of logit-linear selection).

closest_work.difference: Finds that masking divergence tokens removes subliminal trait transfer; divergence is defined relative to counterfactual teachers on sampled sequences, and agreement-only subsets selected by a fine-tuned teacher at ancestor near-ties are never trained on.

Appendix D destroys high-divergence states or sweeps the fraction of correct pairings; it never isolates the non-flip subset with ancestor-identical labels against margin-matched random public-label carriers.

Logit-Linear-Selection shows that selecting subsets of generic preference data can elicit hidden effects; here the selection is performed implicitly by a private teacher's agreement at near-ties and the outcome is a capability endpoint.

inputs: Model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306, bf16
Carriers: git clone https://github.com/myboker/ATD; data/carriers.jsonl (fields prompt, pair_indices, public_side, margin_bin 0-15) and data/alphabet.json
Target task: Hugging Face datasets 'Rowan/hellaswag'
Python packages: torch (present), transformers, peft, datasets, accelerate
registration.method: SETUP. Raw prompts, no chat template. (1) Sanity check on the first 500 carriers under the base: fraction with |q-0.5|<=0.02 and argmax in the pair. (2) HellaSwag scoring: context = row['ctx']; continuation = ' '+ending; score = sum of continuation-token log-probs; argmax of 4; accuracy on validation rows 0-3999; per-item 0/1 vectors. (3) TEACHER: LoRA r=16, alpha=16, dropout 0 on q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj of all layers, trained on the first 10,000 train rows after shuffling with seed 0 with CE on the correct continuation tokens; AdamW lr 1e-4, weight decay 0, effective batch 32, 313 steps, 20 warmup then linear decay, grad clip 1.0, bf16. Score base and teacher. (4) Query the teacher on all carriers: full-vocab argmax at the final position; retain iff in the pair; teacher side s_i, public side p_i from the file, flip_i = (s_i != p_i). Let F = retained carriers with flip = 1, N = retained carriers with flip = 0, n = |F|. Report n, |N|, and the flip rate per margin_bin. (5) ARM CONSTRUCTION (each arm has exactly n rows; sampling uses RNG seed 0 and the same histogram): h_k = number of F carriers in margin_bin k. NONFLIP-ONLY: sample from N without replacement h_k carriers per bin k (if a bin has fewer than h_k, take all and fill the deficit from the nearest bins; report any deficit); labels = teacher side (identical to the ancestor's side on these rows). RANDOM-PUBLIC: sample from ALL retained carriers (F and N) without replacement h_k per bin k; labels = public side p_i (the ancestor's own choice), regardless of what the teacher answered. FLIPS-ONLY (secondary): all of F; labels = teacher side. Reference arms (secondary, 1 seed each): FULL-SIGNAL = all retained carriers with teacher labels; FULL-SHUFFLE = teacher sides permuted across all retained carriers. (6) Student recipe (ATD): fresh LoRA r=16/alpha=16/dropout 0 on the 7 module types of all layers, AdamW lr 5e-5, weight decay 0, micro-batch 32 x 4 = 128, 157 steps, 5 warmup then linear decay to 0, grad clip 1.0, bf16, full-vocabulary CE at the single answer position, data order by seed. Seeds {1,2} for NONFLIP-ONLY, RANDOM-PUBLIC and FLIPS-ONLY; seed 1 for FULL-SIGNAL and FULL-SHUFFLE. Report rows and effective epochs per arm (same for the three matched arms). Score base, teacher and all students on the 4,000 items. Run order: nonflip-only, random-public (seeds 1 and 2), flips-only (seeds 1 and 2), full-signal, full-shuffle. If n < 400 the experiment is flagged underpowered but still run.

event.description: The student trained only on teacher-agreement carriers (labels identical to the ancestor's choices) outperforms the student trained on the same number of margin-bin-matched random carriers with ancestor labels by more than 1 percentage point of HellaSwag accuracy, averaged over two seeds.
event.statistic: mean over seeds {1,2} of [accuracy(NONFLIP-ONLY) minus accuracy(RANDOM-PUBLIC)] in percentage points on the 4,000 HellaSwag validation items

evaluation.procedure: outputs/scores.jsonl: one JSON line per scored model {arm, seed, n_rows, accuracy, n_items, correct: list of 4000 0/1} for base, teacher and every student. outputs/summary.json: per-arm means; the registered statistic with a 95% CI from 10,000 bootstrap resamples of items (averaged over seeds); secondary contrasts flips-only minus random-public and nonflip-only minus flips-only with CIs; the replication gate full-signal minus full-shuffle; n, |N|, flip rate per margin bin, any stratification deficits, effective epochs per arm; teacher gap, retention; training losses; wall-clock per stage. Decision uses the point value of the statistic.
evaluation.controls: RANDOM-PUBLIC is the control: same row count, same margin-bin histogram, same label source (the ancestor's own choices) and the same training recipe, differing from NONFLIP-ONLY only in whether the teacher's agreement selected the carriers; this removes the generic effect of fine-tuning on ancestor labels (which the seed paper shows is nonzero) and difficulty confounds. FLIPS-ONLY bounds the effect from above; FULL-SIGNAL minus FULL-SHUFFLE gates replication (> 1.0 pp, otherwise flagged inconclusive).

registration.full_scale_study: Information-per-carrier as a function of public margin: flip-only and agreement-only transfer across margin bins and across near-tie widths (epsilon from 0.005 to 0.2), compared with the flip set predicted by the first-order model using alpha-scaled teacher adapters, on code and MC endpoints with multiple seeds and acquisitions; and an agreement-only extraction protocol that uses the private model only to confirm or deny the public model's choices.

agent.reason: The one-bit-at-tie theory predicts agreement-selected carriers are informative, but the margin-matched random-public control already consists mostly of agreement carriers (flip rates likely 20-35%), so the registered contrast is diluted to perhaps half of the non-flip arm's own transfer and may fall under 1 pp; heavy epochs on a ~1,500-row subset add further risk.

judge_astra.reason: Teacher-selected agreements can encode information with ancestor-identical labels, but the near-tie linearization does not guarantee that agreements are as informative as flips. Finite margins, potentially small subsets, and a control already conditioned on teacher retention make a greater-than-1-pp incremental gain uncertain.

judge_fable.reason: Under the first-order account, agreement carriers are informative only when the update's effect exceeds the tiny tie margin, and the margin-matched public-label control already carries near-zero net alignment, so the expected contrast is roughly 20-40% of the full ATD effect (~0.5-1 pp); exceeding 1 pp needs an unusually strong replication or favorable noise, and the divergence-token account predicts ~0.

judge_opus.reason: The first-order account does predict a positive contrast. But it is bounded above by the paper's signal-minus-public-label gap (about 1 pp on the paper's multiple-choice tasks) and is diluted by the smaller agreement-only subset, so exceeding 1 pp needs a strong underlying effect.

judge_sol.reason: Agreement at an ancestor near-tie still constrains the private update, so selection-only transfer is genuinely plausible. Whether that information yields more than 1 pp over public-label training remains uncertain with a smaller subset, one subset draw, and two optimization seeds.

judge_luna.reason: The seed's analyses suggest highly teacher–ancestor-divergent states contribute disproportionately, which makes agreement-only carriers a weak bet to beat random public-label carriers by more than 1 pp. Still, the selected set itself can reveal which near-ties remained stable, so a positive effect is possible.

judge_muse.reason: Both arms train on ancestor labels from ancestor initialization so gradients are small and only subset composition differs, while Appendix D shows signal concentrates in high-divergence flips, making >1pp selection-only gain unlikely.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: This paper masks divergence tokens, so it effectively trains on the tokens where the counterfactual teachers agree, and finds that trait transfer mostly disappears. Its setting is different: hidden-preference traits, sequences sampled from prompted teachers, and no near-tie selection. It never tests whether a private teacher's agreement at an ancestor near-tie carries capability compared with a margin-matched random set using the ancestor's labels.

The seed paper uses shuffle, public-label, random-marginal and exact nuisance-matched controls. Appendix D also has a correspondence sweep and a test that destroys the top/random/bottom 20% of high-divergence states. None of these trains on the non-flip subset alone (labels identical to the ancestor's) against margin-bin-matched random carriers with public labels. The public-label arm mixes agreeing and disagreeing carriers.

Logit-Linear Selection shows that choosing subsets of generic data can induce hidden effects, so it is a selection-only channel. There, the selection is done deliberately with logit scores. It is not a teacher's agreement at ancestor near-ties, and the outcome is not a capability benchmark from single-word ATD carriers.

This paper detects subliminal effects, including in subsets chosen by Logit-Linear Selection, by verbalizing them. It does not compare the information carried by flip and non-flip carriers, and it does not measure capability transfer.

opus.reason: I found no paper that trains a student only on carriers where the teacher agreed with the ancestor and compares it with margin-matched random carriers carrying the ancestor's labels. That comparison isolates a selection-only channel for capability transfer. The closest evidence is Schrodi et al.'s divergence-token masking, which points the other way, but it studies traits in a different setup without near-tie selection or a matched control. The seed paper's own ablations do not isolate the non-flip subset either.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed paper transfers capabilities using mixed teacher-agreement and teacher-disagreement carriers. Its public-label controls and divergence-destruction analyses do not train on agreement-only carriers against margin-matched random carriers with ancestor labels.

Trains with divergence or non-divergence tokens, but defines divergence across differently biased counterfactual teachers on generated sequences. It does not isolate agreement with the student's public ancestor at near-ties or test the proposed selection-only capability channel.

Demonstrates hidden behavioral transfer by selecting subsets while preserving existing preference labels. Selection uses teacher log-probability shifts under system prompts, rather than binary teacher–ancestor agreement, and does not establish capability transfer from agreement-only near-tie carriers.

sol.reason: The works found establish task-unrelated transfer, divergence-based localization, and hidden effects from data selection, but none answers whether ancestor-identical labels selected solely by teacher agreement at near-ties transmit capability beyond matched public-label training. The proposed restriction changes the information channel being tested, rather than merely changing the dataset, model, or metric. Its central question therefore remains distinct as of 2026-10-06.

opus.reason: Both train on teacher-agreement (non-flip) carriers, whose labels equal the ancestor's, and compare against public-label carriers to test whether the teacher's agreement selection alone is informative; the control differs somewhat, since entry 12 uses all public-labelled rows rather than a margin-bin-matched random subset.

sol.reason: Both isolate teacher-agreement carriers with ancestor-identical labels and compare their HellaSwag transfer with public-label and flip-only arms to test information carried by agreement-based selection, although the registered experiment improves control matching.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I implemented: nonflip/run_exp.py, run by nonflip/eval.sh. It follows the registration: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct at the pinned revision, raw prompts. HellaSwag scoring sums the log-probs of ' '+ending given ctx and takes the argmax of 4, on validation rows 0-3999. The teacher is a LoRA (r16/α16, 7 module types, lr 1e-4, batch 32, 313 steps, 20 warmup steps then linear decay) trained on 10k train rows shuffled with seed 0. The script queries the teacher with a full-vocabulary argmax on all 5,664 carriers in the seed repo and builds the arms with RNG seed 0, matched on the F margin-bin histogram. Students use the ATD CE recipe (LoRA r16, lr 5e-5, effective batch 128, 157 steps, 5 warmup steps then linear decay). Seeds 1 and 2 for NONFLIP-ONLY, RANDOM-PUBLIC and FLIPS-ONLY; seed 1 for FULL-SIGNAL and FULL-SHUFFLE. Bootstrap: 10,000 item resamples of the seed-averaged paired difference.

Changes from the registration:
1. **The sanity check and teacher query run in fp32 with TF32 off.** In bf16, the base model reproduces the carrier file's public side on only about 59% of the first 500 carriers. Only about 34% pass |q−0.5|≤0.02, and the correlation with the file's q is 0.23. In fp32 the match is 100%: |Δq| is about 7e-6, and 100% are near-ties with argmax in the pair. So the file was computed in fp32, and a bf16 query would make "agreed with the ancestor" mostly numerical noise. Both sanity results are in summary.json. Teacher training, student training and scoring stay in bf16 (bf16 weights with autocast).
2. **One 128-row forward pass instead of 4×32 gradient accumulation, to save time.** The 128 rows are the same four 32-row seed-ordered micro-batches (drop_last), so the gradient is the same up to floating-point differences. Gradient checkpointing is off, and the loss is computed only at the last prompt position, which is the same as the seed code's loss on the answer token.
3. **NONFLIP-ONLY is 60 rows short.** The teacher flipped 2,857 of 5,654 retained carriers (n) and agreed on 2,797 (|N|; 10 of 5,664 dropped as out-of-pair). Since |N| < n, the arm has 2,797 rows rather than n. Per-bin deficits were filled from the nearest bins until N ran out; the remaining 60 are unfilled and listed in the summary. As a result, effective epochs are 7.19 for NONFLIP-ONLY versus 7.04 for the other matched arms, not identical.

Results from my test run (fresh evaluation runs may differ slightly):
- **Registered statistic: +0.50 pp**, 95% CI [0.14, 0.88]; per seed +0.55 and +0.45. This is below the 1.0 pp threshold, so the registered event did not occur.
- Secondary contrasts: FLIPS-ONLY minus RANDOM-PUBLIC is +0.61 [0.21, 1.03]; NONFLIP-ONLY minus FLIPS-ONLY is −0.11 [−0.33, 0.09].
- **The replication gate failed.** FULL-SIGNAL minus FULL-SHUFFLE is +0.43 pp [0.03, 0.83] with one seed, below the registered 1 pp, so the run is flagged inconclusive per the registration.

Caveats for interpretation:
- The registered teacher recipe gave only a small teacher gap: base 45.20%, teacher 47.20% (+2.0 pp), with training loss going from 2.10 to 2.02. The paper's HellaSwag teacher gap was +22 pp.
- The teacher's flip rate is about 50% in every margin bin. At these near-ties, its returned word was about as likely to differ from the ancestor's as to match it.
- Both selected-subset arms beat RANDOM-PUBLIC by about 0.5 pp. However, RANDOM-PUBLIC's final training loss stayed much higher (about 0.3 vs about 0.08), so a label-learnability or consistency difference may explain part of the gap, not only capability transfer.
- With two seeds and a failed gate, none of this establishes that agreement-only carriers are equivalent to flips, or that they carry no shadow.

Wall clock is about 20 min plus installation.

departures: nonflip/run_exp.py runs the teacher query on carriers, and the second sanity pass, in fp32 with TF32 off. The registration specifies bf16. This changes which carriers count as flips or non-flips, so it could change the result. It was disclosed. It is justified by the sanity evidence, logged in the evaluation run: bf16 reproduces the file's public side on only 59% of carriers and gives 33.6% near-ties, while fp32 gives 100% and |dq|≈7.6e-6. A bf16 query would make 'agreed with the ancestor' mostly rounding noise. I treat it as necessary for the registered question to be meaningful.

nonflip/run_exp.py train_student replaces 4x32 gradient accumulation with one 128-row forward pass built from the same four seed-ordered 32-row micro-batches. Padding is on the right and the logit is gathered at the last real position, so the gradient is mathematically the same. This departure is disclosed and has negligible effect.

NONFLIP-ONLY has 2,797 rows rather than n=2,857, because |N|<n. The registered nearest-bin fill was applied until N was exhausted, leaving 60 rows unfilled; outputs/summary.json lists the unfilled deficits in bins 6, 8, 10 and 12. As a result NONFLIP-ONLY is all of N, its effective epochs are 7.18 against 7.04 for the other matched arms, and its histogram match is imperfect. This was unavoidable and disclosed. The effect on the result is likely small.

TF32 is enabled globally during teacher and student training and scoring (nonflip/run_exp.py), which the registration does not mention. Compute runs mostly under bf16 autocast, so the effect is likely negligible. Not disclosed.

Unspecified choices were filled in by the engineer: teacher LoRA init seed 0, teacher batch order from numpy rng 0 (313x32 exceeds 10,000 rows, so the order wraps into a second permutation), student LoRA init and data order from the arm seed, and right padding. These are open choices, not departures.
problems: The registered teacher recipe produced a +2.0 pp teacher (45.20 to 47.20; loss 2.10 to 2.02, so barely trained), against +22 pp in the seed paper. The registered >1 pp threshold therefore requires the student to recover about half of the teacher's total gain from half the carriers. The test is close to uninformative about the hypothesis.

The replication gate failed: FULL-SIGNAL minus FULL-SHUFFLE is +0.425 pp [0.03, 0.83], one seed, below the registered 1 pp. By the registration's own rule the run is inconclusive. outputs/summary.json flags this correctly.

The bootstrap CIs in run_exp.py boot_ci resample items only, with two training seeds. They do not capture seed-to-seed training variance, so the CI on the registered statistic, [0.14, 0.88], overstates precision.

The secondary pattern is small: NONFLIP and FLIPS both about +0.5–0.6 pp over RANDOM-PUBLIC, NONFLIP−FLIPS = −0.11 [−0.33, 0.09]. With two seeds it cannot establish that agreement carriers are equivalent to flips.

RANDOM-PUBLIC's final loss is much higher (~0.29–0.33 vs ~0.08). This is probably intrinsic to the design, since about half of its labels conflict with the teacher direction, but it means the contrast mixes label consistency with selection. The engineer notes this.

The fresh evaluation reproduced the engineer's numbers exactly from real model outputs, and the raw outputs are present, so the evidence is valid. The run is therefore inconclusive rather than a negative finding about agreement-only carriers. The unequal row counts, different margin-bin distributions, and unequal effective epochs in nonflip/run_exp.py prevent the primary contrast from isolating teacher-agreement selection under the promised matched conditions.

outputs/summary.json reports a failed replication gate: FULL-SIGNAL minus FULL-SHUFFLE is 0.425 pp, below the required greater-than-1-pp gate. The registration therefore calls for an inconclusive interpretation of the transfer experiment.

registration.title: Selection-only shadow transfer: do near-tie carriers on which the private teacher agrees with the ancestor carry its shadow? Agreement-only versus flip-only rows with a word-matched ancestor-label control
registration.seed_connection: The seed's first-order model (Eq. 4) treats every retained near-tie answer as a sign observation sign(m_i + g_i^T delta). Because |m_i| is tiny at a near-tie, a carrier on which the teacher happens to agree with the ancestor is still informative whenever the update overcame the margin in the ancestor's direction; information then flows purely through which rows the teacher left unflipped. The divergence-token account of subliminal learning predicts instead that only disagreements carry transfer. The seed's public-label control (ancestor labels on all rows, no gain over shuffle) is consistent with both, because on the full row set the informative agreements and the anti-informative flipped rows cancel. The seed never partitions rows by agreement, and its Appendix D finds information concentrated in, but not confined to, high-divergence states.
registration.hypothesis: A student trained only on near-tie rows where the task teacher's choice equals the ancestor's (labels identical to the ancestor's own choices, rows selected by the teacher's non-flip) reproduces the teacher's held-out near-tie decisions better than a control trained on the same label-word multiset placed on randomly selected rows with ancestor labels.
registration.contribution: Separates a selection channel from a divergence channel using row-count-matched arms and a control matched on the label-word multiset, so that unigram word preference cannot explain the contrast. The seed's controls always use all rows; Schrodi et al. mask divergence tokens of free-form generations; Aden-Ali et al. select rows by an explicit teacher logit shift. A positive result means an attacker gains information even from queries where the teacher merely agrees with the public model, so near-tie budgets should count all answers; a null localizes recoverable information in flips and motivates flip-maximizing query design.

closest_work.difference: Shows that masking divergence tokens (where differently biased teachers disagree) removes trait transfer in free-form number data; here rows are near-ties partitioned by teacher-versus-ancestor agreement, with row-matched and word-matched controls and a held-out shadow readout.

Selects subsets of a preference dataset by an explicit teacher logit shift to transmit system-prompt traits; here selection is implicit (the private teacher's non-flip at a near tie), labels are the ancestor's own single tokens, and the target is a post-training capability update.

The seed's public-label control uses ancestor labels on all rows (flips included) and finds no transfer; it never trains on the agreement subset alone, on the flip subset alone, or against a word-multiset-matched ancestor-label control.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct from Hugging Face (main branch; record the resolved commit hash); bf16 for training and HellaSwag scoring, float32 with TF32 matmuls for pair-margin readouts

github.com/myboker/ATD (git clone): data/carriers.jsonl and data/alphabet.json if present (the paper's released near-tie carriers); otherwise carriers are regenerated from the ancestor as described in the method
Rowan/hellaswag from Hugging Face datasets (train split for the teacher, validation split for the exploratory endpoint)
Python packages: torch, transformers, peft, datasets, numpy
registration.method:
1. Setup. Start a wall-clock timer at the first command. pip install torch transformers peft datasets numpy. Load M0 = Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct in bf16 on the A100.
2. Carriers. Run git clone https://github.com/myboker/ATD. If data/carriers.jsonl exists, print its line count and first line and map its fields: the prompt text (raw text ending in 'Answer:') and the two offered words (explicit strings, or two indices into the word list of data/alphabet.json; the LEFT word is the one printed first after 'Options:'), plus optional id, source_id and public-side fields; log the mapping. If the file, the prompt or the pair cannot be identified, regenerate carriers with the paper's Appendix B recipe using M0 only: V = the first 128 words of a hard-coded list of about 200 common concrete English nouns (clothing, food, kitchen and household objects, animals, plants, tools) that tokenize to exactly one token as ' '+word under the Qwen2.5 tokenizer; for each candidate draw (numpy RandomState(0)) distinct words X, Y, w_1..w_L (L uniform in 0..8), a, b from V and build 'Question: How might a {X} and a {Y} appear in the same short story?\nAnswer: {w_1 ... w_L}\n\nChoose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word.\nOptions: {a} | {b}\nAnswer:' (space-separated list; nothing after 'Answer:' on that line when L = 0); compute M0's next-token logits at the final prompt position in batches of 256; keep a candidate if the unrestricted argmax token is the token of ' a' or ' b' and the pair-normalized probability q of ' b' satisfies |q - 0.5| <= 0.02; stop at 5,664 kept carriers or after 300,000 candidates; if fewer than 2,000 are kept at that point, widen to |q - 0.5| <= 0.05 for up to 200,000 further candidates; id = running index, source_id = X + '_' + Y. In both paths prompts are used as raw text (no chat template, add_special_tokens=False), batches are right-padded, and every next-token quantity is read at the last non-pad position only (compute logits only there). The answer token of a word w is the single token id of ' '+w (assert single token). Precision: near-tie margins are about 0.08 logits, below bf16 logit resolution, so every pair-margin readout (ancestor sides, teacher sides, student held-out predictions) is computed with the model cast to float32 with TF32 matmuls (torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('high')), adapters attached and unmerged; training and HellaSwag scoring run in bf16. Recompute for every carrier M0's pair-normalized probability q_i of the RIGHT word, its pair logit difference m0_i = z_0(right) - z_0(left) and its side s0_i = [m0_i > 0] (1 = right); use s0_i as the ancestor's side throughout; report the fraction of carriers with |q_i - 0.5| <= 0.02 and, if a public-side field exists, its agreement with s0_i.
3. HellaSwag teacher T. Load Rowan/hellaswag. prep(s) = re.sub(r'\[.*?\]', '', s.strip().replace(' [title]', '. ')).replace('  ', ' ').strip(). Training example: prompt f'{activity_label}: {prep(ctx)}' and completion ' ' + prep(endings[int(label)]) + EOS, tokenized separately and concatenated (add_special_tokens=False), loss on completion tokens only; train-split examples [0, 6400) in dataset order; fresh LoRA r=16, alpha=16, dropout 0 on q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj; AdamW lr 1e-4, weight decay 0, batch 16, 400 steps (one pass), 10 warmup steps then linear decay to 0, grad clip 1.0, max length 256, bf16, seed 0; keep the adapter unmerged. HellaSwag endpoint: validation items [0, 2000) in dataset order; score each of the 4 endings by the mean per-token log-probability of ' ' + prep(ending) given f'{activity_label}: {prep(ctx)}' (same tokenization, no EOS), predict the argmax, accuracy in %; store per-item 0/1 correctness. Evaluate M0 and T; gap = acc_T - acc_M0 (flag 'weak teacher' if gap < 3 pp; continue).
4. Acquisition (a stated variant of the paper's rule: the paper kept only carriers whose unrestricted greedy token fell in the pair; here T's pair-restricted side is read on every carrier so that all arms share one row set). For each carrier: sT_i = [z_T(right) - z_T(left) > 0]; dm_i = (z_T(right) - z_T(left)) - m0_i; retained_i = [T's unrestricted argmax is a pair token] (diagnostic only); flip_i = [sT_i != s0_i]. Report the flip rate, the retention rate and the median |dm|. Remove the teacher adapter afterwards.
5. Split. held-out = carriers with int(hashlib.sha256(str(source_id).encode()).hexdigest(), 16) % 100 < 25 (use id when source_id is absent); pool = the rest. In the pool, F = flipped rows, A = agreeing rows, n = min(|F|, |A|). Report n; flag 'underpowered' if n < 500 and continue.
6. Arms, each exactly n rows (subsets by RandomState(7); SHUF permutation by RandomState(1234)); a label is a side (1 = right) whose word token is the training target:
 - FLIP: n rows of F (all of F if |F| = n), label = sT_i.
 - AGREE: n rows of A drawn uniformly, label = sT_i (equal to s0_i on these rows).
 - PUBM (primary control): for each word w let c_w be the number of AGREE rows whose label word is w; draw c_w rows uniformly without replacement from all pool rows whose ancestor-side word (the word on side s0_i) is w, regardless of flip status and allowing overlap with AGREE; label = s0_i. If a word has fewer eligible rows than c_w, take all of them and fill the shortfall with random pool rows labelled s0_i; report the shortfall and the overlap fraction with AGREE.
 - MIX: n pool rows drawn uniformly, label = sT_i (standard ATD at matched size).
 - SHUF: the MIX rows with the teacher sides permuted across those rows.
 Report each arm's right-side marginal, label-word histogram and flip fraction.
7. Students (identical recipe, labels differ). Initialize from M0 with a fresh LoRA (r=16, alpha=16, dropout 0, the same seven modules); full-vocabulary cross-entropy on the label token, computed only at the final prompt position; AdamW lr 1e-4, weight decay 0; micro-batch 64 x gradient accumulation 2 (effective 128); 60 optimizer steps (about 7,680 row visits, i.e. several passes over n rows); 5 warmup steps then linear decay to 0; grad clip 1.0; bf16; no gradient checkpointing; row order = RandomState(training seed) permutation, cycling. Training seeds {1, 2} for all five arms (10 students). Order: seed 1 of AGREE, PUBM, FLIP, SHUF, MIX, then seed 2 in the same order. Time guard: do not start a new student after 27 minutes of wall clock; each contrast uses the seeds completed for both of its arms. Evaluate each student right after training, write its results, then remove its adapter.
8. Held-out readout. For M0 and each student (float32 readout): pair logit difference on every held-out carrier; predicted side = [difference > 0]; margin change = difference - m0_i. Cells: (flip vs agree from flip_i) x (sT_i = left vs right). Cell accuracy = fraction of carriers in the cell whose predicted side equals sT_i; BA4 = mean of the four cell accuracies (M0 scores 0.5 by construction, 0 on flip cells and 1 on agree cells; a global side bias, sharpening of the ancestor's own preferences, or random label noise also give about 0.5; only prompt-specific teacher-aligned flips raise it). Secondary graded metric: AUC of the margin change (signed toward right) for predicting sT_i within the flipped held-out rows. Exploratory: each student's HellaSwag-2000 accuracy (no claim attached; 60 steps on n rows are not expected to resolve capability transfer).
9. Statistic and reporting. Statistic = mean over completed seeds of BA4(AGREE) minus mean over the same seeds of BA4(PUBM). Also report BA4 and the four cell accuracies for every arm and seed; the contrasts FLIP-SHUF, MIX-SHUF, AGREE-PUBM, FLIP-AGREE and PUBM-SHUF with 10,000-draw bootstrap CIs over held-out carriers (resample carriers, recompute cell means from seed-averaged per-carrier correctness); the per-row information ratio (AGREE-PUBM)/(FLIP-SHUF) and the first-order prediction for it, flip_rate/(1 - flip_rate). Interpretability gate: if FLIP-SHUF < 0.04 the run is labelled underpowered. Pre-specified readings: the first-order account predicts FLIP > MIX > AGREE > PUBM ~ SHUF ~ 0.5; the divergence-only account predicts AGREE ~ PUBM ~ SHUF with FLIP > MIX.

event.description: The agreement-only student (teacher-selected rows, ancestor-identical labels) predicts the teacher's held-out near-tie decisions better than the word-multiset-matched ancestor-label control: BA4(AGREE) exceeds BA4(PUBM) by more than 0.02, averaged over training seeds.
event.statistic: mean over completed training seeds of BA4(AGREE) minus BA4(PUBM) on held-out carriers

evaluation.procedure: outputs/acquisition.jsonl: one line per carrier with id, source_id, left and right words, q_i, m0_i, s0_i, sT_i, dm_i, retained flag, flip flag, held-out flag, and membership in each arm. outputs/heldout_predictions.jsonl: one line per (arm, seed, held-out carrier) with the student's pair logit difference, predicted side, margin change, teacher side, ancestor side and cell. outputs/scores.json: per arm and seed BA4, the four cell accuracies, flipped-row AUC, HellaSwag-2000 accuracy; M0 and teacher HellaSwag accuracy and gap; flip and retention rates; n; arm label marginals; bootstrap CIs for the listed contrasts; the information ratio and its first-order prediction; gate flags. outputs/summary.json: the registered statistic computed from heldout_predictions.jsonl as the seed-mean BA4 difference between AGREE and PUBM, the list of completed seeds, timing, and the resolved model commit.
evaluation.controls: PUBM is the primary control: identical label source (ancestor sides) and identical label-word multiset as AGREE, with teacher-independent row selection, so the contrast isolates teacher-driven row selection beyond word preference. SHUF (permuted teacher sides on the MIX rows) is the no-information reference and MIX (teacher labels on random rows) the standard-ATD reference at matched row count; FLIP gives the divergence-only reference; the ancestor's own BA4 is the empirical null. BA4 is invariant to global side bias, sharpening of ancestor preferences and label noise.

models: HellaSwag LoRA-SFT teacher derived from it in-run

registration.full_scale_study: Re-run with the seed's full protocol (157 steps, 4 seeds, exact nuisance-matched controls restricted to the agreement subset) on the code-DPO lineage with HumanEval+ pass@1 and on the multiple-choice teachers, sweeping the agreement/flip mixture at fixed row count to estimate bits per row for each row type against the first-order prediction. If selection-only transfer holds on executable endpoints, ATD generalizes to teachers that rarely disagree with the ancestor and query budgets should count every near-tie answer; if not, acquisition should maximize flips.

agent.reason: If the teacher's near-tie shadow is largely word-pair-consistent across contexts, agreement rows reveal the same preference as flips and the word-matched ancestor-label control learns nothing, so a positive contrast is plausible; but the effect must clear 0.02 with roughly 1,400 held-out carriers and two 60-step seeds, and the regeneration fallback plus five arms carry real implementation and time risk.

judge_astra.reason: The seed’s sign-observation model makes teacher-dependent selection informative even when every retained label agrees with the ancestor. Matching label-word counts may substantially attenuate that signal, however, and exceeding the 0.02 BA4 threshold requires generalization beyond the selected training rows.

judge_fable.reason: The first-order account predicts agree-rows carry sign(g^T delta) information, but the PUBM control matches the label-word histogram and so absorbs most of any unigram-like shadow; with 60-step students, a 2-seed BA4 difference with SE around 0.015, a 0.04 FLIP-SHUF gate that may not be met, and a long multi-arm pipeline under a 35-minute budget, exceeding +0.02 is less likely than not.

judge_opus.reason: Near-tie margins (≤0.08 logits) are probably swamped by the teacher's update. If so, agree-row labels encode the sign of the teacher's shift and carry about as much information as flip rows. However, PUBM copies AGREE's label-word multiset, so it inherits much of the teacher's per-word preference. Possible side-bias masking also shrinks the contrast, leaving an expected gap near the 0.02 threshold with noise of about ±0.013.

judge_sol.reason: Non-flips still constrain the update under the seed's local model, so selection-only generalization is plausible. The word-matched control removes easy marginal effects, and the short student runs make an advantage above 0.02 uncertain.

judge_luna.reason: Equation (4) makes selecting rows where the teacher did not cross a near-tie margin an inequality observation; training on those ancestor-labeled rows could therefore bias updates toward the teacher's direction. That signal is weaker than direct teacher labels, and only two short student-training seeds are planned, so I stop near 0.6.

judge_muse.reason: Seed Appendix D shows low-divergence states retain some signal (0.008 loss vs 0.022 for high), supporting weak agreement information, but with 60 steps on ancestor-identical labels gradients start small so flipping enough held-out rows to gain BA4 >0.02 is tight.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed paper never splits ATD rows into teacher–ancestor agreements and flips. Its controls (exact nuisance-matched, shuffle, public-label, random-marginal) all keep the full row set. Its Appendix D permutes the top, bottom or a random 20% of carrier states ranked by divergence, rather than training on the agreement subset alone, and it reports a teacher-direction cosine, not a held-out near-tie readout.

This paper masks divergence tokens in free-form number sequences produced by teachers given different trait biases, and finds that masking mostly removes the transferred bias. It does not test whether rows that the teacher selects but labels identically to the ancestor carry information, and it does not study post-training capability updates or near-tie binary carriers.

This paper shows that choosing a subset of an existing preference dataset, using an explicit teacher logit shift and keeping the original labels, can transmit system-prompt traits. That is a selection-only channel in spirit. However, it uses the teacher's logits to choose rows, not the private teacher's implicit decision not to flip at an ancestor near-tie, and it does not compare agreement-only against flip-only rows with a control matched on the label-word multiset.

This paper detects subliminal effects (including in data selected by logit-linear selection) by optimizing prompts. It does not partition near-tie carriers by agreement or measure selection-only transfer of a capability update.

opus.reason: I found no paper that trains a student only on near-tie rows where the private teacher agrees with the ancestor, or tests that agreement-only arm against an ancestor-label control matched on the label-word multiset. Divergence-token masking (2509.23886) and logit-linear selection (2602.04863) each touch one side of the question, but with different data, different selection mechanisms and different readouts. Neither settles whether the teacher's choice of which near-tie rows to leave unflipped carries the shadow of a post-training update, and the seed's own controls and divergence ablation never isolate the agreement subset.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed trains on mixed agreement/disagreement carriers and ablates states ranked by divergence, but does not isolate agreement-only rows against a word-multiset-matched ancestor-label control.

Tests divergence-only versus non-divergence-token loss masking in generated sequences, including teacher-versus-original-model comparisons for misalignment. It retains masked tokens as context and does not test teacher-selected, ancestor-identical single-word labels on independently constructed near-tie prompts with the proposed matched control.

Demonstrates subliminal transfer through subset selection using explicit teacher log-probability shifts in preference data, not selection based solely on teacher–ancestor non-flips with unchanged ancestor labels.

sol.reason: Prior work establishes selection-mediated subliminal transfer and studies the importance of divergent tokens, so neither broad idea is new. However, none of the work found answers whether teacher–ancestor agreement alone selects informative near-tie rows when labels remain ancestor-identical, using a word-multiset-matched control and held-out teacher-decision readout.

Although entry 12 also partitions flips and agreements, this experiment measures held-out teacher-choice reconstruction against a word-matched selection control rather than downstream capability transfer.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I implemented: the registered pipeline in atd_sel/run.py, launched by run_eval.sh. It does the following, in order:
- Reads the near-tie carriers from the paper's released data and checks them.
- Computes the ancestor's sides with fp32 readouts.
- Trains a HellaSwag LoRA-SFT teacher (400 steps, as registered) and scores HellaSwag on 2,000 validation items.
- Reads the teacher's pair-restricted side on every carrier.
- Splits off a held-out set by hashing source_id.
- Builds the five row-matched arms (FLIP, AGREE, PUBM, MIX, SHUF) with the registered RNG seeds.
- Trains 10 students (seeds 1 and 2; 60 steps, effective batch 128, lr 1e-4), with the registered 27-minute time guard.
- Computes the held-out fp32 BA4, the four cell accuracies, the flipped-row AUC and HellaSwag for each student, plus bootstrap CIs (10,000 draws over held-out carriers).
- Writes all registered outputs, recomputing the statistic from heldout_predictions.jsonl.

Changes from the registration:
1. `git clone` failed because git is not installed on the machine. The script falls back to /workspace/seed/data/carriers.jsonl, which is the same repository's released file (5,664 rows). It verifies the mapping against each prompt's Options line: LEFT = pair_surfaces[0], RIGHT = pair_surfaces[1]. The carriers were not regenerated.
2. Precision: weights are loaded from the bf16 checkpoint and held in fp32 (an exact cast). Pair-margin readouts run in fp32 with TF32 matmuls, as registered. Training and HellaSwag scoring run under bf16 autocast rather than with pure bf16 weights, so the optimiser updates fp32 LoRA weights.
3. If a BA4 cell were empty, it would be skipped; none were (held-out cell counts 211/514/171/516).

Result from my test run (full protocol; about 11.5 min after pip install):
- Teacher gap: +4.50 pp on HellaSwag (56.75 → 61.25). Flip rate 0.494, retention 0.994, median |dm| 1.20 logits. n = 2,110 rows per arm.
- **Registered statistic: BA4(AGREE) − BA4(PUBM) = +0.140**, above the 0.02 threshold (bootstrap CI [0.110, 0.170]).
  - AGREE BA4 was 0.720 and 0.755 by seed; PUBM 0.602 and 0.593.
  - The ancestor (M0) scores 0.502.
- Other contrasts: FLIP−SHUF +0.260 (gate passed), MIX−SHUF +0.236, FLIP−AGREE +0.031 [0.009, 0.053], PUBM−SHUF +0.089 [0.059, 0.118].
- Information ratio 0.54, against a first-order prediction of 0.98.
- The ordering was FLIP > MIX > AGREE > PUBM > SHUF.
- Student HellaSwag scores stayed between 56.65 and 57.15, so there is no capability claim (the registration expected none).

Caveats on interpretation:
- The teacher's update is large compared with the near-tie margins (median |dm| ≈ 1.2 logits against margins of about 0.08). Agreement rows are therefore largely sign observations of the update itself.
- The teacher has a strong right-side preference: its label right-marginal is 0.73. PUBM matches AGREE's label-word multiset exactly (no shortfall; 55% row overlap), but not its side marginal (0.51 vs 0.72), and the registered control does not match side.

registration.title: Can the public ancestor alone predict where a private update will move near-tie decisions? Random-LoRA sensitivity probes versus realized margin changes and flips of in-run teachers
registration.seed_connection: ATD selects queries using only the ancestor's margin |q - 0.5|, and the seed shows this near-tie filter is what makes the channel work (active vs passive). Under the seed's own first-order model a near tie moves by g_i^T delta, so carriers whose margin gradient g_i is large should move more, and flip more often, under any update, whereas the realized change also depends on how the specific update aligns with g_i. The seed localizes information with teacher-ancestor divergence, which requires the teacher; it never asks whether sensitivity is predictable from the ancestor alone, i.e. whether the acquisition could be targeted beyond the margin.
registration.hypothesis: An ancestor-only sensitivity score (RMS change of a carrier's pair margin under random rank-16 LoRA perturbations of the ancestor) predicts how much a real private update moves that carrier's pair margin: Spearman correlation above 0.15 with the absolute margin change realized by an independently trained HellaSwag teacher.
registration.contribution: Turns the seed's first-order interpretation into a testable, teacher-free prediction and, if confirmed, a drop-in improvement to ATD's query selection (rank near-ties by sensitivity). Uses a graded target (realized margin change) that does not saturate when the update overwhelms all near-tie margins, plus the flip-based version with margin stratification, word-identity residualization and a permutation null, and validates on two unrelated updates. A null shows that where the shadow lands is specific to the update rather than to the ancestor's local geometry.

closest_work.difference: The seed selects on |q - 0.5| only and localizes information with teacher-ancestor divergence, which needs the teacher; this experiment predicts divergence from ancestor-only perturbation probes and tests the prediction against two real updates' realized margin changes and flips.

Argues in a kernel model that high-entropy synthetic inputs are the best probes for transfer; here the probe quality of individual inputs is scored by parameter-perturbation sensitivity in an LLM and validated against real updates, with entropy as a baseline feature.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct from Hugging Face (main branch; record the resolved commit hash); bf16 for teacher training, float32 with TF32 matmuls for all margin readouts

github.com/myboker/ATD (git clone): data/carriers.jsonl and data/alphabet.json if present; optionally any released file with the paper's code teacher's response per carrier (e.g. data/signal.jsonl) for a secondary analysis; otherwise carriers are regenerated from the ancestor as described
Rowan/hellaswag (train split) and openai/gsm8k config 'main' (train split) from Hugging Face datasets
Python packages: torch, transformers, peft, datasets, numpy, scipy, scikit-learn
registration.method:
1. Setup. Start a wall-clock timer. pip install torch transformers peft datasets numpy scipy scikit-learn. Load M0 = Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct in bf16 on the A100.
2. Carriers. Run git clone https://github.com/myboker/ATD. If data/carriers.jsonl exists, print its line count and first line and map its fields: the prompt text (raw text ending in 'Answer:') and the two offered words (explicit strings, or two indices into the word list of data/alphabet.json; the LEFT word is printed first after 'Options:'), plus optional id, source_id and public-side fields; log the mapping. If the file, the prompt or the pair cannot be identified, regenerate carriers with the paper's Appendix B recipe using M0 only: V = the first 128 words of a hard-coded list of about 200 common concrete English nouns (clothing, food, kitchen and household objects, animals, plants, tools) that tokenize to exactly one token as ' '+word; for each candidate draw (RandomState(0)) distinct words X, Y, w_1..w_L (L uniform in 0..8), a, b from V and build 'Question: How might a {X} and a {Y} appear in the same short story?
Answer: {w_1 ... w_L}

Choose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word.
Options: {a} | {b}
Answer:'; compute M0's final-position logits in batches of 256; keep a candidate if the unrestricted argmax is the token of ' a' or ' b' and the pair-normalized probability q of ' b' satisfies |q - 0.5| <= 0.02; stop at 5,664 kept or after 300,000 candidates; if fewer than 2,000 are kept, widen to |q - 0.5| <= 0.05 for up to 200,000 further candidates; id = running index. Prompts are raw text (no chat template, add_special_tokens=False), right-padded, every next-token quantity read at the last non-pad position only. The answer token of word w is the single token id of ' '+w (assert). Precision: near-tie margins are about 0.08 logits, below bf16 logit resolution, so every margin readout in this experiment is computed with the model cast to float32 with TF32 matmuls (torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('high')), adapters attached and unmerged; only teacher training runs in bf16. For every carrier record M0's pair logit difference m0_i = z_0(right) - z_0(left), q_i, s0_i = [m0_i > 0], the full-vocabulary next-token entropy H_i (nats), the probability mass ppair_i on the two pair tokens, position_i = number of words on the 'Answer:' line of the prompt, and the left and right word strings. Report the fraction with |q_i - 0.5| <= 0.02.
3. Random-LoRA sensitivity probes (ancestor only). Wrap M0 in a PEFT LoRA (r=16, alpha=16, dropout 0, modules q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj). For probe k = 1..8: torch.manual_seed(1000 + k); overwrite every lora_A weight with N(0, 1/d_in) entries (d_in = that module's input dimension) and every lora_B weight with N(0, sigma^2) entries; forward all carriers; record m_k,i = perturbed pair logit difference. Calibrate sigma once with probe 1 on the first 512 carriers by bisection over log10(sigma) in [-4, 0] (12 iterations) until the RMS of (m_1,i - m0_i) over the subset lies in [0.27, 0.33] logits; use that sigma for all probes (small relative to typical logit scales; the ranking by sensitivity is scale-free to first order). s_i = sqrt(mean_k (m_k,i - m0_i)^2). Report the split-half reliability (Spearman between s from probes 1-4 and from probes 5-8). Record in the summary that for i.i.d. factors Var(g_i^T delta_theta) = (r sigma^2 / d_in) * sum over modules of ||d m_i / dW||_F^2, so s_i estimates a module-weighted gradient norm of the carrier margin. Unload the probe adapter.
4. Real updates: two LoRA-SFT teachers from M0, each a fresh adapter (r=16, alpha=16, dropout 0, same modules; AdamW lr 1e-4, weight decay 0, 10 warmup steps then linear decay, grad clip 1.0, loss on completion tokens only, bf16, seed 0). T_HS: Rowan/hellaswag train [0, 6400), prep(s) = re.sub(r'\[.*?\]', '', s.strip().replace(' [title]', '. ')).replace('  ', ' ').strip(), prompt f'{activity_label}: {prep(ctx)}', completion ' ' + prep(endings[int(label)]) + EOS, batch 16, 400 steps, max length 256. T_GSM: openai/gsm8k 'main' train [0, 3200), prompt f'Question: {question}
Answer:', completion ' ' + answer + EOS (the full solution string), batch 8, 400 steps, max length 384. For each teacher (adapter attached, float32 readout) and every carrier: m_T,i, realized change dm_i = m_T,i - m0_i, side = [m_T,i > 0], flip_i = [side != s0_i], retained_i = [unrestricted argmax in pair] (diagnostic). Report flip rate, retention rate, median and 90th percentile of |dm_i|. Remove each adapter after its readout.
5. Secondary, only if the repo provides the paper's code teacher's side per released carrier id (log the file and field used): flipC_i = [released side != s0_i].
6. Statistics. Primary: Spearman rank correlation rho between s_i and |dm_i| of T_HS over all carriers, with a 10,000-draw carrier bootstrap CI. Secondary: the same for T_GSM; Spearman of each baseline feature (H_i, ppair_i, position_i, |q_i - 0.5|, |m0_i|) with |dm_i| for both teachers; partial Spearman between s and |dm| after residualizing log s and log |dm| on left-word and right-word identity (two-way additive means fitted by 5 alternating sweeps) and on position; flip analyses per teacher: flip rate per |q_i - 0.5| decile (a decreasing profile means the margin still matters; a flat profile near 0.5 means the update overwhelms all near-tie margins and flips cannot be predicted by any geometry), the decile-stratified Mann-Whitney AUC of s_i for flip_i (size-weighted mean over deciles) with a within-decile label-permutation null (200 permutations; report the 95th percentile), the same stratified AUC for flipC if available, mean |dm| and flip rate in the top versus bottom quintile of s_i, and a logistic regression of flip on standardized (s, |q - 0.5|, position, H) with coefficients.

event.description: The ancestor-only random-LoRA sensitivity score predicts how far the HellaSwag teacher's update moves each carrier's pair margin: Spearman correlation above 0.15 between s_i and |dm_i| over all carriers.
event.statistic: Spearman rank correlation between the random-LoRA sensitivity s_i and the absolute realized pair-margin change |dm_i| of the HellaSwag teacher, over all carriers

evaluation.procedure: outputs/carrier_scores.jsonl: one line per carrier with id, words, q_i, m0_i, s0_i, H_i, ppair_i, position_i, the eight probe margins, s_i, and for each teacher m_T,i, dm_i, side, flip and retained flags (plus the released code flip if available). outputs/stats.json: calibrated sigma, split-half reliability, the primary Spearman with its bootstrap CI, all secondary Spearman and partial correlations, flip rates per margin decile, stratified AUCs with permutation-null percentiles, quintile contrasts, regression coefficients, flip and retention rates, |dm| quantiles. outputs/summary.json: the registered statistic (primary Spearman), timing, the resolved model commit and the carrier source (released or regenerated).
evaluation.controls: Baseline ancestor features (entropy, pair mass, list position, public margin) show whether predictive power is trivial; word-identity residualization removes per-word effects; the second, unrelated update (GSM8K) tests whether the relation is update-generic; margin-decile stratification and within-decile permutation give the flip null (~0.50 AUC); the flip-rate profile across margin deciles diagnoses whether margins matter at all. No training controls are needed because no student is trained.

closest_work.difference: The seed paper picks carriers only by the ancestor's near-tie margin. It finds that near-boundary (active) selection beats passive selection, and it locates information using the teacher. As far as I read, it never tests whether a perturbation score computed from the ancestor alone predicts how much a real update moves each carrier's margin or flips its answer.

This is a kernel learning-dynamics theory of subliminal learning, with experiments on the canonical ghost-output setting. It argues that high-entropy inputs make good broadband probes. It does not score individual LLM prompts by their sensitivity to random-LoRA perturbations, and it does not check such scores against the margin changes produced by real teacher updates.

This paper uses paired victim and base outputs, with features such as margin and entropy, to infer the structure of a PEFT adapter (family, layer locality, rank). It does not predict per-input sensitivity from the base model alone, and it is not about near-tie carriers for distillation.

This paper links LoRA fine-tuning to the NTK and relates the NTK spectrum to adaptation performance. It does not test whether per-example sensitivity to random perturbations predicts realized output changes on unrelated prompts.

opus.reason: I found no paper that tests whether a score computed only from the ancestor, such as random-LoRA sensitivity or a gradient-norm proxy, predicts where a private fine-tuning update moves near-tie decisions on unrelated carriers. The seed paper and the related subliminal-learning and linearization papers cover nearby ideas: near-tie selection, theories of which inputs make good probes, and NTK views of fine-tuning. None of them runs this test on a per-carrier basis against real teacher updates. My searches were limited, so a less visible paper could still exist.

closest_work.difference: ATD selects carriers using ancestor near-ties and analyzes information concentration using realized teacher–ancestor divergence. It does not test whether ancestor-only perturbation sensitivity ranks carriers by their response to an independently learned update.

TokUR uses training-free low-rank random weight perturbations to estimate token-level uncertainty and assess reasoning correctness. It does not validate these scores against off-task margin changes caused by separately trained adapters.

This paper uses gradient-derived finite-difference probes, reference training trajectories, and task-gradient covariance to model margin responses and bound forgetting. Its predictions use update-specific information rather than an ancestor-only random-perturbation norm.

The kernel analysis explains subliminal transfer and compares broad versus structured input distributions. It does not score individual near-tie prompts using ancestor parameter sensitivity or test those rankings against real teacher updates.

sol.reason: Sensitivity-based probing and low-rank perturbation ensembles are established ingredients, so those alone are not novel. That conditional predictive question distinguishes the registered experiment from prior uncertainty estimation, integrity detection, and update-specific response modeling.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I implemented (sens/run_experiment.py, run through run_eval.sh): the registered experiment as written. In the end-to-end test run (about 6.5 min, two identical runs) the primary statistic was Spearman(s_i, |dm_i| for the HellaSwag teacher) = 0.166, with a carrier-bootstrap 95% CI of [0.141, 0.191]. That is above the 0.15 threshold, but the CI includes 0.15. The registered event is decided only by the point value, so it is met, and only narrowly.

Setup:
- Carriers: the released data/carriers.jsonl, 5,664 rows, read from /workspace/seed/data. A git clone of the same repo is the fallback. Fields used: prompt, pair_surfaces[0] as the left word and pair_surfaces[1] as the right word. A check confirmed both words appear in the "Options:" line.
- Model: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, main branch. The resolved commit is written to summary.json.
- Readouts: all margin readouts use float32 with TF32 matmuls, at the last non-pad position, with adapters left unmerged.
- Random-LoRA probes: r=16, A ~ N(0, 1/d_in), B ~ N(0, sigma²), seeds 1000+k. sigma was calibrated by bisection; it gave log10 sigma = -2.375 with RMS 0.316.
- Teachers: two LoRA-SFT teachers (HellaSwag 400×16, GSM8K 400×8) trained in bf16 with the registered hyperparameters. Data order is a RandomState(0) permutation; the registration did not specify one.
- Statistics: everything listed in the registration.
- Restore check: after every adapter unload, the base model's margins match the original M0 margins exactly (max diff 0.0).

Deviations and assumptions:
- Carriers are read from the seed copy instead of a fresh git clone. It is the same repo.
- The registered regeneration fallback is not implemented. It was never needed because the released carriers exist.
- In the partial Spearman, position is treated as a third categorical factor in the additive sweeps.
- The secondary released code-teacher analysis uses data/signal.jsonl, field hard_targets[0] (0 = left, 1 = right). It is 100% consistent with the completion field.
- Extras beyond the registration: the Spearman of s with the baseline features, flipC computed against the released public_side, and the cross-teacher |dm| correlation.

Observations (all from one run):
- Split-half reliability of s is only 0.28, so 8 probes give a noisy score and the correlation is probably attenuated. That is an inference, not something tested.
- GSM8K teacher: rho = 0.177, CI [0.151, 0.202].
- Partial Spearman after removing word identity and position: 0.135 for both teachers.
- Baseline features (entropy, pair mass, position, |q - 0.5|) all have |rho| ≤ 0.065 with |dm|.
- Top versus bottom quintile of s: mean |dm| is 1.64 vs 1.06 (HellaSwag) and 1.04 vs 0.66 (GSM8K).
- Flips: both in-run teachers flip about 49% of carriers, and the flip rate is flat across margin deciles. The update overwhelms near-tie margins: median |dm| is 1.02 and 0.66 logits, against near-tie margins of about 0.08 logits.
- Stratified AUC of s for flips is at the permutation null: 0.506 HellaSwag and 0.501 GSM8K, versus a null 95th percentile of about 0.511.
- So s predicts how much margins move, but not which side they end up on.
- Released code teacher: flip rate 0.40, and it decreases across margin deciles (0.47 down to 0.32), so the margin matters for that teacher. The stratified AUC is 0.514, just above the null 95th percentile of 0.512 (permutation p ≈ 0.04, a weak effect).
- The |dm| of the two in-run teachers correlate with each other at Spearman 0.14.

registration.title: Is the near-tie shadow reproducible across independently trained teachers of the same task? Bit-level agreement and black-box task identification without training a student
registration.seed_connection: The seed's observability claim and its source-specificity analysis rely on representational diagnostics that use the teacher's logits, and its five-acquisition robustness result shows that transfer is reproducible across teachers. It does not show whether the near-tie decisions themselves are reproducible: two teachers trained on the same task with different data and seeds could flip the same carriers (a systematic, task-determined shadow) or largely different ones (an idiosyncratic shadow whose transfer rests on a small consistent component). Appendix E reports that code and math teacher directions are near-orthogonal, which suggests cross-task bit agreement should be low, but same-task bit agreement is unknown.
registration.hypothesis: Independently trained teachers of the same task agree on the near-tie carriers substantially more than teachers of different tasks after correcting for flip rates: the mean chance-corrected agreement (kappa) of same-task pairs exceeds that of cross-task pairs by more than 0.10.
registration.contribution: A student-free, purely black-box measurement of how systematic the behavioral shadow is, and of whether one-bit near-tie answers identify the fine-tuning task of a held-out teacher, compared against random-pair probes on the same contexts. Yao et al. infer PEFT structure from rich outputs; Okatan et al. and Schrodi et al. note seed- and teacher-specific idiosyncrasies in subliminal transfer; none measures reproducibility of hard near-tie decisions across teachers or their task-identification value.

closest_work.difference: Infers PEFT family, locality and rank of a private adaptation from rich victim/base residuals; here the question is task identity and cross-seed reproducibility from single-bit decisions on near-tie prompts.
Shows in synthetic Transformers that different-seed students leak less than same-seed students; here reproducibility is measured directly in teacher decisions on an LLM and tied to task identity.

Reports that mixing data from several same-bias teachers weakens trait transfer, hinting at teacher idiosyncrasy; here idiosyncrasy versus task-specific consistency is quantified on fixed carriers with chance-corrected agreement.
