registration.title: Readout-fidelity ladder on fixed near-tie carriers: greedy one-bit token versus pair probability versus full next-token distribution, measured on a capability endpoint
registration.seed_connection: ATD trains the student on one greedy token per near-tie carrier, and the seed's Discussion leaves open whether its limits come from how little the selected observations reveal or from how the student learns from them. The seed tested only observation width (multi-token answers), not observation fidelity at the chosen positions. Holding carriers, teacher and training recipe fixed and widening only the readout of each carrier decision (one bit, then the pair probability, then the full next-token distribution) bounds how much capability-relevant information the selected observation points contain and how much the one-bit readout discards.
registration.hypothesis: On identical near-tie carriers, a student trained on the teacher's full next-token distribution at the answer position gains more than 1 pp of HellaSwag accuracy over the student trained on the teacher's hard token, i.e. the selected observation points carry materially more capability-relevant information than the one-bit readout extracts.
registration.contribution: Quantifies, with pairing-destroying controls at every rung, how much capability transfer is lost by the hard-token readout relative to pair-probability and full-distribution readouts on actively selected near-tie prompts, and separates pair information from off-pair information. Schrodi et al. compare hard and soft distillation only for trait transfer on sampled number lists; the seed tests hard tokens and a multi-token variant. The outcome decides whether follow-up work should buy more bits per query or better carriers; a null (FULL ~ HARD) is itself informative because it bounds the information at the observation points.

closest_work.difference: Compares soft and hard distillation for animal-preference traits transmitted through free-form number completions, without a capability endpoint, a fixed near-tie query set, or pairing-matched controls; here carriers are fixed near-ties, the endpoint is held-out task accuracy, and the ladder separates pair-probability information from full-vocabulary information with a permuted-distribution control.
Scales the number of off-task examples to make latent traits recoverable; here the number of carriers is fixed and only the information per carrier changes.

The seed uses greedy single tokens (and a multi-token variant) and names the hard-token observation as a possible bottleneck without testing a soft-label or full-distribution ceiling on the same carriers.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct from Hugging Face (main branch; record the resolved commit hash); bf16 for training and HellaSwag scoring, float32 with TF32 matmuls for the carrier acquisition
github.com/myboker/ATD (git clone): data/carriers.jsonl and data/alphabet.json if present; otherwise carriers are regenerated from the ancestor as described
Rowan/hellaswag from Hugging Face datasets (train split for the teacher, validation split for the endpoint)
Python packages: torch, transformers, peft, datasets, numpy
registration.method:
1. Setup. Start a wall-clock timer at the first command. pip install torch transformers peft datasets numpy. Load M0 = Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct in bf16 on the A100.
2. Carriers. Run git clone https://github.com/myboker/ATD. If data/carriers.jsonl exists, print its line count and first line and map its fields: the prompt text (raw text ending in 'Answer:') and the two offered words (explicit strings, or two indices into the word list of data/alphabet.json; the LEFT word is printed first after 'Options:'), plus optional id and public-side fields; log the mapping. If the file, the prompt or the pair cannot be identified, regenerate carriers with the paper's Appendix B recipe using M0 only: V = the first 128 words of a hard-coded list of about 200 common concrete English nouns (clothing, food, kitchen and household objects, animals, plants, tools) that tokenize to exactly one token as ' '+word; for each candidate draw (RandomState(0)) distinct words X, Y, w_1..w_L (L uniform in 0..8), a, b from V and build 'Question: How might a {X} and a {Y} appear in the same short story?\nAnswer: {w_1 ... w_L}\n\nChoose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word.\nOptions: {a} | {b}\nAnswer:'; compute M0's final-position logits in batches of 256; keep a candidate if the unrestricted argmax is the token of ' a' or ' b' and the pair-normalized probability q of ' b' satisfies |q - 0.5| <= 0.02; stop at 5,664 kept or after 300,000 candidates; if fewer than 2,000 are kept, widen to |q - 0.5| <= 0.05 for up to 200,000 further candidates. Prompts are raw text (no chat template, add_special_tokens=False), right-padded, every next-token quantity read at the last non-pad position only (compute logits only there, which also keeps training memory small). The answer token of word w is the single token id of ' '+w (assert). Precision: near-tie margins are about 0.08 logits, below bf16 logit resolution, so the ancestor and teacher carrier readouts are computed with the model cast to float32 with TF32 matmuls (torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('high')), adapter attached and unmerged; training and HellaSwag scoring run in bf16. Recompute M0's side s0_i = [z_0(right) > z_0(left)] for every carrier; report the fraction with |q - 0.5| <= 0.02.
3. Teacher T. Load Rowan/hellaswag; prep(s) = re.sub(r'\[.*?\]', '', s.strip().replace(' [title]', '. ')).replace('  ', ' ').strip(); training example: prompt f'{activity_label}: {prep(ctx)}', completion ' ' + prep(endings[int(label)]) + EOS, tokenized separately and concatenated, loss on completion tokens only; train examples [0, 6400) in dataset order; fresh LoRA r=16, alpha=16, dropout 0 on q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj; AdamW lr 1e-4, weight decay 0, batch 16, 400 steps, 10 warmup steps then linear decay to 0, grad clip 1.0, max length 256, bf16, seed 0; adapter kept unmerged. Endpoint: HellaSwag validation items [0, 4000) in dataset order; score each of the 4 endings by the mean per-token log-probability of ' ' + prep(ending) given f'{activity_label}: {prep(ctx)}' (no EOS); argmax; accuracy in %; store per-item 0/1 correctness for every evaluated model. Evaluate M0 and T; gap = acc_T - acc_M0 (flag 'weak teacher' if gap < 3 pp; continue).
4. Acquisition (all carriers are used; the paper's retention rule is replaced by the pair-restricted readout so that every arm shares one row set). For each carrier run T once (float32) and store at the final position the full-vocabulary probability vector p_T,i (float32 array of shape 5,664 x vocab in CPU RAM), the pair-normalized probability p_i of the RIGHT word, the hard side h_i = [p_i > 0.5], and retained_i = [unrestricted argmax in pair] (diagnostic). Report the retention rate, the flip rate [h_i != s0_i], mean |2 p_i - 1| (pair information beyond the sign), and the mean teacher probability mass on the two pair tokens (how much off-pair information exists). Sharpened pair target: p'_i = p_i^(1/tau) / (p_i^(1/tau) + (1 - p_i)^(1/tau)) with tau found by bisection so that the mean over carriers of max(p'_i, 1 - p'_i) equals 0.95 (if the mean of max(p_i, 1 - p_i) is already >= 0.95, set tau = 1 and skip the SOFT-sharp arm as redundant). Draw one permutation pi of the carriers from RandomState(1234). Remove the teacher adapter.
5. Arms (loss at the final position only; p_theta = student full-vocabulary softmax; left_i and right_i the pair token ids):
 - HARD-sig: cross-entropy on the token of side h_i (the ATD objective).
 - HARD-shuf: cross-entropy on the token of side h_{pi(i)} (sides permuted across carriers; each label stays within its own pair; side marginal preserved; pairing destroyed).
 - SOFT-sig: -[p_i log p_theta(right_i) + (1 - p_i) log p_theta(left_i)].
 - SOFT-sharp: the same with p'_i (optimization-scale diagnostic: same information as SOFT, gradient scale comparable to HARD).
 - FULL-sig: KL(p_T,i || p_theta) = sum_v p_T,i(v) [log p_T,i(v) - log p_theta(v)].
 - FULL-shuf: KL(p_T,pi(i) || p_theta) (whole distributions permuted across carriers; same multiset of target distributions, pairing destroyed; unlike HARD-shuf the permuted target may put its mass on words not offered in prompt i, which is stated as a difference in kind).
6. Students (identical recipe, targets differ). Initialize from M0 with a fresh LoRA (r=16, alpha=16, dropout 0, the same seven modules); AdamW lr 1e-4, weight decay 0; micro-batch 64 x gradient accumulation 2 (effective 128); 100 optimizer steps (about 2.3 passes over the carriers); 5 warmup steps then linear decay to 0; grad clip 1.0; bf16; no gradient checkpointing; row order = RandomState(training seed) permutation, cycling. Training order: HARD-sig seed 1, HARD-shuf seed 1, FULL-sig seed 1, SOFT-sig seed 1, FULL-shuf seed 1, HARD-sig seed 2, HARD-shuf seed 2, FULL-sig seed 2, SOFT-sig seed 2, SOFT-sharp seed 1, FULL-shuf seed 2. Time guard: do not start a new student after 28 minutes of wall clock; contrasts use the seeds completed for both of their arms. Evaluate each student on the endpoint immediately after training, write its results, log its final LoRA update size (sum over modules of ||B A||_F) as an optimization-scale diagnostic, then remove its adapter.
7. Statistic and reporting. Statistic = mean over completed seeds of [acc(FULL-sig) - acc(HARD-sig)] on the 4,000 validation items (seed-paired). Also report every model's accuracy; the contrasts HARD-sig - HARD-shuf (bottom-rung check of the paper's effect under this teacher and step budget), SOFT-sig - HARD-sig, SOFT-sharp - SOFT-sig, FULL-sig - FULL-shuf, FULL-shuf - HARD-shuf, each with a 10,000-draw paired item bootstrap CI on seed-averaged per-item correctness; the teacher gap; the acquisition diagnostics; the LoRA update sizes. Pre-specified readings: FULL - HARD large and FULL - FULL-shuf large means the carriers' decisions carry far more capability information than the one-bit readout extracts (readout is the lever); FULL ~ HARD means the selected observation points reveal little beyond their sign (carrier selection or the learning procedure is the lever); FULL - HARD large but FULL - FULL-shuf ~ 0 means the gain is the teacher's marginal output distribution (format and word preferences), not prompt-specific shadow; SOFT ~ HARD with SOFT-sharp ~ SOFT means the sign carries essentially all pair information.

event.description: The full-distribution student outperforms the hard-token student on HellaSwag by more than 1 pp (mean over completed training seeds, first 4,000 validation items), on identical near-tie carriers and training recipe.
event.statistic: acc(FULL-sig) minus acc(HARD-sig) on the 4,000 HellaSwag validation items, in percentage points, averaged over the completed training seeds

evaluation.procedure: outputs/acquisition.jsonl: one line per carrier with id, pair words, s0_i, p_i, h_i, p'_i, retained flag, flip flag, pair mass of the teacher, and pi(i). outputs/per_item.jsonl: one line per evaluated model (M0, T, each student with arm and seed) with the 0/1 correctness vector over the 4,000 fixed items. outputs/scores.jsonl: one line per model with accuracy in % and, for students, the LoRA update size and training loss curve. outputs/summary.json: the registered statistic (seed-paired mean of FULL-sig minus HARD-sig), the list of completed seeds, all secondary contrasts with bootstrap CIs, teacher gap, retention, mean |2p - 1|, mean pair mass, tau, timing and the resolved model commit.
evaluation.controls: HARD-shuf and FULL-shuf use the same carriers and recipe with the prompt-target pairing permuted, isolating the information in the pairing at the bottom and top rungs; HARD-sig versus HARD-shuf replicates the paper's effect under this teacher; SOFT-sharp separates optimization scale from information content for the pair-probability rung; M0 and T bound the achievable gain; all arms share one row set, one teacher, one step budget and one permutation.

models: HellaSwag LoRA-SFT teacher derived from it in-run

registration.full_scale_study: A bits-per-query versus transfer curve across tasks (code/HumanEval+ with the seed's code-DPO lineage, ScienceQA, GSM8K), teacher types (DPO, full SFT) and student scales (0.5B-8B), adding intermediate readouts such as top-k rankings over the carrier alphabet and repeated-sample frequency estimates of the pair probability, with 4 seeds and exact nuisance-matched controls, to determine whether richer readouts or better carrier selection is the lever for black-box capability extraction.

agent.reason: Full-distribution matching at the answer position constrains the student far more than one bit and plausibly transfers more of the teacher's update, but whether that converts into more than 1 pp of HellaSwag over the hard-token student at 100 steps with a modest teacher is a near coin-flip, and the time guard may leave only one seed.

judge_astra.reason: Full distributions could recover more teacher information and avoid distortion from forcing pair-only hard labels. But a potentially modest teacher gain and unequal optimization behavior under the fixed short schedule make a greater-than-1-pp advantage uncertain; a small contrast would not establish that additional information is absent.

judge_fable.reason: Full-distribution matching on unrelated inputs with a same-init student should transfer more than one bit per carrier (consistent with data-free distillation and the subliminal-learning logit results), but the effect must exceed 1 pp on a single completed seed with ~0.7 pp noise, and the 13-model, 4,000-item evaluation ladder is likely to be truncated by the time guard.

judge_opus.reason: Full-distribution matching is a cleaner, magnitude-weighted signal and avoids the hard-label noise penalty, which cost about 0.5–1 pp in the seed's shuffle arms. On the other hand, hard near-tie labels amplify the teacher's effect, generalization from a single carrier position is uncertain, and the run will likely complete only one seed, so a gap above 1 pp is roughly a coin flip.

judge_sol.reason: Full-distribution targets could preserve more of the teacher's update and avoid distortion from forcing every response into the offered pair, making a greater-than-1-pp advantage plausible. Fixed optimization budgets and extensive evaluation add uncertainty, and an advantage could partly reflect avoiding hard-label damage rather than extracting additional capability information.

judge_luna.reason: The seed leaves observation fidelity open, and its multi-token result shows that wider supervision can help on at least one endpoint; teacher probabilities may convey margin magnitude beyond the hard sign. However, full distributions may be dominated by ancestor behavior or provide weak optimization signals, so a gain exceeding 1 pp over hard labels is only moderately likely.

judge_muse.reason: Full distributions add magnitudes plus off-pair mass, but with fixed 100 steps hard labels give larger focused gradients while FULL diffuses over 150k vocab and mimics off-pair failures (seed retention only ~32%), making >1pp gain over HARD unlikely.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed paper trains only on hard greedy tokens, with cross-entropy and with a pair-margin variant (RPM) that subtracts the ancestor's margin. Its one extension is a wider 20-token hard readout. It never trains on the teacher's pair probability or full next-token distribution on the same carriers. Its Discussion explicitly leaves open whether the bottleneck is the observations or the learning procedure.

Contrasts soft and hard distillation conceptually for trait transfer (owl preference) through number lists, and studies divergence tokens and logit leakage. It has no capability endpoint, no fixed near-tie query set, no permuted-distribution controls, and no hard/pair/full readout ladder on identical carriers.
Varies how many off-task examples are used, not how much information each example carries. It concerns trait recoverability rather than held-out task accuracy.
Studies cross-trait transfer matrices in subliminal learning. It does not compare readout fidelity and does not measure capability transfer.

opus.reason: I found no prior work that holds near-tie carriers fixed and varies only the readout per carrier (hard token, pair probability, full next-token distribution), each with a control that shuffles prompt–target pairings, and scores the result on a capability benchmark such as HellaSwag. The seed paper tested a different learning objective and a wider multi-token readout, but never a soft-label or full-distribution upper bound, and it names this as an open question. Subliminal-learning papers that discuss soft versus hard distillation study traits, not capabilities, and do not use this controlled ladder.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Compares hard NLL and full-distribution KL on identical off-task prefixes, but studies stochastic-label noise in recovering a bounded residual-stream steering vector. It does not test greedy binary near-tie readouts of a capability-trained weight update, include a pair-probability rung, or isolate prompt-specific capability transfer with permuted-target controls.

Reports hard-token ATD capability transfer, including HellaSwag, and explores reference-relative pair-margin training and multi-token observations. It does not compare hard labels, pair probabilities, and full next-token distributions at the same carrier positions.

Studies hidden-trait transfer through sampled and greedy number completions, especially divergence-token masking. It does not report this fixed-near-tie, three-rung readout comparison on a capability endpoint.

sol.reason: The general matched-carrier hard-versus-soft comparison was already studied before the cutoff in 2610.04907. However, its sampling-noise and constrained steering-vector recovery results do not settle whether deterministic near-tie signs discard capability-relevant information from a post-training weight update, nor distinguish pair-confidence information from off-pair information. I found no prior work answering that specific question with the registered fidelity ladder and pairing-destroying controls.
Entry 13 likewise holds near-tie carriers fixed, compares hard-token, pair-probability and full-vocabulary distillation, and measures the resulting HellaSwag capability transfer.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I implemented: ladder.py, run with `bash run.sh`, which does the pip install, starts the wall-clock timer and runs the experiment. It follows the registered method: the seed's 5,664 carriers; a HellaSwag LoRA-SFT teacher (r16, 400 steps, lr 1e-4); carrier readouts in float32 with TF32 and the adapter left unmerged; the six arms HARD-sig/shuf, SOFT-sig, SOFT-sharp, FULL-sig/shuf, all with the loss at the last position only; students with LoRA r16, lr 1e-4, effective batch 128, 100 steps, 5 warmup steps then linear decay to 0; the registered training order and the 28-minute guard; and evaluation on the first 4,000 HellaSwag validation items by mean per-token log-prob. The permutation uses RandomState(1234), and the bootstrap is a 10,000-draw paired item bootstrap on seed-averaged per-item correctness. The script writes outputs/{acquisition,per_item,scores}.jsonl, outputs/summary.json and result.json.

Deviations and clarifications:
(1) The machine has no `git`, so the clone fails. The script logs this and reads carriers from /workspace/seed/data/carriers.jsonl, the seed repo's own copy. Field mapping: prompt=`prompt`, left/right=`pair_surfaces[0/1]`, id=`id`, public_side=1 means right. All pair surfaces tokenize to a single token (checked with an assert). I did not implement the carrier regeneration fallback because the file is always present.
(2) Ordering assumption: the teacher's 6,400 training rows are the first 6,400 in dataset order, shuffled once with RandomState(0) (seed 0). The registration fixes the row set but not the order within it.
(3) The model was loaded from the main branch; the resolved commit, 989aa798…, is recorded in the summary.
(4) As registered, the retention rule is replaced by the pair-restricted readout, so every arm uses all carriers.

Test run on this machine (full config, 21.6 min, all 11 students finished; log and summary saved in test_run_log.txt and test_run_summary.json):
- Accuracy: M0 59.90, teacher 63.05, so the teacher gap is +3.15 pp (just above the 3 pp weak-teacher flag).
- Acquisition: retention 99.2%, flip rate 49.4%, mean |2p−1| 0.48, teacher pair mass 0.96, tau 0.147.
- The recomputed fp32 near-tie fraction is 97.6%, and M0's side agrees with the file's public_side on 97.4% of carriers.
- **Registered statistic (FULL-sig − HARD-sig): −0.09 pp** (per seed −0.10 and −0.075; 95% CI [−0.29, +0.11]). This is below the 1 pp threshold, so the event did not occur in the test run.
- Secondary contrasts, none of which excludes zero:

| Contrast | Δ (pp) | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|
| HARD-sig − HARD-shuf | +0.40 | [−0.04, +0.84] |
| SOFT-sig − HARD-sig | −0.19 | [−0.41, +0.04] |
| SOFT-sharp − SOFT-sig (1 seed) | +0.15 | [−0.15, +0.48] |
| FULL-sig − FULL-shuf | +0.43 | [−0.28, +1.14] |
| FULL-shuf − HARD-shuf | −0.11 | [−0.81, +0.59] |

How to read this: every student scored about 60%, close to M0 and well below the teacher. Even the bottom-rung replication (HARD-sig vs HARD-shuf) is not significant under this teacher and 100-step budget. With only two seeds, the result says FULL is not more than 1 pp better than HARD under these conditions. It does not show that the two are equivalent in general.

The evaluation run on a fresh machine may differ slightly from these numbers because of GPU nondeterminism.

registration.title: Import-repair audit of ATD's released HumanEval+ result: how much of the signal-minus-exact gain survives giving every solution the same import header?
registration.seed_connection: The seed's flagship evidence is a +5.34 pp HumanEval+ pass@1 gain of ATD signal students over exact nuisance-matched control students (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, 4 seeds). The seed argues that this gain reflects capability because execution scoring cannot be faked by imitation. A drafter's reading of the released scored records suggests that some signal/control discordant cells differ only in whether the solution imports names it uses, such as typing.List. This is unverified. Load-time NameErrors are scored as failures exactly like wrong algorithms. Nobody has measured how much of the aggregate gain comes from import hygiene rather than program logic.
registration.hypothesis: If every released solution in both arms gets the same import header, more than half of the signal-minus-exact HumanEval+ difference disappears.
registration.contribution: Splits ATD's execution-scored flagship result by failure mode using only released artifacts. It separates gains in writing boilerplate imports from gains in program logic. The answer tells us whether the seed's capability-transfer reading of HumanEval+ holds and which scoring protocol follow-up work needs. The same repair is applied to base and teacher solutions where available, to check whether the teacher's own gap is import-driven.

closest_work.difference: Reports the +5.34 pp gain and two hand-picked algorithmic examples, but never decomposes the gain by failure type. We re-score all released solutions after a shared import repair.
EvalPlus defines base+plus scoring. It does not ask whether a contrast between two fine-tuned models is driven by import or load-time failures.
Shows that subliminal transfer can hinge on incidental context. We test an analogous incidental factor (imports) in an execution-scored capability-transfer claim.

inputs: ATD repository github.com/myboker/ATD (MIT). Expected files are released EvalPlus records for signal and exact arms over 4 seeds, with per-task solution text and base/plus status. The drafts name them data/frozen/signal_s20260823.json ... signal_s20260826.json and exact_s20260823.json ... exact_s20260826.json. Also expected is atd/analyze.py with its crossed seed-by-task bootstrap. If teacher and base-model records are released, use them too.
evalplus==0.3.1 from PyPI. It downloads the HumanEval+ dataset automatically; record get_human_eval_plus_hash().
Python packages: numpy
registration.method:
0) Artifact check. Clone the repository and locate the per-seed scored HumanEval+ records for the signal and exact arms. Search the repo for json/jsonl files containing 'HumanEval/' task ids and solution text if the paths differ from those named in the inputs. If records with solution text for at least 4 signal seeds and 4 matched exact seeds cannot be found, write outputs/import_repair_summary.json with status 'artifacts_missing' and stop; the event then does not occur.
1) pip install evalplus==0.3.1 numpy. Record the HumanEval+ dataset hash.
2) Load the records. For each (arm, seed, task_id) keep the solution string and the released pass bit (base_status=='pass' and plus_status=='pass'). Compute the released contrast as 100 x mean over seeds and tasks of (signal_pass - exact_pass). Report whether it equals +5.34 to two decimals. If atd/analyze.py exposes a contrast or bootstrap function, use it to reproduce the released interval [1.22, 9.60].
3) Build three variants of every solution. Never modify the released files.
- O: unchanged.
- R1: prepend the top-level import lines of that task's HumanEval+ prompt (lines of problem['prompt'] that start with 'import ' or 'from ').
- R2: R1 followed by a fixed header, one statement per line: 'from typing import *'; 'import math'; 'import re'; 'import string'; 'import itertools'; 'import functools'; 'import collections'; 'import heapq'; 'import bisect'; 'import statistics'; 'from functools import reduce, lru_cache, cmp_to_key'; 'from itertools import accumulate, chain, combinations, permutations, product, groupby, zip_longest, repeat, islice'; 'from collections import Counter, defaultdict, deque, OrderedDict'.
In R1 and R2, move any 'from __future__' lines to the very top.
4) Score each variant in a single EvalPlus run, not one run per arm and seed. EvalPlus scores one solution per task_id per sample entry, so write one JSONL per (arm, seed, variant), each in its own fresh directory, and run 'python -m evalplus.evaluate --dataset humaneval --samples FILE --parallel 12' on all of them sequentially. A cell passes only if both base and plus pass. If teacher or base-model records exist, score them under O, R1 and R2 as well.
5) For each variant v compute Delta_v = 100 x mean over seeds x 164 tasks of (signal_pass - exact_pass).
6) Retention = Delta_R2 / Delta_O, where Delta_O is the re-scored unchanged solutions in this environment.
7) Secondary analyses:
(a) per arm and variant, counts of fail->pass and pass->fail flips relative to O;
(b) the number of signal/exact-discordant cells in O that become concordant under R2, split by direction;
(c) per arm, the number of O failures whose base and plus fail-test lists are both empty or whose error message is a NameError (load-time failures);
(d) the teacher-minus-base gap under O, R1 and R2, if records exist;
(e) the seed's 19-task agreement analysis repeated under R2. These are the tasks that the teacher passes and the base fails. Report the fraction solved by signal versus exact cells.

event.description: Less than half of the signal-minus-exact HumanEval+ difference survives the shared import header (variant R2).
event.statistic: retention = Delta_R2 / Delta_O, where each Delta is signal minus exact HumanEval+ pass@1 in pp over 4 seeds x 164 tasks, both re-scored in this environment

evaluation.procedure:
Score every cell with EvalPlus (pass = base and plus both pass). Aggregate signal minus exact over the 4 released seed pairs. Compute 95% intervals with a crossed seed-by-task bootstrap: 100,000 draws, resampling seeds and tasks independently. Apply the same resampled indices to O and R2 in each draw, which gives an interval for retention. If Delta_O <= 0, retention is undefined and the event does not occur. Files:
- outputs/pass_vectors.jsonl: one row per arm/seed/variant/task with the pass bit and the EvalPlus statuses.
- outputs/import_repair_summary.json: artifact status, dataset hash, the reproduced released contrast, Delta_O, Delta_R1 and Delta_R2 with intervals, and retention with its interval.
- outputs/failure_breakdown.csv: secondary analyses (a)-(e).
evaluation.controls: Re-scoring the unchanged solutions (O) controls for drift in the evaluation environment. Both arms get the identical header, so a change in Delta can only come from import failures that differ between arms. R1, which adds only the imports the task's own prompt declares, is a minimal repair that brackets R2. Nothing is retrained, so seed variance is exactly the released variance. Teacher and base re-scoring, where possible, shows whether the teacher's own gap is import-driven.

registration.full_scale_study: If retention < 0.5: re-run ATD with fresh acquisitions and seeds and the seed's exact control, under an import-neutral code protocol (completion-style prompts that keep the prompt's imports, or automatic header insertion). Use HumanEval+, MBPP+ and a harder benchmark to test whether any algorithmic gain remains, and whether the shadow transfers a context-copying habit. If retention >= 0.5: extend the decomposition to runtime-error versus wrong-answer failures, to support the algorithmic reading.

agent.reason: Several cues suggest import hygiene could be a large share of the gain. The base HumanEval+ score is unusually low, the teacher's gain is specific to HumanEval+ rather than MBPP+, and import-driven discordances reportedly appear in the first few typing tasks. Against this, the event needs roughly 18 or more net import-only cells, the seed's own worked examples are algorithmic, and the released artifacts might be missing or incomplete.

judge_astra.reason: Import repairs could substantially reduce a contrast equivalent to only about nine net tasks per seed, but the suggested import failures are unverified and the paper reports algorithmic differences too. Availability of all matched solution artifacts is another prerequisite.

judge_fable.reason: Depends entirely on the ATD repo releasing per-seed EvalPlus records with solution text, which the registration itself flags as unverified; even if present, an import-hygiene artifact explaining more than half of a +5.34 pp contrast between two near-identically trained arms is a strong claim, and 24+ sequential EvalPlus runs strain the 35-minute budget.

judge_opus.reason: The event needs released per-seed EvalPlus records with solution text, and I put that at about 0.6 since the specific date-seeded file names hint at real artifacts. Given the records, there is circumstantial support for an import effect: HumanEval+ base (43.3) sits roughly 12 pp below my unverified recollection of the official score while MBPP+ does not, and the teacher's gain is concentrated on HumanEval+. But the drafter saw only 'some' import-only cells, and the paper's highlighted fixes (HE/158, HE/18) are algorithmic, so more than half of the net ~35 cells being import-driven is far from assured.

registration.title: Is ATD's near-tie requirement only a greedy-readout artifact? Confident carriers labelled by the sign of the teacher's logit shift versus near-tie carriers labelled by the teacher's greedy word
registration.seed_connection: The seed attributes ATD's gains to querying where the public ancestor is nearly indifferent; active selection beats passive selection by +4.27 pp at a matched query budget. Its motivating linearization is y = sign(m(theta0) + g^T delta). Under that model a near-tie matters only for visibility: a greedy readout reveals sign(g^T delta) only when the ancestor margin m(theta0) is small. If the teacher's shift relative to the ancestor is read directly, as logprob access allows, confident carriers should be equally informative. This MVE separates two explanations: near-ties are needed because the readout is quantized, or near-tie decision states carry special capability information.
registration.hypothesis: On confident carriers built from the same contexts (ancestor pair probability 0.05-0.20 or 0.80-0.95), labels equal to the sign of the teacher's pair-logit shift relative to the ancestor transfer more than 70% of the HellaSwag gain that greedy teacher labels transfer on near-tie carriers.
registration.contribution: Tests why active near-boundary selection works, in the LLM capability-transfer setting. If the event occurs, the boundary matters only for quantized readout. That implies a logprob-exposing API leaks the post-training update through ordinary non-tied prompts. If the event does not occur, near-tie states themselves concentrate capability-relevant directions, which is a finding about where post-training shadows live.

closest_work.difference: Compares near-tie and passive prompts only under greedy labels, so it cannot tell whether passive prompts lack information or merely hide it behind the ancestor's margin.
Theory of one-bit measurements sign(<a,x>+b) with offsets. Here the ancestor margin plays the offset, and the question is empirical capability transfer between LLMs.
Decision-only black-box distillation in vision turns boundary distances into soft labels. It does not ask whether boundary proximity is still needed once a reference-relative shift is observed.
Locates subliminal trait signal in divergence tokens. It does not separate readout visibility from how informative a decision state is, and it studies traits rather than capabilities.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct at revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306 (Hugging Face)
Rowan/hellaswag from Hugging Face, train and validation splits. If the default loader fails, use revision 'refs/convert/parquet'.

Seed repository github.com/myboker/ATD (MIT): data/carriers.jsonl (near-tie carrier prompts with offered word pairs) and data/alphabet.json (the 128 single-token carrier words). The fallback if absent is in the method.
Python packages: torch, transformers, peft, datasets, numpy
registration.method:
COMMON SETUP
- Load M0 once in bf16 with SDPA attention and TF32 matmuls. Attach and remove a fresh LoRA adapter for each run. No gradient checkpointing.
- Carriers are raw text: no chat template, add_special_tokens=False. The answer is one token, id = tokenizer.encode(' ' + word).
- Scoring. Take the post-final-norm hidden state at the last prompt position, cast it to float32, and multiply by a float32 copy of the output embedding to get logits z. For a carrier offering left word a and right word b: l = z[b] - z[a], q = sigmoid(l), greedy = argmax z over the full vocabulary. l_0 is M0's l and l_T is the teacher's l.
- Always score M0 and the teacher on identical batches, using the same model with the LoRA disabled or enabled. Noise floor: score all carriers once more with M0 in a different batch order and batch size, and report the distribution of |l_0 - l_0'|.

CARRIER FALLBACK
If data/carriers.jsonl or data/alphabet.json is missing, build carriers from the Appendix A template of the seed paper:
'Question: How might a {X} and a {Y} appear in the same short story?\nAnswer: {w1} {w2} {w3} {w4} {w5} {w6}\n\nChoose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word.\nOptions: {a} | {b}\nAnswer:'
Use 128 common concrete English nouns that are single tokens with a leading space, chosen with no code, math or task terms. Sample all slots uniformly with seed 0. Keep near-ties until 6,000 are kept or 80,000 candidates are scored.

TEACHER
- LoRA on M0: r=16, alpha=16, dropout 0, on q/k/v/o/gate/up/down.
- Data: 6,400 HellaSwag train items sampled with seed 0.
- Training: 400 steps, batch 16, AdamW lr 2e-4, wd 0, 10 warmup steps then linear decay, gradient clip 1.0, bf16, loss on target tokens only.
- Plain-text prompt: 'The following describes an everyday activity. Choose the most plausible continuation.\nContext: {ctx}\nOptions:\n- {e0}\n- {e1}\n- {e2}\n- {e3}\nAnswer:'. Target: ' {correct ending}'.
- ctx = activity_label + ': ' + ctx_a + ' ' + ctx_b.capitalize().
- Apply lm-eval-harness HellaSwag preprocessing to all strings: strip; ' [title]' -> '. '; delete bracketed tags; collapse double spaces.

EVALUATION
- A fixed sample of 3,000 validation items (numpy seed 0), using the same prompt.
- Score each ending by the mean per-token log-probability of ' {ending}'. Accuracy = argmax correct. Option-likelihood scoring avoids letter-prior artifacts.
- Evaluate M0 and the teacher and report the teacher's gap.

STEPS
(1) Near-tie versions. Recompute q under M0. Keep a carrier if |q-0.5| <= 0.02 and M0's greedy token is a or b.
(2) Confident versions of the same contexts. Replace 'Options: a | b' with a random ordered pair of distinct alphabet words (seeded). Try up to 16 pairs. Keep the first variant with 0.30 <= |q-0.5| <= 0.45 and M0 greedy in the pair.
(3) Teacher queries on both versions. Keep a context only if the teacher's greedy token lies in the offered pair in both versions. Hold out 10% of kept contexts for diagnostics. N_train = min(3,500, remaining). Flag the run as underpowered if N_train < 2,000.
(4) Labels, with s = +1 for the right word and -1 for the left word.
- T-greedy: the teacher's greedy side on the near-tie version.
- F-shift: sign(l_T - l_0) on the confident version.
(5) Controls. For each arm and seed, permute that arm's labels within 8 strata of its own pool: M0 preferred side (2) x quartile of |q-0.5| within the pool (4).
(6) Students: 4 arms (T-greedy, T-ctrl, F-shift, F-ctrl) x seeds {1,2,3} = 12 runs.
- Fresh LoRA, same modules, r=16, alpha=16. AdamW lr 5e-5, wd 0.
- Effective batch 128 (32 x accum 4). Steps = max(40, round(3.5 x N_train / 128)). 5 warmup steps then linear decay; clip 1.0; bf16.
- Compute logits only at the answer position. All arms of a seed use the same data order.
- Loss for every arm: the reference-relative pair-margin objective, -log sigmoid(s x (l_theta - l_0)), where l_theta = log p_theta(b|x) - log p_theta(a|x) from the full-vocabulary log-softmax and l_0 is frozen. This starts every carrier at the same loss regardless of the ancestor's margin.
(7) Evaluate all 12 students.
(8) Diagnostics.
- Retention per version.
- Confident-pool flip rate.
- Mean |l_T - l_0| per pool, and the fraction of F-shift labels whose |l_T - l_0| is below the 95th percentile of the noise floor.
- Agreement of the near-tie greedy side with sign(l_T - l_0).
- Delta(F-shift) recomputed within tertiles of |l_T - l_0|, by retraining nothing: report the held-out carrier agreement of each student with its label, per tertile.
- For each student, held-out agreement of sign(l_student - l_0) with its arm's label definition.

event.description: Shift-sign labels on confident carriers transfer more than 70% of the HellaSwag gain that greedy labels on near-tie carriers transfer, each against its own stratified-permutation control. The near-tie greedy transfer must be at least 1.0 pp, with a 95% interval excluding 0. Otherwise the event does not occur and the run is recorded as inconclusive.
event.statistic: R = Delta(F-shift) / Delta(T-greedy), where Delta(arm) is the seed-averaged HellaSwag accuracy of the signal student minus its control, in pp

evaluation.procedure:
Delta(arm) = mean over 3 seeds of [acc(signal) - acc(control)] on the 3,000 items. 95% intervals come from a crossed bootstrap that resamples seeds and items independently, 10,000 draws, with the same indices for all arms. R and its interval are computed per draw. Also reported: per-seed Deltas, the teacher-minus-M0 gap, and all diagnostics. Files:
- outputs/carriers.jsonl: per kept context, both versions' prompts and pairs, l_0, q, teacher greedy token, l_T, split, labels and per-seed control labels.
- outputs/item_scores.jsonl: per (model, arm, seed, item), the prediction and correctness.
- outputs/heldout_diagnostics.jsonl: each student's pair logit on held-out carriers.
- outputs/train_log.jsonl: loss per run and step.

registration.title: Is the behavioural shadow a context-free word ranking? Out-of-fold Bradley-Terry relabels versus agreement-matched random flips of the teacher's near-tie choices
registration.seed_connection: The seed's controls show that the prompt-word correspondence matters. These are a label shuffle and an exact permutation preserving the chosen-word multiset and per-bin flips. But a teacher that merely re-ranked the 128 carrier words, ignoring context, would also beat all of those controls: the exact control keeps word frequencies but breaks pairwise consistency. Whether the shadow carries context-dependent decisions or only a roughly 128-dimensional word ranking is untested. The answer decides how low-bandwidth the channel really is.
registration.hypothesis: Students trained on out-of-fold Bradley-Terry relabels transfer at least 0.5 pp more HellaSwag accuracy over a shared shuffle control than students trained on the teacher's labels with random flips that match the Bradley-Terry relabels' disagreement rate. Here the relabels come from one score per carrier word plus a side bias, fit to the teacher's near-tie choices.
registration.contribution: Splits shadow information into a context-free word-score component and a context-dependent remainder. Comparing against a random-flip arm at equal agreement removes the confound that well-fitting relabels simply overlap with the teacher's labels. A CPU fit on the seed's released coding labels, with exact-control and public-label references, measures how much of the published shadow word scores explain.

closest_work.difference: Explains hidden effects through log-linear structure in preference subset selection. It does not test whether a teacher's choices reduce to per-item scores or whether such scores carry capability.
Shows trait transfer is mediated by one steering vector in activation space. We ask the analogous low-dimensional question in label space, for capability shadows.
Its controls preserve word multisets and margin bins but never test a context-free relabeling, so they cannot separate word rankings from contextual decisions.

Rowan/hellaswag from Hugging Face, train and validation splits. If the default loader fails, use revision 'refs/convert/parquet'.

Seed repository github.com/myboker/ATD (MIT): data/carriers.jsonl, data/alphabet.json, and, if present, the released coding-teacher labels and exact-control labels (named data/signal.jsonl and data/exact.jsonl by the drafts; verify the paths and fields). The fallback is in the method.
Python packages: torch, transformers, peft, datasets, numpy, scikit-learn
registration.method:
COMMON SETUP
- Load M0 in bf16 with SDPA attention and TF32 matmuls. Fresh LoRA per run. No gradient checkpointing.
- Carriers are raw text: no chat template, add_special_tokens=False. The answer token id = tokenizer.encode(' ' + word).
- Logits at the last prompt position are computed in float32 from the final hidden state times the output embedding. For left word a and right word b: q = sigmoid(z[b]-z[a]); greedy = argmax z over the full vocabulary.

CARRIER FALLBACK
If the repository carrier files are missing, generate carriers from the template:
'Question: How might a {X} and a {Y} appear in the same short story?\nAnswer: {w1} {w2} {w3} {w4} {w5} {w6}\n\nChoose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word.\nOptions: {a} | {b}\nAnswer:'
Use 128 common single-token concrete nouns, seeded. Keep M0 near-ties until 6,000 are kept or 80,000 are scored.

TEACHER
- LoRA r=16, alpha=16, dropout 0, on q/k/v/o/gate/up/down.
- Data: 6,400 seeded HellaSwag train items.
- Training: 400 steps, batch 16, AdamW lr 2e-4, wd 0, 10 warmup steps then linear decay, clip 1.0, bf16, loss on target tokens only.
- Plain-text prompt: 'The following describes an everyday activity. Choose the most plausible continuation.\nContext: {ctx}\nOptions:\n- {e0}\n- {e1}\n- {e2}\n- {e3}\nAnswer:'. Target: ' {correct ending}'.
- ctx = activity_label + ': ' + ctx_a + ' ' + ctx_b.capitalize(), with lm-eval-harness HellaSwag preprocessing.

EVALUATION
3,000 fixed validation items (numpy seed 0). Score each ending by mean per-token log-probability; accuracy = argmax correct.

STEPS
(1) Near-tie pool. Keep carriers with |q-0.5| <= 0.02 under M0 and M0 greedy in the pair.
(2) Teacher greedy token. Retain carriers whose teacher greedy token is in the pair. Hold out 500 carriers (seed 0). N_train = min(3,500, remaining).
(3) Bradley-Terry fit on the training carriers.
- Feature x_i in R^128 has +1 at b_i and -1 at a_i. Target y_i = 1 if the teacher chose b_i.
- Use L2-regularized logistic regression with an intercept, which acts as the side bias. Choose C in {0.01, 0.1, 1, 10} by 5-fold CV accuracy.
- BT-OOF label for carrier i = the side predicted by a model fit on the other 4 folds (fold assignment seeded).
- Report the BT-OOF agreement with the teacher (A_BT) and the accuracy on the 500 held-out carriers.
(4) FLIP labels. Start from the teacher labels and flip a uniformly random subset of round((1 - A_BT) x N_train) carriers, drawn per seed. FLIP therefore has the same agreement with the teacher as BT-OOF, but its errors are random rather than word-structured.
(5) Arms, all trained with the seed's full-vocabulary CE on the one-hot label word:
- SIGNAL: teacher labels.
- BT: BT-OOF labels.
- FLIP: agreement-matched flips.
- SHUF: a global random permutation of teacher sides, drawn per seed and mapped onto each carrier's own pair.
4 arms x seeds {1,2,3} = 12 students.
- Student recipe: LoRA r=16, alpha=16, all linear projections; AdamW lr 5e-5, wd 0; effective batch 128 (32 x 4).
- Steps = max(40, round(3.5 x N_train / 128)); 5 warmup steps then linear decay; clip 1.0; bf16; logits only at the answer position.
- All arms of a seed share the data order.
(6) CPU analysis of the seed's released coding shadow, if present. Run the same BT fit with 5-fold CV on the released signal labels, the exact-control labels and the public-model sides. Report CV accuracy for each.
(7) Diagnostics.
- Side-marginal of each arm.
- Held-out teacher agreement of each student, measured as the sign of the student's pair logit versus the teacher's greedy side.
- Correlation between the fitted BT word scores and the per-word mean shift of each student.

event.description: Out-of-fold Bradley-Terry relabels transfer at least 0.5 pp more HellaSwag accuracy over the shared shuffle control than teacher labels flipped at random to the same agreement. This would mean that the word-score structure, not mere label overlap, carries the capability. Requires Delta(SIGNAL) >= 1.0 pp with a 95% interval excluding 0, and A_BT >= 0.55. Otherwise the event does not occur and the run is recorded as inconclusive.
event.statistic: D = Delta(BT) - Delta(FLIP) in pp, where Delta(arm) = seed-averaged acc(arm) - acc(SHUF)

evaluation.procedure:
Compute per-item correctness for M0, the teacher and all 12 students. Intervals for the Deltas and D come from a crossed bootstrap resampling seeds and items independently, 10,000 draws, with the same indices for all arms. Also reported: R = Delta(BT)/Delta(SIGNAL), A_BT, BT CV accuracy for the HellaSwag teacher and for the released coding labels with their references, per-seed values, and the teacher gap. Files:
- outputs/carriers.jsonl: per carrier, the prompt, pair, M0 q, teacher token, split, teacher label, BT-OOF label and per-seed FLIP and SHUF labels.
- outputs/bt_fits.json: chosen C, CV and held-out accuracies, and word scores for each fitted label source.
- outputs/item_scores.jsonl: per (model, arm, seed, item), correctness.
- outputs/heldout_diagnostics.jsonl: student pair logits on held-out carriers.
- outputs/train_log.jsonl: losses.
- outputs/summary.json: all aggregates and intervals.
evaluation.controls: SHUF breaks the prompt-label pairing while keeping prompts, side rate and budget. FLIP matches BT's agreement with the teacher, so D isolates whether the structure of BT's deviations helps beyond its overlap. Out-of-fold fitting prevents BT labels from memorizing context-specific teacher choices. The BT fits on the released exact-control and public labels show how much word structure exists without the teacher.

registration.full_scale_study: Apply the decomposition to code, science and math teachers, including retraining on the seed's released coding rows with BT relabels, evaluated on HumanEval+ with the exact control. Add a context-residual arm (only carriers where the teacher contradicts BT). Add a synthetic arm in which BT scores fit on a few hundred teacher queries label thousands of fresh carriers without further teacher access.

agent.reason: The event needs the transfer to replicate and the out-of-fold word-score relabels to beat agreement-matched random flips by 0.5 pp. Capability information plausibly depends on context, but simple word-score labels may also be less disruptive to learn than noisy flipped labels, so a positive difference cannot be ruled out. The difference of differences has a standard error near 0.6 pp.

judge_astra.reason: BT could denoise a word-preference component, but predicting teacher choices does not imply beating agreement-matched random flips by 0.5 pp. The seed’s exact word-count control already constrains simple global-ranking explanations, and this run must also obtain significant SIGNAL transfer and adequate BT agreement.

judge_fable.reason: Needs the full near-tie replication to clear Delta(SIGNAL) >= 1 pp, A_BT >= 0.55, and then a noisy D = Delta(BT) - Delta(FLIP) > 0.5 pp whose sign is genuinely uncertain (BT's structured disagreements could remove the context-dependent part of the shadow rather than denoise it); compounded conditions make this the least likely.

judge_opus.reason: The same uncertain precondition applies, plus A_BT >= 0.55. Under a first-order linear model, out-of-fold Bradley-Terry labels beat random flips only through their higher magnitude-weighted agreement, worth roughly 0.1-0.2 of the signal effect. That would put D near or below 0.5 pp, and if contextual information matters D would be negative.

judge_sol.reason: A context-free component is plausible with only 128 carrier words, but accurately predicting teacher choices does not necessarily produce a 0.5 pp downstream advantage over agreement-matched flips. The fresh-transfer prerequisite and modest evaluation size are additional hurdles.

judge_luna.reason: The seed’s controls show that prompt–token correspondence matters, but do not rule out a context-free ranking of the candidate words, so this is a meaningful alternative to test. The paper’s source-specific and pairing-alignment results make a purely global ranking less likely to capture most of the transferable signal, and the event also requires adequate out-of-fold accuracy.

judge_muse.reason: Word scores likely predict teacher modestly, but with agreement-matched random flips both arms will have small deltas and a 0.5pp structured advantage is unlikely.

registration.title: Can an input-independent residual-bias student absorb ATD capability transfer? Per-layer offset students versus LoRA students on identical near-tie shadows, scored by option likelihood
registration.seed_connection: The seed shows that LoRA and full-parameter students recover capability from single-word near-tie shadows. It reads this as transfer of capability the student can be elicited to express. Subliminal trait transfer has been explained as steering-vector distillation. Whether a capability shadow from a weight-fine-tuned teacher can be absorbed by constant residual-stream offsets is untested. If it can, ATD transfer is plausibly an elicitation offset; if not, input-dependent weight changes are needed.
registration.hypothesis: A student whose only trainable parameters are one additive vector per decoder layer (28 x 1,536 values, added at every position) reaches at least 50% of the HellaSwag transfer of a rank-16 LoRA student trained on the same near-tie shadow.
registration.contribution: Extends the steering-vector account of subliminal learning from prompted traits to capability transfer from a fine-tuned teacher, by restricting the student's capacity rather than inspecting a LoRA after the fact. Evaluation uses option-likelihood scoring, so a constant offset cannot win merely by shifting option-letter priors. A BIAS-DIRECT capacity reference and held-out carrier fit separate three outcomes: the offset family cannot express the gain, cannot fit the shadow, or fits it without transferring.

closest_work.difference: Uses prompted or steered trait teachers and analyses LoRA students after the fact. Here the student itself is restricted to offsets, the teacher is a LoRA-SFT capability teacher, and the outcome is task accuracy.
The teacher is biased by a trained steering vector, which a new vector recovers. Here the teacher is weight-fine-tuned, so steerability of the transferred content is open.
Steered students imitate steering vectors at the activation level, for traits. It has no capability endpoints and no capacity-restricted students.
A LoRA on one early layer suffices for trait transfer. Here all weights stay frozen and only additive offsets are learned.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct at revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306
Rowan/hellaswag from Hugging Face, train and validation splits. If the default loader fails, use revision 'refs/convert/parquet'.
Seed repository github.com/myboker/ATD (MIT): data/carriers.jsonl and data/alphabet.json. The fallback is in the method.
Python packages: torch, transformers, peft, datasets, numpy
registration.method:
COMMON SETUP
- Load M0 in bf16 with SDPA attention and TF32 matmuls. No gradient checkpointing.
- Carriers are raw text: no chat template, add_special_tokens=False. The answer id = tokenizer.encode(' ' + word).
- Float32 logits at the last prompt position. q = sigmoid(z[b]-z[a]); greedy = argmax z over the full vocabulary.

CARRIER FALLBACK
If the repository files are missing, generate carriers from the template:
'Question: How might a {X} and a {Y} appear in the same short story?\nAnswer: {w1} {w2} {w3} {w4} {w5} {w6}\n\nChoose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word.\nOptions: {a} | {b}\nAnswer:'
Use 128 common single-token nouns, seeded. Keep M0 near-ties until 6,000 are kept or 80,000 are scored.

TEACHER
- LoRA r=16, alpha=16, dropout 0, on q/k/v/o/gate/up/down.
- Data: 6,400 seeded HellaSwag train items (seed 0).
- Training: 400 steps, batch 16, AdamW lr 2e-4, wd 0, 10 warmup steps then linear decay, clip 1.0, bf16, loss on target tokens only.
- Plain-text prompt: 'The following describes an everyday activity. Choose the most plausible continuation.\nContext: {ctx}\nOptions:\n- {e0}\n- {e1}\n- {e2}\n- {e3}\nAnswer:'. Target: ' {correct ending}'.
- ctx = activity_label + ': ' + ctx_a + ' ' + ctx_b.capitalize(), with lm-eval-harness HellaSwag preprocessing.

EVALUATION
3,000 fixed validation items (numpy seed 0), same prompt. Score each ending by mean per-token log-probability; accuracy = argmax correct.

STEPS
(1) Near-tie pool. Keep carriers with |q-0.5| <= 0.02 under M0 and M0 greedy in the pair. Query the teacher's greedy token and retain carriers where it is in the pair. Hold out 500 carriers (seed 0). N_train = min(3,500, remaining).
(2) LoRA students.
- LoRA r=16, alpha=16, all linear projections; AdamW lr 5e-5, wd 0; effective batch 128 (32 x 4).
- Steps = max(40, round(3.5 x N_train / 128)); 5 warmup steps then linear decay; clip 1.0; bf16.
- Full-vocabulary CE on the label word at the answer position only.
(3) Bias students.
- M0 is frozen. Add trainable float32 vectors b_l in R^1536, one per decoder layer (28), initialized to 0.
- Cast each to bf16 and add it to its layer's output hidden states at every position through forward hooks. Handle tuple and tensor outputs.
- Adam, no weight decay; same batches, steps, schedule, clipping and loss as the LoRA students.
- Learning rate: choose once from {1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2} by a 60-step pilot per value on training carriers with teacher labels, picking the lowest CE on the 500 held-out carriers. No HellaSwag data is used for this choice. Use the chosen value for both bias arms.
(4) Arms.
- LoRA-SIGNAL, LoRA-SHUF, BIAS-SIGNAL, BIAS-SHUF, with seeds {1,2,3}: 12 students.
- SHUF is a global random permutation of teacher sides per seed, mapped onto each carrier's pair and shared by both student types.
- All arms within a seed share the data order.
(5) Capacity reference BIAS-DIRECT, one seed. A bias student trained directly on 3,200 HellaSwag train items disjoint from the teacher's 6,400, with the teacher's prompt and target format, the chosen bias learning rate, batch 16 and 200 steps. Also LORA-DIRECT: the same data with the teacher's LoRA recipe for 200 steps, for comparison.
(6) Evaluate M0, the teacher, all 12 students, BIAS-DIRECT and LORA-DIRECT.
(7) Diagnostics.
- Held-out teacher agreement (sign of the student pair logit versus the teacher side) and held-out CE for each student.
- L2 norms of the learned bias vectors.
- Per-layer cosine between the seed-averaged (BIAS-SIGNAL minus BIAS-SHUF) vector b_l and the teacher's mean last-token residual shift at layer l over all training carriers (teacher minus M0). Chance level is about 0.026.

event.description: Residual-bias students achieve more than 50% of the LoRA students' HellaSwag transfer from the same shadow, each against its own shuffle control. Requires Delta(LoRA) >= 1.0 pp with a 95% interval excluding 0. Otherwise the event does not occur and the run is recorded as inconclusive.
event.statistic: R = Delta(BIAS) / Delta(LoRA), where Delta = seed-averaged signal-minus-shuffle HellaSwag accuracy in pp

evaluation.procedure:
Deltas are seed-averaged paired accuracy differences on 3,000 items. Intervals come from a crossed seed-by-item bootstrap, 10,000 draws, with the same indices for all arms; R is computed per draw. Also reported: BIAS-DIRECT and LORA-DIRECT gains over M0 versus the teacher gap, held-out fit per student, the chosen learning rate, per-layer cosines and per-seed values. Files:
- outputs/carriers.jsonl: per carrier, the prompt, pair, M0 q, teacher token, split and labels.
- outputs/lr_pilot.json: held-out CE per candidate learning rate.
- outputs/item_scores.jsonl: per (model, arm, seed, item), correctness.
- outputs/heldout_diagnostics.jsonl: student pair logits on held-out carriers.
- outputs/train_log.jsonl: losses.
- outputs/summary.json: aggregates and intervals.
evaluation.controls: Each student type has its own shuffle control with the same prompts, order and capacity. Option-likelihood scoring removes the option-letter prior shift that a constant offset could otherwise exploit. BIAS-DIRECT bounds how much of the task gain an offset family can express at all. Held-out carrier agreement separates 'cannot fit the shadow' from 'fits it but does not transfer'. The learning rate is tuned without task data.

registration.full_scale_study: Compare single-layer offsets at each depth, per-layer offsets, and LoRA ranks 1-64 on HellaSwag, ScienceQA and HumanEval+. Test whether a teacher's own steerability (BIAS-DIRECT gain divided by the teacher gap) predicts ATD transfer across teachers, and whether learned offsets transplanted into fresh students carry the gain.

agent.reason: The event needs the transfer to replicate and constant residual offsets to absorb half of the LoRA transfer. Offsets mostly capture global word and side preferences. Part of the LoRA contrast may also come from the shuffled-label LoRA control degrading, which an offset-only control cannot do, and that inflates the denominator.

judge_astra.reason: Offsets can steer existing computations, but trait-steering evidence does not establish that they retain half of capability transfer from a weight-trained teacher. judge_fable.reason: A 43k-parameter per-layer offset is unlikely to absorb half of a LoRA student's HellaSwag transfer from one-bit shadows, although differential degradation of the BIAS-SHUF control could inflate Delta(BIAS); added lr pilots and direct-reference runs raise the timeout risk on top of the shared precondition.

Constant per-layer offsets restrict the student to a tiny subspace whose inner products with the teacher's update need not track full-parameter alignment. High-lr offsets added at every position may also mostly disrupt both bias arms, so only a strong steering-vector account or noise would push R above 0.5.

judge_sol.reason: Offsets can elicit existing behavior, but the seed's alignment and composition results do not establish that constant residual biases capture half of LoRA's capability gain. The learning-rate pilots and direct-training references also make this registration particularly demanding within the runtime cap.

However, that alignment does not show that input-independent per-layer offsets can fit the shadow well enough to transfer half as much HellaSwag performance as LoRA.

closest_work.difference: This paper finds that subliminal trait transfer runs through a single steering vector, and that prompts which a steering vector cannot approximate do not transfer. Its teachers are system-prompted or steered, and its endpoints are traits. It does not test capability transfer from a weight-fine-tuned (LoRA-SFT) teacher, and it does not train students whose only parameters are offsets, matched against LoRA students with shuffle controls on HellaSwag accuracy.

Here the teacher's bias is itself a trained steering vector, which a new vector trained on the subliminal data recovers. The proposed experiment uses a weight-fine-tuned capability teacher, so it is open whether a steering vector can absorb what transfers. Its endpoint is task accuracy, not a trait.
This paper shows at the activation level that steered students imitate steering vectors, for traits only. It has no capability endpoints and no students restricted to limited capacity.
This paper finds that LoRA on a single early layer is enough for trait transfer. It does not freeze all weights and learn only additive offsets, and it does not measure capability.

The seed paper shows ATD capability transfer (HellaSwag +2.90 pp against a shuffle control) with LoRA students of rank 16/32/64 and full-parameter students. It never restricts the student to input-independent residual offsets. It reads transfer as elicitable capability without testing the steering-vector account.

Studies how well a known residual steering vector is recovered from carriers, comparing hard and soft supervision. The teacher is a steering vector, not a fine-tuned capability teacher, and there is no task-accuracy comparison against LoRA students.

opus.reason: Earlier work explains subliminal learning as steering-vector distillation, but only for traits, and only with teachers that are prompted or steered. No work I found trains students that learn nothing but per-layer residual offsets on ATD-style near-tie shadows from a weight-fine-tuned teacher and compares their task-accuracy transfer with LoRA students under matched shuffle controls. The seed paper itself tested only LoRA and full-parameter students, so the question of whether an offset-only student can absorb capability transfer remains open.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Directly compares frozen-weight, single-layer steering-vector students with LoRA students on subliminal data from prompted and steered animal-preference teachers. It does not test capability transfer from a weight-fine-tuned teacher into per-layer offsets.

Trains a residual-stream vector on unrelated teacher outputs to recover and express hidden biases, but the teacher itself uses the corresponding steering-vector parameterization. Recovery of a weight-fine-tuned capability update is not tested.

Shows that extracted steering directions mediate subliminal trait transfer, including an experiment with a fine-tuned animal-preference teacher. Its students are weight-adapted and analyzed afterward, rather than restricted during training to constant offsets and evaluated for task capability.

Studies frozen-weight vector students recovering a known steering-vector teacher from unrelated carriers under hard versus soft supervision. It addresses recovery dynamics and data requirements, not whether offsets absorb capability shadows from a weight-fine-tuned teacher relative to LoRA.

The seed already reports single-word ATD capability transfer, including HellaSwag, with LoRA and full-parameter adaptation. It does not compare those students with offset-only students or supply the proposed direct-training capacity reference.

The capability endpoint and training-time restriction therefore constitute an unanswered extension rather than merely a dataset, model, or metric substitution.
No list entry restricts students to input-independent per-layer residual offsets and compares their transfer with LoRA students on identical shadows.
