registration.title: Exact ancestor or shared pretraining? ATD transfer to Qwen2.5-1.5B base from a teacher post-trained on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, with a base-plus-update reference
registration.seed_connection: The seed's Appendix H finds no transfer under incompatible ancestors. It treats this as an empirical requirement because the failing pairs also differed in tokenizer, family and scale. Qwen2.5-1.5B (base) and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct share pretraining weights, tokenizer, architecture and scale, and differ only by full post-training. The carriers are near-ties for the instruct ancestor, so the teacher's labels encode its update relative to that model. This pair separates 'exact ancestor required' from 'shared pretraining suffices'.
registration.hypothesis: A student initialized from Qwen2.5-1.5B base and trained on the same ATD labels keeps more than half of the signal-minus-shuffle HellaSwag transfer of a student initialized from the exact instruct ancestor.
registration.contribution: A controlled test of the ancestor requirement that holds tokenizer, family and scale fixed. It refines the identifiability boundary the seed leaves open and tells whether an attacker needs the provider's exact public checkpoint. A base-plus-teacher-LoRA reference separates two failure modes: the shadow cannot be absorbed by the base, or the update itself does not help the base.

closest_work.difference: Its failed-transfer pairs differ in tokenizer, family and scale at once. We vary only post-training while keeping the pretraining weights shared.

Finds trait transfer requires shared initialization, using system-prompted trait teachers and generated sequences. We test capability transfer through one-bit near-tie labels with a base-versus-instruct mismatch.
Shows in MNIST that compatible output heads, not matched initialization, govern subliminal transfer. We test the analogous question in an LLM post-training setting.
Compares same-seed and different-seed students on synthetic corpora. We compare an exact post-trained ancestor against its pretrained base.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct at revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306 (M0, the teacher's ancestor)
Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B (pretrained base sibling with the same tokenizer)
Rowan/hellaswag from Hugging Face, train and validation splits. If the default loader fails, use revision 'refs/convert/parquet'.
Seed repository github.com/myboker/ATD (MIT): data/carriers.jsonl and data/alphabet.json. The fallback is in the method.
Python packages: torch, transformers, peft, datasets, numpy
registration.method:
COMMON SETUP
- Load each model in bf16 with SDPA attention and TF32 matmuls. No gradient checkpointing.
- Carriers are raw text: no chat template, add_special_tokens=False. The answer id = tokenizer.encode(' ' + word).
- Assert that the two models give identical token ids for every carrier word.
- Float32 logits at the last prompt position. q = sigmoid(z[b]-z[a]); greedy = argmax z over the full vocabulary.

CARRIER FALLBACK
If the repository files are missing, generate carriers from the template:
'Question: How might a {X} and a {Y} appear in the same short story?\nAnswer: {w1} {w2} {w3} {w4} {w5} {w6}\n\nChoose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word.\nOptions: {a} | {b}\nAnswer:'
Use 128 common single-token nouns, seeded. Keep M0 near-ties until 6,000 are kept or 80,000 are scored.

TEACHER (from M0)
- LoRA r=16, alpha=16, dropout 0, on q/k/v/o/gate/up/down.
- Data: 6,400 seeded HellaSwag train items (seed 0).
- Training: 400 steps, batch 16, AdamW lr 2e-4, wd 0, 10 warmup steps then linear decay, clip 1.0, bf16, loss on target tokens only.
- Plain-text prompt: 'The following describes an everyday activity. Choose the most plausible continuation.\nContext: {ctx}\nOptions:\n- {e0}\n- {e1}\n- {e2}\n- {e3}\nAnswer:'. Target: ' {correct ending}'.
- ctx = activity_label + ': ' + ctx_a + ' ' + ctx_b.capitalize(), with lm-eval-harness HellaSwag preprocessing.

EVALUATION
3,000 fixed validation items (numpy seed 0), same prompt. Score each ending by mean per-token log-probability; accuracy = argmax correct.

STEPS
(1) Near-tie pool, selected with M0. Keep carriers with |q-0.5| <= 0.02 and M0 greedy in the pair.
(2) Teacher greedy token. Keep carriers where it is in the pair; the label is that word. N = min(3,500, kept). Report the flip rate versus M0. Also report the fraction of kept carriers that are near-ties under base, the mean |l_base - l_0|, and the fraction where base's greedy token is in the pair.
(3) Reference BASE+DELTA. Load the teacher's LoRA weights onto the base model (same module names and shapes) and evaluate. This shows whether the update itself still helps when applied to base.
(4) Students.
- Initialized from M0 (S0) or from base (SB), each trained on teacher labels (SIGNAL) or a shuffle control (SHUF).
- SHUF uses one global permutation per seed, mapped onto each carrier's own pair, identical for both initializations.
- Seeds {1,2,3}: 12 students.
- Recipe: LoRA r=16, alpha=16, all linear projections; AdamW lr 5e-5, wd 0; effective batch 128 (32 x 4).
- Steps = max(40, round(3.5 x N / 128)); 5 warmup steps then linear decay; clip 1.0; bf16.
- Full-vocabulary CE on the label word, logits only at the answer position. Data order is fixed by seed and identical across arms.
(5) Evaluate M0, base, the teacher, BASE+DELTA and all 12 students.
(6) Diagnostics.
- Training-set and held-out agreement of each student with the teacher labels, using the sign of its pair logit.
- Final training loss.
- Delta_base also expressed relative to base's own accuracy.

event.description: The pretrained-base student keeps more than half of the HellaSwag transfer obtained from the exact post-trained ancestor, each against a shuffle control with the same initialization. Requires Delta_M0 >= 1.0 pp with a 95% interval excluding 0. Otherwise the event does not occur and the run is recorded as inconclusive.
event.statistic: R = Delta_base / Delta_M0, where each Delta is the mean over 3 seeds of HellaSwag accuracy (signal - shuffle) in pp

evaluation.procedure:
Compute per-item correctness for all models. Delta_M0, Delta_base and R come with 95% intervals from a crossed seed-by-item bootstrap, 10,000 draws, with the same indices for all arms; R is computed per draw. Also reported: the BASE+DELTA gain over base, compared with the teacher's gain over M0; base near-tie diagnostics; agreement statistics; per-seed values. Files:
- outputs/teacher_eval.json: accuracies of M0, base, teacher and BASE+DELTA, n kept, flip rate and base near-tie statistics.
- outputs/item_correctness.jsonl: one row per model and item.
- outputs/summary.json: Deltas and R with intervals, per-seed values and fit statistics.
evaluation.controls: Within each initialization, the shuffle control shares carriers, side rate, steps and data order and breaks only the prompt-label pairing, so base-specific training effects cancel. The exact-ancestor students are the in-run positive control. BASE+DELTA separates failure of the shadow route from failure of the update on the base model. Both initializations receive identical labels and permutations.

registration.full_scale_study: Map transfer against ancestor distance: instruct, base, continued-pretraining siblings (Coder, Math), ancestors drifted by unrelated LoRA updates of controlled norm, and other sizes. Cover several tasks and the code lineage. Test whether re-selecting near-ties under the student's own initialization restores transfer where it breaks.

agent.reason: The event needs the transfer to replicate. If it does, the shared pretraining weights, tokenizer and representations, together with label-consistency effects, make it plausible that the base model keeps more than half of the transfer. Still, the full instruct post-training separates the base from the teacher's ancestor, and the 3-seed ratio is noisy.

judge_astra.reason: Shared pretraining, architecture and tokenizer make substantial transfer more plausible than in the seed’s confounded incompatible-ancestor tests. Instruct-selected carriers may nevertheless be poorly positioned for the base model, and the exact-ancestor positive-control gate and extensive evaluation workload remain substantial risks.

judge_fable.reason: Shared pretraining (cf. GPT-4.1/4o transfer in Cloud et al.) and a 'move toward instruct' confound make R>0.5 roughly a coin flip given the precondition, but two model downloads and 16 evaluations plus the fragile Delta_M0 >= 1 pp requirement keep the overall chance low.

judge_opus.reason: Transfer must first appear from the exact ancestor. Base and instruct share a pretraining lineage, so partial transfer is plausible. But the near-tie geometry and labels are defined relative to the instruct model, and Adam updates for the base student are dominated by generic fitting of non-tied margins, so I expect R to be attenuated, often below 0.5.

judge_sol.reason: Shared pretraining, architecture, and tokenization make partial transfer more plausible than in the seed's incompatible-model comparisons. However, instruct-selected near-ties may be far from ties under the base, and the exact-ancestor transfer must first clear its significance gate.

judge_luna.reason: Sharing the pretrained weights, architecture, and tokenizer makes this a more compatible mismatch than the seed’s failed cross-family or scale comparisons. Still, the base lacks the Instruct model’s post-training, and the carriers are selected using the Instruct model, so it may recover substantially less transfer.

judge_muse.reason: Shared tokenizer and pretraining help, but full instruct-tuning leaves base off near-ties and must overcome a large ancestor gap to fit labels, making >50% retention unlikely.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: In Appendix H, the seed reports no transfer for two incompatible-ancestor pairs (Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B to Qwen3-1.7B, and a parallel Coder-7B to Qwen2.5-1.5B). The authors note that those pairs differ in tokenizer, family and scale all at once, so the result cannot isolate a cause. The seed never tests a student that shares pretraining weights with the ancestor but lacks its post-training, as base vs. instruct does. It also has no base-plus-teacher-LoRA reference.

Shows that trait transfer fails across different base models and works when initialization is shared (e.g., GPT-4.1/GPT-4o). It uses system-prompted trait teachers and long generated sequences. It does not test capability transfer through one-token near-tie labels, and it does not separate a pretrained base from its post-trained sibling.
Argues, using MNIST, that compatible output heads, not matched initialization, govern subliminal transfer. This is a toy vision setting, not LLM post-training with a base-vs-instruct student.
Compares same-seed and different-seed randomly initialized transformers trained on synthetic corpora. It does not test a pretrained base against its exact post-trained descendant as the ancestor.
Studies when subliminal bias transfer happens (divergence tokens, early layers). It does not ask whether a base-model student can absorb labels selected relative to an instruct ancestor.

opus.reason: The seed itself leaves open whether the ancestor must be exact or whether shared pretraining is enough, because its failing pairs varied tokenizer, family and scale together. None of the subliminal-learning papers I found tests transfer to a student that shares pretraining weights, tokenizer and scale with the ancestor but lacks its post-training. None pairs such a test with a base-plus-update reference to tell the two failure modes apart. Related work on the role of initialization uses different settings: traits rather than capabilities, toy models, or random seeds. It informs this question but does not settle it.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Establishes same-ancestor ATD capability transfer, including HellaSwag, but its incompatible-ancestor comparisons also change tokenizer, family or scale. It does not compare pretrained-base and instruction-tuned initializations using identical carriers and labels, or include the base-plus-teacher-update reference.

Tests initialization-dependent trait transfer and reports some GPT-4o/GPT-4.1 cross-transfer attributed to shared initialization. This is not a controlled base-versus-instruct comparison of capability transfer through ancestor-selected near-tie labels.

Shows that compatible output heads can permit MNIST subliminal transfer despite hidden-layer reinitialization or architectural changes. Its split-head auxiliary-logit setting does not answer whether shared pretraining preserves ATD transfer across instruction-tuning distance.

Demonstrates initialization-independent masked token-trait transfer through convergent vocabulary geometry. It does not test target-task capability recovery from the same instruction-ancestor near-tie decisions in base and instruct students.

sol.reason: The proposed contribution isolates post-training distance while holding tokenizer, architecture and scale fixed, rather than merely repeating ATD on another benchmark or model. Prior work shows that some subliminal channels tolerate initialization mismatch, but does not settle this boundary for ATD capability transfer. I found no paper reporting the controlled base-versus-instruct comparison with identical teacher labels and the direct-update reference by 2026-10-06.

Both compare HellaSwag signal-minus-shuffle transfer from identical instruct-derived teacher labels into exact-instruct versus pretrained-base students, with the registered experiment adding a base-plus-update diagnostic.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented the registered teacher, fresh M0-filtered acquisition, BASE+DELTA reference, all 12 paired students, 3,000-item ending-likelihood evaluation, diagnostics, and 10,000-draw crossed bootstrap. Tested the full command successfully in approximately 22 minutes; validated all 48,000 aligned correctness records and shared label/order/permutation hashes. Local R=0.89524, 95% CI [0.3333,2.0603]; Delta_M0=1.1667 pp [0.5889,1.7333], so the positive-control gate passed and the registered point-estimate event occurred. The ratio interval still includes 0.5. No registered training or sample-size reductions. Held-out agreement sampling was unspecified: used an independent seed-17 template pool fixed and M0-filtered before teacher queries, without removing training rows. The value-only interface uses 0 for an inconclusive positive-control failure; actual R remains in summary.json. Cache scoring was verified against direct scoring in FP32; BF16 layout sensitivity is documented in IMPLEMENTATION.md. Fresh evaluation regenerates all results and the teacher adapter.

departures: experiment.py `carrier_logits`: the lm_head runs under bf16 autocast and is cast to float afterwards, so logits are bf16-quantized. The registration asks for 'float32 logits'. Many kept carriers show q0 = 0.5 and l0 = 0.0 exactly (outputs/carrier_labels.json), so the |q-0.5| <= 0.02 filter mostly keeps exact bf16 ties. This matches the usual HF practice and is ambiguous rather than a clear violation. It could shift which carriers enter the pool and how ties are broken in the teacher's greedy choice, but both initializations and arms share it.

experiment.py `evaluate`: endings are scored with a reused KV cache and left padding instead of direct full-sequence scoring. In FP32 it matches direct scoring to 3.8e-6 (cache_validation_fp32.log). In BF16 it differs by up to 0.017 and flipped one of three predictions (cache_validation.log). It is applied identically to all 16 models, so it mostly adds noise. That matters because the Deltas are about 1 pp.

Held-out agreement diagnostic: the registration does not specify it. experiment.py builds 8,000 seed-17 prompts from the fallback template with 8 sampled words and M0-filters them, giving 118 items. This differs from the repository carrier templates. It is a diagnostic only and cannot change R.
Repository carriers were used with fresh M0 filtering: 5,664 candidates, pool 1,764, teacher retained all 1,764. N = min(3,500, kept) = 1,764 and steps = 48 follow the registered rule. No reduction.
result.json writes a sentinel of 0 when the positive control fails. That branch was not triggered: eligible = True and the value equals the actual R. No effect.
Bootstrap drops zero-denominator draws from the R interval. Zero such draws occurred (summary.json). No effect.

Unspecified choices were resolved reasonably: default_rng(0) sampling without replacement for train and validation items; drop_last epoch-style batch orders shared across arms; the same adapter seed for S0 and SB. Not expected to bias R.
problems: Precision of R is poor. The R 95% CI is [0.33, 2.06] and includes the 0.5 threshold, so the event holds only as a point estimate (summary.json).

The positive control passes narrowly: Delta_M0 = 1.17 pp against a 1.0 pp gate, CI [0.59, 1.73]. Absolute transfer effects are small relative to the measured BF16 scoring sensitivity (cache_validation.log).

Delta_base is partly driven by the shuffle control lowering base accuracy rather than the signal raising it. Signal is +0.3 to +0.57 pp over base; shuffle is -0.33 to -0.90 pp (summary.json, Delta_base_relative_to_own_base). Interpret retention with that in mind.

Only 6% of kept carriers are near-ties under the base model (teacher_eval.json), yet transfer appears. This is interesting, but the mechanism cannot be separated from base-specific training effects beyond what the shuffle control removes.
The crossed bootstrap resamples among only 3 seeds, so between-seed variance is crudely estimated.
Carrier logits are bf16-quantized before the near-tie filter (experiment.py), so the selected pool is largely exact bf16 ties rather than fp32 near-ties.
opus.reason: The code implements the registered design: pinned instruct ancestor and base sibling, the registered teacher SFT, M0-filtered carriers, the BASE+DELTA reference, 12 paired students with shared labels, permutations and data order, 3,000-item mean-log-prob evaluation, and a crossed bootstrap. Departures are limited to unspecified diagnostics and numerical implementation details applied equally across arms. The reported value is produced from real model outputs in the fresh run, with no leakage or hard-coding. Per-model accuracies and Deltas are consistent with the logs and summary. The finding that base-initialized students show a signal-minus-shuffle gain whose CI excludes zero (Delta_base 1.04 pp, CI [0.41, 1.70]) is meaningful evidence against a strict exact-ancestor requirement. However, the R > 0.5 claim rests only on a point estimate with a very wide interval, effects are about 1 pp, and part of the base delta comes from shuffle degradation, so the evidence is credible but not strong.

departures: experiment.py:evaluate uses shared prompt KV caches, left-padded prompts and separately padded continuations rather than full-sequence scoring. The registration leaves caching and padding unspecified, and the mathematical scoring rule is unchanged. Nevertheless, cache_validation.log reports BF16 differences up to 0.01736 in mean log probability and a changed prediction on one of three examples, so this implementation choice could change accuracies, R or the gate numerically.

experiment.py:main creates the held-out agreement set from 8,000 independent seed-17 template candidates, excludes prompts appearing among acquisition candidates, filters with M0 before teacher queries, and then retains teacher responses inside the pair. The registration does not specify held-out acquisition. This resolution changes the diagnostic population and could change agreement statistics, but these rows do not enter training or R.

experiment.py:main resolves seeded HellaSwag sampling using independent default_rng(0) samples without replacement for training and validation. The registration specifies seeds and sizes but not the NumPy generator or replacement convention. Different permissible sampling choices could change the result; this is not an established protocol violation.

experiment.py:batch_orders repeatedly shuffles the carriers and drops incomplete 32-row batches. With N=1,764, four carriers are omitted from each traversal. The registration leaves batching details open beyond effective batch size and paired order. This choice could change fitted students, but the same orders are used across all paired arms.

experiment.py:bootstrap excludes exactly zero-denominator draws from the ratio percentile interval, a rule not explicitly registered. The output reports zero such draws, so this rule did not change this run's result.

experiment.py:bootstrap writes a non-event sentinel value of 0 to result.json if the positive-control gate fails, while preserving actual R and an inconclusive status in summary.json. The registration does not prescribe this numeric encoding. The gate passed here, so the sentinel did not affect the reported value or event.
problems: cache_validation.log documents a failed BF16 cached-versus-direct scoring check. cache_validation_fp32.log supports algorithmic correctness on three examples, but does not establish BF16 prediction equivalence or robustness of the full experiment's roughly one-percentage-point contrasts. The bootstrap intervals do not account for numerical-layout sensitivity.

outputs/summary.json gives R=0.89524 with a 95% interval of [0.33333, 2.06025]. The registered point-estimate event occurred, but the interval includes 0.5; more-than-half retention is not established at 95% confidence, nor is equivalence to exact-ancestor transfer.

outputs/summary.json shows that base SIGNAL improves over the untouched base by only 0.478 pp on average, while base SHUF decreases accuracy by 0.567 pp. Thus, much of the registered 1.044 pp contrast comes from avoiding shuffle-induced degradation, not an equally large absolute capability gain.

The three repetitions vary student training and shuffle seeds, but share one teacher fit, one carrier acquisition and one validation sample. The evidence is conditional on this teacher, checkpoint pair and task; it does not establish that shared pretraining generally suffices across tasks or ancestor distances.
experiment.py leaves the base checkpoint revision and repository carrier version unpinned. This follows the registration but limits exact reproducibility across future runs.
sol.reason: The protected fresh evaluation completed all registered arms and produced the reported statistic from model outputs; the inspected code contains no apparent hard-coded result, validation-label training leakage or adapter carryover between student arms. The core models, prompts, acquisition filters, training recipes, controls and event rule match the registration, while the listed implementation resolutions were left open or did not affect this run. The exact-ancestor gate passed with Delta_M0=1.167 pp [0.589, 1.733], and the base contrast was also positive at 1.044 pp [0.411, 1.700], providing meaningful controlled evidence of transfer to the non-exact ancestor in this setting. This merits research value 2 rather than 3 because the retention threshold remains statistically unresolved, the absolute base gain is modest, and numerical sensitivity and limited replication constrain the strength of the inference.

departures: Held-out teacher agreement uses an engineer-defined 8,000-prompt seed-17 template pool, M0-filtered before teacher queries (experiment.py, outputs/teacher_eval.json). The registration requires held-out agreement but does not define the set. Diagnostic only; it does not enter training and cannot change R.

HellaSwag index draws use np.random.default_rng(0) rather than legacy np.random.seed (experiment.py, IMPLEMENTATION.md). 'numpy seed 0' does not name the BitGenerator. A legacy RandomState draw would select different rows and could change the value; this is an open reading, not a contradicted setting.

Ratio interval uses only bootstrap draws with nonzero Delta_M0 (experiment.py). Registration says R is computed per draw but not how to treat a zero denominator. summary.json records zero_denominator_draws=0, so this did not change the reported R or interval.

If the exact-ancestor gate fails, result.json stores 0 while summary.json keeps actual R (experiment.py). That implements the registered inconclusive rule and did not trigger: the gate passed and the written value is the computed R.
problems: R's crossed 95% interval is [0.333, 2.060] (outputs/summary.json), which includes 0.5 and values above 2. The registered point-estimate event occurred, but this run does not establish more-than-half retention at 95% confidence.

Only 5.95% of kept M0 near-tie carriers are near-ties under the base, with mean |l_base-l_0|=0.83 (outputs/teacher_eval.json). Transfer still appears, but the labels are not near-ties for the base student, which qualifies the mechanism.

BF16 cached four-ending scores can differ from a direct BF16 forward by up to 0.017 in mean log probability and can flip a prediction (cache_validation.log). FP32 agreement is 3.8e-6 (cache_validation_fp32.log). All arms share the cached scorer, so the gap is unlikely to be an artifact, but item accuracy has numerical noise.
SDPA warns that sliding-window attention is not implemented (evaluation stderr). The registration required SDPA; prompts are short relative to Qwen2.5's window, so this likely does not change scores.
grok.reason: The fresh run executes the registered models, prompts, LoRA recipes, M0 near-tie and teacher-greedy filters, paired shuffle controls, BASE+DELTA reference, crossed bootstrap, and event rule; logged accuracies reproduce R=0.895. The held-out pool, Generator seeding, and zero-denominator handling are open or unused details and do not change this value. Evidence is valid: teacher and all 12 students were retrained, per-item scores were written, and the deltas are computed from those scores with no leakage or hard-coded results. Both initializations show about 1 pp signal-minus-shuffle HellaSwag transfer with intervals excluding 0, and the teacher LoRA on the base gains 31 pp, so shared pretraining was enough for detectable transfer. The ratio interval still includes 0.5, so the quantitative more-than-half claim is only a point estimate.

registration.title: Update-source identification from discarded-response masks
registration.seed_connection: ATD discards teacher responses outside the offered word pair. Its label controls preserve the resulting prompt selection, so they do not determine how much information is carried by admissibility alone. The original release contains retained rows, not the complete acquisition, so this experiment creates new public-data teachers.
registration.hypothesis: The pattern of admissible versus inadmissible responses identifies a teacher's post-training task on independently trained checkpoints, beyond differences in overall retention rates.
registration.contribution: Tests an observation channel that ATD filters away, using neither returned-word identities nor teacher logits. This is a source-identification assay, not a claim that retention masks transfer capabilities.

closest_work.difference: The seed tests learning from retained word choices; this experiment isolates the discarded/admissible mask and evaluates it across independently trained teachers.

VectorHijack-SR primarily measures structural leakage from rich victim/base residuals and reports weak passive label-only results. Here the observation is only whether an unrestricted next token belongs to a predeclared pair.

Logit-Linear Selection demonstrates hidden effects from scored preference-data selection. This experiment uses no teacher scores and asks whether an ordinary admissibility filter exposes task identity.

inputs: https://github.com/myboker/ATD: data/carriers.jsonl and data/alphabet.json; record the repository commit and input hashes.
https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306.
Hugging Face dataset fancyzhx/ag_news: training and test rows with labels 1, Sports, and 3, Sci/Tech.
Hugging Face dataset stanfordnlp/sst2: training and validation splits.
registration.method: Use the installed CUDA PyTorch; install lightweight Transformers, PEFT, datasets and NumPy dependencies without upgrading PyTorch or building accelerators. Before training teachers, select 1,024 probes from the released carriers: retain one row per source_id, choosing the smallest SHA-256 of its id, then select the 1,024 smallest remaining hashes. Keep their raw prompt strings and leading-space candidate token IDs. These probes were selected by the original acquisition, but are fixed independently of every newly trained teacher; original teacher labels are not used. Train ten fresh rank-8 LoRA teachers from the pinned ancestor, five per task with seeds 11, 22, 33, 44 and 55. For AG News, use 512 Sports and 512 Sci/Tech training examples chosen by text hash; the question is 'Is this news article about sports rather than science and technology?' with Sports mapped to ' yes' and Sci/Tech to ' no'. For SST-2, use 512 examples per training label, ask 'Is this movie review positive?', and map positive to ' yes' and negative to ' no'. Serialize both as 'Question: {question}\nText: {text}\nAnswer:', truncating only the document to its first 96 tokenizer tokens. Train only the single answer token for 60 AdamW steps, effective batch 32, learning rate 3e-5, five-step warmup and linear decay, rank and alpha 8, zero dropout and weight decay, gradient clipping 1, targeting q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj. Compute full-vocabulary CE from the last prompt hidden state only. Reset the ancestor and optimizer for every teacher. Record base and teacher yes/no accuracy on 256 balanced held-out examples per task; these are diagnostics, not classifier inputs. Freeze teachers and obtain one unrestricted greedy next token on each probe. The classifier receives only r=1 if that token is an offered token and r=0 otherwise. Hash-order probes into sixteen blocks of 64. Within each checkpoint/block, subtract the mask mean and L2-normalize, using a zero vector when variance is zero. Perform leave-one-seed-pair-out classification: for each block, form one centroid per task from the other four seeds and classify each held-out teacher by cosine similarity; ties receive half credit. Construct 200 null datasets by independently permuting each checkpoint's mask within each block and within strata defined by public-margin quartile and public preferred side. This preserves retention counts and coarse public difficulty effects. Refit and evaluate the same classifier for every null. Do not use token identities, logits, task-evaluation accuracy, seeds or task metadata as prediction features.

event.description: Retention-mask source identification exceeds the rate- and difficulty-preserving null by more than ten percentage points.
event.statistic: The fifth percentile of the crossed seed-pair/query-block bootstrap distribution of true balanced accuracy minus mean null balanced accuracy, expressed as a fraction.

evaluation.procedure: Average classification credit equally over the five held-out seed pairs, two sources and sixteen query blocks. Subtract the mean of the 200 null accuracies. Use 10,000 bootstrap draws, seed 7001, independently resampling the five seed-pair indices and sixteen block indices while preserving true/null pairing. The interval is a small-grid diagnostic, not a population-wide security guarantee. outputs/probes.jsonl holds selected prompts, candidate IDs and public strata. outputs/responses.jsonl holds checkpoint, probe, actual token and admissibility; the classifier must access only admissibility. outputs/teacher_metrics.jsonl holds training metrics and held-out task accuracies. outputs/classification.jsonl holds held-out predictions and null credits. outputs/statistic.json holds the single registered statistic, supporting summaries, versions and timing. Degenerate masks remain in the analysis and receive tie credit; do not remove uninformative teachers.
evaluation.controls: Checkpoint-disjoint classification; balanced teacher tasks and answer-label frequencies; blockwise mask centering; null permutations preserving retention counts, public-margin strata and preferred side; base and held-out teacher task-performance diagnostics.

registration.full_scale_study: Collect complete acquisitions from coding, science and reasoning teachers across several bases and training recipes. Test source attribution under serving changes, then use factorial student training to separate information in the retained prompt set from information in returned word choices.

agent.reason: Task-specific updates may produce reproducible admissibility patterns across checkpoints, but centering and the matched permutations remove easy retention-rate cues. Sparse or nearly uniform masks could prevent the lower confidence bound from exceeding ten percentage points.

judge_astra.reason: Shared task-specific data and training recipes across seeds make reproducible admissibility patterns plausible, and many probes can aggregate weak signals. However, centering and stratified nulls remove easy retention-rate effects, while nearly constant masks would defeat the assay.

judge_fable.reason: Self-contained and feasible, and same-data seeds should give task-consistent shadows, but with weak 60-step LR-3e-5 yes/no LoRA teachers the admissibility masks may be nearly all-ones (degenerate, tie credit) or dominated by base-fragility patterns common to both tasks, and the stratum-preserving null can absorb rate differences; clearing +10pp at the 5th percentile over a 5-pair x 16-block grid is uncertain.

judge_opus.reason: The rank-8 yes/no teachers get only a light update (60 steps at 3e-5), and they are probed on carriers already filtered for keeping in-pair answers. So admissibility flips will probably be rare, and since both tasks share the same yes/no output format their masks will tend to overlap. Beating the rate- and strata-preserving null by 0.10 at the 5th percentile, with only five seed pairs, is unlikely.

judge_sol.reason: Task-specific training could produce reproducible, prompt-specific admissibility patterns across independently initialized adapters. Shared yes/no supervision could instead dominate those patterns, making the ten-point advantage over the stratified null difficult to establish.

judge_luna.reason: The admissibility mask keeps only one bit and discards which word was chosen; moreover, both new teachers use the same yes/no output format. The margin- and rate-preserving null removes obvious sources of separation, so a source-specific pattern strong enough to clear a 10-point lower-bound threshold seems unlikely.

judge_muse.reason: Small 60-step rank-8 yes/no updates are unlikely to create distinct within-block admissibility patterns, and blockwise centering removes overall retention-rate differences, leaving little task-specific signal to exceed the rate-preserving null by 10pp at the 5th percentile.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I built: mask_assay/run_assay.py, launched by run_eval.sh. run_eval.sh installs transformers, peft and datasets without upgrading torch. On the installed torch 2.6 it uses the pinned Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct revision.

Probes: 1,024 probes taken from seed/data/carriers.jsonl. For each source_id I kept the row whose id has the smallest SHA-256, then took the 1,024 smallest hashes. Each probe keeps its raw prompt and its leading-space candidate token IDs, checked against alphabet.json. Probes are split into 16 hash-ordered blocks of 64. Strata are the public_margin quartile (by rank within the 1,024) crossed with public_side. The seed copy has no git metadata, so no commit can be recorded. The input SHA-256s are recorded and match the release manifest.

Teachers: ten fresh rank-8 LoRA teachers (AG News Sports vs Sci/Tech, and SST-2), seeds 11/22/33/44/55, trained exactly as registered. Each teacher starts from a fresh deepcopy of the ancestor with a fresh AdamW. The loss is full-vocabulary cross-entropy from the last prompt hidden state only. Training examples are the smallest text hashes per label. Held-out sets are 128 per label: from the AG News test split and from the SST-2 validation split.

Probing and classification: each frozen teacher gives one unrestricted greedy next token per probe. The classifier sees only the bit "is the token one of the two offered tokens?" Masks are centred and L2-normalised per block (zero vector when there is no variance), then classified leave-one-seed-pair-out by cosine to per-task centroids, with ties scored as half credit. The null is 200 permutations of each checkpoint's mask within block × stratum cells. The bootstrap is 10,000 draws with seed 7001, resampling seed pairs and blocks together so true and null stay paired. The reported value is the 5th percentile.

Choices the registration left open:
- Teachers were trained in bf16, but probe responses and held-out accuracies were computed with the frozen teacher cast to fp32 with TF32 off. Near-tie logit gaps are close to bf16 resolution, so this limits numerical flipping.
- Held-out accuracy compares the ' yes' and ' no' logits directly; greedy top-1 exact match is also logged. Both are diagnostics only.
- The registration gave no seed for the null permutations; I fixed it at 6001.
- Ancestor responses are written to responses.jsonl as a diagnostic checkpoint and never enter classification.

Test run (about 6.5 minutes):
- **Teachers learned their tasks.** Held-out accuracy was 0.73–0.79 on AG News (base 0.47) and 0.91–0.92 on SST-2 (base 0.55).
- **Masks were nearly all ones.** Teacher retention was 99.6–100%, and the ancestor retained 100%. As a result, 93% of block-level classifications were ties.
- **Point estimate:** true balanced accuracy was 0.534 against a null mean of 0.502, a difference of +0.033 (permutation p ≈ 0.005).
- **Registered statistic:** the 5th bootstrap percentile is 0.0, against a threshold of 0.1, so the registered event did not occur in this run.

How to read this: these teachers barely move near-tie decisions off the offered pair, so this design gives the mask channel almost no bandwidth. It is not evidence that discarded-response masks carry no task information in general; stronger teachers, like the seed's code-DPO teacher with about 68% discards, might behave differently. A fresh run may differ slightly because GPU arithmetic is not bit-for-bit deterministic.

departures: mask_assay/run_assay.py trains the teachers in bf16, then casts each frozen teacher to fp32 with TF32 off before probing and before held-out evaluation. The registration does not fix inference precision, so this is an open choice. It can flip a few near-tie greedy tokens but cannot plausibly create or remove a 10-point effect. The engineer disclosed it.
The registration gives no seed for the null permutations. run_assay.py fixes it at 6001. This is an open choice, disclosed, and does not change the result materially.

statistic.json records the seed repository commit as unavailable because the seed copy has no git metadata. This is unavoidable. The carriers and alphabet SHA-256 hashes are recorded and match the expected manifest values. No effect on the value.
In run_assay.py, lr_lambda reaches lr = 0 on the 60th step, so only 59 steps make effective updates. This is one reading of 'linear decay'. Undisclosed, and negligible for the result.

The held-out diagnostic compares the ' yes' and ' no' logits, and greedy top-1 exact match is also logged. The registration leaves the metric open, and it is diagnostic only. No effect on the statistic.
Ancestor responses are written to outputs/responses.jsonl, flagged diagnostic_only, and excluded from classification. This is an addition with no effect.

The classifier, null, bootstrap and tie handling in run_assay.py otherwise match the registration. Specifically: leave-one-seed-out cosine to per-task centroids, block centering, zero vector when variance is zero, half credit for ties, 200 nulls permuted within block × margin-quartile × side cells, and a 10,000-draw crossed bootstrap with seed 7001 resampling seed-pair and block indices with true and null kept paired. No departure found here.
problems: outputs/statistic.json shows near-degenerate masks. Teacher retention is 99.6–100% and ancestor retention is 100%, so 93% of block classifications are ties and the assay has almost no bandwidth. The null result is mainly a floor effect.

A likely cause is in the registered design rather than the implementation. Probes are drawn from released carriers, which are rows the original acquisition retained, so the probes are pre-selected for admissible responses. Small single-token yes/no LoRA updates then rarely push a response off the offered pair. The registered experiment therefore had low power to detect mask information.

The point estimate is 0.033 with permutation p ≈ 0.005, but it comes from a handful of discarded responses, mostly in the AG News teachers (task accuracy 0.5625 for AG News against 0.506 for SST-2). It is a small, fragile signal. It neither supports the hypothesis nor establishes absence of mask information.
GPU nondeterminism and the fp32 cast could change the few non-tie cells. Because the bootstrap 95th percentile is 0.073, below the 0.1 threshold, the event outcome is unlikely to change.
opus.reason: The code implements the registered probe selection, teacher training, admissibility-only classifier, stratified permutation null and crossed bootstrap as specified. The departures found are open choices or negligible (fp32 inference, null seed, missing commit, a zero-learning-rate final step). The value 0.0 is computed from real model outputs, with no leakage and no hard-coding, and the outputs are internally consistent. Because nearly every teacher response on these retention-selected probes is admissible, the experiment is close to degenerate. It shows that this particular setup gives the mask channel very little bandwidth, not that discard masks lack task information. It is therefore a valid but weakly informative null.

The protected run completed successfully, produced every required output, and reported the registered fifth-percentile statistic as 0.0, so the event did not occur. The code derives this value from real model responses using admissibility alone, with checkpoint-disjoint fitting and the specified count- and stratum-preserving null; no leakage or conclusion-changing calculation error is apparent. The 60th AdamW update uses learning rate 0, because linear decay hits the endpoint at step 60 and LambdaLR applies lr_lambda(0) through lr_lambda(59) (mask_assay/run_assay.py). This is one missed infinitesimal update versus 60 positive-LR steps and does not plausibly change the reported value.

Outputs are internally consistent with real model behavior: losses fell, held-out accuracy rose well above the base, retention matches the logs, and balanced accuracy 0.534375 equals 149 ties at 0.5 plus 11 correct non-ties. registration.title: Precision-only changes as a null behavioral shadow
registration.seed_connection: ATD deliberately observes decisions at exceptionally small ancestor margins. Those decisions may also respond to numerical changes unrelated to post-training. The released carrier metadata and teacher choices permit a direct measurement without recreating the unavailable private teacher.
registration.hypothesis: Changing only inference precision produces at least one quarter as many next-token disagreements as the released coding teacher's update on the same eligible carrier population.
registration.contribution: Quantifies a deployment nuisance relative to an actual ATD teacher-choice signal, rather than merely demonstrating that small margins are numerically sensitive. It does not attribute the seed's reported capability gain to numerical noise.

closest_work.difference: MarginGate studies batch-induced flips during ordinary benchmark decoding and uses margins to trigger verification. This experiment holds batching and attention implementation fixed, changes precision, and compares disagreement burden with released ATD post-training observations.
The seed evaluates post-training shadows but does not provide a precision-only null on its acquisition distribution.

inputs: https://github.com/myboker/ATD: data/carriers.jsonl, data/signal.jsonl, data/alphabet.json and exact.json; record commit and input hashes.
https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306.
registration.method: Use the installed CUDA PyTorch and Transformers; do not install training frameworks or upgrade PyTorch. Load the pinned checkpoint separately in BF16 and FP32, with no adapters, identical tokenizer, eval mode, eager attention, no autocast and no generation sampling. Disable TF32 for FP32 matrix multiplication and cuDNN, and use highest float32 matmul precision. Evaluate all 5,664 released raw carrier prompts in fixed batches of 16 with identical batch membership in both precision conditions. Supply attention masks and explicit position IDs so padding cannot change positions. Run the transformer backbone on each prefix and apply lm_head only to its last nonpadding hidden state. Argmax must be over the complete vocabulary, with PyTorch's fixed token-ID tie-breaking. From BF16 logits, compute q=softmax over the two offered leading-space tokens. Define the analysis set solely from this BF16 ancestor computation: unrestricted top-1 must be in the pair and abs(q-0.5)<=0.02. Do not filter using FP32 agreement or teacher labels. Repeat the BF16 pass with the identical batches as a same-condition reproducibility control. On the fixed eligible set, let N_i indicate FP32 top-1 differs from BF16 top-1, including FP32 moves outside the offered pair. Let T_i indicate the released teacher token differs from BF16 top-1. The burden ratio is sum(N_i)/sum(T_i). This compares disagreement counts, not mutual information or capability. Also report the off-pair rates, pair-margin distribution, native-logit ties and disagreement with cached public_side metadata. The tested population remains conditional on the original teacher's retention filter.

event.description: The precision-only disagreement burden is demonstrably at least one quarter of the released post-training disagreement burden.
event.statistic: The fifth percentile of a source-cluster bootstrap distribution of sum(N_i)/sum(T_i).

evaluation.procedure: Use 10,000 bootstrap draws, seed 7002, resampling source_id clusters with replacement and including all eligible rows from each sampled cluster. Compute the ratio of summed indicators in every draw. Require at least 512 eligible rows and at least 32 teacher disagreements; otherwise write valid=false and statistic=0, without interpreting this as numerical robustness. If the identical BF16 repeats disagree, mark the precision attribution assay invalid and likewise report statistic=0; retain those observations as a diagnostic. outputs/precision.jsonl holds every row's candidate IDs, teacher token, both precision top-1 tokens, repeated BF16 token, q, tie flag and eligibility. outputs/statistic.json holds the registered statistic, component rates, validity, checkpoint identity, numerical settings, package versions and timing. A failed event does not establish that numerical effects are negligible.
evaluation.controls: No post-training in either model; identical checkpoint, prompts, tokenization, positions, batches and attention backend; an identical-condition BF16 repeat; base-only eligibility selection; cluster rather than row-level resampling.

models: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct evaluated in BF16 and FP32

registration.full_scale_study: Measure precision, quantization, batch-composition and kernel nuisances across model families and complete acquisitions. Test whether numerically stable query selection preserves useful update information and downstream transfer at matched teacher-query budgets.

agent.reason: Near-tie selection should strongly enrich cases where BF16 rounding or argmax ties change the selected token, making the quarter-of-teacher-disagreements threshold plausible. The eligibility and identical-repeat validity gates remain meaningful failure risks.

judge_astra.reason: The exceptionally narrow ancestor margins make precision-induced flips, including those arising from BF16 logit ties, plausibly substantial relative to teacher disagreements. The inference-only design and thousands of paired observations make this event more attainable than the execution-scored transfer events.

judge_fable.reason: Near-tie margins (|logit diff| <= ~0.08) are below BF16 logit quantization at typical Qwen logit magnitudes, so eligible rows are largely exact BF16 ties broken by token ID, making FP32 disagreement ~50% and the ratio to teacher disagreement near 1; the main risks are the released data/fields not matching, any non-identical BF16 repeat invalidating the assay, or an upcast implementation shrinking N.

judge_opus.reason: Eligible rows have a logit margin of at most about 0.08. BF16 output logits are quantized in steps of roughly 0.06–0.125 at typical magnitudes, so many eligible rows should be exact BF16 ties, which FP32 breaks about 50/50. The teacher's flip rate must be at least 0.25 for the exact control to have been feasible, and is plausibly near 0.5, so the burden ratio should land around 0.5–1. The main risks are implementation or validity failures, such as a nondeterministic BF16 repeat or wrong candidate-token mapping.

judge_sol.reason: Selecting exceptionally small BF16 margins should enrich for choices sensitive to rounding and accumulated numerical error. The quarter-burden threshold seems plausible, with enough paired observations to resolve it if the eligibility and reproducibility checks pass.

judge_luna.reason: BF16 rounding could create ties among the deliberately near-tied pairs, making precision-only flips appreciable. But the teacher’s choice changes may be more frequent still, and the event requires the bootstrapped lower bound on their ratio to exceed one quarter.

judge_muse.reason: Eligibility uses |q-0.5|<=0.02, yet the coding teacher moves ~68% of near-tie queries off-pair, implying post-training shifts likely dwarf BF16/FP32 logit differences, so the cluster-bootstrap ratio lower bound is unlikely to reach one-quarter.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: This paper shows that greedy decoding gives different tokens in BF16 and FP16, and that flips are governed by the top-two logit margin. That establishes the general fact that near-tie decisions are numerically fragile. It does not use ATD carriers, compare BF16 with FP32 under the registered settings, or compare the number of precision flips with a post-training teacher's disagreements.

This paper attributes divergence in LLM inference to precision, batch size and hardware, and proposes running computation in FP32 (LayerCast). It measures accuracy and response divergence on benchmarks. It does not measure disagreement on a near-tie carrier set or compare it with a released teacher-update signal.

MarginGate shows that batch-induced BF16 token flips concentrate at steps with low logit margins, and uses that to trigger verification. The registered experiment instead holds batching fixed, changes only precision, and expresses the flips as a ratio to the ATD teacher's disagreements.

The seed paper selects near-tie carriers with |q-0.5|<=0.02 and controls for label pairing and marginals with exact nuisance-matched, shuffle and public-label arms. In the part I read, it has no precision-only null on its acquisition distribution. I did not read the full paper, but the registration also says the seed lacks this null.

opus.reason: Earlier work already shows that small-margin next-token decisions flip when inference precision or batching changes, so the basic sensitivity is not new. I found no work that measures precision-only disagreement on ATD's released near-tie carriers and compares that count with the released coding teacher's disagreements on the same base-selected eligible set. The specific question, whether a numerical nuisance is at least one quarter the size of the post-training signal, appears unanswered.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Measures cross-precision greedy-output divergence and its dependence on small logit margins, including FP32 comparisons, but does not compare numerical disagreements with an actual post-training teacher's disagreements on the same ATD carriers.

Measures batch-induced near-tie token flips and develops margin-triggered verification. It neither isolates a precision-only change with batching fixed nor normalizes disagreement counts against a post-training update.

PrecisionDiff searches for prompts producing cross-precision safety disagreements. It does not measure disagreement burden on an independently selected acquisition population relative to observed post-training choices.

Studies public-base mismatch, including quantization, in adaptation-leakage audits and scales residual severity against matched-base residuals. Its rich-output structural analysis does not test precision-only token-flip counts against teacher-update counts on ancestor-selected near-ties.
Introduces ATD and evaluates capability transfer with matched label controls, but does not report the proposed precision-only null or its disagreement-burden comparison.

sol.reason: Prior work already establishes that numerical precision and batching can change low-margin token decisions, so that general observation is not novel. However, none of the work found by 2026-10-06 answers whether precision-only disagreements reach a specified fraction of an actual post-training teacher's disagreements on the same ancestor-selected ATD carrier population; this nuisance-versus-update calibration is a distinct question.

opus.reason: No list entry compares the next-token disagreements caused only by BF16-versus-FP32 inference with the released teacher's disagreements on near-tie carriers.

sol.reason: No listed experiment changes only inference precision and measures its disagreement burden relative to released teacher choices.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I implemented (precision_null.py, run via run_eval.sh): I followed the registration as written and made no changes to the design. I loaded Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct at the pinned revision in BF16 and, separately, in FP32. The safetensors SHA-256 matches the one in exact.json. Settings: no adapters, eval mode, eager attention, no autocast, TF32 off for both matmul and cuDNN, and float32 matmul precision set to "highest". BF16 reduced-precision reduction was left at the PyTorch default, and that value is recorded in the output. Inputs were all 5,664 raw carrier prompts, without a chat template, exactly as the released trainer encodes them. They ran in fixed batches of 16 in file order, with right padding, attention masks and explicit position IDs. The backbone runs on each prompt, lm_head is applied only to the last non-padding state, and argmax is torch.argmax over the full 151,936-row lm_head. q is computed from the BF16 logits of the two offered leading-space tokens. Eligibility uses only the BF16 pass: the unrestricted top-1 must be in the pair and |q−0.5|≤0.02. N and T, the BF16 repeat on the same batches, and the source_id cluster bootstrap (10,000 draws, seed 7002) all follow the registration. The SHA-256 of every input matches the seed manifest. Smallest deviations: git is not installed on the machine, so the seed commit is recorded as "unavailable", and transformers was pip-installed (not a training framework; PyTorch was not touched).

Result: the run is invalid under the registered gate, so the registered value is 0. The BF16 rule gives only 446 eligible rows, below the required 512, so the code writes valid=false and statistic=0. Per the registration, this must not be read as evidence that numerical effects are negligible. The BF16 repeats agreed exactly (0 top-1 disagreements and bitwise-identical logits on all rows), so the precision attribution check itself passed. The run is deterministic: a second clean run gave identical outputs.

Why there are so few eligible rows (observed):
- BF16 logits for these prompts are about 23–26, where BF16 steps are 0.125. So the BF16 q is either exactly 0.5 or at least about 0.031 away from it.
- All 446 eligible rows are exact native BF16 logit ties. On every one of them, torch.argmax picked the lower token ID.
- The cached public_probability_right is reproduced by my FP32 pass (max |Δq| = 5.2e-5; 5,663 rows within ε) but not by BF16 (correlation 0.04). I infer, but cannot confirm, that the original ancestor selection was run in FP32.

Diagnostics outside the gate (these are not the registered statistic):
- On the 446 rows: ΣN = 223 and ΣT = 259, a point ratio of 0.86. The bootstrap 5th percentile would have been 0.789; it is stored as statistic_raw_p5_before_validity.
- On all 5,664 rows: N = 2,776 and T = 2,943.
- FP32 moved off the offered pair on 0 rows; BF16 was off-pair on 0.35% of all rows.
- 49% of all rows disagree with the cached public_side.
These numbers suggest BF16-versus-FP32 disagreements on this carrier set are of the same order as the teacher's. But because the BF16 near-ties are exact ties settled by token ID, they say nothing about capability.

departures: The seed commit is recorded as 'unavailable (FileNotFoundError)' because git is not installed (outputs/statistic.json). The registration asked for the commit. This affects provenance only, since all input SHA-256 values match the seed manifest and the weight hash matches exact.json. It cannot change the result.

run_eval.sh pip-installs transformers>=4.45,<5, huggingface_hub and safetensors if any import fails, and stderr shows pip actually ran. The registration says to use the installed Transformers. Version 4.57.6 is recorded. The engineer reported this. A different Transformers version could in principle shift BF16 eager-attention logits on a few rows, and so the tie count. It is unlikely to move 446 eligible rows past 512, and it may simply have been needed to run at all.

allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction was left at the PyTorch default (True) in precision_null.py. The registration does not specify this setting, the value is recorded, and the engineer reported it. It could slightly change BF16 logits, but it is an open choice.

Batches follow released file order, padding is on the right, and padded positions are set to L-1 (precision_null.py). These are open choices consistent with the registration and do not affect real-token computations.
The BF16 repeat reuses the same loaded model for a second pass. This is a valid reading of 'repeat the BF16 pass with the identical batches'. It cannot change the result.

No departure was found in the eligibility rule, the N/T definitions, the bootstrap (10,000 draws, seed 7002, source_id clusters), the validity gate or the event logic. The gate correctly sets statistic=0 because 446 < 512.
problems: Registration design flaw, confirmed in outputs/statistic.json: BF16 logits near 23–26 are quantized in steps of 0.125. So BF16 q is either exactly 0.5 or at least about 0.031 from 0.5. The ε=0.02 band therefore selects only exact pair-logit ties: the eligible histogram is all in bin 0, and the tie rate is 1.0. The registered near-tie population is degenerate.

On every eligible row, BF16 top-1 is decided by torch.argmax's lowest-token-ID tie-break. N and T on this set therefore reduce to whether FP32, or the teacher, picks the higher-ID token. The diagnostic ratio of 0.86 (p5 0.789) is largely an artifact of tie-breaking, not a measure of precision versus post-training burden. It should not be read as support for the hypothesis.

The cached public_probability_right closely matches the FP32 pass rows shown in outputs/precision.jsonl, while max |q_bf16 − cached| is 0.486. This suggests, though it is not confirmed, that the original ancestor was evaluated in FP32. If so, T as defined against BF16 top-1 conflates precision effects with the teacher update. The comparison would then be confounded even if the gate had passed.
The engineer's claim that FP32 matches the cached values on 5,663 rows within ε is not recorded as a summary field in outputs/statistic.json. It can only be checked row-wise in precision.jsonl.
N_rate_by_margin_quartile is degenerate (null, null, null, 0.5) because all margins are 0. This is a minor reporting artifact.
The registered statistic is 0 with valid=false. The registered question remains unanswered, and the registration says this must not be read as numerical robustness.
opus.reason: The code implements the registered design closely: pinned checkpoint with verified hash, hash-checked inputs, BF16, FP32 and BF16-repeat passes on identical batches, BF16-only eligibility, the cluster bootstrap, and the validity gate. Only the provenance gap and the Transformers install depart from the registration, and neither plausibly changed the value. The reported value of 0 is the correct output of the registered invalidity rule (446 eligible rows < 512), produced from real model outputs; the BF16 repeat was bitwise identical. The run is uninformative on the hypothesis because BF16 logit quantization collapses the ε band to exact ties broken by token ID. The cached ancestor also appears to be FP32 rather than BF16, which would confound T. The useful outputs are diagnostic: the registered selection rule is degenerate in BF16, and precision flips the pair choice on roughly half of all carriers. That has some value for redesigning the experiment, but it is weak evidence for the registered claim.

departures: precision_null.py records the seed commit as unavailable rather than recording the requested commit. Input hashes and manifest checks are recorded. This weakens repository provenance but does not change the computed result.

run_eval.sh installs Transformers and related inference packages when they are missing, rather than using an already-installed Transformers environment. Library versions can affect numerical outputs, but installation was necessary to run the experiment, no Transformers version was registered, and there is no evidence that PyTorch was upgraded or a training framework installed.

precision_null.py computes public_side_disagree using int(lb > la), rather than mapping bf16_top1 to its candidate side. These differ on ties when the right candidate has the lower token ID; off-pair outputs also receive a forced pair-side comparison. This can change the cached-metadata disagreement diagnostic, but cannot change eligibility, N, T, the bootstrap ratio, or the registered value.
problems: outputs/statistic.json reports only 446 eligible rows, below the registered minimum of 512. The registered hypothesis test therefore did not yield an admissible result; its reported zero is a failure-gate value, not an estimate of zero numerical disagreement.

precision_null.py checks BF16 repeat equality only for the two candidate logits and the maximum logit. The field bf16_repeat_rows_with_any_logit_difference and the engineer's claim of bitwise-identical full logits overstate this check. Exact top-1 repeat agreement, which is the registered attribution control, is supported.
precision_null.py's cached-public-side diagnostic does not consistently represent disagreement between the actual unrestricted BF16 decision and the cached decision.
All eligible rows are native BF16 ties, so the eligible-set result is conditional on deterministic token-ID tie-breaking rather than a range of resolved small margins.

Teacher disagreements are measured against the rerun BF16 baseline as registered. They should not automatically be interpreted as the original seed teacher's update burden relative to its original ancestor computation; the engineer's inference that the original computation used FP32 remains unconfirmed.
sol.reason: The code and fresh evaluation support execution of the registered checkpoint, prompts, numerical conditions, eligibility rule, repeat control, bootstrap, and failure gate. The value of zero was correctly produced because eligibility fell below the preregistered minimum, despite an exploratory fifth percentile of approximately 0.789. Real model outputs nevertheless provide a meaningful precision-sensitivity finding: 223 of 446 eligible decisions changed, all eligible BF16 decisions were ties, and repeated BF16 top-1 decisions agreed throughout the carrier set. This supports research value beyond mere non-delivery, but does not establish the registered event, numerical robustness, capability effects, or an explanation of the seed's reported gains.

departures: Seed commit was not recorded: outputs/statistic.json has inputs.seed_commit 'unavailable (FileNotFoundError)' because git is absent (precision_null.py). This does not change the result; carriers, signal, and alphabet SHA-256s match the bundled manifest.

run_eval.sh pip-installs transformers, huggingface_hub, safetensors, and numpy if missing. The registration said to use installed Transformers and not upgrade PyTorch; PyTorch was not upgraded. Needed for the run to start and unlikely to change the gated value 0, since the loaded safetensors SHA-256 matches exact.json and the specified dtype, eager attention, TF32-off, and highest FP32 matmul settings were applied.

outputs/statistic.json shows all 446 eligible rows are native BF16 full-vocabulary ties and pair-logit ties (rates 1.0; every eligible |q-0.5| quantile is 0). On that set N is whether FP32 argmax differs from torch.argmax's lower token id, so point_ratio 0.861 and statistic_raw_p5_before_validity 0.789 are tie-break artifacts and were correctly excluded from the event.
precision_null.py codes public_side as lb > la, so exact ties become side 0; the eligible public_side_disagreement_rate 0.493 is not a meaningful side comparison.

precision_null.py's bf16_repeat_logits_identical check, reported as bf16_repeat_rows_with_any_logit_difference, compares only the two pair logits and the top-1 logit, not the full vocabulary. The registered top-1 repeat control did pass (0 disagreements), but bitwise identity of all logits is not established.

The engineer notes' max |q_fp32 - cached public_probability_right| = 5.2e-5 is not computed in outputs/statistic.json. Shown precision.jsonl rows are consistent with a close FP32 match, but that maximum is not an evaluation output.
grok.reason: The implementation follows the registered model, revision, raw prompts, batching, precision settings, BF16-only eligibility rule, cluster bootstrap, and failure gate, and the evaluation value 0 is produced from real forwards by that gate. BF16 logits near 23–26 have ulp 0.125, so |q−0.5| is 0 or at least about 0.031 and the 0.02 band contains only 446 exact ties, which is a real property of the registered filter rather than an implementation miss. Because the protocol defines this outcome as non-evidence about the nuisance magnitude, and the only ratios in range are token-id tie breaks, the run is valid but does not test the hypothesis.

registration.title: Does coding transfer survive a generic system prompt?
registration.seed_connection: The seed reports executable coding gains from ordinary-word training. Closely related subliminal trait studies find strong dependence on named system prompts and shared context. This experiment asks whether ATD capability transfer has the same practical fragility.
registration.hypothesis: Replacing the named Qwen system prompt with a generic helpful-assistant prompt preserves at least half of ATD's coding advantage over its exact matched control.
registration.contribution: Tests context robustness of an execution-scored capability rather than an animal preference. Both models are evaluated under both prompts, so ordinary system-prompt effects are distinguished from changes in the signal-minus-control advantage.

closest_work.difference: Shows context-dependent subliminal trait expression and localization to shared tokens. This assay uses raw ATD carrier training and tests held-out executable code performance under an explicit system-prompt replacement.

Studies hidden-bias transfer, including sensitivity to paraphrasing and context. Here the intervention is solely at capability evaluation, with the seed's exact nuisance-matched training arm retained.
The seed demonstrates coding transfer but does not report this paired system-prompt robustness contrast.

inputs: https://github.com/myboker/ATD: data/signal.jsonl, data/exact.jsonl, data/alphabet.json and exact.json; atd/train.py and atd/evaluate.py provide reference implementations.
https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, revision 989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306.
HumanEval+ fetched through EvalPlus 0.3.1; require all 164 tasks and record the downloaded test-data hash.
registration.method: Use installed CUDA PyTorch and install Transformers, PEFT, NumPy and EvalPlus 0.3.1 without upgrading PyTorch or building accelerators. Do not run the repository's four-seed default pipeline. Train exactly two fresh students, one on all released signal rows and one on all released exact-control rows. Use paired seed 20260823, identical initial LoRA matrices and data order, raw prompts without chat wrapping, rank and alpha 16, zero dropout, all q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj modules, AdamW learning rate 5e-5 and weight decay 0, 157 optimizer steps, batch 32 with accumulation 4, five warmup steps, linear decay and gradient clipping 1. Match the repository's scheduler convention. Compute full-vocabulary CE only from the last prompt hidden state and the released single-token label; avoid projecting every prefix position to the vocabulary. Native SDPA and BF16 are sufficient; use no gradient checkpointing if memory permits. Freeze both students. Evaluate all 164 HumanEval+ tasks under two explicit system messages: named='You are Qwen, created by Alibaba Cloud. You are a helpful assistant.' and generic='You are a helpful assistant.'. Use the same user content in both: 'Complete the following Python programming task. Return only one complete Python implementation without Markdown or explanation.\n\n' followed by the original task prompt. Serialize with the pinned tokenizer's chat template, explicitly supplying the system message. Generate one greedy completion per arm/task/context, left-padded batches of 32, max_new_tokens=384, stopping on EOS or im_end. Sanitize with EvalPlus using the entry point, and execute its base and extra tests in isolated CPU subprocesses. A pass requires both suites to pass. Truncations, syntax failures and timeouts count as failures; do not retry or select alternative completions. This fixed token budget is an MVE modification of the seed's 4,096-token evaluation.

event.description: A positive ATD coding advantage is present under the named prompt, and the generic prompt retains more than half of that advantage.
event.statistic: The fifth percentile of the paired-task bootstrap distribution of min(delta_named, delta_generic - 0.5*delta_named), with accuracy differences expressed as fractions.

evaluation.procedure: For every task, align all four pass indicators. delta_named and delta_generic are signal accuracy minus exact-control accuracy in their respective contexts. Use 10,000 paired task-bootstrap draws, seed 7003, recomputing both differences and their minimum in every draw. This single minimum statistic prevents an apparent retention result from being accepted when the named-prompt transfer contrast itself is unsupported. The interval is conditional on one optimization seed and the released acquisition. outputs/training.jsonl holds arm-level step losses and configuration. outputs/generations.jsonl holds task, arm, context, raw and sanitized code, token count and truncation. outputs/execution.jsonl holds aligned base/extra test statuses. outputs/statistic.json holds the registered number, four accuracies, contrasts, hashes, versions and timing. Failure of the event alone does not establish context dependence; inspect whether baseline transfer was present and how wide the contrasts are.
evaluation.controls: Released exact nuisance-matched labels; identical training initialization, order and update budget; a two-arm by two-context evaluation; identical generation and execution settings; no context or checkpoint selected by benchmark results.

models: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct with separately trained signal and exact-control rank-16 LoRA adapters

registration.full_scale_study: Cross acquisition and optimization seeds with several system prompts, chat templates and coding benchmarks. If robustness persists, compare capability transfer with trait transfer under matched training; if attenuation is subsequently well resolved, localize the context-gating mechanism with token-position interventions.

agent.reason: Training on raw carriers without the named system identity gives some reason to expect coding transfer to survive its removal. However, the event requires both a supported single-seed transfer contrast under the shortened generation budget and a confidence-bounded half-retention result.

judge_astra.reason: The seed's coding results support expecting some advantage under both prompts, but establishing the registered lower bound on retained advantage is considerably harder than observing two positive differences. One training seed, 164 tasks, and the shortened generation budget leave substantial uncertainty.

judge_fable.reason: Requires a single-seed, 164-task paired bootstrap to put delta_named's 5th percentile above zero (needs ~4-5pp with ~2.5-3pp SE) under a changed chat-template/384-token protocol, then also retain >half under the generic prompt; the heavy train+generate+EvalPlus pipeline must also finish in 35 minutes.

judge_opus.reason: The event first needs a single-seed replication of a roughly 5 pp effect that survives a task bootstrap with SE around 2.7 pp. It also needs delta_generic − 0.5·delta_named to be robustly positive. The system-prompt swap flips some greedy outcomes and adds noise, so even full retention would usually fail that second condition.

judge_sol.reason: Removing the model-identity clause is a mild evaluation-only perturbation, so substantial retention of the coding advantage is plausible. However, one optimization seed, shorter completions, and the joint lower-bound criterion make success less certain than simply observing positive transfer.

judge_luna.reason: The seed reports a positive coding contrast, and removing the model name from an otherwise similar helpful-assistant prompt may leave much of a weight-level capability change intact. Prompt dependence is not tested in the seed, however, and this event also requires bootstrap support for both baseline transfer and retention of at least half of it from a single training seed.

judge_muse.reason: The seed shows 15/15 positive acquisition effects and specific coding-rule adoption, which should not depend on Qwen naming, favoring retention; but the single-seed min-statistic requires both a significant named advantage and >half retention, which 164-task noise may push below zero.
