registration.title: Can a safety-SFT update transmit a safety preference through ATD?
registration.seed_connection: The seed shows that task-unrelated one-token choices can transfer coding and other task improvements, but it does not test a safety-alignment update or a held-out safe-versus-unsafe response preference.
registration.hypothesis: Provided a locally trained safety teacher improves on held-out safety preferences, a student trained only on its near-tie carrier choices will rank held-out safe responses above unsafe responses more often than an exact-matched control.
registration.contribution: Tests whether the ATD channel can carry a safety-preference update to a same-ancestor student. The endpoint is an annotated response-ranking proxy, not a claim of broad real-world safety.

closest_work.difference: Tests coding, knowledge, reasoning, and reading-comprehension updates through ATD, but not a safety-SFT update.
Provides public safe-versus-unsafe preference data; this experiment uses such labels to evaluate taskless transfer from a locally trained safety teacher.
Studies subliminal signals in preference labels; this experiment tests safety-preference transfer from single ordinary-word choices on unrelated near-tie carriers.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct from Hugging Face.
PKU-Alignment/PKU-SafeRLHF from Hugging Face, using its prompt, response, and safety-label fields.
Seed ATD repository at https://github.com/myboker/ATD: data/carriers.jsonl, data/alphabet.json, atd/controls.py, and atd/train.py.
Transformers, Datasets, PEFT, and the ATD repository's compatible training dependencies.
registration.method: Load the public PKU-SafeRLHF training data, retain rows with exactly one response marked safe, normalize prompts, and deduplicate exact normalized prompts. Split by a fixed SHA-256 hash into disjoint 80% teacher-training and 20% evaluation pools; select up to 512 training and 256 held-out prompts deterministically, and exclude held-out prompts whose character 5-gram Jaccard similarity to any training prompt is at least 0.8. If either quota cannot be filled, mark the pilot invalid. Starting from Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, train a rank-8 all-linear LoRA teacher for 100 AdamW updates with learning rate 5e-5, effective batch size 8, maximum sequence length 1,024, and loss on the safe assistant response only, using one fixed seed and the model's chat template. On held-out safety pairs, compute length-normalized response log-likelihoods for the base and teacher; teacher validity requires the lower endpoint of a paired 95% prompt-bootstrap interval for the teacher-minus-base mean safe-minus-unsafe likelihood margin to be above zero. For acquisition, inspect the released carrier candidate pairs, verify both words are single tokens in the 0.5B tokenizer, and score all available carrier prompts with the unadapted 0.5B base. Freeze prompts satisfying the near-tie threshold abs(q - 0.5) <= 0.02 and whose unrestricted base top-1 token is one of the candidates before querying the teacher. Query the teacher once per frozen prompt with greedy decoding and retain only responses in the offered pair, without resampling. Retain at most 2,048 rows using a deterministic margin-stratified hash; fewer than 256 retained rows makes the pilot invalid. Construct an exact nuisance-matched control on the retained rows using the repository procedure; if it is infeasible, report the pilot as invalid rather than changing control type. Train signal and control students from the same base with rank-8 all-linear LoRA, learning rate 5e-5, effective batch size 64, and 100 optimizer updates, using the same fixed seed and row order. Students see only carrier prompts and one-token labels, not safety examples. Score base, teacher, signal, and control on the held-out safety pairs using length-normalized response log-likelihoods.

event.description: The pilot supports safety-preference transfer if at least 256 carrier labels are retained, the teacher-validity check passes, and the lower endpoint of the paired prompt-bootstrap interval for signal-minus-control safe-ranking accuracy is above zero.
event.statistic: Lower endpoint, in percentage points, of the 95% paired bootstrap interval over held-out safety prompts for signal safe-ranking accuracy minus exact-control safe-ranking accuracy.

evaluation.procedure: Write acquisition rows with base margins and retained teacher tokens, plus one held-out safety-pair record per prompt with length-normalized safe and unsafe log-likelihoods and ranking outcomes for base, teacher, signal, and control. Compute the teacher-validity interval and the registered signal-minus-control accuracy interval using 10,000 paired bootstrap resamples of prompt IDs. Also report signal versus base for context. The intervals reflect held-out prompt variation, not teacher or student seed variation; failure of the validity check or acquisition quota is uninformative about transfer.
evaluation.controls: Signal and exact control use the same retained carrier rows, candidate pairs, base initialization, training order, optimizer, and update budget. The exact control matches the completion multiset and public-margin-bin disagreement counts while disrupting prompt-token pairing. Safety evaluation prompts are disjoint from teacher-training prompts after exact and near-duplicate filtering.

registration.full_scale_study: If the event occurs, repeat across independently trained safety teachers and student seeds, add additional safety-preference datasets and held-out adversarial prompts, and measure benign-prompt over-refusal alongside safety ranking.

agent.reason: The local safety teacher may improve held-out preferences, but the event also requires enough retained carrier labels and a measurable student-control difference on a limited prompt set. The hard-token channel may transfer too little for that ranking endpoint.

judge_astra.reason: This experiment adds several uncertain gates: teacher improvement, sufficient 0.5B near-ties from the existing carrier pool, and exact-control feasibility. Even after those gates pass, an improved likelihood margin need not produce a detectable safe-ranking accuracy advantage on 256 held-out pairs.

judge_fable.reason: Multiple gates (teacher validity, ≥256 retained near-ties re-scored under a different 0.5B base, feasible exact control, a long pipeline within 35 minutes) precede a weak endpoint: a lightly SFT'd 0.5B teacher yields a faint shadow, and a signal-minus-control safe-ranking accuracy difference on 256 prompts would need ~5 pp to clear zero, which is well above the plausible effect.

judge_opus.reason: The run must first pass three gates: a 256-row near-tie yield when the 1.5B-selected carriers are reused on 0.5B, a teacher-validity check, and control feasibility, which needs the weak 100-step teacher to flip at least 25% of near-ties. Together these pass perhaps half the time. Even then, transfer from a weak teacher scored on 256 binary safety rankings with one seed has only a modest chance of excluding zero.

judge_sol.reason: Several uncertain gates must pass: teacher improvement, sufficient near-ties after recalibration to the 0.5B model, and exact-control feasibility. Even afterward, small likelihood-margin shifts may not flip enough of the 256 response rankings to produce a positive accuracy confidence bound.

judge_luna.reason: A same-ancestor safety-SFT teacher could leave a recoverable shadow, but the seed provides no safety-transfer evidence. Teacher validity, sufficient carrier retention, and improved held-out ranking must all hold; moreover, safe-response likelihood improvements need not change ranking accuracy after taskless distillation.

judge_muse.reason: Seed shows small multiple-choice transfer (+0.8 to +2.9pp) with 3 seeds and large eval sets; with 0.5B model, <=2,048 rows, 256 prompts and single seed, joint teacher-validity plus significant ranking gain is possible for a preference update but unlikely to reach significance.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed paper introduces ATD and tests it on coding (HumanEval+), ScienceQA, OpenBookQA, HellaSwag, RACE, CommonsenseQA, PIQA and GSM8K updates. I read the full text, including the appendices on where transfer fails, and found no safety-SFT teacher and no safe-versus-unsafe preference endpoint.

This paper shows that a safety-relevant trait, misalignment, passes from teacher to student through number sequences and code. But it uses long, extensive teacher generations rather than one actively selected word on near-tie prompts, transmits misalignment rather than a safety-SFT improvement, and does not score held-out PKU-SafeRLHF-style pairs against an exact nuisance-matched control.
This paper studies subliminal signals carried by binary preference labels, not by teacher single-token choices on unrelated near-tie carriers. It does not test transfer of a safety update.

This paper studies subliminal transfer of misalignment from a harmful teacher through benign generated data under SFT and on-policy distillation. It does not use ATD-style one-word, near-tie acquisition or test a beneficial safety-preference update.

This paper shares adapted-model knowledge through outputs on random, task-unrelated carriers and reports preference retention and GSM8K gains. It does not use single-token near-tie queries or evaluate safety-preference transfer.

opus.reason: I found no paper that runs ATD-style single-word near-tie distillation from a safety-SFT teacher and scores held-out safe-versus-unsafe response ranking against an exact matched control. The nearest results either show misalignment, rather than a safety improvement, moving through long unrelated outputs (Cloud et al.; Askin et al.), or apply the ATD channel only to capability tasks (the seed paper). The question this experiment asks therefore appears unanswered.

Demonstrates subliminal transfer of misalignment through number sequences and reasoning traces, not transfer of a safety-improving update through actively selected single-word choices.
Transfers animal preferences through binary judgments over numerical completions using judge likelihoods; it does not test a safety-trained teacher or the ATD acquisition channel.

Prior work establishes related capability, preference, and misalignment transfer, but I found no paper answering whether a safety-SFT update transfers through unrelated near-tie single-word choices to improve held-out safety ranking. Those related findings do not settle this specific safety-transfer question.
No list entry distills a safety-SFT teacher through unrelated carriers and evaluates held-out safe-versus-unsafe response ranking.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented and end-to-end tested the registered safety-SFT/ATD pipeline, importing the seed repository's exact-control MILP and audit. Fixed model/data revisions, one seed, registered ranks/batches/learning rates/update counts, 0.02 near-tie threshold, one greedy teacher token per frozen query, 10,000 paired prompt bootstraps, and all required raw-output files. Selected-position vocabulary projection implements full-vocabulary CE efficiently. No acquisition threshold, quota, control, or event was relaxed. Test: teacher-validity margin improvement passed (mean 0.07457, 95% CI [0.04089,0.11172]); all 5,664 released candidate pairs were scored, but only 143 passed the 0.5B near-tie/top-1 filter, and 143 labels were retained. Thus the registered pilot is invalid, students were not trained, and no transfer conclusion is warranted. Necessary clarification: one selected annotated response is empty, so evaluation consistently includes assistant end-of-turn for every response in likelihood and token length; all pairs remain included. Because result.json requires a number for an invalid pilot with undefined transfer CI, value -100 pp is an explicitly documented non-support sentinel, not an estimated interval; summary has a null transfer interval and missing-arm scores are null. Unspecified implementation defaults and the fixed 120-second MILP timeout are documented in IMPLEMENTATION.md. Unit tests passed for exact matching constraints, bootstrap units, and normalization. The evaluation command reruns from scratch and installs dependencies; tested runtime was under 3 minutes including initial downloads.

departures: safety_experiment.py greedy_carriers scores carrier prompts as raw text with tok.encode and no chat template. I cannot check whether this matches the seed repository's scoring convention. The 0.5B public probabilities in carrier_labels.jsonl sit close to the released 1.5B metadata, which suggests the formatting is consistent. If it is not, the number of near-ties (143) could change, and so could whether the 256-label quota is met.

safety_experiment.py response_encoding adds the assistant <|im_end|> token to every scored response and to its length. It does the same in teacher SFT. The engineer reported this, and it was needed because one held-out response is empty. It could shift the teacher-validity margins slightly. It cannot affect the transfer statistic, which was never computed.

result.json reports -100.0, a documented sentinel, instead of the registered statistic, which is undefined because no students were trained. This was reported, and summary.json keeps a null interval. The number is not a measurement, though a careless reader could take it for a strong negative.

LoRA alpha 8, dropout 0, weight decay 0, gradient clipping 1.0 and a constant learning rate are fixed in safety_experiment.py and teacher_training_config.json. The registration leaves these open, and they were reported. They could affect teacher strength, but the teacher passed validity.

Data preparation keeps the first eligible row per normalized prompt and orders by ascending SHA-256. The near-duplicate filter compares against the 512 selected teacher prompts, not the whole 80% training pool. The registration's wording is ambiguous on this, and only 1 prompt was excluded. This does not affect the reported outcome.
safety_experiment.py has a fixed 120-second MILP time limit for the exact control. It was never reached, because control construction was not attempted. No effect.

Carrier logits are projected in float32 from bf16 hidden states (greedy_carriers). This is an implementation choice that could move a few rows across the 0.02 boundary. With 143 against a quota of 256, it is very unlikely to change validity.
The teacher was trained and evaluated even though acquisition had already failed the quota. This order is consistent with the registration and has no effect on the result.
problems: result.json holds a numeric sentinel (-100) that is not the registered lower confidence bound. Any automated aggregation must treat it as missing, not as evidence against transfer.

The registered transfer question went untested. Only 143 of the 5,664 released carriers met the 0.5B near-tie/top-1 filter, against the 256 required (summary.json acquisition). Signal and control students were never trained.

Raw-prompt carrier scoring without a chat template (safety_experiment.py) cannot be checked against the seed repository from the material given. Uncertainty about the convention leaves some doubt about the exact near-tie count.

Teacher validity passed, but the effect is modest: ranking accuracy 55.5% to 58.2%, mean margin gain 0.075. The teacher training loss in teacher_training_trace.jsonl is noisy and barely declines, so a valid run might have had little signal to transmit.

The registration sized the run as a pilot without checking whether the released carriers, presumably calibrated on the 1.5B model, yield enough near-ties for the 0.5B tokenizer and model. This feasibility gap is the binding failure.
opus.reason: The code follows the registered pipeline closely: deterministic hash split with near-duplicate filtering, the registered LoRA teacher settings, a bootstrap teacher-validity gate, carrier selection with the 0.5B base frozen before any teacher query, and one greedy teacher token per prompt. It stops correctly at the registered invalidity rule rather than relaxing the threshold or swapping the control. The protected run reproduces the engineer's numbers: 143 retained labels and a teacher-validity CI of [0.041, 0.112]. The reported outcome therefore comes from real model computations, and the -100 value is a clearly documented sentinel, not an estimate. The run gives no evidence for or against safety-preference transfer through ATD. Its only finding is about feasibility: the released carriers yield too few 0.5B near-ties under the registered threshold. That is credible but weak, informative only for redesign, so the research value is low.

departures: safety_experiment.py, response_encoding: scores assistant end-of-turn as part of every response and its length, rather than response text alone, and includes it in teacher SFT. This documented clarification handles one empty evaluation response and can change likelihood margins, rankings, and teacher validity. It is a reasonable necessary adjustment; it cannot resolve the independent carrier-quota failure.

outputs/safety/summary.json: only 143 carrier labels were retained, versus the required minimum of 256. Consequently, exact-control construction and both student trainings were not attempted, and their score fields and transfer intervals are null. This is the registered invalid-pilot rule being honored, not a quota relaxation; it leaves the transfer hypothesis untested.

safety_experiment.py, finish, and result.json: the undefined registered confidence-bound statistic is encoded as the hard-coded number -100.0. The registration does not specify this numeric encoding, although the engineer reports that the result interface requires a number. This changes the scalar report, but not the correctly recorded invalid status or false support event. It is not an estimated bound.

safety_experiment.py and IMPLEMENTATION.md: add a 120-second timeout for exact-control optimization, with timeout treated as invalid rather than substituting another control. This could prevent a future otherwise-feasible experiment from completing, but the control branch was not reached here and it did not affect this run.

safety_experiment.py: supplies registration-open defaults, including pinned revisions, prompt normalization and deterministic selection details, LoRA alpha/dropout, optimizer weight decay and clipping, microbatching, constant learning rate, numerical precision, margin-bin count, and capped-row stratification. These choices can influence outcomes generally, but no conflicting registered settings are evident; capped-row selection and control settings were not exercised.
problems: result.json presents -100.0 under the name of the registered lower confidence bound, although that bound was never computed. The companion summary documents the sentinel correctly, but the scalar itself is not valid quantitative evidence for the registered endpoint.

outputs/safety/summary.json and safety_pair_scores.jsonl establish that neither student arm exists. There is therefore no signal-minus-control comparison, no transfer confidence interval, and no evidence establishing either safety-preference transfer or its absence.

The observed teacher accuracy increase from 55.47% to 58.20% is descriptive. The positive bootstrap interval concerns likelihood-margin improvement, not accuracy improvement or broad behavioral safety.

The observed feasibility failure is specific to these released carriers, this base model, and the registered filter. It does not establish that other carrier pools or configurations cannot support a safety-transfer experiment.
sol.reason: The substantive execution faithfully followed the registered method through its prescribed acquisition-invalid branch, without relaxing the threshold, quota, or control requirement. The fresh evaluation corroborates a teacher-margin improvement of 0.07457 with a 95% interval of [0.04089, 0.11172], but only 143 eligible labels were available. Validity is marked invalid specifically for the reported numerical endpoint: -100 is an acknowledged sentinel, not a confidence bound derived from student outputs. The real teacher and acquisition measurements remain useful diagnostics, but the registered transfer experiment was not delivered and its hypothesis remains unresolved.

departures: Assistant end-of-turn (<|im_end|>) is included in every response likelihood, token length, and teacher SFT loss (safety_experiment.py response_encoding; summary.json evaluation_empty_response_count=1). The registration asks for length-normalized annotated-response likelihoods. Needed for one empty response; it can change teacher-validity margins slightly but cannot change the binding result, which is the base-model near-tie count of 143.

result.json value is the hardcoded sentinel -100 rather than the registered signal-minus-control CI lower endpoint (safety_experiment.py finish; summary.json result_encoding). The registration leaves the numeric field undefined when the pilot is invalid. This sets the reported number but does not change the registered event, which already fails if the quota or the CI is unavailable.

A 120-second MILP timeout is treated as invalid, distinct from certified infeasibility (safety_experiment.py, IMPLEMENTATION.md). The registration only invalidates an infeasible exact control. Not executed, so it could not change this result.

Teacher updates use token-mean microbatch loss scaled by example fraction, plus unspecified AdamW weight decay 0, grad clip 1, LoRA alpha 8, dropout 0, and a constant LR (safety_experiment.py train_adapter). These can change teacher weights relative to an unspecified full effective-batch update, but the freeze count is from the unadapted base and is already 143, and the teacher kept all 143 labels, so the invalidity cannot flip.

Base and teacher forwards use sdpa while sliding-window attention is unimplemented (safety_experiment.py load_base; evaluation stderr). Sequences here are far shorter than the window, so this is unlikely to change near-tie membership enough to reach 256.

Held-out 5-gram Jaccard filtering is against the 512 selected training prompts only, not the full 80% pool (safety_experiment.py prepare_data). A broader reading of 'any training prompt' would not change carrier acquisition or the reported sentinel; one held-out prompt was excluded.
problems: The registered transfer contrast was not estimated: 143 retained carrier labels are below the pre-registered 256 minimum, so students and the exact control were not run (outputs/safety/summary.json acquisition and invalid_reasons).
result.json reports -100 for the registered CI statistic; that number is a non-support sentinel, not a bootstrap endpoint, and can be misread as a large negative effect if summary.json is ignored.
One empty annotated response makes pure text length-normalization undefined; the end-of-turn convention is an unregistered scoring change (summary.json, safety_experiment.py).
Teacher-validity and any future transfer intervals are prompt bootstraps from a single teacher seed, as the registration itself notes (summary.json interpretation).
sdpa sliding-window warning (evaluation stderr) is a numerical caveat, though it should not bind on these lengths.
grok.reason: The fresh run followed the registered safety split, LoRA recipe, 0.02 near-tie plus top-1 filter, greedy one-token teacher query, and invalid-pilot rule. All 5,664 released carriers were scored on the unadapted 0.5B model and only 143 were frozen and retained, so the transfer interval is undefined and the event correctly did not occur; teacher margin validity did pass (mean 0.07457, interval about [0.0409, 0.1117]) and matches the saved paired scores. The -100 result is an explicit sentinel, not an estimated effect, and the listed implementation departures do not move the base-model count across 256. This is valid evidence that the registered acquisition cannot be completed here, but it is uninformative about whether a safety-SFT update transfers through ATD.

registration.title: Near-tie enrichment of base-instruct disagreement on unrelated forced choices
registration.seed_connection: Seed introduces ATD where near-tie prompts selected on public ancestor are queried against private teacher to expose behavioral shadow. This tests the core observability premise without any student training, using public base versus instruct as a known-ancestor proxy.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B from HuggingFace Hub
Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct from HuggingFace Hub
Alphabet words from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/myboker/ATD/main/data/alphabet.json
registration.method: Load M0 as Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B and MT as Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct with AutoModelForCausalLM in bfloat16 on CUDA and AutoTokenizer use_fast True, set pad to eos if missing. Build alphabet by downloading alphabet.json, keeping words where tokenizer.encode(' '+w, add_special_tokens=False) is exactly one token for M0, require at least 50 remain. Use 4 neutral frames: In a calm scene with a {w1}, where could a {w2} appear? / Imagine an ordinary scene containing a {w1}, a {w2}, and a {w3}. What happens next? / What might a person notice about a {w1} and a {w2}? / How might a {w1} and a {w2} appear in the same short story? Fill placeholders with random alphabet words, plus answer list of 3 to 12 random alphabet words. Full prompt is Question: {q} Answer: {alist} Choose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word. Options: {a} | {b} Answer: with random distinct ordered pair (a,b). With seed 0 generate up to 12000 candidates. For each run M0 forward batch 32 to get last-position logits, get ida idb for ' '+a and ' '+b, compute q as softmax over the two logits for b, top1 as argmax over full vocab. Keep as near if abs(q-0.5)<=0.02 and top1 in pair, as far if 0.15<=abs(q-0.5)<=0.40 and top1 in pair, until 300 near and 300 far, require at least 150 each. For each kept prompt run MT forward to get greedy top1, retain if in pair, require at least 100 retained per arm. M0 choice is its top1 side, MT choice is its top1 side, flip is MT!=M0. Compute near_flip_rate and far_flip_rate and statistic.

event.description: Near-tie flip rate exceeds far flip rate by more than 5 percentage points
event.statistic: near_flip_rate_minus_far_flip_rate

evaluation.procedure: Read outputs/carriers.jsonl with one record per prompt containing arm q m0_side mt_side retained flip, and outputs/scores.json with retained counts per arm, near_flip_rate as flips divided by retained near, far_flip_rate similarly, and statistic as near minus far. Statistic is proportion difference 0 to 1.
evaluation.controls: Both arms use identical frames, alphabet distribution and top1-in-pair requirement and differ only in abs(q-0.5) filter, so difference isolates boundary proximity. Report retention counts and side rates as diagnostics.

registration.full_scale_study: If enrichment holds, run full ATD loop with task-specific teachers and signal versus shuffle students to test whether enriched observability predicts transfer.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I built: run_enrichment.py, an inference-only experiment, implemented as registered. M0 is Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B and MT is Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, both loaded in bf16 on CUDA with fast tokenizers. There are 4 neutral frames plus an answer list of 3–12 alphabet words and a random ordered pair (a, b). With seed 0 I generate 12000 candidates and score them with M0 in batches of 32, using left padding and position ids computed from the attention mask. q is the softmax over the two candidate logits, taken for b. Both arms require M0's full-vocab top-1 to be one of the pair. A candidate goes to "near" if |q−0.5|≤0.02 and to "far" if 0.15≤|q−0.5|≤0.40, until each arm has 300. MT then gives its greedy full-vocab top-1 on every kept prompt. A row is retained if that token is in the pair, and a flip means MT's side differs from M0's. The script writes outputs/carriers.jsonl, outputs/scores.json (retention counts, side rates and diagnostic Wald/bootstrap CIs) and result.json.

Deviations (small):
(1) The registered alphabet URL (github raw myboker/ATD/main/data/alphabet.json) returned 404. The script tries the URL first and otherwise falls back to the same file in the seed repo, seed/data/alphabet.json. All 128 words are single tokens.
(2) Prompt lines are joined with newlines, matching the seed repo's carrier format (Question/Answer, a blank line, the instruction, Options, Answer:). The registration text showed these flattened.

Test-run result: the registered statistic is +0.192. Near: 133/295 retained flip (0.451). Far: 76/294 (0.259). Diagnostic bootstrap 95% CI [0.118, 0.270]. About 9.5k candidates were scored, and retention was about 98% in both arms. The run is deterministic, so evaluation should reproduce these numbers on the same hardware.

Important caveat:
- In bf16, the final logits are quantised. 285 of the 300 near carriers have exactly q=0.5, i.e. the two logits are tied in bf16. M0's "choice" on those rows comes from argmax tie-breaking, not a real preference, so the near arm's flip rate is partly a quantisation artifact.
- I kept bf16 because it was registered. As a diagnostic only, run_eval.sh repeats the identical pipeline in float32 and writes to outputs/diag_fp32/; this does not affect result.json. In fp32 there are 0 exact ties, and the gap is +0.270: near 0.508 vs far 0.238, bootstrap CI [0.196, 0.342]. So the enrichment does not depend on the bf16 artifact.

Interpretation limits:
- MT has a strong second-option bias: it picks side b in 75–77% of retained near rows and about 61% of far rows. Much of the near-tie "disagreement" may therefore be a generic position bias that tips near-ties, not update information tied to specific prompts.
- A near flip rate of about 0.5 is also what you would get from essentially random agreement.
- This experiment measures only observability (flip enrichment) for base vs instruct. It says nothing about whether the shadow carries information about a capability, or about transfer.
- Single seed, one repetition.

departures: Alphabet source (run_enrichment.py load_alphabet): the registered URL returned 404, so the script loaded seed/data/alphabet.json. The engineer reported this and the eval log confirms it. Nothing in the evidence shows this file is byte-identical to the registered file. All 128 words passed the single-token filter, and the file comes from the seed's own repo. If the word list differed, carrier composition could change slightly, but a large effect on the near-minus-far gap is unlikely.

Prompt formatting (run_enrichment.py): lines are joined with '\n' and a blank line, following the seed repo's carrier format. The registration text shows the prompt flattened. The engineer reported this. Prompt layout can shift logits, so it could change individual carriers. The registration's single-line rendering is plausibly a JSON flattening, so this reads as a choice left open rather than a change of question.

Batching implementation (run_enrichment.py last_logits): uses left padding, explicit position_ids from the attention mask and add_special_tokens=False. None of this is specified in the registration. It is a legitimate implementation choice and Qwen adds no BOS token. In bf16 it could cause tiny numeric differences only.

MT is queried on the raw prompt with no chat template (run_enrichment.py). The registration says only 'run MT forward', so this is consistent with it. Using a chat template would likely give different MT behaviour, but that would be a different experiment.
Extra diagnostics (run_eval.sh): a second float32 run writes to outputs/diag_fp32/, and scores.json gains Wald/bootstrap CIs and tie counts. These are additions only and do not affect result.json.

Statistic, thresholds, arm sizes (300/300), retention rule (MT top-1 must be in the pair), exclusion rule (M0 top-1 must be in the pair), seed 0, the 12000-candidate cap, batch 32, bf16 and both models all match the registration. 9536 candidates were scored before both arms filled.
problems: The bf16 near arm is degenerate (outputs/scores.json). 285 of 300 near carriers have q exactly 0.5 and there are only 3 distinct q values. For these rows M0's 'choice' comes from torch argmax tie-breaking over token ids, not from any model preference. The registered near arm therefore mostly measures MT against an arbitrary token-id rule. The fp32 diagnostic (outputs/diag_fp32/scores.json) has 0 ties and a larger gap of +0.270, which suggests the direction is robust to this artifact.

The hypothesis is close to mechanically true. When M0 is at a tie its side is essentially a coin flip, so MT disagreement near 0.5 is expected whatever MT's behaviour. Far carriers, where M0 has a clear preference, will agree more simply because base and instruct are correlated. The near flip rates (0.451 in bf16, 0.508 in fp32) match chance agreement. So the result shows that ties are uninformative about MT. It does not show that near-tie selection exposes update-specific signal.

MT shows strong position bias toward option b: 75% of near rows and 61% of far rows (outputs/scores.json). Much of the near-arm disagreement may be generic second-option bias rather than prompt-specific divergence. The design has no control for position, such as counterbalancing (a,b) order per prompt.

Single seed and single repetition. The registration specifies no inferential test. The CIs reported by the engineer are diagnostics and do not account for seed or prompt-family variability, although the gap is well above the 0.05 threshold.
The alphabet file substitution (seed/data/alphabet.json for a 404 URL) cannot be verified as identical to the registered resource.
opus.reason: The code implements the registered pipeline closely: same models, bf16, frames, filters, arm sizes, retention rule, statistic and event. The only departures are the forced alphabet fallback and the newline formatting, neither of which plausibly changes the conclusion. The reported value of 0.192 comes from real model outputs and was reproduced on the fresh machine, and the fp32 diagnostic (+0.270) shows the enrichment is not just an artifact of the 285 exact bf16 ties. The evidence is nonetheless weakly informative about the seed's observability premise. A near flip rate of about 0.5 is what one expects when the ancestor's choice is a coin flip, and MT's strong option-b bias confounds any reading of update-specific signal. The registered event occurred credibly, but it mostly confirms a near-tautology rather than isolating observability of meaningful teacher updates.

Casting the already quantized logits to float32 does not recover the lost distinction; consequently, the primary result largely concerns quantized ties.

outputs/scores.json: MT chooses side b on 75.3% of retained near carriers versus 60.9% of far carriers; M0's corresponding rates are 53.2% and 39.1%. These diagnostics expose a possible explanation, not proof that bias explains the entire gap.

run_enrichment.py and the registration's controls: Both arms share a candidate generator, but conditioning on different M0 margins need not preserve identical word, frame or option distributions. The observed comparison therefore supports an association with selected margin bands, not isolation of a causal effect of boundary placement alone.

outputs/diag_fp32/scores.json and run_enrichment.py: The float32 diagnostic reselects carriers and changes both models' precision, scoring 7104 candidates rather than 9536. Its positive gap supports enrichment without exact ties in that separate pipeline, but it is not a paired precision check on the registered carriers and does not resolve the position-bias concern.

run_enrichment.py: The statistic conditions on MT's top-1 remaining in the pair. This exclusion is registered and retention is similarly high in both arms, so it is not a fidelity defect or an evident explanation of the large gap; nevertheless, the result concerns retained forced choices rather than all selected prompts.

The evidence covers one seed, one model pair and one prompt construction, with no capability-specific teacher or student training. The diagnostic intervals describe carrier-level uncertainty, not robustness across seeds, model families or tasks. The fallback alphabet is also not included or checksummed in the supplied archive.
sol.reason: The fresh evaluation produced 133/295 near flips and 76/294 far flips, yielding 0.192344 and satisfying the registered greater-than-0.05 event. The primary models, precision, selection thresholds, quotas, retention rule and statistic match the registration, but the potentially consequential prompt-format change makes fidelity unfaithful. The code computes the value from real model forward passes without apparent hard-coded results or leakage, so the evidence is valid despite its interpretive limitations. Extensive bf16 ties, uncontrolled option-position effects and confidence-based sample selection make this weak evidence for the broader observability premise; the positive float32 diagnostic strengthens the narrow association but does not establish capability-bearing information or transfer.

registration.title: Single-sample temperature robustness of greedy behavioral shadows
registration.seed_connection: Seed queries teacher by greedy decoding over full vocabulary. Real black-box APIs sample. This tests whether the one-bit greedy shadow survives realistic sampling noise on the same near-tie carriers.
registration.hypothesis: A single temperature-1 sample from the teacher agrees with its greedy choice on near-tie carriers at high rate.
registration.contribution: First decoding-robustness test of ATD shadows, measuring greedy versus sampled agreement on near-ties to inform realistic black-box threat models without student training.

registration.method: Load M0 as Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B and MT as Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct in bfloat16 on CUDA with fast tokenizer. Build alphabet by downloading alphabet.json and keeping words where ' '+w is single token for M0, require at least 50. Use same 4 neutral frames and full prompt format Question Answer Choose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word. Options: a | b Answer: as unrelated forced choice. With seed 1 generate up to 10000 candidates, run M0 forward batch 32 to compute q over pair and full-vocab top1, keep near if abs(q-0.5)<=0.02 and top1 in pair until 250 kept, require at least 150. For each get MT greedy top1 by forward argmax, retain if in pair, require at least 120 retained. For each retained run MT forward to get last-position logits in float32, divide by temperature 1.0, softmax, draw one token with torch multinomial using generator seeded by 1000+index, record sampled id. Agreement is sampled id equals greedy id, counting out-of-pair samples as disagreement. Also compute M0 greedy versus M0 sampled agreement as reference. Write per-prompt records and summary.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I built: atd_temp/run.py, launched by run_eval.sh, which pip-installs transformers if it is missing. It writes outputs/carriers.jsonl (one record per retained carrier), outputs/scores.json and result.json. Two test runs finished in about 20 s each and produced identical outputs (same md5).

Result: the agreement rate was 0.763 (190/249), with a Wilson 95% interval of [0.706, 0.812]. The event ">0.70" therefore occurred on this one run. The lower bound is only just above 0.70, so this is one seed's estimate, not a large margin.
- Prediction check: the teacher's mean probability on its own greedy token was 0.779, which predicts about the agreement observed.
- Out-of-pair samples: 4.8% of teacher samples fell outside the two offered words. They count as disagreements, as registered.
- Retention: 250 near-ties were kept after scanning 7,591 candidates; the teacher's greedy token was in the pair for 249 of them.
- Greedy flip rate (teacher vs M0's greedy choice): 46.6%.
- Agreement on flipped carriers was 0.767 (n=116) and on non-flipped ones 0.759.
- M0 self-agreement reference: 0.361 (expected 0.393). It is low partly because only 0.78 of M0's probability mass sits on the two offered words.

Deviations from the registration:
1. The alphabet URL (raw.githubusercontent.com/myboker/ATD/main/data/alphabet.json) returned 404. The code tries it first and then falls back to the same file in the seed repo, /workspace/seed/data/alphabet.json. All 128 words are single tokens.
2. The registration says "same 4 neutral frames", but the seed's released carriers contain at least 6 question frames. I used 4 of them verbatim: "How might a X and a Y appear in the same short story?", "In a calm scene with a X, where could a Y appear?", "What might a person notice about a X and a Y?" and "Imagine an ordinary scene containing a X, a Y, and a Z. What happens next?". Frame slots and the running answer list (1–19 words) are filled from the alphabet. The prompt format follows the seed exactly, as a raw prompt with no chat template.
3. In bf16, the teacher's greedy argmax could change with batch padding: on one carrier, a recomputation in a different batch gave a different argmax. So each carrier's last-position logits are computed once (float32 cast of bf16), and the greedy token and the temperature-1 sample both come from those same logits. M0 is handled the same way. Sampling follows the registration otherwise: softmax, then torch.multinomial with a CPU generator seeded 1000+index. The M0 reference sample uses the same seed for the same carrier.

Caveat on interpretation: because M0 runs in bf16, 238 of the 249 retained M0 "near-ties" are exact logit ties (q=0.5). For those, M0's greedy token is decided by argmax's lowest-index rule. The teacher has exact ties on only 5 carriers. This does not change the registered statistic, but the near-tie set is largely made of bf16-quantized ties.

Not done: student training, so no claim about how sampled labels affect transfer.

departures: Alphabet source (atd_temp/run.py load_alphabet): the registered URL returned 404, so the code fell back to /workspace/seed/data/alphabet.json. The engineer reported this. Prompt construction (atd_temp/run.py make_prompt): the 'Answer:' line is filled with a random list of 1–19 alphabet words, and the frame slots are filled from the alphabet. The registration does not specify this detail; the engineer describes it as following the seed. It affects which carriers are tied and could modestly affect the value.

Teacher logits (atd_temp/run.py): MT logits from the batched greedy pass are reused for sampling instead of running a separate MT forward pass on retained carriers. The engineer reported this, citing bf16 batch-padding argmax instability. It keeps greedy equal to the argmax of the sampled distribution. It is a defensible implementation detail with negligible effect.
Alphabet filter (atd_temp/run.py): the single-token check additionally requires identical encoding under the MT tokenizer. This was not reported. It has no effect, since 128/128 words were kept.

problems: Agreement is mechanically a single Bernoulli draw from the teacher's probability on its greedy token. The observed 0.763 just tracks mean p_greedy (0.779, in outputs/scores.json). The sampling step mainly adds noise to a quantity that is already computed exactly, so the experiment says little beyond teacher confidence on these prompts.

Near-tie set (outputs/carriers.jsonl): because M0 runs in bf16, 238 of 249 'near-ties' are exact logit ties (q=0.5, with m0_p_a == m0_p_b). M0's greedy token on those is decided by argmax's lowest-index rule. The carrier population is therefore largely a quantization artifact.

M0 self-agreement (0.361): this is a weak 'noise baseline'. M0 is near 50/50 on the pair by construction and puts only 0.78 of its mass on the pair. It is not a comparable reference for teacher sampling noise.

The experiment measures local, full-vocabulary, temperature-1 next-token sampling on raw prompts, conditional on teacher greedy retention. It does not establish robustness under deployed API decoding configurations, complete generated answers, or student transfer.

sol.reason: The fresh evaluation produced 190 agreements among 249 retained carriers, yielding 0.763052 and satisfying the registered event; the supplied code computes this value from model logits and sampled tokens without evident fabrication or leakage. Fidelity is unfaithful because the explicitly registered additional teacher forward was replaced by cached batch-dependent logits, a change with a demonstrated numerical mechanism for affecting results. The evidence nevertheless supports a meaningful, narrow finding about single-token agreement on this selected carrier set, consistent with the teacher's mean greedy-token probability of 0.779. Predominantly quantized ancestor ties, one carrier seed, and the absence of deployed-API or student-transfer tests prevent a broader robustness claim.

registration.title: Task fingerprinting from one-bit unrelated word choices without distillation
registration.seed_connection: Seed shows shadows are source-specific via downstream transfer after student training. This tests whether task identity is directly decodable from one-bit carrier responses without training any student.
registration.hypothesis: Per-word choice rates on shared near-tie carriers identify which task a same-ancestor teacher was trained on above chance.
registration.contribution: Replaces expensive student-training transfer test with cheap supervised fingerprint from the same one-bit observations, separating lexical fingerprint signal from correspondence-dependent transfer.

closest_work.difference: Surveys fingerprinting and watermarking for ownership without testing task fingerprinting from unrelated one-bit forced choices.
Requires training a student to reveal teacher trait, not direct classification of teacher task from carrier responses.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct from HuggingFace Hub
allenai/openbookqa train split from HuggingFace datasets
allenai/piqa train split from HuggingFace datasets
Alphabet words from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/myboker/ATD/main/data/alphabet.json
registration.method: Use M0 Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct in bfloat16. Train teacher A on 600 OpenBookQA train examples and teacher B on 600 PIQA train examples, each as LoRA r8 alpha8 dropout0 target q_proj,v_proj, AdamW lr 1e-4 batch 8 for 60 steps warmup 5 completion-only loss. Format OpenBookQA as Question: stem Choices: A. c0 B. c1 C. c2 D. c3 Answer: with completion ' X' letter, PIQA as Goal: goal Choice A: sol1 Choice B: sol2 Answer: with completion ' A' or ' B', verifying letters are single tokens else use choice text. Build alphabet from alphabet.json filtered to single token for M0, require 50+. Build shared carriers with 4 neutral frames and prompt Choose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word. Options: a | b Answer:. With seed 2 screen up to 12000 candidates with M0 forward batch 32, keep near if abs(q-0.5)<=0.05 and top1 in pair until 500 kept. Query both teachers by forward argmax, retain only where both in pair, require at least 200 retained. Randomly split retained 50-50 train test seed 42. On train estimate for each word w P_A(w) as (times A chose w when offered plus 1) divided by (times w offered to A plus 2), similarly P_B. For each test observation with chosen word c predict A if P_A(c) greater than P_B(c) else B, breaking ties randomly. There are 2 test observations per carrier, one per teacher, balanced chance 0.5. Accuracy is correct divided by total.

event.description: Held-out teacher identification accuracy from per-word rates exceeds 60 percent
event.statistic: held_out_teacher_identification_accuracy

evaluation.procedure: Read outputs/carriers.jsonl with pair choices per teacher and train test split, and outputs/scores.json with retained counts, train size, test size, per-teacher accuracies and overall accuracy as statistic 0 to 1.
evaluation.controls: Test set is balanced by construction so chance is 0.5. Report per-teacher accuracies and side marginals to rule out trivial always-predict-one-teacher rule.

registration.full_scale_study: If fingerprinting succeeds, scale to more tasks and test whether fingerprint strength predicts ATD transfer magnitude.

agent.reason: Tiny 60-step teachers and sparse per-word counts around 4 observations per word make 60% held-out accuracy from lexical rates alone unlikely.

judge_astra.reason: The paper's source-specific signal need not yield strong word-frequency fingerprints, especially with sparse per-word counts and two small, similarly trained adapters. Lexical or answer-format biases could nevertheless make these particular teachers distinguishable.

judge_fable.reason: Two tiny q/v-LoRA teachers trained 60 steps on similar MC formats will agree on many carriers, and per-word rates estimated from ~4–10 observations per word are noisy, so overall accuracy is likely 0.5–0.58; a letter-after-'Answer:' bias may also cut retention.

judge_opus.reason: Carriers where both teachers pick the same word contribute exactly 50% under this classifier, so accuracy is capped at 0.5 + 0.5 times the teacher-disagreement rate. Two tiny LoRA teachers (r8, 60 steps, lr 1e-4) will rarely disagree, and the train split has only about 2 offers per word, so exceeding 60% is very unlikely.

judge_sol.reason: The seed's source-specific shadows make fingerprinting plausible, but do not guarantee stable differences in marginal word-choice rates. Similar lightly trained teachers and sparse observations per word make exceeding 60% a demanding target.

judge_luna.reason: The seed’s controls and analyses point to prompt–token correspondence as important, whereas this classifier uses only marginal chosen-word rates. With about 250 training carriers per teacher to estimate rates across many words, accuracy above 60% seems unlikely, though stable task-specific word preferences could make it possible.

judge_muse.reason: Seed exact-multiset control and correspondence curve show signal is in prompt-token correspondence not unigram marginals; with ~100 train obs over 50+ words per-word rate estimates will be noise-dominated near 0.5.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed paper shows that the shadow is source-specific only indirectly. It trains same-ancestor students and maps transfer across source and target tasks (and checks representational alignment). It never classifies the teacher's task directly from the one-bit near-tie choices, and it does not use a per-word-rate classifier.

VectorHijack-SR uses paired victim/base residuals and a classifier, but it infers adapter structure (PEFT family, rank, layer locality, version linkage), not the training task. It relies on rich outputs from classification backbones, not single-word forced choices on unrelated carrier prompts.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I built: fingerprint.py, run through run_eval.sh. It follows the registered pipeline. Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct is loaded in bf16. Teacher A is a LoRA trained on 600 OpenBookQA train examples and teacher B on 600 PIQA train examples. Both use r8, alpha 8, dropout 0, q_proj/v_proj, AdamW at lr 1e-4, batch 8, 60 steps, 5 warmup steps and completion-only loss. Registered prompt formats; " A"–" D" are confirmed to be single tokens, with a fallback to the choice text otherwise. The carriers come from 4 neutral frames, a running list of 1–20 alphabet words and the registered instruction and options line. Screening uses M0 only, with seed 2, batch 32 and at most 12000 candidates. A carrier is kept if |q-0.5|≤0.05 and M0's top-1 token is one of the pair, until 500 are kept. Both teachers are queried by forward argmax over the full vocabulary, and a carrier is retained only if both teachers answer within the pair. Retained carriers are split 50/50 with seed 42. Per-word rates use (chosen+1)/(offered+2), estimated on the train half. Each test observation is labelled A if P_A(c)>P_B(c), else B, with random tie-breaks. Accuracy is computed over 2 observations per test carrier.

Deviations (small, same question):
1. The registered alphabet URL (raw.githubusercontent.com/myboker/ATD/main/data/alphabet.json) returned HTTP 404. The code falls back to the identical file in the seed repo (seed/data/alphabet.json, 128 words, all single tokens).
2. "allenai/piqa" does not exist on the Hub (DatasetNotFoundError, and the parquet-convert revision also failed). The code falls back to the baber/piqa mirror of the PIQA train split; scores.json records which source was used.
3. The LR schedule was not fully specified. I used linear warmup over 5 steps, then linear decay.
4. The registration requires at least 200 retained carriers. If fewer were retained, the script would still write the outputs and print a warning.

Result from my test run (it varies slightly on rerun because of GPU nondeterminism):
- 10,240 candidates screened, 500 near-ties kept, 498 retained; 249 train and 249 test carriers, so 498 test observations.
- **Held-out accuracy was 0.506** (252/498). The descriptive one-sided binomial p is 0.41, but it treats the paired observations within a carrier as independent.
- Per-teacher accuracy was 0.466 for A and 0.546 for B, and 46% of predictions were A, so this is not an always-predict-one-teacher rule. 153 predictions were random tie-breaks.
- The registered event (>0.6) did not occur. This does not show that the teachers are indistinguishable: it only shows that this per-word classifier did not separate them.

Caveats:
- The teachers are weak under the registered recipe. On a 200-item sanity check (held-out OBQA/PIQA train items, option-letter argmax), the base scored OBQA 0.51 / PIQA 0.63, teacher A 0.52 / 0.64, and teacher B 0.525 / 0.69.
- The teachers chose different words on 43% of retained carriers, but the per-word rates do not separate them.

Exploratory observation (not registered, and not used for the statistic): the teachers differ strongly in which side they pick. Teacher A chose the second-listed word on 27% of test carriers and teacher B on 55%. By my own arithmetic on those marginals, a position-based rule would score about 0.64. So the outputs do contain teacher-specific information; the per-word rate statistic averages over both positions and washes it out. That is my inference and was not tested as a registered classifier. scores.json reports side marginals, agreement with the public choice, retained counts and the teacher sanity accuracies.

registration.title: Paraphrase robustness of near-tie flips
registration.seed_connection: Seed fixes a single forced-choice instruction for all carriers. This tests whether teacher-ancestor flips are a template artifact or persist when the same decision is asked with different wording.
registration.hypothesis: Flips versus base on the original template predict flips on a paraphrased template above the paraphrase base rate.
registration.contribution: Tests template generality of behavioral shadows, distinguishing robust update signal from instruction-specific artifact and linking ATD to prior paraphrase fragility findings.

closest_work.difference: Finds subliminal trait transfer is fragile to prompt paraphrasing, not testing preservation of ATD near-tie flip directions across templates.
Uses paraphrases as student training data to show transfer, not as carrier-template robustness test for flip preservation.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B from HuggingFace Hub
Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct from HuggingFace Hub
Alphabet words from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/myboker/ATD/main/data/alphabet.json
registration.method: Load M0 Qwen2.5-0.5B and MT Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct in bfloat16. Build alphabet from alphabet.json filtered to single token for M0. Original prompt uses Question Answer prefix plus Choose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word. Options: a | b Answer:. Paraphrased prompt uses identical Question Answer prefix and same pair but instruction Pick one of the following two words and output only that word. Choices: a / b Response:. With seed 3 screen up to 10000 original candidates with M0 forward batch 32, keep near if abs(q_orig-0.5)<=0.02 and M0 orig top1 in pair until 250 kept. For each build para version, run M0 and MT forward on both versions to get greedy top1 by argmax. Retain only where all 4 top1 are in pair, require at least 100 retained and at least 20 original flips. Define flip_orig as MT_orig!=M0_orig, flip_para as MT_para!=M0_para. Preservation is mean flip_para among flip_orig equals 1. Base_para_rate is mean flip_para over all retained. Statistic is preservation minus base_para_rate.

event.description: Flip preservation lift over paraphrase base rate exceeds 15 percentage points
event.statistic: preservation_minus_base_para_flip_rate

evaluation.procedure: Read outputs/carriers.jsonl with orig and para sides and flips per retained carrier, and outputs/scores.json with retained count, orig flip rate, para flip rate, preservation rate and statistic as preservation minus base rate.
evaluation.controls: Same contexts and pairs across templates isolate wording effect. Base para rate serves as chance baseline for preservation, controlling for overall flip prevalence.

registration.full_scale_study: If robust, test natural continuations without instruction; if fragile, test multiple paraphrases to map template sensitivity.

agent.reason: Word-preference shifts should largely survive similar forced-choice wording, though strict 4-way retention and paraphrase fragility add downside risk.

judge_astra.reason: The selected ancestor margins are almost zero, so paraphrasing can change the ancestor's choice and disrupt flip-indicator agreement even if the teacher's update remains informative. The 15-point lift and four-way in-pair retention requirement make this a demanding event.

judge_fable.reason: On near-ties the base model's side is decided by a ~0.08-nat residual, so any template change (new instruction, '/' separator, 'Response:') effectively re-randomizes the base side; flip_para is then nearly independent of flip_orig and the lift should hover near zero regardless of how template-robust the teacher's preferences are.

judge_opus.reason: M0's original-template choice at a near-tie is effectively a coin or token-id tie-break, independent of MT and of M0's choice on the paraphrase. As a result, flip_orig is nearly independent of flip_para even if MT's preferences are perfectly robust to wording, so the expected lift is about 0 with a standard error near 0.05; retention requirements may also bind.

judge_sol.reason: Shared contexts and candidate pairs should produce some association across templates, but small wording changes can reorder choices selected precisely for their near-indifference. A 15-percentage-point lift, together with four-way in-pair retention, is substantially less certain than simple observability.

judge_luna.reason: The same context and word pair are retained, and the two instructions are semantically close, so flips may reflect preferences that persist across wording. But the seed tests only one template, and near-tie selection is not repeated for the paraphrase, leaving room for wording-induced changes in the decisions.

judge_muse.reason: Base-instruct word-preference shifts likely persist across minor instruction rewording with same context and pair, though base-model brittleness could reduce stability; >15pp lift remains plausible.

What I built: paraflip.py, run with run_eval.sh. It follows the registered method. M0 is Qwen2.5-0.5B and MT is Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, both in bf16. Prompts are raw text with no chat template, and greedy top-1 is the argmax over the full vocabulary at the last position. Batches are left-padded. Screening uses seed 3, batches of 32 and at most 10,000 candidates. A candidate is kept if |q_orig−0.5|≤0.02 and M0's original-template top-1 is one of the two words, until 250 are kept. Each kept carrier then gets the paraphrased instruction ("Pick one of the following two words and output only that word.\nChoices: a / b\nResponse:"), and M0 and MT are run on both versions. Only carriers where all four top-1s fall in the pair are retained. The statistic is P(flip_para | flip_orig) − P(flip_para). The script writes outputs/carriers.jsonl, outputs/scores.json and result.json.

Changes from the registration:
(1) The registered alphabet URL (raw.githubusercontent .../myboker/ATD/main/data/alphabet.json) returned HTTP 404. The script tries it, then falls back to /workspace/seed/data/alphabet.json, the repo's own copy of the same file: 128 words, all single-token under the Qwen2.5 tokenizer, which is shared by both models. scores.json records which source was used.
(2) The seed repo does not include its Question/Answer context generator. I rebuilt it from the released carriers.jsonl: six question templates filled with alphabet words, then an "Answer:" list of 1–20 random alphabet words, then a random pair of distinct words.

Result (two runs gave the same output): 7,335 candidates screened, 250 near-ties kept, 240 retained. Both registered requirements were met (240 ≥ 100 retained; 121 ≥ 20 original flips). Original flip rate 0.504, paraphrase base flip rate 0.346, preservation 0.397. **Statistic = +0.051**, well below the 0.15 threshold, so the registered event did not occur. In the 2×2 table of original vs paraphrase flips, the one-sided Fisher test gives p≈0.062. This is weak evidence of an association, not proof that there is none.

Supplementary diagnostics, which do not change the registered value:
- When the four top-1s are recomputed one prompt at a time (no padding), the statistic falls to +0.004.
- M0's original-template top-1 from the scoring pass matches the screening pass in only 72% of kept carriers.

Together these suggest that at |q−0.5|≤0.02, bf16 batch/padding rounding alone can tip M0's choice. Part of what counts as a "flip" is therefore numerical noise in the base model's side rather than a teacher–ancestor difference, and that noise would push preservation toward the base rate.

Scope and caveats: there is one paraphrase and one seed. The "teacher" here is the Instruct model rather than a narrow post-training update like the paper's code-DPO teacher. Also, M0 and MT agree across the two templates on only 53% and 62% of carriers, so near-tie choices themselves are highly sensitive to the wording.

departures: Alphabet source (paraflip.py load_alphabet; stdout; scores.json config.alphabet_source). The registered URL returned 404, so the run used seed/data/alphabet.json. All 128 words are single-token under the Qwen2.5 tokenizer. The change was disclosed and was needed for the run. The file is described as identical but this cannot be checked here. It is unlikely to change the result.

Question/Answer context generator (paraflip.py QTEMPL / make_candidate). The engineer rebuilt it from the seed's released carriers: six question templates, an answer list of 1–20 random words and a random distinct pair. The registration only says 'Question Answer prefix', so this is an open choice. It was disclosed. The carrier pool could differ from the seed's distribution and could shift the value somewhat.

Batching and padding (paraflip.py last_logits). Scoring uses left-padded batches of 32, which the registration does not specify. A supplementary unpadded batch-1 recompute (scores.json supplementary) gives +0.004 instead of +0.051. The choice does change the number, but both values are far below the 0.15 threshold, so the event outcome is unchanged. It was disclosed.

M0 original-template top-1 is recomputed in the scoring pass rather than reusing the screening pass, as the registered method implies. Screen and recompute agree on only 72% of carriers (scores.json). This is consistent with the registration and was disclosed.
Raw-text prompting with no chat template for the Instruct model (scores.json config.prompting). The registration leaves this unspecified. It is an open choice and was disclosed.
Instruct-model tokenizer encoding is asserted to equal the M0 tokenizer for every alphabet word, and the M0 tokenizer is used for both models. There is no effect on the result.
Supplementary outputs are added (Fisher test, contingency table, unpadded recompute, agreement rates). They do not alter the registered statistic in result.json.
problems: Near-tie selection in bf16 makes the M0 side largely numerical noise. Every visible carriers.jsonl record has q_orig_m0 exactly 0.5, i.e. bf16 logit ties, so argmax tie-breaking and batch composition decide M0's choice. M0's top-1 changes between screening and scoring in 28% of carriers. The 'flip' variable therefore mixes teacher–ancestor differences with rounding noise, which biases preservation toward the base rate. The registered statistic cannot cleanly separate a template artifact from a robust update signal (paraflip.py, scores.json).

The registered statistic depends on padding: 0.051 batched versus 0.004 unpadded (scores.json supplementary.unpadded_batch1_recompute). The event outcome is the same either way, but the point estimate is not stable.

Sampling uncertainty is moderate. With 121 original flips, preservation has a standard error of about 0.045, so a lift close to 0.15 is not tightly excluded by this one run. There is a single seed, a single paraphrase and one repetition.

The teacher is Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, a broad instruction-tuning update, not a narrow post-training teacher like the seed's. This limits transfer of conclusions to the seed's setting (registration choice, disclosed).
The context generator was rebuilt rather than taken from the seed, and the identity of the alphabet file with the registered URL cannot be verified (paraflip.py).

registration.title: Tiny-budget taskless transfer on multiple-choice science with likelihood eval
registration.seed_connection: Seed shows 5.34pp HumanEval gain with 5664 rows, 157 steps and execution eval on 1.5B. This is a minimal ATD loop on 0.5B with small SFT teacher, few hundred carriers, few dozen steps and fast likelihood eval.
registration.hypothesis: Signal student exceeds shuffle student on held-out OpenBookQA accuracy.
registration.contribution: Tests whether ATD transfer appears in a tiny-budget regime with different teacher recipe and cheap eval, enabling rapid iteration beyond expensive code execution endpoints.

closest_work.difference: Classic distillation matches task logits or ensembles on task data, not single unrelated word choices without task data or logits.
Studies task vectors as weight differences with arithmetic editing, not capability recovery through unrelated behavioral decisions.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct from HuggingFace Hub
allenai/openbookqa train and test splits from HuggingFace datasets
Alphabet words and single-token CE training reference from https://github.com/myboker/ATD
registration.method: Use M0 Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct bfloat16. Train code-teacher analogue on OpenBookQA: take 800 train examples seed 0, format as Question: stem Choices: A. c0 B. c1 C. c2 D. c3 Answer: completion ' X' letter, LoRA r8 alpha8 target q_proj,v_proj AdamW lr 1e-4 batch 8 80 steps warmup 5 completion-only loss. Evaluate base and teacher on 500 test by letter likelihood: one forward per question, log softmax at final position, gather ' A' ' B' ' C' ' D' ids, predict argmax, require teacher minus base at least 2pp as precondition else still continue and note weak teacher. Build alphabet from alphabet.json single-token filtered. Build carriers with 4 neutral frames and prompt Choose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word. Options: a | b Answer:. Screen up to 15000 candidates seed 4 with M0 forward batch 32, keep near if abs(q-0.5)<=0.02 and top1 in pair until 1300 near. Query teacher by forward argmax, retain if in pair, target 400 retained minimum 200. Signal rows are prompt plus teacher choice. Shuffle rows keep same prompts and pairs but permute sides across rows with seed 123 preserving side marginal, each label stays in own pair. Train signal and shuffle students from M0 as LoRA r8 same targets, full-vocab CE on single completion token only, batch 16 50 steps lr 5e-5 warmup 5 seed 0 same order. Evaluate both on same 500 test by letter likelihood. Statistic is signal minus shuffle accuracy times 100.

event.description: Signal minus shuffle accuracy on held-out OpenBookQA exceeds 1 percentage point
event.statistic: signal_minus_shuffle_accuracy_pp

evaluation.procedure: Read outputs/eval.json with base teacher signal shuffle accuracies on same 500 test ids, outputs/carriers.jsonl with signal and shuffle labels, and outputs/scores.json with teacher gap and statistic as signal minus shuffle in percentage points.
evaluation.controls: Shuffle arm reuses signal prompts pairs count order optimizer and steps and differs only in label permutation, isolating prompt-token correspondence. Teacher gap is reported separately from transfer.

registration.full_scale_study: If tiny transfer holds, scale carriers steps and seeds and add exact nuisance-matched control and cross-task endpoints.

A greater-than-1-point gap remains plausible through either genuine transfer or single-run variability, with weak teacher improvement and carrier scarcity substantial risks.

judge_fable.reason: Fifty LoRA steps at lr 5e-5 on a few hundred rows barely moves a 0.5B model, so signal and shuffle students will both sit within a few questions of base on 500 OBQA items; a >1pp gap would mostly have to come from noise, and the near-tie quota (1300 from 15k) is unlikely to be met.

judge_opus.reason: The teacher is tiny and likely has a small gap, there are only a few hundred carriers (likely fewer than the target 1300 near-ties), and students train 50 steps at lr 5e-5 with an r8 LoRA on 0.5B. The seed's much larger MC runs moved about 15 to 40% of the teacher gap, so expected transfer here is well under 1 pp. A single seed gives roughly ±1 pp of noise, so exceeding 1 pp would need luck.

Transfer remains plausible, but an uncertain teacher improvement and a single-seed, 500-question evaluation make a greater-than-one-point contrast unlikely and potentially noisy.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I built: the registered tiny ATD loop, all in atd_tiny/run_tiny.py and run with run_eval.sh. It runs in about 1 minute after installs. Two full runs from scratch gave identical outputs.

- **Teacher:** M0 is Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct in bf16. The teacher is a LoRA (r8, alpha8, q_proj/v_proj) trained on 800 OpenBookQA train examples (seed 0) with AdamW, lr 1e-4, batch 8, 80 steps and warmup 5. Loss is computed only on the ' X' answer-letter token.
- **Evaluation:** letter likelihood on all 500 test items. One forward pass per question, log-softmax at the final position, take the ' A'..' D' token ids, predict the argmax.
- **Carriers:** the alphabet is seed/data/alphabet.json; all 128 words are single tokens. There are 4 neutral frames and the registered instruction prompt. Screening used M0 with seed 4, batch 32, keeping a candidate if |q-0.5|<=0.02 and M0's top-1 token was in the pair. The teacher was then queried with forward argmax, keeping a row if its answer was in the pair.
- **Shuffle control:** a permutation of the teacher's sides with seed 123. This preserves the side marginal and keeps each label inside its own pair.
- **Students:** LoRA r8 q,v started from M0, trained with full-vocabulary cross-entropy on the single token, batch 16, 50 steps, lr 5e-5, warmup 5, seed 0. Both arms see the same data order.

Result:
- Base 54.2%, teacher 56.8%: a +2.6 pp gap, so the 2 pp precondition was met.
- Signal student 53.8%, shuffle student 54.0%.
- **Statistic = -0.20 pp, so the registered event (> +1 pp) did not occur.** A descriptive paired item bootstrap gives a 95% CI of [-1.2, +0.8] pp.
- Both students scored slightly below base.

This is one seed on 500 items, where 1 pp is 5 items. The run has low power, so a null here does not show the effect is absent at this scale. The training budget was also very small: 248 rows, 50 steps, LoRA on q,v only.

Departures from the registration and choices it left open:
1. **Fewer carriers than targeted.** The full 15,000-candidate screening budget produced only 248 near-ties, not the targeted 1,300. The teacher's argmax was in the pair for all 248, so 248 rows were retained: below the target of 400 but above the minimum of 200. I did not enlarge the screening budget, so it stays as registered.
2. **Frames were my own.** The 4 frames are modelled on the seed's released carriers ("In a calm scene with…", "How might…short story", "What might a person notice…", "Imagine an ordinary scene…"). Each prompt has a running word list of 1–19 words, and the nouns in the question are drawn from the alphabet. Prompts are raw text with no chat template, as in the seed data.
3. **Learning-rate schedule.** The registration did not specify one, so both teacher and students use the seed trainer's linear warmup then linear decay. Gradient clipping is 1.0.

registration.title: Tight near-ties flip more than far pairs under a small task delta
registration.seed_connection: ATD motivates near-tie selection via Eq.4 y~=sign(m0+gT delta), predicting smaller |q-0.5| gives higher flip probability. Seed compares active versus passive transfer but never reports flip-rate versus margin.
registration.hypothesis: Greedy flip rate versus the public ancestor is higher on tight near-ties than on far-from-tie pairs for the same small SFT delta.
registration.contribution: Inference-only margin dose-response using a small public task delta without any student training or benchmark execution, isolating observability from transfer.

closest_work.difference: They identify divergence tokens post-hoc via counterfactual teachers; this tests prospective prediction that flip probability decreases with |q-0.5| using a small SFT delta.
They show trait transfer via unrelated data; this tests the tie-sensitivity mechanism ATD claims makes transfer possible.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct from HuggingFace
allenai/sciq train split from HuggingFace datasets
wordfreq pip package for alphabet construction
registration.method: Do not use seed repo data files; generate everything from scratch. Install transformers, peft, accelerate, datasets, wordfreq, torch, numpy. Load Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct in bfloat16 on CUDA with fast tokenizer, plain text no chat template. Build alphabet: take wordfreq.top_n_list en 1000, keep alphabetic lowercase len>=3, exclude task words code python function return import math science physics chemistry biology history answer question data model train token, keep words where tokenizer encodes space+word as exactly 1 token, take first 100. Use 10 fixed neutral stems cycling, e.g. How might a lobster and a heart appear in the same short story? / Describe a market visited by a baker and a sailor. / What did the garden and the clock share on a quiet afternoon? / Tell a short tale about a hat and a river. / How would a cat and a lamp meet in a village? / Imagine a picnic with a violin and a cloud. / What happens when a key meets a feather in a library? / Describe a walk taken by a painter and a dog. / How might a candle and a window appear together at dusk? / Tell a story fragment about a bridge and a song. Carrier template is Question: {stem} newline Answer: {prefix} newline newline Choose exactly one of these two words. Reply only with that word. newline Options: {w1} | {w2} newline Answer: where prefix is 6 random alphabet words excluding w1,w2 joined by space, seed 0. Mine carriers: sample random distinct pairs per stem, tokenize prompt batch 16, get last-position logits, compute q=softmax over the two offered token ids, compute full-vocab argmax. Keep as tight if |q-0.5|<=0.02 and argmax in pair, as loose if |q-0.5| in [0.30,0.40] and argmax in pair. Try up to 20000 candidates until 800 tight and 800 loose kept. Record prompt, w1,w2, q, public_side 0 for w1 1 for w2. Train task delta: first 400 sciq train as Question: {question} newline Answer: {correct_answer} truncated 256 tokens, SFT LoRA r16 alpha16 dropout0 targets q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj, AdamW lr1e-4, 40 steps, batch8 grad_accum4 effective32, loss only on answer tokens. Query M0+adapter greedily on all 1600 prompts batch8 one token, retain iff argmax equals one of pair ids with no resampling, flip=1 if teacher side != public side. Require >=500 retained per arm else mine more. Write outputs.

event.description: Greedy flip rate on tight near-ties exceeds flip rate on far pairs by more than 5pp
event.statistic: flip_tight_minus_flip_loose

evaluation.procedure: Load outputs/scores.json holding n_tight_retained, n_loose_retained, flip_tight, flip_loose. Compute statistic=flip_tight-flip_loose as fraction. Write outputs/scores.json with counts, rates and statistic and outputs/per_row.jsonl with one row per prompt holding prompt id, q, public_side, teacher_side or discarded, flip.
evaluation.controls: Same stems and prefix distribution and same greedy retain-iff-in-pair rule for both arms; only public margin bin differs. Reports retention counts as diagnostic.

registration.full_scale_study: If event occurs, sweep epsilon bins 0-0.02 to 0.35-0.45 with multiple task deltas and test whether downstream transfer gain tracks flip-rate.
