sol.what_came_out: Across 16 Qwen3-0.6B LoRA builds trained on eight Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-generated corpora and evaluated on 512 URL and mention extraction tests, between-wording correctness disagreement exceeded within-wording disagreement by 45.31 percentage points, with a paired 95% bootstrap interval of 43.55–47.07 points conditional on those corpora.

prerequisite.reason: Oracle checks passed and the code maintained identical student scaffolds, while URL wording-A accuracy of 70.70–80.47% supplied a non-floor signal despite the mention task's weak performance.

evidence.reason: The conditional interval places the aggregate excess disagreement clearly above zero, supporting the claimed direction, although mention accuracies of 0–5.86% cannot establish stability on that task.

next_step.reason: The large source-order effect reproduced across the URL builds justifies a broader study across teachers, equivalent orderings, synthesis seeds and tasks to establish its generality.

registration.title: Semantic interface compatibility between independently compiled functions
registration.seed_connection: The seed composes compiled functions and treats JSON key order and whitespace as semantically irrelevant in its evaluation. This experiment tests whether a downstream learned function actually respects that equivalence when an upstream implementation is replaced.
registration.hypothesis: A semantics-preserving JSON canonicalizer recovers more than five percentage points of pipeline accuracy lost when an otherwise correct upstream compiled function emits a different legal key order.
registration.contribution: A controlled component-substitution test that separates interface-representation failures from upstream semantic errors. It does not claim that formatting sensitivity is new or that the seed's semantic metric is wrong; it tests the stronger compatibility requirement needed for reusable neural components.

closest_work.difference: FormatSpread demonstrates sensitivity to meaning-preserving prompt formats. This experiment measures actual producer-consumer substitution failures, verifies upstream semantic correctness, and applies a value-preserving normalization intervention at the interface.

Program-as-Weights demonstrates reusable neural programs and application pipelines. This experiment evaluates whether two implementations satisfying the same output contract remain interchangeable for a learned consumer.

inputs: Model: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
PyTorch, Transformers, PEFT, NumPy, and Python's json module.
Programmatically generated short record descriptions, their exact JSON representations, and an executable record-selection oracle.
The provided seed paper and repository as architectural references; this experiment uses no hosted compilation or teacher calls.
registration.method: Generate latent lists of 1-3 records. Each has a unique id from A-H, an active Boolean, and integer priority 0-9. Render them as short descriptions such as 'A is active with priority 3' or 'Priority 2 belongs to B; B is inactive', preserving list order. Freeze four training renderings and two additional test renderings before training. The producer specification requests a JSON array of objects with exactly id, active, and priority, normalized Boolean values, and preserved record order; object-key order and whitespace are explicitly unrestricted. Compile producer P_A using compact targets with key order id, active, priority, and producer P_B using compact targets with key order priority, active, id. Both receive the same specification, latent training records, and semantic targets. Separately compile consumer C: given such a JSON array, return the id of the active record with smallest priority, breaking ties by first array occurrence, or Z if none is active. Consumer training inputs use the P_A serialization. Its specification explicitly says key order and whitespace do not matter. Use 512 latent training examples per component, fresh 256-item held-out test records, and two complete builds with seeds 17 and 29. All labels are generated by code. Train six adapters total with frozen BF16 Qwen3-0.6B, random rank-16 LoRA, alpha 32, dropout 0, attention and MLP projection targets, AdamW 3e-4, cosine decay, 60 updates, effective batch 16, maximum complete sequence length 384, and answer-only loss. Disable thinking. Producers use greedy decoding capped at 128 new tokens; consumers choose the highest-likelihood label among A-H and Z. For every test input run both producers, validate schema and exact semantic equality to the latent records, and run C on P_B's raw output and on a canonicalized version. The canonicalizer only parses and reserializes valid JSON into the P_A key order, preserving every value and array position; assert parse-equivalence before invoking C. Invalid producer output fails both paths. Also run the P_A pipeline and C on oracle JSON in both key orders. There is no repair of wrong values, no extra model call for validation, and no test-driven training selection.

event.description: Canonicalization recovers more than five percentage points of total test-set pipeline accuracy specifically on cases where producer P_B already satisfied the semantic interface contract.
event.statistic: Lower endpoint of a paired 95% bootstrap interval for mean I(P_B semantically correct) * [I(C(canonicalized P_B) correct) - I(C(raw P_B) correct)], averaged equally over the two builds and using all test records as the denominator.

evaluation.procedure: Freeze the test records using seed 9001. Parse producer outputs with strict schema checks, compare arrays to the latent truth without treating object-key order as meaningful, and compute the registered paired effect. Incorrect producer cases contribute zero to the primary contrast, preventing upstream value errors from being credited as interface repairs. Bootstrap 2000 times, seed 404, over latent test records while preserving both builds and both serialization paths; use the 2.5th percentile. records.jsonl holds latent records, descriptions, splits, and oracle outputs. component_outputs.jsonl holds raw producer outputs, validity, semantic correctness, and consumer outputs on oracle interfaces. pipeline_outputs.jsonl holds raw/canonicalized producer strings, parse-equivalence checks, and both final predictions. training.jsonl holds configurations, losses, and timings. scores.json holds the primary statistic, interval endpoints, component accuracies, and unconditioned end-to-end accuracies. Intervals describe these builds, not arbitrary pipelines.
evaluation.controls: P_A and P_B use identical semantic data and unrestricted-key-order contracts. Compact serializers avoid a large output-length confound. Canonicalization is verified to preserve values and array order. Oracle-producer evaluations isolate consumer sensitivity, and semantic gating excludes upstream extraction mistakes from the primary effect.

registration.full_scale_study: Evaluate interface substitutability across independently trained producers, consumers, schemas, and compilers. Compare canonicalization, serialization-diverse training, and explicit interface test suites on larger composed applications.

agent.reason: The small consumer could learn position-dependent shortcuts, but changing only JSON key order is milder than many published formatting perturbations. Semantic gating and the five-point lower-confidence-bound requirement make this harder than merely detecting some formatting sensitivity.

judge_astra.reason: A consumer trained exclusively on one serialization could learn position-dependent shortcuts that canonicalization corrects. Nevertheless, pretrained JSON-order robustness and the producer-correctness gate may attenuate the total-set gain below the confidence-bound threshold.

judge_fable.reason: A consumer fine-tuned on one key order likely degrades on the other, but the base model's JSON familiarity may limit the drop; the gated statistic needs roughly a 10+ point raw-vs-canonicalized gap among P_B-correct cases for the lower bound to exceed 5 points, which is plausible but uncertain.

judge_opus.reason: A 0.6B consumer briefly fine-tuned on one key order may bind each object's attributes to the id by position, which would mis-bind ids in multi-record cases when the id moves to the end of each object. Pretrained JSON parsing could instead make it largely order-invariant, so the outcome is close to bimodal, and the effect must reach roughly 9 points after gating on producer correctness.

judge_sol.reason: Training the consumer on one serialization creates a plausible opportunity for positional shortcuts that canonicalization would correct. Nevertheless, pretrained key-value binding may already be robust, and gating on producer correctness reduces the total-test-set effect available to exceed the five-point threshold.

judge_luna.reason: Training the consumer on one serialization creates a genuine distribution shift that canonicalization directly removes, but explicit key-order instructions and field names may let the model generalize, while semantic gating limits the effect to correct producer outputs.

judge_muse.reason: A consumer trained only on one key order may still parse reordered JSON from pretraining, and producer errors further shrink the gated 5pp effect, though narrow fine-tuning could still induce format overfitting.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Program-as-Weights compiles fuzzy functions into adapters and shows them used in pipelines. It does not swap one producer for another that meets the same contract and emits a different legal JSON key order, and it does not measure how much accuracy an interface canonicalizer recovers.

The seed paper composes compiled functions and scores outputs semantically, ignoring key order. It never tests whether a learned downstream function actually treats differently ordered but equivalent JSON from a substituted upstream function as the same input.

FormatSpread shows that LLMs are sensitive to prompt formatting that does not change meaning. It does not study fine-tuned producer–consumer pipelines, check that the upstream output is semantically correct before counting an effect, or test a value-preserving normalization step between components.
This paper shows that shuffling input order hurts general LLM tasks. It does not cover JSON key order passed between independently trained adapters, and it has no canonicalization intervention.
OrderBench separates schema-valid output from semantically correct output in structured LLM generation. It does not look at how sensitive a downstream consumer is to legal variation in serialization.

opus.reason: My searches found prior work on format and order sensitivity in prompting, and on reusable neural functions, but no paper that substitutes one compiled producer for another, keeps only cases where the producer's output is semantically correct, and measures how much accuracy key-order canonicalization recovers for a learned consumer. The general fact that LLMs are format-sensitive is known, but the specific question of whether compiled neural components remain interchangeable when only the representation changes appears unanswered. These conclusions rest on titles and abstracts from a handful of searches; I did not read the full text of any paper, including the seed, so a closer match could have been missed.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: PromptPort measures cross-model extraction portability and repairs outputs rejected by strict parsers, including malformed or wrapped JSON. It does not test a learned consumer receiving already-valid, semantically correct JSON in a different legal key order.

Lost in Serialization evaluates representation sensitivity in pretrained and fine-tuned graph reasoners. It does not substitute independently trained producers or measure pipeline recovery through value-preserving interface canonicalization.

DictLLM tests sensitivity to permutations of dictionary entries and introduces a permutation-invariant encoder. It does not evaluate producer substitution or deterministic normalization of an otherwise correct producer's output.

FormatSpread establishes sensitivity to meaning-preserving prompt formatting, but studies prompt templates rather than independently compiled producer-consumer interfaces and canonicalization-based pipeline recovery.

Memory Canonicalization evaluates downstream cross-model interpretation after rewriting ambiguous memories and separating emotional fields. Its intervention changes interpretive content and structure rather than only reserializing parse-equivalent JSON from substituted producers.

The seed demonstrates composition and accepts semantically equivalent formatting in component evaluation, but does not report a controlled substitution test of legal serializations at a learned consumer's interface.

sol.reason: Prior work establishes formatting and serialization sensitivity, cross-model transfer problems, and benefits from several forms of canonicalization. However, among papers available by 2026-10-06, I found none answering the registered question through independently trained producer substitution, exact upstream semantic validation, and paired value-preserving JSON normalization before a fixed learned consumer. The distinct contribution is that controlled interface-compatibility test, not the general observation that formatting can affect model behavior.

opus.reason: Pipeline entries (#6, #30, #37, #49, #58) locate component errors or compare modular with monolithic systems; none tests whether a learned consumer tolerates a different legal JSON key order from a substituted producer, or whether canonicalization repairs this.

sol.reason: The composition experiments on the list do not substitute semantically equivalent producer serializations and test whether value-preserving canonicalization repairs downstream interface failures.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented the registered experiment without changing its hypothesis, method, event, or controls. The runner installs dependencies, downloads pinned Qwen3-0.6B, trains six independent adapters for seeds 17/29, and regenerates all required outputs and result.json. Strict schema validation, value/array-order-preserving canonicalization, oracle interfaces, semantic gating, and the joint 2000-replicate paired bootstrap are implemented. Unspecified implementation choices are documented and logged. Tested the exact command end-to-end twice; final runtime approximately 3.3 minutes. Independent model-free artifact audit passed. Observed primary effect 0.04296875, paired interval [0.021484375, 0.06640625], registered statistic 0.021484375: event not met. Both producers were semantically correct on all tests; P_B pipeline accuracy increased from 93.16% to 97.46%. The interval does not establish absence of a gain above five points.

departures: experiment.py uses AdamW weight decay 0.01, betas (0.9, 0.999) and eps 1e-8, and cosine decay to zero with no warmup. The registration leaves these open, they are logged in outputs/frozen_config.json, and they are unlikely to change the result.

experiment.py resets the build seed before each adapter, so within a build P_A, P_B and C share the same initial LoRA tensors and batch order. This is an open choice. If anything it strengthens the P_A/P_B control, and it does not plausibly bias the primary contrast.

Both builds use the same training lists (train seed 1234) and the same test lists (seed 9001). The two builds differ only in LoRA initialization and data order. The registration does not specify a training-data seed, so this is an open choice. It narrows between-build variation but does not affect how the statistic is computed.

Each description uses one rendering template per list, chosen at random from the frozen train or test templates. Whether templates were per list or per record was left open, so this is not a substantive departure.
experiment.py enables TF32 matmuls and keeps the LoRA weights in FP32 while the base stays frozen in BF16. These are open numerical choices and are unlikely to change the result.

experiment.py computes the training loss by applying lm_head only at answer-prediction positions. This is mathematically the registered answer-only shifted cross-entropy and should not change the result.
The answer target ends with tokenizer.eos_token_id (<|im_end|>). This is an implementation detail of answer-only loss and has no expected effect.
The metric names in the earlier run's experiment.log (final_B_*_label_accuracy) differ from the final outputs (interface_and_final_*). This is cosmetic and does not touch the evaluated value.
problems: Both producers were 100% semantically correct, and canonicalized P_B strings are byte-identical to oracle_json_A. The primary effect therefore reduces exactly to C(oracle A) accuracy minus C(oracle B) accuracy. It measures consumer key-order sensitivity, not any producer-side variation. This is consistent with the design, but the producer half of the substitution test is uninformative here.
The consumer was trained only on P_A key order, so some sensitivity to a different order was to be expected. The finding is narrower than general 'interface compatibility of reusable components'.

There are only two builds, and they share training data. The bootstrap resamples test records only, so the interval does not reflect training-seed variance. outputs/scores.json correctly scopes this as 'these builds'.
The interval [0.021, 0.066] contains values above the 0.05 threshold. The null on the registered event does not establish a gain of at most 5 points. The engineer states this correctly.

experiment.log from an earlier run shows a PEFT warning about an existing peft_config. The final unload() deletes that attribute, and the protected run's stderr shows no such warning. There is no evidence of adapter stacking in the evaluated run, but this was a latent risk.
opus.reason: The code implements the registered design closely: model, LoRA configuration, update count, batch size, data sizes, frozen renderings, strict schema validation, value-preserving canonicalization with an asserted parse-equivalence check, oracle-interface controls, semantic gating, and the record-level paired bootstrap with seed 404. The unregistered choices are open ones and are logged. The protected run reproduced the engineer's numbers exactly from real model outputs. The per-record log-probabilities and the 13 recoveries versus 1 regression (build 17) and 11 versus 1 (build 29) are internally consistent, and I found no leakage or hard-coding. Point effect 4.3 pp, 95% interval [2.1, 6.6] pp, so the registered event (lower bound > 5 pp) did not occur. The result is still a credible, controlled finding: a consumer whose specification says key order is irrelevant loses about 4 points of accuracy on a legal alternative key order, and canonicalization restores it. Its value is limited because it comes from a toy task, a single small model and two builds, and because both producers were perfect, so the test reduces to consumer key-order sensitivity.

problems: outputs/scores.json: The bootstrap quantifies test-record uncertainty conditional on two fixed builds; it does not estimate variability across arbitrary training runs or pipelines.
outputs/scores.json: The 95% interval spans the five-percentage-point threshold, so the experiment neither establishes the registered greater-than-five-point effect nor rules it out.

experiment.py: Evidence is limited to one small model, one synthetic schema and selection task, and a consumer trained on one serialization. Broader component-substitutability claims would require additional experiments.
sol.reason: No departures from the registered experiment are evident; unspecified choices such as sampling details, standard LoRA initialization, and optimizer defaults are documented and consistent with the registration. The fresh evaluation and supplied code support the reported value as computed from newly trained models and paired predictions, with semantic gating and the registered joint bootstrap implemented correctly. Both producers achieved exact semantic correctness on all test records, while canonicalization improved mean pipeline accuracy by 4.296875 percentage points, with a 95% interval of approximately 2.15–6.64 points; the matching oracle-interface results support attribution to consumer representation sensitivity. The registered event was not met, but this remains a meaningful controlled finding rather than evidence that compatibility problems or gains above five points are absent.

departures: No specified data, model, sample size, decoding, exclusion rule, statistic, or control was contradicted. Open choices in experiment.py that could change the numeric value relative to another legal implementation, all logged in outputs/frozen_config.json: exact renderings beyond the two examples and one style per list; chat-template prompt wrapping of the specified contracts; train seed 1234 and the uniform sampling scheme; AdamW weight decay 0.01 (library default) and cosine-to-zero with no warmup; resetting seeds 17 and 29 so P_A, P_B, and C share LoRA init and batch order; including the chat end token in the answer-only loss.

Canonicalizer in experiment.py reserializes with compact separators, so whitespace is normalized as well as key order. Inspected strings are already compact and pipeline accuracies equal the matching oracle-interface accuracies in outputs/scores.json, so this did not plausibly change the reported value beyond the registered key-order intervention.
Consumer exact-tie break is argmax label order in experiment.py. Unspecified, and inspected label log-probabilities have large margins, so it did not plausibly change the reported value.
problems: The registered event is not met: outputs/scores.json gives point effect 0.04296875 and paired interval [0.021484375, 0.06640625], so the lower endpoint is below 0.05 while the interval still extends above 0.05. This neither confirms recovery greater than five points nor shows that such a recovery is absent.

The effect is sparse (build 17: 13 recoveries and 1 regression; build 29: 11 and 1; both producers semantically correct on all 256 items in outputs/scores.json), and the interval is scoped only to these two builds, so the pre-registered five-point claim is unresolved rather than precisely settled.
grok.reason: The fresh run trained the six registered adapters on pinned Qwen3-0.6B, used the specified seeds, sizes, greedy and label-likelihood decoding, semantic gate, oracle interfaces, and paired seed-404 bootstrap, and wrote the lower endpoint 0.021484375. Outputs, per-build counts, and the printed training log are internally consistent with real model predictions rather than hardcoded scores, and no leakage or exclusion rule altered the contrast. Unspecified prompt, schedule, and initialization details were legal completions of the registration, not changes to the question. The supported finding is a real but sub-threshold format effect: with perfect upstream semantics, canonicalization recovered about 4.3 points and restored training-order accuracy, yet the pre-registered lower bound does not clear five points.

grok.what_it_asks: Whether a semantics-preserving JSON canonicalizer recovers pipeline accuracy that a learned consumer loses when a semantically correct upstream function emits a different legal key order.

in_the_paper.reason: The paper composes compiled functions and ignores key order in its grader, but it neither runs a producer-substitution canonicalization test nor names that question as undone.

relation.reason: The experiment uses the paper's spec-specialized shared interpreter as a working part and tests an interface-substitutability property the paper does not claim.

obvious.reason: Most first follow-ups would target the accuracy-compiler tradeoff, teachers, or user studies; only one or two would specify canonicalizer-versus-raw key-order substitution.

who_would_care.reason: A clear answer would change interface handling for groups that compose this kind of compiled function, not practice across a whole research topic.

misreads_paper.reason: The plan's statements that the seed composes functions and treats key order and whitespace as semantically irrelevant match the composition sections and the LEM grader.

answerable.reason: The raw-versus-canonical contrast can be read as interface recovery only if the trained producers and consumer actually learned their tasks, which the design cannot guarantee.

grok.what_came_out: On two Qwen3-0.6B LoRA builds and 256 held-out records, canonicalizing producer B raised equally weighted pipeline accuracy from 93.16% to 97.46%, a gated recovery of 0.043 whose paired 95% bootstrap interval was [0.021, 0.066].

prerequisite.reason: Both producers were semantically correct on every test item and the consumer reached 97.5% on the training key order, so the adapters learned the tasks the contrast assumes.

evidence.reason: Canonicalization recovered 4.3 points with a paired interval of 2.1 to 6.6 that excludes zero, a clear gain in the claimed direction even though it sits somewhat under five points.

next_step.reason: The run isolates a reliable key-order penalty that canonicalization fully removes, which is enough to justify a larger study of the same interface question.

opus.what_it_asks: Does reserializing a semantically correct upstream compiled function's JSON into the key order a downstream compiled consumer was trained on recover end-to-end accuracy, compared with feeding the consumer the raw differently-ordered JSON, and so show whether independently compiled neural functions are interchangeable behind a semantically equivalent interface?

in_the_paper.reason: The paper reports composition demos and an evaluation metric that ignores key order, but it never tests whether a compiled consumer is sensitive to legal serialization differences from a substituted producer, and it does not name this question as future work.

relation.reason: The experiment uses the paper's compiled-function setup (LoRA adapters on a frozen Qwen3-0.6B interpreter, composed into a pipeline) to test an interface-substitution property the paper makes no claim about.

obvious.reason: Formatting sensitivity is a known worry, but a producer-substitution test with key-order canonicalization at the interface between compiled functions is a specific angle that only one or two of ten researchers would likely list.

who_would_care.reason: The answer mainly matters to people building pipelines from PAW-style compiled adapters, who would decide whether to add canonicalization layers or serialization-diverse training.

misreads_paper.reason: The plan says the paper composes compiled functions and treats key order and whitespace as irrelevant in its LEM evaluation, and both statements match the paper's text and grader prompt.

answerable.reason: The gated contrast is readable only if producer P_B actually learns to emit semantically correct JSON in its own key order, so that there are correct cases whose interface differs from the consumer's training format.

opus.what_came_out: On Qwen3-0.6B LoRA components with synthetic 1-3-record lists, canonicalizing P_B's output raised pipeline accuracy from 93.2% to 97.5%, a gated effect of 4.30 points with paired 95% bootstrap interval [2.15, 6.64] over 256 test records × 2 builds (26 recoveries vs 2 regressions), matching the consumer's 97.5% vs 93.2% accuracy on oracle JSON in the two key orders.

prerequisite.reason: Both producers were 100% schema-valid and semantically correct in both builds, and the audit shows P_B emitted the priority-active-id order, so the interface-only contrast is readable.

evidence.reason: A clear positive recovery whose interval excludes zero (lower bound 2.1 points) appeared consistently in both builds; the point estimate (4.3) is somewhat below the 5-point figure, and a smaller-than-stated effect in the claimed direction counts as support.

next_step.reason: The effect is clear but may come only from a consumer trained on a single fixed key order, which the paper's teacher-synthesized data might not share.
next_step.what: Repeat with a consumer trained on serialization-diverse JSON, or compiled with teacher-synthesized data as in the paper, to see whether the key-order sensitivity persists.

sol.what_it_asks: The experiment compares a learned record-selection consumer fed a semantically correct replacement producer's raw JSON with the same consumer fed canonicalized JSON to learn whether normalization recovers accuracy lost to a legal key-order change.

in_the_paper.reason: The paper demonstrates composition and uses formatting-tolerant semantic grading, but neither measures canonicalization after producer substitution nor explicitly identifies this question as unfinished.

relation.reason: It extends separately trained adapter components with an interface-normalization intervention, testing substitutability rather than disputing the paper's correctness results or composition demonstrations.

obvious.reason: Formatting robustness and JSON normalization are familiar, but their specific comparison at an independently trained producer-consumer interface would likely appear on only one or two first-ten lists.

misreads_paper.reason: The plan accurately describes the paper's composition demonstrations and formatting-tolerant evaluation without attributing a demonstrated semantic-substitutability guarantee to it.

sol.what_came_out: Across two Qwen3-0.6B LoRA builds on 256 held-out synthetic record lists, canonicalization increased replacement-producer pipeline accuracy from 93.16% to 97.46%, a 4.30-percentage-point gain with a paired 95% bootstrap interval of 2.15–6.64 points for these fixed builds, while both producers achieved 100% semantic correctness.

prerequisite.reason: The consumer achieved 97.46% accuracy on original-order oracle JSON, both producers were semantically correct on every test case, and canonicalization preserved parsed values and array order.

evidence.reason: The paired interval excludes zero and supports an accuracy recovery from canonicalization, although it does not establish that the recovery exceeds five percentage points.

next_step.reason: The positive paired effect with correct producers and value-preserving normalization justifies a larger study of interface compatibility across more schemas, components, and builds.

registration.title: Boundary-matched rehearsal for a small specification update
registration.seed_connection: The seed presents compiled artifacts as versionable software, but does not evaluate how to revise one clause while preserving unchanged behavior. This experiment tests an inexpensive update strategy rather than recompiling every function from scratch.
registration.hypothesis: When updating a compiled function, rehearsal examples immediately outside the changed semantic region improve worst-region updated-specification accuracy more than an equal number of label-matched random unchanged examples.
registration.contribution: A localized software-revision assay with exact changed and unchanged regions. It tests boundary-matched rehearsal against a controlled random-rehearsal comparator, rather than claiming novelty for replay or counterfactual augmentation themselves.

closest_work.difference: SAUL preserves unrelated factual knowledge using random-fact augmentation. This experiment studies conditional behavioral rules and directly compares boundary-matched with label-matched random rehearsal under identical patch budgets.

DMLE studies cross-form editing of mathematical and physical rules through layer-specific interventions. Here the intervention is a small per-function LoRA update, evaluated on exact changed, near-unchanged, and far-unchanged input regions.

This work uses counterfactual examples for active learning. The proposed experiment applies controlled contrasting examples to an already compiled artifact undergoing an explicit specification revision, with regression rather than cold-start learning as the central concern.

inputs: Model: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
PyTorch, Transformers, PEFT, and NumPy.
Locally generated refund and shipping records with executable old-specification and new-specification oracles.
The provided seed paper and compile.py for architectural reference only; no hosted initializer or teacher is needed.
registration.method: Implement two versioned functions. Refund V0: eligible iff unopened AND NOT final_sale AND days <= 30. Refund V1 extends the limit to 60 days only for members; all other conditions remain. Fields are days 0-90 and three Booleans. Output A for eligible and B otherwise. Shipping V0: C/manual if weight > 20 kg; otherwise A/fast if urgent AND domestic; otherwise B/standard. Shipping V1 also sends fragile parcels to manual, with manual taking precedence. Weight is an integer 1-40 and the other fields are Boolean. Both V0 specifications explicitly state that the soon-to-be-relevant member or fragile field currently changes nothing. Build deterministic natural-language renderers with four training templates, shuffled fact order, irrelevant identifiers, and two held-out evaluation templates. For each task and seeds 17 and 29, train an old adapter on 512 class-balanced V0 examples: frozen BF16 base, rank-16 LoRA, alpha 32, dropout 0 on attention and MLP projections, AdamW 3e-4, cosine decay, 80 updates, batch 16, maximum complete sequence 256, answer-only loss, and disabled thinking. Clone its weights into two patch arms. Both receive the identical 32 fresh examples where V0 and V1 disagree, labeled by V1, and use the complete V1 runtime scaffold. Boundary rehearsal adds 32 unchanged examples made by minimally moving those changed records outside the edit region: flip one relevant Boolean or move the numeric field to an adjacent decision boundary, retaining only cases on which V0 and V1 agree. Random rehearsal instead draws 32 fresh unchanged records, matched to the boundary set's output-label counts and rendering-template frequencies. Reset optimizers identically and patch each arm for 24 updates, batch 16, learning rate 3e-4 with cosine decay. Add two diagnostic references: old weights with only the scaffold changed, and a fresh V1 adapter trained for 80 updates on 512 V1 examples. Pre-generate 192 tests in each of three regions per task: changed, unchanged but one semantic-field edit from a changed case, and other unchanged cases. For numeric fields, an adjacent semantic boundary means days 30 or 61 for refunds and weight 21 for shipping. Use new identifiers, combinations, and held-out renderings. Deduplicate rendered strings across train, patch, and test splits. Predict by highest-likelihood allowed output label. The executable oracles isolate update dynamics from teacher errors; they are not proposed as a necessary deployment dependency.

event.description: Boundary-matched rehearsal improves the minimum accuracy across changed, near-unchanged, and far-unchanged regions by more than five percentage points relative to random rehearsal.
event.statistic: Lower endpoint of a paired 95% bootstrap interval for the mean difference S_boundary - S_random, where S is the minimum of the three region accuracies for each task and seed, averaged equally across tasks and seeds.

evaluation.procedure: Generate and freeze tests with seed 9001 before any adaptation. Evaluate the old artifact, scaffold-only update, both patch arms, and clean V1 rebuild. Compute the registered worst-region contrast without checkpoint selection. Bootstrap 2000 times with seed 404 over records within task and region, preserving all methods and training seeds; recompute each minimum and use the 2.5th percentile. cases.jsonl stores record fields, renderings, both oracle labels, region assignments, and splits. rehearsal_sets.jsonl stores changed examples, matched counterfactuals, random controls, and pairing information. predictions.jsonl stores all model labels, candidate scores, and correctness under both versions. training.jsonl stores configurations, losses, update counts, and timings. scores.json stores the primary statistic, interval endpoints, region accuracies, and old-correct-to-new-wrong regression counts. Intervals are conditional on these tasks and builds; a failed event does not establish that the two rehearsal strategies are equivalent.
evaluation.controls: Patch arms start from identical old weights, share changed examples, use the same new scaffold, and receive equal rehearsal counts, label histograms, and optimization exposure. Scaffold-only and clean-rebuild references reveal whether editing was necessary and whether the patch budget is adequate. Worst-region scoring prevents improvement confined to the edited region from hiding regressions elsewhere.

registration.full_scale_study: Study longer sequences of specification revisions, richer rule families, and teacher-generated contrasting examples. Measure accuracy, regressions, synthesis cost, and update latency against full rebuilds and conventional replay.

agent.reason: Boundary-matched examples directly constrain overgeneralization of the revised rule, providing a plausible advantage over random rehearsal. Nevertheless, the revised scaffold and shared changed examples may already suffice for these simple policies, and improvement must survive worst-region scoring.

registration.title: Does a behavior-preserving LoRA rewrite survive four-bit artifact packaging?
registration.seed_connection: The repository's convert_to_gguf function separately quantizes both LoRA factors to Q4_0 before packaging. This experiment tests whether mathematically equivalent adapter representations remain behaviorally interchangeable after that export operation, while holding the interpreter fixed.
registration.hypothesis: Two mathematically equivalent factorizations of the same trained adapter produce more than two percentage points of excess prediction disagreement after Q4_0 packaging compared with their unquantized numerical-control disagreement.
registration.contribution: An artifact-level semantic regression assay, not a new quantization method. It measures individual-call substitutability under the seed's actual adapter quantizer, whereas aggregate accuracy can conceal which calls change. The experiment isolates adapter export rather than claiming to reproduce the complete quantized PAW runtime.

closest_work.difference: LoRAQuant already uses SVD reparameterization for adapter quantization; that transformation is explicitly borrowed here. This experiment applies uniform GGUF Q4_0 export and measures paired behavioral identity against unquantized controls, rather than proposing mixed-precision allocation or optimizing aggregate task performance.

RoLoRA rotates the model and uses rotation-aware training for weight-activation quantization. Here the base model and activations are unchanged, no post-training optimization occurs, and only an equivalent representation of the trained adapter is exported.

inputs: Model: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
SST-2 train and validation splits: https://huggingface.co/datasets/stanfordnlp/sst2
BoolQ train and validation splits: https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/boolq
PyTorch, Transformers, PEFT, datasets, NumPy, and the public gguf Python package.
The provided seed repository's convert_to_gguf implementation, specifically its use of GGMLQuantizationType.Q4_0 on both factors.
registration.method: Use a standalone local training loop, not the seed's hosted compilation entry point. Define two reusable binary functions: sentiment classification on SST-2, with A=positive and B=negative; and passage-grounded yes/no answering on BoolQ, with A=yes and B=no. Keep a fixed natural-language scaffold per function and disable thinking. Before sampling, exclude examples whose complete prompt and target would exceed 384 tokens; do not truncate passages. Sample 512 class-balanced training examples and 512 class-balanced validation examples per dataset with fixed seed 9001. Public split membership must remain intact. Train one adapter per task and seeds 17 and 29: frozen BF16 base, random rank-64 LoRA with alpha 16 and dropout 0 on q/k/v/o and gate/up/down projections, answer-only loss, AdamW 2e-4, weight decay 0, cosine decay, 80 updates, batch 16. Keep adapter parameters in FP32 for the export comparisons. For each learned update B*A, construct an equivalent balanced SVD factorization without a dense full-weight SVD: compute thin QR decompositions B=Qb*Rb and A_transpose=Qa*Ra; SVD the small core Rb*Ra_transpose=U*S*V_transpose; set B_star=Qb*U*sqrt(S) and A_star=sqrt(S)*V_transpose*Qa_transpose. Preserve the original alpha/r scaling. Check relative Frobenius error of B*A versus B_star*A_star for every projection, requiring less than 1e-4; failure is an implementation failure, not evidence for the hypothesis. Create six evaluation conditions from each adapter: original factors unquantized, SVD factors unquantized, original factors Q4_0 round-tripped, SVD factors Q4_0 round-tripped, original factors Q8_0 round-tripped, and SVD factors Q8_0 round-tripped. Use gguf.quants.quantize and dequantize on contiguous FP32 matrices exactly as in the seed's factor export, then load the recovered factors into the same GPU interpreter. No base-model quantization, merging, calibration, retraining, or basis selection on validation data is allowed. Evaluate all conditions by A/B continuation likelihood on identical validation inputs. Use PyTorch SDPA and ordinary GPU inference; do not build llama.cpp or another runtime. This tests the adapter quantization operation, not low-bit kernel speed or complete Q6_K runtime fidelity.

event.description: Equivalent adapter factorizations acquire more than two percentage points of additional prediction disagreement after Q4_0 export.
event.statistic: Lower endpoint of a paired 95% bootstrap interval for mean(D_Q4 - D_float), where D_Q4 is original-versus-SVD prediction disagreement after Q4_0 round-trip and D_float is the corresponding disagreement without quantization, equally averaged across datasets and training seeds.

evaluation.procedure: Record all six conditions' predictions and label margins on every held-out item. Compute the registered disagreement contrast; also record each condition's gold-label accuracy and its correct-to-wrong and wrong-to-correct transitions relative to the original unquantized adapter. Bootstrap 2000 times with seed 404 over validation items within dataset, retaining all export conditions and both training-seed outputs for each item; use the 2.5th percentile. data_manifest.json stores dataset identifiers, revisions, selected row identifiers, prompts, labels, and length-filter decisions. factor_checks.jsonl stores numerical-equivalence errors, tensor shapes, and quantization reconstruction errors for every projection. predictions.jsonl stores predictions, margins, correctness, condition, and seed. training.jsonl stores configurations, losses, timings, and package versions. scores.json stores the primary statistic, both interval endpoints, the Q8 control, and accuracy/transition diagnostics. Report upper bounds as well: failure of the registered positive event alone does not demonstrate semantic preservation.
evaluation.controls: The underlying learned update, interpreter, scaffold, input set, and decoding are fixed. Unquantized original/SVD comparisons measure numerical reparameterization effects, while Q8 comparisons test whether disagreement is specific to stronger compression. Both Q4 representations have the same rank and bit-width budget. No claim is made that SVD is a new method or that either representation must improve accuracy.

registration.full_scale_study: Audit complete exported neural-function artifacts across adapter bases, bit widths, interpreter quantizations, and real runtimes. Develop per-function post-export regression gates and investigate whether canonical factorization improves release stability rather than merely average benchmark accuracy.

closest_work.difference: LoRAQuant applies SVD reparameterization to LoRA adapters before quantizing them. It uses this to give important singular components higher precision and quantizes the rest to ultra-low bits, then reports aggregate task performance on LLaMA-2 and Mistral. It does not measure whether the original and the SVD-equivalent factorizations, both put through the same uniform GGUF Q4_0 round-trip, give the same prediction on each item, and it uses no unquantized or Q8_0 disagreement baseline.

RoLoRA rotates the base model and trains with rotation awareness for weight-activation quantization. The registered experiment leaves the base model and activations untouched and only exports an equivalent factorization of an already-trained adapter, with no training after export.
GLoRA points out that operating on raw LoRA factors depends on which equivalent factorization is chosen, but it studies this for federated aggregation, not quantization or export.

This paper uses GGUF quantization error to make a model behave differently once quantized, as an attack on full base models. It does not examine whether harmless, mathematically equivalent rewrites of an adapter stay interchangeable after Q4_0 export.

registration.title: A crossed test of specification wording at synthesis and scaffold stages
registration.seed_connection: The seed uses a specification both to generate supervision and to construct the training/runtime scaffold. Its aggregate evaluation does not separate these sources of build variability. This experiment studies those two interventions without assuming that their effects are additive.
registration.hypothesis: For the registered equivalent specifications, synthesis-wording disagreement exceeds same-wording regeneration disagreement plus the training-and-runtime scaffold disagreement by more than five percentage points.
registration.contribution: The contribution is a controlled diagnostic of two specification pathways, not a new claim that prompts matter. Fixed-weight scaffold swaps additionally distinguish immediate inference sensitivity from changes induced during training. The primary contrast is descriptive, not an additive decomposition of causal contributions.

closest_work.difference: Training Prompt Matters studies equivalent training prompts with fixed supervision. This experiment independently varies the specification used to synthesize supervision and the scaffold used to train the student.

Program-as-Weights evaluates specification perturbations through an amortized compiler. This experiment separates synthetic-data wording, regeneration, training-scaffold wording and fixed-weight inference-scaffold sensitivity.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 from https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 for local synthesis.
Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B from https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B for compiled functions.
Two procedural Boolean policies fully specified in the method.
CUDA-enabled PyTorch, Transformers with Qwen3 support, PEFT and NumPy.
registration.method: Implement two policies over eight Boolean fields. Triage fields are action, today, vip, newsletter, quoted, cancelled, snoozed, security. Its positive clauses are security AND NOT quoted; and, separately for each of action, today and vip, that field AND NOT newsletter AND NOT quoted AND NOT cancelled AND NOT snoozed. Refund fields are receipt, damaged, window, unopened, digital, final_sale, recalled, registered. Its positive clauses are recalled AND registered; receipt AND damaged; receipt AND window AND unopened AND NOT digital AND NOT final_sale. Return 1 if any positive clause holds, otherwise 0. Mechanically render two equivalent English specifications. A begins 'Return 1 if any of the following conditions holds', gives the clauses in listed order as prose, and ends 'Otherwise return 0'. B begins 'The default output is 0. Override it with 1 whenever at least one of these cases applies', gives the identical clauses in reverse order as numbered lines, and says no other exceptions apply. Expand every conjunction and negation explicitly as field-is-true or field-is-false statements. Both specifications contain the same schema and single-digit output contract; do not use an LLM to paraphrase them. For each task, wording and synthesis seed 101 or 202, issue exactly 32 teacher requests, each requesting four diverse examples in a JSON object with an examples array. Each example must have an input object containing exactly the eight Boolean fields and an output string equal to 0 or 1. Use temperature 0.8, top_p 0.95, a 640-new-token cap, the non-thinking chat template and GPU generation batches of 16. Restart the sampling RNG stream for each pool using its registered synthesis seed, and retain request order. Validate JSON syntax, keys, types and output alphabet only; do not filter or correct semantic errors. Retain the first 96 valid examples per pool, preserving duplicates. If any of the eight pools is incomplete, report incomplete synthesis rather than filling it procedurally. Canonically serialize accepted inputs in schema order for student training. Unload the teacher. Cross every pool with both training scaffolds, yielding 16 adapters. A scaffold consists of its specification followed by the JSON input and the output contract. Use fresh zero-B-initialized LoRA with rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0 and q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, gate_proj, up_proj and down_proj targets. Freeze the BF16 base. Use AdamW with zero weight decay, cosine learning rate 2e-4 to 2e-5, 32 optimizer steps, effective batch 16, microbatch 8, maximum sequence length 512 and output-only loss including EOS. Reset initialization seed 17, optimizer state and the example-index shuffle stream for every fit. Cycle shuffled indices as needed; all pools have the same size. Evaluate every adapter with both inference scaffolds, although its packaged prediction is defined to use its training scaffold. Evaluate all 256 assignments for its policy in canonical and reversed JSON key order. This is a behavioral census that can include training assignments, not a held-out logical-generalization estimate. Disable thinking and greedily generate at most four tokens; strip whitespace and normalize to 0, 1 or INVALID. Also evaluate the unadapted interpreter under both scaffolds. Batch inference, dynamically pad sequences and reuse the loaded base between fits. No hosted APIs or PAW initializer are used.

event.description: The registered synthesis-wording contrast is substantially larger than regeneration variability and the training-plus-runtime scaffold contrast.
event.statistic: S = D_word - D_seed - D_scaffold, using packaged predictions. D_word compares synthesis wordings A and B at matched synthesis seed and fixed training/runtime scaffold. D_seed compares seeds 101 and 202 at fixed synthesis wording and scaffold. D_scaffold compares training-and-runtime scaffold A with training-and-runtime scaffold B for the same generated pool. Each disagreement is the fraction of unequal normalized predictions, averaging tasks, applicable factor levels, truth assignments and the two serializations equally. Set S=-1 with an incomplete-run status if a required pool or fit is missing.

evaluation.procedure: Write S and its three components to outputs/summary.json. Also report disagreement under fixed-weight inference-scaffold swaps, the complete synthesis-wording by training-scaffold by inference-scaffold accuracy table, and pairwise accuracy difference-of-differences at each fixed third factor. Do not interpret S as a partition of total variability or extrapolate two synthesis seeds to a population of paraphrases. Report teacher oracle-label accuracy, duplicate rate, distinct-assignment coverage, label balance, student oracle accuracy and INVALID frequency separately. outputs/teacher_generations.jsonl holds prompts, raw responses, RNG information and validation decisions. outputs/training_examples.jsonl holds retained pairs, pool IDs and audit-only oracle labels. outputs/training.jsonl holds losses, learning rates and elapsed times. outputs/predictions.jsonl holds every raw and normalized prediction, artifact identity, inference scaffold and oracle label. outputs/config.json records exact specifications, model revisions, package versions, settings and cold-start wall-clock timings. Oracle labels must not influence training, acceptance or selection.
evaluation.controls: Same-wording regeneration estimates ordinary synthesis variability. Fully crossing pools and training scaffolds separates the interventions. Fixed-weight scaffold swaps identify immediate inference sensitivity. Common initialization, schedules, counts and decoding remove avoidable training differences. Interactions and correctness are reported rather than assumed away.

registration.full_scale_study: Extend to many independently constructed policies, equivalent renderings, synthesis seeds, teacher families and interpreter sizes. Compare canonicalizing specifications before synthesis with canonicalizing only the packaged scaffold, measuring reproducibility and correctness rather than disagreement alone.

registration.title: Can disjoint policy patches be composed by adding effective LoRA deltas?
registration.seed_connection: The seed presents compiled neural functions as versioned artifacts. This motivates testing whether independently learned, behaviorally disjoint edits can be combined without another training run. The seed does not claim to implement such patch merging.
registration.hypothesis: Adding effective weight deltas for two disjoint policy edits retains more than 95% of the joint-update model's correct decisions in each edited and unchanged region of the registered behavioral census, for both training seeds.
registration.contribution: Task arithmetic is established. This experiment tests specification-level disjointness within one function, uses regional casewise regressions rather than average multitask accuracy, and evaluates every reference through the same materialized-weight numerical path.

closest_work.difference: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic establishes weight-vector arithmetic across tasks. This experiment tests two formally disjoint edits to one executable policy and measures failures inside each edit scope and outside both.

Model Editing by Standard Fine-Tuning studies edits and locality-preserving supervision. This experiment asks whether independently trained functional patches can be combined without further optimization.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B from https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B.
A procedural request-routing task and four exact policies defined in the method.
CUDA-enabled PyTorch, Transformers, PEFT and NumPy.
registration.method: Requests contain channel in {email, chat, ticket}, Boolean urgent, deadline, cancelled, vip, newsletter, quoted, archived and automated fields, and an irrelevant request_id. Define f0 = (urgent OR deadline) AND NOT cancelled. Define fA = f0 OR (channel=email AND vip AND NOT cancelled), fB = f0 AND NOT(channel=chat AND newsletter), and fAB = fA AND NOT(channel=chat AND newsletter). Positive output is I and negative output W. Exhaustively enumerate the 768 channel/Boolean states and assert that CA={fA!=f0} and CB={fB!=f0} are disjoint; they contain 16 and 48 states. Let U be their complement. Use one constant scaffold for every model: 'Apply the compiled request-routing policy to this JSON request. Return only I or W.' Do not put changing rules into the prompt. Using data seed 314, create 768 initial requests, half from each f0 label, sampling states uniformly within label. Create one common update pool with 256 requests from each of CA, CB and U, sampling uniformly within region and balancing f0 labels within U. Give every request a unique nonce and independently randomized JSON key order. Label the same update inputs under fA, fB and fAB. For each optimization seed 7 and 19, train f0 for 80 steps, clone its adapter into A, B and joint branches, and reset optimizer state. Train A and B for 40 steps each and the joint branch for 80 steps. Construct a shuffled/cycling update-index stream of 1280 presentations; both single patches consume this stream, while the joint branch consumes it twice. Thus the joint branch and the two patches combined have identical input multiplicities and total optimizer steps, though their learning-rate trajectories differ. Use rank-16 LoRA, alpha 32, dropout 0, all seven attention/MLP projection types, a frozen BF16 base, output-only loss including EOS, AdamW with zero weight decay, cosine learning rate 2e-4 to 2e-5 per stage, effective batch 32, microbatch 16 and maximum sequence length 256. Share initialization and input order within each seed; never tune using evaluation results. After training, convert the original BF16 base values and every saved factor to FP32. For each adapted matrix compute D=(alpha/r)BA in FP32. Materialize all four references as Wbase+D0, Wbase+DA, Wbase+DB and Wbase+DAB, and the merged candidate as Wbase+DA+DB-D0. Evaluate all five as clean, adapter-free FP32 models with identical inference settings and TF32 disabled. Do not compare an active BF16 adapter with a folded BF16 candidate. Check the matrix formula numerically and verify that non-adapted parameters are unchanged. Build a common test census containing four independently rendered requests for each of the 768 states, using data seed 315, fresh IDs and random key orders. Evaluate all five models on these 3072 requests for each training seed. Disable thinking, decode greedily for at most four tokens and treat anything other than I or W after whitespace stripping as incorrect. This deliberately uses exact supervision to isolate the weight-composition question; it is not a reproduction of the seed's teacher or warm-start recipe.

event.description: The merged artifact stays within a five-percent casewise regression budget in both edit scopes and the unchanged region for both fitted seed pairs.
event.statistic: S is the maximum over the six seed-by-region cells of count(joint correct AND merged incorrect)/count(joint correct), using fAB as the oracle for both models. This is an exact statistic on the registered finite census, not a confidence bound on deployment risk. Set S=1 and mark inadequate-reference if f0, either single patch or the joint model scores below 0.85 against its own oracle in any region. A numerical materialization-check failure also produces S=1 with an implementation-failure status, not evidence against additivity.

evaluation.procedure: Compute regional conditional harmful regressions, repaired errors and absolute accuracies. outputs/summary.json contains S, all gates, six regional regression rates and per-state failure tables, explicitly exposing the small numbers of distinct states in CA and CB. Do not treat four renderings of a state as four independent logical tests or attach rendering-level population confidence bounds. outputs/examples.jsonl contains initial, update and test requests, semantic state IDs, region membership and all policy labels. outputs/training.jsonl contains schedules, losses, learning rates and timing. outputs/predictions.jsonl contains raw outputs and correctness against the relevant oracle for every materialized model. outputs/merge_checks.json contains factor scales, formula residuals, dtypes and unchanged-parameter checks. outputs/config.json records prompts, revisions, seeds, optimizer settings, inference settings and cold-start timings. No coefficient search, post-merge training or model selection is permitted.
evaluation.controls: Original, single-patch and compute-matched joint references distinguish merging failure from failure to learn the policies. Common update inputs and a constant scaffold remove support and prompt-change confounds. Effective-matrix arithmetic avoids factor-addition cross terms. Identical FP32 materialization and inference remove the active-adapter versus folded-BF16 numerical confound.

registration.full_scale_study: Study many functions with disjoint, overlapping and conflicting edits, multiple rendering distributions, longer patch histories and teacher-generated supervision. Test whether specification overlap predicts merge failures and whether finite regression suites can authorize updates at a useful risk budget.

agent.reason: Disjoint behavioral scopes do not imply independent parameter updates, making the worst-region five-percent regression budget demanding across both seeds. Shared initialization and replay nevertheless provide a plausible route to successful approximate composition if the competence gates pass.

judge_astra.reason: Shared initialization and disjoint edit regions favor successful merging, but the patches can still modify shared features and decision margins. Staying below 5% conditional regressions in every region for both seeds, while passing all reference-competence gates, is substantially harder than preserving average accuracy.

judge_fable.reason: Naive delta addition from a common f0 start plausibly preserves most behavior, but the max over six cells with a 5% budget (CA has only 64 requests, so ~3 flips fail) plus 24 reference-competence gates at 0.85 (patch A on the 16-state CA region after 40 steps is fragile) make the conjunction demanding.

judge_opus.reason: The two edits are separated by both channel (email vs chat) and f0 status, so first-order spillover of each task vector onto the other's region is plausibly small. However, neither patch is penalised for over-reinforcing the pre-edit label in the other region. The criterion also allows at most 5% regression in every one of six cells, and the CA cell has only 16 states (64 renderings), so one failing state breaks it.

judge_sol.reason: Disjoint logical edit scopes do not ensure disjoint parameter updates, especially with the opposing label balances of the two patch datasets. Effective-matrix arithmetic removes an important numerical confound, but the regional retention requirement across both seeds and the reference-competence gates make success demanding.

judge_luna.reason: Disjoint edit regions make effective-delta addition plausible, but success requires every seed-by-region cell to stay below the regression cap and all reference models to clear the competence gates. The small 16-state edit region makes even a few state-level regressions consequential.

judge_muse.reason: Each patch largely preserves the other region since those labels match the starting policy, favoring additivity, but retaining 95% of the joint model's correct decisions in the tiny 16- and 48-state edit scopes for both seeds is strict.

closest_work.difference: This paper establishes adding and negating task vectors across separate tasks and scores them by average per-task accuracy. It does not test two formally disjoint edits to one Boolean policy, compare a merge (A + B − base) against a jointly trained reference with the same compute, or count regressions case by case within each edit's scope and outside both.

This paper explains why task arithmetic works (weight disentanglement, localized regions in function space) using vision-language multitask benchmarks. It does not run a controlled test with an exact oracle on whether patches to disjoint parts of one function compose.

This paper merges a fine-tuned knowledge-editing model back into its base model to keep the new facts while preserving general ability. It does not add two independently trained, behaviourally disjoint patches and measure regressions by region against a jointly trained model.

This paper finds that summing edit vectors for multilingual knowledge editing (locate-then-edit methods, MzsRE) causes interference, and compares merging variants. Its setting is factual edits across languages, not LoRA patches to an executable classification policy with an exhaustively enumerated state census.
This paper studies single or batched edits made by fine-tuning with locality-preserving supervision. It does not combine independently trained edits after training.
The seed paper describes compiled functions as artifacts that can be versioned and composed, but it does not merge weight patches or test whether edits are additive.

opus.reason: Task arithmetic and edit-merging studies (Ilharco et al., tangent-space task arithmetic, model merging for knowledge editing, multilingual edit-vector summation) already establish the general idea and show that interference is possible. None of the papers I found tests whether two LoRA patches to disjoint parts of one function's specification compose by adding their effective weight deltas. None scores this with casewise regressions against an exact oracle, region by region, relative to a compute-matched joint model. My searches were broad, but they returned nothing that reports this experiment or settles the question in a nearly identical form, so the contribution looks distinct even though the underlying technique is well known.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Task Arithmetic in the Tangent Space formalizes non-interfering composition on disjoint input regions and measures prediction disagreement after merging. Its experiments use separate task datasets, not policy branches trained on identical inputs whose target labels differ only within formally disjoint edit scopes.

Efficient Modular Learning through Naive LoRA Summation directly adds effective LoRA matrices and compares against merged-data training. It studies separate QA domains rather than independently learned, locality-preserving edits to one existing policy.

CollabEdit merges independently edited factual models, includes task-arithmetic baselines, and compares with global editing while measuring locality. It uses MEMIT and MALMEN factual updates rather than LoRA branches supervised on a common input pool under different complete policy versions.

Mapping Post-Training Forgetting in Language Models at Scale already measures casewise correct-to-incorrect regressions and repaired errors, including after model merging. It does not test composition of specification-disjoint policy patches.

sol.reason: Delta addition, disjoint-support task arithmetic, and casewise regression measurements all have precedents, so those ingredients are not independently novel. I found no prior experiment testing the central intervention here: independently training complete policy updates on identical, overlapping inputs, with changes confined to disjoint semantic scopes, then composing their unit-scale deltas and comparing against a joint update inside and outside those scopes. The seed paper composes callable neural functions through ordinary software, not independently trained weight patches.

opus.reason: No list entry tests composing independently trained, disjoint policy patches by adding effective LoRA weight deltas without further training.

sol.reason: No listed experiment combines independently learned, disjoint policy edits through effective-weight arithmetic and measures regional regressions against a joint-update reference.

Test result: S=1.0, inadequate-reference; B-only U accuracies were 0.728338 (seed 7) and 0.659091 (seed 19), below the 0.85 gate. All numerical materialization checks passed.
