registration.title: Does compensatory consumer training trade pipeline gains for interface fidelity?
registration.seed_connection: The seed demonstrates compositions of separately compiled functions. A possible extension is to train a consumer on actual producer outputs, but that can encourage compensation for producer errors instead of compliance with the consumer's own specification.
registration.hypothesis: At fixed predicted-input support, compensatory supervision improves the current pipeline by more than three percentage points over both a learned contract-correct consumer and exact contract application, while losing more than three percentage points to the contract-correct consumer when given correct intermediate values.
registration.contribution: Contradictory supervision overriding instructions is not itself novel. The experiment separates compensation from altered input support using a predicted-input, contract-correct training control, an exact downstream rule baseline and a same-format oracle substitution.

closest_work.difference: Diagnosis Is Not Prescription studies patching hazards and linguistic co-adaptation in agent pipelines. This experiment manipulates consumer supervision and replaces only the intermediate numerical value using an exact oracle.

Small Language Models are the Future of Agentic AI motivates specialized components. This experiment tests a concrete conflict between producer-specific specialization and a reusable component contract.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B from https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, reused for separate producer and consumer adapters.
A procedural duration-expression generator with exact integer-minute labels, defined in the method.
CUDA-enabled PyTorch, Transformers, PEFT and NumPy.
registration.method: Build producer P, which converts an English duration to integer minutes, and consumers implementing b(m)=A for m<60, B for 60<=m<180 and C for m>=180. Generate six equally weighted expression families: numeric integer minutes 1..240; numeric h hours and r minutes with h=0..3 and r in {0,5,...,55}, excluding zero total; decimal hours q/4 for q=1..16, rendered with two decimal places; spelled-out integer minutes 1..59; spelled-out hours 1..3 plus spelled-out minutes in {5,10,15,20,30,45}; and the fixed expressions 'a quarter of an hour', 'half an hour', 'three quarters of an hour', 'an hour', 'one and a half hours', 'two and a half hours', 'three and a half hours', with values 15,30,45,60,90,150,210. Implement a deterministic conventional English number renderer for 1..59, including hyphenated compounds. Sample uniformly within each family. Use three producer-training wrappers: 'Duration: {e}.', 'The timer lasts {e}.', 'Set a wait of {e}.' Consumer-source wrappers are 'Elapsed time was {e}.', 'The requested interval is {e}.', 'Allow {e} in total.' Test wrappers are 'The appointment will run for {e}.', 'Record an interval lasting {e}.', 'Time remaining: {e}.' Use data seeds 314, 315 and 316 to create respectively 288 producer-training examples, 960 consumer-training sources and 768 tests, with equal counts per family. Semantic values may overlap across splits; the wrappers are disjoint. Retain the exact generator value, never a model-inferred label. For each adapter seed 11 and 23, train P for exactly 24 steps with an explicit conversion instruction and integer-only contract. Do not corrupt it, search checkpoints or adjust training based on its error rate. Generate P outputs for the consumer sources and tests. A valid output consists solely of ASCII decimal digits after whitespace stripping and parses to an integer in 0..1440. Invalid outputs are pipeline failures. On valid consumer-training sources create three paired datasets: Cclean receives true minutes and label b(true minutes); Ccomp receives predicted minutes and label b(true minutes); Ccontract receives the same predicted minutes as Ccomp but label b(predicted minutes). Consumers see only a canonical JSON object with a minutes field, never expression text or family. All receive the same explicit threshold specification. Train the three consumers for 64 steps from identical fresh adapter initialization and using the identical source-index schedule. For P and all consumers use a frozen BF16 base, rank-16 LoRA, alpha 32, dropout 0, all seven attention/MLP projections, AdamW with zero weight decay, cosine learning rate 2e-4 to 2e-5, effective batch 32, microbatch 16, maximum length 256 and output-only loss including EOS. Disable thinking; use greedy decoding capped at eight tokens for P and four for consumers. On each valid-producer test case evaluate each consumer with both predicted and true minutes, serialized identically. Also evaluate the exact Python threshold function on both values. Identical consumer inputs may be cached, but retain source-level outcomes. Keep invalid-producer cases in separately reported overall pipeline scores. Before interpreting the event, require at least 384 valid consumer-training sources and 384 valid tests per seed, and at least six percent class-changing producer errors among valid cases in each split. Require Ccontract to achieve at least 0.90 threshold-contract accuracy on both test intermediate sets and Cclean at least 0.90 on true-minute tests. These are prespecified support/competence gates, not permission to change P or select examples.

event.description: Compensatory supervision produces a material current-pipeline benefit beyond exact contract application and a material loss of fidelity under an oracle intermediate.
event.statistic: Let A denote accuracy against the original duration-derived class, averaged equally across seeds using each seed's valid-producer tests. Define G=A(Ccomp,predicted)-max(A(Ccontract,predicted),A(exact threshold,predicted)) and L=A(Ccontract,true)-A(Ccomp,true). S is the fifth percentile of the paired cluster-bootstrap distribution of min(G,L). If any registered support or competence gate fails, set S=-1 and report the specific inconclusive status.

evaluation.procedure: Use 2000 bootstrap replicates, sampling clusters defined by expression-family and true-minute value within each family. Carry all source realizations, both seeds and all consumer outcomes together, then recompute valid-case masks, seed averages, G, L and their minimum. The interval conditions on the fitted producers and consumers, not a population of training seeds. outputs/examples.jsonl holds expressions, split membership, family and true values. outputs/producer_outputs.jsonl holds raw outputs, parsed values, validity and class-changing errors. outputs/consumer_predictions.jsonl holds all six consumer/intermediate outcomes and exact-rule outcomes. outputs/training.jsonl holds losses, schedules and timing. outputs/summary.json holds S, point contrasts, intervals, gates, family results, producer numeric accuracy, label conflicts conditional on predicted minutes, contract violations and overall pipeline scores including invalids. Separately report A(Ccomp,true)-A(Ccomp,predicted): the registered tradeoff does not by itself establish that replacing P with an oracle decreases Ccomp's absolute accuracy. A failed tradeoff can also mean compensation without a fidelity cost. outputs/config.json records generator definitions, prompts, revisions, seeds and timings.
evaluation.controls: Ccomp and Ccontract have identical input support and differ only in target labels, addressing the support-shift explanation. Cclean retains the original oracle-training comparison. The exact threshold baseline prevents apparent gains from merely repairing an undertrained reference consumer. Same-format oracle substitution removes formatting changes. Headroom gates distinguish an uninformative near-perfect producer from evidence against compensation.

registration.full_scale_study: Test extraction, routing and tool-argument pipelines with multiple independently trained producer versions. Compare mixtures of oracle and producer-exposed supervision, and measure actual downstream regressions after producer upgrades rather than inferring them from a ranking reversal.

agent.reason: The fixed producer may lack sufficient threshold-crossing errors, and its remaining errors may not be systematically correctable from predicted minutes alone. Beating exact contract application while also producing a bootstrap-supported oracle-input loss above three points is a restrictive conjunction.

judge_astra.reason: The producer may not supply enough class-changing errors to pass the headroom gates, and predicted minutes alone may not identify repairable errors. Even successful compensation need not cause the required oracle-input fidelity loss, making the joint lower-bound event especially demanding.

judge_fable.reason: The event needs both compensation gains exceeding the exact-threshold baseline and a ≥3-point fidelity loss at a bootstrap lower bound; this requires producer errors that are systematic, consumer-learnable, and land on values that also occur as true minutes, which depends on accidental error structure of a 24-step producer, and several gates can fail.

judge_opus.reason: A briefly trained producer likely makes few threshold-crossing errors, so the at-least-6% class-changing gate may fail. Even if it passes, a consumer that sees only an integer can compensate only where errors dominate a given value; that probably cannot yield a robust gain of more than 3 points over the exact rule together with a fidelity loss of more than 3 points.

judge_sol.reason: Many plausible duration-conversion errors preserve the broad class intervals, threatening the required producer-error headroom. Even with sufficient class-changing errors, conflicting targets for identical predicted minutes could prevent compensation from substantially outperforming the exact threshold rule.

judge_luna.reason: The fixed-support contract control isolates compensation well, but the event requires both a calibration gain and a substantial loss on oracle intermediates. The producer may be too accurate to clear the six-percent error gate, or its errors may be too irregular for the consumer to exploit.

judge_muse.reason: Material gain over exact thresholds requires systematic producer bias recoverable from predicted minutes alone, which is unlikely with broad classes and overlapping supports, and the 6% class-changing-error gates add further inconclusive risk.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: This paper argues that downstream LLM-pipeline modules adapt to the errors their upstream modules typically make (its 'Linguistic Contract' hypothesis). It supports the claim with correlations between a co-adaptation measure and harm from prompt-level patching in agent pipelines. It does not vary consumer training labels (compensatory vs. contract-correct) while holding input support fixed. It also has no exact-rule baseline and no oracle that swaps in the true intermediate value in the same format.

The seed paper compiles and composes separately trained neural functions. It does not test whether training a consumer on a producer's actual outputs trades pipeline accuracy for fidelity to the consumer's own specification.
A position paper arguing for specialized small models. It reports no experiment on producer-specific compensation versus reusable component contracts.

opus.reason: My searches found no paper that sets compensatory supervision against contract-correct supervision on identical predicted inputs and then measures both the pipeline gain and the accuracy loss when the true intermediate value is supplied. The closest work (2605.21958) proposes upstream–downstream co-adaptation as a mechanism, but it uses correlations and does not test the hypothesis with this controlled design. The broader idea of training downstream models on predicted inputs is long-standing in NLP, but I found no arXiv study that answers this specific question about trading interface fidelity for pipeline gains.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Concept Bottleneck Models compares consumers trained on true versus predicted intermediate concepts and reports a tradeoff between ordinary task accuracy and accuracy after oracle correction. It does not hold predicted-input support fixed while changing supervision to contract-correct labels, or compare compensation against an exact downstream rule.

Diagnosis Is Not Prescription reports pipeline patching hazards and evidence consistent with downstream compensation for upstream errors. It does not experimentally manipulate consumer supervision to isolate compensation, and its interventions are not same-format substitutions of an exactly labeled numerical intermediate.

Measuring What Matters uses synthetic concept-bottleneck benchmarks with known labeling rules and studies intervention failures. Its experiments vary concept specification, annotation source, architecture and constraints rather than compare compensatory and contract-correct supervision on identical predicted inputs.

sol.reason: The general tradeoff between adapting to imperfect intermediates and responding faithfully to corrected intermediates is established prior work, not a new contribution. However, I found no paper that answers the registered, narrower question using matched predicted-input supervision, an exact contract baseline and same-format oracle substitution together. These controls distinguish compensation from input-support effects and reference-consumer undertraining, rather than merely changing the dataset, model or metric.

opus.reason: The pipeline entries (6, 30, 37, 49, 58) locate errors or compare modular with monolithic designs, but none trains a consumer on producer outputs to test compensation against contract fidelity.

sol.reason: Unlike the listed pipeline-error diagnostics, this experiment manipulates consumer supervision at fixed predicted-input support to test compensation gains against losses of interface fidelity.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented the registered generator, two fixed producer trainings, three paired consumers per seed, exact-rule control, same-format oracle substitution, all gates, and the 2,000-replicate paired cluster bootstrap. All six required raw outputs and result.json are regenerated. No registration changes, producer corruption, checkpoint selection, or error-conditioned sampling. Pinned the tested Qwen revision and dependency versions; BF16 model/adapter storage uses FP32 AdamW master updates. Full command tested successfully twice in approximately 3.5 minutes; training counts, identical consumer schedules, and initialization hashes audited. Tested S=-1 (inconclusive): all four 6% class-changing-producer-error gates failed (observed 0.13–0.52%); source-count and consumer-competence gates passed. This gate failure is not evidence against the hypothesis.

departures: experiment.py analyze(): the bootstrap draws n_clusters (family, true-minute) clusters with replacement from the pooled set of all clusters. The registration says to sample clusters 'within each family', which most naturally means stratified resampling per family. This could shift the ungated percentile slightly. It cannot change the reported value, because the gates force S=-1.

experiment.py train_adapter(): adapters are stored in BF16, but AdamW keeps FP32 master weights and moments. The registration only specifies AdamW with zero weight decay, so this is an open precision choice that the engineer disclosed. It is unlikely to change the result.

experiment.py train_adapter(): the loss is the token mean within each microbatch of 16, averaged over two microbatches, rather than a token mean over the full 32 examples. This is an open implementation choice with negligible effect.
experiment.py main(): TF32 matmul is enabled, and the Qwen3-0.6B revision and package versions are pinned. Both are reproducibility choices that the registration permits. Not result-changing.

experiment.py analyze(): bootstrap replicates with zero valid cases in a seed would be recorded as -1. This rule is unregistered but conservative, and with about 767 valid tests per seed it is practically never triggered. Not result-changing.

experiment.py parse_producer(): leading zeros are accepted and outputs with more than 4 significant digits are rejected. This is consistent with the registered rule (ASCII digits only, integer in 0..1440). Not result-changing.
evaluate.sh: torchvision and librosa are uninstalled to avoid import conflicts. These packages are unused, so this does not change the result.
problems: outputs/summary.json: all four registered class-changing producer-error headroom gates failed. Observed rates were 0.52% and 0.26% for seed 11 (sources, tests) and 0.21% and 0.13% for seed 23, against a required 6%. S is therefore -1 and the tradeoff hypothesis is untested; the run is neither for nor against compensation.

Design issue (registration): an honestly trained 0.6B producer on these simple duration families makes mostly within-class numeric errors (e.g., 200->180, 205->195). The registered setup therefore had little foreseeable chance of meeting its own 6% headroom gate. With roughly 2–5 class-changing training examples per seed, the Ccomp-versus-Ccontract supervision contrast is nearly vacuous.
README.md / summary.json: the ungated point contrasts (G=-0.0065, L=0.0020) are correctly labelled descriptive only. At this error headroom they carry essentially no information about compensation.
experiment.py: the bootstrap is not stratified by family, which arguably departs from 'within each family'. This is immaterial given the gate failure.
opus.reason: The code implements the registered generator, producer training, the three paired consumers with identical initialization and schedule, the exact-rule baseline, oracle substitution, the gates and the cluster bootstrap. The only departures found are open implementation choices or immaterial ones. The protected run reproduced the engineer's numbers exactly and wrote S=-1 because the prespecified producer-error headroom gates failed, which is the correct outcome under the registration. The evidence is genuine and correctly handled, but it only shows that this producer is far too accurate at the class level (about 0.1–0.5% class-changing errors) for the experiment to say anything about compensation versus interface fidelity. That makes it a valid but uninformative, inconclusive result.

departures: experiment.py: If there are zero valid consumer-training sources, the code raises RuntimeError instead of reporting the registered gate-failure status and S=-1. This branch was not exercised: the two seeds had 960 and 954 valid sources. It did not change this result, but would prevent the prescribed reporting in a zero-valid-source run.

experiment.py, analyze(): A bootstrap replicate with no valid cases for either seed receives -1 for all four contrasts, an additional convention not specified in the registration. This could affect ungated bootstrap percentiles if exercised, but cannot change the reported S here because the observed support-gate failures independently require S=-1.
problems: outputs/summary.json and protected evaluation: All four producer class-changing-error gates failed. Consumer-source rates were 0.521% and 0.210%; test rates were 0.261% and 0.130%, versus the required 6%. Thus the registered tradeoff test is inconclusive despite passing the source-count and consumer-competence gates.

The observed valid-test exact-rule accuracy, derived from the producer metrics, averaged approximately 99.8055%. Even a perfect compensatory consumer could therefore improve over that baseline by only about 0.1955 percentage points on these tests, far below the required three percentage points.

The ungated contrasts are descriptive only: G was approximately -0.652 percentage points and L approximately +0.195 percentage points. They do not establish absence of compensation or equivalence, and the separately reported oracle substitution improved Ccomp accuracy by approximately 0.195 percentage points rather than demonstrating an absolute oracle-induced regression.
sol.reason: The executed code matches the registered generator, models, fixed training counts, paired supervision controls, exact baseline, same-format oracle substitution, decoding settings and principal statistic. The listed edge-case extensions did not plausibly affect the reported value. The fresh evaluation completed successfully, regenerated all required outputs, and supports S=-1 as the prescribed consequence of empirically measured gate failures rather than a hard-coded experimental finding. The producer preserved downstream classes too accurately to provide the necessary treatment contrast or improvement headroom. This is a faithful, valid execution with weak research evidence about the proposed tradeoff, not a supported refutation of the hypothesis.

departures: experiment.py analyze() codes a bootstrap replicate as -1 if a resampled cluster set has no valid cases for a seed, a rule the registration does not define. It could not change the reported value: the class-changing-error gates already force S=-1, and with 767–768 nearly all-valid tests such replicates are not a plausible contributor.

experiment.py reuses the base after PEFT unload; evaluation stderr warns that a leftover peft_config may attach multiple adapters for consumers. The registration assumes a frozen base and fresh consumer adapters. This could not change reported S, which is fixed by producer class-changing rates from the first adapter, measured before any consumer is created.

registration.title: Can length-correlated arrivals damage short compilation runs at fixed exposure?
registration.seed_connection: The seed overlaps synthesis and training while stating that accepted examples and their prescribed order are preserved. This experiment tests a fully specified alternative arrival-to-slot assignment mechanism. It does not assert that the seed's released or deployed scheduler implements that mechanism.
registration.hypothesis: Under the registered length-correlated arrival stress test, arrival-to-slot relabeling reduces long-command exact accuracy by more than three percentage points relative to both genuine shuffling and a request-structure-matched random-arrival control.
registration.contribution: Data-order sensitivity is established. This experiment isolates content-correlated arrival order while matching examples, labels, multiplicities, request blocks, initialization and optimizer steps, and measures the induced learning-rate-weighted exposure.

closest_work.difference: Fine-Tuning Pretrained Language Models studies sensitivity to initialization and data order. This experiment fixes initialization within comparisons and targets a specific arrival-dependent slot assignment.

Curriculum Learning-Guided Progressive Distillation deliberately schedules difficulty. This experiment tests whether a transport-inspired order unintentionally creates a damaging curriculum during a short cosine schedule.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B from https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B.
SCAN training data from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brendenlake/SCAN/master/simple_split/tasks_train_simple.txt.
SCAN test data from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brendenlake/SCAN/master/simple_split/tasks_test_simple.txt; dataset paper arXiv:1711.00350.
CUDA-enabled PyTorch, Transformers, PEFT and NumPy.
registration.method: Parse SCAN IN/OUT records. Map I_WALK, I_RUN, I_LOOK, I_JUMP, I_TURN_LEFT and I_TURN_RIGHT one-to-one to walk, run, look, jump, left and right, preserving all order and repetitions. Use one fixed natural-language scaffold explaining the alphabet and SCAN semantics: primitives emit their actions; a directional motion turns once before moving; opposite turns twice before the motion; around repeats turn-plus-motion four times; turn opposite emits two turns and turn around emits four turns; twice/thrice repeat the entire modified action phrase; X and Y executes X then Y, while X after Y executes Y then X. Require only space-separated action words. With data seed 314 select 768 unique official training commands, 256 each with reference action lengths 1..8, 9..16 and 17..48. Select 600 official test commands before fitting, 200 per bin. Use the 17..48 bin as primary. For each schedule/optimization seed 17 and 29, form a 3072-index list containing each training index four times and shuffle the entire list. SHUFFLE retrieves each scheduled index directly. For both arrival arms, maintain a map from original slot index to consecutive integers: assign the next integer on an index's first occurrence, then retrieve that position from a completion-ordered pool. To construct requests, independently shuffle examples within each length bin and partition them into eight-example blocks, yielding 96 requests; preserve within-request order. ARRIVAL orders these requests by the sum of tokenized input-plus-mapped-output lengths, breaking ties by request index. RANDOM_ARRIVAL independently shuffles the same request blocks. Both use the same relabel mapping from scheduled slots to completion positions. This changes content-correlated arrival order without changing request-block or first-exposure machinery. Repeat all three arms for each of the two seeds. Train exactly 96 steps at effective batch 32, consuming the full schedule. Use identical fresh zero-B LoRA initialization within each seed, rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0, all seven attention/MLP projections, a frozen BF16 base, AdamW with zero weight decay, cosine learning rate 2e-4 to 2e-5, microbatch 16, maximum sequence length 384 and output-only loss including EOS. Assert that every example appears exactly four times in every arm. Reject rather than silently truncate overlength training examples. Disable thinking and use batched greedy generation capped at 96 tokens. No actual teacher latency is measured, no asynchronous service is implemented and no correspondence to uninspected repository code is assumed.

event.description: Length-correlated arrival order causes a material long-command loss beyond both ordinary shuffling and the matched random-arrival mechanism.
event.statistic: For each comparison compute seed-averaged long-bin exact accuracy differences R=EM(RANDOM_ARRIVAL)-EM(ARRIVAL) and H=EM(SHUFFLE)-EM(ARRIVAL). S is the fifth percentile of the paired-bootstrap distribution of min(R,H), using 5000 replicates that resample the same long-command test IDs jointly across all arms and seeds. If either reference arm has long-bin accuracy below 0.20 in either seed, set S=-1 and mark a low-competence pilot.

evaluation.procedure: Normalize predictions only by splitting whitespace. Unknown words, extra actions, missing actions or wrong order are errors. Report exact accuracy in all bins, per-seed contrasts, both primary point differences and S. The bootstrap conditions on the two fitted seed triples and the selected SCAN test distribution, not production arrivals. outputs/examples.jsonl holds selected source records, mapped targets and bins. outputs/schedules.jsonl holds every presentation, original slot, relabeled position, request ID and proxy arrival order. Record per-example first-exposure step and per-bin learning-rate-weighted exposure, defined by summing the learning rate at each presentation in that bin. outputs/training.jsonl holds loss, learning rate and elapsed time. outputs/predictions.jsonl contains raw generations and exact-match decisions. outputs/summary.json contains the primary statistic, intervals, competence gates, exposure diagnostics and accuracy tables. outputs/config.json contains the exact scaffold, model revision, data hashes, seeds and cold-start timings. Failed competence gates or broad intervals do not establish schedule equivalence.
evaluation.controls: Exact multiplicity assertions eliminate data-loss and oversampling explanations. Shared initialization and fixed oracle labels isolate scheduling. RANDOM_ARRIVAL holds request blocks and relabel machinery fixed, making it essential to attribution rather than an optional diagnostic. SHUFFLE provides the ordinary offline baseline. Proxy arrivals are explicitly a stress test, not observed service latency.

registration.full_scale_study: Collect real local-teacher completion traces across specifications and generation strategies. Measure accuracy-latency tradeoffs for deterministic assignment, bounded shuffle buffers and delayed learning-rate decay, and distinguish realistic arrival correlations from deliberately adverse schedules.

agent.reason: The arrival mechanism shifts long-example exposure toward lower learning rates, providing a plausible source of harm. However, short-to-long exposure could help learning, and the event requires a supported advantage for both reference schedules plus adequate reference competence.

judge_astra.reason: The arrival mapping should delay long examples into lower-learning-rate portions of training, providing a credible mechanism for damage. However, short-to-long exposure can also help learning, and the event requires a sufficiently large loss against both competent reference arms.

judge_fable.reason: Long-bin SCAN exact match for a 0.6B LoRA after 96 steps on 768 examples may fall below the 0.20 competence gate, and even if it passes, a short-first exposure shift with cosine decay is unlikely to produce an ≥8-point long-bin loss against both references needed for the paired-bootstrap 5th percentile to clear 3 points.

judge_opus.reason: Long-command exposure under ARRIVAL is shifted later, with about 23% less learning-rate-weighted exposure, but this is effectively a short-to-long curriculum with a recency advantage, so the true effect may be near zero or positive. The event needs about a 7-point deficit against both controls at the 5th percentile, and the long-bin 0.20 competence gate may also fail.

judge_sol.reason: The arrival assignment is designed to postpone long-command exposure toward lower learning rates, making material degradation plausible. However, an easy-to-hard curriculum might help compositional learning, and the event requires competent references plus a bootstrap-supported loss against both controls.

judge_luna.reason: Length-sorted arrivals could expose long examples to lower learning rates, but the same ordering is also an easy-to-hard curriculum and the registered arrivals are only a proxy for service behavior. The bootstrap lower tail and both comparison arms must clear the three-point threshold.

judge_muse.reason: Length-sorted first exposures with cosine decay could disadvantage long commands, but short-first curricula often help and only a fraction of presentations shift, while the 0.20 long-bin competence gates may fail with brief training.

closest_work.difference: The seed paper describes overlapping teacher synthesis with training. It says incoming examples fill open slots for earlier batches 'without changing the accepted examples or their prescribed training order', but it reports no experiment on arrival order or slot assignment. The proposed experiment builds an alternative arrival-to-slot relabeling mechanism and stress-tests it.

This paper shows that data order and initialization seeds cause variance in fine-tuning. It does not isolate a content-correlated (length-sorted) arrival order against a matched random-arrival control, use short-schedule LoRA, or measure accuracy by length bin.

This paper evaluates human-inspired data-ordering and curriculum strategies for LLM fine-tuning on medical QA. It deliberately designs curricula rather than testing an accidental length-correlated order from a streaming relabel scheme, and it does not use SCAN, a request-block-matched control, or learning-rate-weighted exposure.

This paper studies curriculum ordering for data-to-text generation as a way to improve results. It does not ask whether an unintended arrival-induced ordering under a short cosine schedule hurts accuracy on long outputs.
This paper schedules difficulty on purpose for progressive distillation. The proposed experiment instead tests whether a transport-inspired arrival order accidentally creates a harmful curriculum.

opus.reason: I found no work that tests whether length-correlated teacher-arrival order, when mapped onto training slots, hurts long-example accuracy in short LoRA compilation runs, compared against both ordinary shuffling and a random-arrival control that keeps the same request blocks. The seed paper raises this question only implicitly, through its streaming scheduler, and does not evaluate it. The existing data-order and curriculum papers show order sensitivity in general or design curricula on purpose, so none of them settles this specific question.

closest_work.difference: DivOPD studies arrival-order batching in asynchronous distillation, but changes which rollout turns receive updates and addresses unused or stale experience. It does not isolate content-correlated ordering while preserving every example's multiplicity.

Studies how learning-rate decay weakens exposure to late, high-quality data under explicit curricula. It does not test length-correlated request arrivals, first-occurrence slot relabeling, or a request-structure-matched random-arrival control.

Compares explicit length-, attention-, and loss-based ordering with random shuffling during instruction tuning. Its ordinary epoch-based curricula do not reproduce the registered arrival-to-slot assignment and repeated-example scheduling mechanism.
The seed describes overlapping synthesis and training while preserving prescribed training order; it reports no controlled experiment on the alternative arrival-dependent relabeling mechanism.

sol.reason: Data-order sensitivity, length-based curricula, and curriculum–learning-rate interactions are established, so those general ideas are not novel. However, none of the work found answers whether content-correlated request arrivals cause additional damage through this slot-relabeling mechanism at fixed example multiplicities, relative to both genuine shuffling and a mechanism-matched random-arrival control. That controlled attribution distinguishes the registered question from the closest prior experiments.

opus.reason: Entries 8 and 48 measure wall-time savings from streaming while preserving training order, whereas this experiment tests whether length-correlated arrival-to-slot reordering harms accuracy at fixed exposure.

sol.reason: Entries 8 and 48 preserve training order to measure streaming speedups, whereas this experiment changes content order through arrival-dependent assignment and measures resulting accuracy losses at fixed exposure.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented the registered SCAN stress test: all three arms for seeds 17 and 29, matched request blocks and relabel machinery, shared fresh zero-B LoRA initialization within each seed, frozen BF16 Qwen3-0.6B, exact multiplicities and 96-step training, exposure diagnostics, strict whitespace-only exact scoring, competence gates, and 5000 jointly paired bootstrap replicates. No registered-design deviations. Fixed unspecified RNG streams and inclusive cosine endpoints; pinned the model revision. Explicitly disabled Transformers generation-default fallback to enforce greedy decoding and preserved all nonterminal generated tokens when scoring. Tested the final command end-to-end in about 8 minutes with cached weights; independent audit passed for every required output. Observed S=-0.2025 with all competence gates passing: the registered event did not occur, which does not establish equivalence.

departures: experiment.py splits seeds into independent schedule, request-block and random-arrival RNG streams via SeedSequence(seed).spawn(3), and fixes bootstrap seed 20260903. The registration leaves these open. This changes which realization is drawn, not the design, so it is not a fidelity defect.

experiment.py computes the cosine learning rate with inclusive endpoints (t/95), so step 1 uses 2e-4 and step 96 uses 2e-5. This is an allowed interpretation of 'cosine 2e-4 to 2e-5' and is applied identically to all arms; it is not outcome-relevant between arms.

experiment.py takes the token mean within each 16-example microbatch and averages the two microbatch means, rather than one token mean over all 32 examples. The registration does not specify this, and it is the same in every arm, so the effect between arms is negligible.

experiment.py generates with batch size 128 and left padding. The registration says 'batched greedy' without a size. BF16 padding effects are possible but shared across arms, so implausible to change the contrast.
experiment.py enables TF32 matmuls and keeps the LoRA adapters in float32 over a frozen BF16 base. This is unspecified and identical across arms.

experiment.py re-initializes the second seed's adapters with PEFT reset_lora_parameters instead of building a new PEFT model. The result is still a fresh zero-B init, shared byte-identically within the seed, so it is not outcome-relevant.

experiment.py computes the proxy request length from standalone tokenizer lengths of the command plus the mapped target, without the chat scaffold, and sorts ascending with request-ID tie-break. This is a reasonable reading of the registered 'tokenized input-plus-mapped-output lengths'.
run_experiment.sh uninstalls torchvision, torchaudio and librosa before installing pinned packages. This affects only the environment, not the result.
problems: summary.json: the paired bootstrap resamples only the 200 long-bin test IDs. It conditions on two training seeds, so variance between schedules and seeds is not represented. That variance looks large: SHUFFLE long-bin accuracy is 0.345 vs 0.43 across seeds, and per-seed R is -0.185 vs -0.125. The bootstrap intervals therefore overstate precision about the schedule mechanism. The registration acknowledges this conditioning.

summary.json: RANDOM_ARRIVAL is itself about 10 points below SHUFFLE on the long bin in both seeds. The request-block/relabel machinery therefore has a sizeable effect of its own. Because min(R,H) is driven by R, the statistic mixes 'ARRIVAL is better' with 'RANDOM_ARRIVAL is worse'.

summary.json: the observed effect runs opposite to the hypothesis. ARRIVAL raises long-bin accuracy, consistent with long examples being seen late and favoured by recency, and lowers short and mid-bin accuracy by roughly 6–9 points. The non-event therefore reflects a reversed sign, not an absence of order sensitivity. RESULTS.md correctly does not claim equivalence.
The finding concerns synthetic proxy arrivals on SCAN with a 0.6B model over 96 steps. It says nothing direct about the seed paper's actual scheduler, as the registration itself states.
opus.reason: The code implements the registered design closely: the same selection sizes and bins, the four-fold schedule with first-occurrence relabeling into completion-ordered pools, matched request blocks across the two arrival arms, shared within-seed LoRA initialization, the registered optimizer and decoding, strict whitespace scoring, competence gates and the jointly paired bootstrap statistic. Every departure is an unspecified implementation choice applied identically across arms. The protected run reproduces the engineer's earlier logs exactly, and an independent validator recomputes S from the raw predictions. That makes the evidence genuine and correctly computed. The registered event clearly did not occur: in both seeds ARRIVAL matched or beat both references on long commands while losing accuracy on short ones. This is a credible, well-controlled negative finding, though based on only two seeds and with an uncertainty estimate that ignores training-run variance.

problems: outputs/summary.json: Bootstrap intervals condition on only two fitted seed triples; they do not quantify variation across additional optimization or schedule seeds.

experiment.py: Arrival orders are synthetic token-length proxies, not measured teacher completion times or an implemented asynchronous service, so the findings cannot establish a defect in the seed paper's scheduler.

experiment.py: Learning-rate-weighted exposure is a presentation-level diagnostic, not actual gradient influence, because training uses token-normalized microbatch losses and adaptive AdamW updates; it does not by itself establish the causal learning mechanism.
sol.reason: No registration departures are evident: the code preserves the specified data, scaffold, controls, initialization matching, multiplicities, training budget, decoding, competence gates and statistic; RNG streams and cosine endpoint conventions resolve unspecified details. The protected fresh-machine evaluation completed all six runs, produced every required output, and its validator recomputed S=-0.2025 from the logged predictions, with all competence gates passing. ARRIVAL averaged 43.75% long-bin accuracy versus 38.75% for SHUFFLE and 28.25% for RANDOM_ARRIVAL, so the registered material-loss event did not occur and the observed point contrasts ran opposite to the hypothesis. This is a meaningful, supported negative finding for the registered stress test, not evidence of schedule equivalence or statistically established superiority over SHUFFLE. The limited seed replication and synthetic arrivals keep its research value at 2 rather than 3.

departures: experiment.py lr_at uses cosine t/95 so logged steps 1 and 96 hit 2e-4 and 2e-5. The registration named the endpoints but not the discrete formula; this open choice could change absolute accuracy relative to another cosine convention, and it is shared across arms.

experiment.py train_arm backpropagates the average of two microbatch token-mean losses rather than a token-weighted loss over 32 examples. Effective batch 32 and microbatch 16 were registered, but the reduction was not; equal microbatch means can interact with length-imbalanced steps and could change the contrasts.

experiment.py predict removes terminal EOS and post-EOS pad token ids before whitespace-split scoring, and disables Transformers generation-default fallback so decoding stays greedy. The registration required whitespace-only action exact match, greedy decoding, and a 96-token cap; EOS stripping is required for that metric and would change the value only relative to a literal include-EOS score that would fail every competent generation.

experiment.py places the specified scaffold in Qwen's chat template as a system message with enable_thinking=False. Packaging was not verbatim-specified; it is shared across arms and could change absolute accuracy but not the registered comparison.

Unspecified but shared runtime choices in experiment.py (NumPy SeedSequence streams, PEFT default Kaiming-A/zero-B, AdamW betas/eps, SDPA, TF32 matmul, generation batch 128) were left open by the registration. They can move numerical results slightly; they do not change the arms, sample, statistic, or event rule.
problems: Seed 17 RANDOM_ARRIVAL long-bin accuracy is 0.225, only 2.5 points above the 0.20 competence gate (outputs/summary.json), so one essential control is weak even though the registered gate passes.

The 5000-draw bootstrap conditions only on the 200 selected long test IDs and the two fitted seeds (outputs/summary.json). H's interval is [-0.105, 0.005], so the SHUFFLE contrast is not precisely signed, although that interval still lies below the +0.03 damage threshold.

Equal averaging of microbatch mean losses in experiment.py is an untested sensitivity that can interact with the length-correlated treatment; the registration did not specify token-weighted accumulation.

Unspecified optimizer, prompt-packaging, and cosine details were fixed without replacing a registered setting, and EOS stripping implements action-word exact match rather than a different metric. registration.title: Do contract-valid JSON changes break otherwise correct neural handoffs?
registration.seed_connection: The seed's semantic metric can accept formatting differences, and the paper demonstrates composed neural functions. These facts do not establish that a learned downstream function treats every contract-valid representation interchangeably.
registration.hypothesis: Changing only contract-permitted JSON key order and whitespace causes new downstream failures on more than five percent of canonically successful executions under the registered substitutions.
registration.contribution: Serialization sensitivity is known. This experiment measures harmful handoff substitutions with exact semantic and type checks, reports the full key-order by whitespace factorial, and avoids an unnecessary learned-producer eligibility filter. The producer is an exact serializer, so this is not a claim about observed replacements from independently trained producers.

closest_work.difference: Lost in Serialization studies invariance of graph reasoners. This experiment tests a typed component handoff and measures new failures conditional on a previously correct downstream decision.

Field Order Should Not Matter studies positional specialization in metadata retrieval. This experiment measures generative policy decisions and separates key-order, whitespace and interaction effects.
Diagnosis Is Not Prescription examines broader agent-pipeline interventions. Here the intervened strings have executable, exactly verified semantic equivalence.

inputs: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B from https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B.
Locally generated typed ticket records and the exact routing function defined in the method.
Python json and hashlib, CUDA-enabled PyTorch, Transformers, PEFT and NumPy.
registration.method: Use records with exactly these keys: ticket, category, urgent, resolved, vip, channel. ticket is an irrelevant nonce string; category is billing, access or delivery; urgent, resolved and vip are Booleans; channel is email or chat. Enumerate all 48 non-ticket combinations. The consumer returns 0 if resolved; otherwise 2 if urgent OR (vip AND category=access); otherwise 1. Its specification explicitly states that JSON object key order and whitespace do not affect meaning and requires exactly one output digit. For every combination create eight training IDs, two validation IDs and eight test IDs, yielding 384/96/384 records. Derive fixed-length nonce IDs from SHA256 of data seed 314, split, combination and within-combination index; assert disjointness. No learned producer or natural-language extraction stage is required: an exact serializer supplies correct intermediate records. Define four encodings in a two-by-two design: schema key order versus reversed key order, crossed with compact separators versus two-space indentation. The compact schema-order encoding is canonical. Train two consumer regimes for each seed 11 and 29. CANONICAL always sees canonical JSON. VARIED sees the same semantic record indices and labels, but each record's four presentations use all four encodings exactly once, cycling from a record-specific fixed offset. Use four shuffled epochs over 384 records, giving exactly 96 optimizer steps at batch 16. Within each seed share fresh LoRA initialization and semantic-example order across regimes. Use a frozen BF16 Qwen3-0.6B, rank-32 LoRA, alpha 64, dropout 0 on all seven attention/MLP projection types, AdamW with zero weight decay, cosine learning rate 3e-4 to 3e-5, microbatch 16, maximum sequence length 384 and output-only loss including EOS. The regimes match examples and optimizer steps, not input-token counts; record both token counts. Keep the same explicit policy scaffold throughout, disable thinking and greedily decode at most four tokens. At evaluation, invoke each fixed consumer on all four encodings of every oracle test record. Verify exact key sets, string types and Boolean types, rejecting Boolean/integer substitutions and duplicate keys; assert type-preserving parsed equality across encodings. Unit-test that changed field values are rejected by this equivalence checker. Canonicalize every alternative back to identical reference bytes and rerun the consumer in the same batch layout as the original canonical evaluation. This restoration is an identity/determinism check. The primary analysis uses CANONICAL models only. VARIED is a secondary training control, not part of event selection. No hosted compiler, teacher or model-based judge is used.

event.description: Verified meaning-preserving handoff substitutions cause a material rate of new failures in canonically trained consumers.
event.statistic: For each CANONICAL seed, restrict to records correctly classified from canonical JSON. Average the harmful-substitution indicator across the three alternative encodings within each record, then across eligible records, then equally across seeds. S is the fifth percentile of its cluster-bootstrap distribution. Set S=-1 and mark inconclusive if either canonical-trained model has canonical validation accuracy below 0.85, fewer than 256 eligible test records, or a failed identical-byte restoration/determinism check.

evaluation.procedure: Use 2000 bootstrap replicates over the 48 latent factor-combination clusters, carrying their ticket IDs, both seeds, both training regimes and all encodings together. Recompute eligibility and equal-seed means in every replicate. outputs/summary.json holds S, the point harmful-substitution rate, interval, eligibility counts and gates. Report accuracy and invalid-output rates on all oracle records as well as the conditional analysis. For the complete two-by-two error-rate table, report the averaged key-order effect, averaged whitespace effect and interaction e11-e10-e01+e00. Report VARIED-model accuracy on all records and on the eligibility sets defined by CANONICAL models, without redefining eligibility to favor VARIED. outputs/data.jsonl holds records, splits and oracle labels. outputs/training.jsonl holds semantic schedules, chosen encodings, token counts, losses and times. outputs/handoffs.jsonl holds every serialized string, equivalence check, raw consumer output, normalized decision and restoration outcome. outputs/config.json records the exact specification, encoders, seeds, model/package revisions and cold-start timings. A zero observed harmful rate or degenerate bootstrap interval must not be described as proof of population invariance; conclusions concern the tested policy and representations.
evaluation.controls: Exact oracle records remove producer mistakes and producer-based selection. Fixed weights and decoding isolate representation changes. The factorial distinguishes order, whitespace and their interaction. Type-sensitive equivalence checks reject substantive changes. Identical-byte restoration checks determinism, while the matched semantic-exposure VARIED arm tests whether format exposure can remove the observed sensitivity.

registration.full_scale_study: Test actual independently compiled producer versions, larger schemas and longer pipelines. Compare boundary canonicalization with serialization-varied training at matched example budgets, separating representation-induced failures from extraction errors and testing formats not encountered during training.

agent.reason: Canonical-only training could induce positional shortcuts, but the pretrained interpreter may already handle these simple JSON variations robustly. Averaging three substitutions and bootstrapping logical-state clusters makes the registered event appreciably harder than merely observing some formatting-induced failures.

judge_astra.reason: Canonical-only training on a small, repetitive schema can encourage positional shortcuts that alternative serializations disrupt. Material sensitivity is plausible, although the competence gates and clustered lower-bound test require substantially more than a few isolated failures.

judge_fable.reason: An aggressively fine-tuned 0.6B consumer that only ever saw compact schema-order JSON plausibly degrades a few to ~15% under reversed keys and retokenized indented JSON, but pretrained key-name reading may preserve most behavior, so clearing 5% at the cluster-bootstrap lower bound is roughly a coin flip.

judge_opus.reason: A pretrained model reading named JSON keys probably uses content-based binding that largely survives key reversal and indentation; the median harmful rate is plausibly a few percent. Overfitting to a single canonical format with rank-32 LoRA could create positional shortcuts. Under reversal 'resolved' stays in the middle while 'urgent' and 'vip' swap, which would hurt about 1/6 of records under pure positional reading. This leaves a real tail above the 5% bound.

judge_sol.reason: Canonical-only training can encourage representation-specific shortcuts, and reversing keys moves the irrelevant nonce behind the useful fields. I consider harmful substitutions fairly plausible, although pretrained JSON competence and cluster-level uncertainty could keep the registered lower bound below five percent.

judge_luna.reason: Canonical-only fitting could specialize to field positions, making reversed key order harmful, but the model's JSON competence and the explicit invariance instruction may support robustness. The event also requires a sufficiently large conditional failure rate and successful competence and restoration checks.

judge_muse.reason: A small model trained only on canonical JSON is likely to overfit to key order and whitespace despite an invariance instruction, so verified equivalent serializations will probably cause new failures above the 5% lower bound.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Studies how sensitive LLM graph reasoners are to serialization, including syntax and formatting factors, and how fine-tuning changes that. It uses graph-reasoning tasks, not a LoRA-specialized consumer reading typed JSON records. It does not use a key-order × whitespace factorial or measure new failures only on records the model already got right.

Shows large accuracy swings from meaning-preserving prompt-format changes in few-shot prompting (FormatSpread). It does not study a fine-tuned narrow function at a typed JSON handoff, and it does not count harmful substitutions on records the model already classified correctly.

Shows that training on multiple equivalent formats improves cross-format robustness, which overlaps with the experiment's VARIED arm. Its formats are answer formats (e.g., multiple-choice vs. other forms), not contract-valid JSON serializations, and it does not report a conditional harmful-substitution rate.

Mixture of Formats reduces prompt-style brittleness through few-shot prompting. It involves no LoRA-trained consumer, no JSON key-order or whitespace manipulation, and no exact type-checked equivalence verification.

The seed paper uses an LLM-judge metric that accepts JSON whitespace and key-order differences in outputs. It demonstrates composed functions but never tests whether a compiled downstream function handles equivalent JSON inputs the same way.

opus.reason: The general effect is well documented: LLMs are sensitive to meaning-preserving format and serialization changes, and training on varied formats can reduce this. However, I found no paper that measures how often a small LoRA-specialized consumer fails after only contract-permitted JSON key-order and whitespace changes, conditioned on correct canonical predictions, with the full 2×2 factorial. The closest work (graph serialization, prompt formatting, answer-format robustness) addresses related questions in different settings and does not decide whether this specific rate exceeds 5%.

sol.label: close variant

closest_work.difference: Field Order Should Not Matter compares canonical-order fine-tuning with permutation-augmented training and measures degradation after meaning-preserving field reordering. The proposed experiment uses a generative routing consumer rather than a retrieval encoder and adds whitespace variation and conditional new-failure measurement.

Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design measures classification sensitivity to formally defined meaning-preserving formatting changes, including atomic spacing changes. The proposal instead perturbs typed JSON records and uses task-specific LoRA training, exact parsed-equivalence checks, and an order-by-whitespace factorial.

Lost in Serialization evaluates fixed base and fine-tuned generative reasoners under equivalent graph reorderings and syntax changes. The proposal substitutes a small routing policy and restricts its primary metric to executions that were correct under canonical serialization.

sol.reason: Prior work already substantially answers the central question: meaning-preserving serialization changes can alter learned consumers' decisions, and canonical-format specialization can introduce order fragility that varied-format training mitigates. The typed equivalence checker, conditional harmful-substitution rate, and complete factorial refine that established experiment rather than introduce a distinct question; using an exact serializer does not add an independently learned producer-interchangeability test. The proposed policy's particular failure rate remains unknown, but that does not make the contribution novel.

opus.reason: The formatting-related entries (7, 16, 39, 47, 54) concern judge tolerance, and none measures whether a trained downstream function fails under meaning-preserving JSON key-order and whitespace changes.

sol.reason: The listed formatting experiments evaluate semantic judges, whereas this experiment changes verified-equivalent JSON handoffs to measure new downstream policy failures at fixed consumer weights.

registration.title: Grounding teacher synthesis with a handful of unlabeled real inputs: does it close the synthetic-to-real gap of compiled 0.6B functions?
registration.seed_connection: Compile by training synthesizes training pairs from the specification alone (teacher prompt: 'Generate n diverse (input, output) example pairs that follow this specification'). Its benchmark, FuzzyBench-Hard, uses test inputs that were themselves LLM-generated, so the paper never measures how a compiled function behaves on real inputs, nor whether the teacher's imagined inputs match the deployment distribution. A developer usually has a few unlabeled real inputs (e.g., actual emails to triage); this experiment tests the cheapest possible use of them.
registration.hypothesis: Appending 8 unlabeled real inputs (sampled from a 32-item pool) to every synthesis call raises the compiled 0.6B function's accuracy on real labeled test data by at least 3 points on average, relative to spec-only synthesis with the same teacher, example count and training recipe.
registration.contribution: Prior dataset-generation work compares generation with annotation of real data, or steers generation with attributes or with feedback from the student, using encoder/LSTM students and GPT-3-era teachers. This MVE quantifies the real-input gap in the compile-by-training regime (spec-first, decoder-only 0.6B interpreter, rank-64 LoRA, ~1-minute compile, modern instruct teacher) and tests a zero-label, zero-feedback-loop intervention that could be a single optional field in the seed's compile API.

closest_work.difference: Ding et al. compare GPT-3 generating data versus annotating real unlabeled data for BERT-style students; they do not test seeding the generator with unlabeled real inputs, nor a spec-compiled decoder student.

ProGen steers generation with feedback from the task model on synthetic data via in-context examples; here the in-context examples are raw unlabeled real inputs with no feedback loop, and the student is a LoRA-adapted 0.6B interpreter trained for 80 steps.
AttrPrompt diversifies generation with hand-designed attributes; this MVE instead injects real inputs directly and measures realism (real-test accuracy) rather than attribute diversity.
The seed evaluates only on LLM-generated test inputs and spec-only synthesis; this MVE adds real-input evaluation and the grounding condition.

inputs: Teacher: Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (HuggingFace, bf16). Student/interpreter: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (HuggingFace, bf16).

Public classification datasets via the HF datasets library, in priority order; use the first six that load without trust_remote_code (minimum five): stanfordnlp/sst2 (text field 'sentence', test pool = validation split); fancyzhx/ag_news (field 'text', test split); dair-ai/emotion config 'split' (field 'text', test split); CogComp/trec (field 'text', coarse_label, test split); ucirvine/sms_spam (field 'sms', single split, carve test out with seed 0); SetFit/subj (field 'text', test split, label_text column); cornell-movie-review-data/rotten_tomatoes (field 'text', test split); takala/financial_phrasebank config 'sentences_allagree' (field 'sentence', single split). Label word names must be read from the dataset's ClassLabel names (or label_text) and mapped to the words used in the spec.
Python packages: torch, transformers>=4.51, peft, datasets, accelerate. No hosted APIs. Seed 0 everywhere.
Seed paper prompts and recipe (reproduced in the method): teacher synthesis prompt, interpreter prompt template, LoRA recipe from compile.py of the seed repository.
registration.method:
TASK SPECS (one natural-language spec per dataset): sst2/rotten_tomatoes: 'Classify the sentiment of a short movie-review sentence. Output exactly one word: positive or negative.' ag_news: 'Classify a short news article (headline and opening sentences) into exactly one topic: World, Sports, Business, or Sci/Tech. Output only the topic name.' emotion: 'Classify the main emotion expressed in a short social-media style message. Output exactly one word from: sadness, joy, love, anger, fear, surprise.' trec: 'Classify an English question by the type of answer it expects. Output exactly one of these codes: ABBR (abbreviation or its expansion), ENTY (an entity such as an animal, color, product, event, or term), DESC (a description, definition, reason, or manner), HUM (a person, group, or organization), LOC (a location), NUM (a number, date, count, distance, or other numeric value).' sms_spam: 'Decide whether an SMS text message is unsolicited spam or a normal personal message. Output exactly one word: spam or ham.' subj: 'Decide whether a sentence from a movie review or plot summary is subjective (expresses an opinion or feeling) or objective (states a fact or describes plot). Output exactly one word: subjective or objective.' financial_phrasebank: 'Classify the sentiment of a sentence from financial news from an investor's point of view. Output exactly one word: positive, negative, or neutral.'

DATA SPLITS per task (seed 0): TEST = 300 items sampled from the test pool. From the train pool (disjoint from TEST) sample 352 items: POOL32 = 32 items used only as unlabeled grounding inputs; REAL320 = the other 320 items used only for the REAL_LABELED reference.

TEACHER CALLS (transformers batched generate, left padding, bf16, chat template; Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 has no thinking mode). Synthesis uses the seed's prompt verbatim: system = 'You synthesize tiny supervised datasets for finetuning small language models from a natural-language task specification. Return strict JSON with a top-level key 'examples'. Each example must be an object with string keys 'input' and 'output'.'; user = 'Generate 8 diverse (input, output) example pairs that follow this specification.

[SPEC]
{spec}
[END_SPEC]'. Sampling: temperature 0.8, top_p 0.95, max_new_tokens 1024, batch of 60 calls per task per condition. Parse: strip code fences, take the substring from the first '{' to the last '}', json.loads, keep items with non-empty string 'input' and 'output', deduplicate on whitespace-normalized lower-cased input, collect 320 unique pairs (run up to two extra rounds of 30 calls if short; at least 240 required, record the count).

CONDITIONS (same teacher, same N, same recipe): (1) SPEC_ONLY: the prompt above. (2) GROUNDED: the same user prompt with this appended: '

The function will be applied to inputs like the following unlabeled real samples. Generate NEW inputs that match their style, length, vocabulary and messiness, but do not copy or lightly paraphrase them:
[REAL_INPUTS]
{8 items from POOL32, sampled without replacement, a fresh sample per call, each on its own line prefixed by '- '}
[END_REAL_INPUTS]'. (3) REAL_LABELED (reference, not part of the registered statistic): the 320 REAL320 inputs labeled by the teacher with the LABEL prompt: system = 'You are a function implementation. Apply the specification to the input and reply with only the output, with no explanation.'; user = '[SPEC]
{spec}
[END_SPEC]

[INPUT]
{x}
[END_INPUT]'; greedy, max_new_tokens 8. (4) ZERO_SHOT_STUDENT: Qwen3-0.6B with the scaffold prompt and no LoRA. (5) TEACHER_ZS: teacher with the LABEL prompt on TEST (compile-loss reference).

SCAFFOLD (shared by all conditions of a task): one greedy teacher call (max_new_tokens 400) with the PAW examples-style compiler prompt: 'You are PAW-Compiler. Write a PSEUDO-PROGRAM that helps a smaller model solve a task. The interpreter will NOT see the original SPEC; your pseudo-program is the only instruction it gets. It must contain: 1. a clear, concise description of the task (what to do, edge cases, output format); 2. 3-6 example input/output pairs. Format exactly:
[PSEUDO_PROGRAM]
Task: <one paragraph>
Examples:
Input: <example input 1>
Output: <example output 1>
...
[END_PSEUDO_PROGRAM]
Rules: encode ALL requirements from SPEC; cover typical cases and edge cases; keep total length under 250 tokens; always include the closing marker.

[SPEC]
{spec}
[END_SPEC]'. Extract the text between the markers; if missing, use 'Task: {spec}'. Truncate to 250 student tokens at an example boundary.

STUDENT PROMPT (seed's render_prompt_template): user message = '{pseudo_program}

[INPUT]
{x}
[END_INPUT]', rendered with tokenizer.apply_chat_template(add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=False); training target = output text + eos token (<|im_end|>). Loss on target tokens only.

TRAINING (seed recipe with random LoRA init, since the PAW mapper warm start requires the hosted API): PEFT LoRA r=64, alpha=16, dropout 0, target_modules q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj; AdamW lr 2e-4, betas (0.9,0.999), weight decay 0; cosine decay to 2e-5 over 80 steps, no warmup; batch 16 (no accumulation); bf16; max_length 1024; schedule = concatenated shuffled epochs over the unique examples (seed 0) cut to 80x16 presentations; torch/python seed 0. Reload a fresh base model + fresh LoRA for every run.

EVALUATION: greedy decoding, max_new_tokens 16, batch 64. Normalize prediction and gold identically: first line only, strip, drop surrounding quotes/periods, lowercase, remove all non-alphanumeric characters (so 'Sci/Tech' -> 'scitech'); accuracy = exact match. Copy check: for each GROUNDED synthetic input, max difflib.SequenceMatcher ratio against POOL32; report the fraction >= 0.8 (and the same statistic for SPEC_ONLY inputs as the chance level). Also report input length statistics (mean student tokens) for SPEC_ONLY, GROUNDED and TEST inputs.

ORDER AND TIME GUARD: do all teacher work first for all tasks (scaffolds, SPEC_ONLY, GROUNDED, REAL_LABELED labels, TEACHER_ZS), free the teacher, then train/evaluate per task in priority order (SPEC_ONLY, GROUNDED, REAL_LABELED). Stop starting new tasks after minute 27 of the run; at least four tasks must be complete for the statistic.

evaluation.controls: SPEC_ONLY is the seed's own recipe with the identical teacher, example count, scaffold and training schedule, so the only manipulated variable is the presence of 8 unlabeled real inputs in the synthesis prompt. REAL_LABELED bounds what real inputs can buy; ZERO_SHOT_STUDENT shows that training matters at all; TEACHER_ZS gives the compile-loss ceiling; the copy-rate check guards against the grounded condition simply memorizing the pool.

judge_astra.reason: Real exemplars should help reduce stylistic and distributional mismatch, particularly for messy SMS and emotion inputs. judge_fable.reason: Grounded (few-shot-input) generation usually narrows the synthetic-to-real style gap by a few points for encoder students, but here the instruction-tuned 0.6B student already carries a task scaffold that blunts style sensitivity, several tasks (sms_spam, sst2) sit near ceiling, and single-seed 300-item tests over 4-6 tasks leave the >3-point threshold near the expected effect; the multi-dataset, five-condition pipeline also carries meaningful timeout/implementation risk.

judge_opus.reason: Grounding should help where real inputs are messy or class-imbalanced (sms_spam, emotion) because synthesis then matches real style and class priors. judge_luna.reason: Real examples may help the teacher match input style and distribution, especially for messages and questions. But the pool is small, copying is disallowed, and spec-only synthesis may already capture these short-text genres, making a greater-than-3-point average gain uncertain.

opus.label: close variant

closest_work.difference: Veselovsky et al. drop the labels from real training texts, put those unlabeled texts into the generation prompt ('grounding'), ask the model for new similar examples, and test classifiers trained on the result against real data, with plain spec-style prompting as the baseline. That is the same manipulation and evaluation. It differs in using one task (sarcasm), ChatGPT as the teacher and an E5 encoder as the student, rather than six or seven classification tasks with a Qwen3-4B teacher and a LoRA-adapted Qwen3-0.6B decoder.

Li et al. compare zero-shot generation with few-shot generation, where real examples are given in the prompt, on about ten classification tasks including AG News and SST-2, and evaluate on real test sets. Their in-context examples are labeled rather than unlabeled, and their students are BERT-style models, not a compiled decoder interpreter.

SynthesizRR seeds generation with retrieved real passages and compares it with 32-shot prompting, showing better fidelity and distillation accuracy. It retrieves from a corpus instead of sampling a small pool of unlabeled deployment inputs, and it uses encoder students.
Ding et al. compare GPT-3 generating data with GPT-3 annotating real unlabeled data. This is like the experiment's REAL_LABELED reference, but they do not seed the generator with unlabeled inputs.
The seed paper uses only spec-based synthesis and tests on LLM-generated inputs. The proposal adds real test sets and the grounded condition inside the seed's own pipeline.

opus.reason: The intervention has already been tested. Veselovsky et al. (2305.15041) put unlabeled real texts into the generation prompt, compared this with plain prompting, and found it gave the best real-test performance of the strategies they tried. Li et al. (2310.07849) found that prompting with real examples beats zero-shot generation across several of the same benchmark datasets, though their examples were labeled. What the proposal changes is the setting (spec-first compile-by-training, a Qwen3-0.6B LoRA student, a 4B instruct teacher, and checks for copying and input length), so it is a close variant that tests prior findings in a new regime rather than asking an unanswered question.

closest_work.difference: BARRED uses task descriptions and small unlabeled seed sets to synthesize training data for LoRA-adapted Qwen classifiers, but combines seed-based dimension decomposition with debate and refinement; it does not isolate raw-input prompting against specification-only synthesis.

Compares real-example-guided and zero-shot synthesis using downstream clinical classification, but automatically labels the exemplars, generates class-conditionally, and includes labeled real examples in student training rather than testing unlabeled-input-only grounding.

SynthesizRR studies distributional realism and student accuracy using retrieved documents to ground synthesis, but relies on labeled seed examples and retrieval-based content transformation rather than a handful of raw unlabeled deployment inputs.
The seed supplies the specification-driven compiler and training framework but does not compare specification-only synthesis with synthesis grounded by unlabeled real inputs.

sol.reason: Grounding synthetic training data in real examples is established, including unlabeled seeds in BARRED, so the broad idea is not new. However, the closest studies do not answer the controlled question of whether simply appending raw unlabeled deployment examples improves real-test accuracy without labeling those exemplars, retrieval, or an additional refinement loop. The distinct contribution is that isolated intervention, not the particular Qwen model size or LoRA recipe.
