registration.title: Do compiled functions implement the exception clauses of their specification, and does clause-targeted synthesis fix under-covered clauses at equal example budget?
registration.seed_connection: A compiled program is supposed to implement the whole specification, including exceptions such as 'ignore /abs/ links' in the seed's running example. But the student never reads the spec during training; it only sees teacher examples requested with a generic 'diverse' prompt. If the teacher under-samples an exception clause, the compiled function may silently ignore it. This MVE measures per-clause coverage of the seed's synthesis prompt and tests a one-line fix inside the compiler.
registration.hypothesis: Allocating the same 320-example budget across spec clauses (generic examples plus batches that must exercise each exception clause) raises the compiled 0.6B function's accuracy on exception-clause test items by more than 5 points on average relative to the seed's generic synthesis prompt.
registration.contribution: Instruction-following benchmarks measure whether an LLM obeys verifiable constraints at inference, and AttrPrompt diversifies generated data along generic attributes; neither asks whether a small model compiled from generated examples inherits every clause of its spec, nor evaluates clause-stratified test sets with gold by construction. The clause-coverage view of program-as-weights is new and yields a concrete compiler improvement.

closest_work.difference: IFEval evaluates LLMs' adherence to verifiable instructions at inference time; this MVE evaluates whether a compiled student encodes exception clauses after training on generated data, and intervenes in data synthesis.

AttrPrompt uses generic attributes (length, style) to diversify class-conditional generation; here the conditioning units are the spec's own exception clauses and the outcome is per-clause accuracy with programmatic gold.
PAW's FuzzyBench construction asks teachers for examples that show edge cases but does not measure clause coverage or stratified accuracy of the compiled program.
The seed uses a single generic synthesis prompt and reports only aggregate LEM.

inputs: Teacher: Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (bf16). Student: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (bf16).
No external datasets: five programmatic tasks with clause lists, construct-then-render generators, gold by construction and clause detectors (defined in the method).
Python packages: torch, transformers>=4.51, peft, accelerate. Seed 0 everywhere.
registration.method:
TASKS with spec, clauses (verbatim fragments of the spec), strata, gold, and clause detectors. T1 arxiv_pdf_ids. Spec: 'Extract the arXiv identifiers from every arxiv.org link in the text whose path is /pdf/ (for example https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.02512.pdf gives 2607.02512). Ignore links whose path is /abs/. Strip any version suffix such as v2. Output a JSON array of identifier strings in order of appearance, or [] if there are none.' Clauses: C1 'Ignore links whose path is /abs/.'; C2 'Strip any version suffix such as v2.'; C3 'Output [] if there are none.' Generator: ids = 2-digit year 07-26 + month 01-12 + '.' + 5 digits; links https://arxiv.org/pdf/{id} or .../pdf/{id}.pdf (optionally v1-v3 before .pdf) or https://arxiv.org/abs/{id}; 1-3 links in sentence templates ('See {l} and {l} for details.', 'Papers to read: {l}, {l}.', 'I skimmed {l} yesterday.'). Strata: main (only /pdf/, no versions), exc_abs (>=1 /pdf/ and >=1 /abs/), exc_version (/pdf/ with version), exc_none (only /abs/ or no links; gold []). Gold: ids of /pdf/ links in order, version stripped. Detectors on an input text: C1 contains '/abs/'; C2 contains an id followed by 'v' and a digit; C3 contains no '/pdf/'. Compare: parse prediction as JSON array (fallback split on newlines/commas, strip quotes/brackets), exact list equality. T2 email_extract. Spec: 'Extract every email address that appears in the text, except addresses whose domain is example.com or example.org, which must be ignored. Output a JSON array of the remaining addresses in lower case, in order of appearance, or [] if none remain.' Clauses: C1 'except addresses whose domain is example.com or example.org, which must be ignored'; C2 'in lower case'; C3 'or [] if none remain'. Generator: first.last@domain or first+2digits@domain from name lists and domains (gmail.com, outlook.com, acme-corp.io, uwaterloo.ca, mit.edu, company.co.uk, nordic-labs.se); templates ('Contact {a} or {a} for access.', 'Send the report to {a}.', 'CC: {a}, {a}; BCC: {a}'). Strata: main (1-3 lower-case non-example addresses), exc_example (1-2 valid + 1-2 example-domain), exc_case (>=1 address with upper-case letters), exc_none (only example-domain; gold []). Gold: non-example addresses lower-cased in order. Detectors: C1 contains example.com or example.org; C2 an address containing an upper-case letter; C3 gold is []. T3 log_severity. Spec: 'Classify a single application log line as ERROR, WARN, or INFO using these rules. A line is ERROR if it contains any of the words failed, failure, exception, or timeout. A line is WARN if it contains any of the words slow, retrying, or deprecated. Otherwise it is INFO. Two exceptions override the rules above: a line that mentions a deprecation (the word deprecated) is WARN even if it also contains an ERROR word; and a line containing the phrase retry succeeded is INFO even if it also contains failure words. Output only the label.' Clauses: C1 'a line that mentions a deprecation (the word deprecated) is WARN even if it also contains an ERROR word'; C2 'a line containing the phrase retry succeeded is INFO even if it also contains failure words'. Generator: '{timestamp} {component}: {message}' with pools: main_error ('Request {id} failed with status 500', 'Unhandled exception in worker {n}', 'Timeout while contacting payment service'), main_warn ('Query took 4.2s, slow response from cache', 'Retrying upload of {file} (attempt 2)'), main_info ('User {id} logged in', 'Scheduled job {name} completed in 120ms'), exc_deprecated ('Deprecated endpoint /v1/{name} returned failed status', 'Exception handler for deprecated API {name} invoked'), exc_retry ('Retry succeeded after timeout contacting {service}', 'Upload failed twice, retry succeeded on attempt 3'). Gold: the spec's rule function (whole word, case-insensitive). Detectors: C1 'deprecated' together with an ERROR word; C2 'retry succeeded' together with an ERROR word. Compare: normalized label. T4 date_iso. Spec: 'The text contains exactly one date. Convert it to ISO format YYYY-MM-DD and output only that. The date may be written in words like March 5, 2021 or 5 Mar 2021, or numerically like 03/05/2021, which is always month/day/year (US order). A two-digit year such as 03/05/21 means 2021.' Clauses: C1 'numerically like 03/05/2021, which is always month/day/year (US order)'; C2 'A two-digit year such as 03/05/21 means 2021'. Generator: year 2001-2026, month 1-12, day 1-28; renderings long words, short words, MM/DD/YYYY or M/D/YYYY, MM/DD/YY; templates ('The invoice is due on {d}.', 'We met on {d} to review the plan.', 'Deadline: {d}'). Strata: main_words, exc_numeric (4-digit year, day in 1-12, day != month), exc_two_digit (2-digit year, day in 1-12, day != month). Detectors: C1 a slash date with 4-digit year; C2 a slash date with 2-digit year. Compare exact after strip/quote removal. T5 phone_e164. Spec: 'The text contains exactly one US phone number. Output it in E.164 format: a plus sign, the country code 1, and the 10-digit number, e.g. +15551234567. Input numbers may be written as (555) 123-4567, 555.123.4567, 555-123-4567, or with a leading 1 such as 1-555-123-4567 or +1 555 123 4567. If the number is followed by an extension such as ext. 204 or x204, drop the extension. Output only the normalized number.' Clauses: C1 'with a leading 1 such as 1-555-123-4567 or +1 555 123 4567'; C2 'If the number is followed by an extension such as ext. 204 or x204, drop the extension'. Generator: area code and exchange first digit 2-9; formats '(AAA) EEE-LLLL', 'AAA.EEE.LLLL', 'AAA-EEE-LLLL', 'AAA EEE LLLL'; leading-1 variants '1-AAA-EEE-LLLL', '+1 AAA EEE LLLL', '+1 (AAA) EEE-LLLL'; extensions ' ext. {2-4 digits}' or ' x{digits}'; templates ('Call the front desk at {p} to reschedule.', 'Support line: {p}', 'You can reach Dana at {p}.'). Strata: main, exc_leading1, exc_extension. Detectors: C1 '+1' or a standalone '1' followed by separator and 3 digits before the number; C2 'ext' or 'x' followed by 2-5 digits. Gold '+1' + 10 digits; compare exact.

TEST SETS: 150 items per task, seed 0, strata balanced (T1 40/40/40/30, T2 40/40/40/30, T3 30 per stratum, T4 and T5 50 per stratum). Exception strata are all strata whose name starts with exc_.

SYNTHESIS CONDITIONS (teacher Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507; temperature 0.8, top_p 0.95, max_new_tokens 1024; parse by stripping code fences, first '{' to last '}', json.loads; keep string pairs; dedupe on normalized input; 320 unique pairs per condition, minimum 240). GENERIC (seed prompt verbatim): system = 'You synthesize tiny supervised datasets for finetuning small language models from a natural-language task specification. Return strict JSON with a top-level key 'examples'. Each example must be an object with string keys 'input' and 'output'.'; user = 'Generate 8 diverse (input, output) example pairs that follow this specification.

[SPEC]
{spec}
[END_SPEC]'; 60 calls per task plus up to two extra rounds of 30. TARGETED: the budget of 320 is split evenly over k+1 variants (generic plus one per clause); the clause variants append to the user prompt: '

IMPORTANT: every example in this batch must specifically exercise the following rule from the specification, and every output must apply it correctly: {clause}'. Each variant collects its share (ceil(320/(k+1)) unique pairs, deduplicated across variants), with the same parsing. Record for both conditions the clause-trigger rate (fraction of synthesized inputs on which each clause detector fires).

SCAFFOLD: per task one greedy teacher call (max_new_tokens 400) with the PAW examples-style prompt: 'You are PAW-Compiler. Write a PSEUDO-PROGRAM that helps a smaller model solve a task. The interpreter will NOT see the original SPEC; your pseudo-program is the only instruction it gets. It must contain: 1. a clear, concise description of the task (what to do, edge cases, output format); 2. 3-6 example input/output pairs. Format exactly:
[PSEUDO_PROGRAM]
Task: <one paragraph>
Examples:
Input: <example input 1>
Output: <example output 1>
...
[END_PSEUDO_PROGRAM]
Rules: encode ALL requirements from SPEC; cover typical cases and edge cases; keep total length under 250 tokens; always include the closing marker.

[SPEC]
{spec}
[END_SPEC]'; extract between markers (fallback 'Task: {spec}'), truncate to 250 student tokens at an example boundary; shared by both conditions.

STUDENT PROMPT AND TRAINING (seed recipe, random LoRA init since the PAW mapper warm start needs the hosted API): user message '{pseudo_program}

[INPUT]
{x}
[END_INPUT]' via apply_chat_template(add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=False); target = output + <|im_end|>; loss on target tokens only; LoRA r=64, alpha=16, dropout 0, targets q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj; AdamW lr 2e-4 cosine to 2e-5 over 80 steps, no warmup, weight decay 0, batch 16, bf16, max_length 1024, schedule = concatenated shuffled epochs cut to 80x16, seed 0; fresh base + fresh LoRA per run. Two runs per task (GENERIC, TARGETED).

EVALUATION: greedy, max_new_tokens 96, batch 64; task comparison functions; accuracy overall, per stratum, and acc_exception = mean of the exception strata accuracies. References: TEACHER_ZS (teacher with the LABEL prompt: system = 'You are a function implementation. Apply the specification to the input and reply with only the output, with no explanation.'; user = '[SPEC]
{spec}
[END_SPEC]

[INPUT]
{x}
[END_INPUT]'; greedy) on the test set, and ZERO_SHOT_STUDENT (0.6B with scaffold, no LoRA).

STATISTIC: mean over the five tasks of [acc_exception(TARGETED) - acc_exception(GENERIC)]. Also report the main-stratum change (to detect regressions) and the correlation across (task, clause) pairs between GENERIC clause-trigger rate and GENERIC per-clause accuracy.

ORDER AND TIME GUARD: all teacher work first (scaffolds, GENERIC, TARGETED, teacher zero-shot), free the teacher, then train/evaluate GENERIC and TARGETED per task, then ZERO_SHOT_STUDENT. Stop starting new runs after minute 28; all five tasks must have both conditions.

event.description: Averaged over the five tasks, the student compiled from clause-targeted synthesis is more accurate on exception-clause test items than the student compiled from the seed's generic synthesis by more than 5 percentage points.
event.statistic: mean over tasks of [acc_exception(TARGETED) - acc_exception(GENERIC)], where acc_exception is the mean accuracy over a task's exception strata on the 150-item programmatic test sets

evaluation.procedure: outputs/scores.jsonl: one line per (task, condition) with overall accuracy, per-stratum accuracies, acc_exception, acc_main, n_train_unique; conditions GENERIC, TARGETED, TEACHER_ZS, ZERO_SHOT_STUDENT. outputs/predictions.jsonl: one line per (task, condition, test item) with input, stratum, gold, raw prediction, parsed prediction, correct flag. outputs/synth.jsonl: every synthesized pair with task, condition, prompt variant, and clause-detector flags. outputs/coverage.json: per (task, clause) the trigger rate under GENERIC and TARGETED and the per-clause stratum accuracy under both. outputs/summary.json: per-task exception and main deltas, the registered mean exception delta, a paired bootstrap 90% interval over exception test items, and the coverage-accuracy correlation.
evaluation.controls: GENERIC is the seed's recipe; TARGETED uses the same teacher, total example count, scaffold and training schedule, so only the allocation of the synthesis budget across clauses changes. Main-stratum accuracy is reported for both to detect regressions caused by over-weighting exceptions. TEACHER_ZS bounds attainable exception accuracy (if the teacher itself fails a clause, targeted synthesis cannot fix it) and ZERO_SHOT_STUDENT shows the untrained interpreter's clause behavior.

registration.full_scale_study: A coverage-driven compiler: automatically extract clauses from arbitrary FuzzyBench-Hard specs with the teacher, allocate synthesis across clauses, and generate per-clause held-out tests (unit tests for neural functions), evaluated by LEM overall and per clause with GPT-class teachers; study budget allocation rules and whether clause coverage explains the seed's data-scaling plateau.

agent.reason: If the generic prompt leaves some exception clauses at low coverage (plausible for 'retry succeeded', two-digit years, extensions), forcing clause batches should lift exception-strata accuracy well beyond 5 points; but a 4B instruct teacher often already includes spec-listed edge cases, in which case the gain would be small, and five generator-based tasks add implementation risk.

judge_astra.reason: Targeting clauses should increase exposure to some evaluated exceptions, giving this intervention a credible mechanism. However, generic synthesis already receives every clause explicitly, and targeting can disproportionately produce easy or empty-output cases, so a greater-than-five-point average improvement is a substantial hurdle.

judge_fable.reason: Generic 'diverse' synthesis probably covers each exception clause in only ~10-25% of pairs, so roughly doubling clause coverage (with explicit correctness reminders) at equal budget should lift exception-strata accuracy noticeably, often beyond 5 points, though T3 override rules and shortcut effects from all-[] batches add variance and the run must complete all five tasks.

judge_opus.reason: Targeted synthesis should clearly help where generic coverage is thin, especially the log-severity overrides. However, because the specs state each exception explicitly, generic synthesis probably already covers most clauses at 10-30% rates. Clause batches dominated by [] outputs could also hurt the mixed-link and mixed-email strata. The expected mean exception gain is close to the 5-point bar.

judge_sol.reason: Clause-targeting should increase exception exposure, and the exception-balanced evaluation makes that intervention promising. However, the generic prompt and shared scaffold already communicate the rules, so inadequate coverage is not guaranteed to be the bottleneck.

judge_luna.reason: Targeted synthesis should increase exposure to rare clauses under the same example budget, and the tests directly measure those clauses. The shared scaffold already states the exceptions and generic synthesis may cover some, so a large gain is not certain.

judge_muse.reason: Generic 'diverse' synthesis rarely exercises stated exceptions such as /abs/, example domains or override rules, while targeted batches force coverage at equal budget.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed paper describes generating data from one specification and reports only aggregate LEM, plus sweeps over which teachers are mixed and how much data is used. It never measures how often the synthetic data triggers each clause, never reports accuracy by clause, and never redistributes the synthesis budget across clauses.

PAW builds FuzzyBench with teacher prompts that ask for edge cases and trains an amortized compiler. It does not test whether a compiled program follows each exception clause, and it does not run a controlled comparison of clause-targeted versus generic synthesis at an equal budget.

Prompt2Model also trains a small model on LLM-generated data from a task description, but it evaluates aggregate task metrics. It does not split specifications into clauses, measure how well the data covers each clause, or test clause-conditioned generation on test sets stratified by clause.

AttrPrompt diversifies generated data along generic attributes in order to train classifiers. In this experiment the conditioning units are the specification's own exception clauses, and the outcome is accuracy on each clause, with gold labels known by construction.
IFEval tests whether LLMs obey verifiable constraints at inference time. It does not train a student on synthetic data or change how that data is generated.

opus.reason: I found no paper that asks whether a small model compiled from teacher-generated examples follows each exception clause of its specification, or that compares clause-targeted synthesis with generic synthesis at an equal example budget using clause-stratified, programmatically graded tests. The seed and PAW report only aggregate accuracy, and work like Prompt2Model and AttrPrompt is related but uses different conditioning units and metrics. Two caveats: the general idea of steering synthetic data toward under-covered cases is familiar, and the arXiv search tool returned mostly noise, so a closely related paper may have been missed.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed trains specification-specific adapters using generic synthetic examples and studies teacher mixtures and data scaling, but does not measure exception-clause coverage or compare clause-targeted synthesis at a fixed example budget.

AttrPrompt compares attribute-conditioned and simple synthesis at matched dataset sizes. Its attributes diversify classification inputs; it does not test whether synthesized supervision transfers individual exception clauses into a specification-specific neural function.

Rule distillation studies internalizing textual rules through teacher logits and hidden states, including conditional behavior, but does not intervene on clause coverage in synthetic input generation.

VeriSpecGen decomposes requirements, generates requirement-targeted tests, and uses clause-localized repairs. It evaluates formal specification synthesis and trajectory training, not exception accuracy of compiled functions under generic versus clause-balanced supervision.

Dual-view retrieval training uses targeted synthetic instruction supervision at matched data budgets, but changes inference-time instructions through polarity reversal rather than allocating examples across clauses of one fixed function specification.

sol.reason: Prior work establishes attribute-guided synthesis, rule internalization, and requirement-targeted testing, so those ingredients are not individually new. However, none of the work I found answers whether generic synthesis under-covers a compiled function's exception clauses and whether explicitly allocating the same example budget across those clauses improves clause-stratified accuracy. The registered experiment therefore asks a distinct question, rather than merely changing models or metrics in an already reported comparison.

opus.reason: Both test whether synthesis prompts that explicitly target edge cases or exceptions (such as /abs/ distractors) beat the generic 'diverse' prompt at a fixed example budget, scored by stratum-specific accuracy on edge-case test strata.

sol.reason: Both compare generic synthesis with targeted edge-case synthesis at a controlled example and training budget, measuring oracle-scored accuracy separately across held-out input strata.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I built: tasks.py has the five programmatic tasks with their specs, clauses, strata, construct-then-render generators, gold by construction, clause detectors and comparison functions. run.py runs the whole pipeline in the registered order: teacher work first (scaffolds, GENERIC and TARGETED synthesis, TEACHER_ZS), then GENERIC and TARGETED LoRA training and evaluation for each task, then ZERO_SHOT_STUDENT, with the 28-minute time guard. Both models run under HF transformers. Settings follow the registration: LoRA r64 / alpha16, 80 steps at batch 16, cosine learning rate from 2e-4 to 2e-5, random init, greedy evaluation. run.sh installs transformers, peft and accelerate, then runs run.py. It writes result.json, the five registered outputs, and also outputs/scaffolds.json and run_log.txt.

Result of my test run of this same command (the run took about 14 min plus install): statistic = 0.0333, so the event (> 0.05) did NOT occur in this run. The 90% paired bootstrap interval over exception items is [0.013, 0.053].
- Per-task exception deltas: arxiv -0.022, email -0.011, log_severity +0.20, date 0, phone 0.
- The mean main-stratum delta is -0.033; email main drops by 0.15.
- The correlation between GENERIC trigger rate and per-clause accuracy over 12 (task, clause) pairs is Pearson 0.31 / Spearman 0.41.
- The one large gain is log_severity C1 ('deprecated' with an ERROR word). Its GENERIC trigger rate was 0.0 and TARGETED was 0.13; accuracy went from 0.6 to 1.0.
- Email C2 (lower case): the 4B teacher produced no upper-case addresses under either prompt (trigger rate 0.0 for both). Both students score 0.0 on that stratum, so targeting could not help.
- Teacher sampling is not bit-deterministic, so a fresh run may give a somewhat different value.

Deviations, each the smallest I could find, applied identically to both conditions:
1. Parsing: for arxiv and email the 4B teacher writes "output" as a JSON array, not a string. Read strictly, "keep string pairs" would have given 0 pairs. I serialize list or dict outputs with json.dumps; non-string scalars are still dropped.
2. Phone task: the teacher mostly repeats the spec's own examples, so deduplication left only 59 unique GENERIC pairs after the registered rounds (60 calls plus 2×30), against 186 for TARGETED. This is below the 240 minimum. To keep the equal-budget control, if a task's two conditions end with different unique counts I trim the larger to the smaller: TARGETED evenly across its variants, GENERIC from the tail. This triggered only for phone (both trained on 59 pairs). Trimmed rows are flagged in synth.jsonl, and summary.json marks the below-minimum case.
3. TARGETED per-variant quota: ceil(320/(k+1)), with the generic variant absorbing the rounding so the total is exactly 320 (106/107/107 for k=2).
4. Sampling: top_k is disabled (top_k=0) so that only the registered temperature 0.8 and top_p 0.95 apply; the model's default would be top_k=20. Greedy is used for the scaffold, TEACHER_ZS and evaluation.
5. Generators: the registered templates have fixed slot counts, but the registration asks for 1–3 links or addresses. I fill each template with a joined list of links or addresses, which keeps the registered sentence frames.
6. Random LoRA init, as the registration already specifies.

Training data are the unique pairs used, with trigger rates computed on them. TEACHER_ZS uses max_new_tokens 96.

departures: run.py parse_pairs: for the list tasks, teacher 'output' fields that are JSON arrays or dicts are serialized with json.dumps instead of being dropped. A strict reading of 'keep string pairs' would leave arxiv and email with zero pairs, so this is needed for the run to happen. It applies to both conditions and does not bias the comparison.

run.py run_synthesis, phone_e164: GENERIC reached only 59 unique pairs, below the registered minimum of 240. The registration gives no rule for this case. The engineer trimmed TARGETED from 186 to 59 so both conditions train on 59 pairs. This changes the TARGETED arm for phone. Both arms score 1.0 on phone exception strata, so it very likely did not change the value.

run.py generate_texts: sampling uses top_k=0, disabling the model's default top_k=20. The registration names only temperature 0.8 and top_p 0.95, so this is an open choice, applied identically to both conditions. It may widen sampling and affect diversity and duplicate rates, with an unknown direction.
run.py run_synthesis: the TARGETED quota is ceil(320/(k+1)) and the generic variant absorbs the rounding (106/107/107), so the total is exactly 320 rather than 321. Negligible effect.

run.py calls_for: TARGETED calls per variant are ceil(60/(k+1)) in the first round and ceil(30/(k+1)) in extra rounds. The registration does not specify TARGETED call counts. Open choice, with minor effect.

run.py norm_input: the 'normalized input' used for deduplication lowercases text. The registration leaves normalization open. However, this collapses inputs that differ only in case, which is exactly the distinction email C2 ('in lower case') is about. Upper-case variants of an earlier lower-case input would be discarded as duplicates. This could contribute to email C2's 0.0 trigger rate in both conditions. The effect is unverified and email's exception delta is small either way.

tasks.py generators: the fixed-slot templates are filled with joined lists of 1-3 links or addresses, and arxiv exc_none items with no links use extra no-link sentences that were not registered. This is needed to meet the registered 1-3 count. It applies to the test set only, equally for both arms, so no bias.
run.py: TEACHER_ZS uses max_new_tokens 96, which the registration does not specify. Reference only, with no effect on the statistic.
Single synthesis and training run per condition, as registered. The bootstrap CI covers only test-item resampling, not synthesis or training variance.
problems: outputs/scores.jsonl, coverage.json: three of five tasks sit at or near ceiling under GENERIC. Date and phone exception accuracy is 1.0 for both arms and arxiv is about 0.96, so they cannot show a gain. The registered mean is effectively decided by one clause: log_severity exc_deprecated, 30 items, 0.6 to 1.0. That makes this a weak test of the hypothesis.

Email C2 has a 0.0 trigger rate even under the TARGETED prompt, and both trained students score 0.0 on exc_case. The intervention never delivered the targeted clause there. Case-folding deduplication in run.py norm_input may have contributed, which is unverified.

phone_e164 trained on only 59 pairs per arm, well below the registered minimum of 240. Teacher outputs are dominated by the spec's own 555-123-4567 example. summary.json flags this, but that task's comparison does not reflect the registered budget.

summary.json: the 90% interval [0.013, 0.053] reflects test-item variance only. With one synthesis and training seed, the gap between 0.033 and the 0.05 threshold is not robustly resolved, even though full_log.txt from the engineer's earlier run reproduced the same numbers.
outputs/summary.json: the email main-stratum drop (0.725 to 0.575) indicates a possible regression from reallocating the budget. It comes from a single run.
opus.reason: The code implements the registered pipeline closely: tasks, strata, the seed and targeted prompts, the shared scaffold, the LoRA recipe, the statistic and the event. The deviations are either needed to run at all (serializing list outputs), open choices (top_k, quota rounding, dedup normalization), or did not plausibly move the value (the phone trimming, where both arms are at 1.0). The reported 0.0333 follows correctly from real per-item predictions: (-0.022 - 0.011 + 0.2 + 0 + 0) / 5. The event, a gain above 5 points, did not occur. The evidence is weak, however. Most tasks are at ceiling, the mean hinges on one 30-item clause, targeting failed to produce coverage for email C2, and phone ran far below the minimum budget. With a single seed, this is a valid but only modestly informative mixed result: targeting helps when a clause is under-covered and the teacher can generate it, and does nothing otherwise.

departures: run.py, parse_pairs: outputs that are JSON lists or dictionaries are serialized into strings instead of being rejected by the registered 'keep string pairs' rule. This changes the eligible training data and could change the result. Serializing lists is a reasonable run-enabling repair for the list-valued tasks; accepting dictionaries is a broader relaxation.

run.py and outputs/scores.jsonl: phone_e164 uses only 59 unique examples per condition, rather than 320 or the registered minimum of 240. This materially changes the experiment's data budget and could change the five-task mean.

run.py, run_synthesis: an unregistered post-synthesis equalization rule trims the larger dataset to the smaller dataset. It actually reduced phone TARGETED from 186 examples to 59, removing examples across its variants. Equal counts are preserved, but this changes the intervention and could change its measured effect.

run.py, run_synthesis: inputs are entered into the cross-variant deduplication set even when their examples are rejected because a variant's quota is already full. Thus an unused candidate can prevent admission of an example in a later variant. This unregistered exclusion rule could change the retained data, clause allocation, and achievable sample counts.

run.py: for tasks with two clauses, TARGETED allocates 106 examples to the generic variant and 107 to each clause variant, rather than applying the literal ceiling quota of 107 to every variant. This can change the retained examples, but reasonably resolves the registration's conflict between ceiling quotas and an exact total of 320.

tasks.py: fixed-slot link and email templates are rewritten to accept joined lists. This changes test-item wording and could change accuracy, although some adaptation is needed to accommodate the registered 1–3-item cardinalities.

tasks.py, _addr: numeric email local parts are rendered as firstNN, without a literal plus sign. If the registered 'first+2digits' notation intended plus-addressing, that input family was omitted and the test distribution changed. The notation is ambiguous, so this is not a definite protocol violation, but it could affect extraction accuracy.

tasks.py, comparison helpers: phone comparison removes quotation marks, backticks, and code fences rather than performing the registered exact comparison; date comparison additionally removes code fences and backticks beyond the specified stripping/quote removal. JSON-list elements are also coerced to stripped strings. These relaxations could change correctness flags; the supplied excerpts do not establish how often they affected the primary scores.

run.py: TEACHER_ZS is evaluated with batch size 256 rather than the registered evaluation batch size of 64. This could affect that reference through numerical or padding-dependent generation differences, but it does not feed into the reported GENERIC-versus-TARGETED statistic.

run.py and tasks.py: random streams use task-name-derived seeds and batch, round, and epoch offsets from seed 0, rather than literal seed-0 initialization throughout. These choices can affect exact examples and training orders, but reproducible substreams derived from the registered master seed are plausibly an implementation choice left open by the registration.

run.py, summary: reported Spearman correlation uses double argsort rather than average ranks for ties. The coverage and accuracy arrays contain ties, so the reported Spearman value is not correctly calculated. This changes an auxiliary result, not the registered event statistic.

run.py: if the time guard leaves tasks unfinished, the code computes a mean and event flag over completed tasks rather than requiring all five paired conditions; ZERO_SHOT_STUDENT may also start after minute 28. These differ from the registered completion requirement and stop rule, but neither affected this run, which completed all conditions before the guard.
problems: The phone comparison is not the registered 320-example experiment: both conditions are below the minimum, and TARGETED data were discarded under a newly introduced rule.

outputs/scaffolds.json contains incorrect email examples. One omits team@company.org even though that domain is allowed; another omits admin@org.example.org even though only the exact domains example.com and example.org are excluded. The scaffold is shared, so this is not treatment leakage, but it compromises interpretation of the email failures.

The visible used examples in outputs/synth.jsonl include incorrect arXiv targets that collapse repeated identifiers instead of preserving every occurrence. Trigger rates therefore measure input coverage, not coverage with correct supervision; no condition-wise label-quality assessment is supplied.

outputs/coverage.json shows that the targeting prompt did not reliably produce clause-exercising inputs: email uppercase coverage remains zero, and several arXiv coverage rates barely change. The experiment tests this prompt-based allocation procedure, not guaranteed successful clause coverage.
run.py reports an incorrect tie-handling implementation of Spearman correlation.

The bootstrap interval resamples test items conditional on these fitted models and fixed tasks. It does not quantify synthesis, training-seed, or task-selection uncertainty, and the experiment has only one registered repetition.

The average benefit is concentrated in log_severity; date and phone exception accuracy are already at ceiling. Main accuracy falls by 3.3 percentage points on average, including a 15-point email decline, limiting the case for a general compiler improvement.
TEACHER_ZS is a useful reference, not an upper bound on attainable student accuracy. The date results themselves show students outperforming that reference.
sol.reason: The protected run completed and produced a mean exception gain of 0.03333, so the registered greater-than-0.05 event did not occur. Fidelity is unfaithful because the phone task violated the registered minimum and its TARGETED dataset was reduced using an unregistered rule that could change the reported value. The primary value is nevertheless supported by real model execution and consistent score arithmetic, with no evident leakage or hard-coded result; the auxiliary Spearman error does not reverse the event conclusion. The 90% item-bootstrap interval, approximately [0.0128, 0.0534], does not establish that the underlying gain is below five points or that targeting has no benefit. The localized log-clause repair and persistent email-case failure provide meaningful, limited evidence, but noisy supervision, regressions, ceiling effects, and missing run-level replication prevent a stronger general conclusion.

departures: run.py parse_pairs serializes list/dict teacher outputs with json.dumps instead of dropping non-string outputs as the registered 'keep string pairs' rule requires. Needed for arxiv/email to yield any pairs (teacher emitted JSON arrays). Applied to both conditions; it enables the registered comparison rather than changing it differentially.

run.py equal-budget trim (unregistered failed-case rule): phone GENERIC yielded 59 unique pairs (<240 minimum, <320 budget) and TARGETED was cut from 186 to 59. Did not change this run's exception delta (both phone exception accuracies are 1.0, so the task contributes 0 either way). Could change main-stratum accuracy and the trained set.

run.py sets top_k=0 during synthesis. Registration specifies temperature 0.8 and top_p 0.95 only, so top_k is unspecified; this disables the library default top_k=20 and could change which examples are synthesized relative to that default.

tasks.py generators join 1–3 links/addresses into the registered fixed-slot sentence frames (email CC/BCC rendering also differs from the three-slot template). Resolves an inconsistency in the registration. Shared test set, so the contrast stays fair, but absolute accuracies could differ from a strict fixed-slot generator.

Call budget is split across variants (about 60 calls per task, not per variant); quotas were still filled except phone.

problems: Phone trained on 59 pairs, below the registered minimum of 240, after an unregistered trim (run.py, outputs/summary.json, outputs/scores.jsonl). Flagged, and it does not move the exception statistic because both conditions are at 1.0 on phone exceptions.

Both students score 0.0 there, below ZERO_SHOT_STUDENT 0.525 and TEACHER_ZS 0.775 (outputs/scores.jsonl). Targeting cannot fix a clause the teacher will not generate.

Mean main-stratum accuracy fell by 0.033 (outputs/summary.json), so the intervention is not free of regressions on non-exception items.

Departures are either required for list-valued tasks to yield pairs, open decoding choices, or the phone shortfall, which does not move the exception statistic because both phone conditions are already perfect. That is a credible, mechanism-supported null, not a definitive precision result, because the item-bootstrap interval crosses 0.05 and synthesis variance is unmeasured.

grok.what_it_asks: Whether splitting a fixed synthesis budget so some batches must exercise each exception clause raises a compiled 0.6B function's accuracy on exception items relative to the paper's generic diverse-example prompt.

in_the_paper.reason: The paper reports only aggregate LEM for its generic synthesis recipe and names teacher-error checks and user studies as unfinished, not clause-targeted synthesis or per-clause accuracy.

opus.what_it_asks: Does a 0.6B student compiled from teacher examples whose synthesis budget is split across the specification's exception clauses handle exception-clause inputs more accurately than one compiled from the paper's single generic 'diverse examples' prompt at the same example count, on programmatic tasks with gold labels by construction?

in_the_paper.reason: The paper uses one generic synthesis template and reports only aggregate LEM; its limitations mention inherited teacher errors but never per-clause coverage or targeted synthesis.

relation.reason: The paper's synthesis prompt and LoRA compile recipe are working parts of the experiment, and the synthesis step is changed in a way the paper does not try, so the paper's claims stand either way.

obvious.reason: Covering edge cases in synthetic data is a common worry, and targeting synthesis at the spec's own clauses is a natural fix, but only a minority would write down this exact equal-budget comparison among their first ten follow-ups.

misreads_paper.reason: The plan's checkable statements (one generic synthesis template, aggregate LEM only, a scaffold encoding the spec) match the paper's text, and 'the student never reads the spec' refers to the original spec, which the scaffold design keeps from the interpreter.

The per-task deltas were arxiv −0.022, email −0.011, log +0.20 (deprecated stratum 0.6→1.0), date 0 and phone 0, and the mean main-stratum change was −0.033, with email main falling by 0.15.

in_the_paper.reason: The paper compares teacher mixtures and data quantities but neither measures clause-targeted synthesis nor explicitly leaves that comparison as an open question.

relation.reason: The experiment changes the paper’s synthesis procedure to test a compiler improvement that the paper does not claim or evaluate.

who_would_care.reason: A decisive answer would inform synthetic-supervision choices across specification-driven task distillation methods, rather than only this PAW implementation.

sol.what_came_out: In one seeded run using Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 supervision and Qwen3-0.6B students on five 150-item programmatic test sets containing 480 exception items, targeted synthesis achieved 89.22% mean exception accuracy versus 85.89% for generic synthesis, a gain of 3.33 percentage points with a paired item-bootstrap 90% interval of 1.28 to 5.34 points.

prerequisite.reason: Both training conditions sharply reduced training loss and improved exception accuracy over the zero-shot student on every task, establishing basic task learning.

evidence.reason: The exception-accuracy interval excludes zero and supports the claimed direction, although it measures item uncertainty for one synthesis-and-training run and the reported main-stratum losses lack uncertainty estimates.

next_step.reason: The positive average is driven by one log-severity clause, so its robustness to independently generated training data must be established before committing to a much larger study.
next_step.what: Repeat the equal-budget comparison with independent synthesis and training seeds, checking whether the log-severity gain and average exception improvement persist.

registration.title: Is the natural-language scaffold still load-bearing after compile by training? Dropping the pseudo-program from a compiled 0.6B function
registration.seed_connection: A compiled .paw program is a LoRA adapter plus a run-time scaffold (the pseudo-program prompt with task description and examples) that is prepended to every input, costing roughly 250 prefill tokens per call on the local interpreter. PAW found the discrete pseudo-program adds 5-40 points for its amortized compiler. After 100 steps of gradient training on thousands of examples, the adapter may have internalized the function, making the scaffold dead weight, or the scaffold may still carry the rule text needed to generalize from synthetic training inputs to real ones.
registration.hypothesis: A function compiled and executed without any task text in the prompt (bare input only) is at most 2 points less accurate on real inputs than the same function compiled and executed with the seed's pseudo-program scaffold.
registration.contribution: PAW decomposed discrete and continuous components only for its amortized prefix-tuning compiler on image tasks, and Webson and Pavlick showed prompt semantics matter little during fine-tuning for NLI with large models; this MVE tests, for gradient-compiled 0.6B functions on real out-of-distribution inputs, whether the scaffold can be removed entirely (and whether it can be removed without recompiling), with a direct prefill-token and latency accounting that bears on on-device deployment.

closest_work.difference: PAW's component decomposition (discrete pseudo only vs continuous only vs both) concerns compiler-generated prefix caches on image tasks; here the continuous part is gradient-trained LoRA from teacher examples and the test inputs are real text.

Webson and Pavlick vary prompt wording during few-shot fine-tuning of large models on NLI; this MVE removes the task text entirely for a 0.6B interpreter compiled from synthetic data and adds a train-with/evaluate-without mismatch condition and latency measurement.
T-Few compares PEFT with in-context learning on cost and accuracy but keeps the prompt template during PEFT; it does not ask whether the template can be dropped after adaptation.
The seed always packages and uses the scaffold and never ablates it.

inputs: Teacher: Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (bf16). Student: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (bf16).

Public classification datasets (HF datasets, no trust_remote_code), first six that load, minimum five, priority order: stanfordnlp/sst2 (field 'sentence'; test pool = validation), fancyzhx/ag_news ('text'; test), dair-ai/emotion config 'split' ('text'; test), CogComp/trec ('text', coarse_label; test), ucirvine/sms_spam ('sms'; single split, carve test with seed 0), SetFit/subj ('text', label_text; test), cornell-movie-review-data/rotten_tomatoes ('text'; test), takala/financial_phrasebank config 'sentences_allagree' ('sentence'; single split). Label names read from ClassLabel names/label_text and mapped to the spec's words.
Python packages: torch, transformers>=4.51, peft, datasets, accelerate. Seed 0 everywhere.
registration.method:
SPECS: sst2/rotten_tomatoes: 'Classify the sentiment of a short movie-review sentence. Output exactly one word: positive or negative.' ag_news: 'Classify a short news article (headline and opening sentences) into exactly one topic: World, Sports, Business, or Sci/Tech. Output only the topic name.' emotion: 'Classify the main emotion expressed in a short social-media style message. Output exactly one word from: sadness, joy, love, anger, fear, surprise.' trec: 'Classify an English question by the type of answer it expects. Output exactly one of these codes: ABBR (abbreviation or its expansion), ENTY (an entity such as an animal, color, product, event, or term), DESC (a description, definition, reason, or manner), HUM (a person, group, or organization), LOC (a location), NUM (a number, date, count, distance, or other numeric value).' sms_spam: 'Decide whether an SMS text message is unsolicited spam or a normal personal message. Output exactly one word: spam or ham.' subj: 'Decide whether a sentence from a movie review or plot summary is subjective (expresses an opinion or feeling) or objective (states a fact or describes plot). Output exactly one word: subjective or objective.' financial_phrasebank: 'Classify the sentiment of a sentence from financial news from an investor's point of view. Output exactly one word: positive, negative, or neutral.' TEST = 300 items per task sampled with seed 0 from the test pool.

SYNTHESIS (once per task, shared by all conditions; seed prompt verbatim): system = 'You synthesize tiny supervised datasets for finetuning small language models from a natural-language task specification. Return strict JSON with a top-level key 'examples'. Each example must be an object with string keys 'input' and 'output'.'; user = 'Generate 8 diverse (input, output) example pairs that follow this specification.

[SPEC]
{spec}
[END_SPEC]'. Teacher Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, temperature 0.8, top_p 0.95, max_new_tokens 1024, 60 calls per task plus up to two extra rounds of 30; parse (strip code fences, first '{' to last '}', json.loads), keep string pairs whose normalized output is a valid label of the task, dedupe on normalized input, keep 320 unique pairs (minimum 240).

SCAFFOLD: per task one greedy teacher call (max_new_tokens 400) with the PAW examples-style prompt: 'You are PAW-Compiler. Write a PSEUDO-PROGRAM that helps a smaller model solve a task. The interpreter will NOT see the original SPEC; your pseudo-program is the only instruction it gets. It must contain: 1. a clear, concise description of the task (what to do, edge cases, output format); 2. 3-6 example input/output pairs. Format exactly:
[PSEUDO_PROGRAM]
Task: <one paragraph>
Examples:
Input: <example input 1>
Output: <example output 1>
...
[END_PSEUDO_PROGRAM]
Rules: encode ALL requirements from SPEC; cover typical cases and edge cases; keep total length under 250 tokens; always include the closing marker.

[SPEC]
{spec}
[END_SPEC]'; extract between markers (fallback 'Task: {spec}'); truncate to 250 student tokens at an example boundary. Record its token length.

PROMPT VARIANTS for the student (both rendered with tokenizer.apply_chat_template(add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=False); training target = label + <|im_end|>, loss on target tokens only): FULL = user message '{pseudo_program}

[INPUT]
{x}
[END_INPUT]' (the seed's render_prompt_template); BARE = user message '[INPUT]
{x}
[END_INPUT]' with no task text at all (the seed's template for an empty pseudo-program).

CONDITIONS per task: (1) FULL: train with FULL, evaluate with FULL (seed design). (2) BARE: train with BARE, evaluate with BARE. (3) MISMATCH: the FULL-trained adapter evaluated with BARE prompts (no extra training; tests dropping the scaffold without recompiling). (4) ZERO_SHOT_FULL: base 0.6B with the FULL prompt, no LoRA. (5) ZERO_SHOT_BARE: base 0.6B with the BARE prompt, no LoRA (sanity floor). (6) TEACHER_ZS: teacher with the LABEL prompt (system = 'You are a function implementation. Apply the specification to the input and reply with only the output, with no explanation.'; user = '[SPEC]
{spec}
[END_SPEC]

[INPUT]
{x}
[END_INPUT]'; greedy) on TEST.

TRAINING (seed recipe, random LoRA init since the PAW mapper warm start needs the hosted API): LoRA r=64, alpha=16, dropout 0, targets q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj; AdamW lr 2e-4 cosine to 2e-5 over 80 steps, no warmup, weight decay 0, batch 16, bf16, max_length 1024, schedule = concatenated shuffled epochs over the 320 pairs cut to 80x16 presentations with the identical example order for FULL and BARE, seed 0; fresh base + fresh LoRA per run. Two training runs per task.

EVALUATION: greedy, max_new_tokens 16, batch 64; normalize prediction and gold identically (first line, strip, drop quotes/periods, lowercase, remove non-alphanumerics); accuracy on TEST. Also report the training loss curves and the fraction of predictions that are not a valid label (format failures) per condition.

LATENCY ACCOUNTING: for each task, mean prompt token count under FULL and BARE over TEST, and wall-clock per call for 50 single-item greedy calls (batch 1, max_new_tokens 8, after 5 warm-up calls) with the FULL-trained adapter under FULL prompts and the BARE-trained adapter under BARE prompts on the A100 (reported as a relative saving; absolute numbers are not representative of consumer hardware).

STATISTIC: mean over tasks of [accuracy(BARE) - accuracy(FULL)]. Secondary: mean over tasks of [accuracy(MISMATCH) - accuracy(FULL)].

ORDER AND TIME GUARD: all teacher work first (scaffolds, synthesis, TEACHER_ZS), free the teacher, then per task in priority order train FULL (evaluate FULL and MISMATCH), train BARE (evaluate BARE), then zero-shot references and latency. Stop starting new tasks after minute 27; at least four tasks required.

event.description: Averaged over tasks, the function compiled and run without any scaffold (BARE) is within 2 percentage points of, or better than, the function compiled and run with the pseudo-program scaffold (FULL) on real test inputs.
event.statistic: mean over tasks of [accuracy(BARE) - accuracy(FULL)] on the 300-item real test sets

evaluation.procedure: outputs/scores.jsonl: one line per (task, condition) with accuracy, format-failure rate, n_test, n_train_unique, mean prompt tokens, and per-call latency where measured; conditions FULL, BARE, MISMATCH, ZERO_SHOT_FULL, ZERO_SHOT_BARE, TEACHER_ZS. outputs/predictions.jsonl: one line per (task, condition, test item) with input, gold, raw and normalized prediction, correct flag. outputs/synth.jsonl: the synthesized pairs per task and the scaffold text with its token length. outputs/summary.json: per-task BARE-FULL and MISMATCH-FULL differences, the registered mean BARE-FULL difference, a paired bootstrap 90% interval over test items, mean prefill-token saving and relative latency saving, and training-loss curves.
evaluation.controls: FULL is the seed's design; BARE uses the identical synthesized pairs, example order, LoRA configuration and schedule, so only the presence of task text in the prompt differs. MISMATCH separates 'the adapter encodes the task' from 'the adapter was trained to rely on the scaffold'. ZERO_SHOT_BARE confirms that the bare prompt is uninformative without the adapter, and ZERO_SHOT_FULL shows what the scaffold alone buys; TEACHER_ZS gives the ceiling.

registration.full_scale_study: A scaffold-free .paw variant evaluated on FuzzyBench-Hard by LEM across task families (short labels vs long structured outputs, where PAW found the scaffold crowds the context), with latency and energy measurements on consumer hardware via the quantized llama.cpp runtime, intermediate designs (paraphrase-only scaffold, examples-only scaffold), and a study of when the scaffold is needed for generalization from synthetic to real inputs as training data shrinks.

agent.reason: A rank-64 LoRA on all modules trained for 1280 presentations of 320 labeled examples should internalize a 2-6-way classification without instruction text, and prior work finds prompt semantics matter little once gradient training has enough examples; the main threat is OOD generalization to real inputs and code-like labels (TREC), where the scaffold's explanation may still be worth a few points.

judge_astra.reason: For these fixed-label tasks, a separate rank-64 adapter receiving 1,280 training presentations can plausibly learn the function without repeating its instructions, especially when trained from the outset with bare prompts. This predicts the registered point-estimate event, not successful inference-only scaffold removal or statistically established non-inferiority.

judge_fable.reason: Null-prompt fine-tuning literature suggests the scaffold matters little once ~300 labeled examples drive LoRA training on short-label classification, but the synthetic-train/real-test shift, arbitrary TREC codes and only 80 steps from a random LoRA init plausibly leave FULL ahead by roughly 1-3 points, so the -2 threshold is close to a coin flip before discounting for run failures.

judge_opus.reason: With 320 examples, meaningful label words and short-label classification, gradient-trained adapters probably internalize the task, so dropping the scaffold should cost about 0-2 points on average. Two things could push the gap past 2 points: the light LoRA budget (alpha/r = 0.25, 80 steps, random init) favours the instructed starting point, and trec's codes are hard to infer from examples alone.

judge_sol.reason: Matched BARE training can plausibly internalize these fixed classification functions, making a difference better than minus two points achievable. The small student, limited synthetic training, and real-input distribution shift still create substantial risk that FULL benefits from explicit task definitions.

judge_luna.reason: A task-specific adapter may learn the mapping from the labeled examples without task text, but BARE removes both the instructions and scaffold examples that could support generalization. The strict 2-point tolerance makes non-inferiority uncertain.

judge_muse.reason: Single-task LoRA finetuning typically internalizes the fixed label mapping, making the 250-token task text redundant. Format learning and arbitrary TREC codes are the main risks, but a >2pp average deficit is unlikely.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Logan et al. show that fine-tuning with 'null prompts' (no task template and no examples) comes close to the accuracy of hand-tuned prompts. Their setting is few-shot fine-tuning of masked LMs on real labelled data. They do not train a 0.6B chat decoder on teacher-synthesised data and test on real inputs, they do not use a compiler-generated pseudo-program scaffold, and they have no train-with/evaluate-without (MISMATCH) condition.

PromptIntern also aims to move a recurring prompt into the weights during fine-tuning to save inference tokens. It does this with progressive template compression and absorption of few-shot examples on NL2Code, using real training data. It does not test whether a scaffold-free adapter trained on synthetic data matches the scaffolded one on real classification inputs.

Webson and Pavlick vary prompt semantics, including irrelevant or null templates, during few-shot fine-tuning for NLI with large models. They do not remove the task text entirely for a small interpreter trained on synthetic data, and they report no latency or prefill accounting.
PAW splits the discrete pseudo-program from the continuous adapter only for its amortized compiler, not for adapters trained by gradient descent on teacher-generated pairs.
The seed always packages and uses the scaffold and never ablates it.

opus.reason: Earlier work suggests prompts matter less after fine-tuning: null prompts (Logan et al.), prompt-semantics insensitivity (Webson and Pavlick), and prompt internalisation (PromptIntern). But all of it trains on real labelled data. None of it tests whether a 0.6B adapter trained on teacher-synthesised data still needs a natural-language scaffold to generalise to real inputs, or whether a scaffold-trained adapter survives losing its scaffold. That literature makes the outcome easier to anticipate, but I found no paper that answers this question, so it is not settled.

sol.label: close variant

closest_work.difference: PromptIntern compares direct fine-tuning with instructions and examples against query-only fine-tuning, tests full-prompt training followed by query-only inference in Appendix A.4, and reports token counts and latency. The proposed experiment changes the models, tasks, supervision source, and non-inferiority threshold.

Generative Prompt Internalization trains prompt-specific QLoRA adapters on synthetic examples and evaluates without the fixed prompt, including SFT-only and train-with-prompt/test-without-prompt baselines. It studies 8B agent applications rather than 0.6B text classifiers and also introduces an auxiliary prompt-generation objective.
The seed packages gradient-trained LoRA adapters with runtime scaffolds but does not compare scaffold-present, scaffold-free, and inference-only removal conditions.

sol.reason: PromptIntern already reports the central scaffold-present versus scaffold-free fine-tuning comparison, the inference-only removal control, and efficiency accounting; Generative Prompt Internalization additionally covers synthetic supervision and prompt-specific adapters. The proposed study is therefore a close variant in a smaller-model classification setting, rather than a new experimental question or intervention. Neither paper establishes the proposed two-percentage-point threshold for this particular setting.

opus.reason: Both train adapters with the scaffold and with a bare input-only template, and evaluate under both prompts, including the cross condition of a scaffold-trained adapter run bare. Both measure accuracy alongside prompt-token and latency savings.

sol.reason: Both vary whether task text is present during training and execution, including scaffold removal after scaffold-based training, and measure correctness alongside prompt-token and latency savings.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I built: run_experiment.py, called by run_eval.sh. It runs the registered MVE end to end on one A100 in about 10 minutes. I ran the submitted command once on a clean outputs directory and it reproduced my development run exactly (statistic 0.00444).

How it follows the registration:
- Teacher is Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 and student is Qwen3-0.6B, both in bf16.
- Synthesis uses the seed paper's prompt verbatim: 60 calls per task, temperature 0.8, top_p 0.95. Pairs are filtered to valid labels and deduplicated on the normalized input, and 320 unique pairs are kept. Every task reached 320 in round 0, so the extra rounds were never needed.
- Each task gets one greedy PAW-style pseudo-program (scaffold). Scaffolds came out between 160 and 210 student tokens, with no truncation and no fallback.
- FULL and BARE prompts are rendered as in the seed's render_prompt_template. The loss is on label+<|im_end|> only.
- LoRA uses r=64, alpha=16, all 7 projections, random init. Training is 80 steps at batch 16, cosine learning rate from 2e-4 to 2e-5, with the same example order for FULL and BARE, seed 0, and a fresh base model for every run.
- All six conditions are run. Evaluation is greedy with 16 new tokens, uses the registered normalization, and reports the format-failure rate. A paired bootstrap gives a 90% interval over test items.

Deviations, kept as small as possible:
1. CogComp/trec and takala/financial_phrasebank failed to load because they are script datasets, which the current `datasets` library no longer supports. As the registration's "first six that load" rule specifies, the tasks are sst2 (validation pool), ag_news, emotion, sms_spam, subj and rotten_tomatoes.
2. For sms_spam, which has a single split, the test pool is a seed-0 shuffled 20% carve-out, and 300 items are sampled from it.
3. Latency for each adapter is measured right after its training run rather than in a final block. The measurement itself is the same: 5 warm-up calls, then 50 batch-1 calls with 8 new tokens.
4. All teacher-side work happens before the teacher is freed: scaffolds, synthesis, then TEACHER_ZS.
The time guard (27 minutes) never triggered.

Results from the test run:
- **Registered statistic:** mean BARE−FULL = +0.0044. The paired-bootstrap 90% interval is [−0.011, +0.021], so by the registered threshold (−0.02) the event occurred. Since the interval reaches only −0.011, the data look inconsistent with an average loss of more than about 1 point, but this is one seed and six tasks.
- **Per task, BARE−FULL:** sst2 +0.013, ag_news +0.123, emotion 0, sms_spam 0, subj −0.083, rotten_tomatoes −0.027.
  - The average hides real differences between tasks: the scaffold helped on subj and rotten_tomatoes and hurt on ag_news.
  - Part of the ag_news gap comes from FULL's 1.3% format failures, such as outputting "BoxingScene"; BARE had none.
- **Mean accuracy by condition:**

| Condition | Mean accuracy |
|---|---|
| FULL | 0.755 |
| BARE | 0.759 |
| ZERO_SHOT_FULL | 0.559 |
| TEACHER_ZS | 0.795 |
| ZERO_SHOT_BARE | 0.000 |
| MISMATCH | 0.000 |

- **ZERO_SHOT_BARE (0.000):** the base model just paraphrases or continues the input, so every output is a format failure. This confirms the bare prompt carries no task information without an adapter.
- **MISMATCH (0.000, all format failures):** an adapter trained with the scaffold cannot simply be run without it. Its raw outputs look like base-model continuations, so the trained behaviour depends on the scaffold context. Dropping the scaffold requires recompiling.
- **Prefill and latency:** dropping the scaffold saves about 188 prompt tokens per call, roughly 80% of the prompt. Wall-clock latency on the A100 showed no saving (mean relative saving −3%). At batch 1 with unmerged PEFT, per-step overhead dominates the timing, so this measurement says nothing about consumer or llama.cpp prefill costs.

Caveats: only 1 repetition and one seed; LoRA was randomly initialized rather than warm-started from the PAW hypernetwork; the tasks are short-label classification only; and accuracy is measured by exact match after normalization, not by the paper's LLM judge (LEM).

registration.title: Decomposing compile-by-training's gap to supervised fine-tuning on real inputs: teacher-invented inputs versus teacher label errors
registration.seed_connection: The seed compiles a specification into a LoRA from (input, output) pairs that the teacher invents from the specification alone, evaluates only on FuzzyBench-Hard (inputs produced by the same kind of generation), and its Limitations section names teacher label errors as the main risk; its only supervision sweep varies the teacher mixture and the pair count. Nothing in the seed says how much accuracy on real inputs is lost because the training inputs were invented, versus because the labels came from the teacher. This MVE re-creates the seed's compile recipe with open models on six real labeled datasets and adds two supervision sources that differ from it by one factor at a time.
registration.hypothesis: Holding teacher, interpreter, pair count and training recipe fixed, the real-test accuracy lost because training inputs were invented by the teacher (REAL-T minus SYN) exceeds the accuracy lost because labels came from the teacher rather than from humans (REAL-G minus REAL-T) by at least 2 points, averaged over six real tasks.
registration.contribution: Ding et al. (2022) and Li et al. (2023) compare LLM-generated data with LLM-annotated or human-labeled data for encoder classifiers, and Prompt2Model attributes its generation-vs-annotation gap to 'domain shift', but none isolates the label component on identical inputs (real inputs with teacher labels vs the same inputs with gold labels) under the seed's regime: specification in context, instruction-tuned 0.6B interpreter, rank-64 LoRA, 100 steps, open 8B teacher. The three-arm design yields, per task, both components plus the teacher ceiling, the teacher's label-noise rate on real inputs, and the optimism of the synthetic held-out estimate that the seed's service would see.

closest_work.difference: Compares GPT-3 as generator vs annotator vs human labels for BERT-style students on SST-2/FewRel with few-shot seeded prompts; does not isolate the label component on identical inputs and uses no spec-conditioned generative interpreter with LoRA.

Relates synthetic-data usefulness to task subjectivity but has no condition in which the same LLM labels real unlabeled inputs under an identical recipe, so it cannot attribute losses to inputs vs labels.
Prompt2Model reports generation-only vs custom annotation on SQuAD for Flan-T5 and attributes the gap to domain shift without separating input shift from label noise.
PAW evaluates its amortized compiler on real datasets but never evaluates gradient-trained programs on real inputs and never tests teacher labeling of real unlabeled inputs as a supervision source.

inputs: Models (HF Hub): Qwen/Qwen3-8B (teacher; Qwen/Qwen3-4B as a time fallback), Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (interpreter/student)
Datasets (HF Hub): cornell-movie-review-data/rotten_tomatoes, SetFit/subj, fancyzhx/ag_news, CogComp/trec, cardiffnlp/tweet_eval (config irony), ucirvine/sms_spam
Python: torch, transformers>=4.51, peft, datasets, accelerate, scikit-learn, hf_transfer
Seed recipe (compile.py of github.com/programasweights/compile-by-training) restated verbatim in the method; no PAW or OpenAI API access is needed or allowed
registration.method:
SETUP. One A100. First command: start downloading Qwen/Qwen3-8B and Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B with huggingface_hub.snapshot_download in background threads (export HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER=1) while running pip install -U 'transformers>=4.51' peft datasets accelerate scikit-learn hf_transfer (torch is assumed present; install if missing) and loading the datasets. Teacher = Qwen/Qwen3-8B, bf16, HF transformers, attn_implementation='sdpa'; if its download has not finished 8 minutes after the first command, use Qwen/Qwen3-4B as teacher and record teacher_used in outputs/summary.json. Student = Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, bf16. Keep both resident on the GPU for the whole run. Render every chat prompt with tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=False). Batched generation uses padding_side='left' with an attention mask; 'greedy' means do_sample=False (pass temperature=None, top_p=None, top_k=None to override the Qwen generation defaults) with max_new_tokens=8, batch 64.

TASKS (six; label words are the exact output vocabulary; every sample uses numpy RandomState(seed); drop rows whose text exceeds 1200 characters before sampling; TEST class mixes are natural, not stratified). T1 rt: cornell-movie-review-data/rotten_tomatoes, column text, label 0->negative, 1->positive; TEST = 400 rows sampled without replacement from split test (seed 0); POOL = split train. T2 subj: SetFit/subj, column text, gold = column label_text (expected values objective / subjective; verify against the dataset features and map integer labels by name if label_text is missing); TEST = 400 from test; POOL = train. T3 agnews: fancyzhx/ag_news, column text, label 0..3 -> world, sports, business, technology; TEST = 400 from test; POOL = train. T4 trec: CogComp/trec, column text, column coarse_label whose feature names are ABBR, ENTY, DESC, HUM, LOC, NUM (map by name, not position) -> abbreviation, entity, description, human, location, number; TEST = all 500 rows of split test; POOL = train. T5 irony: cardiffnlp/tweet_eval config irony, column text, label 0 (non_irony)->literal, 1 (irony)->ironic; TEST = 400 from test; POOL = train. T6 sms: ucirvine/sms_spam, column sms, label 0->ham, 1->spam; the dataset has a single train split: shuffle it with seed 0, TEST = first 400 rows, POOL = the remaining rows. If a dataset fails to load after one retry (also try the un-namespaced id, e.g. rotten_tomatoes, ag_news, trec, sms_spam), skip the task and record it. Task order: rt, subj, agnews, irony, sms, trec.

SPECS (verbatim). rt: 'Classify the sentiment of a one-sentence movie review as positive or negative. Output exactly one word: positive or negative.' | subj: 'Decide whether a sentence taken from a movie review or plot summary is subjective or objective. subjective = expresses an opinion, feeling, evaluation, or judgment of the writer. objective = states facts or describes plot events without expressing an opinion. Output exactly one word: subjective or objective.' | agnews: 'Classify a short news item (a headline followed by the first sentence of the article) into one of four topics: world (international affairs, politics, conflicts), sports, business (companies, markets, economy, finance), technology (science and technology). Output exactly one word: world, sports, business, or technology.' | trec: 'Classify an English question by the type of answer it asks for: abbreviation (asks what an abbreviation stands for, or for the abbreviation of something), entity (asks for a thing such as an animal, color, event, food, product, substance, symbol, technique, term, or title), description (asks for a definition, description, explanation, reason, or manner), human (asks for a person, group, or organization, or to describe a person), location (asks for a place such as a city, country, mountain, or planet), number (asks for a number, date, count, distance, money amount, percentage, period of time, or other quantity). Output exactly one word: abbreviation, entity, description, human, location, or number.' | irony: 'Decide whether a tweet is ironic or literal. A tweet is ironic when its intended meaning differs from its literal meaning, as in sarcasm, saying the opposite of what is meant, or pointing out a situation whose outcome contradicts expectations; otherwise it is literal. Output exactly one word: ironic or literal.' | sms: 'Classify an SMS text message as spam or ham. spam = unsolicited commercial or scam messages such as advertisements, prize or lottery notifications, requests to call a number or text a code, or subscription offers. ham = ordinary personal or legitimate messages between people. Output exactly one word: spam or ham.'

PROMPT U(x) (used for teacher labeling, student training and all evaluations): one user message = spec + '\n\n[INPUT]\n' + x + '\n[END_INPUT]', rendered with the chat template. Training target = label word + tokenizer.eos_token (Qwen3: <|im_end|>); loss on target tokens only. PARSER (same everywhere): lowercase the generation, replace '-' and '/' by spaces, extract alphabetic tokens with the regex [a-z]+, and take the first token that is one of the task's label words as the prediction; if none, the prediction is 'invalid' (scored wrong; invalid rate recorded).

SYNTHESIS (arm SYN; the seed's prompts verbatim). system = 'You synthesize tiny supervised datasets for finetuning small language models from a natural-language task specification. Return strict JSON with a top-level key 'examples'. Each example must be an object with string keys 'input' and 'output'.' ; user = 'Generate 8 diverse (input, output) example pairs that follow this specification.\n\n[SPEC]\n{spec}\n[END_SPEC]'. Sampling with the teacher: do_sample=True, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 0, max_new_tokens 1024, batches of 64 copies of the prompt, torch.manual_seed(1000*task_index + batch_index) before each batch. Parsing: json.loads on the first balanced top-level {...} block; if that fails (e.g. truncated output), extract every substring that is a flat JSON object with no nested braces and json.loads each one. Keep items whose input and output are strings, whose input has at least 3 characters, and whose output has at most 40 characters and parses (PARSER) to a label word; drop items whose input duplicates an earlier accepted input (case-insensitive exact match). Stop when 880 unique valid pairs exist or after 5 batches; record calls, acceptance and duplicate rates. Shuffle accepted pairs with seed 0: the first 800 = SYN training set, the next 80 = SYN-VAL (synthetic held-out). If fewer than 880 exist, SYN-VAL takes the last 80 and SYN the rest (at least 480 required, else skip the task).

REAL ARMS. Sample 900 rows from POOL with seed 1 (text only; gold set aside). Label each with the teacher by greedy U(x); parse. REAL-T = the first 800 sampled inputs with a valid teacher label, paired with the teacher's label; REAL-G = the identical 800 inputs paired with their gold label words. If SYN has fewer than 800 pairs, subsample REAL-T and REAL-G (same inputs) to the SYN count. Record teacher label accuracy against gold on these inputs (label-noise rate) and the label distributions of SYN, REAL-T, REAL-G and TEST.

COMPILE (identical for SYN, REAL-T, REAL-G; the seed's Finetuned Standard recipe minus the amortized warm start, whose hypernetwork is only available through the authors' service; the scaffold is the spec-only prompt U). Reload Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B from the local cache for each run; PEFT LoraConfig(r=64, lora_alpha=16, lora_dropout=0.0, target_modules=[q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj], bias='none', task_type='CAUSAL_LM'), default init; cast trainable parameters to float32 and run forward passes under torch.autocast('cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16). AdamW lr 2e-4, betas (0.9, 0.999), weight decay 0, no warmup, cosine decay to 2e-5 over 100 optimizer steps (lr_t = 2e-5 + (2e-4 - 2e-5) * 0.5 * (1 + cos(pi*t/100))); batch 24 sequences per step (3 passes over 800 pairs; reshuffle each pass with seed 0); sequence = prompt tokens of U(x) followed by target tokens, right-padded, labels -100 on prompt and padding (the 1200-character cap keeps sequences under 512 tokens; truncate the input text if one exceeds it); loss = HF causal-LM cross-entropy (token-level mean over target tokens in the batch); no early stopping or checkpoint selection. Evaluate each run on TEST (greedy, max_new_tokens 8); evaluate the SYN run also on SYN-VAL (correct iff the parsed prediction equals the teacher's synthetic label).

REFERENCES. TEACHER-ZS = teacher greedy U(x) on TEST. STUDENT-ZS = untrained Qwen3-0.6B greedy U(x) on TEST.

DIAGNOSTICS per task: shift AUC = mean 5-fold cross-validated ROC-AUC of scikit-learn LogisticRegression on TfidfVectorizer(ngram_range=(1,2), min_df=2, sublinear_tf=True) features separating SYN inputs from REAL-T inputs; mean input length in characters for SYN and REAL-T; label distributions; synthesis statistics; wall-clock per stage.

ORDER AND TIME GUARD. After setup, loop over tasks in the listed order: synthesis, labeling, three compile runs, two reference evaluations, write results to disk, then the next task. If more than 26 minutes have elapsed since the first command when a new task would begin, skip the remaining tasks and record them as skipped. The registered statistic is computed over completed tasks; at least four completed tasks are required, otherwise outputs/summary.json records 'inconclusive'.

event.description: Averaged over completed tasks, the input component of the gap (accuracy of the function trained on teacher-labeled real inputs minus accuracy of the function trained on teacher-invented inputs) exceeds the label component (accuracy with gold labels minus accuracy with teacher labels on the same real inputs) by at least 2 accuracy points on real test sets.
event.statistic: mean over completed tasks of [(acc(REAL-T) - acc(SYN)) - (acc(REAL-G) - acc(REAL-T))] on TEST, strict label match, 0-1 scale

evaluation.procedure: For each (task, arm) compute accuracy = fraction of TEST items whose parsed prediction equals the gold label word (invalid = wrong), macro-F1 (sklearn, labels = the task's label words, invalid predictions mapped to a token outside the label set, zero_division=0), n and invalid rate. Registered statistic = unweighted mean over completed tasks of [(acc(REAL-T) - acc(SYN)) - (acc(REAL-G) - acc(REAL-T))]. Secondaries: mean input component acc(REAL-T) - acc(SYN); mean label component acc(REAL-G) - acc(REAL-T); total gap acc(REAL-G) - acc(SYN); the same three in macro-F1; per-task values and signs; TEACHER-ZS and STUDENT-ZS accuracies; teacher label-noise rate on the REAL inputs; SYN-VAL accuracy of the SYN run minus its TEST accuracy (optimism of the synthetic estimate); shift AUC per task and its Spearman correlation with the input component (descriptive only, six points); paired bootstrap 95% CIs (1000 resamples of test items, seed 0) for each per-task difference and for the registered mean (resampling within each task and averaging). outputs/scores.jsonl: one line per (task, arm or reference) with accuracy, macro-F1, n, invalid rate, pool size, label distribution. outputs/predictions.jsonl: one line per TEST item per arm/reference with input, gold, raw generation, parsed prediction (plus SYN-VAL predictions flagged as such). outputs/pools.jsonl: every SYN, SYN-VAL, REAL-T and REAL-G pair with its arm, teacher label and gold label where applicable. outputs/summary.json: registered statistic, components, CIs, per-task table, diagnostics, teacher_used, skipped tasks, per-stage wall-clock.
evaluation.controls: REAL-T and REAL-G use identical inputs, so their difference isolates label source; SYN and REAL-T use the same teacher, pair count, recipe, prompt, seed and test set, so their difference isolates the input source (including class-prior mismatch, which is reported via label distributions and the macro-F1 versions of the statistic); TEACHER-ZS bounds what teacher labels can transmit and STUDENT-ZS is the no-compile floor; the teacher label-noise rate is measured so that a REAL-T advantage cannot be attributed to cleaner labels. Single training seed; per-task signs and test-item bootstrap CIs are reported.
