registration.title: Does mask-progress indexing improve a learned cross-domain prompt-cache correction?
registration.seed_connection: Flash-dLLM spends computation refreshing selected cached positions. Progress-related activation directions suggest that some shared cache drift might instead be corrected using a known scalar: the change in the fraction of visible tokens.
registration.hypothesis: A progress-indexed K/V correction calibrated on mathematical infilling states reduces code-state cache error by more than 10% of uncorrected error beyond the best aggregate control among uncorrected reuse, a learned progress-independent offset and norm-matched wrong-direction corrections.
registration.contribution: The contribution is held-out cross-domain cache repair, not discovering a progress direction. The learned constant-offset control tests whether progress indexing adds value beyond a generic fitted drift vector. The experiment remains conditional on one calibration sample and does not identify a pure internal clock mechanism.

closest_work.difference: Subliminal Clocks steers residual activations using denoising-progress directions. This experiment repairs stale prompt K/V and tests whether progress indexing improves held-out fidelity beyond a learned constant correction.
Archer controls prompt-state reuse and refresh using response-state distance. This experiment leaves prompt positions unrecomputed and applies a small calibrated additive correction.
Polestar identifies representations to recompute using drift signals. This experiment applies a shared vector without selecting or recomputing prompt positions.

inputs: Model, tokenizer and modeling code: https://huggingface.co/GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5.
Calibration: Hugging Face openai/gsm8k, main/train, public questions and reference answers.
Evaluation: Hugging Face google-research-datasets/mbpp, sanitized/test, public task text and reference code.
Cache motivation: https://github.com/VILA-Lab/Flash-dLLM; its fused kernels are not required.
Installed CUDA PyTorch, transformers==4.49.0, accelerate, datasets and einops; no evaluation harness, code execution or flash-attn build.
registration.method:
Load one BF16 checkpoint on the A100 and freeze all weights. Reuse its actual normalization, projection, residual and MLP modules. Capture prompt keys immediately before RoPE and after any key normalization, and prompt values before aggregation. Implement a response forward with externally supplied prompt K/V and dynamically recomputed response states. Dense execution with prompt memory columns overwritten is acceptable. Apply corrected keys before their original-position RoPE, with no additional normalization afterward.

Independently shuffle the two dataset splits using seed 1729. Select up to 32 eligible GSM8K calibration examples and 48 eligible MBPP evaluation examples. Format prompts as 'Question: {question}\nAnswer:\n' and 'Write a Python function for this task:\n{task text}\nPython code:\n', respectively. Tokenize prompt and reference response consistently without automatic response EOS. Require prompt lengths 32–192 and reference responses of at least 32 tokens; truncate responses only to 128 tokens. Check eligibility before expensive model work. Require at least 24 calibration and 32 evaluation examples; if fewer qualify, report insufficient coverage without changing filters.

These are controlled infilling states, not generated trajectories. For each example, construct two response permutations deterministically from its dataset ID and seeds 7 and 19. Reveal the first floor(0.25L), floor(0.50L) and floor(0.75L) indices of each permutation. Prompt tokens are always visible. Define tau as visible tokens divided by all real, unpadded positions. The 25%-revealed state is the anchor for both later levels.

On calibration examples only, run full forwards at all three levels and both patterns. For each layer and tensor type A in {pre-RoPE K, V}, let d_A be the mean over prompt positions of A_current-A_anchor. Fit b_A=sum(delta_tau*d_A)/sum(delta_tau^2) through the origin. Each prompt contributes the average of its four transition terms to the numerator and denominator, so prompt length does not weight the fit. Also fit a progress-independent offset a_A as the prompt-macro mean of d_A over the same transitions. Fix correction strength at one; do not tune on evaluation examples.

For every held-out code transition, compute the full current reference distribution. Reuse prompt memory from the anchor and recompute all response positions from current tokens. Compare stale memory; progress correction A_anchor+delta_tau*b_A; constant correction A_anchor+a_A; three wrong-direction corrections using independent coordinatewise Rademacher sign flips of b_A with seeds 271, 314 and 159; and oracle fresh prompt memory. The sign flips preserve each layer/tensor vector's norm. Always start from an untouched anchor copy; never accumulate corrections across forwards. All conditions see identical current tokens. Score full-vocabulary TV at still-masked response positions, plus top-token agreement and reference-token probabilities as secondary diagnostics.

Use sequential processing and minimal downloads. Stop computation by minute 32 and finish reporting before minute 35. An unfinished primary comparison or missing validation is inconclusive.

event.description: Progress-indexed correction transfers across domains and improves fidelity beyond both generic learned drift correction and uncorrected reuse.
event.statistic: The one-sided 95% prompt-bootstrap lower bound for [min(E_stale,E_offset,E_random)-E_progress]/E_stale, where E_random averages the three wrong-direction controls and all errors are prompt-macro-averaged TV.

evaluation.procedure: Within each evaluation example, average TV over masked positions, then equally over the two current reveal levels and two mask patterns. Average equally over examples. Recompute the complete minimum-control contrast in 2000 whole-prompt bootstrap replicates with seed 1729; its fifth percentile is the primary statistic. Report the point estimate, two-sided interval and every control separately. These intervals condition on the single fitted calibration set and do not measure calibration-sample uncertainty. Require E_stale>0.02; otherwise report insufficient measurable cache error. outputs/inputs.jsonl stores dataset IDs, tokenized prompts/responses, eligibility counts, permutations and tau values. outputs/correction_vectors.pt stores slopes, constant offsets and random-control seeds. outputs/cache_scores.jsonl stores per-state and per-position errors. outputs/controls.jsonl stores exactness and identity checks. outputs/summary.json stores the primary statistic, errors and coverage. outputs/manifest.json stores revisions, dependencies and elapsed times. Failure of the event does not establish that progress information cannot repair caches.
evaluation.controls: Strict mathematics-calibration/code-evaluation separation; fixed correction strength; a fitted progress-independent offset; three norm-matched wrong-direction controls; stale memory; and oracle fresh prompt memory. Validate ordinary inference against the unmodified checkpoint on four inputs, requiring mean TV at most 0.0002 and maximum TV at most 0.002. Fresh-prompt replay must have mean TV at most min(0.0002,0.01*E_stale) and maximum TV at most 0.002. At delta_tau=0, progress and random corrections must be identity operations and reproduce the anchor prediction; this identity is not expected from the constant-offset arm. Validation failure invalidates the comparison. Even a positive result would not separate progress effects from correlated newly revealed content.

registration.full_scale_study: Repeat with independent calibration samples, self-generated trajectories, longer contexts and another diffusion backbone. Use matched-mask-count content interventions to separate progress from content effects. Only after robust fidelity transfer should the correction be integrated into a fused cache path and compared with adaptive refresh on task quality and wall-clock cost.

agent.reason: A shared correction could transfer some mask-progress information across domains, but beating a learned constant offset by the registered margin is demanding. Content-dependent drift, nonlinear progress effects and position-specific changes may overwhelm the transferable component.

judge_astra.reason: Generic mask-progress drift may transfer, but the correction must outperform a fitted constant offset on code after calibration on mathematics. That incremental advantage is substantially harder than improving over stale reuse, particularly when averaging removes token-specific drift.

judge_fable.reason: A single mean drift vector fitted on GSM8K and applied to all MBPP prompt positions is unlikely to reduce error much, and the progress-indexed version differs from the fitted constant offset only by a ±33% rescaling, so beating the best control by >10% of stale error is nearly implausible; E_stale>0.02 is also uncertain.

judge_opus.reason: One shared per-layer vector can only fix common-mode prompt drift, and progress scaling should beat a fitted constant offset by only a few percent of the stale error. The 0.02 error gate and maths-to-code transfer add further risk.

judge_sol.reason: Shared progress-related drift might transfer, but prompt-state changes also depend on revealed content and position, which averaged additive corrections cannot fully capture. Beating the learned constant offset by an additional 10% of stale error across domains is particularly demanding.

judge_luna.reason: Mask progress could create a shared activation shift, but the calibration mixes progress with revealed-token content and must transfer from math to code. The offset control may capture much of the same drift, making a substantial incremental gain less likely.

judge_muse.reason: A single math-fitted global vector is unlikely to capture position-specific code drift beyond a constant offset, and domain shift plus content confounding makes >10% transfer unlikely.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Subliminal Clocks shows that LLaDA-1.5 and Dream encode denoising progress (tau) in their residual streams. It steers those activations with mean-vector differences, compared against norm-matched random perturbations, and measures the effect on entropy, confidence and KL. It never treats the progress direction as a way to repair stale prompt K/V caches, and it has no cross-domain test of cache fidelity against a learned constant offset.

Archer reuses prompt K/V within a bounded state neighbourhood and refreshes it when the state has moved too far. It manages reuse and refresh; it does not apply a calibrated additive correction to the stale prompt cache.

Polestar uses token representation drift to pick stale positions and recompute them sparsely. The experiment instead applies one shared vector, scaled by the change in the fraction of visible tokens, and recomputes no prompt positions.
Elastic-Cache, by the seed paper's authors, decides when and where to recompute caches using attention-aware drift tests and depth. It applies no fitted correction to cached K/V.

OnlineCache trains a learnable error corrector for feature caching, but for image and video diffusion transformers (FLUX, DiT, CogVideoX). It is a jointly trained network, not a progress-indexed K/V offset calibrated on mathematics prompts and transferred to code in a masked diffusion LLM.

opus.reason: Prior dLLM caching work I found (Elastic-Cache, Polestar, Archer, EntropyCache, SPA-Cache, Flash-dLLM) handles stale caches by deciding when, where or which positions to recompute. None corrects the stale prompt K/V with a calibrated additive drift vector. Subliminal Clocks establishes the progress direction and steers along it, but does not use it for cache repair. I found no paper testing whether progress indexing improves held-out, cross-domain cache fidelity beyond a learned constant offset and norm-matched random-sign controls, so the question looks unanswered. My searches could have missed something, but none of the cache papers matched on mechanism.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Subliminal Clocks extracts denoising-progress directions and steers residual activations, measuring confidence, entropy and distribution changes. It does not test stale prompt-K/V repair or its advantage over fitted progress-independent correction.
Archer reuses prompt K/V while recomputing response states, but controls staleness through response-distance-triggered refresh rather than a learned additive correction.

Trajectory-Consistent Calibration fits site-specific statistical transforms along corrected image-diffusion trajectories. It does not test a shared mask-progress slope for prompt K/V or isolate progress indexing against a learned constant offset.

LearniBridge learns transferable low-rank corrections for cached image/video features through final-block LoRA adapters. Its feature-dependent reconstruction does not answer whether scalar mask progress improves additive prompt-cache repair across language-task domains.
Polestar identifies high-drift representations and sparsely recomputes them. It does not repair unrecomputed prompt positions using a shared calibrated vector.
Flash-dLLM accelerates cache updates with fused kernels, selective recomputation and draft-and-verify decoding, rather than learning corrections for stale prompt K/V.

sol.reason: The prior work found establishes denoising-progress steering, prompt-cache reuse and learned or statistical cache correction, but does not answer whether a transferred additive prompt-K/V correction gains fidelity specifically from mask-progress indexing beyond fitted generic drift. The proposed intervention and controlled comparison are substantive differences, not merely changes of dataset, model or metric.

opus.reason: No list entry fits a progress-indexed additive K/V correction on math and tests whether it transfers to code-cache repair against offset and wrong-direction controls.

sol.reason: No listed experiment learns a progress-indexed cache correction and tests cross-domain transfer against constant-offset and wrong-direction controls.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I implemented (run_experiment.py, launched by run.sh): GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5 at revision 84346fd, loaded in BF16 with all weights frozen and the checkpoint's own HF modeling code under transformers 4.49.0. Prompt K/V is supplied from outside by dense execution in which the prompt memory columns are overwritten, at batch size 1. Two hooks per block do this:
- a wrapper on `rotary_emb.forward`, which sees K after any key norm and before RoPE, so corrected keys still receive their original-position RoPE and no extra normalization;
- a forward hook on `v_proj`, which captures or overwrites prompt V.

Response positions are always recomputed from the current tokens.

Data handling:
- GSM8K main/train and MBPP sanitized/test were each shuffled with seed 1729, using the registered prompt formats.
- Eligibility was checked before any model work. 32/32 calibration and 48/48 evaluation examples qualified; for MBPP, 147 had to be scanned.
- Two permutations per example, seeded deterministically from SHA-256 of the dataset ID combined with seeds 7 and 19. Reveal counts are floor(qL/4) for q = 1, 2, 3, with the 25% state as the anchor. tau = (P + revealed)/(P + L).

Calibration and comparison:
- The slope b_A is fitted through the origin on macro-averaged per-prompt terms; the offset a_A is the prompt-macro mean drift. Correction strength is fixed at 1.
- Three sign-flip controls (seeds 271, 314, 159) preserve the norm of each layer/tensor vector.
- Every condition starts from an untouched copy of the anchor memory.
- Error is full-vocabulary TV at still-masked positions; top-token agreement and reference-token probability are recorded as secondary diagnostics.
- The bootstrap uses 2000 whole-prompt replicates with seed 1729.

Implementation choices not fixed by the registration:
- The prompt is tokenized with the tokenizer's default special tokens and the response with add_special_tokens=False and no EOS.
- Dataset IDs are "gsm8k/main/train/{original index}" and "mbpp/sanitized/test/task_{task_id}".
- The delta_tau=0 identity check covers the first 8 evaluation examples (64 checks). It requires bitwise-identical memory plus the TV thresholds.
- The "unmodified checkpoint" validation compares 4 inputs run before the hooks are installed with the same inputs run through the hooks in pass-through mode. Because the hooks are pure pass-throughs, this check is close to trivially satisfied.
- A compute deadline at 31 minutes after shell start marks the run inconclusive if hit. My test run finished in about 2 minutes.

Result of my test run (the fresh run should reproduce it):
- All validations passed with TV exactly 0: ordinary inference, oracle fresh-prompt replay, and the delta_tau=0 identity checks.
- E_stale = 0.0148, which is below the registered 0.02 floor, so summary.json reports status "insufficient_measurable_cache_error".
- The registered statistic (one-sided 95% bootstrap lower bound) is -0.039. Point estimate -0.013; two-sided 95% CI [-0.043, 0.013].
- E_progress = 0.0150, E_offset = 0.0152, E_random_avg = 0.0150. Plain stale reuse was the best control.

registration.title: Does fresh-reference attention-times-drift select more useful cache refreshes?
registration.seed_connection: Flash-Cache selects decoded positions using aggregated raw attention logits. Attention concentration alone need not identify which stale representations are most worth recomputing. This experiment compares equal-budget refresh interventions on fixed states.
registration.hypothesis: At a fixed budget of 32 decoded-position refreshes, a fresh-reference-assisted attention-times-drift ranking reduces masked-position Jensen-Shannon error by more than 20% relative to both raw-logit and normalized-attention rankings.
registration.contribution: This is a controlled test of one refresh-utility proxy, not an optimal oracle or an upper bound on all drift-aware policies. Fresh tensors are used only to rank positions; selected positions must actually be recomputed under the shadow forward's stale context. Small single-position diagnostics distinguish inaccurate utility scores from failure to realize the fresh-reference update.

closest_work.difference: Elastic-Cache uses attention-guided dynamics to trigger refresh. This experiment compares equal-cardinality refresh sets on identical states and measures downstream restoration rather than a refresh trigger.

Polestar already uses representation drift for sparse updates. This experiment tests the specific attention-times-relative-drift proxy against two attention-only rankings and investigates why it succeeds or fails.
Attention Sinks in Diffusion Language Models studies sink dynamics and removal. Every KV position remains available here; only the positions whose representations are recomputed change.

inputs: Model, tokenizer and original modeling code: https://huggingface.co/GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5.
GSM8K: Hugging Face openai/gsm8k, main/train, question text only.
HumanEval: Hugging Face openai/openai_humaneval, test, prompt text only; no code execution.
Source for attention-tracking comparison: https://github.com/VILA-Lab/Flash-dLLM, especially llada/flash_cache_triton.py.
Installed CUDA PyTorch, transformers==4.49.0, accelerate, datasets and einops; no new Triton kernel or evaluation harness.
registration.method:
Use one BF16 model on the A100 in evaluation mode, with FP32 attention softmax and scoring. Reuse the checkpoint's modules and instrument post-RoPE K/V and attention logits. Implement shadow caching by computing a dense forward while overwriting memory columns at non-recomputed positions with old K/V before attention. Discarding those positions' dense query computations is an implementation convenience, not a latency claim.

Select 16 prompts per dataset using shuffle seed 2718 and a 64–384-token prompt filter. Format mathematics as 'Question: {question}\nAnswer:' and use HumanEval prompts verbatim. Append 64 masks. Generate a fresh-computation trajectory for at most 24 commitments, committing one highest-confidence argmax from the first 16 remaining masks at each step, with positional tie-breaking. Never commit MASK; stop if no eligible prediction exists. Stop collecting after EOS. Use current states at commitments 16 and 24, each with caches from four and eight commitments earlier.

For each case capture the old full-sequence K/V, fresh current K/V and current reference outputs. Let W be the current first 16 masks and R the positions whose identities changed since the old state. W and R are mandatory recomputations. Optional positions are tokens already visible in the old state, including prompt tokens. Select exactly 32-|R| optional positions, giving every policy 32 decoded-position refreshes plus W. All other memory columns, including unchanged masked suffixes, remain old.

First run a baseline with only W and R recomputed. From this baseline collect presoftmax QK/sqrt(d_k) logits and normalized attention from W, using layers with zero-based index greater than one. Define the raw ranking as the sum across these layers of mean logits over W and heads. Define normalized attention analogously using softmax weights over the complete attended sequence. Define the drift ranking as the sum over these layers and heads of mean attention to i multiplied by [norm(K_fresh_i-K_old_i)/(norm(K_fresh_i)+1e-6)+norm(V_fresh_i-V_old_i)/(norm(V_fresh_i)+1e-6)], using per-head L2 norms. Break ties by position. Fresh K/V are used only in this ranking, not transplanted into selected positions.

Run separate shadow forwards for the three primary selections. Selected positions' K/V must come from that forward's own hidden states. Include recency and three fixed-seed uniform-random optional sets as descriptive controls. All arms use the same tokens, old cache and W. Compute full-vocabulary Jensen-Shannon divergence in nats from the fresh reference at W; do not feed any shadow prediction back into generation.

For the first two selected prompts in each dataset, at commitment 16 and age eight when available, perform single-position refresh diagnostics. Take the union of the top two optional positions under each primary ranking, then fill to eight distinct positions by seeded uniform sampling. For each position, recompute only it in addition to W and R. Record actual JS reduction, the predicted drift score, and layerwise norms/cosines comparing its achieved KV change with the fresh-reference change. This is a diagnostic sample, not an exhaustive optimal-selector search.

Stream cases and avoid saving all full attention matrices. Include downloads and installation in runtime; stop compute by minute 32 and serialize before minute 35. Incomplete primary comparisons are inconclusive.

event.description: The fresh-reference-assisted drift proxy materially improves refresh selection against both attention-only alternatives.
event.statistic: The one-sided 95% prompt-bootstrap lower bound on 1-E_drift/min(E_raw,E_normalized), using prompt-macro-averaged Jensen-Shannon errors.

evaluation.procedure: Average JS over W within each case, then over state/age cases within each prompt, then equally over prompts. Recompute the complete contrast in 2000 dataset-stratified prompt-cluster bootstrap samples with seed 2719; the fifth percentile is the registered statistic. Report two-sided bounds, every policy's error, and descriptive results by age and dataset. Require at least 48 cases from 24 prompts, including at least eight prompts per dataset, and min(E_raw,E_normalized)>0.0001 nats. Otherwise report an inconclusive headroom estimate. outputs/states.jsonl stores IDs, old/current tokens, W, R and eligible positions. outputs/selections.jsonl stores per-position aggregate scores, selected sets and random seeds. outputs/state_errors.jsonl stores per-position errors for every arm. outputs/refresh_diagnostics.jsonl stores achieved versus predicted changes and single-position benefits. outputs/controls.jsonl stores numerical validation. outputs/summary.json stores the primary statistic, coverage and descriptive summaries. outputs/manifest.json stores revisions, dependencies and timing.
evaluation.controls: Every policy refreshes exactly the same number of decoded positions; changed tokens are always fresh and attention is never pruned. Include both raw and normalized attention, random selection and recency. Validate hooked ordinary inference, refresh-all replay and zero-age caching on four smoke cases. Maximum per-position TV must be at most 0.002, and mean validation JS must be at most min(0.000001,0.01*min(E_raw,E_normalized)); otherwise the comparison is invalid. The diagnostic forwards test whether full-reference drift is attainable under stale surrounding context. A negative result concerns this proxy and tested budgets, not all drift-aware policies.

registration.full_scale_study: If the proxy shows useful restoration, develop a cheap estimator using cache age, sampled updates or local representation changes. Compare with Elastic-Cache and Polestar in actual decoding, accounting for estimator overhead and task quality. If it fails, use the single-position diagnostics to decide whether better utility estimation or more faithful refresh computation is the more promising direction.

agent.reason: Fresh-reference drift supplies information absent from attention alone, but the proposed product remains an imperfect utility proxy. Recomputing selected positions under stale context and leaving masked-suffix memory unchanged may limit improvement below the required margin.

judge_astra.reason: Weighting attention by drift could avoid spending refreshes on highly attended but stable positions. However, normalized attention may already select most useful positions, and fresh-reference drift need not be realizable when surrounding representations remain stale.

judge_fable.reason: The oracle attention×drift ranking should pick slightly better refresh sets, but high-attention and high-drift positions largely coincide (recent generated tokens), and stale masked-suffix columns form an irreducible floor that shrinks relative gains; a >20% error reduction with a bootstrap lower bound plus a very strict 1e-6 JS validation and a complex multi-arm pipeline make success unlikely.

judge_opus.reason: The oracle-assisted drift ranking should help somewhat, but a 24-28 refresh budget covers most decoded tokens under any reasonable ranking. Stale masked-suffix error is shared by all arms, diluting differences, so a 20% lower bound against the better attention ranking is unlikely.

judge_sol.reason: Attention-times-drift could avoid spending refreshes on stable high-attention positions. Its advantage may be limited by recomputation under stale surrounding context and untouched masked-position errors, making a 20% improvement over the better attention-only ranking uncertain.

judge_luna.reason: Attention multiplied by relative K/V drift has a plausible link to cache-error contribution, and the equal-budget comparison is well controlled. However, fresh-reference drift may not predict the effect of recomputing under stale context, and the proxy must beat both attention-only rankings by a substantial margin.

judge_muse.reason: Oracle attention-times-drift should beat attention-only by downweighting stable high-attention positions, but stale-context realization and beating the better of two baselines by 20% is demanding.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Polestar-Cache picks stale KV positions using drift, defined as the KL divergence of each token's attention distribution between consecutive steps and computed on clustered hidden-state proxies. It is judged by end-to-end accuracy and throughput. It does not compare an attention-weighted relative K/V drift score against raw-logit and normalized-attention rankings at equal refresh budgets on fixed states, and it does not use Jensen-Shannon restoration at masked positions.

Elastic-Cache decides when to refresh with a drift test on the single most-attended token, and decides where with a layer-depth schedule. It does not rank individual decoded positions by attention multiplied by drift, and it has no equal-budget comparison of selectors.

This is the seed paper. Flash-Cache ranks positions by aggregated raw attention logits and is judged on speed and accuracy. It does not test drift-aware alternatives or normalized attention as a refresh selector.

EntropyCache uses the entropy of decoded tokens to decide when to recompute, and always recomputes the k most recent tokens. That makes it a recency-style policy, not an attention×drift ranking, and it was not tested in a controlled per-state comparison.

CONDUIT ranks stale tokens by attention weighted with value norms, but for reusing vision-prefix caches across requests in VLMs, not for refreshing dLLM caches during denoising. Its score is a value-norm proxy, not drift relative to a fresh reference.

opus.reason: Prior dLLM caching work does use drift (Polestar, Elastic-Cache) or attention (Flash-dLLM) to decide refreshes. I found no work that fixes the states and the refresh budget and then compares an attention×relative-K/V-drift ranking against raw-logit and normalized-attention rankings by masked-position JS restoration, with single-position checks of whether the predicted drift is actually achieved. Related ideas exist in cross-request KV reuse for RAG and VLMs, but those settle a different setting, not this question for dLLMs.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Polestar uses attention-distribution drift for sparse refresh and compares selectors on identical trajectories at matched budgets, but measures identification of stale KV positions rather than downstream restoration by the proposed attention-times-relative-KV-drift score.

Flash-dLLM selects refresh positions using aggregated raw attention logits; it does not compare fresh-reference-assisted drift ranking with raw and normalized attention under fixed-state refresh interventions.

CONDUIT motivates attention-times-displacement ranking but evaluates attention weighted by cached value norms for visual-cache refresh, not measured fresh-reference relative K/V drift in diffusion decoding.

This paper compares matched-budget cache-repair selectors and distinguishes clean-state transplantation from actual stale-context recomputation, but studies causal document edits and does not test the proposed attention-times-drift selector.

sol.reason: Drift-guided sparse refresh, matched-budget selector comparisons, and the distinction between transplantation and recomputation already appear in prior work. However, none of the papers found answers whether fresh-reference attention-times-relative-K/V-drift improves downstream restoration over both attention-only rankings under actual stale-context recomputation on fixed dLLM states.

opus.reason: List entries compare raw logits, normalized attention, recency or random refresh selection, or correlate attention with drift, but none tests an attention-times-drift refresh ranking by actually recomputing at equal budget.

sol.reason: Unlike the listed attention-ranking and drift diagnostics, this experiment selects refresh sets using attention-times-drift and measures their realized downstream benefit after recomputation under stale context.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I built: exp/run.py, launched by run_eval.sh. It loads LLaDA-1.5 in BF16 and runs it through my own dense forward. That forward reuses the checkpoint's own modules (attn_norm, q/k/v projections, rotary_emb, attn_out, ff_norm, ff/up/out projections, ln_f) and computes attention softmax and scoring in FP32. Shadow caching works by overwriting post-RoPE K/V at every position that is not being recomputed with the old cache before attention. Prompts: 16 per dataset (GSM8K train formatted as "Question: …\nAnswer:", HumanEval prompts verbatim), shuffle seed 2718, prompt length 64–384 tokens, 64 masks appended. The fresh trajectory commits one highest-confidence non-MASK argmax per step from the first 16 masks, up to 24 commitments, and stops after an EOS or <|eot_id|> commitment. Cases use states 16 and 24 with ages 4 and 8. W and R are always recomputed. Every policy then refreshes exactly 32-|R| optional positions, i.e. 32 decoded-position refreshes plus W. Arms: the three primary rankings (raw logits, normalized attention, attention×relative K/V drift; all aggregated over layers with index >1 from the baseline forward), plus recency and three seeded random sets. The selected positions' K/V come from each forward's own hidden states; fresh K/V are used only for ranking. JS is full-vocabulary, in nats, at W. The bootstrap is 2000 dataset-stratified prompt-cluster samples with seed 2719. Single-position diagnostics run on 2 prompts per dataset at state 16, age 8: 8 positions each (top-2 union plus seeded fill), recording achieved vs fresh K/V change per layer.

Result from my test run of the exact submitted command (about 1.4 min including pip): status valid; 116 cases from 29 prompts (13 GSM8K, 16 HumanEval). Three GSM8K prompts committed EOS early and gave no cases, as the protocol specifies. Prompt-macro JS (nats): no optional refresh 0.0259, raw 0.0193, normalized 0.0196, drift 0.0180, recency 0.0206, random 0.0235–0.0244. The contrast point estimate is 0.068 (two-sided 95% bootstrap interval 0.015–0.136). The registered one-sided 5% lower bound is 0.0219, well below 0.2, so the registered event did not occur. This result is about this proxy at this budget only, not about drift-aware policies in general.

Diagnostics (n=32, descriptive only): the Spearman correlation between score and single-position JS reduction is about 0.28 for drift, 0.25 for raw and 0.30 for normalized. Refreshing one position under stale context recovers only part of the fresh K change: mean cosine about 0.59, and the residual is about 0.82× the norm of the fresh change. So both the utility estimate and how much of the fresh update is actually realized are limited.

Changes and interpretations to flag:
- **Validation reference uses FP32 softmax.** For the "hooked ordinary inference" check, I compared against the checkpoint's own forward with its _scaled_dot_product_attention patched to FP32 softmax, matching the registered FP32-softmax precision. The other validation checks passed exactly (TV 0; mean JS about 2e-8, which is floating-point noise). registration.title: Compact partial reductions for Flash-dLLM attention-tracking statistics
registration.seed_connection: The supplied source description identifies a query-by-key FP32 tracking buffer in llada/flash_cache_triton.py that is immediately reduced over queries and heads. This experiment first verifies that premise in the pinned source, then tests whether removing the auxiliary materialization matters after the seed's other I/O optimizations.
registration.hypothesis: A compact per-query-block tracking reduction preserves the stock scores and outputs within registered tolerances while achieving a geometric-mean attention-and-tracking stage speedup greater than 1.2 across four fixed workload shapes.
registration.contribution: Streaming reductions are standard; the contribution is an implementation-scoped test of this particular tracking statistic, including multi-writer correctness, per-shape regressions and whole-model timing. Reduced buffer size alone does not establish a runtime benefit, because reductions can increase register pressure and launch overhead.

closest_work.difference: FlashAttention avoids materializing attention matrices for the attention output. This experiment retains an additional column-wise tracking statistic required by the selective cache updater.
FlashInfer provides customizable efficient attention. This experiment changes only the seed implementation's raw-logit tracking reduction, not its attention engine or scheduling policy.

Expected Attention estimates importance when attention scores are unavailable. This experiment computes the existing statistic rather than estimating future attention or intentionally changing rankings.

inputs: Repository: https://github.com/VILA-Lab/Flash-dLLM, particularly llada/flash_cache_triton.py, llada/generate.py and llada/model/modeling_llada.py.
Model and tokenizer: https://huggingface.co/GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5.
Profiling text: Hugging Face wikitext, wikitext-2-raw-v1, validation split.
Installed CUDA PyTorch and its compatible Triton version, transformers==4.49.0, accelerate and minimal download dependencies. Do not install the full evaluation harness or compile flash-attn.
registration.method:
Load the seed repository's LLaDA model and public checkpoint once in BF16 on the A100. Pin and record source and checkpoint revisions. Inspect the actual tracking buffer, indexing, caller reductions, padding convention and layer-selection condition before modifying anything. Save a source excerpt and patch. The baseline must remain semantically unchanged; record any import-only compatibility edits. If the stated auxiliary materialization is absent, or stock writes collide so that there is no defined reduction to preserve, report an unsupported-source result rather than repairing the baseline and claiming a speedup.

Add a selectable compact variant. Inside each tracking-enabled attention tile, before scaling raw QK for softmax, reduce the raw logits over the query rows in FP32, with invalid or non-tracked contributions set to zero. Store one partial sum per query-block ID, request, head and key position. Each partial output cell must have exactly one producer; never replace multiple writers with racing stores or assume mask_num implies one query block. In the caller, sum partials over query blocks and divide by the stock tracking buffer's query-axis extent, including the stock treatment of zero-filled rows, then average over heads and accumulate layers exactly as the baseline does. Keep attention softmax, projections, RoPE, cache writes, token budgets and decoding rules unchanged. When a request has one contributing query block, the same layout naturally has one partial row.

Use all four combinations of batch size {1,8} and actual per-request attended KV length {512,2048}. Construct prompts from successive tokenized Wikitext validation passages and request 128 generation tokens. Set block_length=16, track_num=4, mask_num=4, threshold=0.9 and verify=False. Determine the source's alignment overhead explicitly and choose prompt lengths so captured attended lengths equal the registered lengths; log real and padding counts rather than relying on an assumed padding formula. Capture the first post-prefill forward state under stock generation: query tokens, original positions, block tables, rotary state, per-layer caches and the attention inputs at zero-based layer 16. This is one captured state per shape, so results are conditional operator measurements, not a distribution-wide decoding benchmark.

For operator timing, replay layer 16's masked-attention stage, including its tracking-buffer allocation/initialization, attention kernel, score reduction and accumulation. Restore persistent input caches and accumulated-score inputs outside the timed region, but do not move the stage's own buffer initialization or reductions outside it. Use synchronized wall-clock latency as the primary timing so host-side allocation and launch costs are included; also record CUDA-event device latency. Separately replay the complete 32-layer forward, including logits and its ordinary tracking work, from identical captured inputs. Restore mutated caches outside timed regions. Process workload shapes sequentially to bound memory.

Compile both variants and perform five warmups before measurement. For each shape run three rounds of 30 interleaved operator measurement pairs, alternating stock-first and compact-first order. Run five paired complete-forward measurements per round as a secondary outcome. Record buffer bytes, launch counts and compiler register/shared-memory metadata when available, without requiring Nsight or calling allocated bytes a measurement of HBM traffic. Include four post-prefill free-running decode steps per workload where generation permits. Installation, checkpoint download and compilation count toward the total run budget. Stop timing by minute 32 and finish reporting before minute 35; do not omit a slow shape to claim success.

event.description: The compact reduction yields a geometric-mean operator-stage speedup greater than 1.2 after numerical and write-ownership validation.
event.statistic: The one-sided 95% paired timing-bootstrap lower bound on the geometric mean across the four shapes of median stock-stage wall latency divided by median compact-stage wall latency.

evaluation.procedure: Compute each shape's ratio from the paired measurements and take the geometric mean over all four shapes. Bootstrap timing rounds and then paired measurements within the selected rounds 2000 times with seed 9001; the fifth percentile is the registered statistic. These are conditional timing intervals, not uncertainty across hardware or model families. Report every shape's latency and speedup, including regressions, plus device-only and complete-forward results separately. A geometric-mean event does not imply a 1.2 speedup for every shape or for whole-model inference. outputs/workloads.json stores actual dimensions, token sources, source premise checks, write-ownership maps, revisions and memory use. outputs/correctness.jsonl stores score/output checks, tracking overlaps and free-running differences. outputs/timings.jsonl stores all paired operator and complete-forward measurements with round and ordering IDs. outputs/kernel_metadata.json stores buffer sizes, launch counts and available compiler metadata. outputs/summary.json stores the primary bound and all per-shape and full-forward results. outputs/manifest.json records package versions, source patch and cold-start elapsed time. Any missing shape or failed mandatory correctness check makes the MVE invalid or resource-inconclusive rather than successful.
evaluation.controls: Verify the stock normalization with a small explicit PyTorch raw-logit reference, including zero-filled rows. Test the compact merge on a small multi-query-block case and construct a producer-ownership table for every registered workload; an assertion about configuration names is insufficient. Repeated stock replays must themselves be stable. In paired model replays require tracking-score agreement with rtol=0.0001 and atol=0.001, aggregate top-64 decoded-position overlap at least 99%, and maximum output-distribution TV below 0.002. Record cache-write differences as well. Report any free-running ranking or token divergence rather than claiming bitwise decoding equivalence; the paired numerical tolerances govern the registered fidelity check. No-tracking timing, if recorded, is only a non-deployable upper-bound diagnostic and is excluded from the primary comparison.

registration.full_scale_study: Extend the reduction to ragged batches, broader query windows and Flash-Verify-enabled decoding. Measure end-to-end latency, throughput and task outputs across representative request distributions. Prioritize only workloads where whole-model measurements show meaningful benefit; a large operator gain with negligible full-forward improvement would not justify a major decoding-acceleration claim.

judge_sol.reason: Eliminating the proposed tracking materialization could save meaningful auxiliary memory work, but merge costs, register pressure and host overhead may prevent a 1.2 geometric-mean stage speedup. closest_work.difference: The seed paper introduces Flash-dLLM's fused KV-cache kernel, scheduled flash attention and a selective cache update that ranks decoded tokens by raw attention logits averaged over masked queries, heads and layers (its Eq. 2). It does not report replacing the materialized tracking buffer with per-query-block partial reductions, and it does not measure how such a change affects operator-stage latency.

Elastic-Cache, by the same authors, uses attention to the most-attended token to decide when to refresh the cache. It does not study how the tracking statistic itself is implemented at the kernel level.

FlashAttention avoids materializing the attention matrix for the attention output. It does not handle an extra column-wise raw-logit statistic, and it does not test this in the dLLM selective-update setting.

EpiKV ranks cached tokens for eviction without the attention matrix by using proxy signals, which changes the ranking. The registered experiment instead computes the existing statistic exactly, in a compact form, and times it.

opus.reason: Two arXiv searches and a reading of the seed paper turned up no work that times a compact, per-query-block replacement for Flash-dLLM's raw-logit tracking buffer while checking numerical fidelity and write ownership. The seed describes the tracking score (Eq. 2) but gives no ablation of how it is implemented. General fused-attention and attention-free eviction papers use related ideas but do not answer this implementation-specific speedup question. Streaming reductions are a standard technique, but that matters less here because the question is a measurement on this particular kernel.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Flash-dLLM defines the raw-logit tracking statistic and optimizes KV projection, RoPE, cache writes and attention scheduling, but does not report replacing tracking-buffer materialization with per-query-block partial reductions.

StreamIndex fuses head-wise indexer-score reduction and uses chunked top-k merging to avoid a large auxiliary score tensor. It does not preserve a column-wise tracking statistic alongside ordinary attention or test the incremental cost within Flash-dLLM's optimized pipeline.
FlashAttention establishes tiled, IO-aware attention without materializing attention matrices, but does not compute the additional query-reduced raw-logit statistic used for selective cache updates.
FlashInfer provides customizable attention kernels, scheduling and composable partial attention states, rather than evaluating compact reductions for this auxiliary tracking statistic.

sol.reason: Streaming reductions and IO-aware fusion are established techniques, so the novelty is implementation-scoped rather than a new general algorithm. Among work available by 2026-10-07, I found no paper answering whether single-producer query-block partials preserve Flash-dLLM's existing tracking semantics while reducing attention-and-tracking latency after its other IO optimizations. The closest papers optimize different intermediate quantities and do not settle that incremental performance question.

opus.reason: No list entry modifies the attention-tracking score reduction kernel to remove the query-by-key buffer and time the change; the list's kernel experiments concern projection/RoPE/cache-write fusion or scheduling.

sol.reason: The listed kernel experiments test cache-update fusion or attention scheduling, not replacement of the tracking-statistic buffer with compact partial reductions.

outcome.executor_notes:
Outcome: the registered event did not occur. The statistic (5th-percentile paired bootstrap lower bound on the geometric-mean stock/compact median wall-latency ratio, 2000 resamples, seed 9001) came out at 0.984 in my test run, against a threshold of 1.2. The point estimate was 0.986. All mandatory correctness checks passed, so the run is valid.

Per-shape stage wall latency, stock vs compact (median µs):
- B1/KV512: 215 vs 234, ratio 0.92
- B8/KV512: 221 vs 234, ratio 0.95
- B1/KV2048: 219 vs 233, ratio 0.94
- B8/KV2048: 408 vs 353, ratio 1.15

So the compact variant was slower on three of four shapes. Device-only geometric-mean speedup was 0.99. Complete-forward geometric-mean speedup was 0.985, with per-shape ratios of 0.96–1.01.

Source premise was verified in the pinned seed code:
- The FP32 buffer S[block_m, heads, batch, max_length] holds raw QK logits, stored before softmax scaling.
- Rows are indexed by offs_m - start_m and writes are masked by q_mask & kv_mask.
- The caller does attn_scores += S.mean((0,1)) only when block_idx > 1.
- In every registered workload each request has exactly one 16-row masked block, so each S cell has at most one producer and the stock reduction is well defined. Ownership tables are in workloads.json.
- In a synthetic case with two masked blocks for one request, stock S writes collide. That case is informational only. The compact merge matched the PyTorch reference there.

Implementation:
- The compact kernel is a copy of the seed masked-attention kernel. Its only change: raw logits are summed over valid query rows in FP32 before scaling, and stored as P[query_block, head, key]. Each P cell has exactly one producer, program (block, head).

- Attention, the QKV/RoPE/cache-write kernels and decoding are unchanged; they are the seed's own kernels.

- Tracking-score agreement with the explicit PyTorch reference: max abs difference about 4e-5.
- Compact vs stock at the operator level: max abs difference about 6e-5. Attention outputs were bitwise equal.
- Complete forward: score differences ≤2.4e-4 (rtol 1e-4 / atol 1e-3 passed), top-64 overlap 1.0, TV 0, cache-write differences 0.

- In all four free-running steps per shape, tokens, query positions and argmax were identical.

registration.title: Draft-leakage audit: does Flash-Verify's single-pass mask view reproduce the exact sequential conditionals it is assumed to compute?
registration.seed_connection: Appendix C (Eq. 4, Theorem 1) of the seed paper treats the mask-view output at chain index k as the model's conditional given the drafts at i_1..i_{k-1}, and the 1-gamma deviation guarantee is stated against that distribution. In the official implementation (llada/generate.py) the mask view at i_k attends to the mask views at i_{k+1..K}, which from layer 2 onward have attended to the draft at i_k itself, so the mask view has indirect access to its own draft; and context tokens never see any draft. Whether the single pass is a faithful proxy for the sequential conditional is never measured in the paper.
registration.hypothesis: In more than 10% of verify events, the accepted prefix length computed from the single-pass mask-view probabilities differs from the length computed from exact sequential conditionals (one separate forward per chain index), i.e. the single-pass construction materially changes acceptance decisions.
registration.contribution: First direct, per-event measurement of the gap between a single-pass two-view verification mask and the exact chain conditionals in a dLLM; isolates self-draft leakage at chain index 1 (where the exact conditional is just a plain forward) from the shared-context approximation at k>=2, with a numerical-noise control. Spiffy only argues its related leakage is small via final accuracy; SSD and FreeDave avoid the issue with batched exact verification.

closest_work.difference: Spiffy's blockwise mask lets draft blocks attend to a context that attends to the true block; Appendix A.2 calls this 'near-lossless' and checks only downstream accuracy. This experiment measures per-event acceptance flips and per-token probability deviations for Flash-Verify's two-view mask, which has an extra self-draft leakage path through later mask views.
SSD verifies chain nodes exactly as separate batched sequences; here exact batched conditionals are used only as ground truth to audit the single-pass approximation.

inputs: GSAI-ML/LLaDA-8B-Instruct from Hugging Face (trust_remote_code; the paper's GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5 may be used instead if it loads with the same code)
openai/gsm8k, config 'main', split 'test' (Hugging Face datasets)
torch, transformers (no Triton kernels needed; the seed repo is not required)
registration.method: Setup: load the model in bfloat16 on the A100, eval mode, batch size 1, no KV cache (every pass is a full forward over prompt+256 generated positions). MASK id 126336; EOS ids {126081, 126348}. Prompts: first 40 GSM8K test problems in order; user message = question + '\nPlease reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}.' formatted with tokenizer.apply_chat_template([...], add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=False), tokenized, then 256 MASK tokens appended. Probabilities always via float32 softmax. Base decoding loop (Flash-Verify exactly as in the official repo, which uses a cumulative-product gate rather than the per-token rule described in the paper): at each step, window W = the 16 lowest-index masked generated positions, excluding positions >= the first committed EOS position e (if any). Draft pass: for i in W compute x_hat_i = argmax, c_i = max prob. Confident set D = {i in W: c_i >= 0.9}; if empty, D = {argmax_i c_i}. Commit D. Search set S = W \ D sorted by c descending, truncated to K = min(|S|, 8) positions i_1..i_K; if K = 0 no verify pass. Verify pass: base sequence x_plus = current sequence with D committed and S still MASK (length L); append K tokens holding x_hat at i_1..i_K whose RoPE position ids equal i_1..i_K. Implement this by replacing the forward of the model's RotaryEmbedding class (type(model.model.transformer.blocks[0].rotary_emb)) so that, when a global position-id tensor of length L+K is set, sin/cos are gathered at those ids for both q and k (check that ids = arange(L) reproduces the unpatched output). Pass a boolean attention_bias of shape (1,1,L+K,L+K) (True = may attend) and never pass attention_mask; read the downloaded modeling_llada.py to confirm bool biases are converted to additive -inf and routed to scaled_dot_product_attention (set config.flash_attention=False). Rows of the bias: (a) base row not in S: True on all base columns, False on all appended columns; (b) base row i_k (mask view): True on base columns except i_1..i_{k-1}, True on appended columns 1..k-1, False on appended k..K; (c) appended row j (draft view): True on base columns except i_1..i_j, True on appended columns 1..j, False on appended j+1..K. Sanity test: K = 0 with an all-True bias must reproduce plain-forward logits. From the verify pass read logits at base positions i_k: p_single_k = softmax(logits[i_k])[x_hat_{i_k}], cumprod_k = prod_{j<=k} p_single_j, accepted prefix m_single = max{k: cumprod_k >= 0.8} (0 if none); commit x_hat at i_1..i_m_single (this drives the trajectory). Terminate when every generated position < e is committed (or all 256). Exact conditionals, computed at every verify event with K >= 1: for k = 1..K build sequence x_plus with x_hat filled at i_1..i_{k-1} (i_k..i_K masked), run plain forwards (batch the K sequences, same length L, no appended tokens, no bias), p_exact_k = softmax(logits[i_k])[x_hat_{i_k}], and m_exact = max{k: prod_{j<=k} p_exact_j >= 0.8}. Noise control at every event: a second verify pass identical to the real one except that every row has False on all appended columns (appended tokens inert); read p_ctrl_1 at i_1, which is mathematically identical to p_exact_1, so |p_ctrl_1 - p_exact_1| is the bf16/kernel noise floor. Log per event: problem id, step, K, m_single, m_exact, lists p_single_k, p_exact_k, p_ctrl_1, and the mask-view argmax tokens. Stop starting new problems after 18 minutes of generation; record n. Save per-problem answers, steps, tokens and correctness.

event.description: The fraction of verify events (K >= 1) in which the single-pass accepted prefix length differs from the accepted prefix length computed from exact sequential conditionals exceeds 0.10.
event.statistic: flip_rate = (#verify events with m_single != m_exact) / (#verify events with K >= 1)

evaluation.procedure: outputs/events.jsonl holds one record per verify event (fields listed in the method). outputs/scores.jsonl holds one record per problem (steps, passes, tokens, extracted answer, correctness, number of verify events). outputs/summary.json holds: flip_rate (registered statistic) with a 95% bootstrap CI over problems; signed mean of (p_single_1 - p_exact_1) and of (p_ctrl_1 - p_exact_1); mean |p_single_k - p_exact_k| per chain index k = 1..8; fraction of events with m_single > m_exact vs m_single < m_exact; mean m_single and mean m_exact; number of problems and events.
evaluation.controls: Noise control pass (inert appended columns) gives the numerical floor for p_1 deviations; the K=0 all-True-bias check and the arange position-id check validate the mask and RoPE patch; the chain-index-1 comparison isolates self-draft leakage because the exact k=1 conditional is just the plain forward of x_plus.

registration.full_scale_study: If flips are frequent, implement a leak-free three-view construction (clean base context, draft view, and a chain mask view that attends only to clean masks and earlier drafts) and exact batched verification, and compare them with the original two-view mask on GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval and MBPP for accuracy, tokens per step and throughput, restating the Theorem 1 guarantee for the construction actually used.

agent.reason: The two-hop path (mask view i_k -> later mask views -> draft at i_k) plus context tokens never seeing drafts should perturb mask-view probabilities by a few percent, and a cumulative-product gate at 0.8 flips its accepted length whenever a boundary product sits within that margin; I expect this to exceed 10% of events but it could land lower if deviations are small and most events sit far from the threshold.

judge_astra.reason: The registered mask permits indirect draft-to-mask information flow across layers, and its shared context states need not match separate sequential recomputations. These structural differences make acceptance-length flips above 10% likely, although the paper does not establish their frequency or magnitude.

judge_fable.reason: The single-pass mask view differs structurally from the exact chain conditional (context never sees drafts; later mask views leak the position's own draft), and with a cumulative-product gate at 0.8 modest probability shifts near the threshold should flip accepted lengths in well over 10% of events; the main risk is the custom RoPE/bias implementation failing or running out of time within the tight engineer budget.

judge_opus.reason: The single-pass mask view differs from the exact chain conditional in several ways: later mask views see the draft at i_k and leak it back, context tokens never see drafts, and bf16 noise adds to both. The cumulative-product gate at 0.8 is sensitive near its crossing point, so deviations of a few percent probably flip the accepted length in more than 10% of events. How large the deviations really are is uncertain, and the run could fail.

judge_sol.reason: The two-view graph permits indirect draft access across layers and shares context between different chain conditionals, making acceptance-prefix flips above 10% likely. The inert-append control still alters other rows’ base-column masks, so it is not a clean numerical-noise control, although the direct comparison with exact conditionals remains informative.

judge_luna.reason: The described mask permits later mask-view rows to relay appended drafts into earlier mask-view states across transformer layers, so single-pass probabilities can depart from true sequential conditionals. Because the event counts only threshold-crossing prefix changes—not every probability difference—I leave substantial room below certainty.

judge_muse.reason: The single-pass construction has indirect self-draft leakage plus context blind to drafts, and the cumulative 0.8 gate makes m sensitive to small shifts; with many events near threshold, exceeding 10% flips seems likely but magnitude is uncertain.

closest_work.difference: Spiffy also uses a single-pass blockwise verification mask with a leakage path, but it only argues the approximation is 'near-lossless' from final downstream accuracy. It does not compare acceptance decisions event by event, or per-token probabilities, against exact sequential conditionals. It also does not study Flash-Verify's two-view mask, where a mask view can reach its own draft through later mask views.

SSD verifies draft chains exactly in a single pass using hierarchical verification trees, so it avoids the approximation rather than measuring it. Here, exact conditionals serve only as ground truth for auditing Flash-Verify's single-pass approximation.

This is the seed paper. It proposes the two-view single-pass verification and states its Theorem 1 guarantee against the sequential conditional. It never checks whether the single pass actually reproduces those conditionals.

opus.reason: I searched for self-speculative and draft-and-verify methods for diffusion LLMs, and for attention-mask leakage in single-pass verification. No paper I found measures how often single-pass verification changes the accepted prefix compared with exact sequential conditionals, with or without a numerical-noise control. Related methods either verify exactly by design (SSD) or check their approximation only through final accuracy (Spiffy). The seed paper came out about two weeks before the cutoff, and I found nothing that audits its specific two-view mask.

closest_work.difference: Spiffy Appendix A.2 identifies indirect cross-layer leakage in its shared-context blockwise verification mask, but validates near-losslessness through downstream accuracy rather than paired per-event probability and acceptance-prefix comparisons against exact conditionals.
SSD evaluates chain states as separate sequences in a batched forward pass. It provides an exact-verification approach, not an audit of discrepancies introduced by a shared two-view mask.

This paper audits Orthrus's losslessness using complete trajectory matching across numerical precisions. It does not examine mask-induced conditional discrepancies or per-event acceptance changes, which the proposed experiment distinguishes from numerical noise.

The seed paper identifies mask-view outputs with sequential conditionals in Appendix C and reports accuracy, throughput and tokens per iteration, but does not directly compare those outputs or their acceptance decisions with separately recomputed conditionals.

sol.reason: As of 2026-10-07, I found no work answering whether Flash-Verify's single-pass two-view construction changes acceptance prefixes relative to exact sequential conditionals through paired per-event measurements. Prior work recognizes related leakage, implements exact verification, or audits finite-precision trajectory divergence, but none settles the proposed mask-fidelity question with its first-index isolation and numerical-noise control.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented the registered full-forward/no-cache audit on GSAI-ML/LLaDA-8B-Instruct, including exact K-sequence verification, the unchanged inert-appended-columns control, cumulative-product acceptance, EOS handling, all raw outputs, and problem-cluster bootstrap CI. Tested the evaluation command end-to-end: 40 problems, 1,303 events, 553 flips; flip_rate=0.4244052187, 95% CI [0.3918914, 0.4571640]. Independent output invariants passed. Compatibility correction: downloaded LLaDA converts allowed Boolean-bias entries to +1, which failed the registered all-True reproduction check in bf16. Subtracted that mathematically neutral row-constant shift after bias casting (allowed entries become 0; blocked edges unchanged). Both arange RoPE and all-True-bias checks then reproduced logits bitwise. Selected the same efficient PyTorch SDPA backend for all passes after model loading. Important limitation, not a control change: the prescribed inert-column control retains base-row exclusions, so it is not mathematically identical to exact k=1 in a multilayer model and cannot be interpreted as a pure numerical-noise floor. This caveat and the compatibility correction are recorded in README and summary.

departures: audit.py patches the model block's `_cast_attn_bias` to subtract 1 after the model converts the Boolean bias, so allowed entries become 0 instead of +1. The engineer reported this in README and summary.json. A shift that is constant across a row leaves softmax unchanged in exact arithmetic. It was needed to pass the registered K=0 all-True check, which then matched bitwise, and plain forwards that pass no bias are not touched. It should not change the result.

audit.py forces PyTorch's memory-efficient SDPA backend for every pass and resets it after model loading. The registration leaves the backend open and only requires flash_attention=False. Only numerical-level effects are possible.

audit.py implements the noise-control pass exactly as registered: appended columns are blocked and base-row exclusions are kept. The registration claims p_ctrl_1 is mathematically identical to p_exact_1. That claim is false in a multilayer model, because rows i_k for k>=2 still omit base columns i_1..i_{k-1} and row i_1 attends to them. The engineer reported this. It does not change the registered statistic, but the control cannot serve as the intended numerical noise floor.
The 18-minute new-problem cutoff never triggered; all 40 registered problems ran in about 444 s of generation. A problem already started is always finished. No effect.

Within a step, the search set is drawn from the start-of-step W even if D commits an EOS; the EOS filter applies from the next step. This is consistent with the registered order, which computes W, then D, then S = W\D. No material effect.

The answer-extraction rule (last \boxed number, else last number) and the problem-cluster ratio bootstrap were not specified by the registration. They are reasonable choices left open. Accuracy and the CI are secondary, and neither affects flip_rate.

The 'exactly as in the official repo' decoding loop could not be checked against llada/generate.py. The code follows the registration's explicit description of window, confidence threshold, chain length, cumulative-product gate at gamma 0.8 and EOS handling.

registration.title: Is the causal draft chain necessary? Flash-Verify versus a plain second pass with the identical acceptance gate
registration.seed_connection: Flash-Verify's extra forward pass has two ingredients: it conditions on the confident tokens committed in the same step, and it chains the search tokens so that the mask view at i_k also conditions on the drafts at i_1..i_{k-1} through a custom causal mask with duplicated positions. Remark 2 of the seed paper argues that merely lowering the confidence threshold is not equivalent to verifying, but no control isolates the chain itself from a plain second pass that conditions only on the committed confident set, which needs no custom mask, no duplicated positions and no kernel support.
registration.hypothesis: Flash-Verify (chain-conditioned mask views) commits at least 15% more tokens per denoising step than a two-pass variant whose second pass is a plain forward on the sequence with the confident tokens committed, using the identical confidence-ordered cumulative-product gate.
registration.contribution: Quantifies how much of Flash-Verify's parallel-decoding gain comes from the draft chain as opposed to within-step re-prediction after committing the confident set, both on-policy (realized tokens per step and accuracy) and off-policy on identical states (per-event accepted counts and per-chain-index probabilities), which the seed paper and prior self-speculative dLLM work do not report.

closest_work.difference: The seed paper compares Flash-Verify only with single-pass confidence-aware decoding at various thresholds; this experiment adds the two-pass no-chain control with the same gate and ordering.
Fast-dLLM's confidence-aware decoding commits from marginals in one pass; the no-chain control here is a two-pass variant that re-predicts after committing, isolating the value of chain conditioning.

inputs: GSAI-ML/LLaDA-8B-Instruct from Hugging Face (trust_remote_code; GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5 may be used instead if it loads with the same code)
openai/gsm8k, config 'main', split 'test'
torch, transformers
registration.method: Setup: model in bfloat16 on the A100, eval mode, batch size 1, no KV cache (every pass is a full forward over prompt+256). MASK id 126336; EOS ids {126081, 126348}. Prompts: GSM8K test problems in order (target 70, stop starting new problems after 18 minutes of generation; both arms are run for a problem before moving on so the problem sets are identical); user message = question + '\nPlease reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}.' via tokenizer.apply_chat_template(add_generation_prompt=True), then 256 MASK tokens. Float32 softmax everywhere. Shared loop: at each step the window W = the 16 lowest-index masked generated positions, excluding positions >= the first committed EOS position e; draft pass gives x_hat_i, c_i for i in W; confident set D = {i: c_i >= 0.9} (if empty, the single highest-c position); commit D; search set S = W \ D sorted by c descending, truncated to K = min(|S|, 8) positions i_1..i_K; if K = 0 the step ends. Count one step per iteration; terminate when every generated position < e is committed (or all 256); tokens = committed generated positions <= e (256 if no EOS). Arm FV (Flash-Verify as in the official repo llada/generate.py, cumulative-product gate): build x_plus = sequence with D committed and S masked (length L); append K tokens holding x_hat at i_1..i_K with RoPE position ids i_1..i_K (replace the forward of type(model.model.transformer.blocks[0].rotary_emb) so sin/cos are gathered at a globally set position-id tensor of length L+K; check ids = arange(L) reproduces unpatched outputs). Pass a boolean attention_bias (1,1,L+K,L+K), True = may attend, never attention_mask (confirm in the downloaded modeling_llada.py that bool biases become additive -inf inside scaled_dot_product_attention; set config.flash_attention=False). Rows: base row not in S: True on base columns, False on appended; base row i_k (mask view): True on base columns except i_1..i_{k-1}, True on appended 1..k-1, False on appended k..K; appended row j (draft view): True on base columns except i_1..i_j, True on appended 1..j, False on appended j+1..K. Sanity: K = 0 with all-True bias equals a plain forward. p_k = softmax(logits[i_k])[x_hat_{i_k}] at the base (mask-view) positions; m = max{k: prod_{j<=k} p_j >= 0.8} (0 if none); commit x_hat at i_1..i_m. Arm 2PASS (no chain): identical except the second pass is a plain forward of x_plus with no appended tokens and no bias; p'_k = softmax(logits[i_k])[x_hat_{i_k}] for the same ordered i_1..i_K; m' = max{k: prod_{j<=k} p'_j >= 0.8}; commit x_hat at i_1..i_m'. Off-policy comparison inside arm FV: at every FV verify event also run the plain forward of x_plus and record m_nochain, the per-k p_k and p'_k, and the independent count #{k: p'_k >= 0.8}. Log per problem and arm: steps, forward passes, tokens, extracted answer (last \boxed{...} content, else last number; numeric match to the gold after '####', commas stripped), correctness.

event.description: Pooled tokens per step of Flash-Verify divided by pooled tokens per step of the no-chain two-pass variant, over the same problems, exceeds 1.15.
event.statistic: ratio = (sum tokens_FV / sum steps_FV) / (sum tokens_2PASS / sum steps_2PASS)

evaluation.procedure: outputs/scores.jsonl holds one record per problem and arm (steps, passes, tokens, answer, correct). outputs/events.jsonl holds one record per FV verify event (K, m_chain, m_nochain, lists p_k and p'_k, independent count). outputs/summary.json holds the registered ratio with a 95% paired bootstrap CI over problems, tokens per step and passes per token for each arm, paired accuracy for each arm with the McNemar discordant counts, off-policy mean accepted tokens per event for chain vs no-chain, the mean of p_k and p'_k per chain index k, and n problems.
evaluation.controls: Both arms use the same prompts, window rule, confident-set rule, ordering, truncation K <= 8 and cumulative-product gate; only the presence of the draft views and custom mask differs. The off-policy per-event comparison removes trajectory effects. Mask and RoPE-patch sanity checks as described.

registration.full_scale_study: If the chain adds little, benchmark the mask-free two-pass variant inside the Flash-Cache kernels on all four benchmarks and lengths of the seed paper (accuracy, tokens per step, throughput, memory), since it removes duplicated positions and custom attention masks from the kernel; if the chain matters, study longer chains (K up to 16) and chain orderings.

agent.reason: Multi-token acceptances under a 0.8 product gate need very sharp conditionals, which chain conditioning (and any self-draft leakage) provides and plain marginals given only the confident set usually do not; but the confident set contributes roughly half of all tokens per step, which dilutes the on-policy ratio toward the 1.15 threshold.

judge_astra.reason: Chain conditioning, potentially supplemented by indirect draft feedback, can increase acceptance enough to clear the 15% threshold. However, the no-chain control already re-predicts after committing confident tokens, so the paper's comparison against single-pass decoding provides limited evidence for this incremental gain.

judge_fable.reason: Chain conditioning should raise p_k for k>=2 (plus leakage inflation), so Flash-Verify likely accepts more than the plain second pass, but much of the gain may already come from re-predicting after committing D, making a >15% total tokens-per-step gap borderline; implementation risk is similar to Exp 1.

judge_opus.reason: Chain conditioning should help, because a product of marginals double-counts uncertainty between dependent neighbours. But the plain second pass is essentially one more confidence-aware pass. In the paper, Flash-Verify's verify pass adds about as many tokens as a confidence-aware step (5.7 vs 2.8 tokens/step), and confidence ordering often makes chain elements non-adjacent, so the expected ratio sits near 1.1-1.25, close to the 1.15 threshold.

judge_sol.reason: Earlier drafts can resolve dependencies that re-prediction after committing the confident set cannot, and the 15% threshold is modest. However, the paper’s single-pass baseline does not establish how much advantage survives this stronger two-pass control.

judge_luna.reason: Conditioning candidates on earlier drafts should often raise the probability of a coherent token chain relative to scoring each candidate with all search slots masked, and a 15% token-per-step margin is modest. It may fail when committing the confident set already improves the plain-pass predictions or chain conditioning lowers draft likelihoods.

judge_muse.reason: Chain context should boost later p_k in GSM8K reasoning with strong dependencies, but re-predicting after committing D may already capture most of the gain, so clearing 15% over the no-chain control is borderline.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed paper only compares Flash-Verify with single-pass confidence-aware decoding over a range of thresholds (Figs. 5-6, Remark 2). It never compares against a plain second pass that conditions only on the committed confident set, so it does not separate the effect of the draft chain from the effect of re-predicting after committing.

FreeDave also drafts in one pass and verifies in a second, but it aims at lossless agreement with one-token-per-step decoding. Its search results do not show a chain-versus-no-chain ablation that holds the acceptance gate fixed.

DC-Leap compares contiguous (prefix) commitment with non-contiguous commitment from single-pass confidences. It does not test whether a second pass conditioned on a causal chain of drafts beats an unconditioned re-forward.

SSD self-verifies drafts with hierarchical verification trees in one forward pass and aims to match stepwise decoding exactly. From its abstract (I did not read the full text), it does not report this ablation inside Flash-Verify's gated, lossy setting.

Spiffy's auto-speculation uses calibrated draft graphs and preserves the output distribution. It does not isolate chain conditioning from a plain within-step re-prediction under a cumulative-product gate.

opus.reason: I read the seed paper's results, ablations and Appendix C. Its only baseline for Flash-Verify is single-pass confidence thresholding, so a two-pass control without the chain, using the same ordering and gate, is missing. The closest self-verification work I found for dLLMs (FreeDave, SSD, Spiffy, DC-Leap) studies different verification designs. None of them reports, either along each method's own decoding run or on identical fixed states, how much of the gain comes from the causal draft chain versus simply re-predicting after the confident tokens are committed.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Flash-dLLM compares Flash-Verify with single-pass confidence-aware decoding and varies thresholds and window sizes, but does not include a plain second pass conditioned on the committed confident set with an identical acceptance gate.

SimSD uses duplicated data/mask positions, temporal causal attention and aligned RoPE for verification. Its diagnostics compare parallel verification with sequential denoising and ablate RoPE alignment, rather than isolating draft-chain conditioning from a matched no-chain second pass.

PSD combines confident parallel commitment with hierarchical verification of future draft states and analyzes their contributions. It does not compare chain-conditioned verification against re-prediction after confident commitment alone under the same ordering and cumulative-product gate.

sol.reason: Causal and self-speculative verification were already established, so those mechanisms themselves are not novel. However, none of the work I found answers the experiment's specific attribution question through a matched two-pass no-chain control, including comparisons on identical verification states; this is a distinct ablation rather than merely a new dataset or metric.

opus.reason: Both ask whether verification gains come from conditioning on earlier drafts rather than from a second pass, using a control second pass that removes the draft conditioning while keeping the same acceptance checks.

sol.reason: Both isolate the value of draft-chain conditioning using a second-pass control without draft-token information, then compare token commitment and accuracy–cost outcomes.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented both registered no-cache arms, confidence-ordered cumulative-product gate, duplicated-position RoPE and exact FV visibility mask, per-event off-policy comparison, answer scoring, paired bootstrap CI and McNemar counts. Default evaluation command tested successfully on 70 paired GSM8K problems; independent output audit passed. Observed ratio 1.4858 (95% paired bootstrap CI 1.4280–1.5490). Necessary numerical adjustment: downloaded model converts bool bias to +1/dtype.min rather than registered 0/-inf, and the all-True sanity check failed. Normalized explicit bias to 0/-inf at the SDPA boundary and used the common math backend for both arms; arange-RoPE and all-True-bias checks then passed with exact logits. No weights, visibility, gate, ordering, controls or evaluation were changed. Both actual forward counts (including FV off-policy instrumentation) and policy-only counts are reported. Details in IMPLEMENTATION.md.
