registration.title: Bonus-token acceptance at the first rejection in Flash-Verify: how often is the verifier confidently right about a different token?
registration.seed_connection: Flash-Verify accepts search tokens in confidence order and discards everything from the first rejection onward, including the rejected position itself. Standard speculative decoding instead commits the verifier's own prediction at the first rejected position. In Flash-Verify the mask view at that position already provides this prediction, and under the paper's own Theorem 1 committing the mask-view mode carries the same 1-gamma deviation bound as any accepted token, so a bonus token costs no extra forward pass.
registration.hypothesis: In at least 10% of verify events the mask view at the first rejected chain position is confident about a token different from the draft (block product including that token >= gamma), so a bonus-token rule adds committed tokens for free.
registration.contribution: Measures the frequency of confident disagreements between the draft marginals and the chain conditionals in a dLLM self-verifier and tests the resulting zero-cost extension on-policy (tokens per step and accuracy). SSD includes a leaf-node bonus token in its lossless batched verification, but no work reports it for the single-pass two-view verifier or quantifies how often it fires.

closest_work.difference: SSD accepts N+1 tokens in the best case via the leaf node's prediction in an exact batched verification tree; here the bonus token is applied to Flash-Verify's single-pass approximate verifier with a cumulative-product gate, and its firing frequency and effect are measured.
The seed paper stops at the first mismatch and rejects that position; this experiment adds the verifier's own prediction at that position.

inputs: GSAI-ML/LLaDA-8B-Instruct from Hugging Face (trust_remote_code; GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5 may be used instead if it loads with the same code)
openai/gsm8k, config 'main', split 'test'
torch, transformers
registration.method: Setup: model in bfloat16 on the A100, eval mode, batch size 1, no KV cache (each pass is a full forward over prompt+256). MASK id 126336; EOS ids {126081, 126348}. Prompts: GSM8K test problems in order (target 80; stop starting new problems after 18 minutes of generation; run both arms per problem before moving on); user message = question + '\nPlease reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}.' via tokenizer.apply_chat_template(add_generation_prompt=True), then 256 MASK tokens. Float32 softmax. Shared loop: window W = the 16 lowest-index masked generated positions excluding positions >= the first committed EOS position e; draft pass gives x_hat_i and c_i for i in W; confident set D = {i: c_i >= 0.9} (if empty, the single highest-c position); commit D; search set S = W \ D sorted by c descending, truncated to K = min(|S|, 8) positions i_1..i_K; K = 0 ends the step. One step per iteration; terminate when all generated positions < e are committed (or all 256); tokens = committed generated positions <= e (256 if no EOS). Verify pass (Flash-Verify as in the official repo llada/generate.py, cumulative-product gate, not the per-token rule of the paper text): x_plus = sequence with D committed and S masked (length L); append K tokens holding x_hat at i_1..i_K with RoPE position ids i_1..i_K (replace the forward of type(model.model.transformer.blocks[0].rotary_emb) to gather sin/cos at a globally set position-id tensor; check ids = arange(L) reproduces unpatched outputs). Boolean attention_bias (1,1,L+K,L+K), True = may attend, never attention_mask (confirm in the downloaded modeling_llada.py that bool biases become additive -inf inside scaled_dot_product_attention; set config.flash_attention=False). Rows: base row not in S: True on base columns, False on appended; base row i_k (mask view): True on base columns except i_1..i_{k-1}, True on appended 1..k-1, False on appended k..K; appended row j (draft view): True on base columns except i_1..i_j, True on appended 1..j, False on appended j+1..K. Sanity: K = 0 with all-True bias equals a plain forward. q_k = softmax(logits at base position i_k); p_k = q_k[x_hat_{i_k}]; cumprod_k = prod_{j<=k} p_j; m = max{k: cumprod_k >= 0.8} (0 if none); commit x_hat at i_1..i_m. Arm FV: nothing more. Arm FV+BONUS: additionally, if m < K, let x_tilde = argmax q_{m+1} and c_tilde = q_{m+1}[x_tilde]; if x_tilde != x_hat_{i_{m+1}} and cumprod_m * c_tilde >= 0.8 (cumprod_0 = 1), commit x_tilde at i_{m+1} (the bonus fires); then the step ends. In arm FV also record, off-policy, whether the bonus would have fired. Log per verify event: K, m, fired, c_tilde, whether x_tilde and x_hat are numeric tokens; per problem and arm: steps, passes, tokens, extracted answer (last \boxed{...} content, else last number; numeric match to the gold after '####'), correctness.

event.description: In the FV+BONUS arm, the fraction of verify events with K >= 1 in which the bonus token fires exceeds 0.10.
event.statistic: fire_rate = (#verify events where the bonus fires) / (#verify events with K >= 1)

evaluation.procedure: outputs/events.jsonl holds one record per verify event per arm (arm, problem id, step, K, m, fired, c_tilde, draft token, verifier token). outputs/scores.jsonl holds one record per problem and arm (steps, passes, tokens, answer, correct). outputs/summary.json holds fire_rate (registered statistic) with a 95% bootstrap CI over problems, the off-policy fire rate in arm FV, pooled tokens per step for both arms and their ratio with a paired bootstrap CI, paired accuracy with McNemar discordant counts, the distribution of m, and n problems.
evaluation.controls: Arm FV on the same problems is the control for tokens per step and accuracy; the off-policy fire count in arm FV checks that firing is not an artifact of trajectory changes; mask and RoPE-patch sanity checks as described.

registration.full_scale_study: If the bonus fires often, integrate it into the Flash-Cache kernels and evaluate on GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval and MBPP at 256 and 512 tokens with five seeds for accuracy and throughput, and extend it to multi-token correction (re-chaining after the bonus) and to a calibrated threshold for the verifier's own token.

agent.reason: A bonus fires only when the mask view is at least 0.8-confident (relative to the accepted product) about a token different from the marginal argmax before any low-confidence rejection; leakage toward the draft and the fact that most first rejections are low-confidence make 5-10% more likely than above 10%.

judge_astra.reason: The bonus requires a confident change of mode, with confidence at least 0.8 and higher when earlier acceptances have consumed probability budget. Rejections caused merely by accumulated uncertainty do not qualify, and indirect draft feedback could further suppress confident disagreements.

judge_fable.reason: Most first rejections are 'agree but cumulative product too low' rather than confident disagreement, and self-draft leakage further suppresses disagreement; a fire rate above 10% of verify events seems unlikely except in low-confidence fallback steps, which are a minority on GSM8K.

judge_opus.reason: For the verifier to be at least 0.8 confident in a token other than the draft argmax, a consistent model needs the committed set to have low joint probability (below about 0.63). That rarely holds when the confident tokens each exceed 0.9, and self-draft leakage pushes towards agreement. Firing therefore depends on model inconsistency, low-confidence fallback steps and EOS-variant disagreements, and probably stays in the low single digits of percent.

judge_sol.reason: A bonus requires a highly confident alternative specifically at the first cumulative-product failure; low-confidence agreements cannot trigger it. The accumulated probability penalty and possible draft leakage make firing in over 10% of events relatively unlikely.

judge_luna.reason: At the first failed draft, a different verifier mode must clear a threshold of at least 0.8, so this requires a high-confidence disagreement and may be rare. Conditional shifts could still produce such corrections in more than 10% of events.

judge_muse.reason: The bonus needs disagreement plus cumprod_m times c_tilde at least 0.8, which for m at least 1 often requires c_tilde above 0.9, so confident disagreements at the first rejection are likely rare.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: SSD is a lossless dLLM self-speculative method that verifies drafts with an exact hierarchical tree and can accept N+1 tokens through the leaf prediction. It does not use a single-pass two-view verifier with a confidence-sorted chain and a cumulative-product gate. It also does not report how often a gated bonus token at the first rejection fires.

The seed's Flash-Verify accepts tokens up to the first mismatch and discards that position. It never commits the mask view's own prediction there, and it does not measure how often the mask view confidently disagrees with the draft.

FreeDave also drafts and then verifies in a second pass, but its target is exact reproduction of one-token-per-step decoding. It does not study an approximate thresholded two-view verifier or a confidence-gated replacement token at the first rejection.

opus.reason: Committing the verifier's own token at the first rejected position is standard in autoregressive speculative decoding, and lossless dLLM schemes such as SSD include something similar, so the mechanism itself is not new. I found no paper that adds a confidence-gated bonus token to a single-pass two-view approximate verifier like Flash-Verify, or that measures how often it fires and how it changes tokens per step and accuracy. The seed paper stops at the first mismatch, and none of the papers I found answers this frequency question.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Flash-dLLM introduces the two-view verifier but stops acceptance at the first rejection. It does not test committing a confidently different verifier token or report that rule's firing frequency.

SSD includes a verifier-derived extra token in batched hierarchical verification, but does not evaluate cumulative-confidence-gated correction at the first rejection in Flash-Verify's approximate two-view pass.

S2D2 corrects the first rejection through residual resampling using the same block-diffusion model in autoregressive mode, rather than measuring confident disagreements under Flash-Verify's cumulative-product gate.

SimSD uses paired data-mask verification and replaces rejected tokens, but employs separate draft and target dLLMs with standard speculative acceptance, not the proposed confidence-gated self-verifier extension or its controlled ablation.

sol.reason: Verifier-derived extra tokens and first-rejection correction are established ideas, so the generic bonus-token mechanism is not new. However, the work I found does not answer how frequently Flash-Verify confidently prefers a different token under its cumulative-product gate, or isolate the on-policy effect of committing that token against unchanged Flash-Verify. That specific empirical question remains distinct as of 2026-10-07.

opus.reason: No list entry tests committing the verifier's own token at the first rejected position (a bonus token); #12 instead drops the prefix-stopping rule.

sol.reason: No listed experiment specifically commits the verifier’s alternative token only at the first rejected position and measures this bonus rule’s firing frequency and decoding benefit.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented and tested the registered paired FV/FV+BONUS experiment using LLaDA-8B-Instruct, full no-cache forwards, literal registered two-view masks and repeated RoPE positions, cumulative-product acceptance, unchanged thresholds/window/search limit/prompts/EOS/stopping rule. Writes all required raw outputs, problem-cluster bootstrap CIs, paired tokens/step and accuracy statistics, and result.json; independent log audit passed. Numerical compatibility change was made before running the arms: downloaded LLaDA converts boolean allowed entries to +1 and blocked entries to finite dtype minimum rather than literal -inf. The stock K=0 control changed bf16 predictions. We normalize the constant +1 to zero, use explicit zero bias for unmasked SDPA passes, and consistently select math SDPA; this preserves mathematical attention and both sanity checks then passed bitwise. Documented in IMPLEMENTATION.md and output metadata. Test completed all 80 pairs: bonus fired 289/2512 events (fire_rate=0.1150477707; 95% problem-bootstrap CI 0.10064–0.12999), FV off-policy 0.12162; tokens/step ratio 1.02853 (paired CI 1.00438–1.05400). Accuracy 61/80 each, four discordances each direction; not evidence of equivalence.

departures: experiment.py stabilize_boolean_bias monkey-patches the block's _scaled_dot_product_attention. It subtracts 1 from the converted bias, so allowed entries go from +1 to 0, and it substitutes an explicit zero bias where attn_mask is None. Mathematically this leaves softmax unchanged, because the +1 is a constant per row. It does change bf16 logits relative to stock LLaDA in both draft and verify passes, so trajectories and exact counts could shift slightly. It applies to both arms, is disclosed in IMPLEMENTATION.md and metadata, and is unlikely to move the fire rate systematically.

experiment.py forces the math SDPA backend and disables flash, mem-efficient and cudnn SDPA. The registration only requires config.flash_attention=False. This is a numerical choice the registration leaves open and is applied to both arms; it could only perturb trajectories slightly.

The registration asks to confirm that boolean biases become additive -inf. The downloaded modeling_llada.py instead fills blocked entries with finfo.min and leaves allowed entries at +1. This is functionally equivalent masking, documented in outputs/sanity_checks.json, and should not change the result.

The registered K=0 all-True control is run after the numerical patch rather than against stock code. The stock path reportedly failed it in bf16, which is disclosed. This weakens what the control demonstrates but does not change the statistic.
The model code revision is not pinned: the remote code was freshly downloaded (commit 08b83a6 recorded) and transformers is pinned to 4.49.0. This does not change the registered experiment.

The registration says the verify pass follows the official repo's llada/generate.py. The code implements the registration's literal mask and gate specification instead, and equivalence to the repo cannot be checked from the files. The literal specification matches the registered rows and gate, so impact on the result is unlikely.
Extra logging and statistics were added (token texts, cumulative products, accuracy bootstrap CI, per-arm CIs). These are additive and do not affect the registered statistic.
problems: The registered statistic clears the threshold only narrowly: 0.1150 against 0.10, with a 95% problem-bootstrap CI lower bound of 0.1006 (outputs/summary.json). The event is decided by the point estimate, as registered, but the margin is thin for a single run on one model and 80 GSM8K problems.

The hypothesis title speaks of the verifier being 'confidently right' about a different token. Only confidence is measured, not correctness of bonus tokens. Some logged fires are tokenization variants (e.g. ' \\' vs ' \\(\\' in outputs/events.jsonl).

The tokens-per-step gain is modest: ratio 1.0285, paired CI 1.004–1.054. Accuracy is tied at 61/80 with 4/4 discordant pairs, which is too small to say anything about quality preservation, as the engineer correctly notes.

The K=0 control in experiment.py compares two math-SDPA paths, explicit zero bias against normalized all-True bias, after patching. Its bitwise pass therefore says little about the stock model's bias handling. The stock control reportedly failed, which is disclosed in IMPLEMENTATION.md.
The results reflect the patched numerical path (math SDPA, normalized bias), not stock LLaDA inference. This is a minor caveat on generalizability.
opus.reason: I checked experiment.py against the registration. The window, confidence threshold, search ordering and limit, two-view attention rows, RoPE position duplication, cumulative-product gate and bonus rule all match, and the only departures are disclosed numerical-path changes that preserve the mathematics and apply to both arms. The fresh evaluation reran generation (per-problem timings differ) and reproduced the deterministic values exactly. The registered fire_rate of 289/2512 = 0.115 is computed from real logged verify events. An off-policy FV control (0.122) agrees, and audit_outputs.py checks internal consistency of m, the fired flags and pass counts. The finding is credible and answers the registered question, but the margin over 0.10 is thin, the throughput gain is about 3%, and the evidence comes from one model on 80 problems, so it is a meaningful but modest result.

departures: outputs/downloaded_modeling_llada.py uses a finite dtype-minimum masking sentinel rather than the registered literal -inf. With allowed keys in every row, this should effectively exclude the same attention edges and is not a plausible material change to the reported value by itself.

experiment.py adds stabilize_boolean_bias(), an attention-method patch beyond the registered RoPE patch, subtracting the downloaded implementation's constant +1 bias. This preserves mathematical attention probabilities but can change finite-precision logits, confidence gates and trajectories, and therefore could change the reported value.

registration.title: Does Flash-Verify's acceptance advantage survive open-ended instruction following?
registration.seed_connection: The seed paper evaluates only math and code with structured outputs and states in its Limitations that behaviour on open-ended generation, where token-level confidence distributions are flatter, is untested. Flash-Verify's gain comes from search tokens whose chain conditionals exceed gamma; with flatter marginals the search set is larger but the conditionals may also stay below gamma, so the direction of the effect is unclear.
registration.hypothesis: On open-ended instruction prompts (Dolly creative writing, brainstorming and open QA), Flash-Verify commits at least 1.4 times as many tokens per denoising step as confidence-aware decoding under the same window and threshold (the paper reports about 2x on GSM8K).
registration.contribution: First measurement of a dLLM self-verification scheme on open-ended text, with the same code run on GSM8K in the same session as an internal reference, plus diagnostics (verify events with zero acceptance, search-set sizes, chain probabilities) that explain where the advantage comes from; prior self-speculative dLLM work (Spiffy, SSD, FreeDave) reports only math, code or multiple-choice benchmarks.

closest_work.difference: Spiffy extends evaluation to MMLU multiple-choice tasks; this experiment uses free-form instruction prompts and measures acceptance statistics of Flash-Verify rather than a draft-graph method.
The seed paper reports tokens per step only on GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval and MBPP; this experiment measures the same quantities on open-ended prompts with an in-run GSM8K reference.

inputs: GSAI-ML/LLaDA-8B-Instruct from Hugging Face (trust_remote_code; GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5 may be used instead if it loads with the same code)
databricks/databricks-dolly-15k (Hugging Face datasets)
openai/gsm8k, config 'main', split 'test'
torch, transformers
registration.method: Setup: model in bfloat16 on the A100, eval mode, batch size 1, no KV cache (each pass is a full forward over prompt+256). MASK id 126336; EOS ids {126081, 126348}. Open-ended prompts: from databricks-dolly-15k keep rows with category in {creative_writing, brainstorming, open_qa} and empty context, take the first 50 in dataset order; user message = the instruction text. Reference prompts: the first 20 GSM8K test problems with user message = question + '\nPlease reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}.'. All prompts formatted with tokenizer.apply_chat_template(add_generation_prompt=True) and followed by 256 MASK tokens. Float32 softmax. Shared loop: window W = the 16 lowest-index masked generated positions excluding positions >= the first committed EOS position e; draft pass gives x_hat_i, c_i for i in W; confident set D = {i: c_i >= 0.9} (if empty, the single highest-c position); commit D. One step per iteration; terminate when all generated positions < e are committed (or all 256); tokens = committed generated positions <= e (256 if no EOS). Arm CA (confidence-aware): nothing more per step. Arm FV (Flash-Verify as in the official repo llada/generate.py, cumulative-product gate): search set S = W \ D sorted by c descending, truncated to K = min(|S|, 8) positions i_1..i_K (K = 0 ends the step); x_plus = sequence with D committed and S masked (length L); append K tokens holding x_hat at i_1..i_K with RoPE position ids i_1..i_K (replace the forward of type(model.model.transformer.blocks[0].rotary_emb) to gather sin/cos at a globally set position-id tensor; check ids = arange(L) reproduces unpatched outputs). Boolean attention_bias (1,1,L+K,L+K), True = may attend, never attention_mask (confirm in the downloaded modeling_llada.py that bool biases become additive -inf inside scaled_dot_product_attention; set config.flash_attention=False). Rows: base row not in S: True on base columns, False on appended; base row i_k (mask view): True on base columns except i_1..i_{k-1}, True on appended 1..k-1, False on appended k..K; appended row j (draft view): True on base columns except i_1..i_j, True on appended 1..j, False on appended j+1..K. Sanity: K = 0 with all-True bias equals a plain forward. p_k = softmax(logits at base position i_k)[x_hat_{i_k}]; m = max{k: prod_{j<=k} p_j >= 0.8} (0 if none); commit x_hat at i_1..i_m. Run both arms on every prompt (both arms per prompt before moving on; stop starting new prompts after 18 minutes of generation, Dolly first then GSM8K, keeping at least 10 GSM8K problems). Log per prompt and arm: dataset, steps, forward passes, tokens, decoded text, mean c over window positions per step, and (FV) per verify event K, m, p_k; compute a degeneration flag per output (any 4-gram occurring 3 or more times) and for GSM8K the extracted answer (last \boxed{...}, else last number) and correctness.

event.description: On the Dolly open-ended prompts, pooled tokens per step of Flash-Verify divided by pooled tokens per step of confidence-aware decoding exceeds 1.4.
event.statistic: ratio_open = (sum tokens_FV / sum steps_FV) / (sum tokens_CA / sum steps_CA) over Dolly prompts

evaluation.procedure: outputs/scores.jsonl holds one record per prompt and arm (dataset, steps, passes, tokens, text, degeneration flag, and for GSM8K answer and correctness). outputs/events.jsonl holds one record per FV verify event (dataset, prompt id, step, K, m, p_k list). outputs/summary.json holds ratio_open (registered statistic) with a 95% paired bootstrap CI over prompts, the same ratio on the GSM8K reference prompts, tokens per step and passes per token per arm and dataset, fraction of verify events with m = 0 and mean K per dataset, mean window confidence per dataset, degeneration rates per arm and dataset, and n prompts.
evaluation.controls: Confidence-aware decoding with the identical window, threshold and EOS rule is the control arm; the in-run GSM8K reference ratio calibrates the setup against the paper's reported gain; mask and RoPE-patch sanity checks as described.

registration.full_scale_study: If the advantage transfers, evaluate Flash-dLLM with the Flash-Cache kernels on chat and writing benchmarks (e.g., AlpacaEval-style prompts with a local judge model, summarization with ROUGE) for throughput and quality; if it collapses, develop task-adaptive gamma or verify-pass skipping policies driven by running confidence statistics, as suggested in the paper's Limitations.

agent.reason: Model-generated free text is low-entropy under the model itself and confidence-aware decoding accepts fewer tokens there, which leaves more room for verification to add tokens, but chain conditionals in free text may often stay below 0.8 so that many verify passes accept nothing; 1.4 is close to where I expect the ratio to land.

judge_astra.reason: Open-ended text still contains predictable local continuations, and FV gets an additional forward pass within each counted step, making a 1.4-fold tokens-per-step gain plausible. Flatter distributions and the stricter product gate weaken transfer from the seed results; passing this event would not establish a throughput or quality advantage.

judge_fable.reason: On flatter open-ended text the confident set shrinks, so even a modest verify gain yields a sizeable ratio, and degenerate repetitive outputs would inflate it, but chain conditionals may also fail the 0.8 gate more often; 1.4 is close to my central estimate, and the longer per-prompt runtime adds timeout risk.

judge_opus.reason: Simple models of open-ended text (choice points every 2-4 tokens followed by near-deterministic continuations) give a Flash-Verify/confidence-aware ratio of about 1.4-1.7, below the roughly 2x reported on GSM8K. Confidence ordering that interleaves far positions, mismatched drafts after choice points, and window-limited repetitive stretches could pull it under 1.4.

judge_sol.reason: Draft conditioning could sharpen diffuse open-ended predictions enough to exceed the 1.4× threshold, but flatter confidence distributions could also produce many zero-acceptance passes. A tokens-per-step gain would not by itself establish better wall-clock throughput or preserved output quality.

judge_luna.reason: The seed reports Flash-Verify gains on structured tasks but explicitly leaves open-ended prompts untested; a 1.4x token-per-step ratio is plausible, especially if confidence-aware decoding often falls back to one token. Flatter confidence could also leave many verify events with no accepted search tokens, so uncertainty is high.

judge_muse.reason: The paper shows fewer early-decodable tokens when confidence is lower, and flatter open-ended marginals will often give m equals 0 under the cumulative 0.8 gate, making 1.4x retention of the GSM8K doubling uncertain.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed paper reports Flash-Verify's tokens per step only on GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval and MBPP. The experiment measures the same acceptance gain over confidence-aware decoding on open-ended Dolly prompts (creative writing, brainstorming, open QA), with an in-run GSM8K reference.

SSD is a lossless self-speculative dLLM method (hierarchical verification trees) tested on LLaDA and Dream with structured benchmarks. It does not measure acceptance on open-ended instruction prompts, and it does not test Flash-Verify's cumulative-product gate.
FreeDave is a draft-and-verify dLLM decoder evaluated only on math and code. It does not look at open-ended generation.

S2D2 is self-speculation for block-diffusion models (SDAR, LLaDA2.1). Its search-result summary mentions accuracy and speed gains over confidence thresholding but no open-ended or creative-writing evaluation. I did not read the full text, and it does not test Flash-Verify on LLaDA-8B.
This paper does include chat benchmarks, but its diffusion drafters serve autoregressive Qwen3 targets. It does not study a dLLM verifying its own drafts during denoising.

opus.reason: I found no paper that measures how a dLLM's self-verification acceptance gain (here, Flash-Verify against confidence-aware decoding) changes on open-ended instruction prompts compared with math. Every dLLM self-speculative or draft-and-verify paper I found (SSD, FreeDave, S2D2, Flash-dLLM) reports math or code only, going by the abstracts and search results I saw. Spiffy, according to the experiment's own description, goes only as far as multiple-choice; I did not check that paper myself. The one chat result I found (BV Loss) concerns diffusion drafters for autoregressive models, which is a different question. The search was limited to a handful of arXiv queries, so I cannot rule out that some dLLM acceleration paper reports open-ended results in its appendix.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Flash-dLLM compares Flash-Verify with confidence-aware decoding on math and code, but explicitly leaves open-ended writing and dialogue untested. The experiment tests that domain transfer with acceptance diagnostics and an in-run GSM8K reference.

S2D2 already evaluates training-free diffusion self-verification against confidence-threshold baselines on IFEval. However, it uses block-size-one autoregressive verification with probability-ratio rejection sampling and routing, rather than Flash-Verify's confidence-ordered search tokens and cumulative-product gate.

Spiffy measures self-speculative acceleration on math, code and MMLU domains using calibrated draft-state graphs. It does not test Flash-Verify's acceptance advantage on free-form creative writing, brainstorming or open QA.

sol.reason: I found no prior work answering whether Flash-Verify retains its tokens-per-step advantage over a matched confidence-aware control on open-ended instruction prompts. S2D2 provides prior instruction-following self-verification evaluation, so the experiment's broad first-measurement claim needs qualification. Nevertheless, its different verification mechanism does not settle the registered domain-transfer question.

opus.reason: Both compare Flash-Verify's tokens-per-step advantage over confidence-aware decoding on open-ended Dolly prompts, with an in-session GSM8K control and degeneration proxies.

sol.reason: Both compare no-cache Flash-Verify with confidence-aware decoding on Dolly open-ended prompts using an in-session GSM8K contrast, measuring token commitment per step/pass and output degeneration.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented the registered batch-1 bfloat16 no-cache CA/FV experiment with 256 generated positions, window 16, epsilon .9, K<=8, cumulative-product gamma .8 gate, specified two-view attention bias, duplicated-position RoPE, EOS rules, both sanity checks, paired bootstrap and all required raw outputs. Dolly runs first with a runtime-based reservation for >=10 GSM8K pairs; the strict 18-minute stop-starting deadline is preserved. Numerical compatibility correction: downloaded HF code maps Boolean True to additive 1 rather than 0. A wrapper normalizes Boolean attention_bias to float32 0/-inf before the original forward (native casts saturate blocked entries to finfo.min); both arms use math SDPA, enforced after the remote constructor resets backend flags. All-True versus plain and arange-RoPE checks had zero differences. Final evaluation command tested end-to-end and outputs validated: 46 Dolly / 20 GSM8K, ratio_open 1.65566 (95% paired CI 1.55538–1.76956), reference ratio 2.05870, generation 839 seconds. Time-limited Dolly count can vary with runtime. Acceptance gain is not a speed/quality claim: Dolly passes/token were higher for FV.

departures: experiment.py normalize_bool_bias: the registration assumed the downloaded modeling_llada.py turns Boolean biases into additive -inf. The saved source (outputs/sanity.json, outputs/downloaded_modeling_llada.py) shows True becomes +1.0 and False becomes finfo.min. The wrapper converts Boolean biases to float32 0/-inf before the original forward. A constant +1 on every allowed key in a row does not change the softmax, every row keeps L allowed keys, and the all-True-versus-plain check is exactly equal. Disclosed. It cannot plausibly change the result.

experiment.py main: the math SDPA backend is forced for both arms, and the backend flags are set again after the remote constructor resets them. This goes beyond the registered config.flash_attention=False. It is a numerical-consistency choice applied identically to both arms. It cannot plausibly change the result.

experiment.py main: the time-budget rule is implemented as a dynamic reservation for 10 GSM8K pairs, based on recent normalized pair cost × 1.25 with a 30 s floor. The registration only said to stop starting new prompts after 18 minutes, Dolly first, keeping at least 10 GSM8K. In the engineer's test runs this rule cut Dolly to 41 and 46 prompts. In the protected run it never bound (summary.json reservations; n_dolly = 50, n_gsm8k = 20), so all registered prompts were run. It could change the result on a slower machine but did not here.

experiment.py generate: the FV search set is taken from the original window W even when the same step commits an EOS in D. The registration does not settle this case. It has negligible effect on the result.

experiment.py summarize: 'mean_chain_probability' is the mean of the individual p_k, not of the cumulative chain products. This is a diagnostic-label difference only. Cumulative products are logged in events.jsonl. It does not affect the registered statistic.
problems: engineer_notes: the quoted headline (46 Dolly, ratio_open 1.65566, CI 1.555–1.770) comes from the engineer's own test run (test_final.log). The protected evaluation produced 50 Dolly prompts, ratio_open 1.6167 and CI 1.499–1.734. The difference is explained by the time-limited prompt count, but the notes do not report the evaluated value.

The ratio falls as more Dolly prompts are added (41 prompts: 1.689; 46: 1.656; 50: 1.617). The estimate depends on which prefix of the prompt list is used. The CI lower bound (1.499) is still above the 1.4 threshold.

summary.json: on Dolly, FV needs more forward passes per token than CA (0.965 vs 0.785). In this no-cache setup, FV's per-step advantage on open-ended prompts does not mean fewer passes or compute savings. On GSM8K passes per token are roughly equal (0.289 vs 0.306).

summary.json: the degeneration rate is 1.0 for both arms on GSM8K. The 4-gram ≥3 criterion therefore flags all GSM8K outputs and does not separate the arms there. Dolly degeneration rates (CA 0.58, FV 0.50) are also high.

scores.jsonl: on several Dolly prompts the two arms produce very different output lengths (e.g., prompt 37: CA 255 tokens vs FV 64; prompt 99: 255 vs 94). The pooled tokens-per-step ratio therefore also reflects trajectory and length differences, not only acceptance on matched content.
Scope limits: one model, a single run, 50 Dolly and 20 GSM8K prompts, and no quality evaluation of the open-ended outputs.
opus.reason: The code implements the registered experiment closely. I checked the window/EOS rules, the confidence threshold and fallback, K≤8 descending-confidence search, the two-view attention bias row by row against the registration, duplicated-position RoPE, the cumulative-product gate at 0.8, and the paired bootstrap. The one substantive change, normalizing the Boolean bias to 0/-inf, is disclosed, effectively softmax-invariant and backed by exact sanity checks. The protected run used all 50 registered Dolly prompts and all 20 GSM8K problems. It gives ratio_open = 1.617 (95% paired CI 1.50–1.73), so the event threshold of 1.4 is cleared, and the in-run GSM8K reference reproduces about 2.06x, which matches the paper's reported gain. The evidence is credible and useful: the FV advantage is smaller on open-ended text, 59% of Dolly verify events accept nothing, and FV uses more forward passes per token than CA there. It is limited by one model, a modest prompt count, sensitivity to the prompt prefix and no quality measurement, so it merits 2 rather than 3.

departures: experiment.py: The registered Boolean attention_bias is converted to float32 0/-inf before the original model forward, rather than passed through the downloaded implementation's native Boolean conversion. outputs/downloaded_modeling_llada.py confirms that native conversion leaves allowed entries at additive 1. This correction can change numerical outputs relative to native Boolean handling, but implements the intended attention semantics and enables the registered all-True-versus-plain sanity check.

experiment.py: Both arms explicitly use PyTorch math SDPA, including resetting backend flags after model construction. The registration disables config.flash_attention but does not specify every SDPA backend flag. Backend selection can affect numerical outputs and runtime; this is an unspecified implementation choice applied consistently to both arms, not an altered experimental contrast.

experiment.py: A dynamically estimated time reservation can stop Dolly sampling before the 18-minute deadline to preserve time for GSM8K. The precise reservation formula was not registered and affected sample sizes in submitted development runs. It did not exclude any registered prompts in the protected evaluation, which completed all 50 Dolly and 20 GSM8K prompts, so it did not change that run's statistic.

experiment.py: Dolly eligibility uses not row['context'].strip(), which also admits whitespace-only contexts rather than requiring a literally empty string. This could change the selected prefix if such rows occur among the eligible candidates; the supplied evidence does not establish that any selected row differs for this reason.
problems: outputs/summary.json: The acceptance gain is not a compute-efficiency gain on Dolly. FV uses 0.9646 forward passes per output token versus CA's 0.7846, approximately 23% more, and verification forwards also contain appended tokens.

outputs/summary.json and experiment.py: The registered statistic compares different generated trajectories and lengths: Dolly output totals are 6,954 FV tokens versus 8,052 CA tokens. registration.title: Attention-ranked versus recency-ranked tracked tokens: fidelity of selective KV refresh to full recomputation
registration.seed_connection: Flash-Cache refreshes, besides the masked window, only a fixed budget of decoded tokens selected by the attention they receive from masked queries (Eq. 2), motivated by Fig. 1b (top-32 attended tokens carry about 50% of attention). The paper never compares this selection rule with the trivial alternative of refreshing the most recently decoded tokens, which in near-left-to-right generation may coincide with the most attended ones and needs no attention bookkeeping.
registration.hypothesis: With a 64-token tracking budget and a 64-token masked query, selecting tracked tokens by received attention yields window predictions at least 20% closer to full recomputation (mean KL over window positions) than selecting the 64 most recently decoded tokens.
registration.contribution: Isolates the value of attention-based refresh selection at a matched budget using a prediction-level fidelity metric that needs no accuracy comparisons, with a random-selection floor and a full-refresh validation; Elastic-Cache uses the most-attended token only to decide when to refresh, and dLLM cache-eviction papers select tokens for eviction rather than for refresh.

closest_work.difference: Elastic-Cache uses the most-attended token's KV drift as a trigger for when to refresh and refreshes layers from a chosen depth; this experiment compares which tokens to refresh at a fixed budget (attention vs recency vs random) by KL to full recomputation.
The seed paper reports only ablations of the budget size beta_t for its attention-based rule; this experiment compares selection rules at a fixed beta_t = 64.

inputs: GSAI-ML/LLaDA-8B-Instruct from Hugging Face (trust_remote_code; GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5 may be used instead if it loads with the same code)
openai/gsm8k, config 'main', split 'test'
torch, transformers
registration.method: Setup: model in bfloat16 on the A100, eval mode, batch size 1. MASK id 126336; EOS ids {126081, 126348}. Prompts: GSM8K test problems in order (target 60; stop starting new problems after 18 minutes of generation); user message = question + '\nPlease reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}.' via tokenizer.apply_chat_template(add_generation_prompt=True), then 256 MASK tokens. Reference trajectory (drives decoding): full forward each step; window W = the 16 lowest-index masked generated positions excluding positions >= the first committed EOS position e; p_ref over W (float32 softmax); commit D = {i in W: max p >= 0.9} (if empty, the single highest-confidence position); terminate when all generated positions < e are committed (or all 256). Partial forward with a KV cache, written from the model's own modules (read the downloaded modeling_llada.py for the exact block order; LLaDA uses LLaMA-style blocks: attn_norm -> q_proj/k_proj/v_proj -> RoPE -> attention -> attn_out -> residual -> ff_norm -> act(ff_proj(x)) * up_proj(x) -> ff_out -> residual; then ln_f and the output head, honouring any q_norm/k_norm, input_emb_norm or scale_logits flags): given the full token sequence, a query position set Q and a per-layer cache of post-RoPE keys and values for all L positions, embed only the Q tokens, and in each layer compute q,k,v for Q, apply RoPE at the true positions of Q (use the block's rotary_emb helpers get_rotary_embedding and apply_rotary_pos_emb with gathered sin/cos), write k,v into the cache at Q, attend from the Q queries to the full cached K,V of all L positions (scaled_dot_product_attention, no mask), and continue; return logits at Q. Validation: with Q = all positions the partial forward must match the HF forward (report max |logit difference| and the KL; the KL must be far below the shadow policies' KL). Shadow caches: three independent caches (policies attended, recent, random), each initialised at step 0 by the partial forward with Q = all positions. At each later step t, for each policy run the partial forward with Q = M64 union T_P, where M64 = the 64 lowest-index masked generated positions (excluding >= e) and T_P = D_{t-1} (positions committed at the previous step) plus the top (64 - |D_{t-1}|) other decoded positions (prompt positions count as decoded) ranked by: attended = score from that policy's previous partial pass, where score(i) = sum over layers of the mean over the 64 masked query rows and heads of the softmax attention weight paid to key i (compute these weights explicitly with q K^T / sqrt(d) for the masked rows; use the initial full pass for the first step); recent = most recently committed first, ties broken by larger position index; random = uniform without replacement with a fixed seed. Read the shadow logits at W, p_P. Metrics per step and policy: KL_P = mean over i in W of sum p_ref_i (log p_ref_i - log p_P_i) in float32; argmax agreement over W; whether the shadow's confident set (threshold 0.9 with the same fallback) and tokens equal the reference's. Also run the policy all (T = all decoded) on the first 3 steps of the first 5 problems as the validation floor. Log per step: problem id, step, |D_{t-1}|, per-policy KL, agreement, commit-set match, and the overlap |T_attended intersect T_recent|/64.

event.description: The mean KL to full recomputation of the recency policy divided by the mean KL of the attention policy, pooled over all steps and problems, exceeds 1.2.
event.statistic: ratio = mean_steps(KL_recent) / mean_steps(KL_attended)

evaluation.procedure: outputs/steps.jsonl holds one record per decoding step with the per-policy metrics and the tracked-set overlap. outputs/scores.jsonl holds one record per problem (steps, tokens, extracted answer and correctness of the reference trajectory). outputs/summary.json holds the registered ratio with a 95% bootstrap CI over problems, mean KL, argmax agreement and commit-set match rate for attended, recent, random and all (validation), the mean tracked-set overlap between attended and recent, the max logit difference of the validation, and n problems and steps.
evaluation.controls: Random selection is the floor; the all-decoded policy validates the partial-forward implementation (must reproduce the full forward); all policies share the reference trajectory, the same masked query set, the same budget and the same automatic inclusion of newly decoded tokens, so only the selection rule differs.

registration.full_scale_study: If attention-based selection is clearly better, sweep budgets (16 to 128), per-layer selection and score normalisations inside the Flash-Cache kernels across the four benchmarks with accuracy and throughput; if recency matches it, replace the attention bookkeeping in the fused kernel with a recency ring buffer and measure the end-to-end throughput and memory gain.

agent.reason: Elastic-Cache's own observation that the most-attended tokens drift least suggests refreshing them buys little fidelity, while recently decoded tokens have both high drift and high local attention and are largely covered by both policies; a 20% KL advantage for attention-ranked selection therefore seems less likely than near-parity.

judge_astra.reason: High attention does not necessarily identify representations most in need of refreshing, particularly when every policy refreshes newly decoded tokens and recency may overlap substantially with attention rankings. Unrefreshed masked positions can also create a shared error floor, while the custom partial-forward implementation adds substantial execution and validation risk.

judge_fable.reason: Both policies refresh the high-drift, highly attended tokens just behind the window; whether refreshing attended prompt/sink tokens beats refreshing mid-range recent tokens by >=17% in KL is close to a coin flip, and the custom partial-forward reimplementation of LLaDA blocks is the hardest engineering task of the five.

judge_opus.reason: Ranking by received softmax attention will spend budget on attention sinks and prompt tokens. Prior dLLM caching work (dLLM-Cache, Elastic-Cache) reports these as having the smallest KV drift. Recency instead refreshes exactly the near-frontier tokens whose KV changes most, so a 20% KL advantage for attention looks unlikely; the custom partial forward also adds implementation risk.

judge_sol.reason: The reported attention concentration supports the hypothesis, but attention importance need not coincide with refresh necessity, and recency may capture many of the same useful positions. Shared stale masked states and substantial custom-forward validation requirements add uncertainty about clearing the registered KL-ratio threshold.

judge_luna.reason: The seed's attention-concentration observation supports attention-ranked refreshes, and recency can discard prompt tokens that remain relevant during long outputs. However, recently decoded tokens may themselves dominate attention, creating substantial overlap and making a 20% KL advantage uncertain.

judge_muse.reason: Attention can retain important prompt and sink tokens that recency evicts, and 1.2x on small KLs is a modest bar, though left-to-right generation may make the two 64-token sets overlap heavily.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed paper defines the attention-ranked tracking set (Eq. 2) and justifies it only with Fig. 1b. Its ablations vary the tracking budget, gamma/epsilon and the masked-window size; it never compares selection rules (attention vs recency vs random) at a fixed budget, and it never measures how closely the cached predictions match full recomputation.

EntropyCache argues for recency: decoded tokens stay volatile for several steps, so it recomputes the k most recently decoded tokens, and it uses decoded-token entropy to decide when to recompute. I could only read its abstract, so I can't confirm it lacks a matched-budget comparison with attention-ranked selection, but the abstract mentions none. It also does not test an attention-ranked refresh set like Flash-Cache's.

Elastic-Cache uses the most-attended token's drift to decide when to refresh, and chooses a starting depth for where to refresh. It does not compare token-selection rules for which decoded tokens to refresh at a fixed budget.

Window-Diffusion reports that decoded tokens briefly change right after decoding and then stabilise. It uses windowed buffers that are refreshed periodically, but it does not compare attention-ranked with recency-ranked refresh sets by fidelity to full recomputation.

d2Cache selects which tokens get KV updates in two adaptive stages, as do similarity- or proxy-based methods such as dLLM-Cache, SPA-Cache and DyLLM. None of the abstracts I found reports a matched-budget comparison of attention vs recency vs random using KL to full recomputation.

opus.reason: I found no paper that compares attention-ranked and recency-ranked selection of decoded tokens to refresh in a dLLM KV cache at a matched budget, with a random baseline, using prediction-level KL to full recomputation. The seed paper only ablates the budget size. The nearby work points both ways: EntropyCache (2603.18489) and Window-Diffusion (2601.20332) support recency-based refresh, while Flash-Cache and MaskKV use attention-based selection. None of these, as far as I could tell, settles the head-to-head question. One caveat: I couldn't read EntropyCache's full text, so an unreported ablation there remains possible.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Flash-dLLM introduces attention-ranked selective KV refresh and varies the tracking budget, but does not compare attention, recency and random selection at a matched budget against full-recomputation predictions.

EntropyCache already recomputes the 64 most recently decoded tokens and studies recency-budget effects. Its comparisons with attention-based caching methods also change refresh schedules and other mechanisms, rather than isolating selection rules on a shared reference trajectory.

d2Cache selects prompt and decoded tokens for refresh using attention-rollout influence. It does not report a matched-budget attention-versus-recency comparison measuring prediction fidelity to full recomputation.

Polestar compares drift, most-attended-token cosine-change, uncertainty and random refresh selection on the same cached trajectory and budget, using identification of stale KV positions as its target. It does not compare received-attention ranking with recency ranking or measure their output-distribution fidelity.

sol.reason: Both attention-guided selective refresh and fixed-budget recency refresh were established before the cutoff, so those ingredients are not new. However, I found no paper that isolates their relative prediction fidelity at a matched refresh budget on the same full-recomputation trajectory; the closest controlled selection study, Polestar, tests different ranking signals and does not settle this comparison.

opus.reason: Both compare attention-based refresh selection with recency and random selection at a fixed budget, scoring next-window predictions against full recomputation with distributional divergence and argmax agreement rather than task accuracy.

sol.reason: Both compare attention-based, recency, and random selective KV refresh at a fixed budget, measuring prediction fidelity against full recomputation with an exact-reference control.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented independent attention-, recency-, and random-ranked selective-refresh shadow caches using downloaded LLaDA modules, true-position RoPE, explicit normalized attention scores, and a shared HF full-recomputation trajectory. Produces all registered outputs, pooled KL ratio, and problem-cluster bootstrap CI. Tested the default command: 60 problems, 4,524 steps; ratio 1.37833117, 95% CI [1.29239, 1.47181]. Necessary validation-control correction: all decoded plus M64 still leaves other masked representations stale and cannot exactly reproduce full recomputation. Preserved that registered query as all_decoded_diagnostic and used Q=all positions for the exact all validation floor. Primary policies, budgets, trajectory, and registered event remain unchanged. Maximum validation KL 4.79e-7 versus attended mean KL 0.07565. Details and source audit in IMPLEMENTATION.md and outputs.

departures: Validation control (experiment.py, IMPLEMENTATION.md, summary.json 'changes'): the registered 'all' policy (Q = M64 ∪ all decoded, shared persistent cache) was replaced by Q = all positions. The registered query is kept as 'all_decoded_diagnostic'. The engineer's reason is correct: masked positions outside M64 stay stale, so the registered query cannot reproduce the full forward (diagnostic KL 0.0049 versus 5e-8). This was reported. It does not touch the primary policies or the ratio, so it cannot change the result.
Extra validation (experiment.py): a full-logit check against the HF forward was added at problem 0, step 0. It is diagnostic only and cannot change the result.

Step 0 is included in the pooled means (experiment.py). At step 0 all three policies use Q = all and have identical near-zero KL. These rows add the same tiny amount to both numerator and denominator, so the ratio is effectively unchanged. The registration does not exclude step 0.
Per-step KL is clamped at 0 to remove log-softmax round-off (experiment.py metrics). The effect is negligible.
The model revision is pinned (08b83a6...) and the random seed is 1729. The registration leaves both open, so neither is a departure from it.

Score and commit-set details are computed as registered: float32 explicit attention weights, averaged over the masked query rows and heads and summed over layers, taken from the attended policy's own previous pass. Commit match compares positions and tokens. The bootstrap is a problem-cluster bootstrap of the pooled ratio. I found no departure here.
problems: Random selection, registered as the floor, is not one. Mean KL is 0.0808 for random, 0.0756 for attended and 0.1043 for recent. Recency is worse than random, and attention beats random by only about 7%. The registered event (recent/attended > 1.2) holds, but the attention rule shows only a small advantage over an uninformed baseline. This is an interpretive caveat, not a defect.

The evidence covers one model (LLaDA-8B-Instruct), one benchmark (60 GSM8K problems), one budget (64) and one reference trajectory. It measures prediction-level KL along the full-recompute trajectory, not shadow-driven generation, accuracy or throughput.
The CI is computed over only 60 problem clusters, and the steps within each problem are strongly autocorrelated. The problem-level bootstrap partly addresses this.

The full-refresh validation (summary.json 'all') covers only 15 steps (first 3 steps of the first 5 problems). It nonetheless shows the partial forward matches HF to KL ≤ 4.8e-7, with a max logit difference of 0.0625 at bf16.
opus.reason: The code implements the registered shadow-cache comparison closely: the HF full-forward trajectory, the W16/M64 windows, the EOS handling, the budget of 64 with automatic inclusion of D_{t-1}, and the explicit attention scores, recency ranking and seeded random ranking. The only change is to the validation control, which was disclosed, is correctly justified, and does not affect the statistic. The fresh-machine run reproduced the engineer's local value exactly (ratio 1.378, 95% CI [1.29, 1.47] over 60 problems and 4,524 steps). That value is computed from real model outputs, and the validation confirms the partial forward matches the HF forward to bf16 precision. The finding is credible and meaningful: recency-ranked refresh is clearly worse than attention-ranked refresh. However, random selection nearly matches attention, which tempers what the result says about the value of attention bookkeeping. The scope is a single model, a single benchmark and a single budget, measured by prediction-level fidelity only.

departures: experiment.py changes the control named 'all' from the registered Q = M64 union all decoded positions to Q = all sequence positions. The registered query is retained with an independent persistent cache as 'all_decoded_diagnostic'. This changes the control's reported KL and interpretation, but not the primary policies or registered ratio. The correction is technically justified because masked positions outside M64 otherwise remain stale.

experiment.py, metrics(), clamps numerically negative KL estimates to zero, whereas the registration specifies the KL expression without clipping. This can slightly change pooled values through floating-point roundoff, but is not plausibly consequential for the observed primary KL values or event.

experiment.py adds explicit failure thresholds: initial full-position validation KL above 0.001 aborts execution, and maximum validation KL exceeding 1% of the smallest primary-policy mean KL prevents result.json from being written. These operationalize the registered validation requirement but add numerical failure rules not explicitly registered. Neither triggered in the protected evaluation, so they did not exclude problems or change its reported value.
problems: The registration's verbal hypothesis and event threshold are not mathematically identical: KL_recent / KL_attended > 1.2 requires approximately 16.7% lower attended KL, not 20% lower KL relative to recency. The observed ratio implies approximately 27.4% lower KL, so this discrepancy does not reverse the finding.

outputs/summary.json reports the corrected all-position validation under 'all'; it must not be interpreted as showing that the registered all-decoded-plus-M64 control reproduces full recomputation. That retained diagnostic has mean KL approximately 0.00491.

Full-refresh validation is concentrated at initialization and the first three steps of five problems. Its very small KL supports numerical fidelity on those checks, but does not provide equally extensive validation of later selective-cache states.

The evidence concerns one model, the first 60 GSM8K test problems, and shadow predictions along a shared reference trajectory. Random selection is relatively close to attention selection, with no reported uncertainty for that comparison; the experiment does not establish a broadly necessary attention-selection advantage, autonomous decoding accuracy gains, or throughput benefits.
sol.reason: The protected evaluation completed 60 problems and 4,524 steps, and the supplied code computes the statistic from actual model predictions and GSM8K inputs rather than hard-coded results. The primary trajectory, refresh budgets, selection rules, prompts, and pooled statistic follow the registration; the disclosed control correction preserves the original diagnostic and does not change the primary comparison. The observed ratio is 1.3783 with a problem-bootstrap 95% interval of [1.2924, 1.4718], supporting the registered event, while full-position validation KL is negligible compared with primary-policy KL. This is a meaningful, credible finding about prediction fidelity, but its restricted scope and the relatively competitive random baseline limit broader practical conclusions.

departures: experiment.py (and outputs/summary.json changes) relabels the registered validation policy all (T = all decoded, Q = M64 union decoded on the first 3 steps of the first 5 problems) as all_decoded_diagnostic and reports all as a Q=all-positions refresh. Primary policies, budget, trajectory, statistic and event are unchanged, so this does not change the reported ratio; it does change the numbers labeled all.

registration.title: Is Flash-Verify's single-pass two-view conditional faithful to the exact sequential conditional it is defined as? A paired exact-shadow measurement on LLaDA-1.5
registration.seed_connection: Appendix C (Eq. 4) identifies the mask-view output at chain position k with the model's sequential conditional p(x^{i_k} | x_+, drafts i_1..i_{k-1}) and derives the per-token guarantee TV <= 1 - gamma (Theorem 1) from that identity. In a multi-layer bidirectional transformer the identity is exact only for k = 1: under the paper's verify mask the context rows never attend the draft view, so for k >= 2 every context representation the mask-view row reads was computed with the earlier drafts still masked, whereas the exact conditional encodes the context with those drafts committed. The paper states the identity without measuring the size of this approximation.
registration.hypothesis: Among search tokens accepted by the two-view chain after at least one committed draft (k >= 2), the fraction whose exact sequential-conditional probability of the committed token is below gamma - 0.1 = 0.7 exceeds the same fraction among accepted k = 1 tokens (exact up to kernel numerics) by more than 5 percentage points.
registration.contribution: First per-conditional, paired measurement of the leakage error of attention-mask-based self-verification in a full-bidirectional masked diffusion LLM, with a k = 1 control that isolates kernel numerics and a rejected-token group that shows whether the error is symmetric. It tests the premise of the seed's bounded-deviation theorem rather than downstream accuracy, and quantifies the magnitude (not just the existence) of near-threshold decision flips.

closest_work.difference: Spiffy acknowledges that blockwise verification masks leak information in full-bidirectional dLLMs and argues the drift is minimal, validating only downstream accuracy; here the per-conditional discrepancy is measured and attributed to chain depth.

SSD computes exact conditionals by a batched forward over full sequences and so never faces the approximation; that batched construction is used here only as the reference against which the two-view output is scored.
Elastic-Cache measures attention drift to decide cache refresh; it does not assess how a single-pass verification mask distorts the conditionals that verification accepts from.

inputs: Model: GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5 from the Hugging Face Hub (trust_remote_code=True, bfloat16); the Hub remote modeling code is used, not the seed repository's Triton-modified files
Data: openai/gsm8k, config 'main', test split (datasets library), first 60 problems
Read-only reference for the mask pattern: seed repository https://github.com/VILA-Lab/Flash-dLLM, file llada/generate.py (causal_mask construction in the verify branch)
pip: torch (CUDA), transformers==4.49.0, datasets, accelerate, hf_transfer (set HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER=1)
registration.method:
SETUP. pip install torch transformers==4.49.0 datasets accelerate hf_transfer; export HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER=1. tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5', trust_remote_code=True); model = AutoModel.from_pretrained('GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5', trust_remote_code=True, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).cuda().eval() (if LLaDA-1.5 cannot be loaded, use GSAI-ML/LLaDA-8B-Instruct, same architecture and tokenizer, and record it). MASK_ID = tok.convert_tokens_to_ids('<|mdm_mask|>') (expected 126336); STOP_IDS = {tok.eos_token_id, tok.convert_tokens_to_ids('<|eot_id|>')} (expected 126081 and 126348). Every forward runs under torch.no_grad() as logits = model(input_ids=..., attention_bias=...).logits (omit attention_bias for a plain forward; never pass attention_mask, which the remote code converts into a causal bias); softmax in float32. No KV cache anywhere; batch size 1 except the shadow batch below.

CUSTOM ROPE POSITIONS. ROT = the class of the first module in model.modules() whose class name is 'RotaryEmbedding'. Define a module-level global POS_IDS (None, or a LongTensor of length T on the GPU) and replace ROT.forward with a function reproducing the original (read it in the downloaded modeling file) except that positions come from POS_IDS: q_, k_ = (q.float(), k.float()) if self.config.rope_full_precision else (q, k); inside torch.autocast(q.device.type, enabled=False): T = k_.shape[-2]; pos = POS_IDS if POS_IDS is not None else torch.arange(T, device=q.device); pos_sin, pos_cos = self.get_rotary_embedding(int(pos.max()) + 1, q_.device); ps = pos_sin[:, :, pos, :].type_as(q_); pc = pos_cos[:, :, pos, :].type_as(q_); q_ = self.apply_rotary_pos_emb(ps, pc, q_); k_ = self.apply_rotary_pos_emb(ps, pc, k_); return q_.type_as(q), k_.type_as(k). Query and key lengths are always equal here. POS_IDS must be None whenever a batch is passed.

CUSTOM ATTENTION MASK. attention_bias is a bool tensor of shape (1, 1, T, T), True = the query row may attend the key column (the remote code converts False into a large negative additive bias). If the bool path misbehaves, pass float32 with 0 for allowed and torch.finfo(torch.float32).min for disallowed.

SANITY GATES (written to outputs/sanity.json; if any fails, stop and declare the run invalid). A: with POS_IDS = None the logits of one prompt are identical before and after patching (argmax identical at every position, max |delta| < 1e-3). B: an all-True bias reproduces the no-bias logits (argmax identical at >= 99.5% of positions, mean |delta logit| < 0.1). C: defined in step (e) below.

PROMPT AND SEQUENCE. content = the question, a newline, then 'Please reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}.'; prompt = tok.apply_chat_template([{'role': 'user', 'content': content}], add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=False) (if there is no chat template use '<|startoftext|><|start_header_id|>user<|end_header_id|>', two newlines, content, '<|eot_id|><|start_header_id|>assistant<|end_header_id|>', two newlines); ids = tok(prompt)['input_ids'] (drop one of two identical leading BOS ids). x = ids (length P) followed by G = 256 MASK_ID tokens; L = P + G. limit = L - 1; whenever a STOP token is committed at position e, limit = min(limit, e); masked positions > limit are never decoded; a problem ends when no MASK remains at positions <= limit. W = the 64 leftmost masked positions <= limit (beta_m = 64 as in the paper). eps = 0.9, gamma = 0.8, K_max = 8.

TRAJECTORY (paper's two-pass Flash-Verify with the per-token prefix rule). Each step: (a) DRAFT PASS: plain forward on x (no bias, POS_IDS = None); for every masked p <= limit: c_p = max softmax, xhat_p = argmax. D = {p in W : c_p >= eps}, or the single p in W with the largest c_p if empty; commit xhat at D, giving x'; update limit. S = the remaining positions of W (still <= limit) sorted by c_p descending, truncated to K = min(8, |.|); chain order i_1..i_K. If K = 0 the step ends. (b) VERIFY PASS (two-view): tokens = x' ++ [xhat_{i_1}, ..., xhat_{i_K}] (draft view at rows L..L+K-1); POS_IDS = [0..L-1] ++ [i_1..i_K]; bias of size T = L+K: a context row r (r < L, r not in S) attends every column < L and no draft column; the mask-view row i_k attends every context column, the mask-view columns i_j for j >= k and the draft columns L+j-1 for j < k; the draft-view row L+j-1 attends every context column, the draft columns L+j'-1 for j' <= j and the mask-view columns i_j' for j' > j (this mirrors the seed repository's causal_mask). Mask-view output at row i_k: ptilde_k = softmax(logits[i_k]), ctilde_k = max, xtilde_k = argmax. mtilde = length of the longest chain prefix with xhat_{i_k} == xtilde_k and ctilde_k >= gamma; commit xhat at i_1..i_{mtilde} in chain order; update limit. (c) EXACT SHADOW (does not affect the trajectory): a batch of K sequences, sequence k = x' with xhat filled at i_1..i_{k-1} and MASK kept at i_k..i_K and at every other masked position; one plain batched forward (no bias, POS_IDS = None). pstar_k = softmax(row i_k of sequence k), cstar_k = max, xstar_k = argmax; from sequence 1 also q'_j = softmax(row i_j) for every j (the marginal with D committed). mstar = longest chain prefix with xhat_{i_k} == xstar_k and cstar_k >= gamma. (d) LOG one line per (step, k) to outputs/positions.jsonl: problem, step, k, K, i_k, xhat, c (draft pass), xtilde, ctilde, ptilde_at_xhat = ptilde_k[xhat], xstar, cstar, pstar_at_xhat = pstar_k[xhat], tv_two_exact = 0.5*sum|ptilde_k - pstar_k|, tv_marg_exact = 0.5*sum|q'_k - pstar_k|, accepted = (k <= mtilde), acc_two_pos = (xhat == xtilde and ctilde >= gamma), acc_exact_pos = (xhat == xstar and cstar >= gamma). One line per verify step to outputs/steps.jsonl: problem, step, K, |D|, mtilde, mstar. (e) SANITY C: for every verify step of the first 3 problems, tv_k1 = 0.5*sum|ptilde_1 - pstar_1| must be < 0.03 (the k = 1 mask-view row attends no row that can see a draft, so it must equal sequence 1's row i_1 up to kernel numerics); store all values in outputs/sanity.json.

TERMINATION, ACCURACY, TIME. Generated text = tokens P..limit-1 decoded with skip_special_tokens=True; answer = content of the last \boxed{...}, else the last number in the text; gold = the text after '####' with commas removed; correct iff numerically equal. outputs/problems.jsonl: problem id, correct, steps, forwards (draft + verify only), valid tokens (limit - P if a STOP was committed, else 256). Stop starting new problems once 18 minutes of decoding have elapsed since the first forward or 27 minutes since the script started, whichever is first; at least 30 problems must complete, otherwise report the run as invalid.

SUMMARY (outputs/summary.json): the registered statistic with its components and Wilson 95% CIs of V1 and V2; by k and by group (accepted / rejected): mean signed gap ptilde_at_xhat - pstar_at_xhat, fraction with |gap| > 0.1, fractions with pstar_at_xhat < 0.8 and < 0.7, mean tv_two_exact, mean tv_marg_exact, argmax disagreement rate (xtilde != xstar); decision level: fraction of verify steps with mtilde != mstar, mean(mtilde - mstar), fractions with mtilde > mstar and mtilde < mstar; among rejected positions with k >= 2, the fraction with acc_exact_pos true; accuracy, tokens/step and tokens/forward of the trajectory; model actually used.

event.description: Accepted chain-verified tokens at k >= 2 violate the gamma-bound by more than 0.1 under the exact sequential conditional at least 5 percentage points more often than accepted k = 1 tokens do
event.statistic: V2 - V1, where V2 = fraction of positions accepted by the two-view prefix rule with chain index k >= 2 whose exact conditional probability of the committed draft, pstar_k(xhat_{i_k}), is below 0.7, and V1 = the same fraction over accepted positions with k = 1

evaluation.procedure: From outputs/positions.jsonl (one line per verify step and chain position with the two-view and exact distributions' summaries and decisions) select accepted positions, split by k = 1 versus k >= 2, and compute V1, V2 and V2 - V1. outputs/steps.jsonl holds per-verify-step accepted prefix lengths under both rules; outputs/problems.jsonl holds per-problem accuracy and counts; outputs/sanity.json holds gates A, B and C (the run is invalid if any fails); outputs/summary.json holds the statistic and all secondary aggregates.
evaluation.controls: Paired design: the exact reference is computed on the same drafts and the same state as the two-view pass, so the only difference is the attention-mask approximation. Accepted k = 1 tokens are the control (no draft in their context, so their gap isolates kernel numerics, calibrated by Sanity C); rejected k >= 2 tokens show whether exact conditionals would have accepted tokens the two-view pass rejected; tv_marg_exact gives the scale of the conditioning effect the mask is supposed to capture.

registration.full_scale_study: If the event occurs: implement exact-but-cheap verification variants inside the cached Flash-dLLM pipeline (recompute the tracked context queries with drafts filled in, or SSD-style batched exact verification sharing the KV cache), measure their throughput and accuracy against the two-view pass on GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval and MBPP at batch 32, and restate the guarantee with the measured deviation. If it does not occur: the Eq. 4 identity is empirically adequate and investment should go to acceptance-rule design rather than mask fidelity.

agent.reason: The k=1 control should be near zero and the two-view error for k>=2 is probably modest because drafts still enter the mask-view row directly through attention; accepted tokens with mask-view confidence in [0.8,0.9] are the main source of violations and I expect the margin-0.1 violation rate to land near, and more often below, the 5-point bar. Plumbing failures (RoPE patch, bias, batched shadow) further reduce the chance of a valid positive.

judge_astra.reason: Conditional mismatch is plausible, but errors exceeding 0.1 in more than 5% of accepted later tokens are a substantially stronger claim. Also, k=1 can receive draft information indirectly through later mask rows in a multilayer transformer, so the registered sanity gate is not guaranteed to pass.

judge_fable.reason: The design assumes the k=1 mask-view row is exact, but under the registered mask later mask-view rows attend earlier draft columns, so k=1 is indirectly self-conditioned and the strict Sanity C (TV<0.03 on every verify step of 3 problems, across bf16 kernel/batch differences) has a good chance of invalidating the run; even if valid, V2-V1 exceeding 5 points is roughly a coin flip since staleness effects may partially cancel self-leak inflation.

judge_opus.reason: Gate C requires TV < 0.03 at every verify step of 3 problems (about 120 steps), and draft leakage through other mask-view and context rows makes this very likely to fail. The registration says to stop and declare the run invalid in that case. Even if the statistic is computed, leakage is strongest at k = 1, so V1 is probably at least as large as V2.

judge_sol.reason: Multi-layer bidirectional updates make the exact-conditional identity doubtful, but the event requires substantial overconfidence among an already filtered accepted prefix, not merely any discrepancy. The strict k=1 sanity gate could also fail because indirect draft influence can travel through later mask-view rows.

judge_luna.reason: The k=1 control should closely match the exact conditional, while for k≥2 the two-view mask leaves shared context representations based on the all-masked state; recomputing them with earlier drafts filled could lower exact token probabilities for some accepted tokens. The 5-point excess is plausible, though confidence-based selection may limit how often the exact probability falls below 0.7.

judge_muse.reason: Accepted k=1 controls numerics with V1 near 0, while k>=2 uses stale context; exact conditionals with committed drafts likely stay >=0.7 when two-view is >=0.8, so a >5pp excess violation rate is possible but unlikely.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed paper's Appendix C says the mask-view output is exactly the sequential conditional (Eq. 4) and derives Theorem 1 from that. It reports only accuracy and throughput. It never compares mask-view outputs with exact conditionals, so the experiment tests a premise the paper assumes but does not check.

Spiffy is a speculative decoder for dLLMs that claims to preserve the output distribution. It is evaluated on downstream speed and accuracy. I found no paired, per-conditional comparison of attention-mask verification outputs with exact batched-forward conditionals, split by chain depth.

SimSD designs a reference-token attention mask that it says produces 'valid logits' for drafts in one pass. It tests this only through throughput and benchmark quality on SDAR models, not by measuring how far the outputs deviate from exact conditionals.

SSD verifies drafts in one pass using hierarchical verification trees and reports output identical to stepwise decoding, measured at the level of final outputs. The experiment uses a batched exact forward only as its reference. SSD does not measure leakage error in a two-view mask.

This paper gives an information-theoretic analysis of parallelization bias and verification cost in masked diffusion models. It does not study how attention-mask approximations used for single-pass self-verification distort the conditionals.

opus.reason: I found no paper, as of 2026-10-07, that compares single-pass two-view or verify-mask outputs in a bidirectional dLLM against the exact sequential conditionals they stand in for, and none that splits the error by chain depth with k = 1 as a control. The seed paper treats the identity as exact without measuring it. Related self-verification methods (Spiffy, SSD, SimSD) report only end-to-end accuracy and speed, so the question appears open.

sol.label: close variant

closest_work.difference: SimSD, Section 4.3, already compares sequential-denoising distributions against single-pass paired data/mask verification, reporting KL divergence, cross-entropy loss and top-1 agreement by verification step. The proposed experiment uses full-bidirectional LLaDA and Flash-Verify, focusing on accepted-token gamma-bound violations and adding first-position and rejected-token controls.

Spiffy explicitly identifies indirect information leakage through shared context representations, but evaluates its impact through downstream accuracy rather than paired conditional-distribution measurements.
SSD evaluates complete sequence states in a verification batch, providing the reference construction used here; it does not audit the two-view attention-mask approximation.
The seed identifies mask-view outputs with sequential conditionals and derives the gamma-bound, but does not report the proposed exact-shadow comparison.

sol.reason: SimSD already investigates the central conditional-fidelity question using essentially the same two-view masking construction, explicitly attributing discrepancies to higher-order hidden-state interactions and measuring their growth across verification steps. The registered experiment adds a targeted audit of Flash-Verify's bound and acceptance-conditioned statistics, but its model, metrics and controls make it a close variant of that prior distribution-level experiment rather than the first such measurement.

opus.reason: Both build a no-cache two-view verify pass with duplicated position ids and compare each search rank's mask-view distribution to an exact full forward with the earlier drafts filled in, reporting TV, argmax agreement, accept/reject flips and accepted-prefix length.

sol.reason: Both compare no-cache two-view verification against separate exact sequential recomputation on identical states, measuring rank-dependent distribution discrepancies, acceptance flips, and accepted-prefix lengths.
