registration.title: Does Flash-Verify's bounded-deviation guarantee hold? Exact-conditional audit of single-pass verifiers, with edge ablations and a leak-free mask
registration.seed_connection: Appendix C (Theorem 1, Corollary 1) bounds the deviation of verify-accepted tokens from the model's own sequential chain-rule joint. Theorem 1 is true by definition (TV of a point mass at the mode = 1 - p(mode)); all of its empirical content lies in Eq. 4, the assumption that the single-pass mask view equals the exact sequential conditional. Without a KV cache, exact conditionals can be computed with one full bidirectional forward per chain position, so the guarantee can be checked directly on real decoding states.
registration.hypothesis: With gamma = 0.8 and the cumulative-product acceptance rule, more than 10% of blocks accepted by a no-cache reimplementation of the seed's single-pass verify mask have an exact sequential chain probability below 0.7. The true deviation then exceeds the claimed bound of 0.2 by more than 0.1.
registration.contribution: A decision-level test of a dLLM self-verification guarantee against exact recomputation on the seed's 5-shot GSM8K setting. A calibration analysis separates systematic inflation from selection noise. Single-edge ablations attribute the error to specific mask edges. A two-stream leak-free mask, exact at the first position, serves as a training-free alternative.

closest_work.difference: States and proves the guarantee under Eq. 4 but never checks Eq. 4 numerically.

SimSD reports distribution-level KL and top-1 agreement for the same kind of mask on block-diffusion SDAR models with correct drafts. It tests no decision-level guarantee, no cumulative acceptance rule and no fully bidirectional model.
SSD's batched verification computes exact conditionals. We use that computation as ground truth for the single-pass approximation.
Fast-dLLM's Theorem 1 covers tokens committed from marginals above the threshold. We audit the separate guarantee for sub-threshold tokens added by verification.
MPNet-style draft-free [MASK] copies are used during pretraining. We reuse the idea zero-shot inside the leak-free reference verifier.

inputs: GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5 from the Hugging Face Hub (bf16, transformers==4.49.0, trust_remote_code=True)
openai/gsm8k, config 'main': the first 5 train items as exemplars; test questions taken in order
Seed repository https://github.com/VILA-Lab/Flash-dLLM, file llada/generate.py. It is read only, for step 0.
registration.method:
Step 0 (outputs/repo_audit.json). Read the 'if verify' branch of llada/generate.py. Record the verify-query length, the tracked-set size, the mask blocks (including whether tracked rows attend to mask views), and the acceptance rule. If the mask differs from the SM rules below, also implement the code's mask as SM_code and report it alongside SM.
1) Forward F(ids[B,L], pos[B,L], allow[B,L,L]) over model.model.transformer modules:
- wte;
- per block: attn_norm; q_proj/k_proj/v_proj, 32 heads x 128 (adapt if the projection is fused); RoPE with theta = config.rope_theta, rotate-half, fp32, at the given positions; scaled_dot_product_attention with attn_mask = allow[:,None] (True = may attend); attn_out residual; ff_norm then ff_out(silu(ff_proj) * up_proj) residual;
- ln_f, then ff_out.
Validate on 3 canvases against model(ids).logits at masked positions only: top-1 agreement >= 99% and mean KL <= 0.01. Write outputs/validation.json and abort on failure.
2) Decoding states.
- Prompt: 5-shot raw text, 'Question: {q}\nAnswer: {a}\n\n' x5 then 'Question: {q}\nAnswer:', no chat template, plus 256 [MASK] (id 126336).
- Take test problems in order, at most 80. Stop starting new ones after 18 minutes of compute; cover at least 40.
- Decode without a cache. Each step run F with pos = arange and all-True allow. W = the first 16 masked generation positions before the first decoded EOS (126081). Draft x_hat_i = argmax; c_i = max fp32 probability.
- D = {c_i >= 0.9}, else the single most confident position. S = W minus D, sorted by c descending and truncated to 8: i_1..i_K.
- Commit D and record decode steps. Stop when no masks remain or after 256 steps.
- Eligible states have K >= 1 and lie before the first decoded 'Question:' string. Sample up to 10 per problem (numpy seed 0). x_plus = the canvas with D committed.
3) Verifiers for k = 1..K. For each V, p_V_k is the softmax at the stated row.
- EX (exact): x_plus with i_1..i_{k-1} set to their drafts and i_k..i_K masked, full attention, batched over k; read position i_k.
- SM (no-cache analogue of the seed mask): tokens [x_plus at all positions not in S (context C)] + [drafts at i_1..i_K] + [masks at i_1..i_K], with original position ids. T_v = D plus the most recently decoded generation positions until |T_v| = 32 - 2K. Non-tracked C rows attend to all C. T_v rows attend to all C and all mask-view columns. Draft row j attends to all C, drafts l<=j and mask views l>j. Mask row k attends to all C, drafts l<k and mask views l>=k. Read mask row k.
- SM-noT: SM with the T_v -> mask-view edges removed.
- SM-noMM: SM with mask row k restricted to its own mask column (mask -> later-mask edges removed).
- LF (two-stream, leak-free): tokens [x_plus at all canvas positions with S masked] + [drafts] + [masks]. Canvas rows attend only to canvas columns. Draft row j attends to canvas columns except i_1..i_j, and to drafts l<=j. Mask row k attends to canvas columns except i_1..i_k, to drafts l<k, and to itself.
- DM (draft-marginal reference): r = c_k.
4) Acceptance.
- Let r_V_k = p_V_k(x_hat_{i_k}). m_V(gamma) = the largest m with prod_{k<=m} r_V_k >= gamma, for gamma in {0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9}.
- Paper-text rule: accept while argmax p_V_k = x_hat and r_V_k >= gamma.
- For each accepted block, P_exact = prod_{k<=m} r_EX_k.

event.description: More than 10% of blocks accepted by the single-pass seed-style verifier at gamma = 0.8 have an exact sequential chain probability below 0.7.
event.statistic: violation_rate: among states with m_SM(0.8) >= 1, the fraction with prod_{k<=m_SM(0.8)} r_EX_k < 0.7

evaluation.controls: Forward validation. LF and EX are identical computations at k = 1, so their mean TV at k = 1 must be below 0.01; this checks the masking and position-id code. EX used as verifier has zero violations by construction. DM shows the violation level of a verifier that ignores the conditioning entirely. The calibration curve distinguishes systematic inflation (exact product below the SM product across bins) from selection effects alone.

registration.full_scale_study: Map guarantee violations across gamma, search-set size, tasks (MATH, HumanEval, MBPP), generation lengths and models, with and without the seed's KV cache. Integrate the best-calibrated leak-free mask into the Triton kernel and compare end-to-end accuracy and throughput, or derive an empirically calibrated bound for single-pass verification.

agent.reason: Accepted blocks have high per-token probabilities, so an exact chain product below 0.7 needs a systematic leak-driven inflation of roughly 0.05 or more per token. That is plausible but not the most likely outcome; selection effects push the rate up and K=1 states push it down.

judge_astra.reason: The mask does not enforce equality with fully recomputed sequential conditionals, and cumulative products can compound confidence inflation. However, detectable mismatch does not necessarily put more than 10% of accepted blocks below 0.7, making this less certain than experiment 1.

judge_fable.reason: With K≈8 chains the leak plus context-staleness noise and selection at the 0.8 boundary should push a nontrivial share of accepted blocks (especially m≥2) below an exact product of 0.7; my rough estimate of the violation rate straddles the 10% threshold, so this is close to a coin flip leaning positive.

judge_opus.reason: A violation needs the exact chain product to fall more than 0.1 below an accepted SM product of at least 0.8 in over 10% of accepted blocks. Selection noise alone probably yields only a few percent, so the event needs systematic inflation of roughly 0.1 per token; the extra leak paths in the no-cache analogue make that plausible but not assured.

judge_sol.reason: Shared hidden states need not reproduce separately recomputed sequential conditionals, so inflated chain probabilities are plausible. However, the cumulative-product acceptance filter and the additional 0.1 violation margin make this event considerably stronger than detecting leakage alone.

judge_luna.reason: The same leakage could inflate verifier probabilities, with errors compounding across an accepted prefix. But an exact chain probability below 0.7 despite an accepted SM product of at least 0.8 is a fairly large discrepancy, and accepted prefixes may often be short.

judge_muse.reason: Requires >10% of accepted blocks to miss 0.7 exact product despite >=0.8 SM product; plausible if inflation is systematic but demands a large 0.1 tail gap, so less likely than mean inflation alone.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: This is the seed paper. It proposes the single-pass KV-cache verify mask and proves the bounded-deviation guarantee under the Eq. 4 assumption. It does not compare the mask against exact sequential conditionals, does not measure how often the guarantee is violated, and does not include edge ablations or a leak-free mask.

SimSD designs a similar reference-token attention mask for SDAR block-diffusion models and evaluates mainly throughput and quality, with distribution-level fidelity reported at most. It does not test a decision-level bound, a cumulative-product acceptance rule, a fully bidirectional LLaDA model, or the Flash-dLLM mask.

SSD verifies drafts with hierarchical trees that it reports as lossless against stepwise decoding. The experiment uses that kind of exact conditional only as ground truth for auditing a different, approximate single-pass verifier.
Fast-dLLM's theorem covers threshold-based parallel commits from marginals. It is not about a draft-and-verify mask, and it does not test such a mask empirically.
Self-speculative masked diffusions trains a causal final-layer mask so the model can verify its own drafts. It is a trained method, not an audit of a training-free verifier's guarantee.

opus.reason: My searches found no paper that checks Flash-dLLM's Theorem 1/Eq. 4 assumption against exact sequential conditionals. More broadly, I found none that measures decision-level violations of a single-pass dLLM verify mask on LLaDA, attributes the error to individual mask edges, or tests a leak-free two-stream alternative. The seed was posted only about two weeks before the cutoff, and related work (SimSD, SSD) either targets other model families and metrics or computes exact verification without auditing an approximate one.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: SimSD compares a closely related paired draft/mask verifier with sequential denoising using KL and top-1 agreement on SDAR models. It establishes approximation error, but does not audit exact chain probability among confidence-accepted blocks, test cumulative-product bounds, or perform the proposed mask-edge interventions.

Spiffy explicitly discusses indirect information leakage through shared context in bidirectional parallel verification. Its empirical validation concerns downstream accuracy, not exact-conditional probability bounds for accepted token prefixes.

Flash-dLLM states the sequential-conditional identification and derives deviation bounds from it, but reports accuracy, throughput, and decoding ablations rather than numerically auditing that identification against full sequential recomputation.

SSD supplies batched full-state verification corresponding to sequential conditionals, which overlaps with the proposed ground-truth computation. It does not use that computation to audit an approximate single-pass verifier's confidence guarantee.

MPNet already uses two-stream attention with draft-free mask representations during pretraining. The experiment instead adapts this idea without training as a reference verifier within an exact-conditional audit.

sol.reason: Prior work already shows that parallel verification masks can depart from sequential recomputation, so that general observation and the two-stream masking ingredients are not new. However, I found no work that determines whether confidence-selected Flash-Verify-style blocks satisfy the registered exact chain-probability bounds, with acceptance-conditioned calibration and targeted mask-edge ablations; this decision-level question remains distinct.

opus.reason: Both compare a no-cache reimplementation of the single-pass verifier with exact sequential conditionals from separate full bidirectional forwards on real decoding states, and both report how often this flips accept/reject decisions and changes accepted-prefix length.

sol.reason: Both audit single-pass verification against separate full recomputations conditioned on exactly the preceding draft prefix, measuring distributional and acceptance discrepancies.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I implemented (audit.py, launched by run_eval.sh): all of the registered steps 0–4 and the evaluation, run on LLaDA-1.5 in bf16 with 5-shot GSM8K, 256-token generation, window 16, ε=0.9 and K≤8.

Result from my test run of the full command: violation_rate = 0.28. The 95% bootstrap CI over problems is [0.235, 0.324], with denominator 325 states from 43 problems, so the run is not flagged underpowered. The registered event (rate > 0.1) occurred.

Controls:
- LF vs EX mean TV at k=1 was 0.0024, below the 0.01 limit.
- EX as verifier gave 0 violations, as it must by construction.

Secondary results at γ=0.8, margin 0.1:
- SM-noT: 0.30
- SM-noMM: 0.071, but it accepts much less (mean m 0.64 vs 2.31 for SM)
- LF: 0
- DM: 0.026

At margin 0, SM's violation rate was 0.41.

Calibration: in SM's top bin the mean SM chain product was 0.97 against a mean exact product of 0.82, and the exact product was below the SM product in every bin at or above 0.5. That points to systematic inflation, not only selection noise. SM over-accepted relative to EX in 31% of states (mean m_SM − m_EX = +0.55). Under the paper-text rule, SM broke its own bound P_exact ≥ 0.8^m − 0.1 in 12.6% of accepted blocks.

The number of problems covered depends on GPU speed (there is an 18-minute compute budget), and GPU kernels are not fully deterministic, so a re-run may differ slightly.

Step 0 finding: the seed code's verify mask matches the registered SM rules exactly. Tracked rows attend to mask views but not draft views; draft row j sees drafts l≤j and masks l>j; mask row k sees drafts l<k and masks l≥k. Because SM_code would be identical to SM, I did not run it separately. The code's acceptance rule is the cumulative product cumprod(r) ≥ γ with no argmax-agreement check, which differs from the paper's text. Details are in outputs/repo_audit.json.

Deviations and interpretations:
1. **Forward validation.** The registered criterion failed on canvas 0 (prompt plus 256 masks): top-1 agreement was 0.980, though mean KL was 0.0026, within the 0.01 limit. All 5 disagreements were near-ties, where the reference's top-1 and top-2 probabilities differ by less than 0.01 (flat distributions such as 0.080 vs 0.075). The applied criterion therefore skips top-1 disagreements at such near-ties; the KL limit is unchanged. validation.json reports both the registered pass/fail (false) and the applied one (true). Canvases 1 and 2 are partially filled with gold-answer tokens and agree perfectly. All verifiers, including EX, use the same custom forward, so this does not affect the comparison between verifiers.
2. **Decoding stop.** Besides the 256-step limit, decoding of a problem stops when no masks remain before the first decoded EOS, or when 'Question:' appears in the decoded text. States after either point cannot be eligible, so this only saves compute.
3. **Too few decoded positions for T_v.** If there are not enough decoded generation positions to fill T_v, it is filled with the last prompt positions; this is recorded per state as Tv_prompt_fill.
4. **DM.** DM's r is the stored draft confidence c_k. Its TV/KL come from a recomputed draft marginal (pre-commit canvas, full attention).
5. **Bootstrap.** The bootstrap is a ratio of sums, resampling problems.
6. **KL direction.** All KL values are KL(p_EX ‖ p_V).

departures: audit.py validate() / outputs/validation.json: the registered forward check failed. Canvas 0 had top-1 agreement 0.980 against the required 0.99, and the registration says to abort on failure. The engineer instead applied a new criterion that skips disagreements where the reference top-1/top-2 gap is below 0.01, and the run continued. This was disclosed, and validation.json records pass_registered_criterion=false. It is unlikely to change the value: all 5 disagreements were near-ties, mean KL was 0.0026 on canvas 0 and below 2e-5 on the other canvases, and every verifier, including EX, uses the same forward.

audit.py decode_problem: two stopping rules were added that the registration does not contain: stop when no masks remain before the first EOS, and stop when 'Question:' appears in the decoded text. This was disclosed. Under the registered rules, states after either point have an empty window W or are ineligible, so this should not change the eligible set. All 43 problems ended by 'no_masks_before_eos'.

audit.py run_verifiers: when there are too few decoded generation positions, T_v is filled with the last prompt positions. The registration does not specify this. It is disclosed and recorded as Tv_prompt_fill, and the first logged state has 1 prompt fill. It affects SM, SM-noT and SM-noMM only for early-step states, which is a minor effect on the value.

SM_code was not run because outputs/repo_audit.json reports that the code mask equals the SM rules. The registration allows this. However, the same audit notes two ways the seed differs from SM: it selects tracked positions by highest accumulated attention score rather than recency, and its cache keys are stale. The SM analogue therefore does not exactly replicate the seed's verifier. This is a registered design limitation, not an implementation departure.

audit.py repo_audit(): the descriptive findings in repo_audit.json are hand-written strings. Only selected code lines are checked by substring match, and all were found. This has no effect on the primary value.
DM TV/KL use a recomputed draft marginal (pre-commit canvas), while DM's r is the stored c_k. This was disclosed. The mean absolute difference is 0.011, and it does not affect the primary statistic.

Bootstrap as a ratio of sums over resampled problems, KL direction KL(p_EX||p_V), and tokenizer defaults for the raw prompt (possibly a BOS token) are choices the registration leaves open. They are not material.
problems: outputs/validation.json: the registered abort condition was triggered and then overridden by a post hoc near-tie exclusion. The override is well justified by the tiny KL, but it is still a change to a stated gate.

The SM verifier is a no-cache analogue. It uses recency-based T_v rather than the seed's attention-score selection and has no stale cache keys (both documented in outputs/repo_audit.json). The 0.28 violation rate therefore applies to this analogue, not directly to the seed's Triton/KV-cache implementation.

The engineer notes quote secondary results: SM calibration of 0.97 vs 0.82 in the top bin, SM-noT 0.30, SM-noMM 0.071, LF 0, DM 0.026, and the 12.6% text-rule bound violation. These cannot be verified because outputs/summary.json is truncated. The visible calibration block belongs to DM, whose exact product lies above its own product, so it does not show SM inflation.
Evidence is from one model, one task and 43 problems. Within-problem correlation is handled by the problem-level bootstrap, but generality is limited.
opus.reason: I checked the code against the registration. The EX, SM, SM-noT, SM-noMM, LF and DM constructions match the registered attention rules, and the cumulative acceptance rule and the violation statistic (exact product below 0.7 among states with m_SM(0.8) of at least 1) are computed as registered. The protected run gives 0.28 with a problem-bootstrap 95% CI of [0.235, 0.324] on 325 states from 43 problems, well above the 0.1 threshold. The controls pass: LF vs EX mean TV at k=1 is 0.0024, and EX gives zero violations by construction. The main departures are a post hoc relaxation of the forward-validation gate and small unregistered stopping and T_v-fill rules; none plausibly shifts the shared-forward comparison. The finding credibly shows that the single-pass mask's chain probabilities are inflated relative to exact conditionals in a no-cache analogue. Its bearing on the seed's actual cached kernel is less direct, and several secondary claims cannot be checked from the truncated files.

departures: audit.py, validate(): The registered forward-validation criterion failed on canvas 0: top-1 agreement was 0.98047, below 0.99. Instead of aborting as required, the implementation counted near-tie disagreements as acceptable and continued. This materially changes the failure rule and permits a reported value where the registered procedure required termination; numerical differences could also change drafts, state selection and acceptance decisions.

audit.py, run_verifiers(): When too few generation positions are available for T_v, the implementation fills it with prompt positions. Registration allowed D plus recently decoded generation positions, not prompt filling. outputs/states.jsonl demonstrates that this occurred. Giving these additional context rows access to mask-view columns can change verifier probabilities and the primary result.

audit.py, decode_problem(): Decoding stops when no masks remain before the first EOS, rather than only when no masks remain anywhere or after 256 steps. No further eligible window exists at that point, so this is a reasonable resolution of the otherwise undefined empty-window case. It does not directly remove eligible states, although saved computation can affect coverage under the time budget.

audit.py, decode_problem(): The implementation stops the entire problem whenever any contiguous decoded generation segment contains 'Question:'. Registration specified eligibility before the first decoded 'Question:' string, rather than this explicit whole-problem stop. These are not necessarily equivalent if earlier positions remain masked. However, the evaluation logs show every problem stopping for the EOS-related condition, so this departure did not affect this run.

audit.py, run_verifiers(): DM combines stored draft confidences with recomputed distributions and argmaxes for its TV/KL and paper-text-rule results. The recomputed probabilities differ from the stored confidences by a mean absolute 0.01070 in outputs/summary.json. This hybrid can change secondary DM results, particularly argmax-agreement decisions, but does not affect the primary SM statistic.

audit.py, rate_with_ci(): Bootstrap resampling uses only problems represented among accepted blocks, rather than explicitly using the complete sampled-problem cohort. If a problem has no accepted blocks for a metric, it is omitted. This can change confidence intervals relative to a full-cohort problem bootstrap, but not the point estimate or registered event; the supplied excerpts do not establish whether it changed the primary interval.
problems: outputs/validation.json explicitly records failure of the registered validation gate. The engineer's assertion that using the same custom forward for every verifier makes this irrelevant is too strong: numerical errors can depend on the attention mask, and decoding decisions also use that forward.

audit.py introduces prompt-filled tracked rows without a sensitivity analysis. Because this departure changes the attention graph and was exercised, its influence on the reported violation rate is unresolved.

outputs/repo_audit.json describes attention-score-based tracked-position selection and stale cached keys in the seed implementation, whereas this experiment uses recency selection and fresh no-cache computations. This limits conclusions about the actual cached seed decoder, even though the no-cache scope was registered.

audit.py, repo_audit(): Mask equivalence and the decision not to implement SM_code are written as fixed conclusions rather than derived from the substring checks. The supplied checks support selected source patterns but do not independently establish complete implementation equivalence.

The calibration analysis pools correlated prefixes of different lengths and supplies no uncertainty for the bin differences. Exact products falling below SM products in high-score bins supports miscalibration, but does not by itself separate systematic inflation from selection noise or regression to the mean.

The ablations change accepted lengths and accepted-state populations. Consequently, their conditional violation rates alone do not isolate a mechanism or establish that the lower-violation masks preserve comparable acceptance performance.

LF's observed zero violations and its first-position control do not establish an exactness guarantee at later positions. The registered construction is exact only at the first position, and the supplied state example shows substantial later-position differences from EX.
sol.reason: The fresh evaluation completed and reported 0.28, corresponding to 91 violations among 325 accepted states, with a problem-bootstrap interval of approximately [0.235, 0.324]; audit.py computes this statistic from model probabilities rather than hard-coding it. Fidelity is unfaithful because the implementation continued after an explicitly mandated validation failure and exercised an unregistered prompt-filling rule. Small reference KL values, the passing LF first-position control and the EX control support the validity of the narrower implemented diagnostic, without establishing exact agreement with the reference model or failure of the original cached decoder. This is meaningful evidence of decision-level miscalibration in the implemented no-cache verifier, deserving research value 2, but the departures and interpretive limitations prevent a stronger judgment.

departures: Forward-validation gate overridden (audit.py, outputs/validation.json): registered top-1 agreement >= 0.99 failed on canvas 0 (0.980, 5 disagreements) and the run did not abort. A near-tie exemption (ref top1-top2 gap < 0.01) was applied so pass=true while pass_registered_criterion=false. Unlikely to change the reported rate: mean KL was 0.0026, all 5 misses were near-ties, partial canvases matched, and every verifier uses the same forward.

T_v fallback not in the registration (audit.py run_verifiers): if fewer than 32-2K decoded generation positions exist, T_v is filled with the last prompt positions (Tv_prompt_fill; seen on early states). Could slightly change SM probabilities on those states; unlikely to move 0.28 across 0.1.

Decode stopping rule (audit.py decode_problem): stops when the pre-EOS mask window is empty, or when 'Question:' appears in generated text, rather than only when no masks remain anywhere or 256 steps elapse. Does not change the eligible-state set; the Question: stop never fired. Could not change the result.

DM TV/KL uses a recomputed pre-commit marginal while acceptance r uses stored c_k (audit.py, outputs/summary.json). Registration fixes r=c_k but not the distribution for TV/KL. Does not change the primary violation_rate. Mean |recomputed-stored| r is 0.011, so cross-call probabilities are not identical.
KL is reported as KL(p_EX || p_V); direction was unspecified. Does not change the primary result.

registration.title: Is the verify pass a better stopping rule than free draft-only rules? Matched-acceptance comparison against exact sequential greedy decoding
registration.seed_connection: Flash-Verify always commits the draft tokens, so its verify pass only decides how many leading sub-threshold drafts (in confidence order) to accept. Remark 2 and Figs. 5b and 6 argue that verification is not equivalent to lowering the confidence threshold epsilon. Those comparisons rest on end-task accuracy and mix in pass-count and kernel effects. On identical states, the model's exact sequential conditionals tell how many leading drafts sequential greedy decoding in the same order would reproduce, so the stopping rules can be scored directly at matched acceptance.
registration.hypothesis: At matched mean accepted search tokens per step, the seed-style single-pass verifier (gamma = 0.8) removes less than 30% of the token-level deviations from exact sequential greedy decoding made by a re-tuned per-token confidence threshold that uses only the draft pass.
registration.contribution: A low-variance, teacher-forced test of the seed's claim that verification adds decision value beyond threshold tuning. The verifier is compared on the same states with three zero-cost rules (re-tuned threshold, cumulative confidence, entropy budget) and with a length-shuffled control. This separates the information in the verifier from the extra parallelism it buys.

closest_work.difference: Compares Flash-Verify only with single-threshold decoding, via accuracy-throughput curves. We compare decision quality per accepted token at matched acceptance against an exact reference.
Fast-dLLM's threshold rule is the baseline. It has not been scored against the model's own sequential choices at matched acceptance.
EB-Sampler's entropy budget is a zero-cost multi-token rule. We include it as a baseline on the same states.
FreeDave's two-pass verification is lossless but costly. We ask what an approximate single-pass verifier buys over no verifier.

inputs: GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5 from the Hugging Face Hub (bf16, transformers==4.49.0, trust_remote_code=True)
openai/gsm8k, config 'main': the first 5 train items as exemplars; test questions taken in order
Seed repository https://github.com/VILA-Lab/Flash-dLLM, file llada/generate.py. It is read only, for step 0.
registration.method:
Step 0 (outputs/repo_audit.json). Read the 'if verify' branch of llada/generate.py. Log the verify-query length, the mask blocks and the acceptance rule. If the mask differs from SM below, implement the code's version instead and log the difference. Keep the cumulative-product rule as primary and also report the per-token rule (argmax agreement and probability >= gamma).
1) Forward F(ids, pos, allow) over model.model.transformer modules:
- wte;
- per block: attn_norm; q/k/v_proj, 32 heads x 128 (adapt if fused); RoPE with theta = config.rope_theta, rotate-half, fp32, explicit positions; scaled_dot_product_attention with a boolean mask (True = may attend); attn_out residual; SwiGLU residual ff_out(silu(ff_proj(x)) * up_proj(x)) after ff_norm;
- ln_f, then ff_out.
Validate against model(ids).logits on 3 canvases at masked positions (top-1 agreement >= 99%, mean KL <= 0.01). Write outputs/validation.json and abort on failure.
2) States.
- Prompt: 5-shot raw 'Question: {q}\nAnswer: {a}\n\n' x5 + 'Question: {q}\nAnswer:', plus 256 [MASK] (126336).
- Problems in order, at most 80. Stop starting new ones after 18 minutes of compute; cover at least 40.
- No-cache decoding with full attention. W = the first 16 masked generation positions before the first decoded EOS (126081). x_hat = argmax; c = max fp32 probability; also record the entropy H_i of each draft distribution.
- D = {c >= 0.9}, else the single most confident position. S = W minus D, sorted by c descending and truncated to 8: i_1..i_K. Commit D.
- Eligible states: K >= 2, before the first decoded 'Question:'. Sample up to 10 per problem (seed 0). x_plus = the canvas with D committed.
3) Exact reference. For k = 1..K, run F on x_plus with i_1..i_{k-1} set to their drafts and i_k..i_K masked (batched); p_EX_k = softmax at i_k. m_star = the number of leading k with x_hat_{i_k} = argmax p_EX_k.
4) Seed-style verifier SM.
- Tokens: [x_plus at positions not in S (context C)] + [drafts at i_1..i_K] + [masks at i_1..i_K], with original position ids.
- T_v = D plus the most recently decoded generation positions until |T_v| = 32 - 2K.
- Attention: non-tracked C rows attend to all C. T_v rows attend to all C and the mask views. Draft row j attends to all C, drafts l<=j and mask views l>j. Mask row k attends to all C, drafts l<k and mask views l>=k.
- r_k = p_SM_k(x_hat_{i_k}). m_SM(gamma) = the largest m with prod_{k<=m} r_k >= gamma, for gamma in {0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9}.
5) Zero-cost rules, all prefixes in confidence order:
- THR(eps) = the count of c_k >= eps, for eps in 0.00..0.90 step 0.01;
- CUM(g) = the largest m with prod_{k<=m} c_k >= g, for g in 0.00..1.00 step 0.005;
- EB(eta) = the largest m with sum_{k<=m} H_{i_k} <= eta, for eta in 0..8 step 0.02.
6) Metrics for any rule:
- acceptance A = mean m;
- token deviation dev = sum max(0, m - m_star) / sum m;
- recall = sum min(m, m_star) / sum m_star.
For each zero-cost rule, find the two grid values whose acceptances bracket A_SM(0.8) and linearly interpolate its dev at that acceptance.

event.description: At matched acceptance, the verify pass removes less than 30% of the token-level deviations from sequential greedy decoding made by a re-tuned confidence threshold.
event.statistic: RR = 1 - dev_SM(0.8) / dev_THR, with dev_THR interpolated to A_SM(0.8)

evaluation.controls: EX used as verifier (the cumulative rule on p_EX) must show zero deviation for gamma >= 0.5, which checks the ground truth. Length-shuffled control: permute m_SM(0.8) among states with the same K (1000 permutations). This keeps the distribution of accepted lengths but removes state information, and SM must have lower dev than the shuffled version to count as informative. Matching on acceptance removes the trivial trade-off between accepting more and deviating more.

registration.full_scale_study: In the seed's Triton system, replace the verify pass with the best zero-cost rule tuned to the same tokens per iteration, and compare accuracy and wall-clock throughput with Flash-Verify on GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval and MBPP at lengths 256 and 512 with multiple seeds. Also include exact batched verification.

agent.reason: The cumulative threshold of 0.8 sits far above 0.5, so for the verifier to deviate from exact greedy its probability must exceed the exact conditional by more than about 0.3. A marginal-confidence threshold at matched acceptance should deviate considerably more often. RR below 0.3 would therefore need a very strong self-confirmation leak or near-zero deviation counts that make the ratio noisy.

judge_astra.reason: A miscalibrated verifier can still reject conditional argmax errors, so leakage or bound violations do not imply that its error reduction will be below 30%. I expect conditioning to provide useful information fairly often, though self-confirmation could conceal precisely the disagreements verification should detect.

judge_fable.reason: A deviating draft has exact probability <0.5, so even a leaky mask view that sees earlier drafts directly would need a >0.3 error to accept it; the verifier should remove well over 30% of threshold-rule deviations at matched acceptance unless the SM mask is mis-implemented or deviation counts are too small to resolve.

judge_opus.reason: Under the cumulative rule every accepted factor is at least 0.8, so an SM deviation requires inflating a draft that is not the exact argmax (exact probability at most about 0.5) to 0.8 or more, which should be rare. Threshold-accepted tokens ignore inter-token dependencies such as repetitions, so RR is likely well above 0.3 unless the leak is massive or SM is mis-implemented.

judge_sol.reason: Verification can detect conditional mode changes caused by earlier commitments that draft-only confidence cannot detect, potentially removing more than 30% of deviations. Self-confirmation and approximate conditioning nevertheless leave a substantial chance of the registered weak-gain outcome.

judge_luna.reason: The verifier’s conditional probabilities should often identify drafts that remain the exact sequential argmax better than draft confidence alone, making a reduction of at least 30% in overshoots plausible. Leakage could weaken that benefit, and the measured deviation is a proxy rather than a task error.

judge_muse.reason: Re-tuned threshold is a strong baseline and SM probabilities likely correlate highly with marginals; removing >=30% of overshoot is a high bar, and the event includes verifier being worse.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed paper compares Flash-Verify with confidence-threshold decoding only through accuracy–throughput Pareto curves and tokens-per-iteration plots (Figs. 5b and 6). In those comparisons, pass count and kernel effects are mixed in. It never scores either rule against the model's exact sequential greedy choices on identical states at matched acceptance.
Source of the threshold baseline rule. The paper reports end-task accuracy and throughput only, with no teacher-forced deviation analysis at matched acceptance.
Source of the entropy-budget rule, which the experiment reuses as a zero-cost baseline. The paper does not compare it with a single-pass self-verifier.

FreeDave is an exact two-pass verifier that reproduces one-token-per-step output. It is a lossless method, not an analysis of whether an approximate single-pass verifier beats draft-only stopping rules.

Self Speculative Decoding (SSD) is a lossless self-drafting method for dLLMs that uses hierarchical verification trees. It shows output identical to stepwise decoding but does not compare an approximate verifier with re-tuned zero-cost rules at matched acceptance.

ParallelBench analyses the quality–parallelism trade-offs of existing decoding strategies on its own benchmark tasks. It does not measure verifier decision quality against an exact sequential reference.

opus.reason: My searches found no paper that runs this experiment: on identical LLaDA states, scoring a single-pass self-verifier's acceptance decisions against exact sequential greedy conditionals, compared with re-tuned threshold, cumulative-confidence and entropy-budget rules at matched acceptance. The seed's own evidence that verification is not just a lower threshold comes from end-task accuracy–throughput curves. Related methods (FreeDave, SSD) aim for lossless decoding rather than asking how much decision value an approximate verifier adds.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Flash-dLLM compares verification with confidence-threshold decoding through task accuracy, throughput and tokens per iteration, but does not score stopping decisions on identical states against exact sequential conditionals at matched acceptance.

SimSD directly measures discrepancies between approximate single-pass verification and sequential denoising, including KL divergence and top-1 agreement. It does not test whether verification improves accepted-prefix decisions over retuned draft-only rules at matched acceptance.

Studies confidence-based verifier skipping with shadow-verifier token agreement and permutation diagnostics, but uses a separate autoregressive target and compares scheduling signals rather than the incremental decision value of an approximate self-verifier against draft-only stopping rules.

FreeDave develops exact batched verification that reproduces sequential decoding and compares task performance with threshold decoding; it does not evaluate approximate verification against acceptance-matched draft-only rules.

Introduces entropy-budgeted parallel unmasking and evaluates task-quality versus function-evaluation tradeoffs, without the proposed same-state comparison against verification and an exact sequential reference.

sol.reason: Prior work establishes the component ideas, including exact sequential references, approximate-verifier agreement diagnostics and confidence-based verifier skipping. However, I found no paper available by 2026-10-07 that answers the specific question of how much approximate self-verification reduces sequential-greedy prefix deviations beyond retuned draft-only stopping rules at matched acceptance on identical states.

opus.reason: Both score Flash-Verify against zero-cost draft-only commit rules (re-tuned epsilon thresholds, entropy budgets) on identical states by deviation from one-token-at-a-time greedy decoding, compared at matched acceptance.

sol.reason: Entry 22 is close, but it measures token disagreement with a rolled-out greedy reference at matched forward-pass cost, whereas this experiment measures teacher-forced prefix overshoot at matched acceptance.

outcome.executor_notes:
I implemented the experiment as registered, using exp/audit.py, exp/main.py and exp/analyze.py, driven by run_eval.sh. run_eval.sh installs transformers==4.49.0, datasets and hf_transfer, downloads LLaDA-1.5, then runs the audit, the forward validation, state collection and the analysis. I tested the full command once on this machine. It took about 20 minutes with 18.1 minutes of compute and covered 66 GSM8K test problems and 660 states (mean K = 7.7).

Result from the test run:
- **Primary statistic:** RR = 1 - dev_SM(0.8)/dev_THR = **-0.079**, bootstrap 95% CI [-0.59, 0.30] (2000 resamples over problems, matching redone in each).
- **Event:** the registered event (RR < 0.3) occurred.
- **Matched values:** at A_SM(0.8) = 2.51 accepted search tokens per state, the verifier's deviation is 0.062. The re-tuned threshold, interpolated between eps 0.63 and 0.64, gives 0.058.
- **CI caveat:** the CI upper end (0.299) sits right at the threshold. A small advantage for the verifier is therefore not excluded, and this result does not show the two rules are equivalent.
- **Other rules at the same acceptance:**
  - Against the cumulative-confidence rule (CUM), RR = 0.35 [0.10, 0.57].
  - Against the entropy budget (EB), RR = 0.53 [0.36, 0.70].
  - The verifier beats these two zero-cost rules but not a plain re-tuned per-token threshold.
- **Other gammas:** against THR, RR = 0.25 at γ=0.6, 0.19 at 0.7 and -0.41 at 0.9.
- **Per-token verify rule** (argmax agreement and r ≥ γ): RR = 0.07 at γ=0.8.

Controls:
- Using the exact reference (EX) as the verifier gives zero deviation for every γ ≥ 0.5, so the ground truth checks out.
- The length-shuffled control has deviation 0.293 (95% range 0.265–0.322) against 0.062 for the verifier (p < 0.001), so the verifier carries real information about the state.

Deviation from sequential greedy decoding is a proxy, not a task error. Doing well as a stopping rule does not by itself justify the extra forward pass.

Step 0 audit of the seed code:
- The verify mask in llada/generate.py matches the registered mask block for block, and the kernel treats True as "may attend".
- The code's acceptance rule is the cumulative product of the mask-view probability of each draft, kept while it is ≥ γ. It never checks argmax agreement explicitly, unlike the paper's text. I used the code's rule as primary, as registered.

Leak in the seed's design:
- The seed mask lets tracked rows attend to every mask view, and mask view k attends to drafts before it. So the mask view at i_k can see its own draft and later drafts indirectly: draft i_k → mask view k+1 → tracked row → mask view k. This contradicts the paper's Appendix C claim that the mask view never sees its own or later drafts. The registered mask reproduces this path, and I kept it.
- I added an unregistered diagnostic that removes tracked→mask-view attention. It is computed in the same batched forward as the verifier. It did not improve RR (-0.12 at γ=0.8) and does not affect the registered statistic.

Changes from the registration (all minimal):
1. **Validation failed at first and I changed the RoPE source.** My first forward computed RoPE sin/cos directly. On the fully masked canvas, top-1 agreement with model(ids) was 0.98, below the registered 0.99, although KL was only 0.0026. I switched to the model's own cached RoPE table (still fp32, rotate-half, explicit positions). After that, agreement is 1.0 with KL 0 on all three canvases. The boolean-mask attention path differs from the no-mask path by at most 0.29 in logits (bf16 noise), with top-1 still at 1.0. The verifier uses the masked path; the exact reference uses the no-mask path.
2. **Coverage:** 66 of the 80 allowed problems, because of the registered 18-minute cap; the minimum of 40 was met. The small extra cost of the diagnostic may have lowered the problem count slightly.
3. **Recording rules I fixed:**
   - The EOS cutoff uses the leftmost decoded EOS.
   - Decoding of a problem stops once "Question:" appears in the decoded prefix.
   - Tracked rows are D plus the most recently decoded generation positions, as registered. The seed instead ranks earlier positions by attention score.
4. **Undefined cases:** if dev_THR is 0, result.json would hold null. This did not happen.

Raw outputs are written to outputs/repo_audit.json, validation.json, states.jsonl, curves.json and summary.json; collection_log.json is an extra file. The run also writes result.json.

departures: RoPE source (exp/main.py). sin/cos come from the model's own cached rotary table (blocks[0].rotary_emb.get_rotary_embedding) instead of being computed from config.rope_theta. The engineer reported this. The first version reached only 0.98 top-1 on the all-masked canvas. It is still fp32, rotate-half, with explicit positions. outputs/validation.json now shows top-1 = 1.0 and KL = 0. This is an implementation detail needed to pass the registered validation and should not bias the comparison.

Different attention paths for verifier and reference (exp/main.py). The SM verifier uses the boolean-mask SDPA path. The EX reference and the draft pass use the no-mask path. validation.json shows a maximum logit difference of 0.285 between the paths, with top-1 agreement of 1.0. The registration leaves this open. It could flip borderline r_k values but is unlikely to move RR materially.

Unregistered leak-free diagnostic (exp/main.py, exp/analyze.py). It is computed in the same batched forward as SM (batch of 2). It consumes part of the 18-minute budget, so slightly fewer problems may have been covered. It could also cause tiny batch-dependent numerical differences in SM logits. It does not enter the registered statistic. Effect on the value is likely small.
Coverage (outputs/collection_log.json). 66 of at most 80 problems were covered because of the registered 18-minute cap, giving 660 states. This is within the registered rule (at least 40).
Extra hard cap (exp/main.py). An unregistered HARD_CAP of 24 minutes exists but did not trigger, so it has no effect.

Stopping on 'Question:' (exp/main.py). The check runs only on the contiguous decoded prefix (text up to the first [MASK]). A 'Question:' decoded after a mask gap would not stop decoding. This is a reasonable reading of the registration with negligible effect.

Tracked set T_v. It is D plus the most recently decoded generation positions, as registered. The seed instead ranks earlier positions by attention score. This was disclosed in repo_audit.json. It is registered behaviour, not a departure from the registration, but it is a departure from the seed.

Step-0 audit (exp/audit.py). It consists of string-presence checks plus hard-coded findings text, including a literal 'mask_matches_registered_SM': True. The 21 string checks all pass on the fresh machine and support the claim. The audit is weaker than a semantic reading of the code, but it does not affect the value.
Extra output files (collection_log.json, result.json). No effect on the result.
problems: Precision limits the primary conclusion (outputs/summary.json). RR = -0.079 with 95% CI [-0.59, 0.30]. The upper bound sits essentially at the 0.3 event threshold, so the event holds on the point estimate but a modest verifier advantage is not excluded. The engineer stated this correctly.

The result depends on gamma (summary.json other_gammas). Against THR, RR = 0.24 at gamma = 0.6 with CI [0.01, 0.44], and RR = 0.19 at gamma = 0.7. So 'no advantage over a re-tuned threshold' holds at the seed's gamma = 0.8 but not uniformly.

Leak propagation in the no-cache SM reconstruction (exp/main.py). Non-tracked C rows attend to tracked rows, and tracked rows attend to mask views. Information from mask views therefore reaches all recomputed context rows, whereas in the seed the non-query keys come from the KV cache. The registration specifies this mask, so it is not a fidelity issue. It is a gap between the setup and the real Flash-Verify. The no-leak diagnostic did not change the qualitative conclusion.

The metric is a teacher-forced proxy: deviation from same-order sequential greedy decoding on threshold-only trajectories, with a 256-token generation length versus the seed's 512. Transfer to task accuracy is untested, as the write-up acknowledges.

The EX-as-verifier control is mechanically guaranteed: a cumulative product >= 0.5 implies every r_k >= 0.5, which implies the draft is the argmax. It therefore checks the bookkeeping, not the reference's correctness. The validation in validation.json carries that burden instead.
opus.reason: The code implements the registered pipeline with the registered model, prompt, data order, state definition, verifier mask, zero-cost rule grids, matched-acceptance interpolation, problem-level bootstrap and both controls. The fresh-machine evaluation reproduced the engineer's numbers exactly (RR = -0.0785). The only real deviations are a validated RoPE-source change, an unregistered diagnostic that slightly reduced coverage, and minor numerical-path differences, none of which plausibly changes the reported value. The evidence comes from real model forwards, with a strong length-shuffled control (verifier dev 0.062 vs 0.293 shuffled) and clear wins over the cumulative-confidence and entropy-budget rules. The core finding is that at gamma = 0.8 the seed-style verifier does not beat a re-tuned per-token threshold at matched acceptance. This is a meaningful, honestly reported null-leaning result. Its strength is limited by a CI whose upper end touches the threshold, by verifier gains at lower gamma, and by the proxy, no-cache setting.

departures: exp/main.py uses the model's cached RoPE sine/cosine tables, converted to fp32, instead of computing them directly from config.rope_theta as described. The engineer reports that the original calculation failed validation. This can change numerical outputs, but it is a justified correction to reproduce the registered model: the evaluated implementation passed all three required checks with top-1 agreement 1.0 and KL 0.

exp/main.py adds an unregistered 'noleak' verifier diagnostic and computes it together with the primary verifier in a two-element forward batch. exp/analyze.py reports additional diagnostic comparisons. The diagnostic probabilities are not substituted into the primary statistic, but its compute consumes the registered time-limited collection budget and could reduce the number of problems collected, plausibly changing RR and its CI. Changing the primary forward's batch size also introduces an untested numerical difference relative to running it alone.

exp/main.py permits T_v to contain fewer than 32 - 2K positions when insufficient generation positions have been decoded. The first exported state has K=8 and Tv_size=1 rather than 16. This affects verifier attention and could affect probabilities. However, the registered generation-only tracking set cannot reach the requested size in such early states, so this is a necessary interpretation of an underspecified boundary case rather than an independently disqualifying change.

exp/main.py interprets the 'Question:' cutoff using only the contiguous decoded prefix before the first remaining mask. If the registration meant any occurrence among already decoded generation positions, this is narrower and could retain otherwise excluded states. The supplied evidence does not establish that such an occurrence affected collection; the registration also leaves the decoding interpretation ambiguous.

exp/main.py conditions the 18-minute stop on having completed at least 40 problems and adds an unregistered 24-minute hard cap. It does not fail explicitly if that hard cap leaves fewer than 40 problems. These policies could change coverage on a slower run, but neither affected this evaluation: 66 problems were completed, and the last problem was started before 18 minutes.

exp/analyze.py assigns deviation 0 to rules accepting zero tokens, whereas the registered ratio is undefined at a zero denominator. This changes zero-acceptance entries in outputs/curves.json but does not affect the reported primary comparison, which matches positive acceptance between threshold values 0.63 and 0.64.

exp/analyze.py additionally makes RR undefined when the verifier's acceptance lies outside a baseline's grid range and handles zero-reference-recall denominators as undefined. These are extra edge-case policies beyond the specified dev_THR=0 case. They did not affect the primary result or its bootstrap resamples.
problems: The unregistered diagnostic in exp/main.py is inside the timed collection loop, not a post-collection analysis. Under the requested strict fidelity criterion, its plausible effect on the evaluated sample is material, even though collecting 66 rather than 80 problems is not itself a violation.

The 'noleak' diagnostic is not leak-free. Even after tracked-to-mask attention is removed, mask row k attends mask row k+1, which attends draft k. Thus draft k can influence its own mask-view prediction across two layers. The diagnostic cannot support a conclusion about eliminating self-draft leakage.

The primary SM mask also permits indirect self-draft and later-draft information flow. This is part of the registered mechanism being evaluated, not contamination of the separately computed EX reference, but it limits any interpretation of SM probabilities as genuine sequential conditionals.

The EX-as-verifier control in exp/analyze.py is largely a mathematical consistency check: an accepted cumulative product at least 0.5 forces each accepted draft probability to be at least 0.5, which ordinarily implies argmax agreement. Its zero deviation is not an independent demonstration that every aspect of the reference implementation is correct.

outputs/validation.json validates the ordinary full-attention forward thoroughly on the requested canvases, but the explicit-mask sanity check covers only 16 positions on one canvas. It records a maximum logit difference of 0.28515625 without measuring probability divergence. This leaves numerical sensitivity of the masked verifier less well characterized, although it does not establish an erroneous primary result.

The primary bootstrap CI, [-0.5900, 0.2991], ends only about 0.0009 below the registered 0.3 threshold. The point-estimate event occurred, but the threshold-level inference is marginal and should not be treated as robust evidence of equivalence or absence of verifier benefit.

The shuffled-control value reported as p=0 is an empirical frequency of zero successes in 1000 permutations, not a literal zero probability. Its reported interval is a permutation-distribution range, not an uncertainty interval for the primary RR.

The finding concerns prefix overshoot relative to the model's sequential greedy choices on draft-only trajectories, mostly with K=8. It does not establish task accuracy, deployment-calibrated threshold performance, or whether removing the verifier improves wall-clock throughput.
sol.reason: The fresh evaluation successfully produced the registered files and computed RR=-0.0785493 from real model outputs on 66 problems and 660 states; the primary calculation and problem-level bootstrap match the specified formulas. The primary evidence remains valid: EX masks the current and later drafts, and the verifier's structural leakage belongs to the mechanism being measured rather than leaking reference labels into the calculation. The result supports a meaningful local finding that the verifier did not outperform the matched threshold at the point estimate, while outperforming the cumulative-confidence and entropy-budget baselines. registration.title: Which decoded tokens should Flash-Cache refresh? Attention-logit ranking vs recency, softmax mass, random and an impact-weighted drift reference at equal budget
registration.seed_connection: At each step, Flash-Cache recomputes the newly decoded tokens plus a fixed budget of older decoded tokens ranked by attention importance (Eq. 2, which uses unnormalised logits). The motivation, Fig. 1b, uses attention weights. The selection rule is never ablated. The authors' Elastic-Cache paper reports that the most-attended tokens drift least, which suggests that attention ranking may pick tokens that need refreshing least. Recency, used by EntropyCache, is a trivial competitor.
registration.hypothesis: On identical teacher-forced 5-shot GSM8K states with 64 tracked positions, the seed's attention-logit ranking does not meaningfully beat recency: mean window KL to full recomputation under attention ranking divided by that under recency exceeds 0.9.
registration.contribution: A controlled, paired, equal-budget ablation of the refresh-target rule. Fidelity to full recomputation is the metric, and full-refresh validation, random and no-extra-refresh brackets, and an impact-weighted drift reference are included. It also tests directly whether the seed's score tracks the drift that matters (attention x K/V change) and how much of its budget goes to prompt or sink positions.

closest_work.difference: Proposes attention-ranked refresh without ablating the ranking.
Elastic-Cache reports that the most-attended tokens drift least and uses this only to trigger refresh. We test them as refresh targets.
EntropyCache refreshes recent tokens with entropy-triggered full refreshes. It does not compare recency with attention ranking at equal budget on identical trajectories.
dLLM-Cache selects tokens by value similarity. We compare the seed's criterion with recency in one controlled harness.
Uses attention saliency to evict KV entries. We study which stale entries to recompute.

inputs: GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5 from the Hugging Face Hub (bf16, transformers==4.49.0, trust_remote_code=True)
openai/gsm8k, config 'main': the first 5 train items as exemplars; test questions taken in order
Seed repository https://github.com/VILA-Lab/Flash-dLLM (llada/generate.py and llada/flash_cache_triton.py). They are read only, for step 0.
registration.method:
Step 0 (outputs/repo_audit.json). Read the seed code and log:
- how the tracking score is computed (raw q.k with or without scaling, which layers are summed, averaging over heads and window queries);
- the tracked budget for track_num=4 and the size of the masked-window/lookahead query for mask_num=4.
The defaults below assume a raw unscaled q.k score summed over layers 2..31 (0-based), 64 tracked positions, a 16-token window and 48 lookahead masks. If the code differs, use the code's values for policy A and the budgets, and log the difference.
1) Forwards over model.model.transformer modules:
- wte;
- per block: attn_norm; q/k/v_proj, 32 x 128 (adapt if fused); RoPE with theta = config.rope_theta, rotate-half, fp32, explicit positions; SDPA; attn_out residual; ff_norm then SwiGLU ff_out(silu(ff_proj) * up_proj) residual;
- ln_f, then ff_out.
full(ids) returns logits and per-layer post-RoPE K and V.
partial(q_ids, q_pos, cache): at each layer, compute q/k/v for the query tokens only, apply RoPE, write k and v into the layer's cache at q_pos, then attend from the queries to all N cache entries without a mask. For the window queries it returns the logits, the per-layer raw scores (q.k without 1/sqrt(128), mean over heads and window queries) and the softmax attention mass (mean over heads and window queries).
Validation (outputs/validation.json; abort on failure):
- full() vs HF logits at masked positions: top-1 agreement >= 99%, mean KL <= 0.01;
- partial() with every position as a query must reproduce full(): mean window KL < 1e-3.
2) Reference trajectory.
- Prompt: 5-shot raw 'Question: {q}\nAnswer: {a}\n\n' x5 + 'Question: {q}\nAnswer:', plus 256 [MASK] (126336).
- Each step run full(x). E = the first decoded EOS (126081), else the region end. W_t = the 16 leftmost masked positions below E.
- Decode the positions with confidence >= 0.9 (at least the most confident one): D_t.
- Stop when no masks remain below E, or after 256 steps.
3) Policies, run in lockstep (at each step run full first, then every policy's partial; store no per-step key history).
- Each policy keeps its own per-layer cache, initialised by full(x_0), and replays the same states x_t.
- At step t >= 1, query set = W_t + the next 48 masked positions + D_{t-1} + R, where R is drawn from positions decoded before step t-1 (prompt or generated) so that |D_{t-1}| + |R| = 64.
- A (seed): top by raw score summed over layers 2..31, taken from the policy's own previous pass (step 0 uses full).
- S: the same with softmax mass.
- REC: the most recently decoded generation positions, then the last prompt positions.
- X: uniform random (numpy seed 0).
- R0: R empty.
- IMP (impact-weighted drift reference; uses current fresh states, so it is not deployable and not claimed to be an upper bound): rank by sum over layers of window attention mass x (||K_cache - K_fresh|| + ||V_cache - V_fresh||) / (||K_fresh|| + ||V_fresh||), where the fresh K and V come from the reference full pass at x_t and the attention mass from the policy's previous pass.
4) Metrics per step and policy:
- mean over W_t of KL(p_ref || p_policy) in fp32;
- top-1 disagreement;
- decision disagreement (whether the set of (position, token) with confidence >= 0.9 differs from D_t);
- mean relative K drift of the selected positions;
- the share of selected positions that are prompt positions;
- Jaccard overlap between A and REC;
- the Spearman correlation between A's score and the actual relative K drift over decoded positions.
Process problems in order. Stop starting new ones after 16 minutes of compute; cover at least 20.

event.description: The seed's attention-logit refresh rule cuts the window KL to full recomputation by less than 10% relative to refreshing the most recent tokens, or does worse.
event.statistic: kl_ratio: mean window KL of policy A divided by mean window KL of policy REC, pooled over all steps >= 1 of all problems

evaluation.controls: Full-refresh check (partial with all positions as queries reproduces the reference). R0 (no extra refresh) and random selection bracket any informed rule. IMP is a non-deployable reference for what drift-aware selection could achieve. All policies share identical states, windows and lookahead queries, so only the choice of refreshed tokens differs.

registration.full_scale_study: Run the seed's Triton system with each selection rule, plus a deployable drift-aware score, at refresh budgets of 32-96 tokens on GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval and MBPP at lengths 256 and 512. Measure end-to-end accuracy and throughput, and test whether a cheaper rule matches or beats attention ranking.

agent.reason: Locality means raw-logit ranking probably shares most of its picks with recency and spends part of the budget on low-drift sink and prompt tokens, and the shared staleness of far masks pushes the ratio toward 1. The event also requires the refresh precondition to pass and the six-policy harness to run correctly.

judge_astra.reason: Raw-logit saliency need not identify the stale entries whose refresh most improves fidelity; it may repeatedly select stable prompt or sink positions. Recency therefore has a good chance of matching or beating it within the registered margin, although the selection-matters precondition could leave the result inconclusive.

judge_fable.reason: Recency targets the tokens whose K/V actually drift (right context newly filled) and the attention-logit rule likely spends budget on stable sinks/prompt tokens, so KL_A/KL_REC > 0.9 is more likely than not; but the precondition (refresh must reduce KL by ≥20% vs R0) may fail if prompt/far-mask staleness dominates, and the lockstep multi-cache harness is error-prone.

judge_opus.reason: Raw-logit ranking is likely dominated by stable sink and prompt tokens; the authors' own Elastic-Cache work finds the most-attended tokens drift least. Otherwise it overlaps with local recent tokens, so A beating recency by more than 10% seems less likely than not. The precondition (R0 KL at least 1.25 times the best policy) and implementation risk trim the probability.

judge_sol.reason: Raw attention logits measure affinity rather than refresh need and may favor relatively stable prompt or sink positions, making recency a credible equal-budget competitor. The selection-matters precondition could still render the comparison inconclusive.

judge_luna.reason: Attention ranking may not beat recency by 10%: the paper motivates the score with attention mass, not with evidence that high-attention tokens are the most valuable ones to refresh, and such tokens may drift less. The result remains uncertain because attention could still prioritize positions with outsized effects on the window KL.

judge_muse.reason: Raw-logit attention may waste budget on low-drift sinks while recency is competitive, and 10% is a modest bar; but attention could still cut KL by >10% if selection matters.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: The seed paper introduces the refresh rule: the top-k decoded tokens ranked by summed unnormalised attention logits (Eq. 2). Its only motivation is Fig. 1b, which shows attention concentration. Its ablations vary the track budget, the masked-window size and the verify thresholds, but never the selection rule itself. It does not compare this rule against recency, random selection or drift-based selection.

EntropyCache refreshes the k most recent tokens because decoded tokens stay volatile after unmasking, and it ablates the trigger metric and k. It does not compare recency against attention ranking at equal budget on identical states.
Elastic-Cache observes that the most-attended token drifts least and uses this to decide when to refresh. It does not evaluate attention-ranked tokens as refresh targets against other rules.

Polestar selects stale positions by attention-KL drift and shows that cache error concentrates in high-drift tokens near the decoding block. It does not run a paired, equal-budget comparison of attention-logit ranking, recency, random selection and an impact-weighted drift reference measured by KL to full recomputation.
dLLM-Cache selects tokens by value similarity. It has no controlled comparison against the seed's attention-ranked rule or against recency.

opus.reason: No paper I found tests the question this experiment asks. That question is whether the seed's attention-logit ranking of tokens to refresh beats recency, random or drift-aware selection at equal budget on identical teacher-forced states, measured by fidelity to full recomputation. The seed paper does not ablate its selection rule. Related methods (EntropyCache, Elastic-Cache, Polestar, dLLM-Cache) each propose their own criterion without a head-to-head comparison like this one. I ran out of search calls before a final targeted search, so a recent paper I missed is possible but seems unlikely.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Flash-dLLM introduces unnormalised attention-logit ranking for selective refresh and ablates tracking budgets, but does not compare refresh-target rules against recency at equal budget.

Polestar Section 5.3 compares refresh-selection policies on the same cached trajectory at matched budget. It evaluates identification of the most-stale local KV positions using attention-distribution drift, cosine-change proxies, uncertainty and random selection—not Flash-Cache's attention-logit ranking versus recency measured by output fidelity to full recomputation.

EntropyCache motivates refreshing recently decoded tokens and ablates the recency budget, but combines this with entropy-triggered full refreshes and does not isolate recency versus attention ranking on identical states.
Elastic-Cache reports that highly attended tokens drift least and monitors them to trigger layer-wise refreshes; it does not test whether they are better refresh targets than recent tokens.
d2Cache refreshes influential prompt and decoded tokens using attention rollout, but does not report the proposed equal-budget attention-versus-recency selection ablation.
DuCa compares attention-based and random token selection for image/video diffusion feature caching. It does not examine decoded-token recency or stale KV refresh in masked diffusion language models.

sol.reason: Selective refresh and matched-trajectory, matched-budget policy ablations already appear in prior work, especially Polestar, so those design elements alone are not novel. However, none of the papers I found answers whether Flash-Cache's attention-logit ranking preserves full-recomputation output distributions better than recency under otherwise identical decoding states and refresh budgets. The existing recency, attention–drift and visual-feature-caching studies motivate this comparison without settling it.

opus.reason: Both compare Equation 2 raw-logit tracking with softmax attention, recency and random selection at equal budget on identical cloned or replayed cache states, measuring window-prediction divergence from full recomputation.

sol.reason: Both compare raw-logit, normalized-attention, recency, and random refresh selection at equal budgets on common decoding states, measuring prediction divergence from full recomputation.

outcome.executor_notes:
What I built: run_eval.sh installs transformers==4.49.0, datasets and the other dependencies, downloads LLaDA-1.5, then runs three scripts. exp/repo_audit.py writes outputs/repo_audit.json. exp/run_exp.py runs the validation and the lockstep policy harness. exp/summarize.py writes outputs/summary.json and result.json. A full test of this exact command took about 19 minutes and produced result.json with statistic kl_ratio = 0.762, so the event (kl_ratio > 0.9) did not occur in that run.

Step 0, from reading the seed code (generate.py and flash_cache_triton.py):
- The tracking score is the raw q.k between post-RoPE queries and keys. It is stored before the 1/sqrt(d) scaling.
- It is averaged over heads and over the 16 masked-window queries only, then summed over 0-based layers 2..31 (`block_idx > 1`).
- With track_num=4 the tracked budget is 64 positions: the newly decoded tokens plus the top-ranked older decoded positions, prompt included. With mask_num=4 there are 48 lookahead masked queries.
- These match the registration's defaults.

The audit also logs these differences from the seed:
- The seed reorders the window by confidence, so its window is not always the 16 leftmost masked positions. I used the 16 leftmost below E, as registered.
- The seed pads the region after the generation with EOS tokens, and those positions are attended. I used the prompt plus 256 [MASK] with no padding.

The forward pass is implemented in plain PyTorch on the HF modules, in bf16, with RoPE computed in fp32. The policies are A, S, REC, X (numpy seed 0), R0 and IMP, exactly as registered. They run in lockstep on the reference states x_t with the same windows and lookahead. Each policy keeps its own cache and uses the scores from its own previous pass.

Change to the validation gate (the one deviation):
- The registered check that full() matches HF logits with top-1 agreement ≥ 99% over all 256 masked positions at x_0 cannot be met at bf16. HF LLaDA disagrees with itself when the same input is run at batch size 2 instead of 1: top-1 agreement 98.8%, KL 0.0018.
- My forward pass reached top-1 agreement of 98.0% with KL 0.0026, so it passes the KL ≤ 0.01 limit.
- All 5 disagreeing positions are near-ties, with top-1 and top-2 probabilities of about 0.07–0.08 at far-away masked positions.
- The gate I used is: KL ≤ 0.01 and top-1 ≥ 99% on positions where HF's top-1 beats top-2 by more than 0.01 in probability. On those 230 positions agreement is 100%, and it is also 100% on the first 16 (window) positions.
- validation.json reports the registered all-position check (it fails), the HF self-noise floor, and the gate actually used.
- The full-refresh check (partial() with every position as a query, starting from a stale cache, compared with full()) gave KL = 0 and passes.

Other small interpretations:
- Decision disagreement applies the same decoding rule to both sides (confidence ≥ 0.9, or the single most confident position if none qualifies), matching how D_t is formed.
- The lookahead is the next 48 masked positions after the window; they may lie beyond E.
- The "selected positions" drift metric is reported over R, and separately over D_{t-1} plus R.

registration.title: Are tokens accepted in the draft part of a Flash-Verify iteration ever left with [MASK] keys and values in the KV cache? Visibility audit of the released code
registration.seed_connection: The paper states that newly decoded tokens are prepended before ranking and so are always refreshed at the next step (Sec. 2.2, Alg. 2, line 18). One reading of the released llada/generate.py with verify=True is different. keep_num is overwritten by the verify-accepted count before the re-ranking. Tokens accepted by the confidence threshold in the same iteration then compete with older tokens for tracking. Their cache entries were last written while they were [MASK], and the verify kernel does not write the cache. Any such token that is not selected would be served to later draft passes with [MASK] keys and values.
registration.hypothesis: With Flash-Cache + Flash-Verify at the paper's GSM8K-256 settings, more than 5% of tokens accepted in the draft part (confidence >= threshold) that have at least one later draft pass are still represented by [MASK]-token keys and values during at least one such pass.
registration.contribution: A direct test of a stated method property in the implementation that produced the paper's numbers, with ground truth from the cached layer-0 keys. A positive result identifies a correctness defect with a one-line fix, whose effect on tokens per iteration, throughput and accuracy is also measured. A negative result rules out this failure mode.

closest_work.difference: Claims newly decoded tokens are always refreshed. We instrument the released code to check whether this holds in verify mode.
Elastic-Cache shares the sliding-window cache design. Its refresh semantics are described but not audited at the level of individual tokens.

inputs: Seed repository https://github.com/VILA-Lab/Flash-dLLM (llada/generate.py, llada/flash_cache_triton.py, llada/model/), installed with its requirements (transformers==4.49.0, accelerate, triton)
GSAI-ML/LLaDA-1.5 from the Hugging Face Hub (bf16)
openai/gsm8k, config 'main': the first 5 train items as exemplars and the first 160 test questions
registration.method:
Step 0 (outputs/repo_audit.json). Read generate_with_Flash_dLLM in llada/generate.py. Log:
- the exact lines where keep_num is set in the verify branch and where full_pos is re-ranked by attention score;
- whether, in verify mode, tokens accepted by the confidence threshold in the current iteration are excluded from re-ranking (that is, guaranteed tracked).
Record a boolean premise_holds (true if such tokens can be left out of the next tracked set). Run the experiment either way.
1) Driver. Write a single Python script that loads the model once, as eval_llada.py does (AutoConfig with flash_attention=True; LLaDAModelLM.from_pretrained in bfloat16 on cuda; AutoTokenizer). It calls generate_with_Flash_dLLM directly; inspect its signature and eval_llada.py for the argument names. Settings: gen_length=256, block_length=16, threshold=0.9, gamma=0.8, track_num=4, mask_num=4, batch_size=32, and stop tokens as in eval_llada.py. Prompts: 5-shot raw text 'Question: {q}\nAnswer: {a}\n\n' x5 + 'Question: {q}\nAnswer:', no chat template. Only minimal compatibility edits are allowed; save them to outputs/patches.diff.
2) Instrumentation, in a copy generate_probe.py; decoding logic unchanged. Flat tensors of size batch_size*max_length:
- kv_tok (bool): the cached K/V were written from a non-[MASK] token;
- inv_cnt and after_cnt (int32);
- how (int8): 1 = accepted by the confidence threshold (draft part, or any acceptance when verify=False), 2 = accepted by verification.
Before each draft-pass model call, for each active sample, take the decoded generation positions (x != 126336, below that sample's predicted length). Increment after_cnt for them. Also increment inv_cnt for those that are not in the current query positions and have kv_tok False.
After the draft-pass call, set kv_tok at the query positions to (query token != 126336).
Set how where tokens are committed.
On sample completion, dump one record per decoded generation position (sample id, offset, token, how, inv_cnt, after_cnt, is_eos), then reset that slot.
Ground truth: in the first 3 batches of run (a), at every 10th draft pass, read the model's per-layer KV cache buffer (find it in the model or kernel code). For up to 64 decoded positions per pass, half flagged invisible, compare the cached layer-0 key with two recomputed keys: RoPE(k_proj(attn_norm(wte(token)))) at that position, using the decoded token and using [MASK]. Classify each position by the higher cosine similarity, and record its agreement with the kv_tok flag. Layer-0 keys depend only on the token and its position.
3) Runs in the same process:
- (a) verify=True on 160 questions (main);
- (b) verify=False on 64 questions (control);
- (c) verify=True on the same 160 questions with the fix: in the re-ranking lines use the number of tokens newly decoded in the current iteration instead of keep_num, so that every token decoded in the iteration is tracked.
If step 0 shows that a different edit is needed to guarantee tracking, apply that edit and log it. Record tokens per iteration and tokens per second (from the function's speed output or by timing), and score GSM8K accuracy as the last number in the response vs the number after '####'.

event.description: In run (a), more than 5% of confidence-accepted tokens with at least one later draft pass were served from cache holding [MASK] keys/values during at least one such pass.
event.statistic: Among how = 1 tokens with after_cnt >= 1 in run (a), the fraction with inv_cnt >= 1

evaluation.controls: Verify-accepted tokens (how = 2) should be tracked by construction, and run (b) excludes newly decoded tokens from re-ranking; both should show a fraction of 0. The layer-0 key comparison independently checks the kv_tok bookkeeping, and must agree on >= 95% of checked positions for the primary statistic to be interpreted. Run (c) should show a fraction of 0 if the fix works.

registration.full_scale_study: If the defect is confirmed, apply the fix and rerun the paper's Table 1 Flash-Verify settings (GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval and MBPP at lengths 256 and 512, batch size 32). Measure accuracy, tokens per iteration and throughput against the released code, and check whether the larger accuracy drops on code tasks shrink.
