registration.method: Use installed CUDA PyTorch, minimal inference dependencies and only the specified small model downloads. Load native AURORA inference modules with explicit local paths, EMA weights, eval mode, dense attention, bf16 autocast and no compilation or distributed execution. Set the encoder runtime target length and target_latent_len to 128. Form 128-token sequences from within-article 126-token WikiText test windows bracketed by EOS; select 128 windows using shuffle seed 912. Encode and standardize them once. The identical known prompt in both arms is Z[:,0:96], and the scored continuation positions are 96 through 99. Implement the two arms through Denoiser.forward's clean_history, concat_attention_mask, concat_position_ids and repaint_tail_len arguments, without editing model weights. Arm A has clean_history=Z[:,0:96] and a 16-position noisy block covering absolute positions 96 through 111, with repaint_tail_len=0. Arm B has clean_history=Z[:,0:84] and a 16-position mixed block covering positions 84 through 99: its first twelve positions are the clean known Z[:,84:96], while its last four are noisy, with repaint_tail_len=12. In both arms historical queries use the standard blockwise clean-history visibility: a historical position sees historical positions in its own or earlier floor(position/16) block, and never the current block. Current queries see all history and all sixteen current positions. Supply additive masks explicitly so the shorter, partially filled history is legal. Position IDs remain the original absolute positions starting at zero. For sigma in {0.70,0.85} and noise seeds 41,43,47, use the identical epsilon at absolute positions 96 through 99; Arm A's additional noisy positions 100 through 111 use their own corresponding clean latents and the same global noise tensor. Run one draft without self-conditioning and a second prediction with the detached draft in each arm. Extract only the four common continuation predictions. Decode them with the same canonical clean prompt Z[:,0:96] in both arms, requesting 100 logits, and score the four reference token IDs. Before the main run, verify that Arm A's explicit mask reproduces the native clean_history path. This is a conditional-denoising MVE: the intervention changes joint noisy-neighbor availability and known-tail processing together, and does not by itself establish a free-generation quality or cache-specific effect.

event.description: The lower bootstrap bound on the mixed-boundary first-four-token loss penalty exceeds 0.10 nats per token.
event.statistic: Lower endpoint of the article-clustered percentile-bootstrap interval for first-four-token cross-entropy in Arm B minus Arm A, averaged over both noise levels and all noise repetitions.

evaluation.procedure: Average reference-token cross-entropy across the four common continuation positions, then across sigma values and the three noise repetitions within each window. Compute the paired Arm-B-minus-Arm-A difference. Bootstrap article IDs 2,000 times with seed 2026, retaining their windows and repeated conditions, and report the 2.5th percentile of the paired mean differences. outputs/items.jsonl holds article/source IDs, masks or mask specifications, position IDs, noisy-block layouts, reference/predicted IDs and losses. outputs/inputs.pt holds standardized latent and noise tensors needed to reconstruct both arms. outputs/scores.json holds the single registered statistic and event outcome. outputs/manifest.json records source revisions, conformance-check results, configuration and timing. Retain the signed estimate and interval endpoints in supporting records; a failed gate is not an equivalence result.
evaluation.controls: Prompt text, its 96 known latents, common target positions, target noise, decoder context, trained block size and weights are fixed. Arm A must match the native full-block mask path. Directly decoding canonical clean prompt-plus-target latents must give identical results under both bookkeeping layouts. Additional noisy neighbors are an explicit part of the treatment, not concealed as an isolated repaint-time effect.

Test randomized boundary-phase training or boundary-aware sampling, measuring beginning-of-response accuracy, premature EOS, factual copying and latency.

registration.title: Reallocate four guidance evaluations to test numerical counterfactual adaptiveness
registration.seed_connection: AURORA-LM applies prompt classifier-free guidance only at high noise and selects its XSum configuration using ROUGE. Numerical facts may need a different allocation of the same guidance-compute budget than global summary planning.
registration.hypothesis: Moving four classifier-free guidance evaluations from the end of the default high-noise guidance window to the final four solver steps improves paired numerical counterfactual adaptiveness by at least five percentage points.
registration.contribution: Tests guidance timing with an exactly matched number of network evaluations and a source intervention with automatically known expected updates. The target is numerical evidence uptake, not external perplexity, generic quality-diversity trade-offs or a learned hallucination detector.

closest_work.difference: GuideDiffuSeq studies guidance schedules and clamping through quality-diversity metrics. This experiment keeps guidance scale and evaluation count fixed while measuring adaptation to source-number replacements.

This work develops factual-adaptiveness tests for autoregressive summarizers and explicitly excludes numerical entity categories. The proposed test targets numerical surface fidelity in a continuous-latent model and intervenes on inference timing rather than training data.

Its temporal schedule interventions primarily concern self-conditioning guidance and external generation metrics. This experiment manipulates prompt CFG and uses paired source-counterfactual correctness.

inputs: AURORA-LM code, particularly its BlockSampler: https://github.com/fyv587/AURORA-LM.
Released XSum denoiser/config: https://huggingface.co/fyv587/aurora-gpt2-xsum, including 300000.safetensors.
Released shared autoencoder/config: https://huggingface.co/fyv587/aurora-text-autoencoder.
GPT-2 embedding/tokenizer files: https://huggingface.co/openai-community/gpt2.
Only the test split of https://huggingface.co/datasets/EdinburghNLP/xsum; use its public parquet representation if the installed datasets version cannot load the original dataset script.
registration.method: Reuse installed CUDA PyTorch and install minimal inference dependencies. Download only the XSum and AE checkpoint/config files plus GPT-2 embedding/tokenizer files; do not download training corpora or external evaluator models. Load the XSum DiffusionGenerator with explicit local paths, EMA weights and eval mode. Disable compilation, FlexAttention, distributed execution and service logging. Use the native 32-step Euler schedule, block size 16, self-conditioning, CFG scale 2.0, first-EOS truncation and a 64-token generation limit. Set runtime latent capacity to 384 and ensure the encoder's target_sequence_len and target_latent_len agree. Construct a fixed-length input set to permit batched inference: tokenize XSum test documents and take the first 256 tokens from documents having at least 256 tokens. In test-ID order shuffled with seed 1729, select the first 64 eligible documents. Eligibility requires a reference summary containing exactly one unique standalone three- or four-digit integer a, with a present completely within the 256-token source prefix. Select a replacement b of the same digit count, absent from the prefix and reference, by scanning deterministic integer candidates. Replace every whole-number occurrence of a in the visible source prefix and reference with b. Accept only replacements preserving the 256-token prefix length, the reference token count and all token IDs outside replacement spans. Selection must not inspect model outputs. Save the original and counterfactual prefixes and references. Compare two schedules. DEFAULT activates CFG at the native solver indices whose sigma is in [0.9,1.0]. LATE removes the four latest indices from that set and instead activates CFG at solver indices 28,29,30,31. Assert that the two sets have the same cardinality and that these late indices were not already in DEFAULT. Add an optional explicit guided-step set to BlockSampler.run, changing only the cfg_active membership test; retain the native conditional/unconditional self-conditioning tracks and all other updates. Batch equal-length prefixes in groups of sixteen. Generate the original and counterfactual prefixes under both schedules for noise seeds 701 and 709. Reset the RNG identically for each matched batch, or explicitly provide identical initial block-noise tensors, so original/counterfactual and schedule comparisons share noise. Verify exact matched guidance-call counts. Do not filter outputs by generated length or original-arm success. Extract numerical literals from outputs, normalizing comma-separated integer formatting. A pair succeeds only if its original output contains a and not b, and its counterfactual output contains b and not a. Empty outputs, omissions and both-number outputs fail. This measures selected numerical surface adaptiveness on standardized truncated inputs, not exhaustive summary factuality or preservation of paraphrased number words.

event.description: The lower bootstrap bound on the late-reallocated schedule's paired numerical adaptiveness gain exceeds five percentage points.
event.statistic: Lower endpoint of the document-paired percentile-bootstrap interval for numerical-pair success rate(LATE) minus numerical-pair success rate(DEFAULT), expressed as a fraction.

evaluation.procedure: For every document, schedule and seed, compute the strict two-output pair-success indicator from the extracted integer sets. registration.title: Does the learned noisy-input subspace align with token-sensitive decoder directions?
registration.seed_connection: AURORA-LM retains a wide decoder-facing latent while learning a narrow noisy-input projection. Its latent-width and Gaussian-corruption experiments do not establish whether the trained projection preferentially observes directions important to the separate frozen decoder.
registration.hypothesis: At equal standardized-latent perturbation norm, the decoder's excess sensitivity to the learned projection's row space over its null space is greater than the corresponding excess for matched-rank random subspaces.
registration.contribution: Measures alignment between the actual trained prior's observation pathway and its decoder, rather than nominal latent capacity or decoder anisotropy alone. This is an interface-geometry diagnostic; it does not establish preservation of natural numerical distinctions or improved generation.

closest_work.difference: The comparison concerns alignment of a language prior's learned low-rank observation pathway with a separate decoder, rather than the general usefulness of narrow noisy-input pathways.
Instead of auditing PCA compression or decoder margins alone, this test conditions on the released denoiser's actual input projection and compares it with matched-rank random subspaces.

inputs: Code: https://github.com/fyv587/AURORA-LM, including the denoiser, autoencoder and checkpoint loader.
Advertised denoiser checkpoint and adjacent configuration: https://huggingface.co/fyv587/aurora-gpt2-owt.
Advertised autoencoder checkpoint and adjacent configuration: https://huggingface.co/fyv587/aurora-text-autoencoder.
GPT-2 tokenizer assets from https://huggingface.co/gpt2; download embedding-loading weights only if the native loader requires them.
Salesforce/wikitext on Hugging Face Datasets, configuration wikitext-2-raw-v1, validation split only.
registration.method:
Run frozen models on CUDA. Reuse compatible installed CUDA PyTorch, install inference dependencies only, and disable compilation, FlexAttention, NPU operators, distributed execution and training logging. Use the native checkpoint loader, activate EMA denoiser weights, and retain the diffusion checkpoint's latent_mean and latent_std. Record code and model revisions and actual configurations; unavailable or incompatible required checkpoints invalidate the experiment rather than authorize a substitute model. Use bf16 inference, float32 latent arithmetic and float64 SVD/QR calculations.

Require the released representation to have one latent per valid token. Use native variable-length autoencoder calls; a shape-only adapter may expose length-dependent query allocation and masks, but must not change learned weights, width, positions or normalization. Verify causal prefix consistency on eight inputs before collecting results.

Parse validation articles using top-level single-equals headings, remove heading-only lines, and tokenize body text. Shuffle eligible articles with seed 42 and take 40 with at least 254 body tokens. From each, construct two non-overlapping 128-token inputs, each comprising EOS followed by 127 body tokens. Require all 40 articles and at least 99% overall clean reconstruction accuracy. Perturbation scoring uses only positions correctly reconstructed in the clean condition; do not select cases using perturbed outputs.

Identify the noisy-input projection, not the self-conditioning projection. Form W = W_up W_down from active EMA weights. Compute its observable row-space basis Q from an SVD, using relative singular-value tolerance 1e-6. Record both component ranks and the composed rank r; use the composed row space even if W_up is rank deficient. Require 0 < r < D. Draw 16 Haar-random D-by-r bases using Gaussian QR with seeds 100 through 115, shared across all windows and positions.

For each window and perturbation seed 11 and 22, draw a Gaussian matrix G with independently generated rows. For each learned or random basis, form G_row = (G Q) Q^T and G_null = G - G_row. Independently normalize every row of both perturbations to L2 norm rho*sqrt(D), for rho in {0.2, 0.5, 0.8}. Reuse G across subspaces and amplitudes. Add the perturbations to clean standardized latents, invert the checkpoint normalization, and decode without denoising. Measure token flips relative to clean decisions. Also decode a full-space equal-norm Gaussian control at rho=0.5. Verify subspace membership and per-position norm matching, and record perturbation RMS after inverse normalization. Identical-input decoder replays on eight cases must reproduce token IDs. Do not train a readout or run the denoiser.

event.description: The learned subspace has at least five percentage points more row-space-versus-null-space decoder sensitivity than matched-rank random subspaces.
event.statistic: The one-sided 95% bootstrap lower bound on mean_article[(flip_learned_row - flip_learned_null) - mean_random_basis(flip_random_row - flip_random_null)], averaged within articles over windows, amplitudes and perturbation seeds.

evaluation.procedure: Calculate learned and basis-specific row-minus-null contrasts for each article, averaging its two windows, three amplitudes and two perturbation seeds. Use 2,000 bootstrap replicates with seed 2026; independently resample articles and the 16 random bases with replacement in each replicate. The fifth percentile is primary_statistic. Report the point estimate, separate one-sided lower and upper 95% bounds, a two-sided 95% percentile interval, amplitude-specific results and variation across random bases. cases.jsonl holds article identities, selection decisions, original and clean-decoded IDs and clean-correct masks. observations.jsonl holds condition-specific decoded IDs or flip masks, norms and contrasts. geometry.safetensors holds projection matrices, singular values, bases and clean standardized latents. manifest.json holds revisions, configurations, timings and validation results. result.json holds the registered statistic and validity status. Failed loading, validation, clean recovery, coverage or completion produces an invalid or insufficient result with a null primary statistic. A failed event does not establish equivalence; an upper bound below 0.05 only excludes the registered meaningful excess under this design.
evaluation.controls: Composed-projection rank verification; 16 matched-rank random bases; coupled Gaussian draws; equal per-position standardized MSE; clean reconstruction ceiling; full-space Gaussian control; numerical replay. Decoder-space norms expose effects of inverse normalization, so any finding concerns the complete standardized-latent decoder interface rather than intrinsic decoder sensitivity alone.

models: fyv587/aurora-gpt2-owt, EMA weights for projection extraction

registration.full_scale_study: Measure alignment across independently trained priors and bottleneck widths, then compare decoder-aligned and random bottleneck initialization under matched training compute. Evaluate natural number, name and rare-subword distinctions alongside generation quality before interpreting alignment as useful information preservation.

agent.reason: A projection learned for denoising should favor useful signal directions, but latent-MSE importance need not coincide with decoder sensitivity. The five-point excess averaged over modest perturbation amplitudes, plus the clean-reconstruction gate, makes this stronger event uncertain.

judge_astra.reason: The projection may learn informative directions, but latent-MSE optimization does not guarantee preferential alignment with decoder decision margins over random subspaces. The paper's reported decoder robustness also suggests that the smaller perturbation amplitudes could dilute the averaged contrast below the five-point threshold.

judge_fable.reason: Even if the released checkpoints load, the decoder's demonstrated tolerance of isotropic corruption up to sigma~0.7 implies that Gaussian perturbations at relative norm <=0.8, even concentrated in a 128-dim subspace, will flip few tokens unless the learned subspace captures nearly all margin-gradient energy; a >=5pp excess over random bases averaged across three amplitudes (two of which are likely near-zero everywhere) is a stretch, and infrastructure/validation failure also counts against the event.

judge_opus.reason: This is the simplest experiment and the most likely to run validly. A perturbation spread over a 128-dimensional row space can concentrate at most D/r ≈ 6× more variance on sensitive directions than isotropic noise. Even with perfect alignment, ρ=0.8 therefore behaves roughly like isotropic noise at σ≈0.66, near the knee of the paper's Fig. 5a robustness curves, so a flip excess averaged over ρ = 0.2/0.5/0.8 probably falls short of a 5-point lower bound.

judge_sol.reason: Full-latent MSE training provides a plausible route to decoder-relevant alignment, but latent-dropout redundancy and relatively modest perturbations could keep the averaged excess below five percentage points. The paper supplies no direct evidence about this learned-subspace geometry.

judge_luna.reason: The paper reports that a 128-wide noisy-input bottleneck improves MAUVE, but not that its learned row space tracks decoder-sensitive directions; the denoiser is trained on latent MSE while the decoder is frozen. The subspace could favor predictable latent structure without exceeding matched random subspaces by the registered five points.

judge_muse.reason: Paper Fig.5a shows near-perfect recovery at corruptions comparable to rho<=0.8, implying floor effects when averaging three amplitudes; isotropic standardized-MSE training provides no explicit pressure for decoder-sensitive alignment, making a 5pp lower-bound excess unlikely.

closest_work.difference: This paper audits continuous diffusion LMs as representation-decoder systems, using decoder margins, local decoder sensitivity and readout simplicity on ELF and other checkpoints. It never compares a trained denoiser's low-rank noisy-input projection with the decoder's sensitivity, and it has no matched-rank random-subspace baseline.

JiT argues that predicting clean data lets narrow or low-capacity input pathways work in high dimensions, and it uses images. It does not test whether a learned bottleneck lines up with the directions a separate text decoder is sensitive to.

The seed paper introduces the narrow noisy-input pathway and tests how latent width and Gaussian corruption affect it. Its abstract does not mention checking whether the learned projection's row space favors decoder-sensitive directions.

registration.title: Do Gaussian robustness probes overestimate recovery under the prior's own residuals?
registration.seed_connection: AURORA-LM characterizes latent robustness using Gaussian corruption and trains its prior with standardized latent MSE. Actual prior errors may have orientations, bias and cross-position structure that these probes do not represent.
registration.hypothesis: At sigma=0.7, native denoising residuals cause at least eight percentage points more token-recovery loss than independent isotropic perturbations with the same per-position standardized error norms.
registration.contribution: Directly tests whether the seed's isotropic robustness probe predicts behavior under its released prior's errors. Correlation-preserving rotations and decoder-space norm controls distinguish possible explanations without treating the primary comparison as a pure decoder-anisotropy test.

closest_work.difference: The test compares native prior residuals directly with norm-matched controls, rather than measuring Gaussian robustness or round-trip mismatch alone.
Residual directions come from ordinary supervised denoising states, not decoder gradients, PCA directions or constructed basin interventions.
The experiment tests whether isotropic decoder augmentation resembles errors supplied by a learned latent prior, without modifying or retraining the decoder.

inputs: Code: https://github.com/fyv587/AURORA-LM, including native model loading and the clean_history denoiser forward path.
Advertised checkpoints and adjacent configurations: https://huggingface.co/fyv587/aurora-gpt2-owt and https://huggingface.co/fyv587/aurora-text-autoencoder.
GPT-2 tokenizer assets from https://huggingface.co/gpt2; obtain embedding-loading weights only if required.
Salesforce/wikitext, wikitext-103-raw-v1, test split only, downloaded as test-only Parquet or streamed.
registration.method:
Load frozen CUDA models with native EMA denoiser weights and diffusion-checkpoint normalization statistics. Reuse installed compatible CUDA PyTorch, install inference dependencies only, and disable compilation, FlexAttention, NPU operators, distributed execution and training logging. Record revisions and actual configurations. Use bf16 forwards with float32 states, residuals and norms. Required checkpoint or compatibility failures invalidate the experiment; do not substitute models or estimate new normalization statistics.

Require one latent per valid token and faithful variable-length autoencoder calls. A shape-only query/mask adapter is allowed, but learned weights, positions and normalization must remain unchanged. Verify causal prefix consistency on eight examples.

Parse test articles at top-level single-equals headings and remove heading-only lines. Shuffle eligible articles with seed 42 and take 40 with at least 252 body tokens. Construct four non-overlapping inputs per article, each EOS plus 63 body tokens. Encode each 64-position sequence. Positions 0:48 are fixed clean history and 48:64 are the target. Define a fixed target scoring mask from clean reconstruction. Require at least 2,400 distinct clean-correct target positions overall and at least 48 per article; otherwise report insufficient recovery. Do not filter using denoiser or control outputs.

For noise seeds 1 and 2, at sigma=0.7 and separately sigma=0.9, form x=(1-sigma)*z_target+sigma*epsilon. At this same x, first obtain a draft with self-conditioning omitted, then obtain the native prediction using the detached draft as self-conditioning. Both passes use the unchanged clean history. Let e=prediction-z_target.

Decode the clean history followed by z_target+e. For four independent isotropic controls per state, draw a Gaussian vector at every target position and rescale it to the corresponding norm of e. These match per-position standardized MSE exactly. Additionally construct four shared channel rotations R from Haar-orthogonal D-by-D matrices, seeds 500 through 503. Decode z_target+eR; a single R is applied to all 16 positions, preserving the standardized residual Gram matrix and every position's norm. Finally decode z_target+[((e*latent_std)R)/latent_std], which preserves residual norms and Gram structure in decoder-input coordinates instead. These rotation controls and sigma=0.9 are explanatory secondary measurements, not additional event criteria.

Use identical normalization, clean history, decoder positions and scoring masks throughout. Verify norm matching and rotation Gram preservation numerically. Derive all noise/control seeds from fixed article, window and replicate identifiers so batching cannot change them. Complete the planned sample; do not reduce it after inspecting effects.

event.description: Equal-MSE isotropic corruption substantially understates token-recovery damage from native residuals.
event.statistic: The one-sided 95% article-bootstrap lower bound on mean_article(isotropic_control_target_accuracy - native_residual_target_accuracy) at sigma=0.7.

evaluation.procedure: Within each article, pool its clean-correct target positions across four windows, average isotropic accuracy over four control directions, and average both native and control accuracy over the two noise seeds. Bootstrap the 40 article-level paired differences 2,000 times with seed 2026; primary_statistic is the fifth percentile. Report the point estimate, one-sided upper 95% bound and two-sided 95% interval. Report both rotation comparisons, decoder-space norms and sigma=0.9 separately. cases.jsonl holds article/window inputs, eligibility decisions and fixed clean-correct masks. reconstructions.jsonl holds decoded IDs, correctness masks and native/control norms for every condition. residuals.safetensors holds target latents, residuals, initial noise and rotation matrices. manifest.json records revisions, settings, timing and validation. result.json holds the statistic, uncertainty, coverage and validity status. Incomplete execution or failed validation is not a negative event. An upper bound below 0.08 can exclude the registered deficit under these on-path conditions, but not establish equivalence or free-generation robustness.
evaluation.controls: Per-position standardized norm matching; fixed clean prefixes and decoder; clean-correct scoring masks; correlation-preserving channel rotations; decoder-space norm-preserving rotations; another registered noise level. The primary isotropic comparison changes correlation and orientation together, and is not interpreted as isolating intrinsic decoder anisotropy.

registration.full_scale_study: Measure residual geometry along actual sampling trajectories and across token classes. Compare decoder adaptation using prior-generated residuals with Gaussian augmentation and latent dropout, testing exact factual distinctions as well as ordinary generation metrics.

agent.reason: I expect native residuals to concentrate more around token-confusion directions than isotropic errors, which can expend norm in decoder-insensitive directions. judge_astra.reason: Native residuals plausibly contain alternative-token errors and systematic shrinkage that equal-norm isotropic noise does not reproduce. judge_fable.reason: Norm-matched isotropic noise should leave the robust decoder nearly intact, while the denoiser's one-shot sigma=0.7 estimate through a 128-dim bottleneck plausibly decodes to the wrong token at 15-40% of positions, so an 8pp deficit is more likely than not if everything runs; the main risks are checkpoint availability, implementation of the two-pass clean-history forward, and the possibility that the denoiser is already >90% accurate at this noise level.

Native error is therefore probably about 3–8%, below the roughly 10% point estimate the event requires; checkpoint and code-porting risks lower the probability further.

registration.title: Does text-preserving prefix canonicalization change the next latent block?
registration.seed_connection: AURORA-LM trains block conditionals on encoder-produced prefixes but conditions later blocks on generated latents. Re-encoding a generated prefix's exact decoded token IDs changes its latent state while potentially preserving its text.
registration.hypothesis: Replacing only generated prefix latents with text-identical encoder-produced latents changes next-block predictions by more than one quarter of ordinary independent-noise variation.
registration.contribution: Adds a downstream causal intervention to round-trip mismatch measurement. Shared sampling noise and a common decoder prefix isolate changes transmitted through the prior's conditioning state. The experiment tests consequential state sensitivity, not whether canonicalization improves quality or preserves useful extra information.

closest_work.difference: Rather than only measuring generated versus re-encoded latent distance, the experiment measures its downstream consequence while preserving all prefix token IDs.
Only completed language-prefix conditioning is replaced; the current noisy block is not projected during sampling.

inputs: Code: https://github.com/fyv587/AURORA-LM, particularly src/aurora/sampling/block_sampler.py and src/aurora/models/model.py.
Advertised checkpoints and adjacent configurations: https://huggingface.co/fyv587/aurora-gpt2-owt and https://huggingface.co/fyv587/aurora-text-autoencoder.
GPT-2 tokenizer and any necessary embedding-loading assets from https://huggingface.co/gpt2.
Salesforce/wikitext, wikitext-103-raw-v1, test split only.
registration.method:
Use the frozen released models on CUDA, native EMA denoiser weights, checkpoint latent normalization, bf16 forwards and float32 sampling states. Reuse installed compatible CUDA PyTorch and install inference dependencies only. Disable compilation, FlexAttention, NPU operators, distributed execution, training logging and EOS early stopping. Record actual code/model revisions and configurations. Unavailable or incompatible required artifacts invalidate the experiment.

Require one latent per valid token. Expose native variable-length autoencoder calls without changing learned weights, positions or normalization, and validate causal prefix consistency. Use the native 16-step sigma schedule and Euler update, Q=16, ordinary previous-step self-conditioning and no prefix CFG or SC-CFG extrapolation. If a noncached clean_history implementation is needed, validate it against the native one-block sampler on eight encoder-produced prefixes with identical initial tensors. Require relative endpoint RMS difference below 0.005 and at least 99% target-token agreement. Rebuild clean-history caches for every intervention arm.

Parse test articles using top-level single-equals headings, remove heading-only lines, shuffle eligible articles with seed 42 and select 48 distinct articles with at least 47 body tokens. Encode EOS plus the first 47 tokens as an initial 48-position prefix. For history seeds 1 and 2, generate exactly two 16-position blocks without EOS truncation, yielding standardized history H of length 80. Decode H to exactly 80 token IDs Y. Re-encode these IDs directly, without conversion to text and re-tokenization, obtaining E. Construct C by taking the original encoder-produced first 48 latents and E's final 32 latents.

A history is eligible only if its first 48 decoded IDs equal the original prompt IDs, decoding E reproduces all of Y, and decoding the spliced C also reproduces all of Y. Thus token preservation is checked after the splice, not merely before it. Examine exactly the 96 planned histories, record every rejection and do not replace candidates after observing continuation results. Require at least 64 eligible histories spanning at least 32 source articles.

Generate one further 16-position block under H with saved Gaussian initialization epsilon_0, under C with the identical epsilon_0, and under H with independently drawn epsilon_1. Preserve absolute positions 80:96, schedules and self-conditioning rules. Reset target state and conditioning caches between arms. Crucially, decode all three continuation latent blocks after the same decoder prefix C. Verify that every decoded 80-token prefix still equals Y. Replay the H/epsilon_0 arm on eight eligible histories using fresh caches and identical tensors; its token IDs must reproduce exactly. Repeated encodings of identical IDs are numerical checks, not independent substantive controls.

event.description: Text-identical canonicalization changes the next block by more than one quarter of independent-initialization variation.
event.statistic: The one-sided 95% article-bootstrap lower bound on D_canonicalization / D_independent_noise, where each D is an article-averaged fraction of differing next-block argmax token IDs.

evaluation.procedure: For each eligible history, compute Hamming disagreement between H/epsilon_0 and C/epsilon_0, and between H/epsilon_0 and H/epsilon_1, over all 16 continuation positions including EOS. Average eligible history-seed observations within each article, then average articles equally to obtain the numerator and denominator. Require the denominator to exceed 0.05. Bootstrap eligible source articles 2,000 times with seed 2026, retaining their history observations together and recomputing the ratio; primary_statistic is the fifth percentile. Undefined bootstrap ratios make the diagnostic insufficient. histories.jsonl holds source IDs, token IDs, round-trip and post-splice checks, displacements and eligibility. continuations.jsonl holds all three outputs, disagreements and replay checks. latents.safetensors holds H, E, C, continuation latents and saved initialization tensors. manifest.json records revisions, settings, seeds, timing and native-path validation. result.json holds counts, numerator, denominator, ratio and uncertainty bounds. Failed validation or incomplete planned execution is reported separately from a failed event. Report the upper one-sided bound as well; failure to cross 0.25 is not evidence of token-equivalent conditioning.
evaluation.controls: Exact prefix-token preservation after restoring the original clean latents; unchanged initial prompt latents; coupled initialization for the intervention; independent initialization for every eligible history; common decoder prefix; fresh caches; identical-state replay; native-sampler validation. Conclusions are restricted to eligible re-encodable histories.

registration.full_scale_study: Randomize periodic canonicalization during longer rollouts and verifiable continuation tasks, measuring factual retention, diversity and matched-wall-time quality. Compare inference-time canonicalization with training on generated prefixes without assuming that moving toward the encoder range is beneficial.

agent.reason: Generated and re-encoded prefixes can differ along directions used by the prior despite identical decoded tokens, making appreciable continuation changes plausible. Exact round-trip eligibility and the requirement to exceed one quarter of independent-noise variation materially reduce the chance of qualifying.

judge_astra.reason: Training does not explicitly enforce identical conditioning behavior for different latents decoding to the same text, making consequential continuation sensitivity plausible. However, exact round-trip eligibility, native-sampler validation and the bootstrap-ratio threshold materially reduce the chance of a qualifying result.

judge_fable.reason: Replacing off-manifold generated prefix latents with encoder latents probably perturbs the fixed-noise continuation enough to flip a sizeable share of 16 tokens relative to fresh-noise variation, but this is the most complex pipeline (block sampling, cache rebuilds, splice, replay and native-sampler validation at tight bf16 tolerance) and the all-80-token round-trip eligibility rule may not yield 64 histories.

judge_opus.reason: Generated latents, which are x0-predictions at σ≈0.41 behind a 128-dimensional input bottleneck, probably differ substantially from re-encodings of the same tokens. Coupled-noise flow sampling over high-entropy 16-token blocks also tends to amplify conditioning shifts, so a ratio above 0.25 is more likely than not if the run is valid. The probability is held down by the complex pipeline, strict validations (endpoint RMS <0.005, exact replay) and artifact availability.

judge_sol.reason: Generated latents need not equal canonical encoder codes, so replacing them can plausibly affect a prior trained on encoder-produced histories despite unchanged prefix tokens. Exact round-trip eligibility and the requirement to exceed one quarter of independent-noise variation substantially temper the forecast.

judge_luna.reason: The paper trains block conditionals on clean encoder latents but uses generated blocks as later prefixes, giving canonicalization a plausible route to change the next-block state despite preserving text. However, reported generation quality suggests the mismatch may be modest, and both exact round trips and an effect exceeding a quarter of initialization variation are demanding.

judge_muse.reason: Decoder robustness to large corruptions allows generated latents to differ substantially from re-encoded latents while preserving tokens, and the prior never sees generated prefixes during training, supporting downstream sensitivity; whether this exceeds one quarter of full re-initialization variation remains uncertain.

closest_work.difference: Cosmos studies compressed, smooth autoencoder latents for text diffusion, along with their robustness and reconstruction. It does not hold the token-level text fixed while re-encoding a generated prefix, and it does not measure how that substitution changes the next block a block-causal prior generates.

Here the experiment's own closest-work list is the only source for this paper; I did not retrieve it. As the experiment describes it, the paper changes or projects the latent state during sampling, while this experiment replaces only completed prefix conditioning and measures the downstream sensitivity of the next block.

This is the seed paper (AURORA-LM). It trains on prefixes produced by the encoder but conditions generation on prefixes it generated itself. I read its opening sections (about the first 18% of the text) and found no study of what happens when generated prefix latents are swapped for re-encoded latents with identical text. I did not read the rest of the paper.

This paper shows that generated latents can sit close to real encoder latents yet still decode poorly. It examines a separate refinement model and decoder recoverability. It does not run a causal intervention in which a text-identical prefix is canonicalized and the effect on later generation is measured.

opus.reason: Several searches turned up nothing that holds a generated prefix's token IDs fixed, replaces its latents with re-encoded ones under shared sampling noise, and compares the resulting change in the next block against ordinary variation from independent noise. Existing work on continuous-latent text diffusion either measures the latent/decoder mismatch directly or proposes fixes for it, so the question of how sensitive the conditioning is to this substitution appears unanswered. I searched only arXiv and did not read every paper in full.

Reports a same-token clean-versus-generated latent audit of decoder margins and trajectory interventions, but not a downstream continuation test isolating changes in prefix conditioning while holding decoded prefix tokens fixed.

Compares continuous latent rollouts with decode-and-re-encode rollouts on reasoning accuracy, rather than a single prefix intervention with verified token preservation, coupled continuation noise, and a common decoder prefix.

Projects intermediate image-generation latents through decoding and re-encoding for inverse-problem reconstruction; it does not test text-identical completed conditioning states separately from the current denoising state.
The seed establishes encoder-prefix training and generated-prefix inference, but its reported ablations do not test text-preserving prefix canonicalization's downstream effect.

This is a distinct question and intervention, not merely a change of model, dataset, or metric.

outcome.executor_notes: Implemented and tested the registered 96-history, 48-article frozen-model CUDA intervention using released EMA weights, native 16-step Euler sampling, fresh cached conditioning for each arm, exact token-preservation eligibility, common decoder prefix, independent-noise controls, eight native-sampler validations and eight exact replays. All registered raw outputs regenerate, with article bootstrap fifth/95th percentiles and explicit invalid/incomplete reporting. No registered hypothesis, intervention, eligibility criterion, control, evaluation or threshold changed. Exposed native variable-length encoding by lowering only its allocation floor; trained weights/positions/normalization unchanged. An extra encoder allocation check initially mistakenly used the sampler's RMS threshold; corrected this auxiliary check to exact same-shape causal invariance plus documented bf16 numerical checks, retaining the registered sampler threshold unchanged. Final loader fetches test parquet only; dependencies and model/data revisions pinned. Two complete tests reproduced lower bound 0.4404265965 (ratio 0.4824982841; upper bound 0.5262867749), all 96 histories eligible; independent raw-output audit passed. See IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md.

The positionwise Hamming metric is shift-sensitive. In the first continuations.jsonl row, the H and C outputs share content but are offset by two tokens, which counts as many disagreements. Both numerator and denominator are inflated this way.

registration.title: Current-state self-conditioning versus additional Euler steps at equal forward count
registration.seed_connection: AURORA-LM's training drafts are computed at the current noisy state, whereas ordinary sampling carries the previous step's prediction. Its consistency objective may reduce this mismatch, but does not establish which use of a fixed inference budget best preserves tokens.
registration.hypothesis: On the released consistency-trained checkpoint, eight Euler steps with current-state drafts recover more target tokens than sixteen ordinary lagged-self-conditioning steps using the same sixteen target-denoising forwards.
registration.contribution: Tests compute allocation on a consistency-trained block-causal latent language prior. The comparison asks whether training-matched drafts warrant their extra cost relative to finer integration; it does not isolate draft age independently of solver resolution.

closest_work.difference: The experiment compares explicit current-state drafts against additional Euler steps on AURORA-LM's consistency-trained checkpoint, using known-token recovery and equal target-forward count rather than introducing a one-forward correction.
The experiment evaluates the inference-time value of restoring the current-state training arrangement after consistency training, under a fixed compute budget.

inputs: Code: https://github.com/fyv587/AURORA-LM, including src/aurora/models/denoiser.py, src/aurora/diffusion/scheduler.py and the native self-conditioning implementation.
Advertised denoiser and configuration: https://huggingface.co/fyv587/aurora-gpt2-owt.
Advertised autoencoder and configuration: https://huggingface.co/fyv587/aurora-text-autoencoder.
GPT-2 tokenizer and necessary embedding-loading assets from https://huggingface.co/gpt2.
Salesforce/wikitext, wikitext-2-raw-v1, validation split only.
registration.method:
Run frozen CUDA models with native EMA denoiser weights, checkpoint normalization statistics, bf16 forwards and float32 latent states. Reuse compatible installed CUDA PyTorch, install inference dependencies only, and disable compilation, FlexAttention, NPU operators, distributed execution and training logging. Record code/model revisions. Require checkpoint-linked configuration or release metadata documenting nonzero self-trajectory-consistency training; a repository default alone is insufficient. If this provenance cannot be established, report an invalid experiment rather than silently testing a different claim.

Require one latent per valid token and faithful variable-length autoencoder calls without changing learned parameters, positions or normalization. Parse validation articles at top-level single-equals headings, remove heading-only lines, shuffle eligible articles with seed 42 and take 40 with at least 254 body tokens. Construct two non-overlapping 128-token inputs per article, each EOS plus 127 body tokens. Positions 0:112 form a fixed true encoder prefix and 112:128 form the target. Require at least 99% clean autoencoder target recovery and all 40 articles.

For corruption seeds 11, 22 and 33, initialize x=0.2*z_target+0.8*epsilon. Derive seeds deterministically from article/window identifiers and retain identical initial tensors across arms. This is on-path corruption recovery, not unrestricted generation.

Construct N+1 grid points by uniformly spacing native schedule time from the inverse image of sigma=0.8 to zero, mapping back to sigma and pinning endpoints to 0.8 and zero. For the documented tan-d map, use tau_start=(2/pi)*atan(0.8/(d*(1-0.8))) with the checkpoint's actual d. Log the complete grids. Each Euler step uses x_next=(sigma_next/sigma)*x+(1-sigma_next/sigma)*prediction, with no forward at sigma=0.

Arm A uses sixteen Euler steps and one forward per step: no self-conditioning on the first step, then the preceding step's clean prediction. Arm B uses eight steps and two forwards at each current state: a draft with self-conditioning omitted, followed by a prediction at the same x and sigma conditioned on that detached draft. Only the second prediction drives the update. Arm C is an eight-step ordinary lagged control. No arm uses guidance. Thus A and B each use sixteen target-denoising forwards; C uses eight. Use identical clean-prefix prefill costs, or exclude the same shared prefill from both primary counts. Clear target caches between forwards while keeping only legitimate fixed-prefix state.

Validate the implemented lagged loop against native 16-step full-noise Euler sampling on eight inputs using the same initial tensors, requiring relative endpoint RMS difference below 0.005 and at least 99% decoded target agreement. Decode all endpoints after the identical true encoder prefix. Score every target position. Also decode clean targets and initial corrupted blocks. Record actual forward counts and synchronized CUDA timings after warmup, including and excluding prefill separately; equal forward count is not asserted to mean equal latency.

event.description: Current-state drafts improve exact target-token recovery by more than three percentage points at equal target-denoising forward count.
event.statistic: The one-sided 95% article-bootstrap lower bound on accuracy_current_state_8_steps minus accuracy_lagged_16_steps.

evaluation.procedure: Compute exact target-token accuracy for each window and corruption seed, then average the two windows and three seeds within each article. Bootstrap the 40 article-level paired differences 2,000 times with seed 2026; primary_statistic is the fifth percentile. Report the point estimate, upper one-sided 95% bound, two-sided 95% interval, endpoint MSE, eight-step lagged results and measured latency. scores.jsonl holds article/window IDs, source and target IDs, clean and initial recovery, arm-specific endpoint IDs, accuracies, MSE, counts and timing. trajectories.safetensors holds targets, initial noise and target-block state/prediction traces. manifest.json records provenance, revisions, schedules, precision and validation. result.json holds the statistic and validity status. Failed provenance, validation, clean recovery, coverage or completion is not a negative event. An upper bound below 0.03 can exclude the registered compute-allocation gain in this recovery setting, but not show that self-conditioning mismatch is absent.
evaluation.controls: Paired corruption and fixed true prefixes; equal sixteen-forward primary budget; eight-step lagged control; identical canonical decoder prefix; clean and initial-corruption recovery diagnostics; native lagged-loop validation; explicit latency measurement. No target information enters the denoiser except through the registered corrupted target.

registration.full_scale_study: Evaluate draft allocation during actual generation across step budgets and matched latency. Train independent small priors with consistency enabled and disabled to test interactions among draft age, solver resolution and first-step conditioning.

agent.reason: Consistency training and finer integration should already reduce draft staleness, so current-state drafts may not outperform sixteen lagged steps by a robust three percentage points. Documented consistency-training provenance and native-loop validation are additional gates.

judge_astra.reason: The paper's sampling results suggest a meaningful benefit from additional integration steps, while consistency training should reduce the mismatch caused by previous-step drafts. Current-state drafts therefore face a demanding three-point lower-bound threshold, with checkpoint-linked training provenance adding another validity risk.

judge_fable.reason: Self-trajectory consistency is designed to make lagged self-conditioning drafts nearly equivalent to current-state ones, so halving solver resolution to pay for current-state drafts is unlikely to gain >3pp token recovery over 16 lagged steps; the provenance and sampler-validation requirements add further invalidation risk.

judge_opus.reason: The checkpoint was consistency-trained on 16-step trajectories, which favors the 16-step lagged arm. Coarser 8-step integration may be slightly more MAP-like for token recovery, but a lower bound above 3 points is unlikely. The run can also be invalidated by the provenance requirement and by native-loop validation.

judge_sol.reason: Consistency training may reduce stale-draft penalties, while the sixteen-step arm benefits from finer integration and accumulated self-conditioning. A greater-than-three-point advantage for eight current-state-draft steps therefore seems unlikely, with checkpoint-specific provenance adding another validity risk.

judge_luna.reason: The paper's consistency ablation supports few-step sampling, but does not show that current-state drafts beat the finer integration of sixteen ordinary Euler steps at equal forward count. The strict checkpoint-linked consistency-provenance requirement adds uncertainty to obtaining a valid result.

judge_muse.reason: Self-trajectory consistency is explicitly designed to reduce lagged-draft mismatch, so halving Euler steps from 16 to 8 likely costs more integration accuracy than current-state drafts recover, making a 3pp gain for 8-step current-state unlikely.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Untied Self-Conditioning diagnoses the same mismatch: training drafts come from the current noisy state, while sampling reuses the previous step's prediction. Its fix, though, is a training-free sampler that uses one forward per step, tested on ELF and LangFlow with generative perplexity. The paper never tests an explicit two-forward current-state draft against twice as many ordinary Euler steps at equal forward count. Its only current-state-draft result is a prediction-risk control in Appendix C.5, not a test of how to spend a fixed budget. It also does not use AURORA-LM, consistency-trained checkpoints or known-token recovery.

Analog Bits introduced self-conditioning and a two-evaluation self-guidance rule. It does not compare current-state drafts with finer integration at a matched budget, and it does not involve consistency-trained block-causal latent text priors.

The seed paper introduces self-conditioning (with drafts at the current state during training), self-trajectory consistency and SC-CFG guidance, which combines with- and without-self-conditioning predictions. It samples with ordinary lagged self-conditioning. It reports no ablation that swaps in current-state drafts at inference or compares that against extra Euler steps.

opus.reason: Recent work identifies the train–inference self-conditioning mismatch (2608.22244), but its fix is a one-forward correction tested with generative perplexity on other models. No paper I found tests whether spending a fixed forward budget on current-state drafts beats spending it on more lagged Euler steps, on AURORA-LM's consistency-trained checkpoint or anywhere else. The seed paper itself only uses ordinary lagged self-conditioning and SC-CFG at inference, so it leaves this compute-allocation question open.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Analog Bits, Appendix G, already proposes two current-state forwards for self-conditioning, followed by optional self-guidance. It evaluates image-generation sampling strategies, but does not report the registered guidance-free, equal-forward comparison against twice as many lagged steps after consistency training.

Studies cold- versus warm-start self-conditioning and additional fixed-point iterations in ELF and LangFlow. Its refinement experiments hold the number of flow steps fixed rather than trade current-state drafts against additional integration steps at equal forward count.

Diagnoses the same current-state-training versus previous-prediction-sampling mismatch, but evaluates a one-forward geometric and history-based correction, not explicit current-state drafts versus finer Euler integration.

The seed studies direct decoding of corrupted latents and consistency-enabled versus consistency-disabled generation across step budgets. It does not compare the two registered inference-budget allocations on a frozen consistency-trained checkpoint.

sol.reason: Current-state two-pass self-conditioning and its train–inference motivation are established prior ideas, so neither is novel by itself. However, among work available by 2026-10-07, I found no experiment answering whether current-state drafts outperform additional ordinary lagged Euler steps at equal forward count after consistency training; that compute-allocation question remains distinct.

sol.reason: No list entry compares current-state self-conditioning drafts with additional lagged-self-conditioning Euler steps at equal denoiser-forward count.

registration.title: Direct-source versus whole-history guidance at matched extrapolation norm
registration.seed_connection: AURORA-LM applies classifier-free guidance to block-causal conditional generation. A weak branch can remove direct source access, earlier response history, or both; these choices need not produce the same guidance direction.
registration.hypothesis: With gold earlier-summary latents, removing direct source attention while retaining summary history produces a more target-aligned equal-norm guidance direction than removing all clean history.
registration.contribution: Separates direct source access from response-history access in a frozen continuous latent prior while matching guidance-vector magnitude. Retained summary latents can themselves encode source information, so this is not a fully source-independent weak branch. The outcome concerns one-state latent prediction, not demonstrated summarization quality.

closest_work.difference: Instead of confidence-dependent remasking, the weak inputs use a fixed source/history decomposition, with equal-norm extrapolation vectors and unchanged target corruption.
The test distinguishes which past context a latent guidance contrast amplifies while holding its magnitude and absolute target positions fixed.

inputs: Code: https://github.com/fyv587/AURORA-LM, especially src/aurora/sampling/block_sampler.py and src/aurora/models/denoiser.py.
Advertised conditional denoiser and configuration: https://huggingface.co/fyv587/aurora-gpt2-xsum.
Advertised shared autoencoder and configuration: https://huggingface.co/fyv587/aurora-text-autoencoder.
GPT-2 tokenizer and necessary embedding-loading assets from https://huggingface.co/gpt2.
EdinburghNLP/xsum on Hugging Face Datasets, test split only, streamed or downloaded as test-only files.
registration.method:
Load frozen CUDA models using the native loader, EMA conditional-denoiser weights and diffusion-checkpoint normalization statistics. Reuse compatible installed CUDA PyTorch, install inference dependencies only, and disable compilation, FlexAttention, NPU operators, distributed execution and training logging. Use bf16 forwards and float32 latent/norm calculations. Record revisions, configurations and model-loading checks; missing or incompatible required artifacts invalidate the experiment.

Inspect and record the native CFG weak branch's history and absolute-position behavior. The registered comparison below uses explicitly specified branches regardless of native defaults. Label the whole-history branch a native-CFG reproduction only if those checks match; do not conceal discrepancies or alter the registered contrast to fit the code.

Require one latent per valid token and faithful variable-length autoencoder calls. In dataset order, select the first 128 test examples whose serialized source has at least 256 tokens and reference summary has at least 48. Use the repository's XSum source/target serialization, retaining native delimiters and adding no instruction. Construct a source segment of exactly 256 valid positions by truncating only document-body content as needed, counting native source-summary delimiters within that segment. Append the first 48 reference-summary token IDs. Require an unambiguous logged boundary and total length 304; do not invent a fallback formatter. This is a cropped-source teacher-forced diagnostic, not the full XSum benchmark.

Encode the 304-token sequence and standardize it. Source latents occupy 0:256, earlier summary latents 256:288, and target latents 288:304. Verify on eight examples that encoding the first 288 tokens gives the same prefix latents within numerical tolerance, establishing that future target text is not visible in history latents.

For noise seeds 11, 22, 33 and 44, form x=0.05*z_target+0.95*epsilon. At sigma=0.95, obtain three clean predictions with self-conditioning omitted: C sees all 288 preceding latents; U sees empty clean history; H sees only the 32 earlier summary latents. No branch sees clean target latents. Preserve absolute positions: C uses positions 0:304, U uses 288:304, and H uses 256:304. Recompute H's denoiser history from its supplied latents; do not reuse source-bearing denoiser caches from C. Validate the explicit C path against the native conditional forward path before scoring.

Define d_all=C-U and d_source=C-H. Let q_all=C+d_all, the experimentally specified scale-2 whole-history extrapolation. Let q_source=C+(norm(d_all)/norm(d_source))*d_source, using target-block Frobenius norms separately per example and seed. If norm(d_source) < 1e-8*max(1,norm(d_all)), set q_source=q_all and record the degeneracy; do not obtain an advantage by silently removing guidance. Verify equal extrapolation norms.

Measure standardized target-block MSE for q_all and q_source. Also record unguided C error, guidance angles relative to z_target-C, renormalization factors and a random equal-norm direction from C. Decode predictions after the same true encoder prefix for secondary target accuracy and decoder cross-entropy; do not label that cross-entropy language-model likelihood. On 16 examples verify that the two constructions coincide for the first summary block, where H and U have no earlier summary history, and that scale 1 returns C in both constructions.

event.description: The direct-source-access contrast reduces clean-latent prediction error by more than two percent relative to the whole-history contrast at equal extrapolation norm.
event.statistic: The one-sided 95% document-bootstrap lower bound on (mean_MSE_q_all - mean_MSE_q_source) / mean_MSE_q_all.

evaluation.procedure: Average each document's standardized target MSE over its four noise seeds. Bootstrap all 128 documents 2,000 times with seed 2026, recomputing the ratio of mean errors for every resample; primary_statistic is the fifth percentile. Require completion of all 128 documents, successful validation and a nonzero mean-error denominator. Report the point estimate, upper one-sided 95% bound, two-sided 95% interval, unguided C results, angle summaries, renormalization factors and degenerate frequency. scores.jsonl holds example IDs, serialized token IDs and boundaries, branch losses, norms, angles, scale factors and secondary decoder scores. predictions.safetensors holds target latents, noise and C/U/H predictions. manifest.json records revisions, native weak-branch findings, configurations, seeds, timings and validation. result.json holds the registered statistic and validity status. Both guided variants may be worse than C; report that prominently rather than interpreting a relative advantage as a benefit of guidance. A failed event is not equivalence, and a positive event is not evidence of improved factuality or generated-summary quality.
evaluation.controls: Equal guidance-vector norm; identical noisy target and C prediction; fixed absolute positions; fresh history caches; no self-conditioning leakage; unguided C baseline; first-summary-block equality and scale-1 checks; random equal-norm direction; common decoder prefix. Retained summary latents are explicitly treated as context-bearing, not source-independent.

registration.full_scale_study: Evaluate source/history-separated guidance during actual summarization with generated rather than gold history, sweeping guidance windows at matched strength and latency. Use automatically constructed numerical and entity source edits to measure responsiveness alongside ROUGE, omission and repetition, and investigate training dropout that separately withholds source and response history.

agent.reason: Removing response history along with source access could produce a less target-aligned guidance direction. However, retained gold-summary latents already carry source information, and renormalization can amplify a weak contrast; neither extrapolation necessarily improves on unguided prediction.

judge_astra.reason: Matching extrapolation norms removes an easy source of apparent improvement, leaving a directional-alignment advantage that the supplied evidence does not establish. Gold-summary latents already carry source information, so renormalizing the direct-source contrast could amplify a weak or unstable difference.

judge_fable.reason: For a reasonably calibrated conditional-mean predictor both equal-norm extrapolations raise MSE by similar amounts and the direction difference is near zero; the source-only contrast is small and noisy and gets scaled up by a large factor, so a reliable 2% relative advantage is doubtful, on top of needing the XSum checkpoint and a faithful three-branch position-preserving implementation.

judge_opus.reason: With matched norms, the two guided predictions differ only through how well their directions align with the residual of an approximately calibrated predictor. A 2% advantage for the source contrast needs source under-conditioning to clearly dominate, which is plausible but not expected for a model trained for many epochs. Dependence on the XSum checkpoint and serialization adds validity risk.

judge_sol.reason: Equal extrapolation norms eliminate a simple magnitude advantage, and an approximately calibrated conditional-mean predictor offers little reason to expect a systematic MSE advantage between these directions. Underfitting could favor the direct-source contrast, but source information retained in gold-summary latents and cropped-source evaluation make the registered gain uncertain.

judge_luna.reason: The paper reports XSum results with guidance but does not test separated source and history branches. Earlier summary latents are themselves source-conditioned, and equal-norm guidance may still worsen prediction error, so a greater-than-two-percent relative MSE advantage is possible but uncertain.

judge_muse.reason: At sigma=0.95 the history-only prediction should lie much closer to the full conditional than the empty-history prediction, so equal-norm renormalization likely amplifies a smaller noisier source-only direction rather than yielding a consistent 2% MSE reduction.

opus.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: History Guidance (DFoT) builds guidance by dropping all or part of the clean history in video diffusion. It does not separate direct access to a source document from access to the response history, it does not match guidance-vector norms, and it does not test text latents or summarization.

Cola DLM is a block-causal continuous latent diffusion LM that is closely related to the seed. Nothing I found shows it comparing weak branches that drop the source versus the whole history at equal extrapolation norm.

This paper gets its weak branch for guidance from confidence-based remasking in discrete diffusion. It does not use a fixed source/history decomposition and does not match norms in continuous latents.

The seed paper uses CFG in conditional block-causal generation but, judging from its abstract, does not test different weak-branch constructions. This experiment is a new diagnostic built on its released models.

opus.reason: I found no paper that compares, in a frozen block-causal continuous-latent text diffusion model, a weak branch that removes only direct source access against one that removes all clean history, with guidance norms matched and teacher-forced latent MSE as the measure. The closest work is history guidance in video diffusion and contrastive decoding with and without context in autoregressive LMs (from memory; my search did not surface it). Both share the general idea of contrasting with and without context, but neither answers this source-versus-history question in this setting. My search was limited, so a closer paper may exist that I did not find.

sol.label: distinct

closest_work.difference: Context-aware decoding already contrasts source-present and source-absent predictions while retaining response history, including on XSum. It does not compare that contrast against removing all history at matched extrapolation norm or evaluate one-state latent prediction alignment.

AURORA-LM reports conditional classifier-free guidance and XSum guidance-scale sweeps, but not the registered source/history-separated weak branches or an equal-norm comparison of their prediction errors.

Adaptive CFG changes the weak branch through confidence-dependent token remasking. It does not isolate direct source access from earlier response history while holding target corruption and guidance magnitude fixed.
History-Guided Video Diffusion composes predictions conditioned on different history subsets and noise levels. It does not test source-only versus whole-history removal at equal extrapolation norm.

Token Perturbation Guidance analyzes guidance directions and norms on independently corrupted clean images, but constructs weak predictions by shuffling internal representations rather than separating source and response-history access; it does not perform the registered norm-matched contrast.

sol.reason: The source-absent, history-retaining contrast itself has clear precedent in context-aware decoding, and flexible weak branches and guidance-direction diagnostics also predate this experiment. However, among work available by 2026-10-07, I found none answering whether direct-source-access guidance is more target-aligned than whole-history guidance when their extrapolation magnitudes are matched and gold response history is retained. That controlled comparative question is distinct, rather than merely a change of model, dataset or metric.

opus.reason: No list entry separates direct-source from whole-history weak branches in classifier-free guidance at matched extrapolation norm. Entry 57 varies only the guidance window.

sol.reason: No list entry separates source access from response-history access in guidance branches and compares their target alignment at matched extrapolation norm.

outcome.executor_notes:
Implemented in exp/run_experiment.py (launched by run_eval.sh, which installs the inference dependencies). It loads the released fyv587/aurora-gpt2-xsum checkpoint (EMA denoiser, latent statistics taken from the diffusion checkpoint) and fyv587/aurora-text-autoencoder through the repo's native DiffusionGenerator/EvalDiffusionTrainer loader. Both loads are strict. Revisions are pinned to their SHAs and recorded in the manifest.

Settings: bf16 autocast forwards, float32 for latent, norm and guidance calculations. operator_optimization.profile is set to "off". On the first run the auto profile enabled FlexAttention, which then crashed inside the encoder. npu_fused_attention is set to false. No compilation, no distributed execution, no logging.

Data: EdinburghNLP/xsum test split, streamed. The source is serialized with the repo's prepare_xsum_conditional rule: GPT-2 tokens with no special tokens added, then the native sentence-boundary truncation at 960. The native layout is [source | target | EOS] and has no delimiter tokens, so the source segment is simply the first 256 source tokens, followed by the first 48 summary tokens. Total length is 304 with the boundary at 256.

DEVIATION (the registration could not be met as written): the whole XSum test split (11,334 rows) contains only 90 documents with source ≥256 tokens and summary ≥48 tokens, not 128. The smallest change that keeps the question is to use all 90 eligible documents. The layout, sigma, noise seeds, branches and bootstrap (2,000 resamples, seed 2026) are unchanged; the bootstrap simply resamples 90 documents.

Branches (self-conditioning omitted in all three):
- C: explicit concat path over latents 0:288, positions 0:304.
- U: empty history, positions 288:304. This is exactly the native CFG weak call: empty clean_history, absolute positions prefix_len + block offset.
- H: summary latents 256:288, positions 256:304, with its denoiser history recomputed from those latents.
- Guidance: q_all = C + (C − U). q_source is C + (C − H) rescaled to the same Frobenius norm as C − U, per example and seed.

Validation checks, all passed:
- Prefix invariance: encoding only the first 288 tokens gives identical latents (difference 0).
- Explicit C matches the native KV-cache conditional path to relative error 0.0085 (tolerance 0.02).
- predict_x0 is the identity, so the denoiser outputs are already clean predictions.
- EMA weights were actually swapped in.
- First-summary-block check: H equals U exactly and the two guided constructions coincide.
- Scale 1 returns C in both constructions, extrapolation norms are equal, and q_all matches the native cfg_combine at scale 2.
- Decoding gold latents gives 100% target accuracy.

Result (one test run): primary statistic (5th bootstrap percentile) = −0.0196. Point estimate −0.0082, upper one-sided 95% bound 0.0026, two-sided 95% interval [−0.022, 0.005]. The registered event (lower bound > 0.02) did not occur. Not occurring does not mean the two contrasts are equivalent.

Both guided variants are worse than unguided C. Mean target MSE is 0.908 for C, 1.277 for q_all, 1.287 for q_source and 1.216 for the random equal-norm direction. So the relative advantage asked about would not, in any case, have shown a benefit of guidance.

Supporting numbers:
- Both guidance directions point slightly away from the residual z_target − C (mean cosine −0.054 for q_all, −0.064 for q_source).
- Mean renormalization factor is 2.79; there were no degenerate cases.
- Secondary decoder scores are in scores.jsonl and the manifest. They come from a single state at sigma 0.95 and are not language-model likelihoods.

registration.title: Does temporal correlation in latent corruption impair token recovery?
registration.seed_connection: AURORA-LM uses a prefix-ordered latent sequence and measures decoder recovery under isotropic Gaussian corruption. This test asks whether the spatial structure of the corruption matters when the latent positions have causal meaning.
registration.hypothesis: At matched per-coordinate variance, temporally correlated Gaussian corruption reduces decoded token accuracy more than independent Gaussian corruption.
registration.contribution: COSMOS and AURORA study decoder robustness to Gaussian perturbations, but this MVE isolates correlation across latent positions in AURORA's causal representation. It tests whether isotropic-noise robustness is an adequate proxy for robustness to structured errors; it does not propose a new training method.

closest_work.difference: AURORA evaluates latent corruption and decoder recovery, but the reported corruption is isotropic across positions; this MVE changes only the position covariance.
COSMOS studies Gaussian noising, masking, and latent robustness in a different representation; this MVE tests serially correlated noise in a prefix-aligned causal latent.
This report emphasizes decoder recoverability under latent perturbation; this MVE tests a matched-variance temporal-correlation contrast using AURORA's released autoencoder.

inputs: Code: https://github.com/fyv587/AURORA-LM
Models: Hugging Face repositories fyv587/aurora-gpt2-xsum and fyv587/aurora-text-autoencoder, plus the GPT-2-small tokenizer/backbone fetched by the repository download script.
Data: EdinburghNLP/xsum test split, https://huggingface.co/datasets/EdinburghNLP/xsum.
registration.method: Install the repository and fetch the XSum checkpoint, shared autoencoder, and GPT-2-small files. Instantiate the released XSum DiffusionGenerator to access its frozen autoencoder; do not run the diffusion prior. Select 48 XSum test articles with at least 64 GPT-2 tokens and use their first 64 tokens as inputs. Encode and per-channel-standardize the first 64 latents. For each input and each sigma in {0.45, 0.55, 0.65, 0.75}, create two corrupted versions, x_sigma=(1-sigma)z+sigma*epsilon: iid standard Gaussian epsilon, and AR(1) epsilon with rho=0.8 across positions per channel, initialized from a unit-variance Gaussian and using innovation scale sqrt(1-rho^2). Use matched underlying random innovations for the two corruption types. Denormalize, decode exactly 64 token positions, and score top-1 token accuracy against the original input. Compute each corruption type's trapezoidal accuracy AUC over sigma, divided by the sigma range, then report iid AUC minus AR(1) AUC. Write per-example and per-sigma accuracies to outputs/corruption_scores.jsonl and aggregate AUCs and their difference to outputs/summary.json.

event.description: The normalized token-recovery AUC under iid corruption exceeds the AUC under matched-variance AR(1) corruption by more than 0.03.
event.statistic: AUC_iid - AUC_AR1, where each AUC is the trapezoidal area of mean token accuracy over sigma={0.45,0.55,0.65,0.75}, divided by 0.30.

evaluation.procedure: Use top-1 exact token accuracy over the 64 original positions, macro-averaged over the 48 inputs at each sigma. The JSONL contains per-input accuracies for both noise types and all four sigma values; the JSON contains the two normalized AUCs and the registered difference.
evaluation.controls: The same texts, autoencoder, normalization, sigma values, per-coordinate noise variance, and matched random innovations are used for both corruption types. No denoiser training or human scoring is used.

models: AURORA-LM-S XSum checkpoint (130M denoiser, loaded to access the pipeline)

registration.full_scale_study: If the event occurs, compare several correlation lengths and channel/position covariance structures, then test whether training the denoiser with realistic correlated residuals improves token recovery and generation quality on longer OpenWebText and XSum sequences.

agent.reason: AURORA’s decoder is trained and evaluated with isotropic corruption, so its robustness to the same variance arranged coherently across prefix positions is uncertain. Correlated noise could damage shared prefix information, but it could also be easier to tolerate than iid noise.

judge_astra.reason: Correlated errors could undermine the decoder's use of information across neighboring latents. However, a predominantly position-local decoder experiences identical marginal corruption, so the paper's iid robustness results provide limited support for an AUC loss exceeding 0.03.

judge_fable.reason: Token identity for position j lives almost entirely in latent z_j, whose marginal corruption is identical under iid and AR(1) noise, so the effect must come from second-order context pooling; the normalized AUC is also diluted by the near-perfect low-sigma points, making a >0.03 gap plausible only if correlated noise strongly degrades context aggregation in the collapse region.

judge_opus.reason: Token j is readable only from latent j, so the identity readout is position-local or difference-like, and matched-marginal AR(1) noise need not hurt more. Accuracy is also likely near ceiling for sigma up to 0.65 with this autoencoder, so a 0.03 normalized-AUC gap would need a sizable leftward shift of the robustness curve, and the sign is uncertain.

judge_sol.reason: AURORA's iid recovery curves do not establish robustness to cross-position covariance. AR(1) noise could undermine prefix-level averaging, but position-local token information could keep the normalized AUC gap below 0.03.

judge_luna.reason: The two corruptions have identical per-position marginals, and the decoder may rely mostly on each token’s aligned latent, so temporal covariance need not reduce accuracy; shared noise could still be harder to average out, making the registered AUC gap plausible but uncertain.

judge_muse.reason: Token j's novel information is visible only in latent j among its decoding prefix, so per-position SNR is matched and isolating new content by differencing favors correlated noise; an iid advantage exceeding 0.03 is therefore unlikely.
